instances.label: Walking a residential route, the reader reaches a socket-mounted electric meter on an exterior house wall (sometimes behind a fence, shrubbery, or in a carport) and checks it while reading: ring seal and utility seal present and unbroken, glass cover intact, no jumper wires or bypass in the socket, no tilt/scorching, no signs of the meter having been pulled and reinstalled after disconnection. Conditions vary: weather, dogs, locked gates, obstructions.

Residential gas meter at the side of a house or in a basement/closet: reader checks the locking seal or lock ring on the index and the shutoff valve, looks for corrosion, bent piping, meter-bar damage, evidence of a bypass hose or of a locked-off meter having been turned back on, and for damaged or missing tamper tags.

Curbside or lawn water meter in a below-grade pit/box: reader lifts or pries the lid (often with a hook), clears mud, water, insects, or debris, then inspects the meter body, register glass, seal wire on the register, and connections for evidence of reversal, bypass piping, or a tampered curb stop, plus damaged lid or box.

Meter bank at a multi-unit apartment or small commercial building: a row of electric or gas meters in an alcove, meter closet, or property-managed meter room with a fixed layout; the reader checks each unit's seals, socket covers, panel locks, and looks for unauthorized reconnection of a disconnected unit.

Commercial/industrial customer's metering point inside a plant, mechanical room, vault, or utility substation yard: CT-metered cabinets with sealed enclosures and test switches; the reader verifies enclosure and test-block seals, checks wiring for unauthorized taps, and notes physical damage to the cabinet or instrument transformers.

Disconnect/reconnect at a commercial or multifamily building meter room or outdoor meter bank: identify the correct socket among stacked meters, open the enclosure, pull/insert the meter or operate the service valve, re-seal and log, with building staff controlling access.

tasks.label: Weigh letters and parcels, compute mailing costs based on type, weight, and destination, and affix correct postage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail window, ordinary domestic parcel: customer hands over a shoebox-size carton, padded/poly mailer or flat-rate box; clerk lifts it onto the counter scale, keys destination ZIP, service class and extras into the POS, quotes the price, prints the shipping label at the counter printer, peels and affixes it to the largest flat face (covering old labels), scans it and drops it in the hamper.

Retail window, letters, cards and large flats: clerk weighs the envelope, checks thickness/rigidity/machinability for surcharges, determines First-Class/flat rate by weight and destination, then affixes the right stamps or a printed postage strip/label and puts the piece in the outgoing tray.

International item with a customs declaration: clerk weighs the parcel or letter-package, asks about contents/value/prohibitions, completes or verifies the customs form, computes the rate by country, service and weight, prints the combined label/customs form set and affixes it (plus pouch) to the parcel.

Oversized, heavy or awkward items: a 40-70 lb box, a poster tube, a bike box, an odd-shaped or poorly wrapped item; clerk hoists it onto a floor or platform scale, checks size/girth limits, rates it, and applies the label to an uneven, curved or non-flat surface, then moves it to the parcel cage.

Business/bulk acceptance at the window or BMEU: a mailer presents trays, sacks or a pallet of presorted mail or a batch of many similar parcels; clerk weighs sample pieces or the whole lot, verifies counts, piece weight and rate eligibility, computes the total postage on the postage statement against the permit account, and round-dates/verifies rather than stamping each piece.

Back office/verification work: short-paid or unpaid mail and pre-labeled customer drop-offs; clerk re-weighs and re-measures items, recomputes the correct rate for the class and destination, and affixes postage-due or additional postage labels before dispatch.

tasks.label: Sort incoming and outgoing mail, according to type and destination, by hand or by operating electronic mail-sorting and scanning devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post office back room: clerk distributes incoming letters and flats received from the plant to individual PO box numbers and carrier/route separations - thumbing mixed stacks, reading names/addresses, throwing pieces into the correct pigeonhole or case separation, pulling misdirects and holds.

Delivery unit parcel operation: clerk pulls incoming parcels, polybags and bundles from hampers and rolling stock, scans each barcode, and sorts them by carrier route, PO box shelf or notice-slip hold - mixed sizes and shapes up to ~30 lb, under morning dispatch time pressure.

Outgoing mail from the retail window and collection boxes: clerk separates the accepted mailstream by type/class (stamped letters, metered, flats, Priority/Express parcels, accountables), faces and postmarks stamped mail, and sorts pieces into dispatch trays/sacks by destination for the outgoing truck.

instances.label: End-of-day window close-out at a mid-size city post office: pull the assigned cash drawer, count bills and coin by denomination, tally checks and money orders taken in, compare the total against the Retail Systems Software point-of-sale totals, complete the daily financial report (PS Form 1412), and turn funds over to the unit reserve.

Opening and closing the till at a retail window: draw the assigned cash drawer from the unit safe, verify the beginning balance against the assigned accountability, arrange bills and coin by denomination in the till compartments, and return the secured drawer at shift end.

During-shift drawer upkeep at the counter between customers: facing and straightening bills, sorting coin into the right compartments, pulling large-denomination bills out of the drawer, buying change from the unit reserve when a denomination runs low, and keeping money-order receipts and vouchers ordered.

Recording transactions as they occur at the window: entering or scanning each postage, parcel, money-order, refund and no-sale entry into the POS terminal so the day's transaction record is complete, itemized and auditable at close.

Single-clerk daily close at a small rural post office or contract postal unit: count all funds on hand at one small counter and safe, validate and total the notes and coin, prepare and record the bank deposit, and file the day's financial report.

Working an out-of-balance or a periodic accountable-stock audit: recount the drawer, count stamp stock, coils, booklets and blank money-order forms on hand, review the transaction journal and receipts to locate the error, and document the overage or shortage on the required form.

instances.label: Retail window: a customer hands letters and parcels across the counter; the clerk takes custody, scans acceptance, and drops the items into the hamper, tub or dispatch sack behind the window. Mixed sizes (envelopes, flat-rate boxes, polybags, odd-shaped items), a line of customers, continuous interruption.

Back-room dispatch: the clerk works accepted and collected mail by destination and loads it into dispatch sacks/pouches, trays and hampers on racks, then closes, labels and stages the sacks for the outgoing truck. Work area shared with other clerks and rolling equipment.

Collection/carrier-return intake: hampers of loose collection-box mail and carrier-returned pieces are dumped and worked — letters faced and trayed, small parcels culled and dropped into sacks/containers for dispatch. Bulk unstructured mixed mail.

Bulk business mail acceptance at the dock: receiving trays, sacks, pallets and carts of presorted mail and parcels from mailer trucks or a rural carrier, verifying counts against paperwork, and moving/placing the mail into sacks, hampers and containers for dispatch.

Small rural office or contract postal unit: one clerk alternates between the window and the back room, low volume, irregular and oversized items, hand-carries the day's mail into a single dispatch sack/hamper and readies it for the highway contract route driver.

instances.label: Daily hold put-away in a city/suburban post office: carriers return parcels marked undeliverable (notice left, PS Form 3849), plus hold-mail and PO Box overflow parcels. The clerk scans each item to 'Available for Pickup', matches it to its notice number, and shelves it in the hold room by route/date. Mixed boxes, padded envelopes and poly bags, most under about 2 cubic feet.

Counter retrieval and handover: a customer presents a PS Form 3849 notice or ID at the retail window; the clerk goes to the hold shelves, locates that customer's parcel among hundreds of similar items, returns to the counter, scans the item out, captures a signature, and releases it.

Oversized or awkward held items: tires, long boxes, heavy or irregular parcels kept on the floor, in hampers, cages or an overflow area; put-away and retrieval require lifting, restacking and maneuvering through a crowded back room.

Disposition and paperwork sweeps: pulling items past the 15-day hold period, endorsing/labeling them for return to sender and moving them into the outgoing dispatch; second-notice processing; logging accountable items (certified, registered, insured) and completing the related forms and scans.

Small rural office or contract postal unit: cramped, non-standard back room with parcels stacked wherever space allows; one clerk does put-away, retrieval, customer handover and documentation between other window duties.

instances.label: Retail window: a customer at the counter asks for a hand cancel (everyday letters, wedding invitations, first-day covers, a dated proof-of-mailing postmark). Back-office batch hand-cancelling at a workroom table: a tub or tray of nonmachinable pieces (square or oversized invitation envelopes, greeting cards, philatelic covers, pieces rejected by the plant) is worked through piece by piece with a hand stamp, hundreds of impressions, each landing on the stamp area, then re-trayed for dispatch.

Small office/station canceling machine: the clerk brings in counter and collection-box mail, culls oversize and rigid pieces, faces and jogs the letters, loads slugs into the machine's feed hopper, runs the cancellation, clears misfeeds and jams, changes the date die and re-inks, and checks impression quality on the output stack.

Large station/plant facer-canceler operation: trays and hampers of collection mail are wheeled to the AFCS induction, dumped onto the feed conveyor at machine pace, the feeder is monitored, rejects and culls are swept and re-worked, and jams in the transport are cleared.

Odd cancellations mixed into other counter duties: postmarking parcels and flats bearing adhesive stamps, defacing stamps on missent or returned pieces, round-dating accountable forms and receipts - irregular shapes and thicknesses handled one at a time between customers.

tasks.label: Cash money orders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine window transaction at a post office retail counter: a customer presents one USPS domestic money order in good condition (typically $20-$300), shows a photo ID, signs the endorsement at the counter in front of the clerk; the clerk inspects the security features (watermark, security thread), scans/keys the item into the retail POS, counts out the exact face value in bills and coins, and issues a receipt.

Higher-value or multiple money orders at the counter (single item up to $1,000, or several presented together by a landlord, small-business owner, or family member): clerk checks photo ID more carefully, matches payee name to ID, may collect Bank Secrecy Act information (PS Form 8105-A) when aggregate thresholds are hit, authenticates each item, counts out a larger sum of cash accurately, and records the transactions.

Money order with irregularities: torn, water-damaged or faded item, missing or wrong payee name, signature in the wrong field, endorsement already made incorrectly, or presenter who is not the payee. The clerk must inspect, explain the defect, instruct the customer on the remedy (endorse now, complete a claim/inquiry form, deposit at a bank instead), and refuse payment when it cannot be resolved.

Cash-on-hand constraint at a small or rural office, or late in the business day: the money order's face value exceeds the cash in the drawer/unit reserve. The clerk must explain the limit and negotiate an outcome - pay part in cash, ask the customer to return, or direct them to a larger office or their bank - and still leave the customer served.

Suspected counterfeit, washed/altered, stolen, or already-paid money order: clerk notices anomalies in the security features or serial number, checks the Money Order Verification System, declines payment, may retain the item, informs the customer, and refers the matter to the Postal Inspection Service.

tasks.label: Scan labels on letters or parcels to confirm receipt.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential route, single-family homes: carrier pulls a parcel from the LLV/ProMaster or satchel at a park-and-loop or curbline stop, scans the shipping label barcode with the MDD handheld to record the delivery/receipt event, then leaves the parcel at the door or in the mailbox. Weather, dogs, uneven walkways, varied porch designs.

Delivery unit (post office workroom) before the route: carrier scans parcels and accountable items out of hampers, GPMCs and the accountable cage into route order and into the vehicle, confirming receipt of each piece into the carrier's custody. Indoor, fixed layout, staff-only floor.

Apartment complex, condo, or business/office building: carrier carries an armload or hamper of parcels into a lobby or mailroom, scans each label to confirm receipt/delivery, and places items in the mailroom, parcel lockers, or with a receptionist. Secure entry doors, elevators, controlled premises.

Accountable/attempted delivery at a customer door: certified, insured, Priority Express or signature-confirmation item scanned at the doorstep at the moment of hand-off to the customer, or scanned as 'notice left' when nobody answers. Residential/small-business door, unpredictable customer interaction.

Acceptance and collection scans on route: scanning labels of Package Pickup items left on a customer's porch or in the mailbox, prepaid parcels handed over at a business stop, and collection-point scans, confirming USPS receipt of items entering the mailstream. Curbside, porch, sidewalk collection box.

sources.title: AmbiSort A-Series: Robotic Small Parcel Sorting | Ambi Robotics
sources.claim: AmbiSort A-Series robotic cells pick mixed parcels (boxes, polybags, flats) from bulk bins, read each parcel's barcode label with fixed scanners, and sort it into the correct final-mile sack — the same read-and-record-a-parcel-label output the carrier produces, inside a purpose-built robotic cell.

It handles the same objects (mixed mail-stream parcels), produces the same accepted output (a recorded barcode read tied to a physical piece), and the only difference is that the robot presents the label to the scanner instead of a carrier presenting it to an MDD.

tasks.label: Obtain signed receipts for registered, certified, and insured mail, collect associated charges, and complete any necessary paperwork.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential single-family doorstep, recipient home: carrier brings a certified/signature-confirmation letter or insured parcel to the door, knocks or rings, waits, confirms an adult/addressee is present, captures an electronic signature on the MDD scanner, scans the item and hands it over.

No one home, or delivery refused: carrier completes and leaves a PS Form 3849 notice slip in the mailbox or on the door, scans the attempted-delivery event, carries the accountable item back to the vehicle and clears it against the station's accountable-mail paperwork at end of route.

Business or commercial stop (office reception, retail counter, mailroom dock): several accountable pieces handed to an authorized receiver who signs electronically on the scanner; items scanned and logged.

Stop requiring paper accountable paperwork: detaching and having the recipient sign a PS Form 3811 green return-receipt card (or firm delivery book / manifest sheet), retaining the paper card for return to the office.
Apartment or multi-unit building: buzzer or key entry, elevator, locate the correct unit door, obtain the recipient's signature, or hand off to a leasing/management office; leave a notice if absent.

Business/bulk pickup return: carrier returns with a full vehicle of mailer trays, tubs and parcel bins from scheduled business pickups (bulk mailers, permit mail), then moves multiple heavy wheeled containers off the vehicle onto the dock and stages them for dispatch.

tasks.label: Sort mail for delivery, arranging it in delivery sequence.

instances.label: City letter carrier at the carrier case on a delivery unit workroom floor before leaving: cases residual (non-DPS) letters and the day's flats — magazines, catalogs, large envelopes, circulars — into the case's route-sequenced slots, then pulls them down into trays in delivery order, handling wrong-address, forwards and odd-sized pieces as they appear.

Rural carrier in a small post office cases a mixed stream of letters, flats and small parcels for a rural route with box-number sequence, working from a case and hampers, integrating DPS letter trays with hand-cased mail into a single delivery order.

Carrier (or carrier at the unit) sorts the day's parcels and SPRs at the delivery unit — pulling them from hampers/cages, matching them to the route and separating them into route/section groups staged for loading.
Carrier arranges parcels in the delivery vehicle in stop order (heavy/oversize items, hot parcels, signature items) so each package can be pulled at the right stop.

On the route, in the vehicle or at a relay box/park point, the carrier 'marries' the DPS letter bundle with the cased flat bundle and parcels for the next block, fingering the pieces into a single street-sequence bundle as delivery proceeds.

Sorting accountable and signature mail (certified, registered, insured, Priority Express) and pieces needing PS Form 3849 notices into route sequence at the unit, after signing for them, so they are delivered at the right stop.

tasks.label: Deliver mail to residences and business establishments along specified routes by walking or driving, using a combination of satchels, carts, cars, and small trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: City motorized curbside route: carrier drives an LLV/Promaster along residential streets, pulls to each mounted box, opens it and inserts the day's sequenced letters, flats, and small parcels for 450-600 delivery points, in traffic, heat, rain and snow, then returns undeliverable mail.

Park-and-loop / foot route: carrier parks, loads a satchel from a relay box or vehicle, walks residential blocks delivering to porch boxes, wall boxes and door slots, climbing steps, opening gates, dealing with dogs, ice, uneven walkways and unfenced yards.

Parcel-heavy residential run (including Sunday/holiday package-only trips): carrier lifts packages from the vehicle, scans them, carries them to doorsteps, apartment lobbies or package lockers, leaves notices for signature items, and handles awkward or heavy items.

Business/downtown route: carrier moves along a commercial block with a hand cart or satchel, enters storefronts and office lobbies, hands bundles to receptionists or drops them in tenant mail slots, obtains signatures for accountable mail and picks up outgoing mail.

Multi-unit delivery: carrier opens cluster box units, apartment gang boxes or lobby box banks with an arrow key and inserts each tenant's mail into the correct small compartment, loads parcel lockers and leaves keys in boxes.

Rural route: long driving route on gravel and county roads, delivering to roadside mounted boxes from the vehicle, plus parcels carried to farmhouse porches, with long distances between stops and severe weather.

tasks.label: Meet schedules for the collection and return of mail.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: City letter carrier on a park-and-loop or walking route: while delivering, takes outgoing mail left in customer boxes, door slots and apartment lobby drops, clears one or two blue street collection boxes at their posted collection times, then drives the LLV back to the delivery unit in time for the outgoing dispatch truck. Public streets, sidewalks, private walkways, all weather, pedestrians, dogs, parked cars.

Rural carrier working from the vehicle: retrieves outgoing mail from roadside boxes with flags up, takes customer package pickups and stamped items, keeps pace over 60-150 miles of paved and gravel road with several hundred boxes so as to return to the post office before the dispatch cutoff. Varied driveways, snow banks, mud, livestock, no institutional control of the surroundings.

Dedicated collection run: carrier drives a route of 30-80 street collection boxes and lobby drop boxes, unlocks each with an arrow-lock key at or after the posted last-collection time, scoops loose letters and flats into sacks/tubs, relocks and scans, and gets the load to the processing plant before dispatch.

Scheduled business or bulk-mailer pickup on the route: arrive at a contracted time at a business mailroom, loading dock or apartment management office, take custody of trays, tubs and sacks of outgoing mail and parcels, scan the pickup, load them into the vehicle and get them into that day's dispatch.

Return leg at the delivery unit: pull into the station lot/dock at the scheduled time, unload collected letters, flats, parcels and accountable items, get the collected volume into the outgoing dispatch hamper/container before the plant truck departs, and stage the vehicle and equipment.

tasks.label: Sign for cash-on-delivery and registered mail before leaving the post office.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: City letter carrier, morning at the delivery unit: queues at the accountable cage window, where the clerk hands over 5-20 accountable items (certified, insured, Priority Mail Express, signature-confirmation pieces) listed on PS Form 3821; the carrier checks each item number and the count against the listing/scanner, signs the receipt, and carries the banded bundle back to the case. Indoor workroom, other carriers waiting, clerk on the other side of ... cage screen.

Rural carrier or small office: the carrier pulls the day's accountables from the hamper or cage themselves, scans each piece into the mobile delivery device, reconciles against the clerk's list, and signs the paper receipt while the clerk multitasks at the retail counter. Cramped workroom, mixed letters, flats and small parcels loose in a tub.

Peak-season or heavy accountable day: 30-80 accountable pieces including parcels and firm holdouts; the carrier must verify a long list piece by piece, spot missing, extra or mis-listed items, resolve discrepancies verbally with the accountable clerk, and only then sign for the corrected total under time pressure to get on the street.

Registered mail: high-value pieces held under continuous chain of custody in the locked cage; the carrier inspects seals/tape and condition, verifies each registry number item by item against the registry/accountable form, signs for them individually, and keeps them secured separately from ordinary mail.

COD (collect-on-delivery) items: the carrier signs for COD parcels and their attached forms, checks item numbers and the amount due on each, and accepts financial accountability for collection before leaving the office.

sources.title: AmbiSort A-Series: Robotic Small Parcel Sorting | Ambi Robotics
sources.claim: AmbiSort robotic parcel sorting cells autonomously pick mixed mailpieces (polybags, flats, boxes) from a bin, read each item's barcode through multi-scanner/scan-tunnel and quality-control zones, and place each item into the correct designated output container.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic parcel induction/sortation. Signing for accountable mail is, physically, item-level identification and controlled transfer of custody of exactly the same objects (letters, flats, small parcels bearing barcoded item numbers): each piece must be read, matched to a list, and moved to a defined container. The scan-verify-place loop demonstrated here is the handling core of the accountable-mail pickup.

sources.developer: USPS Automated Guided Vehicles and Robotics team
sources.title: All systems go – USPS Employee News
sources.claim: USPS itself operates a parcel robotic sortation system in which a robot works inside a closed cell with a conveyor and autonomous ... to pull and distribute items, described by USPS as essentially fully automated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic order pulling and sortation of postal items inside a USPS facility. It shows that the handling and item-transfer half of accountable-mail pickup is done today by USPS robots, but only inside a fenced/closed purpose-built cell fed by conveyor and AMRs.

sources.title: Handwriting Robots - Handwrytten
sources.claim: Handwrytten operates a fleet of custom handwriting robots that hold real ballpoint pens and write text and signatures on cards and paper; the robots run autonomously without a connected computer and use barcode scanning to confirm the correct stock is written on, and are installed in third-party logistics facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handwriting on fixtured paper. Signing PS Form 3821 requires exactly this - applying a specific pen signature to a sheet held in a known position - and the barcode-scan interlock shows the robot can tie the written output to the correct document/job.

sources.title: Want To Charm Clients With Handwritten Notes? This Robot Writes Them (Forbes)
sources.claim: Handwrytten's service can reproduce an individual's own signature style with a pen-holding robot, and operates a fleet of about 175 machines commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic signature/handwriting production at commercial scale, establishing that the pen-signature output required to close out the accountable receipt is machine-producible today.

sources.system: Digit (Agility Robotics) at GXO's SPANX fulfillment facility
sources.title: Industry-first multi-year agreement with Agility Robotics | GXO
sources.claim: Humanoid mobile manipulators are deployed in structured human work facilities, but the demonstrated work is gross tote movement between cobots and conveyors, not item-level document verification, discrepancy resolution with a clerk, or paper signing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile manipulation inside a human-built facility. Cited to bound the E2 judgment: the most capable fielded E2 mobile manipulators move standardized totes on fixed routes and have not been shown taking custody of loose mixed mailpieces at a service window or executing a signed accountability transfer.

tasks.label: Hold mail for customers who are away from delivery locations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casing operation on the post office workroom floor: with a hold card in the case separation, the carrier pulls letters and flats addressed to the hold-flagged address out of the residual/cased mail, rubber-bands them with the hold slip, and places the bundle in the unit's hold tub or shelf.

Delivery-point-sequenced (DPS) letter stream: the carrier fingers through DPS trays (or holds pieces out on the route and returns them) to remove letters for addresses under an active hold before the mail goes to the street.

Parcels and accountable mail for held addresses: during load-up or package sortation at the delivery unit, the carrier identifies parcels addressed to a hold-flagged address, scans them 'hold mail,' and stages them on the hold shelf/hamper with the customer's other accumulated mail.

End of hold with delivery option: the carrier collects the accumulated letters, flats and parcels, loads them in the vehicle, and delivers them at the residential address - into the curbside or wall box, at the door, or handed to the customer; oversize accumulations that do not fit require a door delivery or notice.

End of hold with customer pickup: the accumulation is retrieved from the hold area at the post office and handed across the counter to the customer after ID verification, and the hold card is pulled from the case.

sources.title: Postal Automated Redirection System - USPS Office of Inspector General audit report 25-029-R25
sources.claim: USPS letter-mail sorting equipment automatically intercepts mailpieces whose address matches a flag in a USPS address database (an active Change of Address) and diverts them out of the normal delivery stream for special handling; deployed nationwide since 2007 in processing plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated interception of letter mail flagged in an address database (COA/forwarding). Holding mail is the same physical operation on the same objects (letter-size mail fed in trays through a plant sorter) at the same precision - read the address, compare it against a flag for that delivery point, and divert the piece into a separate pocket instead of the route bin. Only the database consulted (hold order rather than COA) and the downstream container differ.

sources.title: Delivery Bar Code Sorter - Wikipedia
sources.claim: USPS delivery bar code sorters read the address on each letter and physically divert it into one of up to 286 ..., i.e. machine separation of letter mail by delivery point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: address-based letter sortation into a designated pocket. Pulling a held address's letters and flats out of the stream into a hold separation is the identical physical act with a different pocket assignment; the objects (letters/flats) and accuracy demands are the same as the carrier's casing/DPS pull.

sources.system: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter (ADUS) / Small Delivery Unit Sorter (SDUS)
sources.title: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter (ADUS) - U.S. Postal Facts (Fact #824)
sources.claim: Package sorting machines installed inside USPS delivery units autonomously sort packages and bundles of mail to designated destinations at 3,400 pieces per hour with 99.95 percent sort accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: barcode-driven parcel sortation to a designated container at the delivery unit. Staging a held address's parcels means routing those scanned pieces to a hold container rather than a route container - same objects (parcels up to 30 lb), same scan-and-divert decision, same delivery-unit machine.

sources.system: ADUS and SDUS package sorting machines at delivery units
sources.title: Repair and Maintenance of Package Sorting Machines at Delivery Units - USPS Office of Inspector General
sources.claim: USPS has deployed automated package sorting machines in delivery units since November 2014 and accelerated rollout of the Small Delivery Unit Sorter under the Delivering for America plan; these machines process packages roughly twelve times faster than manual sorting.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that machine sortation of parcels by scanned destination is a deployed, production capability at the very facilities where carriers stage hold mail; supports the parcel-hold instance at the machine tier.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A fleet of autonomous mobile manipulator robots has completed over 300,000 pharmacy item deliveries inside hospitals, navigating corridors and elevators to bring items from a central point to a designated recipient location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point delivery of small parcels/packets to a specified recipient location inside an institution-controlled building. Delivering an accumulated hold-mail bundle to a recipient within such a facility involves comparable objects (small packages and envelope bundles), comparable placement precision, and the same kind of mapped indoor route.

sources.title: Cleveron brings robotics-based parcel tower to locations worldwide - CEP-Research
sources.claim: A robotics-based parcel tower stores several hundred parcels and, when a customer authenticates with an order code at the console, the machine retrieves and hands over the parcel within seconds; deployed in retail stores in multiple countries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic storage of held items and authenticated hand-over to the customer. The hold-mail pickup instance is the same act - retain the accumulation in a store location and release it to the identified customer - with comparable objects (parcels and banded mail bundles).

sources.system: Humanoid parcel sorters at Jianggao logistics site, Guangzhou postal centre
sources.developer: China Post Group (robot vendor not named in report)
sources.title: China Post deploys humanoid robots to sort 1,200 parcels per hour - Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: Humanoid robots working alongside robotic arms and unmanned forklifts grip parcels from containers and place them onto sorting lines at a China Post logistics hub, reportedly at up to 1,200 parcels per ....
sources.transferJustification: Context only for postal parcel handling by general-purpose robots; autonomy and reliability are not established in the source, so it is not relied on for any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Turn in money and receipts collected along mail routes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: City letter carrier ends the street portion of the route and returns to the delivery unit with a small amount of coins and bills collected for postage-due, customs, or COD items, plus the matching receipt copies and undelivered accountable pieces; counts the money, completes the clearance report (PS Form 3821), and hands the money and receipts across the accountability window to the closeout clerk or supervisor.

Rural carrier who sold stamps, prepared money orders, and accepted certified/insured mail on route returns to a small post office with a larger mixed amount of cash plus customer checks, money-order receipts and transaction records; reconciles the funds against the day's recorded sales (e1412/RRECS records), and turns cash and receipt copies in to the postmaster or closeout clerk.

A day on which no money was collected: at the delivery unit the carrier turns in only paperwork — signed delivery and accountable-mail receipts, the accountable sign-out sheet, clearance report, keys/scanner — to the supervisor for clearance.

The money turned in does not match the receipts or scanner records (overage or shortage): carrier and supervisor jointly recount the cash and coins, retrace the day's transactions, and complete shortage/overage documentation before clearance is accepted.

Large station or station with a cash-accountability procedure: carrier seals the day's collected funds and receipt copies in a cash pouch/envelope with a deposit slip and either deposits it into the unit's drop safe or hands it to the unit reserve custodian, obtaining a stamped/signed receipt.

sources.system: G+D robotic cash center cell (BPS M7 / second-level packaging)
sources.title: How robotic automation will transform cash centers | G+D Spotlight
sources.claim: G+D has delivered robotic cash-processing cells to a central bank in which robot arms take banknote bundles from processing systems, consolidate them into cash packs, strap, label and convey them, with serial numbers tracked throughout — machine handling and accounting of physical currency in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intake, consolidation and accounting of banknote bundles in a cash center. It transfers because the physical core of turning in collected money is moving currency into an accountable system and having each note counted and recorded; the objects (banknote bundles) and precision are comparable.

sources.title: Automation Solutions for Cash Management | G+D
sources.claim: G+D's NotaTray loading module uses a robotic gripper to fill loose banknotes into banknote processing systems, buffering up to 40,000 notes for continuous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic feeding of loose banknotes into a counting/authenticating machine. This is the manipulation step a machine would need when money presented in a fixture must be transferred into the accounting system.

sources.system: CorPoint / retail smart safes (remote cash capture)
sources.developer: Fiserv (with safe vendors such as Tidel, PayComplete)
sources.title: CorPoint and Smart Safes for Retail Cash Management | Fiserv
sources.claim: Retail smart safes accept mixed cash and coin deposited by staff, count and validate the money, secure it, and post the deposit for provisional credit — the machine-accounted equivalent of a worker turning in the day's collected funds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-shift turn-in of collected retail cash. Same objects (loose bills and coins collected from customers), same accepted output (funds counted, secured, and credited to the employer's account with a transaction record).

sources.system: Glory Vertera ETD / GLR series teller cash recycler
sources.title: Glory introduces 'plug and play' electronic teller drawer | ATM Marketplace
sources.claim: Glory's Vertera electronic teller drawer and GLR-series recyclers automatically authenticate, count, validate and store deposited banknotes at bank teller counters and as self-service devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine acceptance and verification of cash handed in over a counter. It substantiates that presented currency can be counted, authenticated and booked without a human counting it, which is the verification half of a clearance turn-in.

sources.title: Advanced Coin Counting Technology for Enhanced Safety and Convenience - Coinstar for Retail
sources.claim: Coinstar self-service kiosks accept poured-in loose mixed coin, count and authenticate it with sensors and machine learning, and issue a voucher for the amount; thousands are deployed in supermarkets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intake and counting of loose mixed coin with a printed record of value. Postage-due and COD money turned in by carriers is largely loose coin and small bills, so the object class and the required output (an accurate counted total with a receipt) match.

sources.title: Ripcord uses robotics to digitize records, processes and avoid paper waste - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Ripcord operates robotic document workcells that take stacks of loose paper, remove staples, feed sheets one at a time for scanning, and index the records, processing over a billion documents per year at its facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and intake of loose paper documents in a purpose-built workcell. Turning in receipts requires exactly this — separating and transferring thin paper forms into an accountable record — with comparable objects and precision.

sources.title: Figure AI Robot Sorts 100,000 Packages in 81 Hours Without Human Help - Seoul Economic Daily
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 humanoids sorted more than 100,000 parcels, including envelopes and polybags, over 81 hours at a conveyor station in a logistics warehouse with no teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained autonomous handling of mail-class flat items (envelopes, polybags) presented at a fixed conveyor station. It supports machine handling of the paper/flat items a carrier turns in, when the items are presented at a station.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi autonomously transports items — including pharmacy deliveries and lab specimens — in secure badge-locked drawers through hospital corridors and elevators, with over one million deliveries across 25+ US hospitals; it transports and drops off items but does not count currency or reconcile accountability paperwork.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secure autonomous transport and handoff of custody-controlled items inside a structured human facility. It is the closest E2 analogue to carrying funds into the office, but it is limited to items loaded by staff into a drawer, with no counting or reconciliation.

tasks.label: Leave notices telling patrons where to collect mail that could not be delivered.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Suburban/urban curbside or wall-mounted mailbox on a vehicle route: parcel won't fit or requires signature, so the carrier fills out a PS Form 3849 notice (item, pickup location, date/hours), opens the customer's box and places the slip inside, then re-secures the box and moves on; done dozens of times per day in all weather.

Foot/park-and-loop route to detached house doors: carrier walks up steps or a porch, and because the box is at the door or the item needs signature, leaves the notice at the door — wedged in a storm door, in a door slot, under a mat or in a wall box — dealing with gates, pets, packages, clutter and varied door hardware.

Apartment/condo building: carrier enters a lobby or corridor with cluster/gang mailboxes or unit doors, slides the notice into the correct small box compartment or under/into the unit door slot, sometimes with a keyed access panel and dozens of boxes in a row.

Accountable mail at a residence (certified, registered, insured, Signature Confirmation, COD): no one answers, carrier completes a detailed notice with item barcode/number and redelivery instructions, leaves it in the receptacle or at the door, scans the item as 'notice left', and carries the article back to the post office.

Business/commercial stop closed or no authorized recipient available: notice left at a storefront or office door, in a commercial mail slot, or with a lobby receptacle on a strip-mall or downtown sidewalk stop.

Rural route: roadside mailbox reached from the vehicle window at the end of long driveways, gates, snow banks, dogs; carrier places the notice slip in the box, raises the flag or leaves the box door signal, sometimes drives up to a porch for oversized items.

sources.system: BlueCrest Epic / Epic Direct Mail inserter
sources.title: BlueCrest | Epic Direct Mail Inserter Solution
sources.claim: Commercial mail-inserting systems automatically feed, print variable data on, and insert individual paper documents into envelopes (a fixtured slot) at up to 24,000 cycles per hour under machine control in a purpose-built machine line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: printing and inserting a paper document into a presented receptacle. Under the E1 counterfactual the notice is printed and the receptacle is fixtured and presented; these machines handle exactly this object (a single paper slip) with the required precision and reliability.

sources.developer: Libiao Robotics (integration by Körber) at Kuehne+Nagel Châtres
sources.title: Kuehne+Nagel deploys mobile sorting robots from Libiao Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile sorting robots receive individual mail items (parcels and envelopes) and deposit each into the correct destination bin at a production facility, with error rate reported as close to zero.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carrying a mail item to an addressed receptacle and depositing it. This is the E1 form of 'leave a notice in the patron's receptacle' — the receptacles are fixtured bins in a robot-built floor, and the system runs autonomously at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics is testing Spot as a package delivery robot that walks from van to doorstep
sources.claim: The most advanced 'last 50 feet' residential delivery robot as of mid-2026 is still in testing: it carries parcels from a van and sets them down on the ground/porch by rotating a conveyor tray; routes must first be driven manually before the robot can repeat them, and no mailbox opening or notice placement is shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residential doorstep item placement. It shows the frontier of unstructured-residential manipulation — setting a box on the ground — which falls short of opening a mailbox or affixing a notice, and is a test rather than a deployment.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics is testing Spot as a package delivery robot that walks from van to doorstep
sources.claim: The leading commercially deployed residential ground-delivery robot performs curb/doorframe-level handoffs only; it cannot climb stairs, and industry leaders describe getting items from curb to doorstep as the hardest remaining part of automating delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: last-mile residential delivery. It shows deployed autonomous ground robots hand items over at the curb/door and do no receptacle manipulation, so they cannot place a notice in a mailbox or on a door.

sources.system: Humanoid parcel sorters at Jianggao logistics site, Guangzhou postal center
sources.title: China deploys humanoid robots to sort 1,200 parcels per hour in massive postal hub
sources.claim: Humanoid robots have been put to work in a postal hub gripping mail items from containers and placing them ... alongside robotic arms and unmanned forklifts, reportedly processing up to 1,200 parcels ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling mail items into designated destinations inside a purpose-built postal facility; autonomy is not established from the reporting, so it is treated as supporting context only.

tasks.label: Maintain accurate records of deliveries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On the delivery route, the carrier records each parcel's delivery event: capturing the tracking barcode with the handheld Mobile Delivery Device, selecting the correct delivery-status code (delivered, left with individual, mailbox, front door), and letting GPS/time stamps transmit to the tracking system so the record matches what was actually delivered.

Accountable/signature-required items (certified, registered, insured, Priority Express, COD, adult-signature): the carrier records recipient name, captures an electronic or paper signature (PS Form 3849/3811 return receipt), verifies identity where required, and logs the item as cleared against the accountable mail record.

Attempted or non-delivery events: the carrier records the attempt reason (no access, no authorized recipient, refused, vacant, undeliverable as addressed), enters the corresponding scan event, and completes the notice-left/redelivery paperwork so the record shows why the item was not delivered.

Office/end-of-tour recordkeeping: reconciling and clearing accountable mail (PS Form 3821), reporting undelivered mail (PS Form 1571), recording hold-mail, forwards and address-change endorsements, and reconciling COD/postage-due funds collected during the route.

Rural route recordkeeping: completing the rural carrier trip report (PS Form 4240) with route counts, mileage and time, logging boxholder and package counts, and recording accountable items handled from the vehicle.

tasks.label: Bundle mail in preparation for delivery or transportation to relay boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: City letter carrier on a park-and-loop/foot route, standing at the carrier case inside the delivery unit: pulls cased letters and flats down shelf by shelf in line-of-travel order, marries them with the DPS letter tray, straps each loop/relay segment with rubber bands, marks or labels the bundles, and loads them into the satchel and vehicle trays.

City carrier on a mounted/curbline route at the case in the delivery unit: pulls down cased residual mail, bands it into section tie-outs with the DPS bundle, and stages the banded bundles in trays for the vehicle; no relay boxes involved.

Rural carrier at the case in a small post office: bundles mail for each section/spur of the route with rubber bands, combining letters, flats and small packets, and loads the banded bundles into trays and hampers for the vehicle.

Heavy downtown/business route: carrier builds several relay bundles at the case, each rubber-banded (often double-banded for weight), identified by relay-box or building, and stacked for the vehicle or a relay truck to drop at relay boxes.

Re-bundling away from the office: at the vehicle at the curb, at a relay box, or on a stoop, the carrier re-bands a bundle that has broken, or bands up the next loop's mail from a tray, outdoors in wind, heat or rain with no work surface.

sources.system: Felins banding/bundling systems (US-2000, M-series inline banders)
sources.title: Postal Strapping | Packaging & Banding Machines | Felins
sources.claim: Felins sells semi-automatic and fully automatic mail bundling/banding systems that apply a paper or plastic band around stacks of mail (flats, letters) to form USPS-compliant bundles, running in mailing houses, fulfillment centers and government mail facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same task object and act: forming a stack of addressed mail pieces into a secured bundle for delivery. The machine bands mixed letter- and flat-size mail exactly as the carrier's rubber band secures a relay bundle.

sources.system: Graphic Whizard SP-400 automatic bander; Felins inline ultrasonic banders
sources.title: Paper Banding Machines & Banders | Felins, Graphic Whizard SP-Bander | Mid-State Litho
sources.claim: Fully automatic banders with conveyor integration band stacks of printed matter and direct mail inline, paired with stackers for unattended production runs in high-volume mailing operations.
sources.transferJustification: Bundling direct mail: the bander receives an accumulated stack from a stacker on a conveyor and secures it, the same physical output (a banded mail bundle) the carrier produces by hand.

sources.system: Muller Martini mailroom system (NewsStack compensating stacker, top-sheet applicator, strapper)
sources.title: Product of the month: Muller Martini Mailroom System | PrintWeek India
sources.claim: Newspaper mailroom production lines automatically accumulate printed matter into route bundles on compensating stackers, apply a top sheet carrying dispatch/route instructions, and strap the bundle for distribution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: building delivery-route bundles of flat printed matter, labeling them with the route/dispatch destination and strapping them — the same operation as strapping out a relay bundle and marking it for a relay box.

sources.system: Envelope-stack packaging robot (custom pneumatic gripper + perception pipeline)
sources.developer: Worcester Polytechnic Institute (Venkataramanan et al., IEEE CASE 2024)
sources.title: Perception-Driven Robotic Manipulation for Packaging Stack of Envelopes: Gripper Design and Manipulation Strategies
sources.claim: A perception-driven robot with a custom gripper handles and packages compressible stacks of paper envelopes moving on a conveyor in an envelope production/packaging line, without damaging the stack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping and transferring a formed stack of envelopes on a conveyor. It shows machine handling of the exact object class (compressible letter stacks) that must be gripped and compressed before banding, in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: USPS parcel sortation robotic arms; Ambi Robotics pods / gantry robots at Pitney Bowes-USPS tier-2 sites
sources.title: Pitney Bowes delivers for USPS - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Robots deployed in postal facilities to date handle parcels (bin picking, induction, transport), not letter/flat bundling at carrier cases; USPS deployments are robotic arms and gantries for parcel sortation.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the state of the art: postal-facility robots handle parcels into sacks, and no cited system pulls sequenced letter mail from a carrier case and bands it in a human-standard delivery unit.

tasks.label: Record address changes and redirect mail for those addresses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Morning case-up / pull-down at the delivery unit on a city letter route: the carrier works letters and flats against the route's active change-of-address and forwarding notices, pulls out the pieces addressed to customers who have moved, endorses or labels them for forwarding, and drops them in the UAA/PARS container for dispatch back to the plant. Standard carrier case, hampers, indoor workroom floor controlled by the postmaster.

Parcels and non-machinable pieces at the delivery unit addressed to customers with a change of address on file: the carrier identifies the piece on the parcel shelf or in the hamper, writes/applies the yellow forwarding label with the new address, and places it in the correct dispatch container. Mixed sizes and shapes, indoor workroom floor.

On the route: the carrier reaches a box or door and finds mail for someone who has moved — a piece pushed back into the box marked "moved," a resident who says the addressee is gone, a newly vacant unit. The carrier records the change for the route and carries the piece back to the office so it enters the forwarding stream. Sidewalks, driveways, weather and dogs as found.

A customer hands the carrier a completed PS Form 3575 change-of-address card, or a written temporary-forward or hold-mail request, at the door, the curb box, or on the way to the vehicle. The carrier records the change (route edit book, mobile delivery device, or turning the card in to the clerk) so that the address's mail is redirected from the effective date.

High-turnover apartment complex or business route: the building manager hands over, or the lobby return slot yields, a bundle of mail for former tenants. The carrier sorts the bundle against the forwarding notices for the building, redirects the pieces with a change of address on file, and endorses the rest. Lobby or mailroom kept by a property manager, cluster box banks, fixed layout.

sources.title: Postal Automated Redirection System, USPS OIG Report 25-029-R25
sources.claim: USPS's Postal Automated Redirection System (PARS) equipment, deployed since 2007 in mail processing plants, automatically reads letter addresses, matches them against the change-of-address database, and prints and physically applies a yellow forwarding label bearing the new address onto the mailpiece before sorting it toward the new destination.

sources.title: Postal Automated Redirection System, USPS OIG Report 25-029-R25
sources.claim: PARS performs the interception and redirection of moved customers' letter mail at national scale and without human intervention for the great majority of pieces, which establishes that the machine, not a person, completes the redirect from start to accepted output.

sources.system: Flats Postal Automated Redirection System (FPARS) on AFSM 100
sources.title: USPS to Implement Flat Redirection System | American Postal Workers Union
sources.claim: The Flats Postal Automated Redirection System ... () extends the same automated redirection to flat-size mail (magazines, catalogs, large envelopes) by modifying AFSM 100 flat sorters to image the piece and apply a forwarding label, replacing manual forwarding work at Central Forwarding System sites.

sources.title: MMO-143-20 – AFSM100 | American Postal Workers Union
sources.claim: FPARS-modified AFSM 100 machines are in routine operational service, as USPS maintains published preventive and operational maintenance guidelines ... them.

sources.title: Comprehensive Statement on Postal Operations 2006 — USPS
sources.claim: The Automated Package Processing System handles parcels end-to-end by machine: it inducts and singulates packages automatically, reads the delivery address optically, and sorts each package to its destination bin, showing that parcel-level address reading and redirection to a new destination is machine-executable when parcels are fed to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated parcel address reading and sortation. It shares the objects (USPS parcels), the perception step (reading the delivery address on an irregular package), and the output (routing the package to a different destination) with redirecting a moved customer's parcel; only the label-application step differs, covered by the print-and-apply evidence.

sources.title: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter (ADUS) - U.S. Postal Facts
sources.claim: USPS runs Automated Delivery Unit Sorters inside delivery units that sort packages and bundles of mail by machine at high throughput and very high accuracy, replacing sorting that carriers and clerks previously did by hand at the case.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is delivery-unit sortation of packages and mail bundles. It shows that when delivery-unit mail is fed into a purpose-built sorter, machine reading and separation of individual pieces to the correct outbound container matches worker accuracy — the same separation step that redirecting a moved customer's mail requires.

sources.system: FOX IV 6955/6957 label printer applicators and integrated labeling stations
sources.title: Shipping Labeling Applications | FOX IV
sources.claim: Commercial industrial print-and-apply labelling systems automatically print a shipping/address label and physically apply it to cartons, totes and packages moving on a conveyor, driven by a scan of the item and a database lookup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automatic printing and application of an address label to a parcel on a conveyor. Applying a yellow forwarding label bearing a new address to a parcel is the identical physical act on identical objects at identical precision; only the source of the address string differs.

sources.system: Small/Automated Delivery Unit Sorter address reading
sources.title: Siemens automates mail sorting in USPS delivery units | Post & Parcel
sources.claim: Siemens supplied address-reading technology for the mail sorting systems installed in USPS delivery units, so that letters that had been sorted by hand by carriers with route knowledge are now sorted by machine at the delivery unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is machine reading and sorting of delivery-unit letter mail formerly cased by carriers. It shows the perception and separation competence needed to pull a moved customer's letters out of the route's mail exists in deployed USPS equipment when mail is fed to the machine.

tasks.label: Return incorrectly addressed mail to senders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Morning casing at the delivery unit: while casing letters and flats the carrier pulls pieces whose address is defective on its face - no such number or street on the route, missing/wrong apartment or unit, incomplete, illegible or wrong-ZIP addresses - endorses the reason and throws them to the return/throwback separation for dispatch back to the plant.

Casing or route: letters and flats correctly addressed to a valid delivery point on the route but addressed to a person or business no longer there and with no forwarding order on file (moved-left-no-address, attempted-not-known, deceased addressee, vacant house). The carrier recognizes this only from personal knowledge of current occupants, endorses ANK/MLNA and separates it for return.

On the route: the customer has left a piece back in the mailbox or hands it to the carrier marked 'not at this address' / 'refused' / 'return to sender'. The carrier collects it from the curbside or door box, carries it in the satchel/vehicle, and endorses and separates it for return at the unit.

Field-discovered undeliverables: at the delivery point the carrier finds no mail receptacle, a demolished or boarded-up property, a removed or blocked box, or a closed business; the mail cannot be left, is retained in the vehicle and processed as return-to-sender back at the unit.

Undeliverable parcels and accountable pieces with a bad or nonexistent address brought back to the delivery unit: the carrier scans them 'Return to Sender', applies the return label/endorsement and places them in the return dispatch container (hamper/sack) for the plant.

Apartment houses, cluster boxes and business mailrooms: mail for former tenants or departed employees pulled from panel boxes or handed back by a building manager or mailroom clerk; the carrier bundles, endorses and returns it from the unit.

sources.system: Postal Automated Redirection System (PARS) / CIOSS letter sorting equipment
sources.title: Postal Automated Redirection System (USPS OIG Audit Report 25-029-R25)
sources.claim: USPS PARS mail processing equipment automatically decides whether an undeliverable-as-addressed letter should be forwarded, returned to sender, treated as dead/waste or destroyed, and physically prints and applies the corresponding label to the mailpiece before sorting it - the machine analogue of the carrier endorsing and separating misaddressed mail.

sources.title: Postal Automated Redirection System (USPS OIG Audit Report 25-029-R25)
sources.claim: PARS machines read and label undeliverable mail in one operation and finalized most PARS mail through automation in FY2023-24, showing the read-decide-label-sort loop runs at national volume on a purpose-built sorting line, not as a demonstration.

sources.title: Postal Automated Redirection System (USPS OIG Audit Report 25-029-R25)
sources.claim: Limitation of the automated redirection system: when no valid or unexpired change-of-address record exists the machine has no way to know the addressee is gone and simply delivers the piece as addressed, leaving identification to the carrier's personal knowledge.

sources.system: USPS OCR letter sorting equipment / Remote Encoding Center
sources.title: For 30 years, USPS employees at the Remote Encoding Center have deciphered illegible addresses
sources.claim: USPS letter-mail machines read about 99 percent of addresses automatically; only residual images go to remote human keyers at the single Remote Encoding Center, so the address reading needed to spot a defective address is machine work with only occasional remote assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated address recognition for delivery sortation. Identifying an incorrectly addressed piece starts from reading the same printed or handwritten address block, on the same mailpieces, on the same equipment.

sources.title: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter Cost Savings (USPS OIG Audit Report 20-095-R21)
sources.claim: The Automated Delivery Unit Sorter, deployed in USPS delivery units and small plants, images and decodes package labels and sorts packages into bins for carrier routes or ..., dropping them into a sack, hamper or wire ... - the physical routing a carrier performs when placing an undeliverable parcel in the return dispatch container.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: label-driven package sortation in the delivery unit. Same parcels, same containers and same accuracy requirement as diverting an undeliverable parcel into the return-to-sender separation.

sources.system: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter (ADUS) / Small Delivery Unit Sorter
sources.title: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter (ADUS) - U.S. Postal Facts
sources.claim: USPS states the delivery-unit package sorter runs 3,400 pieces per hour at 99.95 percent sort accuracy, i.e. worker-grade reliability for routing packages to a designated separation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: package sortation at a delivery unit; establishes that machine routing of parcels to a chosen separation meets the reliability an employer accepts.

sources.title: 12 cool facts about the AI-powered robots that help deliver your Amazon packages
sources.claim: Amazon's Robin robotic arm picks individual packages off a conveyor, scans the shipping label and places each one on its destination, with over 1,000 arms in service having sorted more than 2 billion packages, including transferring damaged packages out of the flow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: label-reading parcel sortation with grasping. Comparable objects (mailers and boxes) and precision; shows a robot can read a label and place the item into an exception destination such as a return container.

sources.title: Amazon Testing Robotic Arm that Identifies Individual Products (Vision Systems Design)
sources.claim: Robin's sortation is vision-based label reading on individual mailers and parcels moving on a conveyor in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reading the address/label on a mailpiece to decide its destination - the perceptual step in separating a misaddressed parcel for return.

tasks.label: Provide customers with change of address cards and other forms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential foot / park-and-loop route: a patron comes out to the carrier at the porch, walkway or sidewalk and asks for a change-of-address (Mover's Guide) form; the carrier finds the packet in the satchel or LLV, hands it over, and usually answers a brief question about filing. Conditions taken as found: steps, gates, dogs, weather, parked cars.

Curbside or rural route worked from the vehicle: a patron is waiting at the mailbox or flags down the carrier; the carrier pulls the requested form (COA packet, PS 8076 hold-mail, PO Box application) from stock kept in the vehicle and hands it out the window at the roadside.

No-contact drop: the carrier leaves a form or notice where the customer's mail is delivered - a COA/Mover's Guide packet, hold-mail form or PS 3849 notice placed in a curbside box, wall box, door slot or behind a screen door at a residence.

Apartment building or business stop: the carrier enters a lobby, mailroom or front office and hands forms to a receptionist, property manager or clerk, or leaves a stack of forms for tenants at the mailbox bank. Premises are controlled and kept to a standard by the building or business.

At the delivery unit / post office lobby: a customer picking up held or accountable mail, or meeting the carrier at the station window, is given the appropriate form (COA packet, hold-mail, redelivery, PS 1093) by the carrier.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile-manipulation service robot, picks specified supply items out of supply closets and delivers them to people in hospital units, fully autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetch-and-deliver of a small requested item to a person inside a human work facility. A paper form or Mover's Guide packet is a light, low-precision object comparable to hospital supplies, and the accepted output (the right item in the right person's hands) is the same.

sources.title: Next-gen room service: How Relay 2 robots are revolutionizing the hotel experience - FOX 5 New York

tasks.label: Register, certify, and insure parcels and letters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rural/curbside pickup of prepaid accountable mail: customer leaves a certified letter with a completed PS Form 3800 sticker (and often 3811 green card) and stamps in the roadside mailbox with the flag up. Carrier reaches from the vehicle, removes the piece, checks that fees/postage are sufficient, scans the barcode on the mobile delivery device to create the acceptance record, postmarks and detaches the customer receipt, leaves the receipt in the box, and secures the item. Outdoors, all weather, dozens of differing box designs and mounts.

Face-to-face acceptance on the route: a customer meets the carrier at the door or vehicle window with an unlabeled letter or small parcel and asks for certified mail or insurance. Carrier determines weight/rate, computes fees, collects cash or check, completes and affixes the certified/insured label and postage, hands over the postmarked receipt, and takes custody of the item.

Business stop with a firm mailing book: carrier picks up a batch of certified/insured items from an office mailroom counter or loading dock, verifies the piece count and article numbers against the PS Form 3877 listing, round-dates and initials the book, scans each item into the acceptance system, and loads them into the satchel or vehicle. Indoor commercial premises with fixed layout.

End-of-route processing at the delivery unit: carrier accounts for all accountable mail collected on the route, verifies forms and fees, scans items into the acceptance/dispatch system, separates registered items into the registry dispatch, and transfers custody to the clerk against signature. Post office workroom floor, indoors.

Registered mail / high-value insured acceptance from a home or small business: carrier inspects the article for required sealing (tape or paper seals at all flap junctions and closures), verifies the declared value and computes the registry/insurance fee, completes PS Form 3806, issues the receipt, and keeps the item under continuous chain of custody separate from other mail.

sources.system: Tension SLAM Line (Scan, Label, Apply, Manifest)
sources.title: SLAM Line Automated Scan Label Apply Manifest Systems
sources.claim: Commercial SLAM (Scan, Label, Apply, Manifest) conveyor lines automatically scan, weigh and dimension a parcel, apply the carrier shipping label, and manifest the shipment — the physical core of registering/insuring a parcel — in purpose-built distribution-center lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated outbound parcel manifesting. Registering/insuring a parcel physically consists of capturing weight and dimensions, rating the piece, affixing a barcoded service label, and creating the acceptance/manifest record; SLAM lines perform exactly these acts on parcels of the same size and weight class a carrier accepts.

sources.title: What's an AFCS? – USPS Employee News
sources.claim: USPS's Advanced Facer Canceler System autonomously positions collection letter mail, cancels/postmarks it, reads existing barcodes, and prints a barcode on pieces that lack one, at roughly 36,000 pieces per hour in postal plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine acceptance processing of collection letter mail. The letter side of certifying mail is verifying/reading the piece, applying the postmark cancellation, and reading or printing the tracking barcode that creates the acceptance record — the acts AFCS performs on the same envelopes.

sources.title: Ambi Robotics Expands Partnership with Pitney Bowes to Automate Middle-Mile Sorting
sources.claim: AI-powered robotic parcel induction and sortation systems are deployed in US parcel hubs, autonomously picking individual parcels, reading their labels and inducting them onto sorters inside fenced automated cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic parcel induction. It substantiates that the physical handling step of an acceptance line — grasping an individual mailpiece, reading its label and placing it into the correct container — is done autonomously at production quality in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Parcel Processing Sortation System (PPSS) with automatic print-and-apply label applicators

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic label application on a parcel line. Affixing the certified/insured service label to the mailpiece is the manipulative step of this task; print-and-apply applicators perform it on comparable objects to a production standard.

tasks.label: Travel to post offices to pick up the mail for routes or pick up mail from postal relay boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift pickup at the carrier's own delivery unit / Sorting & Delivery Center: carrier goes to the case and staging area, collects the route's DPS letter trays, flat tubs, hampers of parcels and accountable mail, wheels the hamper across the workroom floor to the dock, and loads the LLV/Promaster parked at the dock in delivery order.

Park-and-loop city carrier retrieves relayed mail from a locked green relay box on a public sidewalk mid-route: walks up with satchel, opens the box with the arrow key, pulls out the strapped bundles and flats left by the relay driver, fills the satchel, relocks the box and resumes delivery, in whatever weather, traffic and pedestrian conditions are present.

Rural or contract carrier drives a personal vehicle or LLV several miles on public roads to the post office at the start of the day, parks at the dock, and loads the route's trays, tubs, parcels and accountable mail into the vehicle, arranging them by line of travel.

Mid-day or second-trip return to the post office, an annex, or a neighboring station to pick up additional volume: drives back on city streets, backs into the dock, loads extra parcel hampers, Express/priority items or a second relay load, and departs again.

Pickup of relayed or staged route mail from a locked relay/collection point on institution-controlled premises - an apartment building lobby relay box, a large office building mailroom, or a campus/plaza staging point - unlocking the container, removing bundles and loading them into the satchel or cart.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rural/HCR carrier makes a curbside stamp sale: a customer waits at the roadside mailbox or flags the delivery vehicle, asks for a booklet or coil of Forever stamps; the carrier pulls it from the stamp stock carried in the vehicle, takes cash or a check, makes change from a cash bank, and records the sale for later settlement. Outdoors, traffic and weather variable.

Stamps-by-Mail order: the customer leaves PS Form 3227-R/3227-A with cash or a check inside the mailbox; the carrier retrieves the envelope at the box, fills the order back at the delivery unit, and deposits the stamps in the customer's mailbox on a later trip, then settles the funds.

City carrier on a foot/park-and-loop route sells stamps at a residential door, porch or sidewalk to a customer who comes out to meet the carrier; hands over a booklet from the satchel, accepts cash, makes change, answers questions about rates.

Money order sale on a rural route: customer hands the carrier a completed money order application (PS Form 6401) with the funds plus fee at the mailbox or door; the carrier verifies the amount and funds, issues a receipt, has the money order prepared at the office and delivers it on the next trip.

Sale at a business or apartment-complex office during the delivery stop: carrier sells stamp booklets or sheets to reception/mailroom staff inside a lobby or management office, takes a business check or cash, and provides a receipt.
