instances.label: Online carcass inspection at a poultry slaughter establishment: the inspector stands at a fixed station on the evisceration line and examines every bird (carcass and, in traditional systems, viscera) at 70-175 birds/minute, identifying septicemia/toxemia, airsacculitis, tumors, bruising and fecal contamination, and retaining or condemning affected carcasses.

Post-mortem inspection at a beef or swine slaughter plant: viewing, palpating and incising heads, viscera (lymph nodes, liver, lungs) and carcasses on the rail, judging abscesses, parasites, lesions and zero-tolerance fecal/ingesta/milk contamination, and directing trimming, retention or condemnation.

Daily in-plant verification at a meat/poultry further-processing or ready-to-eat establishment: pre-operational sanitation checks of disassembled equipment, observing dressing and handling procedures, taking product and cooler temperatures, collecting product samples for pathogen testing, checking labels and records, and documenting noncompliance.

Inspection of a non-meat food facility (dairy plant or farm bulk tank, seafood processor, cannery, bakery, produce packer, cold-storage warehouse) by an FDA or state inspector: walking the process, judging equipment condition and cleanliness, observing employee practices and process controls, checking product for filth/decomposition/temperature abuse, drawing samples, and reviewing records.

Lot inspection and certification of food products at a packinghouse, terminal market or cold-storage warehouse: drawing representative samples from pallets or bins, cutting and examining individual units for decay, mold, insect damage, internal defects, extraneous/foreign material and cracked or leaking eggs, and deciding whether the lot is fit for human consumption and what grade it meets.

sources.system: USDA-ARS line-scan (hyperspectral/multispectral) poultry carcass inspection system
sources.developer: USDA Agricultural Research Service (Chao, Kim, Chan et al.)
sources.title: Machine vision system for on-line wholesomeness inspection of poultry carcasses (Poultry Science)
sources.claim: A USDA-ARS line-scan machine vision system inspected chicken carcasses autonomously on a commercial evisceration line running at 140 birds/minute, classifying wholesome versus systemically diseased birds, verified in real time against a veterinarian's calls.

sources.system: On-line automated poultry carcass inspection machine vision system
sources.title: On-Line Automated Inspection of Poultry Carcasses by Machine Vision (AGRIS record)
sources.claim: An earlier ARS machine-vision poultry inspection system was tested on-line in a commercial poultry plant, classifying wholesome and unwholesome carcasses with 94% and 87% accuracy respectively.

sources.system: SensorX / SensorX SmartSort X-ray bone and contaminant detection
sources.date: 2021 (product in continuing commercial use as of 2026)
sources.title: SensorX: Your secret weapon in the fight against food contamination
sources.claim: SensorX is a commercially installed X-ray inspection unit on poultry and meat processing conveyors that autonomously detects hazardous bone fragments and other hard contaminants and rejects the affected product from the line; named processors (e.g., Boscher Volailles, BRF Thailand) run it in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-line contaminant inspection of meat products. It transfers to the inspector's product-safety determination because the same objects (fillets, portions) are judged for hazardous foreign material and unfit units are physically removed, at line speed.

sources.system: TOMRA 5C optical sorter with BSI/foreign material detection
sources.title: TOMRA 5C optical sorting machine wins prestigious Japan Food Journal award
sources.claim: TOMRA 5C optical sorters are installed on commercial processing lines (between IQF tunnel and packing station) where they autonomously make final food-safety checks, recognizing and ejecting foreign material, extraneous vegetable matter and defective product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect and foreign-material sorting. It substantiates the product-fitness decision an inspector makes on sampled lots, since the machine judges each unit for decay, extraneous matter and contaminants and removes unfit units.

sources.system: Spectrim sorting platform and Inspectra2 internal quality grader
sources.date: 2022 (commercial installations, ~200 new citrus lanes per year in California)
sources.title: How TOMRA Sorting and Grading Solutions can help Apple Packhouses meet operational challenges
sources.claim: TOMRA/Compac packhouse grading platforms are installed in fruit packhouses where Spectrim autonomously grades external defects and Inspectra2 non-destructively detects internal defects such as core rot, internal browning and water core, diverting affected fruit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grading of fresh produce in packinghouses. Transfers to lot inspection because the same commodities are examined unit-by-unit for the internal and external defects (rot, decay, damage) an inspector cuts and scores by hand.

sources.system: Moba Egg Inspector (4th generation, on Omnia/Magna graders)
sources.date: 2025 (product page updated 2025-2026; systems in commercial grading stations)
sources.title: Egg Inspector - Detects Leaking- and Dirty Eggs - Moba.net
sources.claim: Moba's Egg Inspector, a camera-and-lighting inspection module on commercial Omnia egg graders, autonomously detects leaking and dirty eggs and rejects leakers through dropgates while diverting dirty eggs to an off-grade lane, with adjustable defect thresholds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated egg candling and grading. It matches the inspector's judgment on shell-egg lots (leakers, dirt, cracks are the same wholesomeness criteria) and physically removes the unfit units.

sources.system: Mettler-Toledo Safeline / Eagle x-ray and metal detection product inspection systems
sources.title: Mettler-Toledo showcases smart product inspection solutions for food manufacturers at interpack 2026
sources.claim: Mettler-Toledo Safeline x-ray and metal detection systems are standard commercial in-line product inspection equipment that detect metal, bone, plastic, glass and ... in packaged and pumped food and automatically reject contaminated product from the line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: critical-control-point contaminant inspection of finished food. Transfers to the inspector's product-safety call for physical hazards, on the same packaged products, when product is conveyed through the machine.

sources.system: Computer vision systems (CVS) for abattoir meat safety assurance (survey of 62 studies)
sources.developer: Sandberg et al. (DTU / University of Liverpool)
sources.title: Applications of computer vision systems for meat safety assurance in abattoirs: A systematic review
sources.claim: A 2023 systematic review of computer vision systems for ante- and post-mortem meat inspection found the literature dominated by broiler work, with very few pig or bovine systems, incomplete validation, and suboptimal specificity, indicating no validated automated replacement for red-meat post-mortem inspection.

sources.title: Spot robot dog inspects Cargill's food factory for safety hazards
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot has been deployed since mid-2024 at Cargill's oilseed crush and refinery plant, autonomously walking routes to perform routine maintenance inspections and visual ... - equipment and hazard rounds, not food-product wholesomeness or sanitation-adequacy determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest deployed mobile plant-inspection robot; it shows autonomous facility rounds exist but are limited to equipment condition and hazard checks, not the sanitation, procedure and sampling judgments this task requires.

tasks.label: Monitor the operations and sanitary conditions of slaughtering or meat processing plants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-operational sanitation inspection before start-up: the inspector walks the kill floor and processing rooms, examines cleaned food-contact surfaces of saws, grinders, conveyors, tables, augers and hoppers — opening guards, reaching inside equipment, using a flashlight — plus floors, drains, walls and overhead structures, and documents findings or writes a noncompliance record.

Operational sanitation monitoring during the production shift: repeated unannounced walkthroughs of the establishment looking for condensation over exposed product, contaminated equipment, aprons and gloves, product contacting floors or unclean surfaces, employee hygiene and dressing-procedure lapses, and pest evidence; directing plant corrective action and documenting.

Slaughter-line operations monitoring in a beef, swine or poultry plant: watching carcasses move past the dressing line for visible fecal, ingesta or milk contamination (zero tolerance), verifying dressing/evisceration procedures, knife-sterilizer temperatures, line speed and station staffing, and tagging or retaining carcasses when contamination is found.

Further-processing / ready-to-eat plant operations monitoring: checking cooking, chilling, curing, and packaging operations, probing product temperatures with a calibrated thermometer, verifying critical limits and process-control parameters, and observing sanitary handling of exposed RTE product.

Ante-mortem and humane-handling monitoring in livestock holding pens, unloading ramps, chutes and the stunning area: wet, crowded, partly outdoor pens with live animals; observing unloading and driving practices, water/space, and effectiveness of stunning, and suspending operations when handling is inhumane.

sources.title: Cargill Deploys AI-Powered Robot Dog 'Spot' at Amsterdam Facility to Enhance Safety, Reliability and Workplace Innovation
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped performs autonomous inspection rounds inside an operating food-processing plant (oilseed crush and refinery), capturing thermal, acoustic and visual ... and flagging equipment and safety hazards such as leaks, overheating and spills — the closest deployed analogue to an inspector's plant walkthrough, but limited to maintenance/safety anomalies rather than sanitation-compliance verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition-monitoring rounds in a food plant. It shows a robot can navigate a working food facility and flag anomalies, but the anomaly classes (overheating, leaks, ventilation faults) are not the food-contact-surface and hygiene-practice judgments this task requires.

sources.system: ARS/Stork in-line multispectral (517/565 nm) fecal detection system
sources.developer: USDA Agricultural Research Service with Stork Food Systems
sources.title: ARS System to Detect Poultry Contamination Passes First Commercial Test : USDA ARS
sources.claim: An automated in-line multispectral imaging system developed by USDA-ARS with Stork Food Systems was installed in a commercial ... and inspected every bird in real time at commercial line speed for fecal and ingesta contamination — the carcass contamination surveillance element of slaughter-line monitoring, performed on carcasses presented by the plant's shackle conveyor.

sources.system: In-line multispectral imaging system for fecal detection
sources.title: In-plant Test of In-line Multispectral Imaging System For Fecal Detection during Poultry Processing
sources.claim: The in-plant test of the in-line multispectral imaging system showed it could inspect every carcass in real time at commercial processing speed, with image-processing methods tuned to maximize detection accuracy and minimize false positives for the FSIS zero-tolerance fecal contamination requirement.

sources.system: Marel IRIS (Intelligent Reporting, Inspection & Selection) with Innova PDS distribution
sources.title: 5 questions about vision grading in poultry processing | JBT Marel
sources.claim: Marel's IRIS vision inspection cameras are commercially installed on poultry killing/defeathering, grading and distribution lines, where the assessment is coupled to a product distribution system that physically filters out and reroutes products failing the criteria — a deployed sense-and-act inspection station operating on carcasses presented by a purpose-built conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-line visual assessment of poultry carcasses/parts with automatic rejection. Same objects, same line speeds and same fixtured presentation as zero-tolerance carcass contamination surveillance, showing the sensing-plus-actuation loop is commercially mature on a slaughter line.

sources.system: Robotic swabbing system with tactile sensing control (UR5e) plus fluorescence/absorbance spectrometer
sources.developer: University of Arkansas (Mahmoudi, Crandall, Wang et al.)
sources.title: Evaluation of Robotic Swabbing and Fluorescent Sensing to Monitor the Hygiene of Food Contact Surfaces
sources.claim: A UR5e robot arm with a force-sensing sponge swab performed environmental hygiene swabbing of food-contact surfaces on a laboratory bench with more consistent pressure and coverage than trained humans, paired with fluorescence/absorbance sensing of protein residue; this covers only the swab-collection sub-step of sanitation verification on a flat, presented surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: environmental hygiene monitoring of food-contact surfaces. It substantiates a robot taking a consistent swab of a flat surface presented to it, but not the plant-wide pre-operational examination of equipment interiors, drains and overheads that the instance requires.

tasks.label: Label and seal graded products and issue official grading certificates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Meat/poultry packing plant: USDA grader applies official grade stamps/shields to carcasses moving on the overhead rail and grade/lot labels to boxed product, then issues the grading certificate or report for the lot. Plant is a cold, wet, standardized food facility with a moving line.

Fresh fruit/vegetable packinghouse, cold storage or terminal market: inspector affixes inspection stickers/lot tags to sampled cartons and to pallets of the graded lot, closes/seals opened cartons and sample containers, and issues the inspection certificate for the lot.

Grain elevator or export terminal: after grading, official personnel apply numbered official seals to loaded railcar hatches, truck hoppers, container doors or barge/hold openings and issue the grade certificate; work occurs at the loadout, outdoors, at height, in dust and weather.

Grain, rice, bean or seed conditioning/bagging facility: inspector applies official lot tags/labels to bagged or containerized graded lots and labels/seals the official sample containers, then prints and issues the grade certificate at the inspection point.

Shell-egg, dairy or processed-products plant: grader applies USDA grade shield labels or printed grade codes to cartons/containers, ensures cases are sealed and marked with the grade, and issues the grading certificate for the lot.

Point-of-production/field setting: inspector at a farm, orchard, grove, nursery or loading dock tags, stamps or seals graded lots (bins, sacks, nursery stock, a loaded truck) and issues the certificate on site; layout varies farm to farm, uneven ground, no fixed equipment.

sources.title: Reliable and fully automatic inkjet marking system - AutoMarker M1
sources.claim: Frontmatec's AutoMarker M1 is a fully automatic inline inkjet system that prints identifying information including the grading class onto carcasses on the slaughter line, integrated with the AutoFom grading system.
sources.transferJustification: This is the marking/stamping step of the task itself: applying the official grade mark to graded product, performed automatically on carcasses presented by the slaughter-line conveyor.

sources.title: Labelers | Print and Apply Labeling | Label Applicators | Videojet
sources.claim: Commercial print-and-apply labelers generate variable-data labels on demand and apply ... and pallets on food production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Applying an official grade/lot label to graded cartons and pallets is the same physical act on the same objects (cases, cartons, pallets) with the same placement precision; only the label content differs.

sources.system: REA LABEL Robotic Labeler (REA LABEL DS + Kawasaki robot)
sources.developer: REA Elektronik / REA JET with Kawasaki
sources.title: Automatic labeling: easier, faster, more reliable
sources.claim: A REA LABEL robotic print-and-apply cell with a Kawasaki robot arm is installed and running in production at GROHE, autonomously printing pallet labels, applying them to varying-height stretch-wrapped pallets delivered by conveyor, and scanning to verify readability inside a fenced cell.
sources.transferJustification: Labeling a graded lot at pallet level is the same act on the same object class (stretch-wrapped pallets of cartons) with machine verification of correct, legible placement; the cell is a fenced, conveyor-fed purpose-built station.

sources.title: Carton Sealing Machine - Case Sealer | Lantech
sources.claim: Lantech automatic case sealers fold and tape-seal cartons inline; a production customer reports deploying the CS1000 sealer with a case erector and cutting line labor by over 40%.
sources.transferJustification: Sealing the graded product's cartons is the 'seal' half of the task; the machine performs it automatically on cases presented by the conveyor at rates and reliability accepted in commercial food packing.

sources.system: MARKOPRINT egg carton coder integrated with MOBA egg graders
sources.title: Certified Egg Carton Coder
sources.claim: MARKOPRINT industrial inkjet coders integrated with MOBA egg grading and packing machines print the legally required code onto egg cartons inline at grading-line speeds.
sources.transferJustification: Marking graded egg cartons with the required code/grade information is the same physical marking act as applying a grade label, performed automatically downstream of the grader on cartons presented by the packing line.

sources.system: RAYHAWK autonomous railcar lid handling system
sources.title: How Autonomous Lid Control Works | RAYHAWK
sources.claim: RAYHAWK's autonomous robotic gantry uses machine vision to detect latch type, open, close and secure railcar lids at grain terminal loadouts, deployed at a grain company site with reported 98% lid-handling reliability in snow, ice and dust; it does not apply official numbered inspection seals.
sources.transferJustification: Closest automated analogue to official sealing of loaded carriers: same objects (railcar hatches at a grain loadout), but it closes and latches lids rather than applying numbered official seals, so it does not substantiate completion of the sealing instance.

sources.system: USDA AMS Specialty Crops Integrated Operating Network (SCION)
sources.title: USDA to issue Specialty Crops Inspection Certificates, Audit Report in new formats
sources.claim: USDA AMS issues official specialty-crop inspection certificates electronically through its SCION platform rather than as manually produced paper documents.
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the documentary half of the instance (issuing the certificate), which is a records act generated and transmitted electronically; the physical labeling/sealing half is substantiated by the robotic evidence items.

tasks.label: Monitor the grading performed by company employees to verify conformance to standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fresh fruit/vegetable packinghouse: inspector stands at or walks the packing line where company graders hand-sort, pulls samples of graded product from the line, bins or filled cartons, and check-grades them against US grade standards (size, color, maturity, blemishes, decay, internal defects requiring cutting), then compares results with the company graders' calls and reports discrepancies.

Shell egg grading and packing plant: USDA-authorized resident grader monitors plant graders/candlers, samples cases off the machine, verifies weight class, shell cleanliness and soundness, cracks/leakers and interior quality, and confirms plant personnel are applying grade standards correctly.

Poultry or meat processing plant: inspector monitors company sorters/graders assigning quality classes to carcasses and parts moving on shackle or cut-up lines, sampling product to verify defects (bruises, tears, missing parts, marbling/yield calls) match the company grade determinations at line speed.

Grain elevator, export terminal or country receiving point: inspector monitors sampling and grade determination performed by company or licensed plant personnel - representative sampling from the flowing stream or truck, test weight, moisture, dockage/foreign material, damaged and heat-damaged kernels - and check-grades file samples against the same standards.

Field-pack or on-farm grading operation: inspector monitors a grading crew working on a mobile field-pack rig or open farm shed (lettuce, melons, berries), in variable light, dust and weather, pulling packed units from the crew's output and check-grading them.

Cold storage warehouse or shipping-point lot verification: inspector selects cartons from pallets of previously graded, packed product, opens and re-grades the sample to verify the packer's grading conformed to the marked grade, and certifies or rejects the lot.

sources.title: Fruit sorting, grading, packing, and filling solutions - TOMRA
sources.claim: TOMRA's Spectrim/5S optical graders with the Inspectra2 NIR module autonomously grade fresh produce for external defects, size, colour and internal quality on packhouse sorting lines and physically divert fruit into grade lanes; sold and installed commercially worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grading of the same commodities the inspector check-grades. The machine makes the independent grade determination (defects, size, colour, internal quality) on product handled by company graders and physically separates off-grade fruit, which is the substance of a verification check-grade; only the reporting step differs.

sources.title: Tomra's sorting and grading solutions - FruitToday
sources.claim: TOMRA Spectrim grading vision systems are deployed at scale in commercial citrus packhouses, including a 200+ lane operation, grading minor and major defects such as blemishes, insect damage, misshapen fruit, ... rot.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the TOMRA product evidence: automated grade determination on packinghouse fruit substitutes for the inspector's independent check-grade of company-graded product.

sources.title: Moba Egg Graders - JDW Poultry Equipment
sources.claim: Moba Omnia egg grading machines automatically inspect eggs for dirt and leaks, detect cracks and blood, weigh each egg by vision, and transfer eggs to the packing lane for the assigned grade in commercial egg plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shell-egg grading itself. Verifying plant graders' work means re-determining weight class, shell soundness and interior defects on sampled eggs; the machine performs exactly these determinations on singulated eggs and physically routes them by grade.

sources.title: Vision grading in the killing and defeathering line - JBT Marel
sources.claim: JBT Marel IRIS vision grading systems automatically grade poultry carcasses and parts for quality defects at full line speed in processing plants and drive downstream product distribution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: quality grading of poultry on the line. The inspector's monitoring consists of independently judging the same defects on the same product presented on the shackle line; the vision system makes that judgment on every bird.

sources.system: USDA-approved beef grading instruments (camera systems listed by AMS)
sources.title: USDA Approved Instruments for Augmenting Beef Grading (AMS)
sources.claim: USDA AMS has approved camera-based instrument grading systems used in US beef plants to predict marbling scores, apply yield grades and measure ribeye area for application of carcass beef grades.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: official carcass grade determination, the same determination an inspector reproduces when verifying plant grading. Cited as corroboration only; the instruments assist rather than replace graders, so autonomy is unclear and it does not carry a positive judgment alone.

sources.title: eCFR :: 7 CFR Part 801 - Official Performance Requirements for Grain Inspection Equipment
sources.claim: Diverter-type mechanical samplers are approved devices that automatically obtain and subdivide representative portions from a flowing grain stream for official US grain inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: official sampling that precedes grade determination. It supplies, under machine control, the representative sample the inspector would otherwise draw by hand when check-grading a company-graded grain lot.

sources.system: Cgrain Value Pro / Cgrain Value Sorter
sources.title: Cgrain - Products
sources.claim: Cgrain Value Pro/Sorter images every kernel of a grain sample, automatically identifies impurities, weed seeds and kernel defects, and the Sorter version physically separates kernels by class; used in commercial cereal production and processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: determination of the visual grading factors (defects, impurities) that a grain inspector re-determines when verifying an elevator employee's grade; same sample, same factors, presented to the instrument.

sources.title: Grain Inspection - an overview (ScienceDirect Topics)
sources.claim: Foss EyeFoss image-analysis instruments are calibrated to predict visual grain ... weed seeds and are used by bulk grain handlers as an objective substitute for human visual grading checks at receival.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: objective replication of the visual grade assessment performed by receival staff - precisely the determination the inspector repeats to verify their grading.

tasks.label: Inspect or test horticultural products or livestock to detect harmful diseases, chemical residues, or infestations and to determine the quality of products or animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-mortem inspection on a red-meat or poultry slaughter line: the inspector examines each carcass and its viscera at line speed for lesions, abscesses, tumors, parasites, arthritis, contamination and other pathology, palpating or incising organs and lymph nodes where required, and marks carcasses/parts for trim, retention or condemnation.

Ante-mortem inspection of live animals: cattle, hogs, sheep or poultry examined in plant holding pens, chutes and on trucks (and sometimes on farms or at auction yards), at rest and in motion, to spot disease signs, CNS abnormalities, lameness/downers and moribund animals, and to tag suspects or condemn.

In-line quality/defect determination of product presented on a packing or processing line: fresh fruit and vegetables at a packinghouse, nuts at a huller/processor, poultry carcasses and parts in a processing plant — judging grade, decay/rot, insect damage, bruising, blemishes, size/color and internal quality, and separating product by grade.

Inspection of packed lots at warehouses, cold storages, terminal markets and import cargo exam stations: selecting cartons across a lot, opening and unpacking them, examining and cutting fruit for internal condition and pests, checking pulp temperatures, and drawing representative samples for pesticide/drug residue laboratory analysis; issuing a condition/grade certificate or release decision.

Regulatory field, orchard, greenhouse and nursery inspection: walking rows or benches at a grower's or nursery's site, examining plants and stock for quarantine pests, virus and disease symptoms and off-types, collecting suspect material for lab confirmation, and certifying the field/lot (phytosanitary, seed and nursery certification programs).

Broad-acre scouting of row-crop fields for infestation level and crop condition: traversing a grower's acreage, identifying pest presence and pressure, weed density and stand problems, and reporting findings for treatment decisions.

sources.title: Single and Dual Lane Sorters | TOMRA
sources.claim: TOMRA's Spectrim optical grading platform, deployed in commercial fresh-produce packhouses worldwide, automatically grades fruit for major and minor defects including insect damage and blemishes and sorts product accordingly.

sources.title: How citrus packhouses can improve profitability with the latest sorting and grading solutions
sources.claim: Spectrim graders are installed in citrus packhouses (including the world's largest citrus packing operation, 200+ lanes) and detect decay ('clear rot') as well as insect damage, with grade thresholds configured to market requirements; a companion NIR unit grades internal quality.

sources.title: Northern Fruit start up new Unitec cherry sorting technologies
sources.claim: A named US packinghouse (Northern Fruit) runs Unitec Cherry Vision electronic grading that automatically detects and removes culls, debris, defects and soft fruit, replacing manual grade determination on the line.

sources.title: 5 questions about vision grading in poultry processing | JBT Marel
sources.claim: Marel's IRIS vision grading system, installed in commercial poultry plants, automatically determines the quality of whole birds and of each anatomical part on the moving line and routes product accordingly, spotting bruises, fractures, skin lesions, feather ....
sources.transferJustification: Same 'determine the quality of products' prong applied to poultry carcasses on a slaughter/processing line; it does not perform viscera examination, palpation/incision or wholesomeness disposition, so it does not substantiate post-mortem disease inspection.

sources.title: Solinftec boosts Solix autonomy with Discovery Mode, Starlink, and obstacle detection - Future Farming
sources.claim: Solinftec's Solix autonomous field robot, operating commercially in US row-crop fields (Illinois and Indiana, expanding to Kansas, Iowa, Wisconsin and Texas ...), scouts crops with AI cameras and reports pest presence, weed density and stand condition with minimal operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Crop scouting for infestation is the same detection act as inspecting plants in the field for infestation; it does not cover quarantine-pest identification, sampling or certification required in regulatory field/nursery inspection.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities (Computers and Electronics in Agriculture)
sources.claim: The ceiling-suspended Scout/ChickenBoy robot autonomously patrols commercial broiler houses with thermal and visible cameras and sensors and flags sick and dead birds and litter problems without contacting the animals.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system to 'inspect livestock to detect harmful diseases': it monitors flock health in a livestock building, but produces flock-level alerts rather than the individual-animal ante-mortem examination, handling and disposition an inspector must deliver.

tasks.label: Feed and water animals, and clean and disinfect pens, cages, yards, and hutches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Home-based / small-scale dog or cat breeder: whelping room in a spare room, garage or basement plus crates and a few outdoor runs. Measures out individual diets, fills and washes bowls, refreshes water, picks up and hoses runs, scrubs and disinfects whelping boxes with quat solution. Layout, flooring and equipment differ house to house; animals present during chores.

Commercial kennel or cattery attached to a breeding business: purpose-built building with rows of concrete runs, floor drains, standard bowls and feed carts. Twice-daily feeding and watering, shifting animals, hosing and disinfecting each run and the isolation/whelping rooms to a written sanitation protocol.

Horse breeding farm, traditional box-stall barn: hay flakes and measured grain per horse, buckets or automatic waterers topped and scrubbed, stalls mucked with fork and wheelbarrow, soiled shavings removed and fresh bedding spread, foaling stall stripped and disinfected before a mare foals.

Cattle breeding operation (seedstock beef or dairy): mixed ration or hay delivered to bunks/feed fence in a free-stall or bedded-pack barn and adjacent drylots, waterers checked and scrubbed, alleys scraped and pens bedded, calf pens/hutches cleaned between calves.

Swine or poultry breeding barn (sow farm gestation/farrowing rooms or a broiler-breeder house): feed lines and feeding stations delivering measured rations, nipple drinker lines checked and flushed, and all-in/all-out pressure washing plus disinfection of emptied rooms between groups.

Rabbitry or other small caged breeding stock (rabbits, guinea pigs, cage birds, show poultry): rows of hutches or cages in a shed, barn or backyard. Pellet hoppers filled, water bottles or nipple lines refilled and cleaned, drop pans and wire floors scraped, cages washed and disinfected between litters.

sources.claim: The Go Cleaner washes emptied broiler houses, including floors, ceilings and feed and water lines, positioning itself with an indoor GPS system and needing no person in the building.

sources.title: Poultry Technology: Rise of the robots | Canadian Poultry
sources.claim: Octopus Poultry Safe autonomously sanitizes and disinfects poultry houses by turning litter and nebulizing biocide, working until the target area is covered; it is listed as a commercial product for poultry producers.

sources.title: Robots for Precision Poultry and Egg Production | UGA Precision Poultry Farming
sources.claim: Independent university review confirms the Octopus Poultry Safe robot was tested sanitizing poultry house floors with liquid disinfectant delivered autonomously.

sources.system: Förster-Technik COMPACT smart / VARIO smart automatic calf feeder
sources.title: COMPACT Smart - Calf feeding – Förster-Technik
sources.claim: Automatic calf feeders prepare and deliver individually metered milk feeds to calves around the clock in ordinary calf barns and clean their own circuits, covering the calf-feeding portion of cattle-breeding chores.

sources.system: AP Compident 8 Electronic Sow Feeding (also Nedap Velos ESF)
sources.title: AP introduces enhancements to Electronic Sow Feeding System | National Hog Farmer
sources.claim: Electronic sow feeding stations identify each breeding animal by RFID and dispense its individual ration automatically in commercial US sow barns, replacing hand feeding of breeding stock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine delivery of individually metered rations to identified breeding animals. Transfers to the feeding half of this task in kennels and horse barns only in a purpose-built caging/penning layout, since animals must come to fixed stations.

sources.system: HIT Active Stable automatic horse feeders
sources.title: Automatic Horse Feeders - Footing Solutions LLC
sources.claim: HIT Active Stable transponder feeders dispense individually programmed hay and concentrate rations to horses kept loose in a herd, a configuration in commercial use in equestrian facilities for over two decades.

sources.title: 3 Tech-Savvy Tips for Efficient Barn Management | Equine Facility Design
sources.claim: The Active Cleaner is a marketed manure-removal robot for equine facilities that detects droppings with a camera and AI and clears the surface automatically, covering the manure-pickup portion of horse housekeeping on hard/loose-housing surfaces (not bedded box stalls).

sources.system: IWT/Tecniplast cage and bottle robotics (Ares, Poseidon, Apollo)
sources.title: BOTTLE & CAGE AUTOMATION (IWT/Tecniplast brochure)
sources.claim: IWT/Tecniplast has installed more than 100 robots in research animal facilities that handle cages and bottles through the dirty- and clean-side wash and re-provisioning process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emptying, washing, disinfecting and re-bedding small-animal cages and refilling water bottles on a purpose-built line. Same objects (small-stock cages, hoppers, bottles) and cleanliness standard as rabbitry/small-caged-stock sanitation.

sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Getinge sells a robotic cage handling system that automates loading and ... of laboratory animal cages through the washer, a purpose-built cage-wash cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning and thermal disinfection of small-animal cages; same cage objects and hygiene acceptance criteria as cleaning hutches/cages for small breeding stock, but requires cages be presented on a conveyor line.

sources.system: Vivarium cage-processing robotics (robotic arm plus automatic bedding dispenser)
sources.developer: reported by Lab Animal (Nature), facility integration of commercial systems
sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium | Lab Animal
sources.claim: A vivarium built in 2012 integrated a robotic arm with an automatic bedding dispenser to process rodent cages, showing machine re-provisioning of bedding as part of the cage cycle in real facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated emptying and re-bedding of small-animal cages, i.e. the cleaning/re-provisioning half of this task for caged breeding stock in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Animal Care Facility Cleaning Solutions | Kennels & Vet | Kaivac
sources.claim: Kennel cleaning products marketed as 'automatic' for animal care facilities are operator-pushed no-touch spray/vacuum machines, not autonomous robots; no autonomous kennel feeding-and-disinfecting system was found.

tasks.label: Observe animals in heat to detect approach of estrus and exercise animals to induce or hasten estrus, if necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy cattle: on a commercial dairy (freestall barn/drylot), the breeder checks the milking herd for heat several times a day — walking pens watching for mounting/standing, checking tail chalk and rub marks, reviewing activity/rumination alerts — and produces the day's breeding list, drafting the cows in estrus into the AI pen; non-cycling cows are occasionally moved to an exercise lot before hormonal follow-up.

Beef cattle (seedstock/cow-calf, AI or embryo transfer): twice-daily heat observation of cows and heifers on pasture, range or large open lots — riding or driving through the herd at dawn and dusk watching for standing heat, checking patches/paint — plus gathering and walking groups to the working pens; heifers may be moved/exercised to stimulate cycling. Weather, distance and rough footing are taken as found.

Swine: in an indoor sow breeding barn, daily heat checking of weaned sows and gilts in stalls or pens by walking a boar down the aisle for nose-to-nose contact, applying the back-pressure test by hand, marking sows in standing heat, and walking/exercising gilts and boars to stimulate cycling.

Horses: on a breeding farm, mares are teased daily at a teasing board/chute or over stall doors with a teaser stallion, behavioral responses are scored and recorded, and transitional or anestrous mares are hand-walked, lunged or put in an exerciser to help bring them into cycle; results feed the veterinarian's palpation/ultrasound schedule.

Dogs/cats: a kennel or home-based breeder watches bitches/queens for proestrus and standing heat — checking vulvar swelling and discharge, flagging behavior, flagging with a stud dog — while exercising and walking the animals daily; layout and housing differ from breeder to breeder.

Sheep/goats: during the breeding season the breeder observes ewes/does in pens and pastures for signs of heat, uses a marker ram/buck with a crayon harness, reads and records marks, and moves and sorts groups between pens.

sources.system: Herd Navigator in-line milk progesterone module on DeLaval automatic milking system
sources.title: In-line milk progesterone monitoring as a tool for precision reproductive management - PMC
sources.claim: Herd Navigator (DeLaval) is a commercially sold module on automatic milking systems that automatically draws and assays milk samples and reports onset of cyclicity, estrus and pregnancy without a human observing the cows.

sources.developer: DeLaval / Lattec (validation by Friggens et al.; study in a commercial dairy herd)
sources.title: Behavioral changes to detect estrus using ear-sensor accelerometer compared to in-line milk progesterone in a commercial dairy herd
sources.claim: The automated in-line progesterone system's estrus alerts were validated against visual observation of estrus behavior at 99% accuracy and 93.3% sensitivity, i.e. at or above the detection rate a human heat-checker achieves in a housed herd.

sources.system: Lely Grazeway selection box (with Lely Astronaut / T4C-Horizon cow recognition)
sources.title: Selection box for grazing - Lely Grazeway - Lely
sources.claim: Automated selection/drafting boxes tied to the herd-management software physically separate individual identified cows out of the herd inside the barn, so a cow flagged in heat is sorted for breeding without a person handling her.
sources.transferJustification: Cow drafting is the physical act that follows heat detection in a dairy barn; it uses the same identified-animal gating hardware and shows the machine can act on the flagged cow.

sources.title: Home - Swine Robotics
sources.claim: The Boar Bot is a wheeled cart that carries a boar down sow-barn aisles for heat checking, but it is steered by a person by remote control and the human still performs the heat check itself.

sources.system: Bionic boar mobile oestrus monitoring device
sources.developer: China Agricultural University (Lei, Zong, Du, Teng, Feng) with Shandong New Hope Liuhe
sources.title: Oestrus Analysis of Sows Based on Bionic Boars and Machine Vision Technology
sources.claim: Automated sow estrus detection using a mobile bionic-boar device plus machine vision is a research prototype reported on a sow farm; the paper reports interaction-recognition accuracy but does not establish autonomous unattended operation replacing the stockperson's heat check.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: SwagBot: The AI-Powered Robot Herding Cattle
sources.claim: SwagBot is an autonomous four-wheeled field robot that moves cattle between paddocks on rugged pasture in university field trials; it monitors animals and pasture but is not shown detecting estrus.
sources.transferJustification: Herding/moving cattle on pasture is the 'exercise or move animals' component of the task; it does not carry over to observing individual animals for signs of estrus.

sources.system: Vence virtual fencing (CattleRider collars, base stations, HerdManager)
sources.title: Vence - Merck Animal Health USA
sources.claim: Vence virtual fencing collars are commercially deployed on US ranches and move cattle around pasture under software control, but the product is for grazing control and location monitoring, not estrus observation.
sources.transferJustification: Machine-controlled movement of cattle covers the 'exercise/move animals' element on pasture; it provides no capability for observing animals for estrus signs.

sources.system: Q-Line LBE Horse Exerciser / automatic horse walkers
sources.developer: Vitafloor (and other walker manufacturers, e.g. Centaur)
sources.title: Q-Line Horse Exerciser LBE - Vitafloor
sources.claim: Programmable automatic horse exercisers are standard commercial equipment on breeding and training farms and walk horses on a set speed/duration program, but staff must lead each horse in and out and no teasing/estrus observation is performed by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: A horse walker performs the 'exercise animals' component for mares, but the instance also requires daily teasing and behavioral scoring, and handlers must halter and load each horse.

tasks.label: Treat minor injuries and ailments and contact veterinarians to obtain treatment for animals with serious illnesses or injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dog/cat breeder at a home-based kennel or cattery: examines a puppy or queen with a minor cut, hot spot, ear infection, umbilical issue or diarrhea; cleans and dresses the wound, applies topicals, gives oral dewormer/meds, checks hydration, and decides when to phone the vet (suspected parvo, dystocia, retained placenta). Small, cluttered, non-standard premises; animals are unrestrained and squirming.

Dairy cattle breeder / AI technician on a commercial dairy: catches flagged cows or heifers in headlocks, palpation rail or chute; treats pinkeye, foot rot, minor lacerations, mild metritis or a swollen post-AI injection site; gives IM/SC injections and intrauterine or topical products; escalates DAs, dystocias and downer cows to the herd veterinarian. Concrete alleys, standard equipment, manure and moving animals.

Horse breeder on a breeding farm: treats a mare's or foal's minor laceration, girth sore, hoof abscess or scratches in a stall, barn aisle or paddock; scrubs and dresses wounds, poultices and wraps legs, gives IM injections, soaks a hoof; calls the veterinarian for colic, foal septicemia or lameness. Large flighty animals, bedding, mud, variable layout.

Beef cow-calf, sheep or goat breeder on a pasture-based operation: locates a sick or injured animal in a pen or pasture, drives or ropes it into a corral/chute, treats scours, pinkeye, foot rot, castration or lambing wounds and fly strike with injections, boluses, drenches and topical sprays; calls the vet for prolapse or hard calvings. Outdoor, dirt/mud, weather and non-standard handling facilities.

Swine or poultry breeding-stock operation (confinement): stockperson-breeder walks farrowing/gestation rooms or breeder houses, treats lame sows, scouring piglets, shoulder sores, vent damage or minor cuts with injections, sprays and oral/water medication, culls hopeless cases, and consults the contract veterinarian. Fixed-layout barn, standard crates/pens, biosecurity-controlled.

Specialty/other breeder (laboratory rodent colony, rabbitry, exotic birds, small fish hatchery broodstock): treats minor ailments in a barrier vivarium or small dedicated facility — dermatitis, malocclusion/overgrown incisors, pododermatitis, fin or skin lesions — with topicals, trimming, injectables or bath treatments, and refers serious cases to the attending veterinarian.

sources.system: SureShot automated robotic bovine health center
sources.title: Pharm Robotics advances automated dairy cow healthcare - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Pharm Robotics' SureShot is the closest system to robotic treatment of livestock: a FANUC arm with 3D vision that reads a cow's RFID at the parlor and injects it. As of July 2025 the fully automated stack had only completed simulated shots on a model ..., i.e. still pre-commercial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated injection of pharmaceuticals into live dairy cows, the same physical act as giving a treatment injection. It is cited to show the frontier is still model-cow demonstrations, so it cannot substantiate completion of the treatment task at any tier.

sources.system: Additional dosing unit for automatic calf feeders (Vario/ CalfRail systems)
sources.title: Additional dosing unit - Förster-Technik
sources.claim: Automatic calf feeders with an additive dosing unit administer vet-prescribed electrolytes, vitamins or medication to individually RFID-identified calves on a pre-set plan, unattended, in commercial group-housed calf barns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated delivery of an oral treatment to an identified sick animal. It substantiates only fluid dosing of a calf that voluntarily drinks; it performs no examination, no wound care, no injection, and does not decide on or arrange veterinary referral.

sources.system: iSPRAY-VISION walkover teat sprayer (and iSPRAY4 on-platform sprayer)
sources.title: iSPRAY-VISION Walkover Teat Sprayer
sources.claim: Automated teat sprayers apply a topical liquid to a specific body region of live, moving cows in rotary and walkover races using AI camera tracking, deployed commercially on dairies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled application of a liquid to a live cow's udder. It shows only a fixed, undifferentiated hygiene spray on every cow passing a race; it involves no lesion assessment, no dosing decision and no contact manipulation, so it does not transfer to treating injuries or ailments.

sources.title: Stingray directs 'laser focus' on second factory
sources.claim: Stingray's laser nodes autonomously detect and destroy sea lice on individual free-swimming salmon around the clock in commercial sea pens; over 2,000 units are deployed across Norwegian farms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous treatment of an animal ailment (sea-lice infestation) on live animals. It is population-level parasite control on salmon in net pens; it does not examine an individual animal, treat wounds, dose medication, or trigger veterinary referral, and it does not apply to terrestrial breeding stock.

sources.title: Vaccination - Maskon
sources.claim: Fully automated fish vaccination machines orient, inject and sort up to 40,000 anaesthetised smolt per hour in hatcheries with a single operator, showing what purpose-built E1 automation of a medical procedure on live animals looks like.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated needle injection of live animals in a purpose-built machine. It performs identical prophylactic injections on uniform, anaesthetised, conveyor-presented fish; it does not diagnose or treat an individual animal's injury or illness, so it does not substantiate this task.

sources.system: Poultry house monitoring robots (e.g. ChickenBoy; mortality-recovery robots)
sources.developer: Faromatics / Birds Eye Robotics (survey of commercial systems)
sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Commercial poultry-house robots monitor flocks and locate dead or sick birds but act only non-contact (monitoring) or by retrieving mortalities; none treats sick or injured birds.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (breeder/broiler house) and same target animals as the poultry instance; it documents that deployed barn robots stop at detection and carcass removal, providing no treatment capability.

sources.title: New autonomous cattle chute featured at FPVX
sources.claim: Cattle handling automation on farms and feedlots covers restraint, not treatment: an autonomous catch-chute self-catches and holds the animal while a human performs the health procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: presenting and fixturing a live bovine, the E1 precondition for this task. It shows the fixture exists commercially while the treatment step itself remains manual, so the E1 counterfactual still lacks a treating system.

sources.developer: academic research team (NVIDIA Omniverse Isaac Sim based)
sources.title: Digital twins as decision-support tools for automation in agriculture: A case study on robotic vaccination - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robotic cattle vaccination remains at the simulation stage: a 2025 study built an NVIDIA Isaac Sim digital twin to train and de-risk an injection robot before any physical deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic injection of cattle in a handling facility. Cited as negative context: as of late 2025 the work is explicitly pre-physical-deployment simulation, so no fielded system exists even for the simplest injection step.

tasks.label: Purchase and stock supplies of feed and medicines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small breeder (dog/cat kennel, small horse or goat operation) makes a supply run: drives a pickup to the farm/feed store or co-op, selects 40–50 lb sacks of feed, mineral, litter and OTC meds, loads a cart, checks out, loads the truck, drives home, then unloads and stacks the sacks in a feed room, garage or barn aisle and puts vaccines in a refrigerator.

Farm or stable takes a scheduled supplier delivery: bulk feed augered/blown into an outdoor bin, or a flatbed drops pallets of sacked feed and mineral in the yard; the breeder checks weight/ticket, moves pallets or sacks with a tractor loader, hand truck or by hand into the barn feed room, restacks on pallets off the floor, and rotates older stock forward. Uneven ground, weather, livestock and dogs nearby.

Commercial breeding operation (large swine/poultry breeder unit, big boarding-and-breeding kennel) receives palletized feed, bedding and veterinary supplies at a dock or dedicated receiving door; a worker moves pallets with a pallet jack, breaks cases onto shelves in a controlled feed/medicine room, refrigerates vaccines and semen-handling supplies, and logs lot numbers and expiry dates into an inventory system.

Medicine and biologics stocking: unpacking cooler-shipped parcels of vaccines, antibiotics, dewormers, syringes and AI supplies; verifying items against the packing slip, checking lot numbers and expiration dates, refrigerating cold-chain items, shelving the rest in a lockable medicine cabinet or farm office, and pulling and discarding expired product.

Inventory and ordering cycle: walking the feed room and bins to count bags and gauge levels, checking medicine stock against upcoming breeding/vaccination schedules, comparing prices with dealers or online vet suppliers, placing the order by phone/portal, and reconciling the delivery ticket and invoice against what actually arrived.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch mobile manipulator autonomously unloads cases from floor-loaded trailers and containers in DHL warehouses, in commercial multi-site deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving inbound freight. Stocking supplies of feed begins with unloading cases/sacks of comparable weight from a delivery vehicle into storage; box weight, stack geometry and required precision are comparable to handling 40-50 lb feed cases.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics' Stretch Available for Commercial Purchase
sources.claim: Stretch is commercially purchasable and handles varied case types weighing up to 50 pounds while maneuvering in trailers and warehouse spaces.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes payload and object variability relevant to feed sacks and cases of medicine cartons, which fall within the 50 lb class handled here.

sources.title: ProMat 2025: Fox Robotics releases FoxBot Mk3 with new capabilities - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot autonomous forklift picks, moves and loads/unloads pallets into and out of ... at warehouse docks; the installed fleet has moved millions of pallets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving palletized deliveries. Pallets of sacked feed and cases of veterinary supplies are handled with the same forklift motions, loads and tolerances as the warehouse pallets FoxBot moves.

sources.system: TWA Reach / Shared Autonomy Platform autonomous forklifts
sources.title: Holman Logistics announces autonomous forklift initiative with Third Wave Automation - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Third Wave Automation's autonomous forklifts perform inbound full-pallet movements, racking, and replenishment of empty locations in commercial warehouses, with one remote operator overseeing multiple trucks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: put-away of received goods to storage. Stocking a feed/medicine store room is the same receive-transport-store sequence with comparable pallet loads inside a human work facility.

sources.title: Amazon's new warehouse robot has a 'sense of touch' that could see it replace human workers | Live Science
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan Stow robot uses force sensing to place roughly three-quarters of item types into storage pods and has begun operations in Spokane and Hamburg fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing assorted small goods into storage locations, comparable to shelving cartons of syringes, dewormer and vaccine boxes; the pods are purpose-built robot storage, so it supports machine-structured storage rather than as-found shelving.

sources.system: Robotic bag palletizer (ABB/Yaskawa-based bag palletizing cells)
sources.title: Robotic Pallet Stacker for 50lb. Bags on 2 Pallets - Tinsley Company
sources.claim: Guarded robotic palletizing cells routinely stack 50 lb bags of livestock feed minerals and supplements onto pallets in feed and pet-food packaging operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stacking sacked feed. The objects are literally 50 lb livestock feed/mineral bags and the output is a stable stored stack, matching the stocking step when bags are presented on a conveyor in a fenced cell.

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax / EasyLoad automated stockroom
sources.title: The new generation of fully automatic storage: BD Rowa EasyLoad
sources.claim: BD Rowa automated pharmacy storage systems accept incoming medicine packs at an input station and store them fully automatically, with cameras reading barcodes and expiry dates; refrigerated articles are supported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stocking medicines into storage with lot/expiry capture, the same operation a breeder performs with vaccines and drugs; storage shelving is purpose-built for the machine rather than ordinary human shelving.

sources.title: These retail robots travel through store aisles, scanning shelves for inventory and insights - Fast Company
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robots autonomously traverse store aisles, scanning shelf and pallet stock levels to drive replenishment, deployed in roughly a thousand stores including BJ's Wholesale clubs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical stock-level auditing that triggers reordering, the physical half of the breeder's inventory-and-purchase cycle, over comparable shelved cases and pallet stacks.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously delivers medications and supplies through hospital corridors, with over a million deliveries across 25+ US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving medications and supplies through a human-built facility to their storage point; shows autonomous in-facility logistics of drug shipments, though not unpacking or shelving them.

sources.system: Lely Vector feed kitchen / feed grabber
sources.title: Feed kitchen and multiple loading solutions | Lely
sources.claim: Lely's Vector system uses an overhead crane-mounted feed grabber in a purpose-built farm 'feed kitchen' to pick stored feed and load the mixing robot automatically, at commercial dairies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling stored bulk feed on a livestock farm; shows autonomous farm feed handling only inside a purpose-built feed storage area built around the machine, not in an as-found barn or yard.

sources.title: Burro Launches Grande 44, Its Most Powerful Autonomous Work Platform
sources.claim: Burro's autonomous outdoor carts move materials across nurseries, vineyards and farms at scale, but loads are placed on and taken off the machine by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor farm material transport. It shows autonomous hauling exists outdoors, but no manipulation: unloading a feed delivery and stacking sacks in a barn is still done by people, so it cannot support an E3 stocking judgment.

tasks.label: Select animals to be bred, and semen specimens to be used, according to knowledge of animals, genealogies, traits, and desired offspring characteristics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine animals to detect symptoms of illness or injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy-type cattle breeder/seedstock dairy operation: routine health check of the milking herd in a freestall barn or parlor - watching for mastitis, off-feed cows, lameness, metabolic disease and injuries, with hands-on checks of suspect cows in headlocks.

Beef cattle, sheep/goat and horse breeding operations: daily walk or drive through drylots, corrals, paddocks, pastures and foaling/lambing stalls observing breeding stock, dams and newborns for gait problems, wounds, bloat, scours, colic or dystocia, then catching a suspect animal in a chute or on a halter for hands-on exam (temperature, udder, hoof, eyes).

Dog or cat breeder in a home-based kennel/cattery: examining sires, dams and neonatal litters - weighing puppies/kittens, checking eyes, ears, skin, umbilicus, palate, hydration and nursing, and monitoring the dam during and after whelping/queening in a house, garage or converted outbuilding.

Poultry breeder-flock producer: walking a breeder or brooding house at least daily to spot sick, lame, injured or dead birds among thousands, picking up individuals to check vent, feet, keel and feathering, and flagging birds for culling.

Swine breeding-herd producer: walking gestation and farrowing rooms in a confinement barn to spot lame or off-feed sows, shoulder sores, prolapses, and scouring or crushed piglets, handling piglets to assess condition.

Rabbit, rodent, laboratory-animal or specialty small-stock breeder (also game birds, reptiles): cage-by-cage inspection of racked or hutched stock in an indoor facility, lifting animals to check eyes, teeth, ears, feet, weight and sores.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities (Computers and Electronics in Agriculture)
sources.claim: Scout (formerly ChickenBoy, Faromatics) is an autonomous ceiling-rail robot in poultry houses whose product specifications include detecting sick and dead birds, imaging for leg health, and identifying wet litter and faulty drinkers, without contacting the birds.

sources.title: A robot that watches over and analyzes broiler houses | WATTAgNet
sources.claim: The ChickenBoy robot is a commercially installed product travelling ceiling rails in working broiler houses, making round-the-clock observations that include mortality detection and event-triggered photos such as when it sees a dead bird.

sources.system: Lely Astronaut A5 with MQC / MQC-C
sources.title: Milk quality - Lely Astronaut A5
sources.claim: The Lely Astronaut A5 robotic milking station, which cows voluntarily enter, automatically analyses each cow's milk and measures somatic cell count to flag mastitis before visible symptoms appear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic milking. It transfers to examining cattle for illness because the same robot that handles the cow performs the per-cow health measurement (udder inflammation, abnormal milk, yield/weight deviation) that constitutes the routine dairy illness screen on an animal presented to the machine.

sources.system: DeLaval VMS V310/V350 with Milk Cell Analysis (MCA)
sources.title: DeLaval unveils faster, smarter, bigger milking robot model
sources.claim: DeLaval's VMS robotic milking system offers an on-board optical biosensor that monitors udder health and detects subclinical mastitis automatically during robotic milking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic milking of cows presented in a purpose-built box; its health-detection output (subclinical mastitis alerts) is the illness-detection step this task requires for lactating cattle.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: Meet SwagBot, the AI-powered robot cattle herder preventing soil degradation
sources.claim: SwagBot is an autonomous field robot ... traverses pasture and is reported to monitor pasture condition and livestock health, but it remains a university research prototype without validated per-animal illness or injury diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pasture herding and monitoring. Cited to show the state of the art for extensive livestock; it does not substantiate individual-animal examination for illness or injury.

sources.system: Pig-house inspection robots (rail-mounted and mobile, incl. Farm Watcher-type systems)
sources.title: Research Progress of Robotic Technologies and Applications in Smart Pig Farms (Agriculture, MDPI)
sources.claim: Reviews of pig-farm robotics describe autonomous rail-mounted and mobile inspection robots using thermal imaging and AI vision for health monitoring, but the reported work is research-stage behaviour and temperature monitoring rather than validated examination of breeding stock for illness and injury.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous barn inspection. Cited as the closest system to swine health examination; the review reports inspection/monitoring functions, not accepted-quality detection of illness and injury in sows and piglets.

tasks.label: Build hutches, pens, and fenced yards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal breeder builds a hutch, cage bank, coop, nest box or whelping box in the farm shop or barn alley: measures and cuts dimensional lumber and plywood, cuts and clips welded wire mesh, nails/screws the frame, fits a hinged door, latch, legs and roof, sized to the breeder's own layout.

Livestock, hog, horse or dog breeder erects pens, stalls, sorting pens or kennel runs inside a barn or kennel building: cuts and welds or bolts tubular steel panels and gates, sets posts against walls and concrete, hangs and levels gates and latches.

Breeder erects a permanent fenced yard, paddock, corral or outdoor run: lays out the line over sloping, rocky or muddy ground, digs or drives corner and line posts, builds brace assemblies, stretches woven-wire/high-tensile/board fencing, staples or clips it, and hangs gates.

Breeder sets temporary or portable fencing to make a turnout yard or subdivide a paddock: treads in or drives stakes, unrolls polywire/electric netting or drags portable panels into position, tensions and connects to an energizer, and forms a gateway.

Breeder repairs or modifies existing housing and fencing in place: replaces a rotten board or chewed-out wire panel on a hutch, re-stretches sagging wire, resets a leaning post, re-hangs a dragging gate, patches a dig-out under a run, working in whatever condition and weather the structure is found.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor Robotic System (robotic sheathing / robotic sub-assembly)
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic cells autonomously square, assemble, sheath, nail/screw and trim timber frame elements inside a fixtured production cell; sold commercially to offsite-construction factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic timber-frame panel manufacture. A wooden hutch, coop or whelping box is the same class of work — dimensional lumber and sheet goods positioned, cut and nailed into a framed, sheathed structure — performed here on fixtured stock at tighter tolerance than farm carpentry.

sources.system: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ F-500 framing station (HOMAG line at JL Schwieters Construction, Hugo, MN)
sources.title: The Next Step Into Automated Off-Site Construction in the US | HOMAG

tasks.label: Record animal characteristics such as weights, growth patterns, and diets.

Dairy (or dairy goat) breeder records cow and replacement-heifer body weights, growth curves and individual concentrate/milk-replacer intake in the freestall barn and calf-rearing pens, for use in sire selection and culling decisions.

Swine breeder records sow body weight and individual gestation/lactation feed intake in the gestation and farrowing barns, plus piglet birth weights, litter weights and weaning weights of the pedigree lines.

Poultry (or rabbit) breeder records weekly body weights of pedigree/parent-stock birds and daily feed consumption in an enclosed breeder house, tracking flock uniformity and growth against the breed standard curve.

Dog or cat breeder in a home-based kennel/cattery weighs each newborn puppy or kitten on a gram scale one to two times a day, logs the growth chart, notes which are nursing or need supplemental feeding, and keeps adult weight and diet records.

Horse breeder records foal and broodmare weights (livestock scale or weight tape), height/growth measurements, body condition scores and grain/forage ration amounts in the stable and paddocks of a breeding farm.

tasks.label: Brand, tattoo, or tag animals to allow animal identification.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beef cow-calf / seedstock operation: newborn calves tagged within a day of birth in a calving pasture, drylot or calving pen. Worker catches or corners the calf while the protective dam is nearby, applies a numbered visual tag (often plus an EID button) with hand pliers, sometimes a second tag or a birth-weight/BQA record, in mud, snow or heat.

Registered beef or dairy cattle processed through a corral and working chute: animal restrained in a headgate/squeeze, worker applies EID and visual ear tags, and applies the breed-association ear tattoo (digit pliers, green ink, ear cleaned and rubbed) to weanlings, heifers or bulls, verifying the number against the registration paperwork.

Branding day / horse or cattle identification marking: hot-iron brand or freeze brand applied to hip, rib or shoulder while the animal is held in a squeeze chute, calf table or hydraulic chute; iron heat, hold time and placement judged by the worker; hair clipped for freeze branding.

Dog, cat or rabbit breeder: puppies, kittens or kits identified in a whelping room or rabbitry (often home-based or a small kennel). Worker hand-restrains the animal, applies an ear or inner-flank tattoo with pliers/pen or a numbered rabbit ear tattoo, and/or implants a microchip with a needle applicator, then records the ID against the litter/pedigree.

Swine, sheep and goat breeding stock: piglets ear-notched and/or tagged in farrowing crates while the sow is present; replacement gilts tattooed; sheep and goats given scrapie/flock ID tags and ear tattoos in a race, tilt table or handling chute in the barn.

Poultry breeder / pedigree hatchery: day-old or young chicks wing-banded or leg-banded and toe-punched for pedigree lines; adult breeders leg-banded in the breeder house. Small, fragile birds handled one at a time at a processing table or in the house.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized identification-marking of live animals. It is the only deployed system found that marks live animals without human handling, but transfer to this task fails: the objects (small fish delivered head-first in a water flume) and the actuators (fin excision, snout wire injection) do not carry over to piercing a calf's, piglet's or puppy's ear with a tag or tattoo applicator on a restrained mammal.

tasks.label: Bathe and groom animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dog breeder bathes an adult breeding dog in the kennel's wash room: lifts dog into a raised tub or walk-in shower, wets coat, shampoos and conditions, rinses to the skin, then towels and force-dries. Dog is on a leash/loop restraint and moves during the process.

Full grooming of a breeding dog or cat before a show, sale, or photo: line-brushing and de-matting the coat, combing furnishings, clipper/scissor work on feet, face and sanitary areas, nail clipping or grinding, ear cleaning and plucking, expressing anal glands. Performed on a grooming table with a live, sometimes squirmy animal.

Horse breeder grooms a broodmare, stallion or foal in crossties or a wash stall: currying, stiff- and soft-brushing the body, detangling mane and tail, picking out four hooves, wiping face/eyes, plus a full soap bath with hose and sweat scraper in warm weather. Animal is loose-tied and can move or shy.

Livestock breeder preps show or sale cattle, sheep or hogs at the farm wash rack: soaking and soaping the hide/fleece with a hose, scrubbing, rinsing, blow-drying, then clipping and fitting the coat with body clippers while the animal stands in a chute or is tied to a blocking chute.

Routine coat/hide maintenance of housed breeding cattle in the barn: keeping hides clean and free of caked dirt, loose hair and external parasites through regular brushing of the herd between milkings or feedings.

Bathing and cleaning of neonates and small stock: rinsing soiled puppies or kittens in a utility sink, spot-cleaning a whelping bitch or a scoured calf, bathing rabbits or small ruminants, drying and combing them afterward. Delicate, chilled-prone animals requiring hand support throughout.

tasks.label: Adjust controls to maintain specific building temperatures required for animals' health and safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial poultry breeder/pullet house (broiler-breeder or layer-breeder flock): worker sets and re-adjusts the house target temperature as birds age and weather shifts, staging exhaust and tunnel fans, air inlets, cool cells, curtains and brooder/space heaters to hold target within a couple of degrees day and night, and responds to high/low temperature alarms.

Swine breeding/gestation/farrowing barn: worker adjusts room setpoints and ventilation stages for sows while holding a much warmer micro-climate for newborn piglets (creep heat lamps, heat mats), changing settings as litters age and as outside temperature swings; failure chills piglets or heat-stresses sows.

Cattle or equine breeding/calving/foaling barn or calf barn, often older and naturally ventilated: worker raises or lowers side curtains and vents, switches circulation/tunnel fans and soakers on or off, opens doors, and turns on tube or radiant heaters in cold snaps to keep the barn in a safe range.

Purpose-built commercial kennel, cattery or rabbitry building on the breeder's premises: worker sets HVAC/zone thermostats, exhaust fan and inlet controls, and radiant/underfloor heat in whelping and nursery rooms, holding warmer temperatures for neonates than for adult stock.

Home-based small breeder (dogs, cats, reptiles, birds) whelping or brooding in a spare room, basement, garage or converted outbuilding taken as found: worker turns up the house thermostat, plugs in and dials space heaters, positions heat lamps/heat mats over the whelping box or rack, and cracks a window or runs a fan when it gets too warm.

tasks.label: Inject prepared animal semen into female animals for breeding purposes, by inserting nozzle of syringe into vagina and depressing syringe plunger.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy cow AI: cow restrained in a headlock or palpation rail in a freestall barn; technician thaws/loads a straw, inserts one arm rectally to grasp and manipulate the cervix, threads the AI gun through the cervical rings and deposits semen in the uterine body, then records the breeding.

Beef cow/heifer fixed-time AI: 40-100 synchronized females run through a squeeze chute or AI barn at a ranch working facility (often outdoors, dusty or muddy, variable animal size and temperament); each animal inseminated rectovaginally in sequence under time pressure.

Swine AI: sow or gilt in a gestation stall/pen with boar exposure for standing reflex; technician wipes the vulva, inserts a spirette/foam catheter, locks it into the cervix and delivers a semen dose from a bottle or bag (often post-cervical catheter for intrauterine deposition), repeated for dozens of sows.

Equine AI: mare restrained in stocks in a breeding shed; tail wrapped, perineum washed, technician guides an insemination pipette by gloved hand through the cervix and deposits extended/frozen semen into the uterine body, timed to ultrasound-monitored ovulation.

Poultry breeder AI (turkey/broiler breeder hens): hens caught and held by a handler on a bench, cloaca everted, a straw or tube inserted into the vagina and a metered semen dose deposited; hundreds of hens per hour on a repeating weekly cycle in a breeder house.

Small-animal / small-flock AI: dog, goat or ewe inseminated vaginally with a syringe and flexible catheter at a breeder's kennel, home whelping room or small barn; single animal, improvised restraint by an assistant, non-standard layout.

sources.system: Lely Astronaut A5 / A5 Next robotic milking system
sources.title: Automatic Milking Robot | Lely Astronaut A5 Next
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial robot working on live dairy cows autonomously locates teats with laser/camera sensing and attaches milking cups in the barn; more than 50,000 units are installed worldwide. It performs no reproductive-tract procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of live cattle anatomy (teat-cup attachment) in a farm barn. Transfer to insemination fails: teats are externally visible and superficially grasped, whereas AI requires blind, tactile intra-rectal manipulation of the cervix and threading a gun through several cervical rings, which no cited system does.
