tasks.label: Clip or shear hair on animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shearing the fiber flock (sheep, alpacas, angora goats) on a breeding operation: animals caught from a pen, set up or restrained on a shearing floor/stand in a barn or shearing shed, full fleece removed with a handpiece in a few minutes per animal without cutting skin, fleece kept intact for grading; dozens of animals in a session.

Clipping/fitting breeding stock for shows, sales, and sale photos (beef and dairy cattle, sheep, goats): animal restrained in a grooming chute or tied in a barn aisle, body clipped with several blade lengths, head, tailhead, topline and legs blended and detailed to breed-standard appearance.

Clipping dogs (and occasionally cats) in a breeding kennel: sanitary trims around vulva/hindquarters before breeding and whelping, belly/udder area clipped before whelping, mat removal and coat tidying on a grooming table with a wriggling, sometimes anxious animal.

Clipping hair to prep for breeding/veterinary procedures on livestock: shaving the flank/paralumbar area for ultrasound or surgery, clipping around the vulva and tailhead before AI or embryo transfer, clipping udders and tails on cows and preputial hair on bulls; animal in a headgate, chute, or stanchion.

Clipping horses on a breeding farm: bridle path, muzzle, ears, fetlocks, clipping the tail area and udder region of broodmares before foaling, and winter body clips; horse held on cross-ties or by a handler in a barn aisle, wash rack, or outside in a yard, animal may fidget or spook.

Boar stud (swine AI): diluted ejaculate split into 45-100 mL doses in bags, bottles or tubes, each labeled with boar ID, dose sperm number and collection/expiry date; concentration from photometer or CASA logged to the stud's lab software; hundreds of doses per collection day in a stud laboratory.

Equine fresh-cooled semen at a stallion station or vet repro clinic: one to a few extended doses per collection loaded into a bag, tube or syringe, hand-labeled with stallion name/date, motility and concentration written on the accompanying breeding certificate, then placed in an insulated shipper for overnight delivery.

Frozen straw production for equine, ovine or caprine at a small stud or clinic lab: extended semen packaged into a few dozen to a few hundred 0.25/0.5 mL straws, printed or color-coded with donor ID and date, sealed and frozen, with quality data recorded in the herd/stud record.

Canine semen at a reproduction clinic or kennel: very small volume (a few mL) chilled or frozen, packaged into 0.5 mL straws or vials, labeled with dog registration/ID and date, motility and concentration recorded on the freeze certificate and clinic record.

Poultry (turkey/broiler breeder) on-farm collection room: pooled semen extended and drawn into insemination tubes/straws for near-immediate use, batch tagged by house/male line and date, concentration checked with a poultry densimeter and logged; work done in the collection room next to the breeder house.

tasks.label: Exhibit animals at shows.

instances.label: Livestock show ring at a county/state fair or breed show: breeder leads a haltered beef or dairy animal (or drives a hog with a whip/cane, braces a lamb) into the ring, sets the animal's feet with a show stick, keeps it calm and posed among other animals and a crowd, tracks the judge's position and follows verbal/hand directions to move, turn, and re-set for placings.

AKC/UKC conformation dog show ring: handler gaits the dog on a loose lead at the correct speed in patterns (down-and-back, triangle), free-stacks or hand-stacks the dog, uses bait and grooming touch-ups to hold expression, and presents the dog to a judge who runs hands over it and checks bite/testicles.

Show-day preparation in the barn or grooming area at the grounds: washing, blow-drying, clipping/shearing to breed style, fitting hair with adhesives and combs, hoof and leg trimming, brushing/scissoring coats, oiling or powdering, and last-minute touch-ups on a restless live animal before entering the ring.

Small-animal show hall (cats, rabbits, cavies, poultry): breeder cages the entries in benching, carries individual animals to the judging table or coop on the judge's call, poses/hands over the animal, returns it, and monitors animals for stress and health through the day.

Getting animals to and from the show: catching and loading them from a home farm chute/pen into a trailer, hauling, unloading at the grounds, bedding and setting up stalls or tie-outs, and hand-feeding/watering show-fit animals between classes.

Swine breeding facility: in the on-farm or boar-stud semen lab, measure extended semen into per-sow doses (60-90 mL tubes/bags or a syringe/catheter set) at the specified sperm concentration, seal and label, then present the loaded dose/catheter for insemination.

Poultry (turkey/broiler breeder) house: an AI crew member repeatedly draws micro-doses (0.025-0.05 mL) of pooled, extended semen into a calibrated syringe or poultry straw and loads it into the volumetric insemination gun, hundreds of times per hour on a strict time limit after collection.

Bull stud / boar stud semen processing lab: after extension to a target concentration, measure and package the ejaculate into individual straws or dose containers of exact volume, sealed and identified, for freezing or shipping.

Dog / small-ruminant breeder or mobile technician at a kennel, client farm or private premises: draw a fresh or chilled semen dose into a calibrated syringe, attach it to the insemination catheter/gun, working on whatever table or floor space is available.

tasks.label: Examine semen microscopically to assess and record density and motility of gametes, and dilute semen with prescribed diluents, according to formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial boar or bull stud production lab: raw ejaculates arrive from the collection room in filtered bottles; the technician subsamples each, measures sperm concentration and motility on a CASA/photometer, records per-ejaculate results in the lab database, computes extender volume from the dose formula, and dilutes the whole ejaculate with pre-warmed extender. Dozens of ejaculates per shift, strict time and temperature limits.

Equine breeding farm laboratory: stallion collected into an AV; gel-free semen is measured for volume, a drop examined under a phase-contrast microscope (or CASA/NucleoCounter) for motility and concentration, results logged on the stallion's record, and the semen extended to the required sperm-per-dose concentration for cooled shipping the same day. A few ejaculates per day, stallion-to-stallion variability.

Small livestock producer (sheep, goat, beef cattle) running an on-farm AI or collection program: portable microscope or handheld analyzer set up in a barn office, trailer or lambing shed; checks gross and progressive motility and rough concentration of fresh or thawed semen, notes it on a paper/app record, and dilutes with a commercial extender per the label formula. Dust, variable temperature and lighting.

Dog (or cat) breeder collecting a stud: semen examined right after collection under a bench microscope in the kennel room or home office, motility estimated and concentration counted with a hemocytometer or chamber, values written into the stud's breeding record, then extended with canine extender for chilled shipment or freezing. Small volumes, one dog at a time.

Poultry/turkey breeder operation: semen collected from many toms/roosters and pooled; small, viscous, time-critical volumes are checked for motility and concentration in a small on-site processing room and diluted with poultry extender at a prescribed ratio before immediate insemination of hens.

sources.title: AndroVision eFlow: Setting higher standards in precision semen analysis
sources.claim: Commercial CASA system with a flow chamber that fills itself with the ejaculate sample, measures sperm concentration and motility automatically, records the result and flushes itself for the next ejaculate, removing manual pipetting into a counting chamber; installed on the bench in boar-stud production labs.

roles.title: Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products
roles.description: Grade, sort, or classify unprocessed food and other agricultural products by size, weight, color, or condition.

tasks.label: Place products in containers according to grade and mark grades on containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fresh-fruit packinghouse (apples, citrus, stone fruit, avocados, table grapes): worker at a grade lane on the packing line takes fruit already sized/graded, places it into trays, cartons, bags or clamshells for that grade, and applies or stamps the grade/size/count marking on the carton. Indoor, fixed line, high volume.

Vegetable/root packing shed (potatoes, onions, carrots, tomatoes, sweet potatoes): worker takes product off a grading table or belt, discards off-grade, fills poly bags, totes or boxes by grade/size, and marks the bag or box with grade/size/lot. Dusty but fixed indoor layout, standard equipment.

Egg grading and packing plant: eggs candled/graded for weight class and quality, placed into consumer cartons or 30-egg flats for that grade, cartons marked with grade (e.g., Grade A Large), pack date and lot code. Highly standardized indoor plant.

Poultry/meat/seafood plant grading station: worker grades and size/weight-classes fillets, parts, shrimp or fish, places them into trays, combos or boxes for the corresponding grade, and labels or stamps the container with grade/weight/lot. Cold, wet, indoor, institution-controlled plant.

In-field pack crew (lettuce, melons, broccoli, berries): crew grades product at a field cart or ground station, packs cartons/clamshells by grade, and stamps or labels the carton with grade and lot; uneven ground, dust, wind, sun, layout changes block to block.

Small/diversified operation (small farm packing barn, farm-stand or CSA shed, nursery/greenhouse): mixed crops and cull standards on the same shift, heterogeneous containers (baskets, waxed boxes, buckets, reused crates), grade written or stamped by hand on the container; layout ad hoc and changes daily.

tasks.label: Weigh products or estimate their weight, visually or by feel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fresh-produce packinghouse grading/sizing line (apples, citrus, potatoes, onions, tomatoes): worker at the roller table or sizer picks up individual items, judges size/weight by eye and hand, and diverts undersize/oversize or off-weight product; checks pack weights against the size class. High throughput, wet, fixed line layout.

Hand-pack-to-target-weight station in a packhouse: worker fills punnets, clamshells, mesh bags or trays with grapes, cherry tomatoes, berries or beans, judging weight by feel while placing product and confirming/topping off on a bench scale so each pack meets declared net weight.

Meat, poultry or seafood processing plant: worker weighs and weight-classes whole birds, carcass parts, fillets or portions on shackle-line or bench scales, sorting into weight bands and catch-weight batches for orders; chilled, wet, sanitary plant.

Egg grading and packing facility: eggs classed into weight grades (small/medium/large/XL) and packed accordingly; worker weighs/estimates and pulls off eggs that do not fit the declared weight class, and checks carton weights.

In-field/orchard at harvest: worker weighs picked lugs, bags, buckets or field bins on a portable platform scale at the row end or on a harvest trailer, judges whether containers are filled to the required weight, and estimates lot weights for piece-rate payment and load records; uneven ground, dust, variable weather.

Receiving/QC bench at a warehouse or receiving station (nuts, dry beans, potatoes, hops, tobacco): worker draws a sample from an incoming load, weighs the sample and its defect/tare fractions on a bench scale, and records the weight-based grade for the lot.

tasks.label: Discard inferior or defective products or foreign matter, and place acceptable products in containers for further processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fresh-produce packinghouse grading line (apples, citrus, pears, potatoes, onions, mature-green tomatoes). Worker stands at a moving belt/roller table, pulls out bruised, rotten, sunburned or misshapen fruit plus stems, leaves, dirt clods and stones, and places acceptable fruit into trays, cartons or bins for further processing. Indoor, lit, institution-run packhouse; product arrives from bin tippers in continuous flow.

Processing-plant bulk-flow inspection station (nuts, dried fruit, IQF/frozen vegetables, potato strips, fresh-cut salad). Worker picks defective pieces and foreign material (rocks, wood, plastic, insects, extraneous vegetative matter) off a high-speed belt; accepted product continues to filling/packing. Wet, cold or dusty plant floor, high line speed, food-safety scrutiny.

Small-fruit packhouse grading and container filling (blueberries, cherries, strawberries, cranberries). Worker removes soft, split, decayed, undersized or stemmed fruit and fills punnets/clamshells to weight for further processing. Very delicate product, high piece counts, gentle handling required.

Bench/table hand-packing of delicate vine produce (table grapes, vine tomatoes, some mushrooms) in a packhouse. Worker inspects bunches, snips out defective berries/trims to weight, discards culls, and places acceptable produce into punnets or clamshells at a human workstation alongside other packers, with product delivered in crates or on a shared conveyor.

Field/harvest-side grading: worker rides a potato/onion/carrot harvester or field-loading rig picking out clods, stones, rot and vines, or works a field-pack crew for lettuce, melons or broccoli, discarding culls and placing acceptable product into field bins/cartons. Outdoors, dust, mud, variable light and weather, layout changes field to field.

Animal-product and specialty-agricultural grading: egg packing station (candling/culling cracked, dirty, leaking eggs and packing good ones into cartons), poultry/fish portion grading into trays, or nursery/horticulture sheds sorting young plants, cuttings and flower bulbs, discarding diseased or off-grade stock into cull bins and good stock into trays.

tasks.label: Grade and sort products according to factors such as color, species, length, width, appearance, feel, smell, and quality to ensure correct processing and usage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tree-fruit packinghouse grading line: worker stands at a roller/belt conveyor in a packing shed as apples, citrus, pears or stone fruit flow past; pulls culls (bruises, rots, insect damage, misshapen fruit), separates by color/blush and size class, routes fruit to grade lanes. Fruit arrives from field bins via dump/flume; indoor, lit, fixed layout, employer sets grade standards.

Vegetable packing shed / farm intake line: worker sorts potatoes, onions, carrots, peppers or leafy product on a grading table or belt, removing rot, green skin, mechanical damage, off-size, clods, stones, plastic and other foreign material before washing/sizing/bagging. Dusty, wet, cool indoor facility with standard line equipment.

Egg grading plant plus nut/dried-fruit/grain plant sorting: candling and grading shell eggs (cracks, dirt, blood spots, weight class) on a grader; or inspecting almonds, pecans, dried fruit, beans and grain on a belt for shell, discoloration, insect damage and foreign material. High-throughput, hygienic indoor plant.

In-field harvest-crew sorting on a machine platform or field pack station: riding a processing-tomato harvester or a melon/leafy-greens rig, pulling green, rotten or blemished fruit, vines, clods and rocks off a moving belt; or grading and packing melons/lettuce at a field-side station. Dust, vibration, heat, glare, variable crop.

Potato/root-crop clod, stone and defect sorting at harvest and farm-yard intake: worker on a harvester's or intake elevator's picking table separating soil clods, stones, wood, plastic, haulm and rotten or damaged tubers from unwashed crop under wet, muddy, variable lifting conditions.

Specialty grading by feel, smell, species and dimension: sorting whole fish/shellfish by species and size at a dock or seafood plant; grading cut flowers, bulbs and nursery stock by stem length, thickness and bloom quality; hand-grading tobacco leaf by color, texture and aroma. Indoor facility or covered dock, institution-controlled.

tasks.label: Load and unload crops or containers of materials, manually or using conveyors, handtrucks, forklifts, or transfer augers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grain/silage harvest: running a tractor and grain cart (or a chase truck) alongside a moving combine or forage harvester in an open field, positioning under the unloading spout and taking on the load on the go over uneven, dusty ground, then hauling the full cart to the field edge.

Bulk transfer with augers and conveyors: unloading grain carts, hopper wagons and trucks into waiting semis at the field edge, and into dump pits, bins and dryers at the farmstead bin site; spotting and positioning portable augers/conveyors, engaging PTO, watching fill and flow, shutting down and cleaning up spillage. Settings range from a muddy field edge to a farm bin site.

Forklift/telehandler work around the farm shop, packing shed, warehouse or dock: unloading pallets of seed, chemical, packaging and parts off delivery trailers, moving bulk bags and totes, and loading finished pallets onto trucks on level surfaces with standard pallets.

Orchard/vegetable harvest: picking up filled harvest bins and pallet loads from between rows or field turn-rows with a forklift, bin trailer or loader and loading them onto trucks/trailers on uneven ground while a hand crew works nearby.

Hand loading and unloading of loose containers in the field: crates, lugs, sacks, feed bags and bulk items such as melons or pumpkins thrown or stacked onto trailers and trucks, mixed sizes, no fixed presentation.
Hay and straw: loading small square or large round bales onto wagons, flatbeds and trucks in the field with a loader, bale spear or by hand, then unloading and stacking them in a barn or stackyard.

tasks.label: Mix specified materials or chemicals, and dump solutions, powders, or seeds into planter or sprayer machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Row-crop farm: operator batches a 1,000+ gal herbicide/fungicide tank mix at the farmstead chemical loading pad or parked nurse/tender trailer — meters water or UAN carrier, measures 2-6 products from 2.5-gal jugs and mini-bulk shuttles, inducts them, triple-rinses containers, agitates, and pumps the finished solution into the self-propelled sprayer.

Same tank-mix batching and sprayer loading done at the field edge: nurse trailer parked on a headland or gravel field entrance, uneven muddy ground, wind and dust, no fixed layout, product jugs stacked on the trailer deck.

tasks.label: Observe and listen to machinery operation to detect equipment malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Row-crop field work: operator runs a tractor with a tillage tool, planter, air seeder or sprayer across open fields, continuously watching gauges/monitors and listening and feeling for engine, driveline, hydraulic or implement trouble (plugged row unit, sheared bolt, hydraulic leak, dragging shank), stopping the outfit before damage occurs. Dust, engine noise, uneven terrain.

Grain harvest: operator runs a combine (or forage harvester) at load, listening for changes in rotor/cylinder sound, belt squeal, bearing whine, feeling vibration, watching loss monitors and header for plugging, slugging or a broken auger flight; must catch trouble within seconds in a dusty, loud field environment.

Hay and forage operations: operator runs mower-conditioner, rake and baler, listening for knotter misses, pickup tine or belt failure, bearing squeal, plug-ups and net-wrap faults; frequent stop-and-inspect cycles in open hay fields.

Stationary post-harvest equipment at a farmstead, elevator, gin or processing shed: operator runs grain dryers, elevator legs, augers, conveyors, huskers/shellers/threshers or gin stands, listening for bearing noise, belt slip, out-of-balance vibration, plugging and smelling for hot bearings during a run.

Orchard/vineyard equipment: operator runs an airblast sprayer, mower or nut shaker/sweeper down tree or vine rows, watching pump pressure and nozzles and listening for PTO, fan or shaker-head trouble in dusty, tight rows.

Livestock facility machinery: operator runs TMR mixer/feed wagons, feed augers, manure pumps, scrapers and skid steers in and around barns and feedlots, listening for gearbox, chain, auger or pump malfunctions while feeding or cleaning.

tasks.label: Manipulate controls to set, activate, and adjust mechanisms on machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Row-crop field operation with a large tractor and implement (tillage, seedbed prep, planting, or ground spraying): operator engages hydraulics/PTO, sets and trims implement depth or down-force, activates section/rate control, raises and lowers the implement at headlands, and adjusts settings on the go as soil, residue and moisture change across an open field.

Combine harvesting a grain field: operator engages header and separator, sets header height/reel speed, sets and continually re-adjusts rotor speed, fan speed, concave and sieve clearances for grain loss and cracking, and activates the unloading auger to a grain cart on the go, in dusty, variable-terrain open fields.

Hay mowing and raking: operator engages PTO and lowers/raises the mower-conditioner or rake, sets cutting height, roll tension and windrow width, and adjusts on the go for stand thickness and terrain in an open hay field.

Baling in the field: operator sets bale size, density, twine/net-wrap cycle and moisture/preservative settings, feeds the windrow at the right rate, and activates tie/wrap and bale ejection each cycle, adjusting for windrow variation and hay moisture.

Livestock feeding and manure handling around barns and lots: operating a TMR mixer/feed wagon or feed truck (setting load weights, engaging mixer/auger/conveyor, dispensing along the feed alley), pushing up feed, and running barn scrapers or manure handling equipment inside a farm-controlled facility.

Orchard/vineyard machinery: setting up and running an air-blast sprayer or between-row mower on a narrow tractor — engaging PTO, setting fan speed, boom/nozzle sections and application rate, and adjusting through dense canopy rows on dusty, uneven ground.

Stationary post-harvest equipment at a farmstead or processing site: setting and adjusting grain dryer temperature and discharge rate to hit target moisture, starting/stopping augers, legs and conveyors, and adjusting husker/sheller/gin-stand feed and cleaning mechanisms.

tasks.label: Operate or tend equipment used in agricultural production, such as tractors, combines, and irrigation equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field operations with a tractor and towed implement on open row-crop or forage ground: tillage/seedbed prep, planting, cultivating, spreading fertilizer, spraying, and mowing/raking hay. Operator drives to the field, sets implement depth/rate, works the field in passes with headland turns, watches for rocks, wet spots, wires and plugging, and refills seed/chemical. Weather, terrain and field layout vary.

Grain harvest: running a self-propelled combine through corn, soybeans, wheat or rice - setting header height, ground speed, rotor/sieve settings for loss and grain quality, handling downed or damp crop, and unloading on the go into a grain cart or truck run alongside.

Baling and bale handling: driving windrows with a round or large-square baler, stopping to tie/wrap and eject, monitoring bale shape and twine/net, then picking up, hauling and stacking bales with a loader, bale wagon or squeeze in the field and stackyard.

Orchard, vineyard and specialty-crop tractor work: air-blast and herbicide spraying, floor mowing, discing, and towing bins/trailers down planted rows with tight headlands, dust, canopy and overhead trellis wire.

Irrigation equipment: starting and tending pumps and center pivots, walking or driving lines to check nozzles and leaks, moving and coupling hand lines or wheel lines, laying and flushing drip tape, and towing pivots between fields; done on irrigated ground in changing conditions.
Feeding runs at a dairy or beef facility: loading and mixing the ration and delivering it to feed bunks in the barn on a fixed daily schedule, with feed pushed up between deliveries.

tasks.label: Adjust, repair, and service farm machinery and notify supervisors when machinery malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adjusting machine operating settings repeatedly during field work as crop, soil, moisture and terrain change: combine concave clearance, rotor and fan speed, chaffer/sieve openings, header height and reel position; planter depth and row-by-row downforce; sprayer boom height and rate. Done from the seat/monitor via the machine's own electrohydraulic actuators, in a dusty open field with the machine moving.

Hand-tool mechanical adjustment in the field or farmyard: tensioning a baler pickup or elevator chain, aligning sickle guards, setting row-cleaner and scraper positions, skid shoes on a mower, disc gang angle, knotter timing, swapping/spacing spray tips. Dirty, hot, awkward access on older or simpler implements.

Daily walk-around service before/after a shift: greasing 15-40 zerks with a grease gun, checking and topping engine oil, coolant and hydraulic fluid, blowing chaff and crop residue off radiator screens and out of the engine bay, cleaning or replacing the air filter, checking tire pressure and looking for leaks, cracks and wear.

Refuelling machines with diesel (and periodically topping DEF) once or twice per shift, at the farm's bulk fuel tank in the yard or from a service truck brought to the machine at the edge of the field.

Breakdown repair and scheduled shop service: replacing shear bolts, sickle sections, belts, chains, hydraulic hoses, bearings, planter discs and meters; unplugging a clogged header, baler or forage harvester; welding a broken bracket; oil-and-filter changes and pre-season overhaul in the farm shop.

Noticing a malfunction (warning light, monitor alarm, unusual noise or vibration, loss of performance), stopping to check the machine, and reporting the problem to the supervisor, farm manager or mechanic with enough description to get parts or help dispatched.

tasks.label: Attach farm implements such as plows, discs, sprayers, or harvesters to tractors, using bolts and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Farm yard or machine shed, firm surface: hooking a towed implement with no PTO (planter, grain drill, disc harrow, field cultivator, ripper, wagon, hydraulic-pump trailed sprayer) to the tractor drawbar — back up to the clevis, drop and clip the hitch pin, connect 2-6 hydraulic hoses to the right remotes, plug the light/ISOBUS harness, hook the safety chain, crank up the jack.

Farm yard: hooking a PTO-driven implement (round baler, mower-conditioner, grain cart, manure spreader, rotary cutter) — drawbar pin plus sliding the splined driveline yoke onto the tractor PTO stub, seating the locking collar, hooking the shield chain, then hoses and harness.

Farm yard: mounting a three-point-hitch implement (mounted sprayer, blade, box scraper, seeder, post driver) — align lower-link ends over the implement pins and secure with linch pins or a quick hitch, fit and adjust the top-link turnbuckle, set sway blocks, then connect PTO shaft and/or hydraulic hoses.

Field, headland or roadside during planting/harvest: re-hooking a towed implement left on uneven, rutted or muddy ground, parked at an odd angle with hitch height mismatched — jack cranking, prying/jockeying the tractor to line up, connecting hoses and harness, often in poor light or weather.

Farm shop or shed: bolt-up work with hand tools — changing plow bottoms/shares or cultivator sweeps, bolting on brackets, suitcase weights, drawbar/hitch swaps, boom sections or a loader subframe, using wrenches and impact tools to torque fasteners.

tasks.label: Load hoppers, containers, or conveyors to feed machines with products, using forklifts, transfer augers, suction gates, shovels, or pitchforks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refilling planting/application machine hoppers and tanks in the field: a tender truck augers bulk seed or dry fertilizer into a planter/air-seeder hopper, or the operator sets bulk seed boxes with a telehandler/forklift and tips them in; uneven headlands, wind and dust, varying box and hopper types, machine parked wherever it ran out.

Harvest-season grain movement at the bin site: unloading the grain cart or truck into a receiving pit or hopper, setting and running portable transfer augers/conveyors to fill bins and a dryer, opening hopper-bottom bin slide gates, switching spouts/distributors; outdoor farmyard, mud, dust, variable equipment placement.

Loading a TMR mixer wagon or tub grinder at a dairy or feedlot: a loader tractor/skid steer/telehandler takes silage from a bunker face, grabs hay or straw bales, and adds commodities from a bay, dumping each into the mixer hopper to a target weight; open feed yard, weather, livestock and staff nearby.

Feeding stationary post-harvest machines inside a packing/processing shed: forklifting field bins onto a dumper or tipping them into the wash-line/grader intake hopper, keeping a huller, sheller, gin feeder or bagging line's conveyor supplied; fixed indoor layout, standard bins and pallets, company-controlled premises.

Hand work with shovel or pitchfork: scooping spilled grain off the pit grate or drive back into the hopper, forking hay, silage or bedding into a feeder or chopper intake, and clearing a plugged auger or conveyor intake by hand; cramped, cluttered, one-off positions in the yard or barn.

Loading bulk materials into spreaders, bulk trailers, or conveyors in the farmyard: bucket-loading lime, dry fertilizer, compost, manure or bedding from a stockpile or shed into a spreader hopper or onto a feed conveyor, judging fill level and avoiding spillage; open yard, piles that change shape daily.

tasks.label: Direct and monitor the activities of work crews engaged in planting, weeding, or harvesting activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Operate towed machines such as seed drills or manure spreaders to plant, fertilize, dust, and spray crops.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Row-crop planting/drilling: operator pulls a planter or grain drill behind a tractor across open corn, soybean or small-grain fields; sets population, depth and down-force, runs guidance/section control, makes headland turns and point rows, monitors seed and starter-fertilizer levels, and refills from a tender; weather-limited planting window, residue, mud spots and terraces.

Broadacre crop spraying/liquid fertilizing: tractor with pull-type or three-point boom sprayer applying herbicide, fungicide, insecticide or liquid fertilizer over row crops, pasture or small grains; boom height and rate control, wind/drift judgement, tank fills at a nurse trailer, avoiding waterways, poles, tile risers.

Dry fertilizer, lime or cover-crop broadcast application with a pull-type spreader/air-flow cart; prescription rate maps, spread-pattern overlap, repeated hopper refills from a tender truck, fields with wet holes, ditches and irregular boundaries.

Manure/slurry application: solid box spreader or liquid tanker towed behind a tractor; loading at the pit or stack in the farmyard, transit on lanes and public roads between farmstead and field, spreading or injecting at rate across pasture or stubble, repeated load-haul-spread cycles.

Orchard/vineyard/permanent-crop spraying and dusting: narrow tractor pulling an air-blast sprayer or sulfur duster down tree or vine rows, dense canopy, dust, tight headlands, PTO-driven implement, night work, PPE and re-entry constraints.

Small, irregular, hilly or specialty-crop fields: short passes, point rows and odd shapes, older tractors and mounted/pull-behind drills, spreaders or sprayers on vegetable beds, hay ground and cover-crop acres; frequent implement changes and hitch-ups.

tasks.label: Weigh crop-filled containers, and record weights and other identifying information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grain/oilseed harvest: operator hauls a loaded grain cart or truck into a farm or elevator scale lane, positions the vehicle so all axles sit on the weighbridge, captures gross and tare weight, and records the load ticket data (grower, field, crop, moisture, destination bin). Institution-controlled scale house and yard, fixed lane layout.

In-field on-machine weighing during grain or forage harvest: grain cart, gravity wagon or forage trailer carries load-cell scales; every unload is weighed and the weight logged against field, truck and destination while the cart works alongside the combine on open, uneven harvest ground.

Fruit/vegetable field or orchard harvest: operator uses a tractor forklift or bin trailer to move filled 800-1,000 lb bins (or stacked totes) to a field-edge platform scale or weighs them on a loader scale, then records weight with grower, block, variety and lot on a tag or handheld. Dirt row ends, dust, varying terrain, crews working nearby.

Packinghouse or receiving station: incoming bins, totes and boxes are weighed on floor scales or in-line conveyor scales as they come off trucks, tare deducted, and weights plus lot/grower IDs recorded or printed onto labels for the grower settlement record. Fixed layout, standard containers, controlled premises.

Piece-rate hand containers: pickers bring buckets, lugs or hampers to a field checking station where each container is weighed and the weight credited to that worker's tally sheet or handheld app, then the container is stacked for haul-out. Temporary station at the field edge.

tasks.label: Walk beside or ride on planting machines while inserting plants in planter mechanisms at specified intervals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large commercial vegetable operation, prepared bare beds in an open field: worker rides a 4-6 row tractor-drawn carousel/cup transplanter, pulling plug seedlings (lettuce, broccoli, cabbage, celery, onions, leeks, processing tomato) from 128-288 cell trays and dropping one into each rotating cup at 40-90 plants/minute per row, all day in heat and dust, keeping spacing and stand count acceptable to the grower.

Plasticulture field: worker rides a waterwheel or punch-type setter over raised beds covered with plastic mulch and drip tape, inserting plug transplants (peppers, melons, tomatoes, strawberry plugs, hemp) into the punched holes or into the setter's perforating cups, with at-plant water applied.

Tobacco setter in Kentucky/Tennessee/North Carolina: 2-4 riders on a mechanical setter feed clipped burley or dark-fired seedlings pulled from 288-cell float trays into the carousel or finger mechanism, on rolling, sometimes wet fields.

Small diversified or organic vegetable farm: one or two riders on a 1-2 row tractor-drawn (or self-propelled) setter, several different crops planted in short runs on the same day, farm-grown seedlings in assorted tray sizes, uneven ground and short irregular field blocks.

Loose vegetative propagules: sweet potato slips, bare-root strawberry crowns, bare-root brassica or onion plants delivered loose in crates and bundles; rider must separate, orient root-down, and place each into a clip-type or shoe-type planter at the right instant.

Tree, vine and nursery stock: worker rides a trailed tree planter or nursery liner planter, placing bare-root forest seedlings, rootstock or nursery liners into the open furrow behind the coulter at set spacing while packing wheels close the trench; cutover ground or nursery field.

tasks.label: Guide products on conveyors to regulate flow through machines, and to discard diseased or rotten products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fresh-pack / grading line in a farm packing shed or produce packinghouse: potatoes, onions, carrots, green beans or tomatoes move over grading belts after washing/sizing. The operator spreads product and regulates the feed rate into the washer, sizer and bagger, and pulls out rotten, diseased, bruised or misshapen items plus foreign material before packing.

Farm storage receiving / load-out: trucks tip freshly harvested potatoes, onions or sweet potatoes into a receiving hopper feeding cleaners, elevators and a piler into the storage building (or back out onto trucks). The operator sets hopper feed to keep flow even and picks clods, stones, vines and rotten tubers/bulbs off the moving conveyor. Dusty, semi-outdoor farmyard, standard farm equipment.

Riding or standing at the sorting table of a harvester working in the field (potato, sweet-potato, onion, processing-tomato, or root-crop harvester): crop and trash pass on the machine's webs and picking belt; the worker culls vines, clods, stones and rotten/diseased product before it drops into the bulk truck, and calls for chain/web speed and flow adjustments. Mud, dust, vibration, changing light and weather.

Hand-harvest crew working with a mobile field conveyor / harvest-aid rig (lettuce, cabbage, melons, peppers, sweet corn): cut product is laid on the moving belt and carried to the packing platform. The worker guides and evens product on the belt so packers are not overloaded and throws off unmarketable, diseased or decayed heads/fruit before they reach the carton.

Stationary post-harvest plant on or near the farm (nut huller/sheller, peanut buying point, grain cleaning shed, cotton gin): the operator feeds and regulates product flow onto conveyors and into the machine to avoid choking or starving it, clears jams, and removes moldy/spoiled product, hulls, sticks and other foreign material from the inspection belt.

tasks.label: Position boxes or attach bags at discharge ends of machinery to catch products, removing and closing full containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field harvest of root/bulk crops (potatoes, onions, carrots, melons, apples): operator positions empty bulk bins, boxes or totes under the discharge conveyor of a moving harvester or field-pack rig, watches fill level, then pulls the full container clear and sets the next empty one, on uneven ground, in dust, with a crew and tractors moving around.

Field bagging: operator hooks burlap/poly sacks or big bags onto the discharge spout of a harvester bagging attachment, seed/grain bagger or bagging wagon, fills to weight, ties/sews or folds the top closed and drops or stacks the full sack in the field.

On-farm stationary post-harvest equipment in a barn or dedicated bagging shed: hanging bags on the spout of a grain cleaner, roller mill/feed mixer, sheller or huller, filling to weight, closing with a tie or sewing head, and stacking full bags on pallets; same layout and same bag stock day to day.

Commercial packing shed / post-harvest plant (potato or onion packhouse, seed conditioning plant, feed mill, gin, nut huller): presenting cartons, bins or consumer/50-lb bags at the discharge of graders, sizers and weigh hoppers, removing full containers, closing them by sewing or heat seal, and moving them onto the pallet line.

Small or diversified operation, farmyard setting: catching product at the discharge of a portable seed cleaner, small mill or hopper wagon into whatever containers are on hand (assorted sacks, totes, buckets, customer-supplied bags), with frequent product and container changeovers and no fixed line.

tasks.label: Irrigate soil, using portable pipes or ditch systems, and maintain ditches or pipes and pumps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hand-move portable aluminum sprinkler pipe (handlines) or wheel-line sets in hay, mint, potato or pasture ground: shut off and drain the line, uncouple 30-40 ft joints, carry and re-couple them 40-60 ft over, reset risers and end plugs, walk the line to clear plugged nozzles and leaking gaskets. Muddy or rutted footing, standing crop, wind, twice-daily set changes.

Border/basin or check flood irrigation of forage or grain fed from a farm head ditch or pipeline riser with fixed gates/valves: open a set, watch the water advance down the check, decide cutoff, close the gate and open the next set on a 12-24 hour rotation, watch for bank seepage. Fixed ditch and gate infrastructure on a leveled field.

Furrow irrigation with hand-set portable hardware: prime and set dozens to hundreds of siphon tubes over the ditch bank, or unroll and punch lay-flat poly pipe / set gated-pipe slide gates, place canvas or portable dams and checks in the ditch, tune flow furrow by furrow, pull the tubes and shift the set. Uneven ditch banks, trash and weeds in the water.

Ditch reshaping and silt removal: run a tractor-mounted V-ditcher/ditch cleaner or an excavator/backhoe along a farm ditch, lateral or field drain to pull out accumulated sediment, restore grade and section, and cast spoil onto the bank, working around buried pipe, headgates and fences.

Ditch and structure upkeep other than reshaping: mow, spray or burn bank weeds and cattails, clear trash racks, screens and culvert inlets, patch washouts and plug gopher/muskrat holes mid-season, reset checks, headgates, flumes and turnouts after a break.

Pump and pipeline maintenance: prime the pump, grease and check oil and packing, replace seals, impellers or foot valves, chase down and repair leaks and blown gaskets in mainline and risers, clean filters and suction screens, adjust or restart the pump/panel, drain and winterize the system.

Orchard or berry harvest: senior worker monitors hand-pickers paid by piece rate, checks filled lugs/clamshells for bruising, over-ripe or stemless fruit, verbally corrects picking technique, keeps punch cards or counts, and redirects workers to blocks that are ready.

Nursery or greenhouse: lead worker instructs seasonal help in transplanting, potting-up, spacing, sticking cuttings, or grading plants; shows the correct depth/spacing once, then circulates to check work and answer questions, keeping the crew on the day's order list.

Field planting: lead hand positions seasonal workers on a mechanical transplanter or along hand-planting rows, sets the pace, monitors plant spacing, skips and misplanted seedlings, and signals the tractor driver or crew to stop and correct.

Shift logistics and communication: bilingual experienced worker relays the manager's instructions to a mostly Spanish-speaking seasonal crew, covers basic safety and heat/hygiene rules at the tailgate meeting, schedules breaks and water, and answers newcomers' questions during the shift.

tasks.label: Participate in the inspection, grading, sorting, storage, and post-harvest treatment of crops.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Packing shed / packinghouse grading line: worker stands at a conveyor or grading table in the farm's packing shed, inspects apples, citrus, potatoes, onions or tomatoes coming from field bins, culls bruised/rotten/undersized units, sorts by size, color and grade, and places fruit into trays, bags or cartons. Indoor, fixed layout, standard line equipment, farm controls who is present.

In-field inspection, grading and sorting during harvest (field-pack crews for lettuce, melons, broccoli, berries, sweet corn): worker inspects each unit as it is cut or picked, trims and culls, judges maturity/size against buyer specs, and places graded product into cartons or field bins on a mobile harvest rig or on the ground. Open field, uneven ground, dust, sun, rain, mud, crew moving continuously.

Nursery/greenhouse grading and sorting of plant material: worker inspects plugs, cuttings, liners or containerized plants for size, root development, damage and disease, culls poor plants, sorts by grade, and stages graded plants on carts or racks for shipping. Greenhouse benches, headhouse, and outdoor container beds; institution-controlled premises kept to a working standard.

Post-harvest treatment: washing/rinsing, hydrocooling, waxing and fungicide drenching of fruit, topping/trimming carrots, onions and greens, curing/drying onions and sweet potatoes, bunching/tying/banding, and re-hydrating nursery stock. Occurs in the packing shed treatment area or curing room with standard line equipment.

Moving harvested product into storage: palletizing cartons or stacking totes and field bins, moving pallets/bins with a pallet jack or forklift into the cooler, CA room or barn, stacking them, and rotating/checking lot labels. Farm cooler or storage barn with flat floors, standard pallets/bins, farm controls access.

instances.label: Nursery/greenhouse propagation and potting work in a headhouse or production greenhouse: pulling plugs or rooted liners, sticking cuttings, transplanting plugs into 4-inch pots, gallon cans, flats or combination hanging baskets, filling with media, and pushing in or sticking a printed variety label/tag on each pot before the finished plants go to the bench. Harvest inside a commercial greenhouse or polytunnel: walking or riding a pipe-rail cart down crop rows picking ripe tomatoes, cucumbers, or tabletop strawberries by ripeness judgment, placing fruit into crates/clamshells on the cart, and moving full containers to the head aisle.

Open-field leafy-green harvest: cutting romaine, spinach, or baby-leaf greens with knife or on a harvest rig, trimming outer leaves, and loading into totes or bulk bins on the machine or truck; long rows on flat irrigated ground, high throughput, crew-paced.

Open-field selective hand harvest of other vegetables, melons, and cut flowers: bell peppers, squash, cucumbers, broccoli heads, cantaloupe, and flower stems — judging maturity plant by plant, cutting or snapping by hand, and field-packing into boxes carried down the row.

tasks.label: Repair and maintain farm vehicles, implements, and mechanical equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled service of a tractor, utility vehicle or pickup in the farm shop/yard: draining and refilling engine oil, spinning off and replacing oil/air/fuel filters, greasing a dozen zerk fittings on the machine and hitch, topping coolant and hydraulic fluid, checking battery terminals and tire pressures, refueling. Machine is dirty, fittings are in cramped spots, fasteners may be seized.

In-field breakdown repair during planting/cultivating/harvest: replacing sheared bolts and shear pins, broken shanks, tines, discs or mower blades, re-tensioning or replacing chains and belts, swapping a burst hydraulic hose or clogged spray nozzle. Done in mud/dust at the headland with hand tools, often kneeling or lying under the implement, under time pressure.

Maintenance of small powered equipment in the shop: string trimmers, chainsaws, backpack sprayers, transfer pumps, walk-behind mowers and tillers — replacing spark plugs and air filters, cleaning carburetors, sharpening chains and mower blades, restringing heads, replacing pull cords and fuel lines.

Cleaning equipment as maintenance: pressure-washing tractors, harvesters, transplanters and sprayers on the farm wash pad, blowing chaff off radiator screens and grilles, rinsing and flushing spray tanks, booms and nozzles, wiping down and lubricating after wash.

Repairing fixed mechanical systems around the irrigation setup, greenhouse and packing shed: irrigation pump and motor repairs, replacing valves, filters and drip-line fittings, changing belts and bearings on packing-line conveyors and graders, fixing exhaust fans, heaters and roll-up curtain motors.

tasks.label: Harvest fruits and vegetables by hand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-field strawberry harvest (California coast, Florida winter crop): crews stoop over raised plastic-mulched beds, judge ripeness berry by berry, pick with a stem twist and place fruit directly into clamshells in a tray, culling misshapen/rotten fruit, over multiple passes per week in sun, mud and dust.

Tree-fruit picking from ladders or orchard platforms: apples in Washington, oranges/tangerines in Florida and California, cherries, peaches and pears. Worker reaches into 3-D canopies, selects by color/size, picks with stem intact into a picking bag, empties into bins; variable tree architecture, shade, wind, uneven ground.

Field leafy-greens harvest (Salinas/Yuma): crews cutting head lettuce, romaine, spinach and baby greens with knives, trimming outer leaves, and placing/wrapping heads onto a moving harvest rig or into cartons at high piece-rate speed, early morning, wet and muddy conditions.

Field fruiting-vegetable picking: staked fresh-market tomatoes in Florida, bell peppers, slicing cucumbers, eggplant and squash, hand-picked into 5-gallon buckets and dumped into gondolas/trailers; ripeness and size judgment, foliage occlusion, repeated passes.

Other field hand-harvest with no in-facility analogue: broccoli/celery/cabbage cutting crews, asparagus snapping, melons cut and passed to a conveyor rig, table-grape bunches cut and field-packed in the vineyard, hand-picked fresh-market blueberries and caneberries; outdoor, uneven terrain, crop-specific quality calls.

Greenhouse / indoor harvest: picking vine tomatoes, cucumbers and peppers on high-wire systems from a pipe-rail trolley, or picking tabletop strawberries in a glasshouse or vertical farm; fixed row layout, level concrete/pipe-rail floor, climate-controlled, grower controls who enters.

tasks.label: Set up and operate irrigation equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Drip/micro-sprinkler set operation in orchards, vineyards or row crops: walk or drive to block valves, open the block, start the booster pump, verify pressure at gauges/flush ends, run the set for the scheduled hours, then close and move to the next block, several blocks per shift.

Surface irrigation (border/furrow/flood): open head-ditch gates, set gated pipe outlets or siphon tubes, walk the field to watch water advance down furrows/bays, shut the set off at the right time (often at night) and shift to the next bay.

Portable sprinkler irrigation: uncouple, drain, carry and re-couple 30-40 ft aluminum hand-line pipe to the next set (twice daily), tow and set wheel lines, position big-gun/hose-reel travelers, connect layflat and portable pumps to hydrants in open fields, over uneven, muddy or crop-covered ground.

Drip tape / micro-tubing installation and retrieval: laying tape along freshly formed beds or under plastic mulch, cutting and splicing, connecting each lateral into the layflat or PVC submain header, punching in emitters/spaghetti stakes for trees or containers, flushing new lines, and pulling and spooling tape at season's end.

Greenhouse and nursery watering: hand-watering benches, plug trays, hanging baskets and container beds with a hose and breaker wand, or setting up and running overhead booms/micro-sprinklers over bench bays, adjusting nozzles, travel speed and controller timers to water crops uniformly.

In-season irrigation maintenance and repair: finding and patching blowouts and rodent holes in drip tape, replacing broken sprinkler heads, gaskets and fittings, clearing clogged emitters and screens, cleaning sand-media/screen filters, and draining/winterizing lines.

tasks.label: Inform farmers or farm managers of crop progress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Identify plants, pests, and weeds to determine the selection and application of pesticides and fertilizers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Greenhouse or covered/container nursery: worker walks bench rows and potted/substrate crops (ornamentals, vegetable starts, cut flowers), turning leaves and inspecting undersides for whitefly, thrips, aphids, mites, caterpillars, mildew and nutrient chlorosis, identifying the crop variety and the problem, and telling the grower what spray, biocontrol or feed to apply.

Open-field vegetable, melon and berry ground: worker moves down seedling rows during hand-weeding/thinning, distinguishing crop from lookalike weeds (nightshade, purslane, nutsedge, volunteers), spotting aphid/worm/mildew hot spots, and deciding which herbicide or insecticide is applied and where.

Broadacre row crops (corn, soybeans, cotton, small grains, hay): worker/scout walks or rides fields checking weed escapes and species for herbicide choice, insect feeding damage, disease lesions, and pale/stunted areas indicating nutrient shortfall, reporting what to spray or feed.

Tree fruit and nut orchards (apples, citrus, stone fruit, almonds): worker inspects canopies, leaf undersides and trunks for mites, scale, borers, aphids, scab/fire blight/greening symptoms, plus weeds in the tree row, to determine miticide/fungicide/herbicide selection and fertilizer needs; ladders, dense canopy, dust and glare.

Vineyards and trellised perennials (wine/table grapes, hops, caneberries): worker walks trellised rows checking canopy for powdery/downy mildew, leafroll symptoms, mites and weeds under the vine, to set spray timing and product selection.

Ambiguous or novel problems in any setting: plant is wilting or off-color for unclear reasons, so the worker uproots or digs it, checks roots for rot/nematodes/grubs, scrapes bark, checks soil and irrigation, distinguishes herbicide drift from deficiency or disease, and collects a sample for the supervisor or lab before a product is chosen.

tasks.label: Regulate greenhouse conditions, and indoor and outdoor irrigation systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Regulating climate in a commercial greenhouse or nursery house: raising/lowering vents and shade or energy curtains, running exhaust fans, wet walls and heaters, misting/fogging for humidity, adjusting setpoints as outside weather changes through the day, and checking sensors and alarms so the crop stays in range.

Operating the indoor irrigation system: setting and running drip, ebb-and-flood, overhead sprinkler or rail-mounted boom zones on a schedule, dosing fertilizer through the injector, changing run times and volumes as the crop grows or the weather shifts, and verifying zones actually ran.

Hand-watering and localized adjustment in a greenhouse or nursery: dragging a hose to water in individual pots, benches, edges and dry spots the overhead system misses, judging by pot weight and plant appearance, and repositioning drip stakes, nozzles or spaghetti tubes on mixed inventory.

Regulating outdoor irrigation in fields, orchards or vineyards: starting/stopping and setting center pivots or linear moves, opening and closing block valves and pumps for drip or micro-sprinkler sets, setting run times and amounts from soil-moisture, weather and crop stage, and confirming pressure and flow.

Field irrigation hardware work: moving hand-line or wheel-line sprinkler pipe between sets, laying out and retrieving drip tape or lay-flat hose, setting siphon tubes/gate openings for furrow irrigation and watching water advance, unclogging emitters and nozzles, flushing lines, cleaning filters and screens, and digging out and patching leaks or breaks.

tasks.label: Feel plants' leaves and note their coloring to detect the presence of insects or disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-field row and vegetable crops (lettuce, melons, tomatoes, cotton, soybeans): while weeding, thinning or harvesting, the worker examines foliage along rows for aphids, mites, worms, leaf lesions and yellowing, turning leaves over, and flags hotspots to the crew leader. Uneven ground, dust, wind, variable sun.

Vineyard, caneberry and strawberry beds: walking trellised rows or raised beds, examining leaf color and undersides for powdery/downy mildew, leafroll reddening, mites and thrips; marking infected vines/beds for treatment.

Tree fruit and nut orchards (apple, citrus, almond, stone fruit): pulling branches down to inspect leaf color and undersides for mites, scale, aphids, fire blight strikes and nutrient chlorosis at varying heights within tall canopies; reporting blocks needing treatment.

Greenhouse vegetable and floriculture production under glass/poly: scouting rows of tomato/cucumber/pepper on gutters or potted ornamentals on benches, feeling leaves for stickiness and flipping them to check undersides for whitefly, thrips and spider mites; logging counts and hotspot locations.

Outdoor container/field nursery stock: walking blocks of potted shrubs, perennials and field-grown trees of many species, feeling leaves for honeydew and checking undersides for scale, mites and foliar disease; tagging blocks for spray. Weather-exposed gravel/ground-cloth yard, blocks reshuffled seasonally.

Indoor propagation house, headhouse or packing shed: handling plug trays, cuttings, transplants or harvested leafy product; noting off-color, wilted or infested material and culling it before it moves on.

tasks.label: Maintain and repair irrigation and climate control systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field/orchard drip system repair during the season: worker walks rows while lines are pressurized, spots blowouts, rodent chews and leaks in drip tape or lay-flat poly, cuts out the damaged section and splices in couplers/goof plugs, pulls and replaces plugged emitters, opens line ends to flush. Mud, dense canopy, uneven ground, hand tools carried in a pouch.

Greenhouse/nursery irrigation maintenance: unclogging or replacing misting and spray-stake nozzles, cleaning disc/screen filters and pressure regulators, patching leaking poly hose and PVC laterals, swapping solenoid valves on a zone manifold, checking overhead boom carriage and spray bars, re-aiming emitters on benches and hanging baskets.

Greenhouse climate-control equipment service: exhaust fan belt/pulley and louver servicing, greasing and motor swaps, cleaning and de-scaling evaporative cooling pads and the pad-wall pump/distribution header, freeing stuck roof-vent racks and gear motors, checking unit heaters, thermostats and aspirated sensor boxes, replacing failed parts — much of it on ladders or lifts overhead.

Pump, filter and mainline station work: backwashing and rebuilding sand-media or disc filter stacks, replacing gaskets and pressure gauges, digging up and repairing a broken buried PVC mainline (cut, prime, glue, backfill), servicing pump seals and foot valves, winterizing/blowing out lines and reassembling in spring.

Sprinkler and center-pivot maintenance in open fields: replacing worn sprinkler heads, nozzles and gaskets on hand-move or solid-set aluminum pipe, straightening/patching damaged pipe, replacing pivot drops and regulators, greasing gearboxes, checking tires, drivelines and end-gun on a center pivot in soft ground.

sources.system: Spot (with Spot CAM+IR / Orbit, Levatas gauge reading)
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is deployed for autonomous routine inspection rounds inside industrial facilities, reading gauges and capturing thermal/visual data on equipment health, but it collects data rather than performing mechanical maintenance or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous equipment-condition inspection in a structured facility. It covers only the 'check the equipment' fraction of maintenance; Spot does not disassemble, splice, glue, thread fittings, or replace failed irrigation/climate components, so it cannot substantiate completion of any repair instance.

sources.title: Priva Kompano | Deleafing robot
sources.claim: Priva's Kompano is a commercially sold greenhouse robot that navigates aisles autonomously alongside workers and performs a manipulation task (tomato deleafing); its manipulation repertoire is crop handling, not servicing irrigation or climate hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside a commercial greenhouse. It shows navigation in the E2 setting, but the end effector and perception are specialized to cutting leaf petioles; no evidence of tool use, fastener work, nozzle/filter servicing, or fault diagnosis on irrigation or climate equipment.

sources.developer: University of Sheffield (with UK water utilities)
sources.title: Tiny robots could help fix leaky water pipes
sources.claim: University of Sheffield 'Pipebots' micro-robots for inspecting and repairing leaks inside live water mains remain a research/development project, with the leak-repair capability the object of a project to develop rather than a fielded service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-pipe leak location and sealing in buried municipal mains. Even taken at face value it addresses only sealing cracks inside large-diameter potable mains, not drip tape splices, emitter/nozzle replacement, filter stacks, or any climate-control hardware; maturity is a development project, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Solar-farm construction and cleaning robots (e.g., automated module installation vehicles)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor robotic handling/installation of uniform components on a prepared site. It transfers poorly: irrigation repair requires locating an unknown fault, removing damaged fittings, cutting/gluing/threading, and verifying a pressure-tight result on non-uniform, degraded hardware, none of which is demonstrated.

tasks.label: Dig, cut, and transplant seedlings, cuttings, trees, and shrubs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Greenhouse/headhouse: transplanting seedling plugs out of 128/288-cell plug trays into packs, pots, or larger trays of bedding plants, herbs, or vegetable starts; trays and pots handled in bulk, thousands of plants per shift, media pre-filled.

Propagation greenhouse: trimming and sticking unrooted cuttings (annuals, perennials, woody softwood cuttings) into propagation trays - sizing the cutting, applying rooting hormone, inserting upright at correct depth in each cell.

Open field, prepared beds (bare or plastic-mulched): setting vegetable, strawberry, or tobacco plug seedlings at fixed in-row spacing, opening the furrow, firming soil and watering in; done by hand crews or crews riding transplanters, hundreds of thousands of plants per block.

Field nursery: digging/lifting field-grown trees and shrubs - balled-and-burlapped root balls, bare-root liners and rootstock - with hand spades or a tree spade, tying burlap and wire baskets, sorting and heeling in the dug stock.

Container nursery/greenhouse yard: potting up rooted liners and small shrubs into larger containers at a potting line or by hand, setting them out on beds; media, pot size and plant size vary by crop batch.

Scattered hand work: digging and transplanting individual plants - filling gaps/replanting misses in field or bed rows, moving volunteer or specimen shrubs, hand-planting on slopes, in small odd-shaped beds, hoop houses, or around irrigation and obstacles.

tasks.label: Maintain inventory, ordering materials as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Greenhouse crop/plant stock count: worker walks benches and rows in a production greenhouse, counting and grading trays, pots and finished plants by variety and size, recording counts for availability lists and flagging inputs (media, plugs, pots) that need reordering.

Outdoor container-nursery or field-block stock count: worker walks or drives growing blocks in a commercial nursery, counting salable containers by variety/size, noting shrink and gaps, and reporting counts for the availability/ordering system.

Consumables check in the farm/greenhouse storeroom: worker inspects shelved and palletized supplies (seed, fertilizer, chemicals, media, pots, trays, twine, tags), notes quantities against min levels, and phones/emails or app-orders replenishment from suppliers.

Receiving a delivery: truck arrives with pallets or loose cases of supplies; worker unloads, checks items and quantities against the packing slip/invoice, notes damage or shortages, and puts the materials away in the correct storage location, updating records.

Packing-shed supply monitoring during harvest: worker tracks consumption of boxes, clamshells, liners, labels and pallets on the grading/packing line, carries replacement stock from storage to the line, and calls in reorders before the line runs out.

Farmyard shed inventory of tools, hardware and irrigation/fence parts: worker sorts through a cluttered, non-standardized barn or shop of loose fittings, spare parts, hand tools and fuel, tallies what is on hand and worn out, and orders replacements.

sources.title: How GEODIS Solved a Costly and Labor-Intensive Inventory Problem with Gather AI

tasks.label: Dig, rake, and screen soil, filling cold frames and hot beds in preparation for planting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial greenhouse or high tunnel: dig/rototill the in-ground growing beds, break clods, remove stones, and rake the surface to a fine level seedbed before direct seeding or transplanting. Fixed layout, level floor, standard bed widths, institution-controlled premises.

Nursery headhouse/potting area: shovel and sift soil, compost, sand and peat through a screen to remove stones, roots and clods, blend a propagation mix, then fill propagation flats, bench frames and seed beds and strike them level. Indoor, standard equipment, controlled premises.

Small farm, market garden or garden-center nursery yard: wheelbarrow screened soil/compost to outdoor cold frames, low tunnels and raised propagation beds; shovel it in around sashes and hoops, rake and firm it to depth. Uneven ground, weather, layout varies site to site.

Building or renewing a hot bed / heated propagation bed: excavate the shallow pit or frame, fork in fresh manure or hot compost, tamp the layer, then cap it with 4-6 inches of screened soil raked level. Heavy outdoor hand digging on ground taken as found.

Nursery yard bulk soil work: move screened topsoil/compost from stockpiles by wheelbarrow, skid steer or conveyor into growing beds, frames and container areas; spread and grade it level and clean up. Hardstand yard operated by the nursery to a working standard.

sources.title: Javo Potting machine Super - Javo - Potting machines - Hortimat
sources.claim: Javo potting machines automatically fill pots and containers with soil/substrate from a bulk soil bunker via supply belt and soil wheel, with automatic container supply, on a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine filling of growing containers with screened media. Same material (nursery growing media), same required outcome (uniform fill to depth, struck level), same purpose-built line setting as an E1 frame/bed filling station.

tasks.label: Inspect plants and bud ties to assess quality.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Greenhouse production/propagation house: worker walks benches and gutter rows of plugs, cuttings, and potted crops, examining plants for size, uniformity, color, flower stage, disease and insect damage, and reports/flags substandard material for culling. Indoor, climate-controlled, fixed bench layout.

Outdoor container nursery block (gravel/fabric beds, drip or overhead irrigation): worker walks rows of potted shrubs and trees assessing plant quality and salability — caliper/height, form, foliage condition, root/pot condition, pest damage — tagging culls and reporting which blocks are ready to ship. Weather, mud, and mixed species.

Budding/grafting quality check in a field nursery (fruit trees, roses, ornamental stock): weeks after budding, worker moves down rows, bends to the bud union near the soil line, examines the bud tie (rubber strip/patch) and the inserted bud to judge take, tie tightness and girdling, and marks failures for rebudding.

Field/vegetable crop inspection: worker walks or rides rows in an open field checking crop plants for stand quality, disease, insect damage, growth stage and readiness/quality before thinning or harvest, reporting problem areas to the crew boss. Uneven ground, dust, variable weather.

Grading/packing area of a nursery or greenhouse: worker at a grading table or line inspects bare-root plants, liners, transplants or finished pots as they come past, sorting into quality grades and pulling unsalable material before packing and shipping. Indoor, fixed layout, standard containers.

tasks.label: Move containerized shrubs, plants, and trees, using wheelbarrows or tractors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor container yard / hoop house at a wholesale nursery: worker picks up 1–5 gallon containerized shrubs (up to ~20–25 lb) from a tightly packed block or from a drop trailer and re-sets them at spacing intervals, or consolidates/collects them after shipping; ground is gravel or ground cloth, rows laid out to a plan, weather exposed.

Greenhouse or headhouse: worker moves potted plants and flats from the potting line to benches or floor beds, loads them onto Danish carts/racks, and pushes or tows loaded carts down aisles to holding or shipping areas; smooth concrete or gravel floor, fixed bay layout, people working nearby.

Tractor or utility vehicle hauling: worker drives a tractor towing loaded trailers/wagons of containerized stock between the potting shed, growing blocks, and the shipping yard on farm lanes, and returns empties; loading and unloading is done by other crew members at each end.

Wheelbarrow/hand-cart moves of mid-to-large containers (7–15 gallon shrubs and small trees, 40–100 lb) over gravel lanes, dirt rows, and sometimes mud, from a staging pile to individual planting or display positions in tight rows; lift, wheel, set down upright, repeat.

Heavy specimen material: 25 gallon+ containers and balled-and-burlapped trees moved with tractor forks, a tree dolly, straps, or two-person carries; positioned into rows, pot-in-pot sockets, or onto a truck bed in tight, uneven staging areas.

sources.title: Harvey - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 ('Harvey') mobile robot autonomously locates, picks up, transports and places potted plants for spacing, consolidation and collection in nursery container beds, hoop houses and greenhouses; sold commercially from 2013 and used in production.

sources.claim: HV-100 robots were bought by nursery customers and put to everyday farm work distributing and collecting container-grown plants in greenhouses and ..., having moved over three million plants.

sources.claim: Burro robots, named Greenhouse Grower's 2025 Technology of the Year, autonomously navigate point-to-point among workers in greenhouse and nursery operations, moving plants from propagation to ....

sources.title: AgriNomix Automation Solutions | AdeptAg
sources.claim: Nursery production lines already handle containers up to 15 gallons under machine control, accumulating and presenting them on buffer belts for forklift pick-off at up to 4,000 containers per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-facility movement of the same nursery containers. Shows large containers can be conveyed and presented under machine control in a purpose-built line, the presentation an E1 counterfactual assumes; PLC-scripted, so not relied on as the decisive cite.

tasks.label: Tie and bunch flowers, plants, shrubs, and trees, wrap their roots, and pack them into boxes to fill orders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cut-flower packing shed/greenhouse grading area: worker takes harvested stems (tulips, chrysanthemums, roses, lilies, sunflowers), grades and counts them into bunches of 5-10, binds with rubber band or twine, slips a sleeve on, cuts stems to length, and sets bunches into buckets or shipping boxes against a customer order sheet.

Field or hoophouse harvest of single-species specialty cut flowers: worker cuts stems, bunches them by count in the row, bands them, drops them in a water bucket, and later boxes the bunches for a wholesale order; done in heat, mud, and variable light.

Mixed-species bouquet and bunch making for farmers-market/CSA/florist orders: worker selects varied stems, foliage, and fillers of differing form, assembles a balanced mixed bunch, ties it, wraps it, and packs the assortment into boxes to fill each order.

Greenhouse/nursery order fulfillment for potted and bedding plants: worker pulls the ordered pots or flats off benches or the floor, sleeves or wraps them, packs them into cartons or trays, tapes and labels the boxes, and stages them on Danish carts for shipping.

Field nursery yard for woody stock: worker handles freshly dug shrubs and trees, wraps root balls in burlap and wire baskets or wraps bare roots in moist media/poly, ties the wrap and pins it, bundles graded stock with twine, and packs/labels it for shipment; wet soil, uneven ground, plant-to-plant variation.
Christmas trees and large evergreens/shrubs: worker shakes and grades the tree, feeds it through a netting/baling funnel, ties the bale, tags it, and stacks or packs it for the load.

sources.date: 2025-09 (page retrieved; product commercial for several years)

tasks.label: Haul and spread topsoil, fertilizer, peat moss, and other materials to condition soil, using wheelbarrows or carts and shovels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Headhouse/greenhouse potting station: worker shovels or scoops growing media from a bulk pile, bale, or bagged peat, wheels it by cart to the potting bench, blends in perlite/lime/controlled-release fertilizer, and fills flats, plug trays and pots, striking off and leveling the media. Indoor, fixed layout, other workers and carts nearby.

Container nursery blocks (gravel/fabric pads, hoop houses): worker hauls sacks/totes of controlled-release fertilizer and bark/media by cart or wheelbarrow out to container beds and top-dresses each pot with granular fertilizer or tops off pots whose media has settled or washed out. Outdoors on nursery-controlled ground, weather and irrigation present.

Greenhouse or high-tunnel in-ground beds between crops: worker wheelbarrows compost, topsoil and peat from a pile outside into the house, dumps loads along the bed, then spreads, breaks up and rakes level with a shovel before tilling in. Narrow aisles, low hoops, irrigation lines and posts in the way.

Open vegetable/row-crop ground before planting: worker hauls compost, lime or granular fertilizer by cart or wheelbarrow from a pile or pickup and spreads it over prepared beds or field strips to condition the soil. Outdoor, uneven and sometimes muddy ground, variable weather.

Orchard, vineyard, or field-grown tree/shrub nursery: worker hauls topsoil, compost or mulch by wheelbarrow to individual trees or vines, spreads a ring around each base, and backfills soil/amendment around root balls of newly set plants. Plants in the ground, uneven terrain, per-plant placement without damaging trunks or drip lines.

Farm site fill work: worker hauls topsoil by wheelbarrow or cart to fill low spots, ruts, washouts, or newly framed beds/plant rows and spreads and rough-levels it with a shovel and rake. Outdoor, unimproved ground, conditions taken as found.

sources.title: Harvey: A working robot for container crops - Robohub
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 is an autonomous mobile robot deployed in commercial greenhouses and nursery fields, where it locates, transports and places container plants without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomous navigation and material handling by this robot in the same nursery/greenhouse settings where the topdressing attachment (evidence 1) is used.
