tasks.label: Repair farm buildings, fences, and other structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Perimeter/field fence repair: worker walks or drives a line of barbed, woven, or high-tensile wire fence after storm, tree-fall, or livestock/deer damage; digs out and replaces rotted or snapped wooden posts and T-posts, resets leaning corner braces, splices and retensions wire, drives staples, rehangs sagging gates. Uneven ground, vegetation, mud, wind, variable damage found on arrival.

Greenhouse/hoophouse structure repair inside a commercial nursery or greenhouse range: patch or replace wind-torn polyfilm, replace a cracked glazing pane, repair roll-up side crank and hardware, straighten or replace a bent hoop or purlin after snow load, fix doors, benches, and hanging-basket supports. Fixed aisles and standard bays, but the damage location and fix vary each time.

Barn, shed, and packing-house repair: replace rotted siding or floor boards, re-fasten or replace a loose metal roof panel, rehang or re-square a sliding door, patch a wall opening, rebuild broken pen or bin partitions. Ladder work, overhead fasteners, cutting lumber/metal to fit, dusty and cluttered interiors and exteriors.

Orchard/vineyard/berry trellis and support repair: reset leaning or pulled end-post anchors, replace snapped line posts and crossarms, re-tension trellis wires, replace broken stakes and vine ties, repair hail/bird-net supports. Work between crop rows amid vines and canopy, on sloped or soft ground, without damaging the crop.

Ancillary farmyard structure repairs: weld or bolt a cracked steel gate or corral panel (often in the farm shop), patch deer/wildlife fence mesh, repair a pump-house or well-head enclosure, rebuild a culvert head wall or wash-out at a field entrance. Mixed shop and field work, hand and power tools, one-off damage.

sources.title: Robotic solar pile driver three times faster than humans – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously surveys, distributes, drives, and inspects piles for utility-scale solar foundations in open-field construction sites, driving up to ~300 piles/day with a two-person crew. It installs new piles at planned coordinates; it does not diagnose damage, extract broken posts, or attach/tension wire or fasteners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving structural posts/piles into soil outdoors, the closest machine analogue to setting a replacement fence or trellis post. It does not transfer to the whole repair instance, which requires finding and diagnosing damage, removing the broken post and old fasteners, splicing/tensioning wire, and stapling.

sources.developer: Farmscan AG / Kidd Farm Machinery / Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: The Roto-Fence project (Farmscan AG, Kidd Farm Machinery, Harper Adams University) demonstrated a tractor-guided, sensor-equipped post driver that autonomously places fence posts along a pre-planned route with centimetre accuracy for rotational grazing fencing. It is new-fence installation, not repair, and does not handle wire, staples, or gates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fence-post installation on farmland (same objects and outdoor setting as fence repair). It does not substantiate completion of a repair instance: no damage assessment, no removal of broken posts, no wire splicing/tensioning or stapling, and it was shown as a funded project demonstration rather than in-service repair work.

sources.system: Path Robotics autonomous welding cells (AW-3 / AW-5)
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics sells vision-guided welding cells that scan a part, generate weld paths without programming or custom fixtures, and autonomously weld steel parts; the cells are deployed in fabrication shops in the US and Canada. They weld presented parts in a cell; they do not disassemble, cut out, fit, or straighten damaged farm structures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous arc welding of steel weldments in a purpose-built cell, the closest analogue to shop repair of a cracked steel gate or corral panel. It covers only the weld pass on a presented part, not the cut-out, fit-up, straightening, and refitting that a structural repair instance requires.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is a cable-suspended roofing robot for asphalt shingle installation on pitched roofs; the company reports it applied shingles faster than a human roofer and is piloting with manufacturers, with tear-off and cutting listed as future capabilities. Independent trade coverage treats full autonomy on real roofs as not yet proven.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening roof covering material on a sloped roof, adjacent to patching a barn roof. It does not transfer: the demonstrated work is repetitive new-shingle layup on a prepared deck, not localized damage diagnosis, panel removal, and custom-fit replacement, and autonomy on production roofs is not established.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous jobsite robot that drills overhead holes autonomously from a BIM drilling plan after a human lays out the site with a total station; it has been used on many construction projects globally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous power-tool work on building structures at a jobsite. It transfers only to pre-planned, repetitive drilling on flat slabs; it cannot assess damage, remove or fit boards/panels/glazing, or fasten varied replacement parts, so it does not substantiate any repair instance.

tasks.label: Plant, spray, weed, fertilize, water, and prune plants, shrubs, and trees, using gardening tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weeding and thinning bedded row vegetables (lettuce, onions, spinach) on a commercial farm: hand-hoeing and pulling in-row weeds, thinning stands, working along planted beds in open field, in variable weather and soil conditions, on a repeated schedule through the season.

Applying pesticides, fungicides or foliar sprays: backpack/handheld or hand-directed spot spraying in orchards, vineyards and vegetable fields, and spray application on greenhouse crops, wearing PPE and following label rates and re-entry rules.

Planting and transplanting in the field: setting out vegetable transplants or plugs into prepared beds, direct-seeding rows, planting liners/vine or tree stock, spacing and firming soil, following marked rows on a farm's prepared ground.

Greenhouse and container-nursery plant care: hand-watering and hose/boom irrigation, applying liquid feed, potting up and moving/spacing containers on beds and benches, spraying, inside a greenhouse, hoop house or graveled nursery block.
Crop maintenance pruning in protected/high-density production: de-leafing and suckering greenhouse tomato and cucumber vines, shearing/trimming uniform young nursery stock to shape and height.

Selective hand pruning of woody plants: dormant cane and spur pruning of grapevines, structural pruning of fruit trees, shaping ornamental shrubs and field-grown trees with shears and loppers, judging each plant individually.

roles.title: Farmworkers, Farm, Ranch, and Aquacultural Animals
roles.description: Attend to live farm, ranch, open range or aquacultural animals that may include cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses and other equines, poultry, rabbits, finfish, shellfish, and bees. Attend to animals produced for animal products, such as meat, fur, skins, feathers, eggs, milk, and honey. Duties may include feeding, watering, herding, grazing, milking, castrating, branding, de-beaking, weighing, catching, and loading animals. May maintain records on animals; examine animals to detect diseases and injuries; assist in birth deliveries; and administer medications, vaccinations, or insecticides as appropriate. May clean and maintain animal housing areas. Includes workers who shear wool from sheep and collect eggs in hatcheries.

tasks.label: Feed and water livestock and monitor food and water supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy operation: deliver mixed ration (TMR) to the feed fence for lactating, dry and heifer groups in a freestall barn, push feed up several times a day, mix/deliver milk and starter to calves in pens or hutches, and check that automatic waterers and troughs are full and flowing. Indoor barn with fixed alleys, cows and people present.

Confined swine barn (gestation/farrowing/finishing): run or verify automated feed delivery from bulk bins to drop feeders, set individual sow rations, check feed line augers and bin levels, verify nipple drinkers/cup waterers flow and water pressure, and flag animals off feed or water.

Commercial poultry house (broiler or layer): manage feed lines/pan feeders and nipple drinker lines, verify bin levels and order feed, walk the house checking that feeders and drinkers function and are at correct height/pressure, flush water lines, and supplement-feed chicks during brooding.

Beef feedlot: mix and deliver rations along concrete bunks in pen alleys with a feed truck on a multiple-times-daily schedule, read bunks to adjust call amounts, and check/clean automatic water tanks in each pen. Outdoor but fixed pen-and-alley layout under farm control.

Pasture or open-range cattle/sheep: haul and place hay bales, range cubes, mineral or protein tubs to animals in pastures during winter or drought; drive muddy/rutted two-tracks and gates; check stock tanks, ponds and pipelines, break ice, restart pumps or haul water. Terrain, weather and layout vary site to site.

Small or mixed operation — boarding/breeding horse barn, small sheep/goat flock, or aquaculture unit: hand-feed hay and individually portioned grain into stalls or pens, fill and scrub water buckets/troughs, and for fish/shrimp operations distribute feed to ponds or pens and monitor intake and feed stocks.

sources.title: Feed to Need with the Lely Vector – Smarter Feeding for Dairy & Beef Farming
sources.claim: The Lely Vector mixing-feeding robot autonomously loads, mixes, delivers and pushes up rations in dairy and beef barns around the clock, and continuously measures remaining feed at the fence to decide when to re-feed — i.e. it both feeds and monitors feed supply.

sources.title: Lely produces 1,000th Vector automatic feeding system

tasks.label: Examine animals to detect illness, injury, or disease, and to check physical characteristics, such as rate of weight gain.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy barn/parlor, milking-time examination: at each milking the worker checks each cow's udder and quarters for clinical mastitis (forestripping, observing milk color/clots, feeling for heat/swelling), notes yield and body weight/condition trends, diverts abnormal milk and flags the cow for treatment. Cows are presented one at a time in a standard parlor stall or robot box.

Dairy operation daily herd walk-through: once or twice a day the worker walks freestalls, close-up and fresh-cow pens and hospital pens looking for lame cows, swollen hocks/knees, cuts and injuries, dull or off-feed cows, retained placenta, ketosis or metritis signs, calving trouble; takes temperatures and does hands-on checks on suspects. Loose-housed cows moving freely, manure, mixed lighting.

Beef feedlot pen checking: each morning the pen rider walks or rides every pen of 100-300 head, reading individual animals for bovine respiratory disease (droopy ears, nasal discharge, gaunt flank, labored breathing), lameness, bloat, pinkeye or injury, and pulls suspects to the hospital chute. Dusty or muddy dirt pens, cattle milling and moving.

Pasture/rangeland stock checks: the worker drives, rides or walks pastures and range checking cow-calf pairs, stockers, sheep, goats or horses for injury, pinkeye, foot rot, prolapse, calving/lambing difficulty, parasite load and body condition, over large areas with brush, hills, weather and scattered animals; suspects are roped or driven in for closer inspection.

Swine confinement barn daily inspection: the worker walks every pen of a farrowing, gestation or finishing barn daily to find lame, scouring, coughing, prolapsed, hernia-affected, tail-bitten, injured or dead pigs, checks sows and litters, and judges/sorts pigs by market weight and growth. Slatted floors, dust, crowded pens, pigs crowding the caretaker.

Poultry house daily flock inspection: the worker walks a broiler or layer house one or more times per day among tens of thousands of birds, observing flock distribution and activity, locating sick, lame or injured birds and mortality, judging feathering and condition, and tracking flock growth/uniformity. Dim light, litter or cage rows, dust.

tasks.label: Provide medical treatment, such as administering medications and vaccinations, or arrange for veterinarians to provide more extensive treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beef cattle/calves at a ranch or feedlot working facility: cattle are moved up an alley into a hydraulic squeeze chute; the worker reads the ID, draws up and gives subcutaneous/IM vaccinations, injectable antibiotics or dewormer, applies pour-on, and records treatments; sick pulls in the hospital pen get individual doses; the vet is called for cases beyond the crew (prolapse, hard calving, outbreak).

Dairy herd: routine vaccinations and reproductive-program hormone shots given to cows restrained in headlocks or as they exit the parlor, plus individual treatment of fresh and sick cows — intramammary mastitis tubes, IM/SC antibiotics, oral boluses, IV fluids — recording withhold times and calling the vet for displaced abomasums or dystocia.

Swine barns: piglet processing in farrowing crates (iron and antibiotic injections), vaccinating weaned and nursery pigs group-by-group in pens, individually injecting sick pigs identified on walk-through, and setting up water-line medication for a room.

Commercial poultry hatchery mass vaccination: eggs vaccinated in ovo at transfer from setter to hatcher trays, and day-old chicks vaccinated on the chick-processing line by spray/gel cabinet or in-line sprayer and by subcutaneous neck injection before boxing.

Hand treatment of other on-farm stock: catching and injecting pullets, breeders and turkeys in the house (or wing-web stab / water-line dosing of a flock), drenching and vaccinating sheep and goats in a race, giving a horse an IM shot or wound care in a stall or paddock, treating rabbits — each animal caught, restrained and dosed individually, with the vet called for serious cases.

Aquaculture: vaccinating salmon/trout smolts or fingerlings at a hatchery before transfer, and treating stock in tanks or net pens for parasites and disease (bath treatments, medicated feed, delousing), with a fish-health vet consulted for diagnoses.

tasks.label: Mark livestock to identify ownership and grade, using brands, tags, paint, or tattoos.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beef cattle at a ranch or feedlot working facility: cows and calves are gathered into pens, run up an alley into a hydraulic squeeze chute or tipped on a calf table, and workers apply visual and EID ear tags, hot-iron or freeze brands, and occasionally ear notches or wattles. Dusty outdoor corrals, animals struggling and kicking, tag/brand placement judged by eye, some calves worked roped-and-dragged in an open pasture at spring branding.

Dairy operation: newborn calves in maternity pens or hutches get a herd-number ear tag plus an official RFID/840 tag within hours of birth; cows in the freestall barn or parlour are marked with paint sticks/spray, leg bands or tail chalk to flag breeding, treatment or cull groups, often while standing in headlocks or moving through the parlour.

Swine barn: piglets are processed in the farrowing room (ear notching, ear tagging, or litter tattooing) while restrained by hand or on a processing cart; market hogs receive the producer's slap tattoo on the shoulder in the load-out chute before shipping.

Swine finishing barn: identifying market-ready hogs by weight/grade in a large finishing pen and paint-marking them (spray or paint stick) so the right animals are pulled for the next load, or marking lightweights for a later group.

Sheep and goats: applying official scrapie ear tags (and management tags) to lambs/kids and adults in a handling race, tipping cradle or shearing shed, plus applying paint brands/raddle marks to flag ownership, sale lots, treatment or breeding groups.

Aquaculture/hatchery: marking and tagging juvenile salmonids or other finfish — adipose fin clipping, coded wire tag injection, or elastomer/PIT tags — at a hatchery, working from raceways or ponds through a tagging trailer or table.

tasks.label: Drive trucks, tractors, and other equipment to distribute feed to animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy farm (200–2,000 cows): worker loads a TMR mixer wagon behind a tractor (or self-propelled mixer) from silage bunkers and commodity bays, mixes the ration, then drives the concrete feed alleys of freestall barns delivering the correct ration to each cow group, and returns several times a day to push feed up to the feed fence.

Commercial beef feedyard or enclosed finishing barn: worker drives a truck-mounted or pull-type mixer along bunk alleys, following the day's feed call sheet, delivering multiple loads to dozens of pens on schedule, judging bunk levels and dropping the right amount per pen in dust, mud, or ice.

Cow-calf ranch, winter feeding on pasture/range: worker drives a pickup with a cake/cube feeder or a tractor with bales across pasture tracks, through gates, in snow, mud, and ruts, unrolling hay or dropping supplement while cattle crowd the moving vehicle; routes and terrain vary daily.

Small mixed-livestock, sheep/goat, or equine boarding operation: worker uses a tractor with loader/bale spear or a UTV/feed cart to haul hay and grain from a shed to ring feeders, paddock troughs, calf hutches, and pens; tight, irregular yards with gates, parked equipment, dogs, and loose animals.

Confinement swine or poultry site: worker drives a truck, tractor, or skid steer around the site to move bulk feed and fill bins/feeders, tops off pans, feeders, and gestation/farrowing feed drops inside standardized houses, and clears bridged or refused feed.

tasks.label: Segregate animals according to weight, age, color, and physical condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Swine finishing/wean-to-finish barn: hogs in large groups (500+ head) must be split into light and heavy feeding groups and market-weight pigs pulled off for shipment; worker judges/weighs pigs and moves them between pens and to the load-out chute.

Dairy: cows leaving the parlor or robot are separated into breeding, fresh, hospital/treatment, dry and heifer groups on the basis of age, days in milk, and physical condition (lameness, mastitis, body condition) noted by the milker.

Beef cattle handling facility (ranch corral, backgrounder, feedlot processing barn): cattle are run through crowding tub, alley and squeeze chute, weighed and read for EID, and sorted three ways into pens by weight, sex, age class and visible condition (lameness, pinkeye, poor doers).

Pasture and rangeland: cutting out individual animals or classes from a mob on grass on horseback, ATV or on foot - pulling a lame cow or scouring calf, separating cull cows, splitting weaning pairs, drafting sheep or goats - in variable terrain with no fixed layout.

Commercial poultry house (broiler, pullet or layer): walking the flock daily to spot and remove sick, injured, runt or dead birds and place culls in a separate area; also splitting off off-size birds ahead of catching, amid tens of thousands of loose birds on litter.

Hatchery and aquaculture grading lines: day-old chicks graded and sorted by sex/feather color and first-quality versus culls; fingerlings, smolt or shellfish graded by size and condition into separate tanks, cages or pens.

tasks.label: Inspect, maintain, and repair equipment, machinery, buildings, pens, yards, and fences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Perimeter/fence-line check on pasture or rangeland: ride, drive or fly the boundary of paddocks and range looking for downed or slack wire, leaning posts, open or damaged gates, limbs on the fence, and stock-water problems; output is locating the faults and reporting them for repair.

Hands-on fence, gate and outdoor yard repair in the field: splice and re-stretch barbed or high-tensile wire, drive or reset a broken post, replace insulators, find and fix an electric fence short, rehang a sagging gate, patch a corral panel or loading chute, fix a leaking stock-tank float, in mud, snow or heat with tools carried on an ATV or truck.

Routine walk-through inspection inside livestock housing (broiler/layer house, hog barn, dairy freestall): check drinker and nipple lines for leaks and blockages, feed lines and augers, fans and inlets, lighting, temperature and alarms, and flag equipment faults for repair.

Hands-on repair and upkeep of pens, gates and building fabric inside barns and corrals: replace a broken nipple drinker or float valve, rehang a gate or fix a latch, bolt in a new pen divider or replace rotten boards, unplug a feed auger, patch a wall or door, replace a fan belt or bulb; done around animals and existing plumbing and wiring.

Service and repair of machinery and farm systems: grease fittings and check fluids on tractors, skid steers, ATVs and TMR mixers, change oil and filters, replace a burst hydraulic hose or worn chain, fix a flat, and maintain manure pumps, generators, hatchery/pond pumps, aerators and filters — in the farm shop, hatchery machine room, or wherever the unit failed.

tasks.label: Mix feed, additives, and medicines in prescribed portions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy operation: worker loads a TMR mixer wagon or feed center per the nutritionist's ration sheet — scoops corn silage and haylage from bunkers, adds hay, high-moisture corn, protein pellets and a weighed mineral/additive premix (e.g., ionophore, buffer, yeast) — mixes for the prescribed time and checks batch weights before the ration is delivered to group bunks.

Beef feedlot / backgrounding yard: batching pen rations at the mill or on the mixer truck, including micro-ingredients and medicated additives (ionophores, chlortetracycline under a VFD) weighed to the gram per pen and mixed into the load, with records kept for feed-safety compliance.

Swine or poultry barn: preparing phase diets and medicated rations — on-farm mixing/batching of ground grain with premix and drug, or dosing medication and vitamin/electrolyte additives into the liquid feed or drinking water line at the prescribed inclusion rate for a room or barn.

Calf/lamb rearing: mixing milk replacer powder with warm water to the prescribed concentration and temperature for each feeding, adding electrolytes, vitamins or vet-prescribed medication to individual animals' portions, and cleaning the mixing equipment.

Individual-animal rations in a barn feed room: horses, show stock or small ruminants — scooping and weighing grain per each animal's feed chart into buckets, adding supplements (mineral, joint, hoof) and top-dressing prescribed powders/pastes for specific animals, twice daily.

Aquaculture hatchery or grow-out facility: preparing feed for tanks/ponds — selecting pellet sizes and quantities per tank per the feed table, blending starter/micro diets, and mixing or top-coating feed with vitamins or prescribed medication before feeding.

tasks.label: Shift animals between grazing areas to ensure that they have sufficient access to food.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beef cow-calf or stocker herd on a fenced farm/ranch pasture: worker checks forage, opens a gate or sets a temporary poly-wire break, moves the herd (on foot, ATV, or with a dog) into the fresh paddock, checks water and back-fences behind them. Muddy, hilly or brushy ground; calves, stragglers and weather all vary.

Extensive western rangeland: cattle scattered over hundreds to thousands of acres must be gathered and pushed to a new pasture or off a riparian/overgrazed area, often several miles on horseback or ATV over rough, largely unfenced country with poor connectivity.

Pasture-based dairy: herd shifted to a fresh grazing break once or twice daily around milking - new break allocated, herd moved out of the paddock down a lane or into the next break, back-fence set to protect regrowth.

Sheep or goat flock moved to a fresh paddock, cell or browse area on a small-to-mid-size operation, typically with dogs or a feed bucket, sometimes across a farm lane; animals are agile and prone to testing boundaries, and terrain includes brush and woods.

Horses and other equines on a boarding or breeding farm: individual animals haltered and led from stall or dry lot out to a grazing paddock (and back), or small groups walked through gates, with attention to pairing, gate handling and horse behavior.
Stock trailered to a distant or leased grazing tract: sort the group in a corral, load onto a trailer through a chute, haul on public roads, unload and settle the animals in the new pasture.
