tasks.label: Protect herds from predators, using trained dogs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fenced farm/ranch pasture (sheep, goats, or cow-calf) with one to three livestock guardian dogs living with the stock: worker hauls feed and water to the dogs in the pasture daily, checks their body condition, collars and injuries, verifies each dog is bonded and staying with its group rather than roaming, walks fence lines, and gets up at night when the dogs bark to run off coyotes or a neighbor's dog. Mud, snow, heat, uneven ground, stock scattered over dozens of acres.

Open range / large allotment band of sheep or cattle: guardian dogs and herding dogs travel with the band across miles of rough country. Worker packs or hauls dog feed to remote camps every few days, moves dogs with the stock between grazing units, beds sheep at night in predator country, reads wolf/bear/coyote sign, and uses herding dogs to gather and hold the band away from a threat.

Farmstead/barnyard operation: pastured poultry, calves, or lambing/kidding stock kept in lots near the buildings with a guardian dog on duty. At dusk the worker moves birds or young stock into pens and closes them, feeds and checks the yard dog, keeps it in the correct lot and away from visitors and equipment, and turns stock back out in the morning.

Selecting, raising and training the dogs: bonding guardian pups with lambs or kids in a barn pen and then a small paddock, correcting chasing, wool-pulling or roaming, socializing pups to handlers and stock, introducing a young dog to the working group, and training/handling herding dogs to gather and hold stock. Includes vaccinations, worming and vet care for the dogs.

High-risk period or active predator incident: nightly patrols with dogs during lambing/calving or after a confirmed kill, using herding dogs to gather stock into a night pen or lighted lot, walking pastures at dawn to find and inspect carcasses, doctoring an injured guardian dog or mauled animal, and coordinating with USDA Wildlife Services or state biologists on nonlethal measures.

sources.system: USDA Wildlife Services / National Wildlife Research Center drone hazing program (Klamath Basin, Oregon)
sources.developer: USDA APHIS Wildlife Services / National Wildlife Research Center
sources.title: Drones vs Wolves - Offrange (Ambrook)
sources.claim: USDA Wildlife Services' most advanced predator-hazing tool for protecting cattle from wolves is a small drone flown by a human pilot with a visual observer; the drone detects wolves with thermal cameras and hazes them with a speaker under continuous human control.

sources.system: NWRC/Colorado State remote-controlled coyote-deterrent vehicle (with Krebs Livestock)
sources.developer: USDA National Wildlife Research Center, Colorado State University et al.
sources.title: How robot ranch hands could protect livestock from predators (New Atlas)
sources.claim: The closest research analogue to a robotic substitute for guardian dogs on sheep pasture — a light-equipped ground vehicle that chased coyotes off at night — was a remote-controlled vehicle, with autonomous weatherproof versions described by the researchers as a future challenge.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (keeping predators off livestock on pasture); cited to show the state of the art is human-piloted rather than autonomous.

sources.title: Börsgården Farm case study — Flox
sources.claim: Flox's autonomous drone deterrence system ran a full four-month season at a Swedish farm, detecting and herding geese away from crop fields with 97% efficiency — autonomous wildlife deterrence in an open field, but protecting crops from herbivorous birds rather than protecting a herd from predators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drone drives nuisance wildlife out of a protected area on a farm. Transfer to this task fails: the system guards a crop field against geese, not a moving flock against canid predators, works daylight sorties rather than continuous night presence with livestock, and does nothing with guardian dogs.

sources.system: Flox autonomous drone wildlife management system at Swedavia airports
sources.title: Swedavia Airports - Flox
sources.claim: Flox's autonomous drone system was ... at three Swedish airports to detect, identify and move wildlife off airside areas — autonomous wildlife dispersal inside an institution-controlled facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection and dispersal of animals in a structured facility (airport). Transfer fails for herd protection: the protected asset is pavement and aircraft, the animals moved are birds and deer, and no livestock, night-long guarding, or dog handling is involved.

sources.system: Aerial Fences ranch drone operation (DJI Dock 2 + FlytBase)
sources.title: How Aerial Fences is Automating Ranch Security and Oversight using Autonomous Drones Powered by FlytBase
sources.claim: A drone-in-a-box system flew fully autonomous patrol missions over a 120-acre Texas ranch, giving early detection of fence damage ... coyote/predator activity and reducing travel — an autonomous system that senses and reports, but does not deter predators or handle animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial surveillance of a working ranch, including predator activity. Transfer fails because detection and alerting is only the monitoring half of the task; the system takes no action against a predator and cannot deploy, feed or supervise guardian dogs.

sources.developer: US Army Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC)
sources.title: Robot Coyotes Join U.S. Army to Guard Airfields as Wildlife Control (Thomasnet)
sources.claim: The US Army ERDC's 'Coyote Rover' predator-mimicking ground robot used to clear wildlife from military airfields is remote-controlled; autonomous navigation and species identification are still being added.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile robotic animal deterrence on institution-controlled ground. Cited to show that even in the most structured outdoor setting the mobile deterrent robot is still human-driven, so it cannot support autonomous herd protection.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: Meet SwagBot, the AI-powered robot cattle herder preventing soil degradation (The Globe and Mail)
sources.claim: SwagBot autonomously navigates paddocks and moves cattle between pastures, showing that autonomous ground mobility and low-stress livestock movement are possible on rangeland — but the system does no predator deterrence and no dog work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous movement of livestock in open paddocks, comparable terrain and animals. Transfer fails for this task because nothing in the demonstrations addresses detecting or repelling predators, guarding stock overnight, or raising, feeding and directing guardian dogs.

sources.title: "Monster wolf" robots in high demand to scare off bears in Japan after record number of attacks - CBS News
sources.claim: The 'Monster Wolf' animatronic scarecrow, sold commercially in Japan and installed beside fields and towns, uses sensor-triggered sound and flashing eyes to scare off bears and wild boar; it is a fixed sound-and-light device with no documented record of guarding a livestock herd to a stockman's standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated deterrence of large wild animals from a farm area. Transfer fails: the unit is stationary, protects crops and village edges rather than a grazing herd, cannot follow stock, respond to an attack, or perform any of the dog husbandry the task consists of.

tasks.label: Order food for animals, and arrange for its delivery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform duties related to livestock reproduction, such as breeding animals within appropriate timeframes, performing artificial inseminations, and helping with animal births.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy herd breeding: worker reviews heat-detection alerts/activity-collar lists, locks target cows in headlocks or a palpation rail in the freestall barn, thaws and loads semen straws, then rectally palpates each cow to grasp the cervix and pass the AI gun to deposit semen in the uterine body; also gives synchronization-protocol injections and records the service.

Swine breeding barn: worker moves a boar down the alley for back-pressure heat checking, then inseminates standing sows in stalls or ESF group pens — wiping the vulva, inserting and locking a spiral/foam catheter into the cervix, and controlling semen flow over several minutes per sow, dozens of sows per breeding day.

Calving in a barn maternity pen: worker checks springing cows/heifers overnight, evaluates progress of a dystocia, reaches in to reposition a malpresented calf, applies OB chains and a calf jack, then clears airways, dips the navel, and gets colostrum into the newborn.

Farrowing house attendance: worker monitors sows in crates during farrowing, sleeves in to assist a stuck piglet, dries and revives weak piglets, ensures nursing/split-suckling, handles retained placenta or a down sow, and cross-fosters litters.

Turkey/broiler breeder house AI crew: catchers pick hens off the floor and present/hold them on an AI chair or pit system while an inseminator everts the cloaca and deposits a semen straw dose; toms are collected by abdominal massage earlier in the day; hundreds to thousands of birds per shift on a weekly cycle.

Pasture/range breeding and birthing for beef cattle, sheep, goats, and horses: turning bulls/rams out with groups, checking pastures for calving/lambing, catching and restraining an animal in the field or a portable chute to assist a birth, pairing up ewes and lambs in jugs, and reviving chilled newborns in mud, cold, or at night.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Lely's Astronaut A5 milking robot autonomously cleans the udder and attaches teat cups with a laser-guided arm on cows in commercial dairy barns — the most advanced deployed example of autonomous manipulation on a live cow — but it acts only on the udder exterior and performs no reproductive procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = machine milking. It shows autonomous sensing and contact with a live cow in a barn, but teat-cup attachment on an external, fixed-geometry organ does not transfer to intra-rectal/intra-cervical manipulation for insemination or to repositioning a malpresented fetus, which require internal tactile search and force control with high injury risk.

sources.system: Collectis automated boar semen collection system
sources.title: FAQ - Collectis - IMV Technologies Global
sources.claim: Collectis is the only commercial automated boar semen collection system, used in AI studs worldwide; a technician still handles the boar and hooks the artificial vagina to the penis, with a PLC controlling pressure — i.e., machine-actuated but human-performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = semen collection, an adjacent reproduction duty. It fails to substantiate autonomous completion because a technician must position the boar and attach the device each time; the machine only regulates pressure.

sources.developer: Various (review by Chen et al., Agriculture/MDPI)
sources.title: Research Progress of Robotic Technologies and Applications in Smart Pig Farms
sources.claim: A January 2026 peer-reviewed review of robotics in intelligent pig farms finds current applications limited to inspection, cleaning, and feeding robots — no breeding, insemination, or farrowing-assistance robots are reported.
sources.transferJustification: Survey of the same facility type (breeding/farrowing barns). It establishes the state of the art there — inspection, cleaning, feeding — and shows no cited system performs insemination or birth assistance.

sources.title: Automated Sow Heat Detection - NEDAP Livestock Management (pig333)
sources.claim: Nedap's automated sow heat detection system in group gestation housing autonomously paint-marks sows identified as in heat and alerts staff; the insemination itself is still performed by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = estrus detection, a sub-step of 'breeding within appropriate timeframes'. It automates identification and marking only; the physical breeding act remains human, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.system: Georgia Tech floor-egg collecting robot; sow farrowing monitoring systems
sources.developer: Georgia Tech Research Institute and others
sources.title: Improved animal welfare and greater efficiency through AI and robotics - THE FURROW
sources.claim: Trade coverage of AI and robotics in livestock farming as of 2026 describes monitoring systems for farrowing sows and a floor-egg-collecting robot for broiler breeder houses nearing commercialization; no robot performing insemination or assisting births is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = floor-egg collection inside breeder houses, the same buildings where turkey/broiler breeder AI occurs. It shows mobile robots can navigate bird houses and pick up eggs, but not catch, restrain, and inseminate live hens.

tasks.label: Patrol grazing lands on horseback or using all-terrain vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine check of large open pastures/rangeland on an extensive cow-calf outfit: drive the two-tracks on an ATV/UTV, locate and count the herd, eyeball them from the vehicle, verify water tanks/troughs are full and pumps running, glance over fence lines and gates; on most days nothing needs fixing and the output is a report that everything is accounted for.

Horseback patrol of rough country a vehicle cannot reach - steep, brushy, timbered range or a Forest Service allotment: locate cattle scattered in cover and draws, ride close enough to look each bunch over, and push strays back toward the main herd or water.

Close-inspection patrol through the herd during calving/lambing or a disease-risk period: repeated passes (often at dawn, dusk, night, in cold or mud) examining individual animals - heifers close to calving, newborn pairs, animals off feed, lame, or with pinkeye/scours - and flagging which need attention.

Patrol that turns into hands-on work encountered en route: opening and closing wire gates, clearing a stuck float valve or frozen tank, splicing a downed fence wire, freeing a bogged or entangled animal, roping and doctoring a sick calf in the pasture, dropping off mineral or salt blocks.

Feedlot or drylot pen riding: daily morning ride through the pens on horseback checking each pen of cattle for early signs of respiratory disease or lameness, and cutting the affected animals out and driving them down the alley to the hospital pen; fixed pen/alley layout, company-controlled premises.

Small operation near the farmstead: short ATV loop around flat improved pastures holding sheep, goats, horses or a small cow herd - headcount, check water and mineral, walk/ride the fence line, look for predator or loose-dog sign.

sources.developer: GrazeMate / Brumby (Sam Rogers), on DJI airframes
sources.title: Robot cowboys: GrazeMate bets on fully autonomous cattle mustering drones (AgFunderNews)
sources.claim: GrazeMate/Brumby operates autonomous drones on commercial cattle stations that fly scheduled missions to move and locate cattle and to photograph water troughs and fence lines, run from an app without an operator flying the aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Mustering plus trough/fence imaging is the same traverse-and-observe function as a check ride over the same open grazing land; the article states the drones photograph troughs and fence lines so ranchers can see if action is needed.

sources.system: Halter smart cattle collars (virtual fencing / active guidance)
sources.title: U.S. Ranchers Create 11,000 Miles of Virtual Fencing With Halter's Smart Cattle Collars
sources.claim: Halter smart collars are deployed commercially across US ranches, autonomously holding virtual paddock boundaries, actively guiding cattle movement, and providing real-time location and behaviour monitoring of every animal on rangeland.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborating only: continuous machine-delivered location/behaviour data on rangeland substitutes for the 'are they all there and where are they' output of a patrol, though the device is worn rather than a mobile robot.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: Robot Leads Cattle to Greener Fields (VOA / Reuters imagery, Allynbrook, Australia)
sources.claim: SwagBot drives itself around grazing paddocks on a working property, judging pasture condition and observing cattle, and moves the cattle between areas.

sources.system: Poultry Patrol autonomous barn monitoring robot
sources.title: Veterinary Angel Network invests in Poultry Patrol's autonomous barn monitoring robots (WATTPoultry)
sources.claim: Poultry Patrol's robot autonomously patrols livestock barns around the clock, moving among the animals and identifying health, welfare and equipment issues between human visits; proof of concept demonstrated in trials at commercial turkey barns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = patrolling livestock housing to check stock: same traverse-observe-flag loop as a pasture check ride, performed among live animals inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: Autonomous inspection robot for dead laying hens
sources.developer: research group publishing in Computers and Electronics in Agriculture
sources.title: Autonomous inspection robot for dead laying hens in caged layer house (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: An autonomous inspection robot drives the aisles of a caged layer house and detects and localises hens needing attention with about 90% accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic stock-checking rounds inside an animal facility; it substantiates that an autonomous mobile robot can cover a livestock building on a schedule and flag individual animals needing attention.

sources.title: Barn cleaner for solid floors | Lely Discovery Collector
sources.claim: Lely's Discovery Collector drives pre-programmed routes autonomously through occupied dairy barns, navigating among free-moving cows, alleys and waiting areas; it is a widely sold commercial product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = repeated autonomous routes through a facility full of loose cattle; it substantiates the mobility and animal-avoidance half of a patrol inside a structured livestock facility.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit / autonomous inspection rounds
sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds - thermal, visual and acoustic - in industrial facilities, and is operating at hundreds of sites worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous patrol/inspection rounds of an institution-controlled work facility with anomaly detection and reporting; the perception-and-report deliverable matches a patrol's output, on maintained but human-built premises.

sources.developer: SkyKelpie with MLA and Queensland DPI
sources.title: SkyKelpie trials autonomous cattle mustering in Queensland (ITBrief)
sources.claim: SkyKelpie demonstrated autonomous drone mustering of livestock in paddock trials in Queensland with Meat & Livestock Australia and ... state primary industries department.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that autonomous aerial systems can work stock over open paddocks taken as found, the same terrain a check ride covers.

tasks.label: Maintain growth, feeding, production, and cost records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Groom, clip, trim, or castrate animals, dock ears and tails, or shear coats to collect hair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Farrowing-barn piglet processing on a commercial swine unit: a worker takes each day-old piglet from the crate, clips needle teeth, docks the tail, notches ears, and surgically castrates the males, working through hundreds of squirming piglets per day in an indoor, climate-controlled barn with sows present.

Working calves and lambs at a ranch or feedlot: animals are gathered into corrals and restrained in a squeeze chute, head-catch or marking cradle (or flanked on the ground at a branding); the worker band- or knife-castrates, docks lamb tails, disbuds/dehorns, and ear-marks animals of varying size and temperament in dusty outdoor pens.

Shearing sheep in a shearing shed or portable shearing trailer: catch and drag each sheep from the catching pen, position it on the board, remove the fleece intact with an electric handpiece in roughly 2-4 minutes without skin cuts or second cuts, and throw the fleece; also crutching and belly-wool removal.

Grooming and clipping horses at a boarding, breeding or training barn: currying, brushing, and vacuuming the coat, picking hooves, pulling/trimming manes and tails, trimming bridle paths, fetlocks and whiskers with clippers, on animals held in crossties or a stall that shift, lean and object.

Cattle coat clipping and hoof work: body-clipping and fitting dairy or beef animals for show and sale prep with clippers and blowers, plus routine claw trimming of dairy cows restrained in a hydraulic tilt or upright trimming chute.

Poultry hatchery/brooder-house beak and toe treatment: day-old chicks or poults are processed at a hatchery station where each bird's beak (and turkey toes) is trimmed/treated, along with vaccination and counting, at a rate of thousands of birds per hour before boxing for delivery.

sources.system: Nova-Tech Poultry Service Processor (PSP) / Infrared Beak Treatment
sources.title: How infra-red beak trimming for layers works - Farmers Weekly
sources.claim: Nova-Tech Engineering's Poultry Service Processor (PSP) is a hatchery machine that performs infrared beak treatment, vaccination and counting on day-old chicks; an operator loads chicks into rubber head-holding mounts four at a time and the machine executes the beak treatment automatically (sub-second infrared flash with adjustable intensity) and sorts the chicks into boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Beak treatment is the poultry form of the task's 'clip/trim' verbs (de-beaking is named among this occupation's duties); the machine performs the cutting/treatment step itself on live birds presented in its fixtures.

sources.title: Nova-Tech Poultry - Nova-Tech Engineering
sources.claim: Infrared beak treatment equipment has been commercialised since 1997 and Nova-Tech poultry equipment is in use at over 600 hatchery locations in 69 countries, i.e. it is the standard deployed method of beak trimming rather than a prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: establishes deployment scale of the machine that performs poultry beak trimming.

sources.system: AWI Robotic Assisted Shearing Scoping Study / smart shearing handpiece
sources.developer: Australian Wool Innovation with 4c Design and partners
sources.title: Wool Harvesting Innovations | Australian Wool Innovation
sources.claim: As of its current research program, Australian Wool Innovation's robotic shearing work is a scoping study in which robotic arms mimic shearing motions on a life-size 3D-printed sheep; the parallel handpiece work is only a semi-automated hand tool. No robot is shearing live sheep in production.

sources.system: Shear Magic Robot (SM Robot / SLAMP manipulator)
sources.title: UWA Agricultural Engineering Legacy — Centre for Engineering Innovation
sources.claim: The only known automatic shearing of a live sheep was the University of Western Australia 'Shear Magic' robot, which in February 1989 shore a sheep with intact fleece on an automatic restraint and manipulation platform; the robot was used only until 1993 and part of it is now a museum-style display.

sources.system: UWA robotic shearing program (ORACLE / Shear Magic)
sources.title: Redefining Robotics for the New Millenium — James Trevelyan
sources.claim: The project leader's own retrospective records that the 1989 automatic loading-and-shearing demonstration took 25 minutes per sheep and that remaining effort had to be aimed at reliability and shearing time; the program ended in 1994 without a working production system.

sources.title: Research Progress of Robotic Technologies and Applications in Smart Pig Farms
sources.claim: A 2026 review of robotic technology in pig farming enumerates the application classes that exist — inspection, feeding, cleaning, semen-delivery, bionic and herding robots — with no robot performing piglet castration, tail docking or teeth clipping.

tasks.label: Spray livestock with disinfectants and insecticides, or dip or bathe animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beef cattle worked through a ranch corral or feedlot processing facility: cattle are gathered into pens and run up an alley/chute, and the worker sprays each animal with insecticide (horn fly, lice, tick, mange) using a hand wand or a mounted spray box, or pushes them through a dip/spray-dip. Dusty, muddy, animals moving and stressed.

Grazing beef cows/stockers on pasture or open range: worker delivers external-parasite treatment away from a handling facility - charging and positioning animal-activated walk-through sprayers, backrubbers and dust bags at water/mineral gateways, or spot-spraying animals from an ATV/truck in the field. Uneven terrain, free-moving animals, weather.

Dairy herd: routine application of teat disinfectant (pre- and post-milking dipping/spraying) on every cow every milking in a parlor or rotary, plus spraying cows with insecticide for flies at the parlor exit or in the freestall barn. High throughput, fixed layout, wet concrete.

Confinement swine and poultry houses: applying disinfectant or insecticide as a spray/mist over animals and their pens (mange/lice spray on pigs, sanitizing mist over litter and birds during disease pressure, disinfecting rooms between groups), and hosing/washing sows or market hogs. Enclosed building, animals present, ammonia and dust.

Sheep and goats in yards: plunge or shower dipping, or running the mob through a jetting/spray race to treat lice and prevent flystrike; wool must be wetted to skin level. Seasonal, large numbers, animals mobbed through a race.

Individual animals bathed or hand-treated: horses washed and rinsed in a barn wash rack or outside, show cattle/pigs washed and scrubbed before sale, medicated dips/shampoos on an individual sick or parasitized animal, and hand application of fly spray around face, legs and udder. One animal at a time, handled on a lead or in a stall.

sources.title: DeLaval teat spray robot wins AgTech Breakthrough Award - DeLaval
sources.claim: DeLaval's TSR2 teat spray robot is a commercial robotic arm with machine vision that autonomously identifies each cow's teats and applies pre- and post-milking disinfectant in rotary milking parlours, with claimed spray accuracy up to 99%.
sources.transferJustification: Applying teat disinfectant to dairy cows is directly the task's 'spray livestock with disinfectants' performed on live animals.

sources.title: DeLaval Teat Spray Robot (TSR) sales continue to grow in America - DeLaval
sources.claim: The DeLaval TSR teat spray robot has been sold and installed on commercial rotary dairies in North America since the mid-2010s, i.e. it is a deployed product rather than a demonstration.

sources.system: Animal-activated cattle sprayers (battery- and solar-powered walk-through units)
sources.developer: various commercial manufacturers (per University of Arkansas Extension)
sources.title: Controlling Horn Flies on Cattle - University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture Extension
sources.claim: Animal-activated livestock sprayers - machine-controlled units that detect an animal with a switch or electronic eye and spray insecticide onto it as it passes through a gateway or parlor exit - are commercially available and extension-recommended for treating cattle for horn flies with no worker present.

sources.title: The Cow Sprayer - Fussell Farms
sources.claim: A commercially sold automated walk-through cattle sprayer applies insecticide over the whole animal (face, back, sides, belly) automatically as each animal passes through a steel frame, with no operator handling the spray equipment.

sources.system: JetEzy automatic jetting race (also Te Pari Sheep Jetter)
sources.developer: Peak Hill Industries; Te Pari Products
sources.title: Automatic Jetting Race JetEzy - Peak Hill Industries
sources.claim: Sensor-triggered automatic jetting races spray sheep with parasiticide at top, bottom and sides as the animals move down the race, wetting the fleece to skin level; these are standard commercial sheep-handling equipment.

sources.title: Poultry Technology: Rise of the robots | Canadian Poultry
sources.claim: The Octopus Poultry Safe robot moves autonomously through commercial poultry houses delivering liquid disinfectant/sanitizer until the target area is saturated, performing the sanitation spraying otherwise done by workers with sprayers inside the house.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying disinfectant spray throughout an occupied animal house (litter, floor, birds' immediate environment) rather than to one animal; same liquid, nozzles, building and biosecurity purpose, so it carries to flock-level disinfectant application.

sources.title: Robots for Precision Poultry and Egg Production | Precision Poultry Farming, University of Georgia
sources.claim: University extension review confirms the Octopus Poultry Safe robot was tested in poultry houses, sanitizing house and floor by delivering liquid ..., among robots designed to work alongside live birds.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: flock/house-level disinfectant spraying inside an occupied livestock building.

sources.title: EVO Cleaner for pig barns - Envirologic
sources.claim: Envirologic's EVO Cleaner is a commercially sold washing robot that automatically washes and disinfects pig barn pens around the clock after being taught the routine, replacing a worker with a pressure washer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and disinfecting the pens that hold pigs rather than the pigs themselves; shows autonomous wash/disinfect spraying inside a swine barn, but does not substantiate washing live animals.

roles.title: Agricultural Workers, All Other
aliases: Disease and Insect Control Field Inspector
roles.description: All agricultural workers not listed separately.

roles.title: Fishing and Hunting Workers
roles.description: Hunt, trap, catch, or gather wild animals or aquatic animals and plants. May use nets, traps, or other equipment. May haul catch onto ship or other vessel.

tasks.label: Steer vessels and operate navigational instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Transit from port to the fishing grounds and back aboard a 40-90 ft commercial fishing vessel: plot the route on the chartplotter, engage the autopilot, monitor radar/AIS/depth sounder, keep a lookout and adjust heading and speed for traffic, weather and sea state in coastal and offshore water.

Handling the vessel during active gear work: towing a trawl or dredge along a tow track, steering while shooting and hauling gillnets, longlines, seines or pots, backing down and holding the boat off the gear so it stays clear of the wheel, matching the deck crew's pace and the sonar picture.

Running a small open skiff or outboard boat inshore - bays, river mouths, tidal flats, kelp beds - among shoals, floating debris, crab-pot buoys and other boats' gear, at working speed, steering by tiller or console with a handheld GPS/plotter and sounder.
Harbor work: navigating narrow marked channels and a crowded fishing harbor, unberthing, coming alongside the offload dock, fuel float or ice dock in wind and current, and tying up.
Navigating in adverse conditions - fog, darkness, heavy seas, ice, or crowded fishing grounds with unlit gear and other working vessels - making close-quarters radar/COLREGS decisions.

sources.title: First Seafloor Mapping Mission in Gulf of Maine - Saildrone
sources.claim: Saildrone Voyager USVs (33 ft) run uncrewed near-shore seafloor-mapping missions in the Gulf of Maine for NOAA, moving autonomously between predetermined waypoints while carrying AIS, radar and cameras, with staff at Mission Control monitoring remotely 24/7 rather than steering continuously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncrewed hydrographic survey. It is the same act rated here - steering a small vessel and working navigational instruments (GPS/plotter, radar, AIS, echo sounder) in coastal water - on a hull comparable in size to an inshore fishing skiff.

sources.developer: Saildrone Inc. / NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center
sources.title: Autonomous Alaska Pollock Survey Begins in the Bering Sea - Saildrone
sources.claim: Saildrone USVs transited over 2,000 nm from San Francisco to the ... and then ran a 60-day acoustic pollock survey for NOAA Fisheries, i.e. long unattended ocean passages and survey tracks in the same waters commercial fishing vessels work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acoustic fish-stock survey. The vessel-handling component - passage planning, autopilot course keeping and traffic avoidance offshore - is the same as a fishing vessel's run to the grounds, in the same Bering Sea conditions.

sources.system: SM300 autonomous command and control on tug Nellie Bly
sources.title: Sea Machines completes world's first 1,000-nautical-mile autonomous voyage | WorkBoat
sources.claim: The commercial ocean tug Nellie Bly, fitted with Sea Machines' SM300, ran a 1,027 nm voyage around Denmark almost entirely under autonomous control, executing dozens of collision-avoidance and traffic-separation maneuvers itself while USCG-licensed mariners supervised remotely from Boston.

sources.title: Sea Machines Robotics delivers autonomous tech for conventional marine operations | WorkBoat
sources.claim: Sea Machines' SM300/SM200 are sold as retrofit autonomy for existing commercial workboats and are reported in use in North America ..., providing waypoint/mission following, obstacle detection and collision avoidance from sensor to propeller.

sources.system: SM300 on Marco skimming vessel (MARAD/MSRC demonstration)
sources.title: World's first autonomous spill response vessel demonstrated - IIMS
sources.claim: An SM300-equipped Kvichak/Marco skimmer boat - a small working craft towing recovery gear - was commanded from shore in Portland, Maine harbor to perform autonomous waypoint tracking, autonomous grid-line tracking and multi-vessel collaborative operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spill-response line running. Same boat class (small aluminum workboat), same act of steering to a planned track inside a harbor using electronic charts, so it transfers to inshore skiff and harbor navigation.

sources.system: Fully autonomous Smart Coastal Ferry (SUPER BRIDGE-X), MEGURI2040
sources.developer: Mitsubishi Shipbuilding / Shin Nihonkai Ferry / The Nippon Foundation
sources.title: MEGURI 2040 Successful Demonstration Test of World's First Fully Autonomous Ship Navigation Systems on Coastal Ferry | Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
sources.claim: The 222 m ferry Soleil navigated a 240 km coastal route fully autonomously at up to 26 knots and berthed and unberthed itself at the pier using turning and reversing maneuvers, with infrared cameras detecting other ships in darkness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coastal ferry navigation and berthing. The acts rated here - steering to a route, radar/IR-based traffic avoidance, and bringing the hull alongside a pier - are the same, at larger scale and tighter tolerance than a fishing boat's dock landing.

sources.system: DFFAS+ autonomous navigation system (GENBU, Olympia Dream Seto, Hokuren Maru No.2 and others)
sources.developer: DFFAS+ consortium (MOL, NYK/MTI, JRC and partners) / The Nippon Foundation
sources.title: MEGURI2040 Stage 2 Achievements Announced: Four Demonstration Vessels Obtain Japanese Government Certification as Autonomous Ships | MOL
sources.claim: Under MEGURI2040 Stage 2, four vessels (a coastal container ship, a 66 m island passenger ferry, a RORO and another) were verified for Level 4-equivalent autonomous ... during commercial operations and certified as autonomous ships by Japan's MLIT, including in the congested, reef-strewn Seto Inland Sea; humans monitor and intervene only when needed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coastal cargo/passenger ship navigation. Steering to a planned route and working radar/ECDIS/AIS for collision avoidance is the identical duty a fishing skipper performs on passage; certification was earned in congested coastal water fishing vessels also use.

sources.developer: NYK/MTI and DFFAS consortium, The Nippon Foundation
sources.title: 5th Demonstration Test of Fully Autonomous Ship Navigation Successfully Completed | The Nippon Foundation
sources.claim: The 95 m container ship Suzaku completed a 790 km round trip in and out of heavily congested Tokyo Bay under a comprehensive fully autonomous navigation ..., with a shore-based fleet operation center monitoring and available to take over.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coastal cargo navigation in dense traffic. Close-quarters COLREGS decision-making with radar/AIS is the same skill the instance requires; Tokyo Bay traffic density exceeds most fishing grounds.

tasks.label: Remove catches from fishing equipment and measure them to ensure compliance with legal size.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pot/trap fishery (Maine lobster, Chesapeake blue crab, Dungeness/stone crab): pot hauled over the rail by a hydraulic hauler onto a small open boat's deck at sea; worker opens the trap door, pulls each animal out of the parlor by hand (often tangled in mesh, clawed, mixed with bycatch and debris), gauges carapace against a brass gauge, checks eggs/v-notch, bands keepers, throws shorts back, rebaits and resets. Wet, pitching deck, weather and spray.

Gillnet fishery (Alaska salmon drift/set net, Great Lakes, inshore Gulf): net comes over a roller or drum; worker picks individually entangled fish out of the mesh one at a time without tearing the web, identifies species, checks size, retains legal fish in the hold and releases undersize/prohibited species. Small open boat at sea or in a river mouth.

Longline / hook-and-line fishery (Alaska halibut and sablefish, Gulf reef fish, salmon troll): fish are hauled to the rail on hooks, gaffed aboard, unhooked, then measured against a fixed minimum length (e.g., 32-inch halibut) with a measuring board or rail marks; undersize fish are released. Open working deck at sea.

Trawl / purse seine bulk catch (Gulf shrimp trawler, Northeast/Alaska groundfish or pelagic vessel): codend hauled aboard and emptied into a hopper or onto the deck, or catch pumped from the net; the mixed catch is separated from bycatch and graded, undersize and prohibited catch returned to the sea, keepers iced or processed. Sorting occurs on a deck or in an onboard processing space.

Dredge and hand shellfish harvest (sea scallop, surfclam/quahog, oyster, whelk): dredge or rake emptied onto a culling board or conveyor; worker culls out undersize animals, shell, rock and trash, checking size with a ring gauge or ruler, and shovels keepers into baskets. Open deck of a working boat.

Inland and small-scale trap/net work (crawfish traps in ponds and basins, fyke/hoop nets, eel and whelk pots, bait operations): worker lifts each trap by hand or over a puller, shakes the catch into a basket or grading box, culls undersize animals and bycatch back to the water, rebaits and resets from a shallow-draft boat.

sources.date: retrieved 2026-07 (undated vessel reference page; Carsoe onboard shrimp factories delivered from ~2019 onward)
sources.title: Regina C trawler | Onboard Shrimp Processing From Carsoe
sources.claim: Carsoe supplies a complete onboard shrimp factory on the trawler Regina C that automatically separates bycatch from the catch and grades the shrimp by size, with no manual sorting step in the line.

sources.title: Shrimp Sorting Equipment | Kerian Speed Sizer - Kerian Machines
sources.claim: The Kerian Speed Sizer is a commercially sold roller sizer that grades head-on shrimp, crawfish, whelk and mussels by size and is used both aboard fishing boats and on the dock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: size-grading of the landed catch. It performs the 'measure to ensure size compliance' half of this task mechanically, on the same animals (shrimp, crawfish, whelk) and in the same onboard setting, but it does not remove catch from gear.

sources.system: Kerian Speed Sizer on Gulf shrimp vessels (Anna Maria Shrimp)
sources.developer: Kerian Machines Inc. / Louisiana Sea Grant
sources.title: Making the grade: Gulf shrimpers take on new tech for a premium product | National Fisherman
sources.claim: Gulf shrimpers have run mixed-size head-on shrimp through the Kerian grader repeatedly without quality damage and use on-deck grading to control size uniformity aboard the vessel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-deck size grading of trawl catch; same fishery, same vessel deck, same size-compliance judgment, but the machine is fed by hand rather than emptying the codend itself.

sources.system: Optimar Vision Grader / species recognition system
sources.title: Fish and seafood processing machines and equipment | Optimar
sources.claim: Optimar's Vision Grader, sold for onboard and shore fish factories, sorts whole fish automatically by species and by size measured from length and volume.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic species and size sorting of whole fish on a conveyor. It substantiates the measuring/culling half of the task inside a purpose-built machine line, not the removal of fish from nets, hooks or pots.

sources.title: MA HC 400 E-LINE RotoCleaner - Mustad Autoline
sources.claim: Mustad Autoline's hook cleaner, fitted inline on autoline longliners, contains a fish detacher and brushes that mechanically strip remaining fish and debris off the hooks as the line is hauled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing residual fish from longline hooks. It removes leftovers to protect hook and line function; the marketable catch is still gaffed aboard and measured by crew, so it does not deliver retained, undamaged, size-checked fish.

sources.system: Onboard vacuum/fish pumps on pelagic purse seiners
sources.developer: various pump makers; practice described by Seafish
sources.title: PS - Purse Seine | Seafish
sources.claim: Modern pelagic vessels routinely empty the purse seine by pumping fish aboard with a fish pump rather than brailing them out by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk removal of catch from the net. The pump is a machine, but the suction head is placed and tended by crew and a crane, so autonomy is not established; it is context only and is not decisive for any judgment.

sources.title: Automation helping oyster farmers - Shellquip
sources.claim: SED/Shellquip supplies commercial vision-based oyster graders used on shellfish farms that sort shellfish by measured size rather than by weight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: culling shellfish to a size threshold. Same objects (bivalves) and the same millimetre-scale size decision as culling undersize oysters or scallops from a dredge, but performed on a fed grading line rather than on a culling board.

sources.developer: various (e.g. Towa Denki); practice described by Seafish
sources.title: Jigging | Seafish
sources.claim: Squid jigging vessels use mechanically powered automatic jigging machines whose barbless jigs let the squid drop off the hooks onboard without hand unhooking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine removal of catch from hooks. It shows unhooking can be mechanised for one species with no legal size limit; it does not show unhooking and measuring size-regulated finfish.

sources.title: Technologies - SMARTFISH H2020
sources.claim: The EU SMARTFISH H2020 project built and sea-tested CatchScanner, a 3D machine-vision unit that analyses catch (species, length) automatically on onboard conveyor belts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic determination of species and length of catch aboard a vessel. It is a sensing module, not a manipulator, so it can only support the measuring step within an existing conveyor line.

tasks.label: Direct fishing or hunting operations, and supervise crew members.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Interpret weather and vessel conditions to determine appropriate responses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Travel on foot, by vehicle, or by equipment such as boats, snowmobiles, helicopters, snowshoes, or skis to reach hunting areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walk-in on foot from a truck, trailhead, or field edge to a stand, blind, or hunting spot: 0.25-2 miles over farm tracks, logging roads, game trails, and moderate hardwood/pine woods, carrying rifle, pack and gear, often in pre-dawn darkness.

Rugged foot travel with no trail: steep mountain slopes, boulder fields, blowdown/thick brush, cattail marsh or cypress swamp with knee-deep muck and water crossings, or breaking through deep snow, carrying a heavy pack, decoys, or traps.

Drive a pickup, ATV, UTV, or 4x4 from home/camp to the hunting area: paved and gravel county roads, then rutted two-track logging roads, mud, ditches, creek fords and steep pitches on public or leased land, sometimes towing a trailer, at dawn or after dark.

Run a skiff, jon boat, or bay boat from a ramp or dock across a lake, river, bay, or coastal marsh to reach duck blinds, trapping grounds, seaweed/shellfish beds, or set nets; wind, current, tide, floating debris and other boats en route.

Winter travel by snowmobile, snowshoes, or skis over snow-covered forest trails, frozen lakes, muskeg and open tundra to run a trapline or reach winter hunting country, in cold, snowfall and poor light.
Fly-in access to remote country: charter bush plane or helicopter to a gravel strip, lake, or ridge-top drop point for a remote hunting camp, or helicopter travel for aerial wildlife/predator work.

sources.system: RACER Fleet Vehicles / RACER Heavy Platform (DARPA RACER)
sources.developer: DARPA with Carnegie Mellon, NASA JPL, University of Washington/Overland AI teams
sources.title: RACER Speeds Into a Second Phase With Robotic Fleet Expansion and Another Experiment Success
sources.claim: DARPA's RACER program ran fully unoccupied autonomous ground vehicles over 3-10 mile courses of unimproved terrain with vegetation, trees, bushes, rocks, slopes, ditches and creek crossings, including at night, in terrain the teams had never seen before.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncrewed military off-road movement. It transfers because the physical act is identical to driving a truck/ATV to a hunting area - a full-size vehicle self-navigating unimproved two-track and cross-country terrain with brush, ruts, ditches and creek crossings, day and night.

sources.title: DARPA's RACER Program Crosses Finish Line, Puts Off-Road Autonomy in Army, Marine Corps Hands
sources.claim: At program completion the RACER autonomy stack was handed to Army and Marine Corps units, navigating complex off-road terrain without GPS or pre-mapped routes.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the RACER experiment evidence: unmapped, GPS-denied off-road route-finding is what a hunter's drive up an unmarked logging two-track requires.

sources.title: Overland AI Unveils ULTRA, a Fully Autonomous Tactical Vehicle for Ground Operations
sources.claim: Overland AI's ULTRA uncrewed ground vehicle carries 1,000 lb payloads at up to 35 mph off-road using RACER-derived autonomy, and has been used by 82nd Airborne units for autonomous resupply movement to forward locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cross-country resupply movement. Comparable vehicle class (UTV-scale), comparable terrain (unimproved backcountry, no map, no GNSS), and the objective is the same - get the platform and its load from a start point to a distant point in the field.

sources.title: Waymo's skyrocketing ridership in one chart | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Waymo operates a driverless commercial robotaxi service at scale on public roads in multiple US cities, on the order of half a million paid rides per week.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless road driving. It covers the paved/graded-road leg of travel to hunting areas (home to trailhead), which is ordinary road driving with traffic; the off-road leg is covered by the RACER/ULTRA evidence.

sources.system: WILN (Weather-Invariant Lidar-based Navigation) on Clearpath Warthog
sources.title: Kilometer-scale autonomous navigation in subarctic forests: challenges and lessons learned
sources.claim: A Clearpath Warthog UGV performed 18.8 km of autonomous navigation on subarctic forest trails through a Quebec boreal research forest during winter, in light and heavy snow, rain and darkness, with only four manual interventions over 14 repeat runs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated autonomous traverse of a known forest route in winter. A trapline circuit or a daily walk/ride to the same stand is exactly a repeated route over snow-covered forest trail, with the same GNSS-denied, low-contrast, snow-loaded conditions.

sources.system: ANYmal quadruped with DigiForest autonomy stack
sources.developer: Oxford Robotics Institute / ETH Zurich (EU DigiForest project) on ANYbotics ANYmal
sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots - System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead
sources.claim: ANYmal quadrupeds autonomously navigated and mapped under-canopy forest plots in field trials run over 18 months in forests in three European ..., surveying up to a 1 ha plot in under 30 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous under-canopy forest survey. The locomotion demand is the same as a hunter's walk-in: a legged machine covering hundreds of metres of natural forest floor with undergrowth, roots and slopes, choosing its own route to reach specified locations.

sources.system: Wild Visual Navigation on ANYmal C/D
sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / Oxford Robotics Institute
sources.title: Wild visual navigation: fast traversability learning via pre-trained models and online self-supervision
sources.claim: The ANYmal C/D quadruped was taught to navigate autonomously in woodland containing dirt, high grass and ... using self-supervised traversability learning, distinguishing walkable vegetation from real obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: off-trail legged navigation in natural vegetation. Walking to a stand through grass and brush requires exactly this judgment about which vegetation is walkable, on the same terrain type.

sources.developer: Saildrone, Inc. (for NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center)
sources.title: Autonomous Alaska Pollock Survey Begins in the Bering Sea
sources.claim: Three Saildrone uncrewed surface vehicles sailed autonomously more than 2,000 nautical miles ... California to the Bering Sea and conducted NOAA Fisheries' 60-day Alaska pollock survey in place of crewed vessels.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: an uncrewed vessel navigating itself from port out to distant fishing grounds - the marine leg of 'travel by boat to reach hunting/fishing areas' - in open coastal Alaskan waters with weather, current and traffic.

sources.system: SM300 autonomous command and control on tug Nellie Bly
sources.title: Tug Completes 1,000 Nautical Mile Autonomous Voyage Around Denmark
sources.claim: The autonomous tug Nellie Bly, running Sea Machines' SM300 autonomous command and control, completed a 1,000+ nautical mile circumnavigation of Denmark in 129 operational hours, with onboard vessel control managed by autonomous technology under remote command.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transit of a conventional workboat in coastal waters, comparable to running a work skiff to a hunting/fishing ground; recorded as unclear because the voyage was commanded by remote mariners, so it is supporting context only.

sources.title: Autonomous GPR surveys using the polar rover Yeti
sources.claim: The Yeti polar rover executed autonomous GPS-waypoint surveys over snow in Antarctica and Greenland, operating reliably at -30 C with good over-snow mobility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous over-snow traverse of a planned route. Travelling by snow machine over frozen lakes, muskeg and open snowfields to reach winter trapping country is the same mobility problem: soft snow flotation, cold, and waypoint route-following.

sources.title: Spot | Boston Dynamics / Humanoid Index entry
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped is sold commercially and runs autonomous inspection missions at power plants, construction sites, ... for operators such as National Grid, BP and Woodside ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated autonomous walking routes around industrial premises, including outdoor gravel, stairs and slopes. It shows self-directed pedestrian-style travel to designated points is routine inside institution-controlled facilities.

tasks.label: Select, bait, and set traps, and lay poison along trails, according to species, size, habits, and environs of birds or animals and reasons for trapping them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Running a land trapline for furbearers (coyote, fox, bobcat, raccoon): walking or driving fencerows, woodlots and field edges, reading sign on trails, digging dirt-hole/flat sets, bedding and staking foothold traps, applying bait and gland lure, blending and anti-freezing the set in mud, snow or frozen ground.

Water sets for beaver, muskrat, otter and mink: placing body-grip traps in creek runs, culverts, dam crossovers and bank-den entrances, castor-mound and slide sets, wiring traps to stakes in flowing or partly iced water on foot or from a small boat.

Nuisance/animal-damage-control work at private homes, farms and businesses: choosing and baiting cage or box traps for raccoons, skunks, squirrels, groundhogs or feral cats and placing them in attics, crawlspaces, decks, roofs and yards where pets, children and clutter are present.

Baiting and setting pots/traps for aquatic animals from a working vessel: stuffing bait bags or jars with herring/redfish, rigging pots for the target species and size regulations, then setting singles or trawls of pots on chosen grounds in swell and weather.

Broadcast toxic baiting of a target pest species over an area: choosing the bait product and application rate for the species and terrain, then distributing poison bait pellets across the block (island, forest, rangeland) at prescribed density with buffers around non-target areas.

Targeted poison placement: setting bait stations, burrow-baiting rodents, or placing toxic devices (e.g., M-44 cyanide capsules, strychnine baits) at points along animal trails, travel routes and den entrances, keyed to species habits and sited to avoid non-target animals, pets and people.

sources.title: Successful drone eradication in Palau paves the way for faster island restorations - Island Conservation
sources.claim: Envico Technologies drones, working with Island Conservation, have completed whole rodent eradications by broadcasting rodenticide bait over islands, including Ngerkeklau (Palau, 2022) and North Seymour (Galapagos, 2019).
sources.transferJustification: Same task element as 'lay poison ... according to species and environs': the drone performs the physical distribution of toxic bait over the target animals' habitat.

sources.title: Drones: Emergence of a transformative technology for island rodent eradications (Conservation Science and Practice)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of six drone-based rodent eradication campaigns in five Pacific nations (8-184 ha treatment areas) using Envico ENV10/ENV50 drones whose bait spreaders were activated autonomously along pre-programmed flight plans over unstructured island terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the poison-laying element of the task: bait product and application rate are prescribed for the target species, and the machine autonomously places the poison across the animals' terrain.

sources.title: About Autolining – Mustad Autoline
sources.claim: Mustad Autoline automatic baiting machines, in commercial use on hundreds of longline vessels, bait hooks at up to 6 hooks per second with 95-97% baiting success as the gear is shot from the vessel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: baiting and setting baited fishing gear for a target species from a vessel. Same bait material (whole herring/mackerel/saury) and deck environment as pot baiting, but the gear is hooks on a line rather than pots, so it substantiates only a machine-centred, fixtured presentation of the work.

sources.title: AutoBaiting – Mustad Autoline
sources.claim: The Mustad AutoBaiter machine pulls hooks and line from storage magazines, cuts and impales the bait automatically, and the baited gear is deployed over the stern of the vessel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated baiting and setting of fishing gear. Bait handling and gear deployment are machine-performed inside a purpose-built deck line, supporting an E1 fixtured presentation of baiting-and-setting pots; it shows no machine choosing or placing traps in the field.

sources.system: ProVision Ltd heavy-lift drone fleet (DJI FlyCart 30, Agras T100)
sources.title: Heavy-lift drones are transforming predator control - Predator Free NZ Trust
sources.claim: In current predator-control practice heavy-lift drones are used only to ferry traps to sites; human trappers still select the site, bait and install every trap.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (setting traps in the field) in one of the most technology-forward trapping programs; machines do transport only, with trap selection, baiting and setting still done by people.

tasks.label: Maintain engines, fishing gear, and other on-board equipment and perform minor repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underway on a 40–100 ft commercial fishing vessel (trawler, seiner, longliner): daily engine-room rounds and minor repairs — checking and topping oil/coolant, changing fuel and lube filters, bleeding fuel lines, swapping belts and raw-water impellers, tracing a hydraulic or seawater leak — in a hot, cramped, oily, pitching space with only the tools and spares aboard.

On deck at sea between sets: repairing fishing gear — mending torn trawl or gillnet webbing with needle and twine, cutting out damaged panels and hanging new mesh, splicing rope and wire, replacing chafed longline gangions and hooks, rebuilding crushed crab pots — wet, cold, rolling deck, done fast so the gear can go back in the water.

Servicing on-board deck machinery and equipment at sea: greasing winch, block and drum fittings, replacing worn hydraulic hoses, shackles and cable, clearing a jammed net reel or power block, servicing deck and bilge pumps, RSW/refrigeration and hold gear, and fault-finding on hydraulics and electronics.

In port between trips or pre-season, at the dock or in a gear shed / net loft with fixed benches, hoists and standard stock: overhauling nets and rigging spread on the loft floor, rebuilding pots and traps, renewing wire and rigging, changing engine oil, zincs and filters alongside, tuning and testing gear before the next opening.

Small-boat, subsistence and trapping operators: maintaining an outboard motor and skiff, small gillnets, fyke nets and traps, snares, ATV or snow machine — worked on at a beach, on a trailer, in a yard or home garage with hand tools and improvised parts.

sources.system: Navy STTR N25A-T023 (Robotic Manipulation Learning for Repair of Marine Diesel Engines)
sources.title: Navy - 25.A STTR - Robotic Manipulation Learning for Repair of Marine Diesel Engines
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation for maintenance of marine diesel engines is still being solicited as a research objective by the US Navy (STTR topic N25A-T023), indicating no fielded system performs engine maintenance manipulation tasks such as opening valves, replacing lids, adding fluids or fitting gaskets.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same class of work (marine diesel engine maintenance manipulation); it is stated as a goal to be demonstrated, so it substantiates that no cited system yet completes such instances.

sources.title: Fairbanks Morse Defense Expands Robotic Welding Capabilities
sources.claim: Fairbanks Morse Defense fields robotic welding that performs specific engine-component repairs (e.g., crank bore/crank line welds) in engine rooms, but the robots are pre-programmed for a single welding process with skilled technicians setting up, overseeing, inspecting and handling complex work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ repair of marine engine components. It covers only one programmed process (welding) with human setup/oversight, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of whole engine-maintenance instances.

sources.title: ANYbotics | Autonomous Legged Robots for Industrial Inspection
sources.claim: The most capable deployed autonomous mobile robots in industrial machinery spaces (ANYmal legged robots) perform inspection rounds — reading gauges, thermal and acoustic checks — not physical maintenance or repair actions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine machinery rounds in plant/engine-room-like spaces. Capability is limited to sensing and inspection, so it cannot carry over to performing maintenance actions or minor repairs.

sources.system: NetFix Fish Farm Net Patching System (PIVOT ROV)
sources.title: NetFix Fish Farm Net Patching System | Deep Trekker
sources.claim: Underwater net repair on fish farms is done with a patching kit mounted on a piloted ROV, i.e., under continuous human control rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repairing holes in netting. It is a pilot-flown ROV accessory applying a patch, so it is teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous net mending.

sources.title: Norway's Remora Robotics raises NOK 164m for its autonomous net-cleaning technology
sources.claim: The one autonomous, commercially installed net robot in the seafood sector cleans and inspects salmon-pen netting; it does not mend gear, service engines or repair deck machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintenance of netting at sea. Its scope is surface cleaning of a fixed cage net, not needle-and-twine repair of torn fishing gear or machinery servicing, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: AquaStar – Autonomous underwater system for targeted assessment and repair - SINTEF
sources.claim: Autonomous repair of holes in fish-farm nets by underwater vehicles remains an ongoing research project rather than a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous repair of netting. Stated as a development goal of an ongoing project, confirming that autonomous net repair is not yet demonstrated to worker quality.

tasks.label: Connect accessories such as floats, weights, flags, lights, or markers to nets, lines, or traps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pot/trap fishery (lobster, Dungeness/snow crab, shrimp pots): on a rolling vessel deck or open dock/gear yard, the worker splices or knots buoy warps to trap bridles, bends on the surface buoy and toggle, seizes gear-marking tags, and adds brick/rebar ballast to traps. Wet, salt-stiffened 3/8-1/2 in. line, heavy traps, weather and vessel motion.

Longline (pelagic tuna/swordfish, demersal): during setting or hauling on a moving deck, the worker clips floats and buoy lines, radio/highflyer marker buoys, weighted swivels and lightsticks onto the mainline at intervals as it pays out at speed, and unclips them on retrieval.

Gillnet hanging and repair in a shoreside net loft or gear shed: tying hanging twine to attach webbing to a corkline and leadline, adding or replacing individual corks and lead sinkers, and rigging end buoys, flags, and bycatch-reduction LED lights on the net.

Trawl or purse-seine net rigging at a commercial net shop or dock: threading/lashing plastic floats onto the headrope, shackling chain, bobbins, and weights to the footrope, and attaching marker buoys or flags to the gear before it goes aboard.

Small-scale, inland, or subsistence work: attaching marker floats, jugs, flags, or lights to trotlines, hoop nets, eel/crab pots, fyke nets, and ice-fishing tip-ups, or bending markers onto trap sets; done from a skiff, riverbank, ice, or truck bed at a remote landing.

sources.developer: National University of Singapore / Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers
sources.title: TieBot: Learning to Knot a Tie from Visual Demonstration through a Real-to-Sim-to-Real Approach
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous knot tying on a deformable object by a dual-arm robot in a fixtured laboratory setup succeeds only about half the time, far below the reliability a fishing employer would accept for gear rigging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous knot tying on a highly deformable object. Connecting floats, weights, or markers to nets and lines is fundamentally knot tying/lashing on deformable rope and webbing; the best demonstrated autonomous knotting is a lab bench demo at 50% success, so it cannot substantiate completion at worker quality.

sources.system: SGTM (Sliding and Grasping for Tangle Manipulation) on a bilateral ABB YuMi
sources.title: Autonomously Untangling Long Cables (RSS 2022)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic manipulation of long ropes/cables is a research capability demonstrated on a laboratory workspace with a bilateral robot, limited to untangling rather than attaching hardware to the line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of long deformable linear objects (rope/cable). It shows the frontier for robot rope handling is untangling thin cables on a bench, not bending buoys, weights, or markers onto wet fishing warp and netting.

sources.title: TyBot an Autonomous Rebar-Tying Robot From: Advanced Construction Robotics
sources.claim: The only autonomously deployed tying robot in the field ties wire around intersections of a regular rebar grid on bridge decks using a dedicated tying gun on a gantry; it does not handle rope, floats, or attachable hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tying of a flexible tie around objects in a field setting. Transfer fails: TyBot works only on rigid, regularly spaced crossing bars presented on screed rails, and cannot grasp rope, thread a float, or terminate a knot on a buoy line.

sources.title: Sewing Machines For Nets - Industrial Netting Machines
sources.claim: Fishing gear shops use operator-fed sewing machines to attach rope to netting; the machines are powered tools guided continuously by a human, not autonomous robots that rig gear.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: attaching rope (float/lead lines) to netting. It cannot support a positive judgment because the netting is fed and guided continuously by a human operator, i.e., not autonomous operation with limited intervention.

sources.title: Mustad Autoline Systems 2023 Catalog
sources.claim: The most widely deployed automation in commercial longline fishing automates baiting, hook handling, hauling, and line storage; attaching floats, buoy lines, flag/highflyer markers and lightsticks to the gear remains crew work.
sources.transferJustification: Same fishery and same gear: deck automation on longliners. It substantiates that deployed fishing-deck automation covers baiting and line handling only, with no machine that connects floats, weights, flags, lights, or markers to the gear.

tasks.label: Wash decks, conveyors, knives, and other equipment, using brushes, detergents, and water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At-sea washdown on a small/medium commercial fishing vessel (longliner, gillnetter, crabber, shrimper): after each haul or set, deckhand hoses the working deck with the saltwater deck hose, scrubs slime, blood, bait and scales off checkers, rails, hatch covers and sorting tables with a stiff broom/brush and detergent, rinses knives, gaffs and totes. Rolling deck, spray, cold, gear and catch strewn about, other crew working nearby.

Processing-deck sanitation aboard a factory trawler / catcher-processor or at-sea processor: at shift end, crew shuts down and washes conveyors, sorting tables, header/filleting machines, tote lines, plate freezers and the surrounding deck with hoses, foam detergent and sanitizer, brushing hard-to-reach frames, to HACCP standards under a QA inspection.

Dockside end-of-trip cleanup: boat moored at the pier or offload dock, crew pressure-washes the deck, fish hold, pen boards, hatches and deck gear with fresh water and detergent, scrubs and stows knives and cutting boards, washes fish totes and bins before the next trip.

Small-boat and shellfish harvest cleanup (lobster/crab boat, oyster or clam boat, dip-net/setnet skiff): rinsing and brushing culling boards, baskets, bushel bags, bait bins, hand tools and the small open deck at the mooring, ramp or on the water; cramped, non-flat surfaces and lots of loose gear.

Hunting, guiding and trapping equipment cleaning: washing knives, saws, skinning tools, game-processing tables, coolers, bait buckets and traps with brushes, detergent and water in a camp, shed, garage or at a rural water tap after field dressing or a trap line.

tasks.label: Harvest marine life for human or animal consumption, using diving or dredging equipment, traps, barges, rods, reels, or tackle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pot/trap fishery (Maine lobster, Dungeness or blue crab, Alaska crab, fish/shrimp pots): from a small-to-medium vessel underway in coastal or offshore waters, gaff the buoy, run the warp through a hydraulic hauler, land the pot on the rail, open it, remove and sort catch, gauge legal size, band lobster claws, discard shorts/bycatch, re-bait the bag, close and re-set the pot, in wind, swell, and spray.

Dredge or tong harvest of bivalves (New Bedford sea scallops, surf clam/quahog hydraulic dredges, Chesapeake oyster dredging/tonging): rig and shoot the dredge over the side, tow along the bottom, haul with winch, dump the mixed pile of shellfish, rocks, mud and bycatch on deck, then cull, shuck or bag legal product and shovel the rest overboard.

Jigging/handlining with powered, computer-controlled jigging machines (cod, pollock, rockfish, squid): set machines on the rail, program depth and jig pattern, machines jig and auto-haul on a strike, catch comes aboard and is dropped free or stripped from the barbless hooks, then iced or pumped to hold.

Troll and rod-and-reel/tackle fishing (Southeast Alaska salmon trolling, tuna trolling, live-bait and deep-drop hook-and-line): rig lures/leaders, set gurdy lines or rods, watch for strikes, play and land each fish by hand with gaff or net, unhook, bleed/dress and ice it, then re-set gear, all on a rolling deck.

Hand harvest by diving or wading (sea urchin and geoduck diving, dive-caught scallops/abalone, intertidal clam digging, hand oystering, seaweed cutting): descend with hook, rake, knife or water jet, locate animals in turbid water or soft mud, pick or dig them, fill bags/baskets and hoist them to the boat or carry them ashore.

Shellfish farm harvest from a barge or work boat on a leased site (mussel longlines, oyster cages/bags/floats): position on the line, grapple and lift gear with crane or winch, feed rope through a mechanized stripper or dump cages, wash, de-clump, grade and tote the market-size product, and re-set or re-seed the gear.

Bulky fishing gear on and off the deck at the start/end of a season: crab pots, trawl nets and doors, longline tubs, dredges and drums craned aboard from the pier, positioned, stacked several high and lashed/secured on deck (and the reverse when gear comes off).

tasks.label: Scrape fat, blubber, or flesh from skin sides of pelts with knives or hand scrapers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Trapper fleshing cased small-furbearer pelts (muskrat, mink, raccoon, fox, coyote, bobcat) after a trapline check: pelt pulled skin-side-out over a fleshing beam in a home shed, garage or basement, scraped with a two-handled fleshing knife or hand scraper; pelts vary in size, fat load and damage, some previously frozen.

Beaver and otter pelts, cut open and flat, carrying heavy fat and a tough membrane; scraped on a beam or fleshing board with a knife or hand scraper in the trapper's home shop, taking care not to cut through the thin leather before stretching and drying.

Fleshing done at an institution-run fur-handling operation — a fur buyer's or auction house's handling shed, a commercial fur-handling service, or an organized pelting shop with standard benches, beams and rotary fleshing machines — working through crates of mixed wild pelts to a buyer's grading standard.

Guide/outfitter or hunter fleshing large flat game hides (deer, bear, elk) at a camp or outdoor rack before salting: hide laid over a beam, log or table, scraped with a knife or hand scraper in variable weather, with dirt and hair contamination.

Coastal subsistence hunter removing blubber from seal or other marine-mammal skins with an ulu or scraper, working on a beach, on ice, or on an outdoor rack in cold, wet conditions; thick greasy blubber that must come off without scoring the skin.

tasks.label: Patrol trap lines or nets to inspect settings, remove catch, and reset or relocate traps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Coastal lobster/crab pot trap-line fishing from a small commercial boat (Maine lobster, Dungeness, stone crab): hydraulic hauler brings each trap of a trawl to the rail, worker opens the door, dumps contents, gauges/v-notch-checks and bands keepers, throws back shorts and bycatch, clears kelp and mud, refills the bait bag, closes the door and sets the trap back overboard; 200-800 traps a day on a rolling wet deck in wind and swell.

Offshore/large-vessel pot fishing (Bering Sea king or snow crab, sablefish or black sea bass pots): 300-800 lb pots hauled with block and crane, dumped onto a sorting table, crew sort by sex/size, rebait with chopped herring and hanging bait jars, stack or relaunch the pot; heavy seas, spray, icing, deck motion.

Gillnet, trammel or set-net operation: net hauled over a roller/drum, worker picks fish out of the mesh one at a time without tearing the twine, clears weed, jellyfish and debris, notes and mends holes, and resets the net at the same or a new location, adjusting depth and anchors to conditions.

Inland/estuarine small trap and net lines: blue crab pots in Chesapeake creeks, crawfish traps in ponds and bayous, hoop/fyke/trap nets and eel pots; worker in a skiff or wading picks each trap by hand, shakes the catch into a basket, culls undersize and bycatch, rebaits and drops it back, moving traps to better ground; shallow, muddy, vegetated water and variable weather.

Land furbearer trapline patrol: circuit by snowmobile, ATV, boat or snowshoe through forest, marsh and farmland; inspect each set for disturbance or snow cover, dispatch and remove the caught animal (beaver, muskrat, coyote, marten) without damaging the pelt, reset or rebuild the set with fresh lure/bait, or pull and relocate the trap to fresh sign.
