tasks.label: Maintain and repair trapping equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shoreside repair of wire lobster/crab pots in a working-waterfront gear yard or co-op wharf: cutting out crushed or corroded mesh panels and hog-ringing in patches, re-hanging parlour heads and funnels with twine, replacing broken runners, bricks, door latches and bungee closures, splicing chafed bridles and re-rigging buoy lines. Damage differs pot to pot and must be diagnosed by eye and hand.

Repairs made on the boat deck while fishing: a pot comes up smashed, twisted, or with a torn head, a bridle or gangion is chafed through, a hinge or latch has failed. The crew straightens the frame, laces or wires the damage, replaces the bait bag or bridle and re-sets the gear, working on a wet, pitching deck between hauls.

Fur trapper's off-season conditioning of foothold and body-grip traps in a home garage or shed: degreasing and boiling in logwood dye, dipping in wax, adjusting pan tension and dog notch, replacing weak springs, chains, swivels and shock springs, straightening bent jaws, re-riveting or welding, then bagging traps by set type. Traps are of many makes, ages and sizes.

Mending netting on trapping gear in a net shed or loft: repairing torn mesh in fyke nets, hoop nets, eel and crab pot heads, and pound-net leads with needle and twine, cutting out the damaged bars, tying square and mesh knots to restore the correct mesh count, re-hanging netting on hoops and frames, and re-lacing chafing gear.

Field repairs on the trapline or at a set site: a sprung or frozen trap is bent back, a broken stake, drowning wire or anchor is replaced, a snare loop or lock is re-formed, a damaged cage trap door is refitted, and the set is re-bedded and re-covered, working in brush, snow, mud or marsh with hand tools carried in a pack.

Seasonal bulk cleaning and preservation of gear brought to the yard: stacks of traps hauled ashore are pressure-washed to strip marine growth, mud and old bait residue, netting is soaked or dipped in preservative and dried, and the cleaned gear is re-stacked for storage. Uniform, repetitive work on batches of like gear.

sources.title: Halo promises cheaper, gentler cage cleaning - FishFarmingExpert.com

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine maintenance (fouling removal) of large netting panels used in fisheries/aquaculture. It transfers only to the cleaning part of gear maintenance - comparable material (knotted net), low precision, machine-controlled brushing - and not to diagnosing and repairing torn mesh, wire frames or hardware.

sources.transferJustification: Same as above: substantiates autonomous machine cleaning of netting, a maintenance sub-activity of fishing gear upkeep, but not repair of traps or nets.

Lobster/crab pots are rigid stackable mesh boxes and seasonal trap cleaning is high-pressure washing of batches of identical gear, so a fixtured conveyor washing line performs the same physical operation to a comparable standard; it covers no repair work.

instances.label: Shooting a bottom or midwater trawl (or scallop dredge) from a trawler: deckhands connect the net, sweeps and trawl doors, release the net down the stern ramp or over the side, pay out and lock the warps to the towing depth, and begin the tow, with vessel motion, spray and heavy moving gear on deck.

Setting strings of baited pots/traps (Maine lobster, Dungeness/king/snow crab, sablefish pots): baiting, hooking pots to a crane/launcher, launching them over the rail one at a time at set intervals while the boat runs, and paying out buoy lines, anchors and end buoys.

Setting a gillnet or purse seine from a small to mid-size vessel: paying the net off a drum or releasing it from a seine skiff, clearing corks/leadline, and anchoring set gillnets or buoying drift nets in coastal or open water.

Setting longline gear (halibut, sablefish, tuna, snapper): throwing the end anchor and marker buoy, baiting hooks and paying out the baited groundline over the stern (by hand on snap-gear boats, through an autobaiter on autoline vessels), then setting the end anchor and buoy.

Small-boat hook-and-line work: dropping jig or troll gear from a rail-mounted machine or gurdy to a chosen depth and working it in the water column, on a 30–50 ft commercial groundfish/squid/salmon boat.

Shore-based or inland small-scale gear: setting beach set nets, fyke/hoop/trap nets in rivers and estuaries, or cast nets and shellfish gear from a skiff, with tides, mud banks, current, ice and site-to-site variation taken as found.

tasks.label: Sort, pack, and store catch in holds with salt and ice.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lobster/crab trap boat, open working deck: hauled pots emptied onto a culling table; worker gauges each animal, sexes crabs, rejects egg-bearing females and v-notched lobsters, culls weak/soft-shell animals, bands claws, crates them and stores them live in a circulating seawater tank or on ice in the hold. Rolling deck, spray, gear underfoot.

Small/mid inshore finfish boat (gillnetter, hook-and-line, small dragger) landing a single dominant species: fish gaffed or shaken aboard, bled/gutted, graded by size and quality, packed into totes or pen boards and layered/slushed with ice in an insulated hold. Open or part-sheltered deck at sea.

Small/mid inshore boat landing a mixed multi-species catch: catch dumped into deck checkers, hand-sorted by species (keepers, market grades, bycatch and undersize returned overboard), then gutted, boxed and iced by species in the hold. Species mix varies trip to trip.

Shrimp trawler or scallop dredger: catch dumped on a picking table/shaker, target separated from bycatch and debris, size-graded, then bagged or boxed, iced or frozen, and stowed in the hold. Larger boats have a conveyor-fed working deck.

Pelagic purse seiner / RSW or freezer vessel: catch brailed or pumped aboard, roller-graded by size (and species where shapes differ), then loaded into refrigerated seawater / slurry-ice tanks or packed and plate-frozen into cartons for the hold. High volume, short handling window.

Freezer/factory trawler or catcher-processor: catch emptied from the codend into a reception hopper, conveyed through graders, headed/gutted or filleted, batched into pans and cartons, plate-frozen, then sorted, palletized and stowed in the refrigerated fishroom/freezer hold.

tasks.label: Track animals by checking for signs such as droppings or destruction of vegetation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-season scouting of wildland hunting ground (national forest, mountain timber, brush country) by a guide or market hunter: walking ridges, benches and creek bottoms looking for deer/elk pellet groups, rubs, scrapes, wallows, browsed shrubs and beaten-down trails; judging freshness of scat and vegetation damage to decide where animals are feeding and traveling and where to place a stand or start a hunt.

Trapper running or setting a line in woods, brush and wetlands: reading otter/beaver/muskrat slides, chewed and felled vegetation, coyote and bobcat scat on trail junctions, runs through grass, tracks in mud and snow, to identify species and choose exact trap-set locations; done on foot or from an ATV/boat in cold, wet, low-light conditions.

Following an animal after a shot or during a pursuit: blood spots, hair, overturned leaves, broken vegetation, hoof marks and fresh droppings tracked step by step through thick cover, often at dusk or at night, until the animal is located and recovered.

Damage/predator-control work on farmland and pasture: inspecting crop fields, food plots and pasture for feral hog rooting, trampled corn, browsed rows, droppings and fence-crossing trails to determine the species responsible and its travel routes, so hunts or traps can be set. Setting is a working farm with fixed field layout and controlled access.

Nuisance/wildlife-control work on private residential and small acreage properties: checking yards, gardens, outbuildings, attics and garden beds for droppings, gnawed or dug vegetation, and trails to identify raccoons, hogs, beaver, deer or coyotes and to place traps.

sources.developer: University of Adelaide / Monash University / Curtin University
sources.date: 2023-08 (arXiv preprint; field trials with radio-tagged wombats)
sources.title: ConservationBots: Autonomous Aerial Robot for Fast Robust Wildlife Tracking in Complex Terrains
sources.claim: ConservationBots is an autonomous small aerial robot that plans its own trajectories and localizes multiple radio-tagged wild animals in complex natural terrain, validated in field trials against an expert human tracker; it depends on VHF collars attached to the animals rather than on reading field sign.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating/tracking wild animals in unstructured terrain. It does not transfer to this task because localization relies entirely on radio transmitters fitted to the animals; the system performs no detection or interpretation of droppings, browse damage, tracks or other field sign left by untagged game.

sources.developer: ANYbotics / Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia and collaborators
sources.title: Botany Meets Robotics in Alpine Scree Monitoring
sources.claim: A commercially available legged robot (ANYmal C) was deployed in Italian alpine scree terrain over two field campaigns to reach botanical monitoring plots and collect imagery for deep-learning plant species identification, showing that legged robots can traverse unstructured natural terrain but were used to assist, not replace, human surveyors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: traversing rough unstructured wild terrain and imaging ground-level biological features for automated classification. Transfer is limited: the robot's role is data collection alongside botanists at pre-chosen plots, with no demonstrated autonomous searching for, or interpretation of, animal sign, and the paper's own framing is robotics-assisted human survey.

sources.system: Drone Deer Recovery (thermal drone recovery services, e.g., DJI Mavic 3T-class aircraft)
sources.developer: Drone Deer Recovery / independent thermal drone operators
sources.title: Thermal Drones Take the Hunt to New Heights: Deer Recovery Made Easy
sources.claim: Commercial drone services in the US that locate deer after a shot use thermal-camera drones flown by a human pilot who interprets the imagery in real time; no autonomous sign-following or trailing capability is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating a wounded animal that a hunter would otherwise trail by blood and disturbed vegetation. It cannot support a positive judgment because the aircraft is flown and the imagery judged by a human pilot throughout (continuous teleoperation).

sources.system: UAV corn-damage segmentation pipeline (DJI Phantom 4 RTK imagery + CNN segmentation)
sources.developer: Poznan University of Technology (Aszkowski, Kraft, Drapikowski, Pieczyński)
sources.title: Estimation of corn crop damage caused by wildlife in UAV images
sources.claim: Deep-learning segmentation of RGB imagery from a consumer UAV can automatically map the location and percentage of corn crop area damaged by wildlife, reaching IoU 0.88; the work is an offline image-analysis pipeline applied to survey imagery, with no statement that the flights were flown autonomously and no attribution of the damage to a particular species or inference of animal travel routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting destruction of vegetation caused by wildlife. Transfer is incomplete: it quantifies damaged area from imagery but does not identify the responsible species, judge freshness, or locate the animals, and flight autonomy is not established, so the end-to-end field inspection is not shown to be done by a robot.

sources.system: Dung Detector (DD), YOLOv5 on drone imagery
sources.developer: Obihiro University of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine (Kawamura et al.)
sources.title: Cattle dung detection in pastures from drone images using YOLOv5
sources.claim: A YOLOv5-based 'Dung Detector' model detects cattle dung in open pasture from drone imagery, demonstrating automated recognition of large droppings on short, uniform grass; it is an image-analysis model applied to collected imagery rather than an autonomous robot performing a field survey.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting droppings to infer animal use of an area. Transfer to wild-game sign is weak: cattle pats are large, high-contrast objects on mowed pasture, whereas deer pellets, scat and rubs occur in litter and cover; autonomy of the survey platform is also not established.

sources.system: Deep-learning orangutan nest detector applied to drone imagery
sources.developer: Liverpool John Moores University / HUTAN / Cardiff University (Wich, Ancrenaz, Goossens et al.)
sources.title: Using Deep Learning to Automate Orangutan Nest Detections on Aerial Images Collected With Drones
sources.claim: Automated detection of animal sign (orangutan nests) in drone imagery of tropical forest canopy achieved precision 0.98 and recall 0.88 with a multirotor drone, but the work is offline analysis of collected aerial images for density monitoring, not an autonomous robot performing a sign survey.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting signs of animal presence (nests) from an aerial platform in unstructured forest. Transfer fails for this task because nests are canopy-top features visible from above, whereas droppings, browse and tracks are ground-level under canopy, and no autonomous flight-plus-onboard-decision loop is documented.

tasks.label: Skin quarry, using knives, and stretch pelts on frames to be cured.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Trapper returns from the line and case-skins small/mid furbearers (muskrat, mink, raccoon, opossum, fox, coyote) in his own fur shed or garage: hangs or benches each animal, cuts around feet, ears, eyes and lips with a knife, pulls the pelt off inside-out, flushes fat on a fleshing beam, then pulls the pelt over a wire or wooden stretcher and hangs it to dry. Animals vary in size and condition (wet, muddy, partly frozen).

Beaver (and otter) handling in the shed: open-skinning a 40-60 lb beaver with a knife, careful fleshing of a heavy fatty hide, then lacing or stapling the round pelt onto a hoop/frame at even tension so it dries to a round, salable shape.

Field skinning and caping of big game (deer, elk, bear, feral hog) at the kill site or off a meat pole in the woods: knife work on the ground or hanging, uneven light and footing, hide removed whole for a rug/taxidermy cape, then salted and tacked/stretched on a frame or rack later.

Guide/outfitter skinning at a commercial hunting camp's skinning shed: carcass hoisted on a gambrel at a fixed station with hooks, table and hoist, hide cased or flat-skinned with knives, fleshed, salted and stretched on a frame for the client's taxidermist.

High-volume pelt handling at a fur buyer's/handler's shed or a cooperative fur-handling facility: dozens of carcasses and green pelts processed at fixed stations (fleshing beams, boards, drying racks) to a grading standard, with consistent lighting, power and layout.

sources.title: Rabbit - Product - Skinning machine | Verderio
sources.claim: A commercial rabbit-skinning machine in abattoirs removes the skin mechanically only after human operators have made the knife cuts on each animal; the machine performs no knife work and no pelt stretching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical pelt/skin removal from a small mammal carcass, the closest industrial analogue to skinning trapped furbearers. It transfers only partially: the knife opening cuts are done by a human on every animal and the machine does not board or stretch the pelt, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Jasopels Skinning Machine T11 - Jasopels
sources.claim: State-of-the-art fur-farm pelting machines are operator-controlled per animal: the worker seats each carcass and drives the pelt-pulling cycle with a foot pedal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine case-skinning of mink, an animal comparable in size to trapped mink/muskrat. It does not transfer, because the machine is loaded and cycled by a human for every animal, i.e. continuous step-by-step human control rather than autonomous completion.

sources.system: Jasopels Conveyor Belt for Body Drum / Slicing Machine / Pelting Robot XXL
sources.title: Conveyor Belt for Body Drum - Jasopels
sources.claim: Mink pelting lines pair a conveyor with a slicing machine and a 'pelting robot', but the line is a set of stations in a purpose-built pelting shed rather than a demonstrated unattended skinning-to-boarding system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial pelting of farmed mink. Autonomy of the full line is not established in the source, and no source shows fleshing and boarding of the pelt being done without an operator, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Machine and method for stretching a pelt before fastening to a pelt board (US 9,453,267)
sources.claim: Commercial pelt-stretching machines tension a mink or fox pelt that has already been placed on a pelt board by hand; the machine performs the stretching/fastening step, not the placement of the floppy pelt on the frame.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stretching a pelt on a board to cure, the second half of this task. It transfers only partially: the source describes a machine that stretches a pelt already mounted on the board, and no cited system mounts the pelt on the frame autonomously.

sources.system: Robotic lamb/sheep Y-cutter (New Zealand abattoir line)
sources.developer: Meat & Livestock Australia / NZ meat-automation suppliers
sources.title: Robotic Sheep and Lamb Y-Cutting Development and Roll Out | Meat & Livestock Australia
sources.claim: In red-meat abattoirs a robotic Y-cutter makes only the first incision that opens the carcass before mechanical pelt removal; the rest of pelt removal and all downstream hide handling remain machine-pulled or manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic knife work on a hanging carcass to begin skinning, in a fixtured abattoir line. It covers only one opening cut on a uniformly presented lamb carcass and no pelt curing, so it does not substantiate completing this task at any tier.

sources.system: Frontmatec AiRA, Mayekawa Hamdas-RX, Scott Automated Boning Room (reviewed commercial abattoir robots)
sources.title: Robotisation and intelligent systems in abattoirs - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Reviews of abattoir robotics list the commercially available systems as carcass cutting and deboning robots, and identify size variation and tissue deformability as the binding constraints on automation; no commercial autonomous whole-animal skinning-and-pelt-curing system is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous knife work on animal carcasses inside purpose-built processing lines. These robots cut and debone uniformly presented carcasses; none skins an intact fur animal or stretches a pelt on a frame, so they cannot substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Transport fish to processing plants or to buyers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skipper/crew of a commercial fishing vessel (dayboat up to ~80 ft dragger, seiner or longliner) runs the loaded boat from the fishing grounds back to the landing port — hours of coastal navigation in vessel traffic, weather, fog and current — with the catch iced or in RSW/brine holds, and ties up at the processing plant's or dealer's wharf.

At the plant/dealer wharf the catch is transferred out of the boat: brailer bags or 100-800 lb totes hoisted by the boat's boom or a dock hoist, or bulk pelagic/groundfish pumped from the hold, then weighed, iced and moved into the plant's chill room. Wet, crowded deck and dock; boat type, hold layout and catch differ trip to trip.

Iced totes (loose or palletized) are trucked from the offload dock to a processing plant miles inland or in another port: the fisherman or a hired driver loads a reefer van/flatbed by forklift or by hand, drives public highways, and unloads at the plant's receiving dock.

Small-scale direct sale: the harvester loads coolers, totes or bushels of fish/shellfish into a pickup and delivers to buyers — a restaurant back door, a farmers-market stall, a dockside or roadside retail customer — hand-carrying and handing off the product.

Delivery at sea or to a buyer's vessel: pumping or brailing salmon/herring into a tender or buying station anchored in an open roadstead, or delivering live crab/lobster from the vessel's circulating tanks into a buyer's holding system alongside.

sources.developer: The Nippon Foundation / MTI (NYK Group), Japan Marine Science, Mitsubishi Research Institute
sources.title: World's 1st Automated Coastal Container Vessel (MASS) Enters Commercial Service | The Nippon Foundation
sources.claim: The purpose-built coastal container vessel GENBU entered regular commercial cargo service on a Kobe–Osaka–Nagoya–Yokohama–Tokyo liner route on 30 January 2026 with SAE Level 4-equivalent autonomous navigation, including an automated berthing and unberthing ... shore-based monitoring — i.e. a loaded vessel makes coastal passages and comes alongside a commercial quay under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carrying cargo by sea from origin to destination berth. It transfers to running a loaded fishing boat home because the act is identical — coastal navigation with a passive payload in the hold, in shared waters, ending in coming alongside a working quay.

sources.developer: Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K Line) team / The Nippon Foundation
sources.title: Japanese Consortia Start Commercial Service of Two Fully Autonomous Ships Under the "MEGURI2040" Project
sources.claim: The 11,413-GT RORO Hokuren Maru No. 2 began fully autonomous crewless commercial voyages in early 2026 on a ~1,600 km round-trip route between Hitachi and Kushiro carrying perishable Hokkaido produce, over a route deliberately chosen through waters crowded with fishing boats and subject to fog.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled coastal carriage of perishable cargo. Transfers to hauling a chilled catch to port: same waters and traffic (fishing fleets, fog), same time-critical perishable payload, same requirement to arrive and berth.

sources.title: Aurora Expands Driverless Trucking Service from Fort Worth to El Paso
sources.claim: Aurora operates driverless Class 8 trucks hauling commercial freight on public highways in Texas, having launched the first commercial driverless heavy-truck service in April/May 2025 and surpassed 100,000 driverless miles across two lanes (Dallas–Houston, Fort Worth–El Paso) by October 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: over-the-road haulage of loaded trailers. It covers the driving leg of trucking fish to a plant, but Aurora's trailers are loaded and unloaded by people at customer terminals, so it does not by itself cover the dockside loading of totes.

sources.developer: Skaginn 3X (BAADER) for Denholm Seafoods, Peterhead, Scotland
sources.title: New Fish Pumping System for Denholm Seafood | Skaginn3X
sources.claim: Denholm Seafoods' quayside plants in Peterhead take pelagic catch directly out of moored trawlers through a fixed pipeline: an automatic screw pump in a purpose-built reception house on the quay conveys 60 t/h of fish in ice slurry 250 m from the vessel into the production hall, eliminating truck transport of the catch.

sources.title: Outrider completes its 1000th autonomous zero-emission trailer move at Georgia-Pacific distribution center
sources.claim: Outrider's autonomous electric yard trucks perform trailer moves — including hitching, connecting lines and spotting at dock doors — as part of daily operations in a Georgia-Pacific distribution yard, exceeding 1,000 autonomous moves, with newer generations deployed driverless to enterprise customers from late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving loaded trailers between docks and staging inside a logistics facility. Transfers to moving a trailer of fish totes between an institution-controlled dock and a plant's receiving door — same vehicles, loads and facility roadways.

sources.title: Seegrid Sets the Standard with Industry-Leading Forklift AMR Payload Versatility
sources.claim: Seegrid's autonomous lift-truck AMRs are in production use at manufacturing and distribution customers, transporting standard 48x40 pallets and non-standard bins and oversized loads between stations without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless pallet transport inside a work facility. Fish are landed in standard plastic totes on pallets, so the same lift-truck AMRs cover moving palletized catch between a receiving dock, a truck and a chill room inside a facility.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain achieves first commercial deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch robot
sources.claim: DHL Supply Chain made the first commercial deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch, a mobile robot that autonomously unloads loose boxes from the back of trailers ... containers onto a conveyor in warehouse dock operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emptying a road trailer of loose cases at a dock. Transfers to unloading cases/totes of packed fish at a plant's receiving dock — comparable object size and weight, comparable dock environment.

tasks.label: Attach nets, slings, hooks, blades, or lifting devices to cables, booms, hoists, or dredges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bottom/midwater trawler at sea (groundfish, shrimp, pollock): deckhand shackles net bridles and sweeps to the warp cables, hooks trawl doors onto towing chains/blocks, and attaches the splitting strap and gilson/lifting hook to the codend so the bag can be hoisted aboard. Heavy wire, chain and screw-pin shackles handled with hammer and spanner on a wet, pitching, often icy deck with gear under tension.

Purse seiner, gillnetter or menhaden/salmon seine vessel at sea: attaching the net to the power block, connecting purse line, rings and skiff bridle, and hooking the brailer or dip net to the boom/hoist to lift fish aboard. Flexible webbing and lines, variable catch weight, small crew, open deck exposed to weather.

Crab or lobster pot vessel at sea: rigging slings/bridles on pots for crane or picking-boom lifts, hooking the boom hook or block into pot bridles and buoy lines, attaching brailer bags of live crab to the hoist. Heavy irregular pots, wet coiled line, deck motion.

Scallop, clam or oyster dredge vessel at sea: shackling dredge frames to towing cables and the tow bar/boom, hooking the dredge to the hoist for dumping, and attaching or replacing cutting blades, teeth, chain bags and rock chains between tows. Heavy steel components, bolted and pinned connections, corrosion, work done between tows on a moving deck.

In-port rigging at the dock, gear yard or net loft: attaching nets, dredges, blades, slings and lifting devices to a pier crane, hoist or the vessel's own boom to load, unload, change or repair gear before/after a trip. Fixed layout, stable platform, good light, no sea motion; premises controlled by the harbor or gear shop.

Small inshore boat or skiff (oyster dredge boat, small pot/handline skiff, kelp or dive tender): attaching a sling, hook or small dredge to a davit, hydraulic hauler or A-frame in a cramped open boat, single-handed or with one crewmate, in coastal chop.

sources.system: Yaskawa GP180 robotic hanger-loading cell (Unitem paint buffer line)
sources.title: Loading of workpieces on an overhead conveyor – Unitem Wroclaw
sources.claim: A Yaskawa GP180 industrial robot with a purpose-designed gripper autonomously picks 30-180 kg paint hangers and hangs them on the moving chain of an automatic paint line, cutting 12 workers from the process; i.e. a machine attaching hooks/lifting devices to a moving overhead hoist line in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging heavy hangers/hooks onto a continuously moving overhead conveyor. It is the same physical act as attaching a sling or lifting device to a hoist line - engaging a fitting with a moving carrier at similar load weights - done autonomously with the work presented in known positions, which is the E1 counterfactual for this rigging task.

sources.system: Robotic paint line tending cell (FANUC R-2000iB/185L)
sources.title: Robotic Paint Line Tending Cell | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: Six fenced FANUC R-2000iB/185L robot cells autonomously load 4-12 ft steel beams (up to 80 lbs) onto the carriers of an existing paint line and unload/stack them at a 15-second cycle with only minor operator replenishment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching heavy rigid workpieces to overhead conveyor/hoist carriers in a fixtured, fenced cell. Comparable object weight and engagement precision to hooking gear onto a hoist when the work is presented in a known position; substantiates E1 only.

sources.system: Optilift crane autonomy + Aker BP AutoHook
sources.title: Milestone reached for autonomous lifting – Optilift
sources.claim: On the Valhall IP platform, Optilift's perception and control system together with Aker BP's AutoHook performed automated on- and off-hooking of containers on a supply vessel's deck at sea with no crane operator intervention and no deck crew (TRL 4, calm weather).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled engagement of a crane hook with a load's lifting interface on a vessel deck at sea. Transfers only where the interface is a purpose-built fitting; it does not cover shackling wire bridles, chains or netting, and tests were calm-weather at TRL 4.

sources.title: Offshore – Optilift
sources.claim: Optilift lists 'AutoHook Control' as an offshore product feature giving automatic on- and off-hooking without ..., conditional on cargo carriers being fitted with the Aker BP AutoHook.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task: automated hook engagement on a vessel deck, but only with engineered AutoHook fittings, so it does not substantiate rope, chain or netting rigging on a fishing deck.

sources.title: Fairbanks Morse Defense's Vestdavit Unveils Industry-First Autohook for Fully Autonomous Vessel Recovery Interface
sources.claim: Vestdavit's AutoHook is a clamp-on davit-wire unit with onboard vision, control and thrusters that autonomously connects the hoisting wire to an unmanned surface vessel for recovery, accepted for operation at Sea State 4 and removing manual connection by crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously attaching a hoist wire/hook to a load's lifting point in a seaway. It engages only a dedicated engineered capture point on a USV, not ropes, chains, shackles or netting, so it supports the act of hook engagement but not whole fishing-gear rigging at sea.

sources.title: Elebia evo20 Automatic crane hook (MDA Controls)
sources.claim: Elebia automatic crane hooks magnetically attract and centre a sling ring and close on it, but the hook is positioned by the crane operator and closed on command from a hand-held remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant hardware for attaching hooks to loads, but human remote control drives positioning and actuation throughout, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment; recorded to show the state of the art in general rigging attachment.

tasks.label: Teach or guide individuals or groups unfamiliar with specific hunting methods or types of prey.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Guided big-game hunt (deer, elk, bear) on a ranch or public land: the guide accompanies one or two paying clients who have never hunted that species, explaining how to read sign, stalk into the wind, judge a legal/trophy animal, and place a shot; instruction is verbal coaching plus occasional hand demonstration under variable weather and terrain.

Waterfowl or upland bird hunt from a blind or over dogs: the guide briefs a small group of novices on decoy spreads, calling sequences, safe shooting lanes and when to rise and shoot, correcting technique verbally through the hunt.

Mentored-hunt or hunter-education setting for youth or new adult hunters: classroom-style talk plus field demonstration of firearm/bow handling, blood trailing and field dressing, delivered to a group at a range, camp or club property.

Teaching a specialty method to a small group: trapping and snare sets, predator calling, bowhunting from a stand, or turkey calling; the instructor walks the learners through the method step by step on site.

Subsistence, crew or commercial context: an experienced harvester teaches new crew members or community members the method and prey identification for a specific harvest (e.g., trapline circuits, shellfish or seaweed gathering, netting), instructing while the group works.

tasks.label: Release quarry from traps or nets and transfer to cages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lobster/crab pot fishing: trap hauled aboard a small or mid-size boat with a hydraulic hauler and landed on the rail; worker opens the trap door, pulls out live lobsters or crabs (often tangled, clamped on mesh, mixed with bycatch and bait bags), and drops keepers into holding crates or a circulating live tank on deck. Wet, pitching deck, animals actively pinching and escaping.

Trawl, purse seine or other net fishery: codend or seine bunt brought alongside/aboard and the catch released from the net into fish holds, RSW tanks or live-storage tanks (dumping the bag, brailing, or pumping). Bulk volumes of fish/shrimp, machine-assisted deck gear, vessel at sea.

Small-boat gillnet or set-net fishery (salmon, herring, inland/Great Lakes): net comes over a drum or roller and the worker picks each fish out of the mesh by hand (or with a fish pick), untangling gills and fins, then drops fish into totes, brailers or a live well.

Inland/nearshore trap fisheries worked from a skiff: crawfish pyramid traps, blue crab pots, eel and bait traps lifted one after another, flipped and dumped onto a sorting board or into a hopper, catch transferred into sacks, baskets or live boxes, trap rebaited and reset — hundreds of traps per day at high tempo.

Live wildlife trapping (nuisance wildlife control, fur trapper, capture crews): checking cage/box or foothold traps set in fields, woods, culverts or around buildings, restraining and removing the live animal (raccoon, beaver, coyote, feral hog, bird) and transferring it into a transport cage on a truck.

sources.system: Ecofive trawler catch reception system (Ulstein Design & Solutions / Cflow handling and monitoring system)
sources.developer: Ulstein Design & Solutions, Cflow, Westcon Yards for Bluewild
sources.title: VESSEL REVIEW | Ecofive – New Norwegian shrimp and whitefish trawler boasts innovative catch handling setup
sources.claim: The factory trawler Ecofive, delivered by Westcon Yards to Bluewild in early 2025, takes the trawl catch aboard through the hull below the waterline so it flows straight into live storage tanks without crew emptying a bag onto deck; the Cflow handling/monitoring system (loading, unloading, segregation) is controlled from the bridge.

sources.system: Cflow live fish handling and monitoring system (Ecofive)
sources.title: The future factory trawler Ecofive - Cflow is on board
sources.claim: Cflow's live-fish handling system on the same vessel moves the catch out of the trawl net and into water-filled reception tanks with no human handling of the animals; control modes and species monitoring are integrated on the bridge.

sources.system: MMC/MacGregor Rapp pelagic catch pumping and dewatering systems (e.g. purse seiners Ruth, Zephyr)
sources.title: Denmark's largest and cleanest (Hook & Net vessel review, Ruth)
sources.claim: Modern pelagic vessels transfer the catch out of the purse seine/trawl by vacuum/impeller pumping through a dewatering box into selected RSW holding tanks, but a crewman controls and continuously monitors the pumping flow.

sources.system: RoSC robotic crustacean sorting arm (Noola Redclaw / University of Lincoln)
sources.developer: University of Lincoln and Noola Redclaw Ltd
sources.title: Robotics for the automatic Sorting of Crustaceans (FS135) - Seafood Innovation Fund
sources.claim: A tank-mounted robotic arm with machine vision was designed and tested to identify, grip and move live crayfish for sorting in land-based crayfish farming; a feasibility-stage system tested on synthetic crayfish in the lab and live crayfish on a farm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking live crustaceans out of water and relocating them is the transfer step of emptying a pot into a holding crate. It is cited only as feasibility-grade evidence: single-animal, calm tank, no trap opening or jumbled-pile picking, so it does not establish worker-quality completion.

sources.developer: Louisiana State University bioengineering student team
sources.title: Crawfish harvesting by robot – Greater New Orleans Interfaith Climate Coalition (quoting The Advocate)
sources.claim: A prototype robotic arm for crawfish trap harvesting lifts, empties, rebaits and resets traps, but it is driven by a human operator with a game controller rather than autonomously.

sources.title: Why Seafood Processors Are Turning to Robotics Automation - Soft Robotics
sources.claim: Soft Robotics markets its AI/3D-vision mGrip pick-and-place gripper for seafood plants, stating it can handle live lobsters among other products; no named installation picking live lobsters from a jumbled catch is described.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveyor pick-and-place of lobsters in a plant. Cited as insufficient — vendor copy with no named live-lobster deployment, and singulated conveyor presentation differs from extracting live, clamping animals from a trap.

tasks.label: Participate in animal damage control, wildlife management, disease control, and research activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Contract/agency damage-control trapping on private or agricultural land: trapper responds to a complaint (beaver plugging a culvert, coyotes killing calves, raccoons in outbuildings, feral hogs rooting crops), reads sign, chooses and baits sets, checks them daily, dispatches or relocates the animal, removes and disposes of the carcass, and reports the outcome to the landowner or agency.

Landscape-scale suppression of invasive small mammals/predators on conservation land: installing and servicing lines of traps or lethal devices for rats, possums, mongoose, feral cats or foxes across forest or rangeland; accepted output is sustained knock-down of pest indices with logged kill data, carcasses left in place.

Culling or removal of overabundant/invasive vertebrates in the field: suburban or park deer culls over bait with firearms, ground and aerial shooting of feral hogs, python or lionfish removal contracts, netting of invasive carp; includes shot placement judgment, safety around people, and carcass recovery, donation or disposal.

Field capture, marking and sampling of wildlife for research and management: drop-nets, box or foothold traps, net-gunning, restraining animals, attaching ear tags/radio or GPS collars, taking measurements, drawing blood, collecting swabs and tissue for disease surveillance (CWD lymph nodes, avian influenza swabs), labeling and submitting samples, releasing animals.

Fish marking, tagging and sorting at hatcheries, weirs and dams for fisheries management and research: sorting fish by size and origin, clipping adipose fins, inserting coded-wire or PIT tags, separating hatchery, wild and invasive fish, recording counts, and returning fish to water.

Cooperative fisheries research aboard a working commercial vessel at sea: deploying experimental or survey gear, sorting the catch on a moving deck, measuring and tagging fish, taking otolith/tissue/water samples, and recording bycatch and effort data in weather and sea state as found.

sources.title: QUT - Crown-of-thorns starfish – nailed it!
sources.claim: QUT's COTSbot autonomous underwater vehicle completed reef field trials in which it navigated the reef, detected crown-of-thorns starfish and injected a lethal dose without human control — autonomous lethal pest control in an unstructured marine setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: culling an invasive pest species for wildlife management. Transfer is limited to marine invertebrates on a reef; it does not carry to shooting or trapping vertebrates on land, which require different effectors, safety judgment and carcass handling.

sources.title: Operational field trialling of Felixer™ grooming traps for the control of feral cats in the Strzelecki Desert, Australia (Wildlife Research)
sources.claim: Felixer grooming traps are automated field devices that discriminate target feral cats/foxes with onboard sensors and algorithms and squirt toxic gel onto them; operational, peer-reviewed landscape-scale trials in Australian arid rangeland.

sources.title: Trap tech: how the AT220 is innovating pest tech – Predator Free NZ Trust
sources.claim: The AT220 is a self-resetting, self-baiting kill trap for possums and rats that operates unattended for months and logs kills to an app; over 35,000 units deployed, with field trials driving rat tracking indices from 46.6% to 0%.

sources.developer: Northwest Marine Technology / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
sources.title: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Builds Mass Marking Program for Great Lakes Trout and Salmon
sources.claim: The AutoFish System is a computer-operated automated trailer that sorts live juvenile salmonids by length, clips adipose fins and inserts coded-wire tags at >60,000 fish per day with no human handling and accuracy better than manual work.

sources.developer: Northwest Indian Fisheries Commission member tribes / Northwest Marine Technology
sources.title: Tagging and Marking Services | Northwest Indian Fisheries Commission
sources.claim: Automated AutoFish tagging/marking trailers remain in routine operational service for tribal and state hatchery programs, tagging and fin-clipping fish before they are revived and returned to rearing ponds.

sources.title: Through the tubes: Using pneumatic tubes to transport fish, this company's fish passage is in demand
sources.claim: Whooshh's Passage Portal automatically scans, identifies and sorts fish — separating hatchery, wild and invasive fish — and transports them, at up to 40 fish per ..., installed at dams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting and handling live fish for management (separating invasive/hatchery/wild fish), which is the same object-handling and identification work performed by hand at weirs and traps.

sources.developer: Colorado Parks and Wildlife (Bishop et al.)
sources.title: A noninvasive automated device for remotely collaring and weighing mule deer – Wildlife Society Bulletin
sources.claim: A prototype automated device attached expandable radiocollars to free-ranging mule deer fawns at bait sites and recorded mass and sex without restraint, but the authors report the need to increase low collaring rates and it performs no sampling or tagging.

sources.system: AI-based smart box trap for wild boar
sources.title: Development of AI-based smart box trap system for capturing a harmful wild boar | ROBOMECH Journal
sources.claim: An AI-based smart box trap autonomously detects wild boar entering a defined activation zone and triggers the door, demonstrating machine-triggered capture of a damage-causing species; it captures only and does not dispatch, remove or dispose of animals.

sources.title: MBARI's advanced technology transforms the monitoring of aquatic ecosystems
sources.claim: MBARI's Environmental Sample Processor autonomously collects and preserves water samples for eDNA and toxin analysis, on moorings and aboard long-range AUVs, in open-water research programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous collection and preservation of research samples at sea. It substitutes for water/plankton sampling only; it does not sort catch, tag fish or take biological samples from animals on a vessel deck.

emergingTasks.label: Operate and maintain drone technology for aerial surveillance of hunting and fishing areas.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Forest and Conservation Workers
roles.description: Under supervision, perform manual labor necessary to develop, maintain, or protect areas such as forests, forested areas, woodlands, wetlands, and rangelands through such activities as raising and transporting seedlings; combating insects, pests, and diseases harmful to plant life; and building structures to control water, erosion, and leaching of soil. Includes forester aides, seedling pullers, tree planters, and gatherers of nontimber forestry products such as pine straw.

tasks.label: Check equipment to ensure that it is operating properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-use check of gas-powered hand equipment (chainsaw, brush saw, string trimmer, auger) at a remote field job site or truck tailgate: fuel/bar-oil levels, chain tension and sharpness, air filter, chain brake, pull-start the unit and listen to it run before the crew begins work.

Nursery/greenhouse round: run and check irrigation, misting and pump systems, seeders/transplanters, fans and heaters - verify pressure gauges, spot clogged or misaligned heads, leaking lines and drips, confirm timers/controllers actuate as set.

Daily/pre-trip check at the agency work yard or shop of vehicles and towed or mounted equipment (crew truck, UTV/ATV, tractor, trailer, chipper, pump trailer): fluids, tires, lights, brakes, hydraulic hoses, PTO; start engines and confirm they run and the controls respond.

Check and calibrate spray equipment before a herbicide/pesticide application, at a tailgate mix-and-load site: pressurize a backpack or ATV/skid sprayer, look for leaks at hoses and fittings, clean screens, verify nozzle output and spray pattern against target rate.

Check installed field equipment scattered across remote forest/wetland sites: fire pumps and hose lays, water-control structures and gates, culverts, gauges, fences, trail cameras and weather stations - operate them where possible and confirm they still function.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped runs fully autonomous nightly inspection rounds at a working cement plant, checking hundreds of machine checkpoints for overheating, defects and leaks; over 33,000 inspections since early 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Same task - checking equipment to confirm it is operating properly - performed on fixed plant machinery inside a structured facility; substantiates robotic completion of routine operational checks of pumps, motors and drives, not of hand tools.

sources.system: ANYmal D / ANYmal X inspection robot
sources.title: ANYbotics | Siemens
sources.claim: ANYmal is sold commercially for continuous condition monitoring of motors, valves, fans, compressors and pumps using thermal, visual and acoustic analysis to detect deviations from normal operation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (verifying equipment operates properly) applied to pumps, valves and motors of the kind found in nursery irrigation head-houses and field pump installations.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot robots autonomously navigate customer facilities on repeatable inspection missions, collecting thermal, visual and acoustic data on industrial assets; over 130,000 assets inspected in 2025, including thermal rounds at POSCO blast furnaces and machine checks at Cargill.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class - routine operational checks of running machinery - carried out autonomously inside institution-controlled industrial facilities.

sources.system: ENORISE production hot test facilities (end-of-line engine test cells)
sources.title: End of line testing : quality assurance & engine test
sources.claim: ENORISE builds production hot-test end-of-line cells covering small gasoline engines up to heavy-duty engines, with automated mechanical handling, automatic docking, filling and draining and an automated test run verifying the engine runs to specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional testing of small gasoline engines. It is the same judgment a worker makes about a chainsaw or brush saw - does the powerhead start, run and perform to spec - made on a unit fixtured and presented in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Durr x-road roll/brake/ABS test stand (with x-brake, x-light, x-wheel stands)
sources.title: Tested Driving Dynamics - Roll / Brake / ABS test stand for passenger cars and commercial vehicles
sources.claim: Durr's x-road roll/brake/ABS test stand performs dynamic driving, brake and ABS function tests on cars and trucks at end of line, running automated test sequences on the vehicle placed on the roller sets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional verification of a vehicle (drivetrain, brakes, ABS, headlamps, alignment) - the same 'does this vehicle work properly' determination a crew makes before taking a truck or tractor out, done with the vehicle brought to the machine.

sources.system: AB Dynamics driving robots (CBAR pedal robots, SR steering robots, Gearchange Robot)
sources.title: Driving robots | AB Dynamics
sources.claim: AB Dynamics pedal, steering and gearchange robots are installed in ordinary vehicles and operate the controls to execute programmed test manoeuvres for braking and performance validation, without a human driver.
sources.transferJustification: Supplies the actuation half of a vehicle operational check - starting, throttling, braking and shifting the machine to confirm it responds - in a purpose-built test environment.

sources.title: LEAK TESTER - ATEQ Canada
sources.claim: ATEQ differential pressure-decay leak testers are integrated into production lines and test benches to pressurize parts and give automated pass/fail verdicts on leak integrity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pressure/leak verification of fluid-handling assemblies. A sprayer serviceability check is the same determination - does the tank, pump, hose and nozzle circuit hold pressure and deliver flow - on a unit fixtured at a station.

tasks.label: Fight forest fires or perform prescribed burning tasks under the direction of fire suppression officers or forestry technicians.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wildfire hand-crew work under a crew boss: hiking into a fire with pulaski, McLeod and chainsaw, cutting and scraping fireline to mineral soil through brush and slash on uneven, often steep terrain, in smoke, heat and shifting wind; line must tie in continuously and be dug to spec.

Mop-up, hose work and patrol after the flame front passes: gridding the burned edge, feeling and digging out hot spots, stirring and mixing ash, felling smoldering snags, dragging and charging hose lays from an engine or portable pump, and patrolling the line until declared cold.

Broadcast interior ignition of a prescribed burn unit (grassland, pine flatwoods, brush, or hard-to-reach terrain) per the burn boss's ignition pattern and timing: laying strip or spot fires across tens to hundreds of acres so the unit burns at the prescribed intensity.

Hand ignition with a drip torch where the plan requires ground work: blacklining along a road or plowed line, lighting under closed canopy, ignition near fences, structures, plantations or sensitive features, and lighting individual slash/hand piles, walking the line and placing fire by eye.

Holding and securing the perimeter during a prescribed burn: patrolling the control line with backpack pump, flapper, rake or engine, catching spot fires across the line, knocking down flare-ups, watching hazard trees, and reporting problems to the burn boss.

Burn-unit and fireline preparation: mowing or disking firebreaks and fuel breaks around the unit, raking and leaf-blowing litter off control lines, cutting and clearing brush along the line, and wetting or prepping lines the day of the burn.

sources.system: IGNIS aerial ignition system (Freefly Alta X / D.A. Flight app)
sources.title: IGNIS System Datasheet - Drone Amplified
sources.claim: IGNIS aerial ignition payload on Alta X/M300-class drones autonomously flies planned waypoint missions inside an operator-set geofence and dispenses delayed-ignition spheres to lay burn lines across a prescribed burn unit; sold commercially and used by US wildland fire agencies.

sources.system: Alta X UAS with aerial ignition spheres (USFS UAS program)
sources.developer: US Forest Service / Drone Amplified / Freefly
sources.title: Automatic Response: Drones & autonomy in aerial firefighting - Vertical Mag
sources.claim: The US Forest Service operates drone aerial ignition as a routine field tool, using Alta X drones to drop ignition spheres to burn out areas that are hard for ground crews to reach.

sources.title: Drone Amplified: Tech Entrepreneurs Attack The Global Wildfire Challenge
sources.claim: IGNIS flies a GPS-guided ignition pattern set in advance by its operator, with terrain-following from uploaded topography, replacing drip-torch crews walking difficult terrain and helicopter ignition.

sources.system: Greenzie autonomy (Wright Autonomous Stander ZK and similar mowers)
sources.title: Greenzie Finds Autonomous Mower Market In College Campuses - Turf Magazine
sources.claim: Greenzie-powered commercial mowers mow large open turf areas autonomously after a perimeter pass, deployed in production on campus grounds, parks and athletic fields (e.g., University of Wisconsin-Madison), with crews on site doing detail work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mowing large vegetated areas. Firebreak/fuel-break mowing is the same cutting operation on comparable vegetation with the same machine class; the transfer holds only where the ground is smooth, mapped and obstacle-poor, as on maintained institutional grounds.

sources.title: Greenzie releases Version 5.0 software to advance commercial-ready autonomy - Landscape Management
sources.claim: Greenzie autonomous mowing is limited to large, flat, obstacle-poor maintained grounds such as athletic fields, ... warehouse lots; V5.0 software released for sustained commercial deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (large-area mowing); this source bounds the environment in which the transfer to firebreak mowing is credible.

sources.system: John Deere Autonomous 9RX tractor with field cultivator (second-generation autonomy kit)
sources.title: John Deere brings autonomous tillage operation to farmers - AgriNews
sources.claim: John Deere's autonomous 9RX tillage system performs full tillage passes in previously mapped fields with no operator aboard, released to customers in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tillage of a mapped field. Disking a firebreak is the same tractor-and-implement pass over comparable ground; the transfer holds where the ground is mapped, smooth and free of stumps and rock, as in a farm field.

sources.title: California agencies eye BurnBot for wildfire prevention - The Robot Report
sources.claim: BurnBot RX2, the leading ground machine for contained prescribed burning and fuel-break creation (tested with CAL FIRE and PG&E), is driven by a human operator who steers the tractor and sets burn parameters.

sources.title: Firefighting Robotic Vehicle System - Fire Apparatus Magazine
sources.claim: Lockheed Martin's Fire Ox is marketed as a semi-autonomous unmanned ground vehicle whose potential missions include suppression, trenching and mop-up; no evidence was found of autonomous completion of fireline or mop-up work on an actual incident.

sources.system: Sikorsky MATRIX optionally piloted Black Hawk with Rain wildfire mission autonomy
sources.title: Rain and Sikorsky Test Advanced Aerial Firefighting Technologies Using Autonomous Black Hawk Helicopter
sources.claim: Autonomous aerial suppression of small fires has been demonstrated (optionally piloted Black Hawk with MATRIX autonomy plus Rain mission autonomy dropping water on staged propane and brush-pile fires in Southern California), but it is a test event, aerial only, and includes no ground line-securing or mop-up.

tasks.label: Perform fire protection or suppression duties, such as constructing fire breaks or disposing of brush.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hazardous-fuels reduction on a forest/brush unit: crew member cuts brush, ladder fuels and small trees with chainsaw and brushcutter on uneven, often steep ground with stumps, rocks and standing timber; cut material lopped and scattered or bunched for later disposal.

Disposing of the cut brush and slash: dragging and piling slash at landings or in-unit, feeding a chipper, loading and hauling material away, or burning slash piles in the wet season under a burn permit.

Constructing and maintaining fire breaks / fire lines on wildland and rural ground: scraping or plowing a strip to mineral soil with hand tools or a tractor-drawn plow/disc, or clearing a vegetation-free strip along roads, property lines and around burn units.
Prescribed burn support on a landscape unit: prepping and holding control lines, drip-torch ignition, watching for spots and slop-overs, and mopping up the perimeter afterwards under a burn boss.

Maintaining defensible space and grassy fuel breaks at developed, agency- or company-managed sites: mowing grass and light vegetation around campgrounds, administrative sites, park grounds, yards and roadside strips kept to a maintenance standard.
Support on an active wildfire incident: hose lays, hot-spotting and mop-up (digging out and cold-trailing smoldering material), patrolling the line in smoke and heat with hand tools.

sources.system: Konecranes CXT biomass / waste-to-energy automated grab crane
sources.date: 2024 (product page, in commercial use for years)
sources.title: Waste to energy and biomass crane automation | Konecranes
sources.claim: Fully automated, operator-free overhead grab cranes handle and feed woody biomass/waste fuel from a bunker into the furnace hopper at waste-to-energy and biomass plants — a purpose-built facility that disposes of bulky woody material presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grapple handling and furnace feeding of woody biomass/mixed waste. Under the E1 counterfactual the brush arrives presented in a bunker; grabbing tangled bulky woody material and burning/consuming it is the same physical act and output (brush disposed) as pile burning or chipping.

sources.title: Autonomous Solutions acquires Scythe Robotics - Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: Autonomous commercial mowers operate unattended across institution-controlled grounds in 30 US states, mowing roughly 2 billion square feet in a single season.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial turf/vegetation mowing on maintained grounds. Defensible-space and grass fuel-break maintenance at campgrounds, admin sites and roadside strips is the same act (cutting light vegetation low over mapped ground) with the same acceptance standard.

sources.title: Meet the founder: Bluewhite's Ben Alfi on mobility, labor challenges, and how to make a tractor autonomous in 14 hours
sources.claim: Retrofitted tractors execute field operations including mowing autonomously in orchards and vineyards, with tens of thousands of hours ... unattended commercial operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tractor-implement work on mapped institutional ground. Pulling a mower or disc along a planned strip to create a fuel break uses the same machine class, implement and path-following precision as autonomous mowing/tillage.

sources.title: SwarmFarm automated refilling unlocks high-volume spray applications

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous slashing/mowing of heavy grass and cover vegetation on institution-controlled farmland; a mown or slashed strip along a mapped line is the fuel-break output sought in the fire-break instance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation of a linear cut to spec along a planned path on open, surveyed ground — the same machine class and precision used to scrape a fire line to mineral soil where the ground is mapped and free of timber.

tasks.label: Operate skidders, bulldozers, or other prime movers to pull a variety of scarification or site preparation equipment over areas to be regenerated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Southern pine cutover: worker drives a crawler tractor (dozer) pulling a bedding plow, combination plow or drum chopper in parallel rows across a recently harvested tract full of stumps, slash, root wads and wet spots; follows GPS row spacing, adjusts depth, stays out of streamside management zones.

Northern/western clearcut scarification: worker drags an anchor chain, drag scarifier, disc trencher or salmon blade behind a grapple skidder or crawler over slash-covered, rocky, uneven ground with moderate slopes, exposing mineral soil in continuous strips ahead of planting.

Open managed ground on agency or company land (retired cropland, pasture, old field, seed-orchard or nursery block): worker pulls a disk harrow, subsoiler/ripper or rangeland drill with a farm tractor over relatively obstacle-free, maintained ground being prepared for tree or grass establishment.

Small or sensitive tracts: worker threads a small tractor, ATV/UTV or skidder with a light scarifier between residual leave-trees in a shelterwood or partial cut, around wetland buffers, cultural sites and property lines, avoiding damage to residuals and soils on a small irregular parcel.

Post-fire or rough-ground rehabilitation: dozer pulls a ripper/scarifier or chain over burned, boulder-strewn slopes, compacted landings and old skid trails to loosen soil for regeneration, working steep pitches and hidden obstacles.

sources.system: John Deere autonomous 9RX / 8R with second-generation autonomy kit (16-camera perception)
sources.title: John Deere rolls out autonomous tractors — Farm Progress
sources.claim: A farmer in southwestern Iowa runs a John Deere 9 Series tractor in Autonomy Mode with no driver aboard, dragging a 2660VT vertical tillage tool along predefined guidance lines, monitored by phone — i.e., autonomous pulling of a ground-engaging implement across a working farm field.

Transfer holds for site preparation because both consist of driving a high-horsepower prime mover in planned parallel passes while towing a heavy ground-engaging implement at controlled depth over an area of soil; the objects (tractor + towed tillage/scarification tool) and precision (row spacing, depth) are comparable.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: tillage with towed implements; same machine class and motion pattern as pulling scarification equipment over a regeneration area.

sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: operating a skidder in real harvest units. Establishes that in-woods prime-mover operation today is teleoperated, not autonomous.

sources.developer: Skogforsk / Umeå University / SLU / Luleå University of Technology and industry partners
sources.title: Autoplant—Autonomous Site Preparation and Tree Planting for a Sustainable Bioeconomy (Forests, MDPI)

sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: autonomous site preparation on clear-cuts. Shows the in-woods capability exists only as a project prototype, not at worker quality or scale.

sources.system: Xt28 concept forwarder with AI control
sources.developer: Umeå University with Skogforsk and Algoryx Simulation
sources.title: The world's first AI-controlled forest machine trained in Umeå — Umeå University

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving of a heavy forest prime mover. Establishes that forest-machine autonomy is at supervised test-ground maturity, not deployed cutover operation.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous equipment retrofit (dozers, excavators, skid steers)
sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US — Construction Dive
sources.claim: Retrofit autonomy software has let bulldozers and excavators perform earthmoving tasks fully autonomously on remote construction jobsites, including grading building pads, with a human overseer monitoring several machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy tracked earthmoving on as-found outdoor jobsites. Transfer is only partial — the ground is cleared and graded and the machine pushes with a blade rather than towing an implement through stumps, slash and root wads.

tasks.label: Spray or inject vegetation with insecticides to kill insects or to protect against disease or with herbicides to reduce competing vegetation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Backpack/hand-sprayer foliar spot treatment of competing woody vegetation and invasive shrubs/vines inside a standing forest or dense brush understory: crew walks through slash, stumps, briars and uneven ground under partial or closed canopy, treating scattered individual stems while avoiding crop trees.

Treatment of contiguous infestations in open terrain - phragmites/cattail marsh, cheatgrass and brush on rangeland, kudzu patches, utility or road right-of-way - applied broadcast or as patch spot-spray with backpack, mist blower, or UTV boom/handgun over mapped areas of a few tenths of an acre to tens of acres.

Broadcast chemical site preparation or seedling release over a harvested cutover or young pine plantation: whole-unit herbicide application at a prescribed rate across tens to hundreds of acres of rough, stump-strewn ground, with buffers around streams and property lines.

Selective spot treatment of scattered individual target plants intermixed with desirable native vegetation (spotted knapweed in a native prairie, garlic mustard, thistle in a restoration planting), where per-plant precision and non-target avoidance decide whether the work is accepted.

Stem injection, hack-and-squirt, or basal bark treatment of individual trees and shrubs: hatchet or lance-injector applied to each stem for invasive tree control, timber stand improvement, or systemic insecticide injection to protect trees from borers.

Insecticide/fungicide/herbicide application over seedling stock at a forest tree nursery or greenhouse: boom or air-assisted spraying over bareroot beds, container blocks, or benches inside an institution-run nursery with fixed layout and aisles.

sources.system: Spray drones (large agricultural UAVs) operated by forestry drone aerial applicators
sources.developer: Clemson University Extension (Land-Grant Press) documenting commercial drone applicators

sources.claim: Commercial drone aerial applicators perform forestry chemical site preparation and seedling release on harvested/planted forest sites in the US Southeast; the spray drone flies the planned mission ... with obstacle sensing over snags and residual trees.

sources.claim: Herbicide GUSS is a driverless orchard sprayer that navigates tree rows with LIDAR and uses sensors to detect and spot-spray weeds on the orchard floor beneath trees; one operator supervises up to eight machines remotely.

sources.system: Micothon M3 Smart Spray tube/rail spraying robot

sources.transferJustification: Same task (pesticide application over nursery/greenhouse plant stock) in an institution-run growing facility comparable to a forest tree nursery.

sources.system: Automated needle-based trunk injection system for citrus
sources.title: Development of an automated needle-based trunk injection system for HLB-affected citrus trees
sources.claim: The closest automated trunk-injection hardware for trees is a vehicle-mounted, human-positioned injection mechanism evaluated in commercial citrus orchards; no autonomous robot performs stem injection or hack-and-squirt on standing trees.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to tree injection; cited to show the state of the art is a human-positioned device on a farm vehicle, not an autonomous system.

tasks.label: Thin or space trees, using power thinning saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-commercial thinning of dense natural conifer regeneration on public or industrial timberland in the Pacific Northwest / Inland West: worker walks the unit on foot with a clearing/brush saw, cutting 1-6 in dbh stems to a target spacing on steep, uneven, slash-covered ground, leaving the best crop trees.

Hazardous-fuels / WUI thinning on national forest or state land: crew members with chainsaws or brush saws remove small-diameter trees and ladder fuels around larger leave-trees, then lop-and-scatter or pile slash; brushy, rocky terrain with standing snags and mixed stem sizes and species.

Timber-stand improvement / crop-tree release in mixed hardwood stands (Appalachians, Lake States, Northeast): worker picks competing stems around chosen crop trees and fells or severs them with a chainsaw, working amid grapevine, brush and downed wood on rolling ground.

Pre-commercial thinning and spacing in young southern pine plantations on relatively flat ground: brush-saw operator walks planted rows and inter-row volunteer regeneration, cutting excess stems to target density in hot, dense, low-visibility young stands.

Spacing/thinning in intensively managed plantings kept by an institution: seed orchards, nursery field blocks, conservation windbreaks, arboretum or park plantations with surveyed rows, mowed alleys and maintained access; worker removes designated cull or excess trees with a power saw.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / University of Bonn / Prefor Oy (DigiForest)
sources.title: SAHA: Supervised Autonomous HArvester for selective forest thinning (arXiv:2601.01282)
sources.claim: SAHA, a 4.5-tonne robotic harvester from ETH Zurich/Bonn/Prefor within the EU DigiForest project, autonomously navigates real northern European forests and reaches targeted trees for selective thinning, under supervised autonomy in field trials.
sources.transferJustification: Selective thinning of standing trees with a powered harvester head is the same operation the worker performs with a power thinning saw: choosing leave/remove stems and severing removed stems at the base.

sources.developer: DigiForest consortium (ETH Zurich, Univ. Bonn, Prefor Oy)
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (arXiv:2604.14652)
sources.claim: In DigiForest field work SAHA performed fully automated cutting of target trees whose positions were given in a prebuilt map, i.e. machine-controlled saw cutting of standing stems at known positions.

sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (HTML v1)
sources.claim: The same DigiForest report shows SAHA's work cycle is not yet closed-loop autonomous: releasing the cut tree required a human trigger, and the harvesters are described as semi-autonomous with remaining technical challenges.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: AirForestry's electric harvesting drone completed a first end-to-end autonomous harvest of thinning-grade trees (40-140 kg) in a working production forest in Sweden - gripping from above, delimbing, sawing near the ground and flying the stem to roadside; commercial operation is planned around six-drone fleets not yet realized.
sources.transferJustification: Airborne selective thinning removes designated small stems from a growing stand, the same silvicultural outcome the worker produces with a power thinning saw.

sources.title: AirForestry - Efficient, Electric, and Sustainable Forestry from the Air
sources.claim: AirForestry's own milestone log dates the first fully autonomous harvest sequence (navigate, identify tree, delimb, fell, lift to roadside) to 2026, following first full-cycle harvests of two consecutive trees in 2025 - single-machine, few-tree demonstrations rather than production thinning.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Robotic Precision Harvesting: Mapping, Localization, Planning and Control for a Legged Tree Harvester (arXiv:2104.10110)
sources.claim: The HEAP legged tree harvester (ETH Zurich) ran fully autonomous precision-harvesting missions - mapping, navigation and approach-and-grasp of stems - both in a prepared test field where upright 'tree trunks' were staged for the machine and in a real forest alley, at 1-2.5 minutes per cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous approach and grasping of stems for precision harvesting. It transfers to the staged/fixtured (E1) version of thinning because stems are presented at known positions and commercial harvester heads with saws perform the severing step the paper omits.

sources.system: Autonomous forestry machines (survey, incl. Rakkatec unmanned harvester)
sources.developer: Umea University / SLU (La Hera et al.)
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed field-robotics study of autonomous forestry machines reports that, apart from laboratory test benches, no real forestry robot machine had been demonstrated, and that vendor autonomy claims (e.g. Rakkatec's unmanned harvester) were unsupported by demonstrations.

sources.title: Multiscope Forester Brushcutter - Milrem Robotics
sources.claim: Milrem's Multiscope Forester Brushcutter is an unmanned ground platform carrying a hydraulic brush-cutting tool for stems under 10 cm on clear-cut sites; published material describes the platform and tool but does not establish autonomous selective stem-by-stem thinning.

tasks.label: Identify diseased or undesirable trees and remove them, using power saws or hand saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-commercial thinning / release cutting in a young conifer plantation or regenerating stand: worker walks the stand on foot over uneven, brushy ground, picks out suppressed, forked, diseased or competing stems (roughly 1–8 in. diameter) and cuts them at stump height with a brush saw or small chainsaw, leaving crop trees at prescribed spacing; hundreds of stems per day.

Timber stand improvement in a mixed hardwood/conifer stand: worker identifies cull, cankered, crooked, or undesirable-species trees (roughly 6–16 in. dbh), notches and fells them with a chainsaw among standing crop trees, avoiding damage to residuals; some stems are girdled instead.

Invasive/undesirable woody species control on conservation land — buckthorn, tamarisk, eastern redcedar, mesquite, autumn olive — in wetlands, prairie, rangeland, or thicket edges: multi-stemmed clumps cut low with chainsaw or hand saw, stumps often treated with herbicide, footing wet or rocky, stems tangled with brush.

Hazard and diseased tree removal along trails, campgrounds, fencelines, and forest roads: larger defective, dead, or leaning trees (often 16–36 in. dbh) that must be directionally felled with notch/back-cut and wedges away from structures, trails, and the public, then limbed and bucked.

Sanitation cutting of insect- or disease-infested trees (bark-beetle pines, oak wilt, emerald ash borer ash) in a managed stand: crew works from a forester's marks or from crown symptoms, fells the infested trees with chainsaws and piles or removes the material to limit spread.

Roguing/culling in a tree plantation, Christmas tree farm, or forest nursery: rows on prepared, mowed ground under an owner's control; worker walks the rows, spots diseased, off-type, or misshapen trees and cuts them out with a hand saw or small power saw.

sources.title: The World's First Drone Tree Harvest in a Real Forest – AirForestry
sources.claim: AirForestry's 6.2 m electric harvesting drone completed a fully autonomous harvest ... its test field — flying to position, identifying the tree, delimbing/felling and dropping the log — for thinning-size stems of roughly 40–140 kg.
sources.transferJustification: Selective thinning is the removal of designated undesirable/suppressed standing stems with a saw at stump height — the same objects, cut precision and end state as removing diseased or undesirable trees in this task.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: AirForestry also operated in a working Swedish production forest, felling trees there; the company presents the in-forest harvest and the end-to-end autonomous sequence as two separate milestones, so the production-forest felling is not established as autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (thinning removal of selected standing trees); recorded to document that the unstructured-forest work has not been shown to be autonomous.

sources.title: Sveaskog and AirForestry formalise drone thinning partnership with seven-year off-take agreement
sources.claim: AirForestry's throughput is still at the level of single trees: in April 2026 harvesting two consecutive trees without ... was reported as a milestone, and commercial thinning off-take deliveries are contracted only from 2028.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; documents the reliability/throughput gap relative to a worker felling many stems per day.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich / DigiForest EU Horizon consortium
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry
