sources.claim: The SAHA 4.5-t robotic harvester (DigiForest, ETH Zurich et al.) autonomously navigates a managed forest to a target tree specified in a prebuilt map and executes an automatic cutting mode; a human operator must press a button to initiate each cut for safety, and tree selection is made by a human via a map interface.
sources.transferJustification: Selective thinning of designated trees with a harvester head is the same physical act (grasp trunk, saw at stump, remove stem) on the same objects as removing diseased or undesirable trees.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab and partners
sources.title: SAHA: Supervised Autonomous HArvester for selective forest thinning (arXiv 2601.01282)
sources.claim: SAHA was field-tested with supervised autonomy on kilometre-long autonomous missions in northern European ..., reaching targeted trees for selective thinning; the work is a research field trial, not a production deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Selective thinning = removing designated undesirable stems; identical objects and cutting precision to the task.

sources.system: Pasture Tree Cutting Robot (KSU AGV + chainsaw)
sources.title: Development and Evaluation of Pasture Tree Cutting Robot: Proof-of-Concept Study
sources.claim: A tracked chainsaw robot built at Kansas State University for cutting invasive eastern redcedar and honeylocust up to 20 cm on prairie was a proof-of-concept operated wirelessly by a human from a tablet, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the invasive/undesirable woody-plant cutting instance; cited to show the only rangeland cutting robot found is human-operated.

sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to prevent wildfires - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kodama Systems' commercial wildfire-thinning offering is a teleoperation and autonomy retrofit for forestry machines, with the deployed product being remotely operated skidders that haul already-felled trees rather than machines that select and fell trees.
sources.transferJustification: Forest thinning operations; cited as negative evidence that the fielded US thinning robotics are teleoperated and cover extraction, not saw-felling of selected trees.

tasks.label: Select or cut trees according to markings or sizes, types, or grades.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-commercial thinning / timber stand improvement: crew member walks a dense young stand (often steep, brushy, uneven ground, slash underfoot) and cuts competing small-diameter stems selected on the spot by size, species and spacing rules with a brush saw or chainsaw, hundreds of stems per acre per day, leaving crop trees undamaged.

Felling individual larger trees that a forester has paint-marked (cull, diseased, storm-damaged or hazard trees along trails, roads and campgrounds) with a chainsaw in a mature managed stand: judge lean and defects, notch and back-cut, drop the tree clear of residual trees and infrastructure.

Habitat restoration work: cutting undesirable or invasive woody species (buckthorn, autumn olive, encroaching juniper/cedar, tamarisk, saplings) out of prairie, wetland edge or rangeland, discriminating target species from natives stem by stem, cut-stump close to the ground, often followed by an herbicide dab.

Selecting and marking: under a forester's supervision, cruising a stand and evaluating each tree against size (DBH), species and grade/form criteria, then applying paint marks or tags to the trees chosen for cutting or leaving, and tallying them.

Plantation/tree-farm harvest: on a Christmas tree farm or nursery block planted in rows, choosing trees that meet the height, density and quality grade ordered, cutting them at the stump with a chainsaw or handsaw, and leaving off-grade trees standing.

sources.title: The World's First Drone Tree Harvest in a Real Forest - AirForestry
sources.claim: AirForestry's heavy-lift electric drone completed an end-to-end autonomous tree harvest sequence - flying to position, identifying the tree, harvesting it and dropping it off - on the company's test field, while its work in an actual production stand was reported as a separate milestone.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: Trade coverage confirms AirForestry treats the production-forest felling and the human-free end-to-end harvest as two separate milestones, i.e. the fully autonomous cycle was not shown in the working stand.

sources.title: TECH UPDATE: Log Bucking and Merchandising - Forestnet
sources.claim: Commercial log merchandising lines (e.g. USNR's LogPro merchandiser) take whole tree stems on conveyors, scan them, and automatically saw them into logs with travelling saw carriages under optimizer control inside a purpose-built mill line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bucking/merchandising whole stems. The workpiece is the same (tree stems), the criteria are the same (measured size and grade), and the cut is executed under machine control; it is the E1 form of 'cut trees according to sizes or grades', with stems conveyed and fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: MPM Engineering / Inotech Intellibuck bucking optimizers with 3D true-shape scanning
sources.title: Tech Update - Log Scanners and Optimizers - Forestnet
sources.claim: Scanner/optimizer systems installed in mills grade each stem and automatically choose and execute the value-maximizing cut pattern, and separately grade and sort the resulting logs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine grading and sorting of stems/logs. It substantiates the 'select according to sizes, types or grades' judgment plus a physical act on the selected piece (cut, kick-out, sort, grade-mark) in a conveyor-fed purpose-built line.

sources.system: SAHA autonomous harvester (DigiForest, EU Horizon project)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich / Oxford Robotics Institute / DigiForest consortium
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (arXiv:2604.14652)
sources.claim: The DigiForest SAHA purpose-built hydraulic harvester navigates autonomously to a target tree specified in a prebuilt map in a real managed forest, but the cut itself must be triggered by a human operator for safety, and only individual modules were field-tested.

sources.title: Carbon Robotics raises funding to destroy weeds on farms - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder autonomously discriminates target plants from non-targets by species using deep-learning vision and destroys only the targets, at commercial scale in row-crop fields.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: species-selective removal of unwanted plants. It substantiates autonomous plant-type discrimination and targeted removal, but on small herbaceous weeds in planted rows rather than woody stems, so it supports only the selection-by-type element.

tasks.label: Prune or shear tree tops or limbs to control growth, increase density, or improve shape.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Summer shearing pass on a commercial Christmas tree plantation: worker walks planted rows of field-grown fir, spruce or pine 3-8 ft tall with a shearing knife, hand shears or powered shear, sweeping the current-season growth back to a conical taper, cutting the terminal leader to length and correcting double leaders; hot weather, grassy or uneven farm ground, thousands of trees per day.

Forest/conservation nursery work: top-clipping conifer seedlings in bareroot beds to control height and shoot:root ratio, and shearing or shaping young container-grown conifer and ornamental stock in blocks or benches; standard bed widths and spacing, irrigation, graded ground, institution-controlled premises.

Lift-pruning a young conifer plantation or natural stand: removing lower live limbs flush to the stem on pine or Douglas-fir up to 8-17 ft with pole pruners, pruning saws and shears, to control growth and improve stem form; sloped, brushy ground with slash, irregular spacing and variable tree size.

Corrective pruning in field plantings - windbreaks, riparian and wildlife restoration plantings, seed orchards: removing double leaders and browse-damaged shoots on young hardwoods and shrubs, coppicing willow, topping seed-orchard trees from ladders or lifts to keep cone crops reachable; scattered sites, unimproved ground, weeds and protective tubes/cages present.

Pruning limbs of established trees along trails, campgrounds, fencelines and road corridors on conservation land, cutting back or shaping crowns with pole saws and chainsaws; terrain and vegetation taken as found, visitors and structures nearby.

sources.system: Woodburn Nursery & Azaleas autonomous 60-ft GPS trimmer (custom-built)
sources.developer: Woodburn Nursery & Azaleas with custom machinery builders (e.g., Wurdinger Manufacturing / Lommers)
sources.title: Nursery tour showcases businesses embracing automation (Capital Press / Newberg Graphic)
sources.claim: A commercial Oregon nursery operates a 60-foot GPS-guided autonomous trimmer that tilts its blades to shear blocks of growing nursery trees into pyramid or cone shapes, replacing twice-yearly hand trimming of whole blocks; deployed in outdoor pot-in-pot production blocks whose plant positions are GPS-mapped.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shearing blocks of growing conifer/ornamental nursery trees to a cone or pyramid envelope. Objects (woody nursery conifers), the cut (a blade sweep along a taper line through current-season foliage), and the precision (uniform cone shape accepted by buyers) are the same as Christmas-tree shearing and nursery-stock shaping; the setting is likewise an institution-controlled outdoor growing block in planted rows.

sources.system: RAP form trimmers / RAP XRL automatic trimmer
sources.developer: RAP (supplied by HortiHands / Pack TTI bv, Netherlands)
sources.title: RAP - Horticultural trimming machines for round, spherical and cone shape plants
sources.claim: RAP form trimmers are commercial nursery machines that shape plants into round, spherical or cone forms; the RAP XRL model is a belt-integrated automatic trimmer for pot production lines running up to 1,000 pots/hour, with knife sets including a 'pyramid' form knife, i.e. the work is conveyed to the machine and shaped without per-plant human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized cone/pyramid form-shearing of nursery plants presented on a conveyor. Same act (shearing shoots back to a geometric envelope to improve shape and density) on comparable woody nursery stock, at the precision growers accept; establishes that the work can be completed when the plant is brought to the machine (E1 counterfactual).

sources.title: TRIMMING - Automatic trimming machines for nurseries - Urbinati Srl
sources.claim: Commercial conveyor-fed automatic trimming machines for greenhouses ... cut young plants to an adjustable, precise height, with models for soft-leaved and semi-woody stems, at up to 1,200 containers per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: top-clipping young nursery plants to a set height to control growth. Same operation as nursery seedling top-clipping in a forest nursery, comparable stems (including semi-woody) and precision (uniform cut height), in a nursery/greenhouse line.

sources.title: New Holland and Bluewhite expand partnership for autonomous tractors - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Retrofit autonomy kits let conventional tractors work driverless along planted rows in soil-grown perennial crops (orchards and vineyards) at commercial scale in the US, with remote supervision rather than an onboard operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous row-following operation of implements in soil-planted perennial crop blocks. It supplies the carrier/navigation half of mechanized shearing in a field plantation (uneven farm ground, planted rows), complementing the shearing head evidence; it does not itself perform pruning.

sources.system: Autonomous pruning robot for planar fruit trees (UR5e-class arm on field platform)
sources.developer: Oregon State University / Washington State University research team
sources.title: An autonomous robot for pruning modern, planar fruit trees (arXiv 2206.07201)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous field system for pruning trellised sweet cherry trees achieved only a 58% cutting success rate in orchard field trials, well below what a grower would accept from a worker.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective removal of woody limbs from standing living trees under machine vision. Directly comparable to lift-pruning and corrective pruning of young forest trees; its sub-worker success rate is the basis for negative judgments on selective limb pruning.

sources.system: Boxwood topiary trimming robot (TrimBot-derived arm with electric shears)
sources.title: Evaluation of a boxwood topiary trimming robot - Biosystems Engineering (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: An autonomous boxwood topiary trimming robot evaluated in a real garden could trim spherical, cylindrical and cuboid bushes on its own, but its shaping accuracy was judged insufficient for practical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous shape-trimming of woody plants in a taken-as-found outdoor setting. Shows that free-navigating shape-trimming robots outside engineered growing blocks do not yet meet acceptable quality, supporting negative judgments for unstructured sites.

sources.system: Gantry tractor (Portaltraktor) Christmas tree shearing rig
sources.developer: European Christmas tree machinery manufacturers (e.g., Egedal-type gantry rigs)
sources.title: Stich - Weihnachtsbäume - Formschnitt (weihnachtsbaumwelt.de)
sources.claim: In commercial Christmas tree production, larger growers already shape trees mechanically with a gantry tractor that cuts each tree at a constant taper angle in high volume, while smaller growers use knives and hedge shears; the machine is driven by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Context only (operator-driven, so it cannot by itself support a positive judgment): it establishes that a fixed-taper mechanical shear produces Christmas-tree shape quality growers accept, which is the output standard the autonomous nursery trimmer would have to meet.

tasks.label: Maintain campsites or recreational areas, replenishing firewood or other supplies and cleaning kitchens or restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily in-season cleaning round of a developed campground or day-use comfort station/shower house: scrub and disinfect flush toilets, urinals, sinks and shower stalls, wipe mirrors and partitions, mop and disinfect the concrete floor. Building is agency-owned with running water and power; standard fixtures, fixed layout, heavy public traffic.

Servicing rustic vault/pit toilets and primitive-site restrooms reached by gravel forest roads: scrub the riser, seat and walls with hauled water and disinfectant, sweep or hose the floor, deal with insects, spiderwebs, mud, vandalism and no power or plumbing.

Supply and refuse round: restock toilet paper, paper towels, soap and seat covers in dispensers; empty and re-line trash and recycling cans at restrooms, picnic sites and trailheads; haul bagged refuse to the dumpster or truck.

Replenishing firewood: load split wood or wrapped bundles onto a truck/trailer, haul it around the campground loop, and refill firewood bins, host sales racks and group-site woodsheds; restock kindling; stack neatly, in weather and on uneven ground.

Litter policing of maintained day-use turf, picnic lawns, beach and gravel areas after weekends and events: pick up cigarette butts, bottle caps, cans, wrappers, broken glass and small debris across mowed grass and gravel in an agency-controlled recreation area.

Campsite turnover cleanup: shovel ash and charred trash from fire rings, rake and level the site and tent pad, scrub picnic tables and grill grates, sweep shelter or camp-kitchen floors and wipe counters, remove abandoned gear and bulky trash left by campers.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is an autonomous bathroom-cleaning robot deployed in hospitals and airports; it cleans toilets, urinals and floors, opens doors, picks up trash and refills its own water and chemicals during daily facility operations.

sources.title: Those viral bathroom-cleaning bots won't be saving our butts anytime soon (Popular Science)
sources.claim: Reporting on Somatic's robot working in a medical facility notes that restocking consumables (paper towels, toilet ...) are still done by human staff.

sources.title: Primech launches upgraded bathroom cleaning robot (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Primech AI's HYTRON mobile manipulator autonomously cleans bathrooms (floors, toilets, mirrors, doors) in airports, hospitals, hotels, malls and offices and completed its first commercial trials ....

sources.title: Primech AI Deploys Hytron Autonomous Cleaning Robots in Multi-Storey School Pilot Program
sources.claim: Primech AI announced deployment of Hytron autonomous bathroom cleaning robots ..., an institution-controlled human work facility.

sources.title: Product – Angsa Robotics
sources.claim: The Angsa robot autonomously cleans outdoor public spaces, collecting small litter from grass and gravel at up to 8,000 m2 and 2,000 items per shift, detecting and avoiding obstacles without extra infrastructure.

sources.title: Angsa Robotics Uses Swift to Increase Efficiency of Autonomous Trash Picking Robots
sources.claim: Angsa's autonomous trash-picking robots are used to keep parks, green spaces and open-air festival grounds free of small litter, using RTK positioning for geofenced autonomous coverage of grass and gravel surfaces.

sources.system: PalletPro XS robotic bag palletizing cell
sources.title: PalletPro XS - Bag palletizing - INNO Robotics
sources.claim: Commercial robotic bag-palletizing cells stack bagged bulk products including firewood and charcoal, picking bags off a conveyor and building stacks to a set pattern inside a guarded cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic palletizing of bagged/bundled goods, explicitly including firewood bags. Under the E1 counterfactual the wood arrives fixtured on a conveyor, so stacking bundles into a rack involves the same object class, weights and placement precision as the palletizing cell already performs.

sources.title: Autonomous Cleaning Bot To Start Scrubbing Public Toilets In 2024 (European Cleaning Journal)
sources.claim: HiveBotics' Abluo is an autonomous restroom-cleaning robot with robotic arms that detects, disinfects and dries toilet fixtures in public washrooms in Singapore.

tasks.label: Erect signs or fences, using posthole diggers, shovels, or other hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Build or repair a wire boundary fence (barbed or woven wire) on rangeland, a wildlife area, or a grazing allotment: dig holes with a posthole digger for braced wood corner/brace assemblies, drive steel T-posts along the line, then stretch, tie and staple wire. Rocky/rooty soil, slopes, brush, limited vehicle access, weather exposure.

Erect a post-mounted sign (trailhead, regulatory, interpretive, boundary notice) at a forest trail, road junction, wetland access or timber-sale boundary: hand-dig or auger a hole in rooty/rocky ground, set and plumb a 4x4 wood or steel post, tamp or concrete it, and bolt/rivet the sign panel square and level.

Erect a deer/livestock exclosure or tree-protection fence around a new planting or restoration unit on cut-over ground: drive or dig in posts amid slash, stumps and uneven microtopography, then hang and fasten woven wire or plastic mesh, including gate/overlap details.

Install a run of boundary/marker posts carrying pre-applied decals (carsonite, fiberglass or steel markers) along a surveyed line in brushy forest or rangeland, driving each post with a hand driver at GPS/flagged points; no separate panel fastening needed on site.

Erect signs and fences at a developed recreation or administrative site kept by the agency (campground, trailhead parking lot, visitor-center grounds, nursery/compound yard): set posts in augered holes with concrete on mowed, level, vehicle-accessible ground and bolt on panels, rails, or cable/split-rail barrier.

sources.system: Roto-Fence (Farmscan AG / Kidd Farm Machinery / Harper Adams University)
sources.developer: Farmscan AG, Kidd Farm Machinery, Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: Roto-Fence, a tractor-plus-post-driver system, autonomously placed fence posts one after another at surveyed points during a live field demonstration in UK pasture; wire/electric line installation was not shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing grazing-fence posts. Transfers to driving marker/fence posts at surveyed points on kept, machine-traversable ground; same object class (posts) and accuracy demand, but no wire stringing or panel fastening demonstrated.

sources.title: Robotic pile driver faster than manual versions, says US startup – pv magazine International
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously surveys, distributes, drives and inspects steel foundation piles on utility-scale solar construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving foundation posts (H-piles) into soil at surveyed points to plumb/height tolerance. Transfers to setting fence and sign posts, but only on graded machine-accessible ground and without any panel or wire attachment.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: The RPD 35 workflow requires piles to be loaded into baskets by a mini excavator and telehandler before the machine runs autonomously, i.e. material presentation is engineered around the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (post/pile setting); cited to show the degree of purpose-built material presentation that the autonomous post driving depends on.

sources.system: Terafab / Terafab V2 automated field factory
sources.title: Terabase Energy advances automated PV construction with robotics, AI tools - pv magazine Global
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab is a purpose-built automated onsite field factory whose robotic line assembles panels onto steel torque tubes and whose rovers install the completed assemblies onto pre-positioned mounts; deployed on five utility-scale projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting rigid panels to structural members on a fixtured line and mounting the assembly on pre-set posts. Comparable objects (flat panels, steel posts/tubes) and fastening precision, in an environment built around the machine (E1).

sources.title: Terabase Energy's Next-Generation Terafab Completes Field Testing, Ready for Deployment
sources.claim: Terafab V2 completed field testing and is described by the developer as an autonomously operating robotic construction system ready for commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as evidence 3: automated fixtured assembly and installation of panel-on-frame structures onto pre-set foundations.

sources.system: Universal Robots screwdriving cells (UR cobots with screwdriving end effectors)
sources.title: Screwdriving Automation: industrial cobots deliver precise and repeatable automotive fastening – Universal Robots
sources.claim: Commercial robotic screwdriving/fastening cells are routinely deployed on manufacturing assembly stations to place and torque threaded fasteners on panels and covers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting panels to frames in a fixtured cell. Transfers to fastening a sign panel or wire mesh to a post when the post is presented in a fixture, as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.developer: Harvard Wyss Institute / Designing Emergence Lab (Melenbrink, Werfel)
sources.title: Romu the construction robot drives sheet piles into ground | Equipment World
sources.claim: Romu, a research robot, autonomously drives posts and interlocking sheet piles into granular soil and was demonstrated outdoors on a beach; it remains a research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous post driving for sand fencing in natural terrain; shows unstructured-terrain post driving exists only at research-prototype scale, short of worker-quality fence or sign erection.

sources.system: Autoplant autonomous site preparation and planting machine
sources.developer: Autoplant consortium (Skogforsk, Umeå University, Bracke Forest; Vinnova-funded)
sources.title: Autoplant—Autonomous Site Preparation and Tree Planting for a Sustainable Bioeconomy (Forests, MDPI)
sources.claim: The Autoplant autonomous forest regeneration machine (crane, scarifier, planting head) was integrated and tested for one week on a Swedish clearcut; forest-terrain autonomous ground-working remains a research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously penetrating forest soil and inserting an object (seedling) on cut-over ground. Closest forest-terrain analogue to post setting, but low-force, small objects, prototype maturity, and no panel or wire fastening.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Gramazio Kohler Research / Robotic Systems Lab) with Eberhard AG
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a six-metre-high dry-stone wall | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's HEAP autonomous excavator built a 65-m-long, 6-m-high dry-stone wall outdoors, scanning and placing multi-tonne boulders autonomously at a company-run circularity park.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor construction of a linear barrier from placed elements. Shows heavy outdoor autonomous manipulation exists, but with no tool-based hole digging and no fastening of wire or panels.

tasks.label: Select tree seedlings, prepare the ground, or plant the trees in reforestation areas, using manual planting tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steep, slash-covered clearcut in the Pacific Northwest / Inland West: crew member carries 300+ bare-root conifer seedlings in planting bags, walks the unit on 30-60% slopes over stumps, logging slash and duff, scalps a microsite with a hoedad, opens a hole, sets the seedling at correct depth with roots straight, firms soil, and repeats 700-1,200 times a day to a contract spacing and survival standard.

Flat to rolling southern pine plantation site that has been sheared, bedded and burned: worker hand-plants loblolly/slash pine bare-root seedlings with a dibble bar along bedded rows at 8x10 ft spacing, culling stunted or damaged stock from the bag, in wet winter soil with stumps and debris present.

Post-fire or high-elevation restoration planting: rocky, ash-covered ground with standing dead snags and downed logs, container stock planted into scattered favorable microsites (shade of logs, north aspects) with a hoedad or planting bar, often at remote sites reached on foot, under agency stocking specifications.

Riparian, wetland or hardwood conservation planting: mixed-species containerized or bare-root stock planted by hand along stream banks, wet meadows or old fields, with hand ground preparation (scalping sod, mattock work) and installation of tubes/mats around each seedling, on ground that varies from mud to compacted pasture.

Seedling handling at the nursery or field cache before planting: grading and culling lifted stock by size, root mass and damage, counting and bundling into bags or boxes, keeping roots moist and cool, and loading planting bags for the crew — done on tables/conveyors in a nursery packing shed or at a shaded field cache.

Hand ground preparation ahead of planting: clearing competing brush and grass from planting spots with hoe, mattock or brush blade, scalping sod, breaking hardpan and mounding on wet spots across a unit before or as seedlings go in.

sources.system: AutoPlant autonomous site preparation and planting machine (Skogforsk / Bracke Forest / LTU / KTH)
sources.developer: Skogforsk, Bracke Forest AB, Luleå University of Technology, KTH
sources.title: Autoplant—Autonomous Site Preparation and Tree Planting for a Sustainable Bioeconomy (Forests 15(2):263)
sources.claim: The Swedish AutoPlant project integrated autonomous driving, planting-spot detection, crane motion planning and a Bracke planting head on a terrain vehicle and demonstrated autonomous site preparation and planting of a seedling at a clearcut regeneration area; it remains a proof-of-concept, and in one control experiment the planting unit itself was replaced by a timing emulator.

sources.title: Här testas en helautonom maskin! - Skogforsk
sources.claim: Skogforsk's own account of the fully autonomous scarifying-and-planting machine tested on a clearcut in Jämtland describes it as extremely slow with everything malfunctioning at the first attempt, improving only after several upgrades — i.e. far from crew-level productivity or reliability in the forest.

sources.system: Vision-based planting position selection system for an unmanned reforestation machine (Bracke prototype planting head)
sources.developer: Luleå University of Technology with Bracke Forest
sources.title: Vision-based planting position selection system for an unmanned reforestation machine, Forestry 98(2):266
sources.claim: A vision-based planting-position selection system for an unmanned reforestation machine was field-tested on Swedish clearcuts; it can pick obstacle-free planting points, but roughly half of the mounding/site-preparation attempts fail in stony moraine soils, showing that autonomous in-forest planting is not yet at production quality.

sources.system: Commercial mechanical / automatic transplanters (TTS, Japan Agri-Trading and others)
sources.developer: various manufacturers (survey by University of Georgia CAES)
sources.title: Mechanical Transplanters for Tree Fruit and Vegetable Seedlings | CAES Field Report
sources.claim: University of Georgia extension review of transplanting machinery states that autonomous transplanters that plant seedlings without a human driver are still essentially concepts, with very few commercial options; commercial machines (semi-automatic and automatic transplanters) are tractor- or UTV-mounted and require human operation.
sources.transferJustification: Field transplanting of seedlings is the closest mechanized analogue to hand planting seedlings; it establishes that even in cultivated fields, driverless seedling-planting machines are not commercially available.

sources.system: ISO Grade 8000 plant sorting machine (vision by Robovision)
sources.title: ISO Grade 8000: Advanced plant sorting machine - ISO
sources.claim: The ISO Grade 8000 is a commercially sold sorting machine in which young plants are conveyed through a multi-camera box, assessed individually in 3D by AI vision, and then picked and sorted by several robots with plug-specific grippers according to grower-set quality criteria.
sources.transferJustification: Grading and culling nursery plug seedlings by size/quality is the same selection judgment a planter or seedling puller makes on lifted stock; objects (young tree-sized plugs) and precision are comparable, but the machine requires plants presented on its own conveyor line.

sources.system: Viscon young plant automation lines (precision transplanting and grading systems)
sources.title: Young plant automation solutions - Viscon Group Young Plant Automation
sources.claim: Viscon supplies commercial turnkey young-plant automation lines that automate sowing, robotic transplanting of plugs and cuttings into growing media, and vision/AI-based grading and sorting, in nursery production facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Machine planting of seedlings into prepared growing medium presented in trays is the fixtured, work-brought-to-the-machine form of 'prepare the ground and plant the seedling'; objects (tree-seedling plugs) and placement precision are comparable to hand planting, but the medium must be presented by the line.

sources.system: Kubota Agri Robo Rice Transplanter NW8SA
sources.title: Evolution and History of Rice Transplanters (Kubota)
sources.claim: Kubota launched the self-driving Agri Robo NW8SA rice transplanter, a commercial machine able to carry out unmanned ... of seedlings in leveled paddy fields under human monitoring, with a person restocking seedling trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized transplanting of seedlings at fixed spacing across a managed field. Transfer is limited: rice seedling mats pressed into puddled mud differ in object and mechanism from setting a conifer seedling's root system into a hole in mineral soil.

sources.system: Bracke Planter P11.a excavator-mounted planting head
sources.title: The Bracke Planter P11.a (Brazil version) | Forsilvitech
sources.claim: Commercial mechanized tree planting devices such as the Bracke P11.a mount on a hydraulic excavator and prepare soil and plant container seedlings, but they are run continuously by a machine operator who also reloads the seedling carousel.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (site preparation plus seedling planting) performed by machine, but under continuous human operation, so it cannot support an autonomous judgment.

sources.title: New Tree Tech: Cutting-edge drones give reforestation a helping hand (Mongabay)
sources.claim: Mast Reforestation (formerly DroneSeed) used drone seed-vessel dropping combined with hand planting of seedlings to reforest about 300 acres of burned land in western Oregon; the drones deliver seed, not planted seedlings, and human crews still hand-planted the seedlings.
sources.transferJustification: Aerial seeding addresses the same goal (reforesting a burn) but its output is broadcast seed rather than planted seedlings meeting stocking/survival specifications, so it is not the same accepted output.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to forest survey crews by clearing site-lines, holding measuring tools, or setting stakes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clearing sight-lines: swinging a machete/brush hook or running a clearing saw to open the line of sight between instrument and target through understory brush, saplings, briars and low limbs on a mature or mixed forest plot, and opening a walkable line along a compass bearing.

Holding measuring tools: standing the stadia rod, prism pole, GNSS rover or the end of a tape/chain plumb over a point the crew chief designates, holding it steady while the reading is taken, then moving on foot through the plot to the next point on voice/radio direction.

Setting stakes: driving wooden lath, plot-center pins, corner and witness stakes at surveyed points in the forest, labeling them and hanging flagging tape so the marks are found again under vegetation.

The same assistance (line clearing, tool holding, staking) performed on open, drivable ground: recent clearcut units with stumps and slash, roadside rights-of-way, rangeland, and young plantations reached by truck or ATV.

Hauling and staging crew equipment between plots — packing tripods, instruments, stake bundles, chain, paint and water over rough, steep, wet or brushy ground, and setting the gear out at each station.

sources.system: ANYmal C/D forest inventory system (DigiForest, Oxford Robotics Institute / ETH Zurich)
sources.developer: University of Oxford ORI, ETH Zurich, ANYbotics
sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots — System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead
sources.claim: An ANYmal quadruped ran autonomous under-canopy forest inventory missions in real forests in Finland, the UK ..., navigating and mapping plots up to 1 ha, but with a safety operator intervening repeatedly and with dense undergrowth and bogs defeating it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ground-level forest survey (tree measurement). It is the closest demonstrated robotic work inside the actual E3 forest setting of this task, and it shows current limits — a safety operator followed the robot, missions were aborted in bog, and areas with dense undergrowth could not be entered autonomously — so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion in forest.

sources.title: Cortador (Grande 15 Brush Cutter) – Burro AI
sources.claim: The Burro Cortador (Grande 15 brush cutter) is sold as a fully autonomous, all-electric vegetation-cutting robot that works vineyard rows, slopes over 30 degrees and open terrain, cutting thick vegetation without supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mechanical clearing of heavy vegetation along planned lines in a managed outdoor work site (vineyard/nursery/campus). Cutting a swath of standing vegetation to open a line is the same physical output a survey helper produces when clearing a sight-line, on comparable ground and with comparable precision requirements.

sources.title: Burro introduces Grande 44 with proven outdoor autonomy built for heavy industry - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Burro's outdoor autonomy platform is also used for autonomous payload transport of up to 1,500 lb across facility campuses and for autonomous mowing/spraying at commercial vineyard operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous carrying and delivery of tools and materials around an outdoor work site, which is what hauling and staging survey gear between stations requires.

sources.developer: Scythe Robotics (acquired by Autonomous Solutions Inc.)
sources.title: Autonomous Solutions acquires Scythe Robotics - Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: Scythe's M.52 autonomous commercial mower operated at large scale for commercial landscape contractors, cutting vegetation on institution-controlled grounds across 30 states in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous vegetation cutting over large maintained areas. It substantiates that unattended cutting of standing vegetation to a specified swath on institution-controlled grounds is a routine, commercially accepted robotic output.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 / FieldLink
sources.title: Trimble goes laser scanning with Boston's robot dog - Construction Management
sources.claim: Trimble and Boston Dynamics sell a turnkey solution in which Spot autonomously walks a predefined waypoint path on a construction site and collects registered survey-grade laser scans with the Trimble X7.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a legged robot autonomously carrying and stationing a survey instrument at operator-designated points on a work site, tied to the project coordinate system — the same function as a helper packing and holding the measuring tool where the crew chief directs.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 robotic pile driver
sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ... surveys, distributes, drives and records foundation piles at planned coordinates on utility-scale solar sites, at roughly 300 piles per day with ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously placing and driving a vertical member into the ground at a surveyed coordinate. That is the same act as setting a stake at a survey point, at equal or better positional tolerance, though demonstrated only on cleared, graded ground with heavy steel piles.

sources.title: CivDot | Construction Robot for Automated layout – Measur Drones
sources.claim: CivDot is a commercially deployed autonomous GNSS layout rover that marks up to 3,000 survey points a day to ~30 mm on construction sites, but it sprays paint and a human worker follows behind to install the physical flags, nails or stakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stake-out of surveyed coordinates in the field. It substantiates autonomous navigation and centimetre-accurate point location on open sites, but explicitly leaves the physical stake installation to a human, limiting what it can support.

sources.title: California agencies eye BurnBot for wildfire prevention - The Robot Report
sources.claim: BurnBot's RX-series vegetation-treatment machines used for fuel breaks in California are operated by a human by remote control from within 500 feet; autonomy is stated as a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized brush/fuel clearing in wildland settings. Cited as the state of the art for clearing woody vegetation in unmanaged terrain, and it is teleoperated, so it cannot support an E3 positive judgment for sight-line clearing.

tasks.label: Sort tree seedlings, discarding substandard seedlings, according to standard charts or verbal instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bare-root conifer nursery packing shed during lifting season: seedlings arrive from the field in tubs/crates or on a belt, worker at a grading table separates tangled seedlings, judges each against a chart (stem caliper, shoot height, root mass, damage, bud condition), throws culls into a waste bin and passes graders to counting/bundling. Cold, wet, high-throughput seasonal work.

Container (plug/styroblock) forest seedling nursery: worker culls substandard plugs from trays at a grading/packing station or on greenhouse benches, judging height, caliper, vigor/chlorosis, missing or dead cells, and consolidates good stock into shipping trays or boxes.

Sorting at or near the planting site / staging area: crew opens bags or boxes of seedlings and, on verbal instruction from the crew boss, discards desiccated, molded, broken-stem, or J-rooted seedlings before planting, working out of tubs on a tailgate or on the ground.

Small state or conservation-district nursery handling mixed bare-root hardwood, shrub, and specialty stock: many species and size classes in one day, large tangled root systems, sorting on outdoor tables or a trailer against species-specific size charts and verbal instructions.

Small-batch sorting for seedlots, genetic families, or special customer orders: seedlings sorted and kept identity-labeled by lot, graded per written spec, counts recorded, careful handling of limited stock.

sources.system: Flier Systems Young Plant Sorter (YPL) with Aris vision
sources.date: 2021-2025 (product listed on AgriExpo since Jan 2021; current product page)
sources.title: Young Plant Sorter (YPL) - Flier Systems
sources.claim: Flier Systems' Young Plant Sorter (YPL) is a commercial machine that grades young plants with Aris vision and chlorophyll-fluorescence technology and mechanically sorts them into quality classes including waste, at up to 8,000 plants/hour; it is marketed for vegetable plants, flowers, trees and breeding crops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grading nursery young plants/plug seedlings against configured quality standards and diverting substandard plants to waste. Same objects (plug seedlings in trays), same accept/cull decision made against a set standard, same conveyor-fed nursery grading setting.

sources.system: BCC / Flier Systems transplanting & sorting machine (Aris vision inside)
sources.developer: BCC AB with Flier Systems B.V.
sources.title: Transplanting & Sorting - BCCAB
sources.claim: BCC AB, a forest-nursery equipment supplier, offers with Flier Systems a grading and sorting machine specifically for the forest nursery sector, using Aris AI vision and chlorophyll fluorescence, handling small plugs at up to 900 cycles/hour with tray track-and-trace.

sources.title: Pic-O-Mat Vision - Viscon Group
sources.claim: The Viscon (Visser) Pic-O-Mat Vision is a commercial automatic plug transplanter whose multi-camera system grades each plant and discards bad plants and empty plugs onto a waste belt, transplanting only plants meeting the selected quality, at up to 20,000 plants/hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: culling substandard plug seedlings from propagation trays. The accept/discard judgment against a quality standard and the handling of small rooted seedlings are the same operations required to sort container tree seedlings.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University National Robotics Engineering Center (with five California strawberry plant nurseries)
sources.title: Carnegie Mellon Engineers Develop Machine That Visually Inspects and Sorts Strawberry Plants
sources.claim: Carnegie Mellon's NREC built and field-tested a machine that inspects harvested bare-root strawberry nursery plants on a conveyor with computer vision and mechanically sorts them by quality; in a 10-day nursery field test with mud, rain and frost it sorted over 75,000 plants at about 5,000 plants/hour with an error rate close to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grading harvested bare-root nursery planting stock into good and cull categories in a nursery packing operation. Objects (dormant bare-root plants with soil-covered roots), the good/cull decision against nursery standards, throughput and dirty conditions match bare-root tree seedling grading.

sources.system: Machine vision conifer seedling grading/QC system (Rigney & Kranzler, Oklahoma State University)
sources.developer: Oklahoma State University / Oklahoma Agricultural Experiment Station
sources.date: 1988 conference paper; system described in New Forests (2000)
sources.title: Machine vision for conifer seedling quality control | New Forests
sources.claim: A PC-based line-scan machine vision system for bare-root conifer seedlings automatically locates the root collar ..., root mass length and projected root/shoot area on seedlings placed on a conveyor, inspecting each seedling in under 0.25 seconds; earlier work classified seedlings as acceptable or cull on these criteria.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same objects (bare-root conifer nursery seedlings) with the exact grading variables used in seedling grading charts; the machine makes the measurement/classification autonomously, with seedling presentation supplied by the conveyor line.

emergingTasks.label: Create field maps using geographic information systems technology.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Fallers
roles.description: Use axes or chainsaws to fell trees using knowledge of tree characteristics and cutting techniques to control direction of fall and minimize tree damage.

tasks.label: Saw back-cuts, leaving sufficient sound wood to control direction of fall.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial hand falling in second-growth conifer timber (Pacific Northwest / inland West), stems roughly 12–30 in DBH, on steep or broken ground where ground machines cannot work. After setting the undercut, the faller saws the back-cut (conventional or Humboldt), holding a hinge of roughly 10% of DBH, often bore-cutting or driving wedges, judging lean, wind, brush and adjacent trees.

Large-diameter timber (over 30 in DBH, legacy/old-growth stems) on steep ground: high-value logs, heavy lean or side-lean, complex hinge geometry (tapered hinge, Dutchman, bore back-cut, back-cut above the undercut), wedges or jacks to swing the tree; a mis-cut hinge risks a barber chair, split butt log or a fatal miss-lay.

Hazard/danger-tree falling: fire-killed snags, rotten butts, dead tops, hollow or wind-thrown leaners along fire lines, roads, landings and salvage units. The faller must probe/sound the stem, decide how much sound wood remains, and shape the back-cut and hinge around punky or hollow wood, with an escape route planned.

Small-diameter thinning, pulpwood and fuels-reduction falling: stems under about 12 in on gentle to moderate ground, hundreds of quick face-and-back-cut sequences per shift, hinge left to lay stems in a consistent direction for skidding or lop-and-scatter.

Falling near values: roadside right-of-way, power lines, structures, fences, streams and recreation sites, where the tree must be dropped into a narrow lay. Precise hinge thickness and taper, wedges or a pull line/skidder assist, sometimes traffic control or a spotter present.

sources.system: SAHA (Supervised Autonomous HArvester, based on RCM Harveri 25)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / DigiForest consortium
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry
sources.claim: SAHA, a 4.5-tonne purpose-built autonomous harvester developed in the EU DigiForest project, autonomously navigates a mapped forest stand, reaches a selected small tree with a bidirectional harvester head, clamps it and cuts it, with cutting automated for trees specified in a prebuilt map (field trials in Switzerland, Finland, UK).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized felling of a selected standing tree. It substitutes for the faller's back-cut because the harvester head controls where the stem goes (by clamping rather than by hinge wood), so the accepted output — the tree comes down in the intended direction without damaging residuals — is the same.

sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (HTML)
sources.claim: In SAHA's field trials the machine drives itself to the mapped tree and positions the clamp autonomously, but a human operator must press a button for each cut, so the felling cycle is supervised rather than unattended.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab (Fang Nan et al.)
sources.title: SAHA: Supervised Autonomous HArvester for selective forest thinning (arXiv:2601.01282)
sources.claim: The SAHA harvester completed kilometre-long autonomous missions in northern European ..., autonomously navigating cluttered stands and reaching targeted trees for selective thinning; the paper frames the capability as supervised autonomy on a small thinning-scale platform.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous selective thinning. Same objects (standing conifer stems) and the same end state (selected tree severed and laid), so performance bears on whether the felling cut can be made under machine control in a forest.

sources.title: Swedish startup achieves first fully autonomous tree harvest by drone
sources.claim: AirForestry's 6-metre heavy-lift electric drone located, delimbed, felled and carried away a thinning-size spruce; the company reports a world-first autonomous aerial tree harvest, with the tree's descent controlled by the suspended harvesting tool rather than by hinge wood.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: felling a selected small tree with controlled descent. It bears on this task because the accepted output (tree severed and brought down without hitting residual trees) is the same, achieved by gripping instead of a hinge.

sources.title: A Swedish drone just did a lumberjack's job with nobody at the controls
sources.claim: Reporting on the AirForestry milestone distinguishes two separate events: felling in a real production forest, and a complete unsupervised fly–identify–delimb–cut–deliver sequence that was run on the company's own test field.
sources.transferJustification: Same felling task as above; cited to establish that the fully unsupervised cutting sequence was demonstrated on a purpose-built test field rather than in the unstructured production stand.

sources.system: MiCROTEC CT Log / Logeye 900 scanning line
sources.title: Cascade Hardwoods Adds Microtec CT Log Scanning
sources.claim: MiCROTEC CT Log scanners are installed in commercial sawmills (e.g., Cascade Hardwoods, Chehalis WA) and automatically detect internal rot, knots and cracks inside logs, feeding the mill's automated sawing optimisation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: judging sound wood inside a stem, which is what 'leaving sufficient sound wood' requires. In a purpose-built log line the machine already senses rot automatically and sets the saw pattern accordingly, so the assessment step transfers when the stem is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Industrial robot timber machining cell vs. CNC joinery machine
sources.developer: Wood Material Science & Engineering study (industrial robot / CNC joinery machine vendors)
sources.title: Robotic timber milling: accuracy assessment for construction applications and comparison to a CNC-machine
sources.claim: Industrial six-axis robots and CNC joinery machines machine fixtured timber members (glulam) to construction tolerances, with measured accuracy of the cut geometry compared across 45 milled specimens; such cells routinely cut wood to a specified remaining thickness from a digital model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine sawing of wood to a controlled depth. A back-cut is exactly a saw cut stopped so that a specified thickness of holding wood remains; fixtured robotic/CNC timber machining achieves this geometry at millimetre precision when the workpiece is presented in a known pose.

tasks.label: Control the direction of a tree's fall by scoring cutting lines with axes, sawing undercuts along scored lines with chainsaws, knocking slabs from cuts with single-bit axes, and driving wedges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Falling large second-growth/old-growth conifers (60-150+ cm dbh) on steep Pacific Northwest ground for a cable-yarding unit: the faller sizes up lean and defect, scores and saws a face/undercut with a long-bar chainsaw, knocks out the slab, back-cuts and drives wedges to swing the tree onto a lay that protects the corridor and leave trees; footing is brush, slash and 40-70% slopes with snags overhead.

Hand falling medium timber (roughly 30-60 cm dbh mixed conifer/hardwood) on moderate ground ahead of ground-based skidding or shovel logging: undercut scored and sawn, slab knocked out, back-cut with wedges driven to lift the tree over slight back-lean, trees laid to a bucking/skidding pattern.

Danger/hazard-tree falling: dead, fire-killed, rotten or broken-top trees along haul roads, fire lines, campgrounds, trails and utility right-of-way; unpredictable holding wood, hollow butts and hangers require shallow scored undercuts, careful wedging and escape planning, with the tree laid clear of the road or structure.

Pre-commercial/fuels-reduction hand falling in dense young stands (stems under ~25 cm dbh): high stem counts, quick undercut-and-back-cut technique, occasional wedge, stems dropped into lanes away from leave trees on natural forest floor.

Complex trees: heavy leaners, windthrown or root-sprung stems, trees with rot or heavy one-sided crowns, and trees that must be laid precisely away from property, streams or a roadway - requiring bore cuts, Dutchman/swing techniques, stacked wedges or jacks to overcome lean.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / University of Bonn / Prefor Oy
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry
sources.claim: SAHA, a 4.5-t driverless hydraulic harvester built in the EU DigiForest project, autonomously navigates real managed forests, reaches a mapped target tree with a bidirectional harvester head and runs an automatic cutting mode that severs and lays the tree (an operator presses a safety button to initiate the cut).
sources.transferJustification: Related task is mechanized selective-thinning felling: instead of undercut, slab and wedges, the harvester head clamps the stem and the boom directs where it goes, but the accepted output for a small stem is the same as this task's - the selected tree severed and laid on a chosen lay without damaging leave trees - and it occurs in the same standing-forest conditions.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich / University of Bonn / Prefor Oy
sources.title: SAHA: Supervised Autonomous HArvester for selective forest thinning (arXiv 2601.01282)
sources.claim: The SAHA harvester was field-tested over kilometre-long autonomous missions in northern European ... for first thinning (removal of smaller/suppressed stems in young stands), with supervised autonomy for navigation, terrain adaptation and arm/head control.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer: machine felling of small thinning stems substitutes for the axe/chainsaw/wedge technique but delivers the same output (selected tree severed and placed clear of leave trees) in the same standing-forest setting; it also bounds the demonstrated stem size to young-stand thinning.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: AirForestry's 6.2 m electric heavy-lift drone completed a full harvest cycle on a tree - locating it, delimbing, severing it and flying the stem out of a working production forest - reported as performed without human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is aerial thinning-felling: the drone grips the stem so the machine, not an undercut and wedges, controls where the tree goes, but the accepted output for a thinning stem - the selected tree severed and removed without damaging surrounding trees - matches this task's purpose.

sources.title: A drone just cut down a tree, stripped its branches, and carried it out of a forest - on its own
sources.claim: The AirForestry drone's lift capacity limits it to the small thinning stems typical of first thinning (about 40-140 kg trees), far below the timber size handled by hand fallers in commercial units.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the size envelope of the only autonomous aerial felling demonstration, showing it does not transfer to medium or large timber felling.

sources.system: Teleoperated steep-country harvesting machines (Univ. of Canterbury / Scion steepland harvesting programme)
sources.developer: University of Canterbury / Scion / Forest Growers Research
sources.title: Semi-autonomous brachiating robot for teleoperated steep terrain tree harvesting
sources.claim: Steep-terrain felling (>20 degree slopes), the ground where hand fallers are used, is beyond conventional harvesters and feller-bunchers, and the research response has been teleoperated machines rather than autonomous felling.

sources.system: Kodama teleoperation/autonomy kits on forestry machines
sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to mitigate wildfire risk - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kodama Systems, the most prominent US forestry-robotics deployment, fields teleoperation and partial-autonomy kits on thinning equipment (starting with skidders); the cutting and handling work is remotely operated rather than autonomous.

tasks.label: Stop saw engines, pull cutting bars from cuts, and run to safety as tree falls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steep-slope Pacific Northwest cable or helicopter unit: mature conifer 20-40+ in dbh, heavy brush, slash and uneven footing; faller finishes the back cut, kills the saw, pulls the bar free and moves down a pre-cleared escape path at ~45 degrees behind the stump while watching the top for widowmakers.

Ground-based harvest unit on moderate terrain: second-growth stems 10-24 in dbh felled at high production for skidder or forwarder extraction; dozens of trees per shift, each ending with saw shut down, bar withdrawn from the kerf and a short retreat clear of the stump and butt swing.

Hazard/danger tree work: fire-killed snags on an incident, storm-broken, rotten or leaning trees near crews, roads or camps; wood strength unpredictable, tops and limbs can fail early, so withdrawing the saw and clearing the area fast is the critical part of the job.

Precommercial thinning and fuels-reduction felling: dense small-diameter stems 4-10 in in brushy regeneration stands; hundreds of quick cuts per day, saw pulled out and a step or two clear as each small stem goes over.

Roadside, utility right-of-way or near-structure felling with a constrained drop zone: wedges, ropes or jacks used to control direction, traffic or crew below; saw shut off, bar withdrawn, faller retreats clear while the tree falls into the planned lay.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: AirForestry's electric heavy-lift drone autonomously felled a tree and flew the stem out of a working Swedish production forest, completing the harvest cycle without human control; trees handled are thinning-grade stems of roughly 40-140 kg. This is a first-of-kind demonstration, not routine production.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: an autonomous machine makes the felling cut and clears itself from the falling stem, which is the machine analogue of stopping the saw, pulling the bar and retreating. Cited to show the frontier in real forests is a single demonstration on very small stems, not worker-quality production felling.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab, University of Bonn, Prefor Oy (DigiForest)
sources.title: SAHA: Supervised Autonomous HArvester for selective forest thinning (arXiv:2601.01282)
sources.claim: SAHA, a 4.5-tonne robotic harvester with a harvester head, autonomously navigates real northern European forests and reaches/grasps selected thinning trees under supervised autonomy; the authors state that fully automated cutting in forests remains uniquely difficult.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous approach to and grasping of trees for thinning). Cited for a negative judgment: the most advanced forest harvester autonomy demonstrated stops at reaching and grasping the tree and does not autonomously execute the felling cut and safe withdrawal.

sources.system: HEAP legged tree harvester (Menzi Muck M545)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Robotic Precision Harvesting: Mapping, Localization, Planning and Control for a Legged Tree Harvester
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's legged excavator harvester (HEAP) performed autonomous navigation and tree grabbing ... real forest, but the felling cut itself was deliberately excluded from the autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous forest harvesting mission). Cited for a negative judgment: the cutting and tree-fall phase, which is exactly this task, was left out of the autonomous pipeline.

sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to prevent wildfires - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced US forestry robotics deployment for thinning national forests is a teleoperated/remote-supervised platform (skidders), i.e. a human drives the machine remotely rather than the machine working autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (mechanized forest thinning work in US woods). Cited for a negative judgment: the deployed system is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment for felling and clearing in the forest.

sources.system: POSCH firewood processors with automatic log feeders
sources.title: Firewood processor - find the right fuelwood machinery here | POSCH
sources.claim: Commercial firewood processors clamp and feed logs up to 70 cm diameter to a harvester chain saw that cuts the billet under machine control, with the cut piece dropping away to a splitter/conveyor and no person in the cutting zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a chain saw driven by machine control severs a clamped stem, the bar is withdrawn from the kerf and the severed piece falls into a guarded drop zone with no worker exposed — the purpose-built-cell equivalent of stopping the saw, pulling the bar and getting clear, at comparable stem diameters.

sources.title: Forestry: Your guide to the latest firewood processors | Forestry Journal
sources.claim: The Palax D460 chainsaw firewood processor feeds the log hydraulically, measures it with optical sensors and lets electronic control decide and execute each cut, i.e. sensing-driven automatic sawing rather than hand-guided cutting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled chainsaw crosscutting of stems presented to the machine. Shows the sensing-and-control loop (measure, cut, retract, release the piece) runs without step-by-step human control in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Joinery machines | Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger CNC joinery machines are fully automatic, CAD-driven saw and machining cells that size and crosscut large structural timbers inside guarded industrial cells, with material fed and positioned by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sawing of large fixtured timber in a purpose-built, guarded cell. Establishes that when the workpiece is brought to the machine, machine control reliably completes the cut, withdraws the tool and discharges the cut piece with nobody in the hazard zone.

tasks.label: Select trees to be cut down, assessing factors such as site, terrain, and weather conditions before beginning work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial clearcut/harvest block on steep Pacific Northwest ground: before starting, the faller walks the unit, reads each tree's lean, crown weight, rot indicators and limb hang-ups, judges slope, snow/mud footing and prevailing wind, and decides which stems to take first and in what sequence and lay.

Selection/thinning or partial-cut harvest in a mixed stand: faller works to a forester's prescription or paint marks, deciding which stems qualify, which must stay to protect residuals and regeneration, and which cannot be taken safely given adjacent leave trees.

Hazard/danger-tree assessment along roads, trails, fire lines or in a burned or storm-damaged stand: faller sizes up snags, broken tops, root-sprung and leaning stems, decides which are removed versus left, and factors wind and unstable ground.

Tree-service or utility right-of-way removal on developed ground: faller assesses targets (houses, wires, vehicles), available drop zone, root and decay condition, and wind/precipitation before deciding which trees come down whole and which need dismantling.

Start-of-shift and mid-shift reassessment: checking wind speed, rain/ice, visibility, ground conditions and crew position, then deciding whether falling proceeds, which part of the unit is worked, or whether work stops.

tasks.label: Measure felled trees and cut them into specified log lengths, using chain saws and axes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production commercial timber falling on managed timberland (Southeast pine, Inland West, PNW second growth): after felling a 12–30 in dbh conifer, the faller walks the stem on uneven, slashy ground, judges defect/sweep, measures with tape or marked stick to specified sawlog/pulp lengths plus trim allowance, reads the bind, and bucks with a chainsaw without pinching the bar or splitting the log.

Steep-slope, large-diameter coastal or old-growth-type falling (30–60+ in butt logs, redwood/Douglas-fir): faller works a downhill-lying stem on 40–70% slope, cuts multiple sawlogs to spec lengths, uses wedges, undercuts/back cuts on the log, side-hill footing, heavy compression/tension binds, chunks of 4–6 ft diameter.

Bucking/merchandising at a roadside landing after skidding: tree-length stems piled or laid out on a cleared landing; the bucker measures and cuts stems into specified log lengths, trims defect, cuts culls for pulp, moving among stacked wood and working machines.

Small-scale, woodlot, right-of-way and land-clearing work on private parcels: mixed hardwoods and small conifers felled, bucked to 8 ft pulp, 16 in firewood or short saw lengths; tolerances loose, ground littered with brush, fences, stumps and slash.

Storm blowdown, salvage and fire-line hazard work: wind-thrown or fire-killed stems that are tangled, spring-loaded, root-wadded or leaning on other trees; faller measures and bucks into removable/specified lengths while relieving high tension and compression, often in poor footing and degraded wood.

sources.system: Inotech Intellibuck stem merchandiser; USNR LogPro merchandiser
sources.title: TECH UPDATE: Log Bucking and Merchandising - Forestnet
sources.claim: Commercial mill merchandiser systems scan the whole stem's true shape, compute the optimum bucking pattern and drive traveling saws to cut stems into specified log lengths; Inotech's Intellibuck handles stems up to 80 ft long and 24 in diameter, USNR's LogPro line integrates scanning, optimization, conveyors and traveling saw carriages.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the faller's bucking — measuring a felled stem and cross-cutting it into specified log lengths — performed by machine on stems of comparable size, but with the stem presented on a purpose-built conveyor/deck rather than lying in the woods.

sources.developer: Various (industry description, Online Expos solid-wood equipment guide)
sources.title: Log Merchandisers & Log Handling - Online Expos
sources.claim: In deployed lineal merchandiser lines the optimizer's bucking solution directly controls the saws, which cut the stopped log to length without a human making the cut decision or trigger.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the bucking step of this task (measure stem, cut to specified lengths) executed under machine control inside a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Oregon Company Starts Up New Wood Pellet Operations - Forestnet
sources.claim: A 2025 startup of an Oregon wood processing facility uses an automated four-saw shifting merchandiser: logs are singulated, debarked, scanned and optimally bucked in-line — a currently operating installation, not a prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Deployed instance of machine measurement and cutting of stems into specified log lengths, the same output the faller produces.

sources.developer: Sawmill equipment industry (Pallet Enterprise technical review)
sources.title: Sawlines: Scanners, Computers Optimize Machines - Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Mill bucking lines measure length with encoders and scanners and output the computed cut solution directly to the buck saw and ..., i.e. measurement and cutting are closed-loop machine functions.
sources.transferJustification: Describes the measuring-and-cutting-to-length function of this task under machine control in a purpose-built environment.

sources.developer: Visser Rien & Obi Okey Francis, Croatian Journal of Forest Engineering
sources.title: Automation and Robotics in Forest Harvesting Operations: Identifying Near-Term Opportunities
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed subject review of automation and robotics in forest harvesting concludes that no fully autonomous systems are working in timber harvesting; log extraction/transport, not felling or processing, is judged the nearest-term robotic operation.
sources.transferJustification: Negative context for in-woods (E3) bucking: establishes that machine felling/processing in the stand remains operator-controlled.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: AirForestry's electric drone autonomously identified, felled, delimbed and flew out a single tree in a working production forest in May 2026 — an autonomous in-forest harvesting first, but a one-tree demonstration of felling/extraction, not measuring a downed stem and bucking it into multiple specified log lengths.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous thinning/felling in a standing forest). It does not substantiate this task: no measuring of a felled stem into specified log lengths, single-tree demo, small thinning stems only.

sources.title: 575 Harvesting Head | Cut-to-Length | TCi Attachments
sources.claim: Modern cut-to-length harvesting heads measure log length automatically and control the bucking saw, but the head is carried and positioned by an operator seated in the machine cab, so the in-woods measure-and-buck cycle as a whole is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed mechanically in the forest (E3), but under continuous operator control from the cab, so it cannot support a positive autonomous judgment.

sources.system: Hakki Pilke 55 Pro / 50 Pro firewood processor
sources.title: Introducing the revolutionary Hakki Pilke 55 Pro – Hakki Pilke
sources.claim: Professional firewood processors with chainsaw cross-cut units position a measuring device automatically to the selected length and saw at the touch of a ..., but log infeed and cycle initiation are operator-controlled at a fixed machine station.
sources.transferJustification: Same measure-and-cut-to-length output with an actual chainsaw on small logs at a purpose-built station; operator-fed, so it is corroborating context rather than a basis for an autonomous judgment.

tasks.label: Insert jacks or drive wedges behind saws to prevent binding of saws and to start trees falling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large second-growth conifer (28-60+ in DBH) on a steep Pacific Northwest/Rockies slope with back or side lean: after the undercut, the faller drives two or more plastic wedges with an axe or single-jack behind the bar during the back cut, stacking or double-wedging, feeling the bar for pinch, watching the kerf open and the top move, on brushy uneven footing with an escape route planned.

Mid-size timber (12-28 in) on moderate ground in a commercial clearcut or harvest unit: one or two wedges set behind the bar partway through the back cut to keep the kerf from closing on the saw and to tip the stem onto the intended lay; production pace, dozens of trees per shift.

Partial cut, thinning, or hardwood selective harvest: wedging to swing a tree with slight side/back lean away from residual crop trees, a skid road, or a property line; tight lay, careful hinge and wedge placement to avoid damaging leave trees.

Hazard/danger tree work in burned units, blowdown, or storm damage: fire-killed, rotten, broken-topped or heavily leaning stems along roads and in salvage units; wedging cautiously where rot, hollow butts, bound-up limbs, or wind make bind and reaction unpredictable.

Heavy back-lean or high-value stem requiring a felling jack: the faller sets a hydraulic bottle jack or powered spindle wedge in the back cut with a pad, then pumps or drives it to lift and tip the tree while keeping the saw free.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: AirForestry's electric harvesting drone completed an autonomous end-to-end harvest cycle in a working production forest, gripping a small stem from the top, cutting it low and flying it out; the tool is sized for thinning-grade trees of 40-140 kg and replaces wedging by holding the stem rather than by inserting anything in a kerf.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized felling of small thinning stems, where the gripping tool serves the wedge's purpose (no saw pinch, controlled fall). Transfer fails here: the stems weigh 40-140 kg, far lighter than the back-leaning timber that requires wedges or jacks, and the drone never inserts a wedge in a kerf.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Robotic Precision Harvesting: Mapping, Localization, Planning and Control for a Legged Tree Harvester
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's HEAP legged harvester (Menzi Muck M545) autonomously navigated a natural forest and grabbed selected trees with a gripper, with a human in the cabin for safety; the demonstrated autonomy covers approach and grasping, not back-cutting, wedging, or directional felling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous approach and grasp of standing trees in forest terrain by a full-size hydraulic machine. It is the closest autonomous manipulation of standing timber found, but it stops at grabbing: no cutting, no wedge or jack insertion, and no control of direction of fall.

sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to mitigate wildfire risk - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kodama Systems fields teleoperated and semi-autonomous forestry machines in California thinning operations, but the automation focus is the skidder; felling itself is done by an operator-run feller buncher.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized felling and extraction in US commercial thinning. Cited to show deployed forestry robotics is teleoperation of extraction machines, with felling under continuous human control, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Teleoperated JD909 feller buncher (Forest Growers Research programme)
sources.developer: Forest Growers Research / University of Canterbury, New Zealand
sources.title: JD909 feller-buncher showing camera angles to enable teleoperation (Automation and Robotics in Forest Harvesting Operations)
sources.claim: A feller buncher was converted for full teleoperation for steep-slope logging research in New Zealand using a purpose-built control booth; the machine remains under continuous human control rather than operating autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine felling of standing trees of faller-relevant size. Cited as the state of the art for machine-controlled felling; because it is continuously teleoperated it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the wedging task.

sources.developer: BaSt-Ing GmbH (sold by D.A. Hughes Forestry)
sources.title: TR300 Remote Controlled Felling Wedge – D.A. Hughes Forestry
sources.claim: The TR300 is a commercially sold powered spindle felling wedge with remote actuation and end-position sensors, but a person must set it in the back cut and trigger it; no machine places the wedge.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (inserting a wedge/jack to lift and tip the tree), but the device is a hand-placed, human-triggered powered tool rather than an autonomous robot, so it cannot support completion at any tier.

sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.claim: An experimental unmanned forestry machine (AORO) autonomously picked up logs from the ground ... drove through varied forest terrain without human intervention, showing autonomy in log handling rather than in felling or wedging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous forwarding (grasping and loading felled logs) in forest terrain. It establishes autonomous timber manipulation in unstructured forest, but only of loose logs on the ground; it shows nothing about back-cut wedging or controlling a standing tree's fall.

tasks.label: Assess logs after cutting to ensure that the quality and length are correct.
