sources.system: John Deere 1270G/1470G wheeled harvester (central lubrication, reversing cooling fan)
sources.title: 1270G WHEELED HARVESTER (John Deere product brochure)
sources.claim: John Deere G-series wheeled harvesters carry a central lubrication system that speeds daily greasing and a programmable reversing cooling fan that clears debris from cooler cores during operation in the stand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing debris from cooler cores, which the operator otherwise does with compressed air as part of daily fire-prevention cleaning; the on-board automated fan reversal performs the same debris removal on the same components.

sources.title: Industrial Vehicle Washing Systems - Manual & Robotic Solutions
sources.claim: InterClean supplies robotic wash systems that clean heavy mining vehicles up to 400-ton haul trucks automatically in a purpose-built bay with no personnel inside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing accumulated dirt and debris from the exterior and undercarriage of very large off-road machines, which is the bulk of the operator's fire-prevention cleaning; comparable machine size and soil, performed under machine control.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks — Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection missions at a 40-acre midstream oil and gas plant, performing anomaly detection, thermal inspection, gauge reading and gas-leak detection — data collection only, with no corrective maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment condition inspection. It bounds what deployed inspection robots do — sensor rounds in a fixed-layout plant — and shows they neither perform tactile/functional pre-use checks nor correct defects.

sources.title: ANYbotics Introduces End-to-End Robotic Inspection Solution
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal is a certified commercial legged robot sold for autonomous inspection rounds in energy and industrial processing plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial asset inspection; establishes the state of the art for autonomous inspection robots (fixed-route sensing in structured plants), which does not extend to pre-use inspection and repair of a mobile machine.

sources.system: Aurora Driver / Kodiak Driver autonomous trucks
sources.title: ‘A totally different world’: Autonomous trucks prepare to go driverless in Texas — Trucking Dive
sources.claim: Even at highly automated driverless-truck terminals, the pre-use safety inspection of the vehicle is still performed by human certified inspectors each day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-use safety inspection of heavy vehicles. It shows that in a capital-rich, structured facility the physical pre-use inspection remains a human job, with no robotic system substituting.

tasks.label: Control hydraulic tractors equipped with tree clamps and booms to lift, swing, and bunch sheared trees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Drive-to-tree or tracked feller-buncher in a southern pine plantation clearcut on flat to rolling ground: shear stems, accumulate 3-6 trees in the clamp arms, swing the boom and lay ordered bunches along the skid trail for the grapple skidder, working amid stumps, slash, dust and other machines.

Thinning or partial cut (row/selective thinning in plantation or shelterwood): maneuver between residual stems, shear selected trees, lift and swing them clear without barking or knocking down leave trees, and bunch them in the trail or corridor.

Natural mixed hardwood or mixed-conifer stand: large, heavy, crooked stems of highly variable size and lean, brush and vines, uneven ground; single-stem or small accumulations lifted, swung and placed in bunches oriented for the skidder.

Steep-slope or wet/rough terrain harvesting (Appalachia, Pacific Northwest, Rockies), often with a leveling or tethered/winch-assisted machine: shear, lift, swing and bunch stems on side slopes, rocky ground or soft soil, managing machine stability and slash mats.

Right-of-way, land-clearing, fuels-reduction or storm salvage work near roads, utility corridors or structures: shear small to medium trees and brushy stems, swing and pile them for chipping or loading, with traffic, power lines, fencing and public access nearby.

sources.system: ANDRITZ log yard crane with Metris ANDI Autonomous Crane AI
sources.title: Log yard cranes — ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ's Metris ANDI crane AI allows fully autonomous operation of log yard cranes with loose wood, using laser scanners and cameras to locate and size the wood the grapple picks, swings and piles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grapple handling of loose tree-length wood — the crane grabs unfixtured logs in random orientations, lifts, swings and stacks them into piles, the same lift/swing/bunch cycle with comparable objects (heavy stems) and comparable placement precision required of a feller-buncher operator building bunches.

sources.system: ANDRITZ autonomous logyard cranes (2 x 25 t, 540 m runway) at Metsä Fibre Kemi
sources.title: Metsä Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill in Finland successfully lifts up the world's first autonomous logyard cranes supplied by ANDRITZ
sources.claim: Two fully autonomous ANDRITZ log yard cranes were installed at Metsä Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill to handle about 7.6 million m3 of wood per year from trucks and trains, plus storage and mill feeding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grapple unloading and stacking of tree-length wood at production throughput; the perception-plus-grapple cycle (pick loose stems, swing, place in an ordered pile) is the mechanical equivalent of bunching sheared trees, with the same object class and placement tolerance.

sources.system: Kemi bioproduct mill autonomous woodyard cranes
sources.title: The first year of the Kemi bioproduct mill — Metsä Fibre
sources.claim: After a year of operation, the Kemi mill's electric woodyard cranes are reported to unload wood from trains and ... using AI and machine vision, i.e. the autonomous log handling is running in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: same as above — routine autonomous grapple lifting, swinging and piling of loose stems in a working wood yard confirms the capability is operational, not merely a product claim.

sources.system: Autonomous log-loading knuckleboom crane (McGill/Université Laval/FPInnovations testbed)
sources.developer: Ayoub, Fernando, Larrivée-Hardy, Lemieux, Giguère, Sharf (McGill University et al.)
sources.title: Log Loading Automation for Timber-Harvesting Industry (IEEE ICRA 2024)
sources.claim: A commercial log loader retrofitted for autonomy completed full autonomous loading cycles outdoors — perceiving logs, planning multi-log grasps, and picking and placing all logs within reach onto a trailer — with an 87% overall success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grapple lift/swing/place of tree-length logs with a full-size hydraulic forestry crane, the same manipulation as bunching, showing the boom-and-clamp cycle can be automated on real forestry machinery in a controlled outdoor yard.

sources.system: Automated log grasping with stereo-camera boom-tip control on a full-scale forwarder
sources.title: Real-time target point identification and automated log grasping by a forwarder, using a single stereo camera (Silva Fennica)
sources.claim: Skogforsk tested automated log grasping on a full-scale forwarder using a single stereo camera for detection and boom-tip control, finding precise, repeatable grasps in full-scale real-time operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grapple targeting and closing on tree-length stems with a forestry boom — the same perception-to-grasp step used when a buncher clamps and lifts sheared trees, but demonstrated only as a research trial.

sources.developer: La Hera et al., SLU / Umeå University (Sweden)
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.claim: A research forwarder platform picked up logs from the ground ... drove through forest terrain without human intervention, described as the first experimental unmanned forestry machine; other authors characterise it as autonomous forwarding in a simplified ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crane log handling in forest terrain; cited to show the state of in-forest autonomy is an experimental prototype in a simplified setting, well short of production felling/bunching rates and reliability.

sources.system: Kodama Autopilot teleoperation and shared-autonomy kits for skidders
sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Kodama Systems uses robotics to prevent wildfires — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kodama Systems' commercialized forestry automation is a teleoperation/shared-autonomy retrofit: remote human operators run skidders and other machines from off-site, with autonomy limited to repeating mapped skid-trail travel.
sources.transferJustification: Same work setting (in-woods heavy forestry machines handling bunched trees); cited as negative evidence that the grapple/boom work in real logging operations is done by remote human operators, not autonomously.

tasks.label: Grade logs according to characteristics such as knot size and straightness, and according to established industry or company standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cut-to-length harvester/processor operator at the stump: while the head delimbs and feeds a stem, the operator judges knot size, sweep, rot and butt defect, selects the product/grade (sawlog, veneer, pulp) via hotkeys or accepts the on-board bucking optimizer's suggestion, and bucks the stem accordingly; muddy, sloped, variable stand conditions, all weather.

Knuckleboom loader operator at a roadside forest landing: rolls and turns each stem/log with the grapple to see all faces, grades it against mill specs (knots, sweep/straightness, diameter, scale defect), and places it in the correct grade/species/length deck before loading trucks by sort. Includes picking veneer/grade hardwood logs out of a mixed deck.

Delimber-slasher or pull-through delimber operator merchandising whole tree-length stems at the landing into products by grade and length, deciding cut points to keep the best grade section clear of knots and crook, and dropping each piece into the right product pile.

Operator/crew member scaling and grading logs on a deck or truckload with a scale stick and tape at the landing: measuring diameter and length, deducting for defect, assigning a grade under an established rule (Scribner/Doyle, mill or agency grade rules), and marking grade/paint or recording it on a tally sheet for the load.

Operator working in a mill log yard, concentration yard or sort yard: unloading trucks with a stacker/loader, grading each log or bundle against the yard's grade rules, building segregated grade decks, and feeding the merchandiser/sorting line infeed.

sources.title: Microtec To Supply Log Scanner To J.D. Irving's N.B. Mill - Wood Business
sources.claim: MiCROTEC's CT Log computed tomography ..., sold and installed in production sawmills (e.g. J.D. Irving's St. Leonard, NB veneer mill), scans logs conveyed through it and grades and sorts them by internal quality (knots, defects) in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is mill-side log grading: same objects (whole logs), same grading criteria the ONET task names (knot size and straightness/sweep plus internal defect), and the same accepted output (a grade assignment that drives which sort the log goes to). It differs only in that the log is conveyed to the scanner rather than assessed where it lies.

sources.system: MiCROTEC CT Log (hardwood installations, incl. Cascade Hardwoods)
sources.title: MiCROTEC - CT Log for hardwood
sources.claim: CT Log units are installed and running in North American hardwood mills (e.g. Cascade Hardwoods, Chehalis WA), grading hardwood logs from internal scans and removing reliance on individual sawyers' subjective judgement.
sources.transferJustification: Hardwood grade/veneer selection is the hardest version of the logger's grading judgment; this shows machine grading of hardwood logs to a value/grade standard is in commercial production, not just research.

sources.system: MiCROTEC Logeye 302 at Koskisen Järvelä sawmill
sources.title: MiCROTEC - Logeye: Efficient log sorting at Koskisen
sources.claim: MiCROTEC Logeye multi-sensor (laser 3D, colour camera, X-ray) scanners are installed on sawmill log sorting lines, where logs are conveyed past the scanner and graded for measurement, curvature/taper and internal quality before sorting.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (assigning a quality grade to round logs and routing them to the matching sort), performed on a conveyorized line instead of a landing deck.

sources.system: MPM Engineering stem merchandizing / bucking optimizer
sources.title: Tech Update: Recovery Optimization Tech - Forestnet
sources.claim: Mill stem-merchandising and bucking optimizers using 3D scan data automatically detect the external shape defects loggers grade on — sweep, crook, taper, flare, catface — and grade logs for highest value, controlling where each piece is cut and sorted.
sources.transferJustification: This is the merchandising/grading decision a delimber-slasher or processor operator makes on a tree-length stem (where to cut and what grade each piece is), executed by machine on a conveyorized merchandiser line.

sources.system: Pinnacle E-Tallyman scanner and log sorter
sources.title: Logyard scanning and sorting systems optimise wetmill ops • WoodBiz Africa / SA Forestry
sources.claim: Automated log sorters singulate bundled logs, feed them through a scanner and mechanically sort them into grade/size bins; 15 E-Tallyman scanner-sorter systems are installed at named sawmills.
sources.transferJustification: Supplies the physical half of the task: the graded log is actually handled and placed into the correct sort bin under machine control, which is the accepted output of a logger's grading decision (log in the right deck).

sources.title: Tech Update: Scanners And Optimizers - Wood Business
sources.claim: Woodtech's Logmeter is a fixed scanning portal at a mill entrance that automatically measures and quality-checks every truckload of logs (lengths, top/butt diameters, excessive sweep and crook, defective log counts) as the truck drives through.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to load-level scaling/grade checking at a yard, but it works only where the load is driven through a purpose-built portal — it does not grade logs lying in decks as found, so it supports E1 and not E2.

sources.developer: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (La Hera et al.)
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine - Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: The first experimental unmanned forestry machine demonstrated autonomous navigation and log grasping in forest terrain; in-woods autonomy is at research-demonstration level and does not include grading logs to industry standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous log handling in the woods; cited only to characterise the state of in-forest autonomy (grasping and hauling, no quality grading), supporting negative E3/E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Drive straight or articulated tractors equipped with accessories such as bulldozer blades, grapples, logging arches, cable winches, and crane booms to skid, load, unload, or stack logs, pull stumps, or clear brush.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grapple or cable skidder work on a clearcut/thinning site: operator drives the articulated skidder over stumps, slash, mud and slopes to bunches of felled trees, grapples or chokers them, drags the turn several hundred yards along skid trails to the landing, drops and re-decks the bunch, then returns — dozens of cycles per shift in dust, rain or snow, coordinating by radio with the feller-buncher and loader.

Knuckleboom/heel-boom loader at a woods landing: unloading the skidder's turns, feeding a delimber/processor, sorting stems into sawlog, pulp and chip decks, stacking the decks, and loading log trucks that back onto an unimproved landing — chaining/binding checks, uneven ground, crew members and truck drivers moving nearby.

Cut-to-length forwarder work: crane-loading short logs from scattered piles along the strip road inside standing timber, hauling the loaded bunk over soft ground and brush mats to roadside, then unloading and sorting into assortment decks at the roadside landing.

Crawler tractor / dozer work on the harvest unit: pushing and piling slash and brush, pulling or shearing stumps, cutting and back-blading skid trails and building/cleaning the landing, installing water bars and doing road maintenance on the tract.

Log handling at a mill log yard, concentration yard or biomass yard: wheel loader or log stacker unloads trucks, builds and maintains sorted log decks on the paved/gravel yard, and feeds the debarker/chipper infeed deck, working around scale traffic, truck drivers and yard staff.

Small-scale/steep-ground extraction with a farm or forestry tractor fitted with a winch and logging arch: hooking chokers by hand, winching stems out of a hollow or off a steep pitch, arching the front ends up and pulling them to a small woodlot landing where they are decked with a loader or tractor forks.

sources.system: ANDRITZ LogPorter log yard crane with Metris ANDI autonomous crane AI
sources.title: Log yard cranes — ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ's log yard gantry crane with the Metris ANDI crane AI is marketed as commercially available and capable of fully autonomous handling of loose wood (logs) using laser scanners and cameras to locate and size the wood.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: grappling, moving, decking and unloading roundwood. The crane picks loose logs from truck bunks and piles and stacks them, the manipulation a loader/knuckleboom operator performs, but with the wood brought to a fixed machine.

sources.title: Log yard cranes — ANDRITZ
sources.claim: The same crane performs the whole log-yard duty cycle — unloading trucks, storing (stacking) logs and feeding the mill — and is sold as a replacement for multiple mobile log loaders.
sources.transferJustification: Substitutes directly for the loader-operator work in this task (unload, stack, deck logs) at production rates, which speaks to worker-quality throughput and reliability.

sources.system: ANDRITZ autonomous logyard cranes at Metsä Fibre Kemi bioproduct mill
sources.title: Metsä Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill in Finland successfully lifts up the world's first autonomous logyard cranes supplied by ANDRITZ
sources.claim: Two fully autonomous ANDRITZ logyard cranes were installed at Metsä Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill (540 m runway, 120,000 m3 storage) to unload wood arriving by truck and rail, stack it in storage and feed the pulping process.
sources.transferJustification: Real deployment of autonomous log unloading/stacking at industrial volume; the manipulated objects (full-length/pulpwood roundwood in loose bundles) and the actions (unload, deck, restack) are those of this task.

sources.system: Kodama Autopilot teleoperation/shared-autonomy kit on a grapple skidder
sources.title: Weyerhaeuser Trains AI to Map Every Tree in its 10M-Acre Estate — Wood Central
sources.claim: The most advanced in-woods log extraction system in commercial forestry practice is Kodama Systems' retrofit on skidders, used by Weyerhaeuser in a pilot where a driverless skidder dragged felled trees at a southern logging site while a human operator controlled it remotely from 400 miles away.

sources.system: Kodama Systems teleoperation/autonomy kit on a skidder
sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to prevent wildfires — The Robot Report
sources.claim: In a 2023 forest-thinning project in the Stanislaus ..., Kodama's teleoperation platform on a skidder autonomously drove bundles of trees along skid ... landing, but the platform is a teleoperation system with autonomy only for selected sub-steps.

sources.system: Teleo Supervised Autonomy on a Volvo L350F wheel loader
sources.title: Teleo secures orders for 34 autonomous vehicles for heavy industry and plans to expand beyond construction — Robotics & Automation News
sources.claim: In the first commercial 'autonomous' logging yard (Fin-Terpuu Oy, Finland) a Teleo-equipped Volvo L350F wheel loader autonomously trams logs between the arrival point and the processing yard, but the log pick-up and drop-off — the grapple work — are performed by a remote human operator.

sources.system: Forwarder crane with stereo-camera perception and boom-tip control (Semberg et al.)
sources.title: Real-time target point identification and automated log grasping by a forwarder, using a single stereo camera for both object detection and boom-tip control
sources.claim: Full-scale research on autonomous log grasping with a forwarder crane outdoors achieved an 87% success rate per loading operation, i.e. autonomous roundwood manipulation on unprepared ground remains at experimental reliability.

tasks.label: Drive crawler or wheeled tractors to drag or transport logs from felling sites to log landing areas for processing and loading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grapple skidder on a Southern pine clearcut: driving a rubber-tired grapple skidder over stumps, slash and rutted mud to bunches laid down by a feller-buncher, clamping a bunch of tree-length stems, dragging 300–1,500 ft along skid trails to the landing, dropping the drag for the delimber/loader, and repeating dozens of turns per day at production rates.

Cable/grapple skidder in a selective hardwood harvest in the Northeast or Appalachians: steep, rocky, wet ground with residual standing timber; operator backs into the felling site, dismounts to set chokers or wraps a winch line on scattered stems, winches them in, then threads a drag downhill/uphill through the residual stand to the landing.

Cut-to-length forwarder or clambunk skidder in Lake States/Northeast/PNW: crane-loading short logs off the strip road into the bunk (or clambunk), driving loaded over brush mats and soft ground several hundred metres to the roadside landing, and unloading into product-sorted decks.

Crawler tractor/dozer skidding on steep, soft or snow-covered ground (PNW/Inland West thinning, winter operations): blading and maintaining skid trails, winching or pushing turns of logs to the landing, sometimes tethered on slopes above 40%.

Small-scale woodlot or land-clearing job: farm tractor with a logging winch, small skidder or compact tractor pulling a handful of stems out of a private woodlot or storm-damaged stand to a roadside landing, with variable, unmapped access and mixed debris.

sources.title: Kodama Systems Shows Off "Roboskidder"
sources.claim: Kodama Systems' commercially offered skidding service on a Weiler S340 wheel skidder at a Louisiana harvest site is run by a human operator remotely; no autonomous skidding cycle is claimed.

sources.title: WSJ: America's Largest Landowner Is Using AI to Digitize the Forest (reposted by Kodama)
sources.claim: Weyerhaeuser's 'driverless' skidder pilot at a Southern logging site was maneuvered by a remote human operator 400 miles away with AI-assisted navigation; the company describes it as a path toward, not achievement of, autonomy.

sources.title: Putting Forestry Equipment on Autopilot – Forestnet
sources.claim: As of early 2025 the autonomous point-to-point driving functions of the leading forestry teleoperation product were still in development, i.e. skidders in the woods are remote-piloted rather than autonomous.

sources.system: Teleo Supervised Autonomy on Volvo L350F
sources.title: Teleo secures orders for 34 autonomous vehicles for heavy industry and plans to expand beyond construction
sources.claim: In a Finnish logging yard a Teleo-equipped Volvo L350F wheel loader hauls logs autonomously between fixed points, but the grapple pick-up and drop-off are still performed by a remote human operator, so no full log-moving cycle is autonomous in that facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving logs across a work yard. It shows autonomous travel with loads but explicitly leaves grapple pick-up and deposit to a remote operator, so it cannot substantiate whole-cycle log moving in a structured facility.

sources.system: ANDRITZ log yard crane with Metris ANDI crane AI
sources.title: Log yard cranes – ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ log yard cranes with Metris ANDI operate fully autonomously on loose (unsorted) logs, perceiving log location and dimensions with laser scanners and cameras, and handle unloading, transporting to storage and feeding the mill at up to 40 picks per hour in all weather.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grappling bunches of felled logs from a presented position and moving them to a deposit point. Same objects (multi-tonne tree-length/pulp logs), same grapple precision, and this is exactly the E1 form of skidding, where logs arrive fixtured at a defined pick point and must be carried to a landing/deck.

sources.system: Autonomous logyard cranes, Metsä Fibre Kemi bioproduct mill
sources.title: Metsä Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill in Finland successfully lifts up the world's first autonomous logyard cranes supplied by ANDRITZ
sources.claim: Two fully autonomous ANDRITZ logyard cranes were installed on a 540 m runway at Metsä Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill to handle about 7.6 million m3 of wood per year arriving by truck and train, including log storage and feeding wood to the process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume mechanised movement of logs from a presented pick point to a deposit pile. Demonstrates the E1 version of log transport at industrial throughput in a purpose-built crane installation.

sources.system: Automated log grasping system on a full-scale forwarder
sources.title: Real-time target point identification and automated log grasping by a forwarder, using a single stereo camera for both object detection and boom-tip control
sources.claim: Skogforsk demonstrated automated log grasping on a full-scale forwarder crane using a single stereo camera for detection and boom-tip control, achieving precise, highly repeatable grasps in real-time full-scale tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-vision grapple loading of logs. Shows that when a log's position is presented within reach, a full-size forestry crane can grasp it autonomously — the manipulation element of skidding under an E1 presentation.

sources.developer: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences / Luleå University of Technology
sources.title: Researchers develop and test the first unmanned forestry machine
sources.claim: A one-off experimental unmanned forwarder (AORO) in Sweden autonomously navigated forest terrain and picked logs off the ground without human intervention — the closest demonstration to autonomous forwarding in the woods, but a research prototype rather than a production machine.

tasks.label: Fill out required job or shift report forms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Drive tractors for building or repairing logging and skid roads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pushing/cutting new skid trails (skid roads) through an active harvest unit with a crawler tractor or dozer-blade machine: blading a travel way over stumps, slash and roots, side-hilling on grades, alignment chosen on the fly by the operator around leave-trees, wet spots and rock, no survey stakes or design model, under canopy.

Constructing a new spur/haul road prism in the woods: cut-and-fill on a side slope, pioneering the grade with a dozer after right-of-way trees are felled, shaping the running surface and inside ditch, stumps and rootwads pushed out, mud and steep pitches.

Building or enlarging a log landing, deck area or turnaround: clearing stumps and slash, cutting and filling to make a level pad big enough for loaders and trucks, on ground taken as found at the edge of the harvest unit.

Repairing/maintaining existing gravel or dirt logging roads and skid roads: blading out ruts and washboard, re-crowning or outsloping, pulling ditches, spreading spot rock, pushing off slide material and downed limbs after storms, often in mud or after rain.

Drainage and close-out work with the tractor blade: installing waterbars/cross-drains and dips, outsloping and seeding-prep of skid roads, blocking and rehabilitating temporary trails and crossings at job completion to meet forest-practice BMPs, with placement judged on the spot from where water will run.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL automated construction system has been used to run automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers and dump trucks in production at dam construction sites, with more than ten automated machines working around the clock placing embankment material at Naruse Dam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bulldozer leveling/spreading of fill to a design surface. Building a road prism or landing with a tractor is the same blade earthmoving to grade with comparable machines and tolerances; it substantiates the earthmoving element of the task in a controlled facility.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for Earthworks | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima extended the same automated bulldozer leveling, roller compaction, backhoe loading and articulated dump hauling to land-development earthwork, automating the whole embankment work sequence including machines running on temporary haul roads, and applied it at land-development construction sites in fiscal 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated embankment/earthwork construction (cut, haul, level, compact) at a controlled worksite; this is the same machine class and same grading-to-model output as building or repairing a road grade, so it transfers to road-prism and pad construction where the site is kept to a working standard.

sources.developer: Shantui (with Huazhong University of Science and Technology)
sources.title: World's First AI-Powered Electric Unmanned Bulldozer Commences Operations
sources.claim: Shantui's DE26-X3 unmanned electric bulldozer entered routine operation at a large open-pit mine, autonomously performing slope construction, retaining-wall building and spoil disposal within designated work zones.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned dozer pushing and shaping earth on a mine spoil dump. Blading material to a planned slope/grade is the core action of building or repairing a haul or skid road, with comparable machine size and precision, in an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit lets excavators, dozers and compact track loaders perform earthmoving tasks fully autonomously on construction sites, including trenching, foundation excavation and grading building pads, monitored remotely.

sources.system: Kodama Autopilot on Weiler S340 skidder

tasks.label: Drive and maneuver tractors and tree harvesters to shear the tops off of trees, cut and limb the trees, and cut the logs into desired lengths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final harvest (clearcut) of a conifer plantation on flat-to-rolling ground: operator drives a cut-to-length wheeled harvester over stumps, slash and soft ground, boom-reaches each standing tree, fells it, feeds it through the head to delimb and top it, and crosscuts it into sawlog/pulpwood lengths per the mill's order, piling assortments beside the strip road at ~20-40 stems per hour.

Commercial thinning along strip roads in a managed pine or spruce stand: operator maneuvers the harvester between residual crop trees in confined spacing, selects which stems to remove, fells them without damaging leave trees, delimbs, tops and bucks them to assortment lengths, and places brush on the trail.

Roadside/landing processing in a whole-tree or tree-length system: operator runs a dangle-head processor or stroke delimber at a rough landing deck, picking tree-length stems from a bunch, delimbing, shearing off the top, and bucking each stem into merchantable log lengths, sorting logs into decks for the loader.

Selective harvest in a mixed natural hardwood stand: crooked, forked, heavily limbed stems of varying species and diameter, dense understory and uneven ground; operator judges stem quality on the fly, fells, limbs, tops and bucks to grade-driven lengths.

Steep or rough terrain and large timber (Pacific Northwest / Appalachian): winch-assisted or tracked harvester/processor on slopes, mud, rock and stump-strewn ground, handling large-diameter stems with heavy limbs, working near a yarder corridor or road with weather and visibility variation.

sources.system: USNR LogPro merchandiser (scanning + bucking optimization line)
sources.title: TECH UPDATE: Log Bucking and Merchandising - Forestnet
sources.claim: Commercially installed log merchandising lines (e.g., USNR LogPro) take tree-length stems on infeed conveyors, scan them, compute an optimized bucking pattern, and cut them into logs of desired lengths with traveling saw carriages under PLC/optimizer control in a purpose-built mill line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mill-yard stem merchandising. The physical act is identical to the bucking element of this task - cross-cutting whole tree-length stems into ordered log lengths at optimized cut positions - on the same objects (stems up to 80 ft), with the work brought to a fixed, purpose-built machine line rather than the machine driven to the tree.

sources.title: TECH UPDATE: Log Bucking and Merchandising - Forestnet
sources.claim: Inotech Canada's Intellibuck stem merchandiser generates bucking patterns from true-shape scanning of entire stems and executes the cuts with electrically positioned saw modules, handling stems up to 80 ft long and 24 in diameter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stem bucking in a mill. Same objects (full-length tree stems) and same required precision (cut placement to the centimetre for assortment lengths) as the 'cut the logs into desired lengths' element of this task, performed by machine decision and machine execution.

sources.title: Peterson 5000H Whole Tree Chipper - ASTEC
sources.claim: Chain-flail delimber-debarkers process whole trees fed continuously through the machine, with rotating flail drums stripping all limbs and bark from the stems; the technology is mature and widely used at landings and chip mills at 40+ tonnes per productive machine hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stationary whole-tree delimbing/debarking. It covers the 'limb the trees / shear the tops' element on the same objects (whole trees with full crowns); the delimbing is executed by the machine continuously once stems are on the infeed, i.e. with the work presented to the machine as a purpose-built line would present it.

sources.system: PONSSE cut-to-length harvester with automated bucking (Opti control system)
sources.title: The cut-to-length method - Ponsse
sources.claim: In cut-to-length harvesting the harvester head itself performs the delimbing, measuring and cross-cutting of a grasped stem, and the machine's control system automatically chooses the cut lengths (automated bucking); the operator still drives the machine and selects and fells each tree.
sources.transferJustification: Same task. Shows that limbing, measuring and length cutting of a presented stem are already machine-executed functions of production harvester heads, while tree selection, driving and boom work remain human; it is therefore supporting context, not a basis for a positive autonomous judgment.

sources.system: Tigercat 570 harvesting head with D7 Control System
sources.title: 570 Harvesting Head | Cut to Length | Forestry Attachments | Tigercat
sources.claim: Production harvesting heads sold today combine hardware with bucking control systems that deliver feeding, delimbing, measuring and debarking of stems, including in roadside processing applications, under operator control from the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (roadside processing and CTL harvesting). Documents that the limbing/measuring/bucking motions are machine functions of the head, but that the machine as a whole is operated by a human in the cab, so it cannot support an autonomous judgment in the forest.

Bonn/Prefor within the EU DigiForest project, autonomously navigates real forests and reaches target trees for selective thinning over kilometre-long missions, but the cut is authorized by a human operator and the machine does not perform full delimbing and cut-to-length bucking at production rates.

sources.title: Swedish startup achieves first fully autonomous tree harvest by drone - Dronewatch Europe

roles.title: Log Graders and Scalers
roles.description: Grade logs or estimate the marketable content or value of logs or pulpwood in sorting yards, millpond, log deck, or similar locations. Inspect logs for defects or measure logs to determine volume.

tasks.label: Evaluate log characteristics and determine grades, using established criteria.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill or reload-yard scaling station: a certified scaler (often a third-party bureau scaler) works a loaded log truck or logs decked beside the scaling ramp, judging each softwood sawlog for defects (rot, catface, sweep, crook, checks), assigning a grade per Northwest/Scribner-type rules and recording it for payment; outdoors, in rain, mud, dust and truck traffic.

Sawmill merchandising deck / saw infeed: logs move singly on a chain conveyor past a grading station or booth; the grader assesses each log's diameter, sweep, knots and visible defect and assigns the sort/grade that routes it to a bin or bucking solution, at line speed.

Log sort yard or concentration yard: logs are unloaded and presented by a knuckleboom loader or lie in decks; the grader inspects each stem for species, defect and grade, paint-marks or hammer-brands the grade and calls the sort, working on foot on uneven ground amid moving equipment.

Woods landing or roadside deck: grading logs where they are bucked and decked in the forest, on uneven muddy ground in variable light and weather, with logs stacked so only parts of each face are visible; grades drive bucking and sort decisions for hauling.

High-value hardwood grade/veneer or export logs: the grader/buyer evaluates individual logs (oak, walnut, maple, or export softwood) for clear-face cuttings, surface and end defect, sometimes end-trimming to see the face, and assigns a grade that sets a substantial per-log price, at a hardwood mill yard or concentration yard.

sources.system: MiCROTEC CT Log and Logeye species recognition

sources.title: Tech Update - Log Scanners and Optimizers - Forestnet
sources.claim: The CT Log computed-tomography scanner, installed on sawmill log lines, reconstructs each log's internal features in real time so logs are graded and sorted by quality automatically at line speed.

sources.title: MiCROTEC - CT Log for hardwood

It establishes that the purpose-built line physically acts on the logs (singulating, conveying, sorting to grade bins) under machine control, so the grading decision is executed on the wood rather than merely reported.

tasks.label: Record data about individual trees or load volumes into tally books or hand-held collection terminals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Measure felled logs or loads of pulpwood to calculate volume, weight, dimensions, and marketable value, using measuring devices and conversion tables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill-gate / scaling-station truck load scaling of sawlogs: scaler meets each incoming log truck at the mill or concentration yard, measures length and small-end diameter of the logs on the load, deducts for visible defect, and computes net board-foot volume by species/grade and load value for the settlement ticket. Outdoors, all weather, trucks arriving on the yard road.

Pulpwood / small-roundwood loads at a mill wood yard: load is weighed in and out on the truck scale (or measured as a stacked load), species and product checked, and conversion tables applied to convert tons to cords/cubic volume and value. Scale-house / weigh lane in a controlled mill yard.

Log deck or merchandiser scaling at the mill: scaler works the log deck / sort yard, measuring individual logs (diameter, length, taper), assigning grade and defect deduction, and computing volume and value per log for sorting, inventory and mill payment. Logs lie in decks and are moved by loaders.

Log-yard inventory scaling: periodic determination of the volume held in decked piles of logs (and residual piles) across a sorting yard or mill yard, using stack dimensions and conversion factors, to reconcile inventory and reported receipts.

In-woods scaling at a logging landing or roadside deck: scaler measures felled logs or a loaded truck on rough, muddy, sloping ground at an active harvest site, in variable weather, to produce the load's volume, dimensions and value before the wood leaves the tract.

sources.developer: Woodtech Measurement Solutions (Woodtech SA); distributed in North America by Carbotech/Autolog

sources.title: Log Scanners - MiCROTEC

tasks.label: Paint identification marks of specified colors on logs to identify grades or species, using spray cans, or call out grades to log markers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill/sort-yard scaler walks along decked logs or a loaded log truck outdoors in the mill yard, spraying a colored mark (dot, stripe, or letter) on the end or side of each log to show grade/species sort; logs lie stacked at random orientations, ends muddy or snow-covered, loaders and trucks moving nearby.

Grading/scaling station on the mill's log infeed or merchandiser line: logs travel singly on a chain conveyor past the grader, who determines or receives the grade and sprays the specified color on the log at line pace (roughly one log every few seconds).

In-woods landing or roadside deck: a bucker/grader or company scaler marks bucked logs with spray paint by grade, species, or destination sort before loading; uneven ground, slash and brush, rain/cold, layout different at every landing.

Hardwood grade/veneer log yard or concentration yard: high-value logs decked on the ground are inspected for species, defect and grade, and marked on the end with paint (grade code, customer, or sort color); careful, log-by-log work with high value at stake.
Grader/scaler at a mill deck or sort yard calls out grades and species aloud to a log marker or tally person who applies the paint or records the grade, rather than painting the logs personally.

sources.title: ABB's PixelPaint enables precision paint jobs at Mercedes-Benz Sindelfingen plant
sources.claim: ABB's PixelPaint robotic painting system is deployed in a Mercedes-Benz paint shop, applying precise paint patterns of specified colors to car bodies presented in the booth under machine control, without a human guiding the gun.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of paint of a specified color in a specified pattern to a workpiece presented in a fixtured, purpose-built cell. Spraying an identification mark on a presented log demands far less precision and finish quality than automotive paint, so performance carries over at E1.

sources.system: Claussen All-Mark Automated Lumber Mill Face Grade Printer
sources.title: Lumber Grade Printers | Claussen Conversion Systems
sources.claim: Claussen All-Mark builds automated grade printers/markers that are installed on the lug tables of North American lumber and panel mills and stamp grade marks on each piece as it passes, without an operator applying the mark.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically applying a grade identification mark to rough wood pieces moving on a mill line. Same act, same material and marking tolerance as painting a grade mark on a log; the log version differs only in the size of the workpiece.

sources.title: Blanca Forestry Products installs Lucidyne GradeScans at its Colorado mill
sources.claim: Lucidyne GradeScan machine-vision graders with deep-learning defect detection are installed and running in US planer mills, grading each wood piece at line speed and passing the grade decision to downstream marking and sorting equipment.

sources.title: Logeye 300 - MiCROTEC
sources.claim: Microtec's Logeye 300 is a commercial multi-sensor log scanner used for log sorting and grading in the merchandising yard or at the saw infeed, i.e. machine grading of individual logs moving on a line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: determining the grade/quality class of each log automatically, which supplies the 'specified color' decision that the marking step executes.

tasks.label: Jab logs with metal ends of scale sticks, and inspect logs to ascertain characteristics or defects such as water damage, splits, knots, broken ends, rotten areas, twists, and curves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill log yard / sorting yard: scaler walks the log decks and ground-stored logs, jabs log ends and suspect areas with the metal point of the scale stick to test for soft rot or water damage, and eyeballs each log for splits, broken ends, knots, twist and sweep before it is scaled and sorted.

Loaded-truck inspection at the mill gate / scaling station: scaler inspects the load as delivered (from the ground or a platform), probing visible log ends for rot and checking for breakage, splits, excessive crook and foreign material, on a sample or whole-load basis for payment and supplier feedback.

Woods landing / roadside scaling by a company or third-party scaling bureau: scaler works on uneven ground beside decked logs in the forest, in mud, rain, cold or heat, jabbing ends for rot and assessing defects log by log before trucking.

Concentration yard, export dock or veneer-log buying yard: high-value hardwood/veneer/export logs are inspected individually and closely for surface and end defects (knots, splits, ring shake, rot pockets, sweep) with probing of suspect ends; grade drives large price differences.

Mill log deck / infeed: grader stationed at the log deck or infeed conveyor as logs are singulated and moved past, jabbing ends and inspecting each log for rot, splits and knots to assign grade or a bucking decision before breakdown.

tasks.label: Identify logs of substandard or special grade so that they can be returned to shippers, regraded, recut, or transferred for other processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill receiving / scale ramp: scaler works a truck or trailer load of softwood logs at the mill gate or scale deck, sighting each log end and side, deducting for rot, breakage and off-spec pieces, marking culls with paint/crayon and flagging whole loads (wrong species, undersize, excessive defect) to be rejected and returned to the shipper.

Sort yard / dryland sort or millpond deck: grader moves among decked logs and piles while loaders work, rolling or sighting logs, marking substandard pieces and calling sorts so the loader operator moves them to pulp, recut, or reject decks.

Mill log deck / sorting-line grading station: logs arrive singulated on a conveyor or sharp chain past a grading position; the grader picks out rotten, crooked, undersize, or oversized logs and diverts them to pulp, recut, or reject bins as the line runs.

Hardwood, veneer, pole or export 'special grade' selection at a concentration or buying yard: high-value logs inspected individually on the ground or on the truck for clear faces, sweep and end defect, marked with paint or crayon and set aside for veneer/pole buyers or for trimming and recutting.

In-woods landing or roadside deck: scaler grades and identifies cull and off-spec logs in a roadside deck under weather and uneven ground, deciding which pieces are sent to another mill, recut, or left as cull.

sources.title: MiCROTEC - CT Log

tasks.label: Measure log lengths and mark boles for bucking into logs, according to specifications.

instances.label: Roadside landing / log deck in the woods: skidded tree-length stems are decked in a jumble on mud, slash and slope; the scaler/bucker walks the deck with a tape or scale stick, judges defect and grade breaks, measures lengths plus trim allowance, and marks each cut point with lumber crayon or paint per the mill's length-and-grade specs before the bucker saws.

In the cutting unit before skidding: felled and limbed stems lying scattered on steep, brushy or snow-covered ground; the worker measures each bole and marks bucking points (often segregating a butt log to a higher grade) so the buckers can cut before yarding.

Mill or concentration log yard: tree-length stems decked in long piles or around a crane; the scaler moves among piles and loader traffic, measures stem lengths and diameters, and marks stems for bucking/trim to the mill's current order file.

Mill merchandiser / slasher infeed deck: stems are singulated onto a chain or deck and presented one at a time; the worker (in a booth or on the deck) measures length and diameter, applies the bucking specification, and sets/marks the cut points ahead of the cut-off saws.

Sort yard for export, pole, or veneer logs: already-bucked logs on the ground or on a sorting deck; the scaler measures each log, checks length/trim and end defect against export or specialty specifications, and marks re-buck or trim lines.

sources.transferJustification: Same task content: measuring stem length/shape and determining the cut points to specification; the machine executes the marked cuts directly rather than crayoning them.

tasks.label: Communicate with coworkers by signals to direct log movement.

instances.label: At a mill or concentration-yard scaling ramp, the scaler stands beside a truckload or bunk of logs and gives hand signals (or radio calls over engine noise) to a knuckleboom/front-end loader operator to set down, rotate, or reposition the load so ends are square and measurable, then signals when the load may be moved off.

On a sawmill log deck, the grader signals the deck or bucking-station operator to advance, hold, roll, or kick a log — thumb-up/hold-palm signals or a horn/light — so grading and length decisions can be applied before the log enters the mill.

In a sorting yard, the grader signals the sorter/loader operator which sort bin or bunk a graded log belongs in (pointing, arm signals, or short radio calls) as logs come off the trailer or sorting chain.
At a truck scale/unloading area, the scaler signals the truck driver to pull forward, stop, or hold while a load is weighed, tarped, or checked, and signals when it is clear to proceed.
At a millpond or water-storage boom, the scaler signals a pond operator or boom-boat operator to move, hold, or separate rafts and bundles of logs so they can be scaled or routed to the jack ladder.

tasks.label: Drive to sawmills, wharfs, or skids to inspect logs or pulpwood.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bureau or company scaler drives a pickup on public highways from the office to a member sawmill, parks at the log yard, and scales/grades logs on the cold deck and in the scaling chute (species, length, diameter, sweep, rot/defect deductions, Scribner volume), writing scale tickets; several hundred logs a shift, outdoors in any weather.

Scaler drives a circuit of two or three sites in a day — a small mill, a pulpwood/chip yard, a satellite scaling station — over 30-80 miles of highway and secondary road in rain, mud, or snow, inspecting arriving truckloads of sawlogs and pulpwood at each stop for volume, weight-ticket verification, and contaminants/defects.

Scaler drives a 4x4 pickup on gravel and rutted forest roads to an active logging landing (skid), walks the decked logs and loaded trucks on uneven ground, inspects and scales them at roadside before hauling, and confirms bucking/sort compliance with the contractor.

Scaler drives to a wharf, barge dock, or rail reload where export or transshipped logs are handled, and inspects/scales loads on trucks and in stacks against export specification (diameter, length, defects, branding) while yard machinery works around him.

Scaler assigned to one large mill or port complex drives a company truck across the yard all shift — between the scale shack, the unloading bunks, and several log decks — inspecting each arriving load and grading logs as they are unloaded or presented in the sorting chute.

tasks.label: Saw felled trees into lengths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a roadside logging landing/deck: the scaler-bucker works piled tree-length stems, marking and cutting merchantable log lengths with a chainsaw, trimming broken/ragged ends and cutting out defects. Sloped, muddy or snowy ground, stems stacked and partly under tension, equipment moving nearby.

In the woods at the stump: bucking felled trees where they lie in slash and brush, limbing as needed, judging lean, bind and tension before each cut, cutting to specified log lengths on uneven terrain with no fixed layout.

On a mill or sorting-yard log deck: chainsaw work on decked logs to cut overlength stems to order length, square up ragged ends, and cut out visible defect so the log meets specification before scaling; controlled yard, fixed layout, loaders and yard traffic.

instances.label: Daily/weekly interior walkthrough of a building under construction (commercial, institutional or multifamily) with trades actively working: superintendent walks each floor comparing installed framing, drywall, MEP rough-in and finishes against drawings and the schedule, noting deviations, missing work and rework items for the daily report and coordination meeting.

Site safety inspection walk of an active jobsite: checking for unprotected floor openings and leading edges, fall-protection use, PPE compliance, housekeeping and trip hazards, workers in machinery swing paths, excavation/ladder access, and documenting findings on a safety checklist.

Close-in verification of a specific scope before it is covered or accepted: pre-pour check of rebar size/spacing/cover, embeds and anchor-bolt layout, formwork bracing; or checking bolt torque, weld/connection condition, plumb and level with tape, level and gauges; hands-on contact measurement against the spec.

Inspection of equipment and temporary works: pre-use/periodic condition checks of heavy mobile plant (excavators, loaders, lifts, trucks) for leaks, damage, tires/undercarriage and functional safety devices, plus scaffold erection/tagging, ladders, aerial lifts and rigging/slings.

Exterior/heavy-civil site inspection: walking or driving an earthwork, roadway or utility-corridor site to verify grade, cut/fill and stockpile quantities against the design surface, check installed pipe/base course progress, and assess general site conditions and access.

Underground mine or quarry inspection: examining the working face, back and ribs, ground support installation, void/stope geometry, muck piles and ventilation/water conditions for compliance and hazards before and between shifts.

tasks.label: Locate, measure, and mark site locations or placement of structures or equipment, using measuring and marking equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior layout on a concrete slab or metal deck of a commercial building under construction: the supervisor establishes control from benchmarks, then measures and snaps/prints wall lines, door and window openings, MEP penetrations, and equipment pad outlines per coordinated drawings, using a robotic total station, tape, and chalk line/marker.

Outdoor layout on open graded ground (solar field, foundation pad, roadway, utility corridor): the supervisor locates design coordinates with a GNSS rover or total station and marks pile/footing points, curb and trench alignments with paint, flags, or hubs across large areas in heat, mud, or dust.

Staking on a congested or partially built outdoor site: setting offset and grade stakes labeled with cut/fill and station information around open excavations, existing utilities, stockpiles, traffic control, and operating equipment.

Overhead and vertical marking inside an active building: locating and marking hanger, anchor, and sleeve points on deck ceilings, elevation/control lines on walls, and equipment mounting points, working from ladders or lifts with laser and tape.

Ad-hoc spot measuring and marking during active work: pulling a tape from an existing reference to verify a dimension and marking a placement or cut line with keel, pencil, or paint on in-place walls, columns, pipe, deck, or ground amid material stacks, crews, and partially built work.

Extraction / heavy civil on rough ground: marking blast-hole collar positions of a drill pattern on a quarry or open-pit bench, or marking excavation limits and slope stakes on broken, unimproved terrain.

Oil & gas well site (extraction): the drilling supervisor/toolpusher assists the rig crew on the drill floor - making up and breaking out connections with tongs and the roughneck, handling tubulars and drill-floor tools, moving and racking pipe during tripping. Standard rig layout, controlled lease access, crew working in a red zone.

Underground mine / surface quarry (extraction): the shift supervisor helps miners with hand tools and equipment at the working face - changing drill bits and cutter picks, hanging ventilation tubing, cable and hoses, handling bolts and resin, wrench work on a stalled loader or conveyor, barring down loose rock. instances.label: Residential rooftop PV start-up at a customer's single-family home: manager verifies string polarity and open-circuit voltage with a meter at the inverter/combiner, checks grounding and torque, closes the DC disconnect and the AC breaker in the service panel, powers up the string inverter or microinverter/gateway, runs the commissioning workflow on a phone/laptop (device discovery, grid profile, CT/production meter verification, monitoring account pairing), confirms production, then walks the homeowner through operation and shutdown.

Commercial or multifamily rooftop/carport PV start-up (100 kW-2 MW): insulation-resistance (megger) and IV-curve/string tests on each combiner circuit, verification of fused combiners, closing of DC disconnects and sequential energization of AC disconnects and switchgear with the facility electrician and utility present, inverter grid-profile setup, data acquisition/SCADA point checks, and completion of the commissioning checklist for the customer and AHJ. Roof and electrical room are still an active jobsite with staged materials.

Utility-scale or large ground-mount block energization on an active construction site: coordinate lockout/tagout release, energize medium-voltage transformer and inverter skid, rack in and close breakers, bring central inverters online block by block, verify communications/tracker interlocks and performance against expected output, and record data for the owner's engineer.

Solar thermal (hot water/space heating) system start-up at a residence or small commercial building: pressure-test and flush the collector loop, fill and purge glycol with a pump cart, bleed air, set expansion tank pressure, program the differential controller and mixing valve, verify pump operation and temperature rise/stagnation protection, then instruct the owner.

Fault found during start-up and corrected before hand-off: an inverter throws a ground fault, isolation, arc-fault or reversed-string error, or the monitoring gateway will not communicate; the manager isolates the offending circuit by opening fuse holders and re-metering, traces the fault on the roof or in a combiner, repairs or re-terminates connectors, then re-energizes and re-runs the commissioning sequence and documentation.

instances.label: Final commissioning / quality check of a newly installed residential rooftop PV system on a sloped shingle roof at a private home: walk the array checking module seating, racking attachments and wire management; measure string Voc/Isc and polarity at the inverter or combiner with a meter; energize and verify inverter startup, rapid shutdown and grid connection; confirm every module/microinverter is reporting expected production in the monitoring app.

Commissioning and performance verification of a commercial rooftop or carport array on a warehouse, school or campus building (institution-controlled premises, flat membrane roof): IV-curve trace each string against expected values, run insulation resistance / continuity tests, check combiner current balance, verify inverter configuration and data acquisition, and issue the commissioning report.

Periodic performance assessment of a large fenced ground-mount or utility-scale array under O&M: scan the whole array with thermal and visible imaging to locate module hot spots, cracked cells, diode failures, string outages and combiner/inverter-level losses, quantify the power loss and produce a component-level fault report with locations.

Functional check of an installed solar thermal (hot water / glycol) system at a home or small commercial building: verify pump and differential controller operation, measure collector inlet/outlet temperature rise and flow, check loop pressure, expansion tank and glycol condition, inspect collectors and piping for leaks or air, and confirm tank temperatures meet expectations.

instances.label: Preliminary exterior feasibility/design-data assessment at a single-family home: drive to the property, capture roof planes, pitch, azimuth, usable area, obstructions and fire setbacks, run a shading analysis, and note roof covering/condition. Full residential pre-installation technical survey at an occupied home: ladder/roof measurements plus attic entry to record rafter size/spacing and sheathing, opening and photographing the main service panel and meter (busbar and main breaker rating, spare spaces, bonding), determining interconnection method and whether a panel upgrade is needed, and siting inverter/rapid shutdown/conduit runs through walls, garages or crawlspaces.

Commercial low-slope rooftop screening on a warehouse, retail box or school: confirm usable roof area, HVAC/skylight/parapet obstructions and setbacks, shading from adjacent structures, roof membrane type and age, and produce a preliminary array layout for the building owner. Rooftop/aerial data only.

Full commercial/industrial site audit: rooftop assessment plus electrical room walk (switchgear/MSB rating, available breaker space, metering, interconnection point), structural drawing review with a walk of the interior, conduit and cable-tray routing through the building, roof access, crane and staging areas, and permitting constraints.

Ground-mount siting assessment on an open land parcel (rural residential, farm, or small commercial): walk/fly the parcel to establish topography and slope, usable area and boundaries/setbacks, tree-line shading, drainage and vegetation, and vehicle access for equipment; output is a feasible array footprint and layout constraints.

Assessment of a home or small building under construction: walk an active jobsite with the builder, verify roof framing and orientation against plans, confirm penetration and mounting locations before roofing/drywall, plan conduit chases and equipment locations, and coordinate with other trades amid changing site conditions.

roles.title: Boilermakers
aliases: Industrial Boiler Service Technician (Industrial Boiler Service Tech)
roles.description: Construct, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliaries. Align structures or plate sections to assemble boiler frame tanks or vats, following blueprints. Work involves use of hand and power tools, plumb bobs, levels, wedges, dogs, or turnbuckles. Assist in testing assembled vessels. Direct cleaning of boilers and boiler furnaces. Inspect and repair boiler fittings, such as safety valves, regulators, automatic-control mechanisms, water columns, and auxiliary machines.

tasks.label: Examine boilers, pressure vessels, tanks, or vats to locate defects, such as leaks, weak spots, or defective sections, so that they can be repaired.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Planned outage at a utility or large industrial boiler: worker enters the furnace on staging/scaffold, visually examines waterwall, combustor and generating-bank tubes for erosion, bulges, pitting and cracking, takes ultrasonic thickness readings, and marks thin/defective tube sections for pad weld or replacement. Sooty, confined, plant-controlled, on a tight outage clock.

Aboveground storage tank, process vessel or large vat at a refinery, terminal, chemical plant or power station: examine floor, shell courses and seams for corrosion, pitting, weld defects and leaks (API 653-type condition assessment), reporting locations needing patching or plate replacement.

Walkdown of an operating or just-shut unit to hunt leaks: locate steam/water weeps at seams, tubes, casing penetrations, handhole gaskets and fittings, plus hot spots on casing/insulation, using sight, sound, thermal imaging and soap tests, so the leak source can be scheduled for repair.

Small firetube/package or heating boiler in a building or small plant boiler room: pull handhole and manhole plates and fire doors, crawl or reach into the cramped fireside and waterside, examine tube sheets, tube ends, staybolts, ligaments and refractory for scale, cracks, wastage and leaks, with mirror, light, borescope and hammer.

Field-erected or newly fabricated vessel/boiler at a construction site, fab yard or drydock: examine plate sections and field welds for defects, check fit-up seams, and watch a hydrostatic or air test for weeping/leaking joints; open-air, changing access, weather and other trades present.

tasks.label: Inspect assembled vessels or individual components, such as tubes, fittings, valves, controls, or auxiliary mechanisms, to locate any defects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outage inspection of an erected boiler's pressure parts in a power plant or industrial plant: entering the furnace/drum, walking scaffold or ropes, examining waterwall and superheater tubes, headers and drum internals for wall loss, erosion, pitting, bulges and cracked attachment welds, taking UT thickness readings and marking areas for repair. Hot, sooty, confined, scaffolded, poor light.

Shop inspection of newly fabricated vessel sections and components on the fab-shop floor: checking longitudinal/circumferential seam welds for undercut, porosity and cracks with weld gauges and visual aids, verifying fit-up, roundness, nozzle and tube-hole dimensions on parts held in rolls, jigs and stands before the piece moves to NDE or shipping.

Routine walkdown inspection of boiler-house auxiliaries: piping, valves, pumps, fans, gauge glasses, regulators and control gear, looking for steam/water/oil leaks, hot spots, corrosion, insulation damage and abnormal instrument readings while the plant runs. Fixed layout, plant-controlled access, elevated walkways and stairs.

Hands-on inspection of individual fittings and controls that have been isolated, removed or opened: safety and relief valves, feed regulators, water columns, blowdown valves, automatic control mechanisms - checking seats, discs, packing, linkage wear and set pressure/leak tightness on a bench or in place, and condemning or passing the part.

Verification inspection after a field repair or new erection: examining replacement tube-to-header and tube butt welds, plug welds and pad welds, checking manway gasket seating and bolt-up, then walking the unit during hydrostatic or steam test hunting weeps and leaks at joints, seams and fittings before the boiler is returned to service.

Internal inspection of other vessels handled by boilermakers during a turnaround: fuel-oil and process storage tanks, digesters, heat exchangers and process vessels - checking floor/shell thickness, seam welds, internal corrosion and pitting after opening the vessel or with the vessel still in service, at a refinery, mill or power plant site.

instances.label: Shop layout of flat plate for new boiler/vessel fabrication: from drawings or CAD, the boilermaker squares and nests parts on a plate lying on a layout table or cutting bed, and marks cut lines, bend/brake lines, hole centers, weld/attachment locations and part numbers with soapstone, scribe and center punch.

Shop layout of developed (geometric) shapes on plate: cone and transition unwraps, elbow/miter segments, saddle and nozzle penetrations laid out by parallel/radial line development with compasses, dividers, trammel points and beam compass, marking cut lines, seam lines and rolling/bend reference lines.

Field repair layout at a plant outage: after templating or measuring the damaged area of a boiler, tank or duct, the boilermaker lays out the replacement patch/insert plate on horses or in the laydown/field shop, marking cut lines, bevel lines and bend lines from the template and field dimensions.

Field marking directly on the installed structure: laying out window-cut boundaries on a waterwall tube panel, drum shell, hopper or vessel wall in place, using wrap-arounds, squares and templates while working from scaffold, a lift or inside a confined boiler with ash, insulation and limited access.

tasks.label: Bell, bead with power hammers, or weld pressure vessel tube ends to ensure leakproof joints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field retube of a firetube/industrial package boiler during an outage at a plant boiler house (hospital, paper mill, food plant): after new tubes are installed, the boilermaker rolls each tube end into the tubesheet with a power expander, flares (bells) it, and beads several hundred tube ends with a pneumatic hammer and beading tool, working inside the cramped, sooty boiler shell and front/rear heads under a confined-space permit, then re-rolls leakers found on hydro.

Outage repair on a watertube boiler or HRSG at a power plant or refinery: a handful to a few dozen leaking or replaced tube ends are rolled and seal-welded into a mud drum, steam drum or header, working off staging inside the unit in awkward and overhead positions on as-found, scaled and distorted tube seats, with code-quality leaktight joints required before hydro.

Shop fabrication of a new pressure vessel, boiler or shell-and-tube heat exchanger at a boiler/vessel fabrication shop: hundreds to thousands of new tube ends are prepped and seal-welded (and roller or hydraulically expanded) into clean, drilled tubesheets on stands or a positioner, to ASME code with NDE and hydro acceptance.

Retube or plug-and-reseal of a shell-and-tube heat exchanger or surface condenser bundle at a refinery, chemical plant or utility: tube ends rolled, flared and in many services seal-welded at the channel head or tubesheet face, done either with the exchanger in place in the plant or on a laydown/shop stand after the bundle is pulled.

New boiler or waste-heat unit erection at a construction site: tube ends welded into drums, headers and panels at height on scaffold or from lifts, partly weather-exposed, with fit-up varying joint to joint and site conditions changing daily.

tasks.label: Locate and mark reference points for columns or plates on boiler foundations, following blueprints and using straightedges, squares, transits, or measuring instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New boiler/HRSG or packaged-boiler erection at an industrial or power-plant construction site: from erection drawings and site control points, establish column grid lines and mark base-plate/column reference points on a finished, flat, drivable concrete foundation mat or slab. Surface open and accessible; other trades working nearby; tolerances on the order of 1/8 in.

Heavy boiler foundation with elevated pedestals/piers, embedded anchor bolts and steel sole plates: mark column reference points on top of 2-4 ft pedestals and on embedded steel plates, punch/scribe marks in steel, and transfer benchmark elevations with transit or level; rebar dowels, forms and grout pockets present.

Boiler replacement inside an existing institutional or industrial boiler room (hospital, school, campus plant): old unit removed and floor cleared; lay out and mark reference points for the new boiler's base frame/columns and anchor locations on the floor or housekeeping pad, working around existing piping, drains and walls.

Marking reference points, centerlines and hole/attachment locations on sole plates, base plates and plate sections before they are set on the foundation, done in a boiler fabrication shop or on a layout table in the site lay-down area, using squares, straightedges, tapes, scribes and punches.

Outage/retrofit layout inside an operating boiler house: locate and mark reference points on existing foundations, sole plates and support steel for replacement columns or plate sections, verifying blueprints against as-built conditions and plumbing points down from existing overhead steel, amid scaffolding, grating, congestion, dirt and poor light.

It is the same act as this task - locating and marking reference points from drawings on a concrete foundation surface - on the same material, at tighter tolerance than boilermaker column layout, using a robotic total station in place of a transit.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Case Studies | HP Official Site

sources.transferJustification: Related task: marking anchor-bolt/equipment reference points on a concrete floor from a model. Same objects (anchor points on concrete for heavy equipment), same instruments (total station), and tolerance at or below boiler column layout needs.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Case Studies | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint has been used inside operating warehouses to mark 1,500 navigation-code locations to a plus/minus 2 mm positional requirement, showing point marking from plans inside a finished, institution-controlled facility.

tasks.label: Shape or fabricate parts, such as stacks, uptakes, or chutes, to adapt pressure vessels, heat exchangers, or piping to premises, using heavy-metalworking machines such as brakes, rolls, or drill presses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boiler shop / fabrication shop: rolling heavy plate blanks (3/8"–1" thick, 8–10 ft wide) into cylindrical cans for a stack or uptake shell on a 3- or 4-roll plate roll. Blank comes off the burning table, is craned onto the roll, pre-bent, rolled, checked against a radius template, and set aside for seam welding.

Boiler shop: press-brake forming of chute and hopper plates, breeching/transition panels, angle flanges and stiffeners from cut blanks — several bends per part, bend allowances from the drawing, angle checked with a protractor or template, parts stacked for fit-up.

Boiler shop: layout/marking, blank cutting (shear or CNC burn table), then drilling, punching, countersinking and tapping bolt-hole patterns in flanges, base plates, doubler plates and structural members on a drill press or CNC drill line; deburr and stamp part marks.

Field shop / laydown area at a plant outage or new-build jobsite: fabricating a one-off adapter piece (duct transition, chute liner, spool, patch section) to dimensions field-measured off as-found equipment, using portable rolls, a portable brake or press, and a mag drill; part later trial-fitted and reworked.

In-place or hand-and-machine irregular work: bumping mitered cone segments and hopper corners on the brake against wooden templates, hot-forming or hammer/peen dressing of odd shapes, and mag-drilling or slotting holes in installed flanges and casing that cannot be brought to a machine; fit verified against the existing structure and reworked until it lands.
