tasks.label: Position, align, and secure structural parts or related assemblies to boiler frames, tanks, or vats of pressure vessels, following blueprints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-build field erection at a power plant / industrial construction site (utility or recovery boiler, HRSG, ductwork): crane-set pressure-part modules, buckstays, casing panels and structural members are landed on the boiler frame at elevation, aligned with plumb bobs, levels, drift pins, come-alongs and turnbuckles per erection drawings, then bolted or tack welded. Multi-tonne pieces, weather, scaffold/steel access, changing site layout.

Outage maintenance/repair at an operating plant: fitting and securing replacement waterwall panel sections, patch plates, seal and casing plates, tube shields, hangers, brackets and supports to an already-erected boiler, working on staged scaffolding inside a confined, sooty, ash-laden furnace or in tight penthouse/duct spaces; parts trimmed and fitted to existing as-found geometry, then tacked/bolted.

Fabrication shop: attaching structural add-on parts (clips, gussets, base plates, stiffeners, lifting lugs, brackets, hanger supports) to boiler frame steel members and to shell/panel weldments per blueprint/3-D model; parts staged nearby, main member on rollers or a turning device; fit, tack, then finish weld to code.

Shop fabrication of boiler pressure-part panels: tubes, fin bars and membrane panel sub-assemblies positioned, aligned and secured into waterwall/economizer panels on a panel bay per drawings, then seam welded; repetitive, well-defined geometry, panels up to ~3 m x 26 m.

Shop assembly of major vessel/tank components: fitting heads to shell cans, aligning shell courses/strakes, setting large nozzles, manways and saddles onto a pressure vessel on rotators/positioners, holding ASME code fit-up tolerances with dogs, wedges and turnbuckles before tacking.

Field-erected storage tanks, vats, stacks and package boiler installations: positioning and securing shell plates/strakes, wind girders, roof rafters and structural supports on a tank pad, or setting and securing a package boiler/deaerator with its platforms, breeching and supports in a plant mechanical room; layout differs site to site.

It transfers because the objects (steel plates, clips, gussets, stiffeners up to 200 kg), the source of instructions (3-D model/blueprint), the fit-up precision (code-quality weld joints), and the securing method (tack then finish weld) are the same as a boilermaker positioning structural parts on boiler frame steel.

tasks.label: Clean pressure vessel equipment, using scrapers, wire brushes, and cleaning solvents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility/industrial boiler internal cleaning during a scheduled outage: working off scaffolding or rope access inside the furnace, scraping and wire-brushing slag, ash, soot and hard fireside deposits off waterwall tubes, superheater banks and headers; confined space, dust, poor light, deposit type and access differ boiler to boiler.

Confined-space interior cleaning of a pressure vessel, steam/mud drum, deaerator or exchanger shell: entering through a manway, hand-scraping sludge and waterside scale off internals and shell walls, wire-brushing and solvent-wiping surfaces so the vessel can be inspected or repaired.

Tube-side cleaning at the tubesheet: brushing, scraping or lancing scale, coke and fouling out of boiler, condenser or heat-exchanger tube IDs, plus cleaning the bundle face, either in place at the unit or at a turnaround wash pad, to a cleanliness the plant inspector will accept.

Bench/shop cleaning of removed pressure-vessel components: valves, fittings, water columns, handhole and manway covers, gasket seats, tube stubs and weld prep areas cleaned with scrapers, wire brushes, power brushes and solvent degreasers in a fab shop or laydown area.

Small firetube / commercial or institutional boiler cleaning in a building basement or mechanical room: brushing soot out of flue passages, scraping the fireside and combustion chamber, vacuuming debris and solvent-wiping surfaces; cramped, cluttered, site-specific installations.

tasks.label: Repair or replace defective pressure vessel parts, such as safety valves or regulators, using torches, jacks, caulking hammers, power saws, threading dies, welding equipment, or metalworking machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial or institutional boiler room (hospital, university, food plant, district heat): replace a defective ASME safety relief valve, pressure regulator, water column, gauge glass or blowdown valve on a firetube/watertube boiler. Isolate and drain, break a seized threaded or flanged joint (torch heat, wrenches, nut splitter), cut and thread new nipple with dies, install and torque the new valve with gasket/sealant, then function/leak test and reset pressure.

Scheduled outage on a utility or large industrial boiler: cut out and replace defective pressure parts inside the unit aded/drum nozzles, tube sections, header stubs, valve connections using torches, grinders, jacks and welding, working from scaffolding in a dark, sooty, confined space with overhead and out-of-position welds, followed by NDE and hydrotest.

In-situ weld repair of a pressure vessel, deaerator, exchanger or drum at a refinery, mill or power plant: gouge/grind out cracks or eroded metal, build up or overlay with weld, fit and weld a patch or replacement seal/seat surface, grind to profile, with preheat and code-required inspection, on equipment fixed in place inside the plant.

Shop repair of a component removed from service and brought to the boiler/repair shop: valve or regulator body, manway, nozzle, tube panel section or vessel head. Disassemble, machine or clad worn seats, cut out and weld in replacement material on a bench/positioner using metalworking machinery and welding equipment, reassemble and pressure test.

Emergency service call on a small commercial or multifamily building boiler: cramped, cluttered old basement mechanical room taken as found, non-standard piping, corroded fittings, poor light and access; replace a leaking relief valve, feedwater regulator or fitting quickly with hand and portable power tools.

Field/remote outdoor work: repair or replace corroded fittings, safety valves and patch sections on process vessels, separators, tanks or trailer-mounted units at a well pad, farm, marine/barge or field-erected tank site; mobile welding rig, weather exposure, no fixed layout, rigging and jacking required.

tasks.label: Attach rigging and signal crane or hoist operators to lift heavy frame and plate sections or other parts into place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New boiler/HRSG field erection at a power-plant construction site: boilermaker selects slings, shackles and spreader bars, chokes or attaches to lifting lugs on multi-ton waterwall panels, drums, headers or steel frame sections lying on cribbing in a laydown yard, checks center of gravity, then hand/radio-signals a crawler or mobile crane operator to hoist the piece and land it on the erected frame; outdoors, wind, mud, congested rigging paths.

Outage or repair work inside an existing utility/industrial boiler: rigging tube panel sections, casing plate, burner or header pieces through tight doors and scaffolding using chain falls, come-alongs, monorail beams and trolleys; slings attached in a dark, ash-covered confined space, then signaling a hoist or crane operator (often out of sight) to lift and spot the piece into the fit-up.

Fabrication shop assembly of boiler modules, pressure vessels or tanks: rigging rolled shell courses, heads and plate sections from a lay-down area onto rolls, turning rolls, positioners or fit-up stands, then signaling the overhead bridge-crane operator (or using a pendant) to lift and set the section for fit-up and tacking; fixed layout, standard equipment, other trades in the same bay.

Field erection/repair of storage tanks, vats, stacks, precipitators or digesters at a refinery, pulp mill or process plant: rigging shell plates and course sections, roof structures or ductwork outdoors alongside hydraulic jacks, and signaling a mobile crane to set each plate for fit-up on an as-found industrial site.

Rigging smaller boiler auxiliaries and parts inside a plant: manway covers, valves, soot blowers, pump/fan components or short duct sections lifted with a jib crane, chain hoist or forklift-mounted boom in a maintenance bay or on the plant floor; attach a sling or eyebolt and signal the hoist operator to set the part in place.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned hoisting and placement of heavy steel workpieces. It transfers to the lift-and-place half of this task because the objects (multi-ton steel plate/slab) and placement precision are comparable, but only where the load is presented in a known position with a dedicated lifting attachment.

tasks.label: Straighten or reshape bent pressure vessel plates or structure parts, using hammers, jacks, or torches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outage repair on an installed boiler at a utility or industrial plant: straightening bowed waterwall tube panels, bent buckstays, casing and seal plates, damper blades or door frames that remain welded into the erected unit. Worked from scaffold or a lift in a sooty, confined, poorly lit furnace using porta-power jacks, wedges, sledges and oxy-fuel spot/vee heats, checked with straightedge and string line.

Field erection/laydown yard at a power plant, refinery or pulp mill: straightening plate sections, duct and hopper panels, casing sheets and structural members (angles, channels, stiffeners, lugs) bent in shipping or rigging, before they are fitted. Done on cribbing or a work stand with hydraulic jacks, come-alongs, sledges and torch heat, with crane assistance; outdoors, weather and layout vary site to site.

Boiler/pressure-vessel or tank fabrication shop: straightening a discrete bent or warped part - a rolled shell plate with a flat spot or off-radius edge, a warped flame-cut plate or reinforcing pad, a bent stiffener or bracket - using the shop press, jacks, wedges, hammers and torch heat, verified with a template, sweep board or straightedge.

Fabrication shop: correcting weld-induced distortion in a fabricated pressure part - peaking at a longitudinal seam, buckled/wavy plate between stiffeners, an out-of-round shell course - using flame or induction heat-straightening patterns (vee and spot heats) plus jacks and strongbacks, held within temperature limits and checked against code tolerance with templates.

Plant maintenance shop / boilermaker tool room: straightening small bent parts brought in from the unit - handrail sections, ladder rungs, tube shields, grate bars, brackets, access-door frames, bolt-on lugs - on a bench, anvil or small hydraulic press with hammer and torch.

sources.claim: Galdabini builds automatic straightening machines and heavy-duty straightening presses that scan a bent workpiece, compute the correction and press it straight - correcting both linearity and twist - for bars, shafts, tubes, rails and structural profiles.
sources.transferJustification: Boilermakers straighten bent 'structure parts' - angles, bars, rails, tube sections, brackets - with jacks and presses; these machines perform that exact operation on the same class of rolled steel sections, running the measure/press/re-measure loop to tolerance under machine control.

sources.system: Songming Robot System (robotic line heating / curved shell-plate forming)
sources.title: Hyundai Heavy reports breakthrough in shipbuilding robotics - Marine Log
sources.claim: Hyundai Heavy Industries' Songming robot system uses a 6-axis articulated robot with high-frequency induction heating and automatic heating-line generation to reshape thick steel shell plates into specified three-dimensional curved surfaces; it was validated in actual shipyard conditions for over a year.
sources.transferJustification: Line heating is the same physical process a boilermaker uses to reshape plate with a torch: localized heating of thick steel to induce plastic shrinkage until the plate matches a target geometry. The robot plans the heat pattern itself and executes it on heavy plate in a forming bay.

sources.system: Gantry-robot induction line-heating system with automatic measurement for hull plate forming
sources.developer: Korean research group, Journal of the Society of Naval Architects of Korea
sources.title: A Study on the Concave Type Hull Plate Forming using Induction Heating System
sources.claim: A gantry-robot heating system combining a high-frequency induction heater with automatic shape measurement was built and applied to forming concave hull plates of the type actually used in ship manufacturing, closing the measure-heat-remeasure loop without a person directing the heat source.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates the whole heat-reshape-verify cycle on heavy steel plate under machine control - the same loop a boilermaker runs with a torch and a template when reshaping or straightening plate.

tasks.label: Shape seams, joints, or irregular edges of pressure vessel sections or structural parts to attain specified fit of parts, using cutting torches, hammers, files, or metalworking machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boiler/pressure-vessel fabrication shop: plate for shell courses and heads is laid out and thermally cut to size with weld-prep bevels; after rolling, the boilermaker trims and grinds the longitudinal and circumferential seam edges so the courses fit within the specified root gap and alignment tolerance. Overhead cranes, rolls, positioners, standard shop lighting.

Shop or on-site prefab area: preparing tubes, nozzles, headers and structural members - saddle/intersection cuts, miters, hole cuts and bevels on pipe and beams, plus grinding off dross - so branch connections and structural joints seat to the specified fit before welding.

Field erection of a boiler or large vessel at a power-plant, refinery or mill construction site: sections and waterwall panels are rigged into place, then torch-trimmed, gouged, ground, and hammered/dogged to close mismatch and attain the specified fit-up gap. Work at height on scaffold, weather exposed, layout unique to the site.

Outage repair inside an installed boiler or vessel: confined, soot-covered furnace interior; cut out damaged tube sections or cracked seams with a torch, bevel and dress the remaining stub ends with grinder and file, and trim the replacement piece so the joint fits within tolerance.

Field repair of tanks, vats, heat exchangers and their structural supports at an operating plant: cut out corroded or cracked plate, shape and trim patch plates or doublers to the as-found opening, gouge out old weld, and file/grind irregular edges to attain fit.

sources.system: HGG SPC 1500-3000 PT/VC pipe and vessel cutting machine
sources.title: SPC 3000: Perform Perfect Hole Cutting and Fewer Secondary Finishing - HGG Group
sources.claim: HGG's SPC 1500-3000 PT/VC CNC machine automates layout, marking, cutting, beveling and ... pipe and pressure-vessel heads from 3 to 118 in., producing the weld preparation along the fit ... nozzle-to-vessel connections after CAD data import.

sources.system: PeddiBot-1200 robotic thermal cutting machine (Staubli robot arm, HGG-powered)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; machine commercially sold for several years)

sources.claim: The PeddiBot-1200 robotic thermal cutting machine scans each incoming profile, adapts the torch path to measured material deviations, and makes copes, trim cuts and bevel cuts that leave structural parts ready for fit-up with little or no hand grinding.

sources.system: EVS robotic thick-plate plasma/flame cutting line
sources.title: Robotic Thick-Plate Cutting: Plasma & Flame with Bevels
sources.claim: Robotic thick-plate plasma/flame cutting cells tilt the torch to cut V, ... weld-prep grooves in one pass on pressure vessel, tank, bridge and shipbuilding plate, delivering a part ready to fit without a secondary gouging or prep step.

sources.system: HGG APC (Advanced Profile Cutting) robotic system
sources.title: HGG Group | New Equipment Digest
sources.claim: HGG's APC profile cutting system pairs a 360-degree rotating robot with laser scanning and a Hypertherm XPR300 plasma source to cut steel profiles and weld preparations accurately in a fabrication cell.

sources.title: MACMegaGrind Robotic Grinding Cell | MESH Automation
sources.claim: Force-controlled robotic grinding cells with custom fixturing perform heavy material removal and weld-seam blending on large, heavy steel parts in fabrication workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grinding/weld blending of heavy steel weldments. The dressing and grinding of seam and edge surfaces to a specified profile is the same material-removal operation on the same class of heavy carbon-steel parts required to attain fit-up of vessel sections.

sources.system: Ultrasonic-driven adaptive robotic plasma arc bevel cutting system
sources.developer: Academic (Int. Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology, 2025)
sources.title: Ultrasonic-driven adaptive control of robotic plasma arc cutting for bevel applications
sources.claim: Sensor-driven adaptive control of robotic plasma arc bevel cutting has been developed and tested ... weld-prep bevels (30 degree bevel, 2 mm root face) of the type used in pressure vessel fabrication, indicating robots can hold weld-prep geometry on varying plate.

sources.system: Persona AI humanoid shipyard welding robot
sources.developer: Persona AI with HD Hyundai / HD KSOE
sources.title: US firm's humanoid robot to perform welding in Korea's shipbuilding
sources.claim: Mobile/humanoid robots intended to do welding and related metalwork on shipyard structures in the field are still prototypes, with a prototype targeted for end of 2026 and commercial use planned for 2027 - i.e., no comparable field-mobile system is deployed for in-situ torch cutting and edge shaping.

tasks.label: Bolt or arc weld pressure vessel structures and parts together, using wrenches or welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop fabrication of vessel/drum shells and heads: rolled plate courses tacked and set on rollerbeds, then longitudinal and circumferential seams welded multi-pass (SAW/FCAW) to ASME code quality with RT/UT acceptance, in a boiler/pressure-vessel fabrication shop.

Shop attachment welding on vessels: fitting and welding nozzles, manways, flanges, saddles, lugs and stiffeners to shells and heads; heavy prepared grooves, multi-layer welds in several positions, code-quality NDE, in a fabrication shop.

Field erection at a power plant or industrial site: joining boiler pressure parts and structures in place - waterwall panel-to-panel seams, tube butt welds, header and drum connections, casing and structural steel - working off scaffolding or lifts at height, out of position, in weather.

Outage maintenance/repair welding on installed equipment: cutting out and welding in replacement tube sections, pad welds, patch plates and seal welds inside boiler furnaces, vessels and ducts; confined space, degraded/distorted parts, restricted access, preheat.

Bolted assembly: making up flanged connections on vessels, heat exchangers and headers, and bolting manway/handhole covers, casing and support connections with impact and hydraulic torque wrenches to specified torque and sequence, in plants and shops.

sources.system: PEMA Nozzle Welding Station (with PEMA positioners/rollerbeds and column & booms)
sources.title: Offshore and process equipment | Pemamek
sources.claim: PEMA Nozzle welding station is a commercially sold robotic station for pressure vessels that laser-scans the prepared groove, auto-generates the robot welding program and performs automated multi-layer welding; it also welds circular and longitudinal seams, support legs and other external components.

sources.system: PEMA boiler panel lines / tube shop welding lines
sources.title: Power generation welding automation | Pemamek
sources.claim: Pemamek supplies boiler panel welding lines and highly automated tube-shop lines (membrane waterwall panels, tube fabrication) that weld boiler pressure parts in purpose-built stations run by a single operator; installed at boiler makers such as Caldema.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop welding of boiler tubes, fin bars and membrane panels. These are the same joints (tube butt welds, fin/panel seams, code quality) produced by field erection and tube-replacement repairs, so performance carries over when the joint is presented fixtured.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 robotic welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics Secures $100M of Venture Capital Funding
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells use vision and AI to find, plan and weld steel parts autonomously without programming or hard fixtures, handling parts up to about 70 ft, and are in production use in US and Canadian fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix structural steel weldment welding. Comparable plate thickness, multi-pass groove welds and scan-based adaptation to as-built fit-up, which is what vessel attachment and repair joints require once fixtured.

sources.title: Welding smarter: How robotic technology is advancing shipbuilding at Seaspan
sources.claim: Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards installed Inrotech mobile welding robots in 2025; the Inrotech Crawler works on ship blocks in the block assembly shop, 3D-laser-scanning butt joints, planning the passes and welding only when the weld can meet the weld procedure specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-pass groove welding of thick plate structures inside a human work facility. It shows scan-and-plan seam welding on large assemblies comparable to vessel shell seams, but the robot does not manipulate or rotate the workpiece.

sources.title: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot | Total Marine Technology Products
sources.claim: TMT's Boltron is a commercially available automated/autonomous flange-bolting robot for site use at refineries, power stations and production plants; it tightens and loosens the nuts on bolted flanges of the type found on heat exchangers and pressure vessels, and has been contracted by the QAL alumina refinery.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Welder, an autonomous construction-site welding robot that laser-measures the groove of steel columns and plans its passes, was put to work welding massive steel columns at the Toranomon-Azabudai high-rise project; it handles prepared column butt joints, not boiler pressure parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ multi-pass arc welding of thick steel butt joints at a construction site. Cited to test whether field welding reaches E3; the joint type and access differ sharply from boiler tube banks and pressure parts.

sources.title: It's Time To Think Differently About Automated Welding for Pressure Vessels (JPT)
sources.claim: Column-and-boom submerged-arc systems with rollerbeds are in production use welding pressure-vessel seams in US fabrication shops, with large reported output gains at vessel and skid manufacturers.

tasks.label: Install manholes, handholes, taps, tubes, valves, gauges, or feedwater connections in drums of water tube boilers, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Planned outage at a power/industrial plant: boilermaker enters the steam or mud drum of a water-tube boiler through the manway, seats replacement generating-bank tube ends in the drum holes and expands/flares them with a tube expander and pneumatic rolling motor to specified torque or wall reduction, working in a confined, dirty, poorly lit drum on temporary scaffolding.

Plant maintenance: installing or replacing drum-mounted fittings — water column and gauge glass, chemical-feed and sampling taps, feedwater connection, small valves — onto drum nozzles in the boiler house, cutting/threading or bolting flanges, dressing gaskets and sealant, torquing with hand tools, often on a platform beside the drum.

Closing the pressure boundary after internal work: fitting manhole (manway) covers and handhole plates with new gaskets to drum and header openings, positioning the internal-type cover through the opening, installing dogs/studs and torquing nuts in sequence so the joint seals at hydrotest.

Shop fabrication of a new package water-tube boiler at a boiler manufacturer: drums on rolling stands, tubes inserted into drilled/grooved drum holes and rolled in, nozzles, taps and handhole seats fitted out, with fixed shop layout, cranes and jigs.

New-unit erection or major retrofit at a construction site or shipyard: drums set on structural steel at height, boilermaker installs tubes into the drum and makes up feedwater, valve and gauge connections in the open, weather and site clutter present, layout differing site to site.

sources.system: Maus Italia MA 2501 CNC tube rolling/expansion work centre
sources.title: MA 2501 – CNC single or double-axis work centre – Maus Italia
sources.claim: Maus Italia's MA 2501 is a commercially sold CNC work centre that performs fully automatic rolling expansion (with torque and tube-size control), tube-end facing, hole grooving and orbital TIG welding of tubes into tube sheets up to 2500 mm diameter, tubes 3/8"–2", at about 600 tubes/hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rolling/expanding tubes into tube-sheet holes of heat exchangers. Boilermakers install boiler tubes in drums with the same class of tool (roller tube expander driven by a torque-controlled rolling motor), the same tube diameters (≈2"), and the same acceptance criterion (expansion torque / percent wall reduction for a leak-tight joint), so a machine that seats and expands tubes to torque in fixtured tube sheets performs the same operation the boilermaker performs in a drum.

sources.system: OCTA/SMI ITS M25 tube insertion machine
sources.title: Tube insertion machine - Precise and automatic threading on heat exchangers | OCTA Group
sources.claim: OCTA Group's ITS M25 tube insertion machines automatically align to the holes of a pre-assembled stack and thread tubes through them at a programmed height, automating the tube-loading step that precedes expansion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting tubes into aligned holes of a heat-exchanger stack. The first half of installing tubes in a boiler drum is exactly this — presenting each tube end to a drilled hole and pushing it to the correct projection before rolling — so an automatic hole-finding tube feeder substantiates that step when the work is fixtured.

sources.system: Longterm Machinery automatic torque-controlled LPG cylinder valve screwing machine (comparable units from Durulsan, ROK Teknik, Atilim)
sources.title: High Quality LPG Cylinder Automatic Torque Controlled Screwing Machine
sources.claim: Automatic LPG cylinder valve screwing machines thread valves into pressure-vessel ports under servo torque control and stop at the set torque, with automatic orientation of the installed valve; these run as unattended stations in cylinder production and filling lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: threading a valve into a port of a pressure vessel to a specified torque without damaging the thread. Installing taps, small valves and gauge connections in a boiler drum is the same operation on a fixtured vessel — engage a tapered/parallel pipe thread and torque it to a leak-tight value — differing mainly in fitting size.

sources.system: Vision/compliance-equipped robotic hydraulic-valve assembly cell (SCHUNK gripper, ATI compliance device)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A production robot cell assembles hydraulic cartridge valves: the robot picks the adjustment screw, has an O-ring seal installed on it, and threads it into the can and locknut using a gripper plus a compliance device to avoid cross-threading, with torque monitored.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of an elastomeric seal followed by torque-controlled threaded make-up. The boilermaker's fitting/cover work is the same sequence — set a gasket, engage the fastener without cross-threading, torque to spec — on larger but geometrically simple parts presented in a fixture.

sources.system: MIRAI-controlled Universal Robots cobots for bolt torquing
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM – Automated bolt torquing | Micropsi Industries
sources.claim: A North American automotive OEM has put seven bolt-torquing tasks into production on Universal Robots cobots running Micropsi's MIRAI AI-vision control, which copes with variation in bolt position, lighting and incoming parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating and running fasteners to torque under part-to-part variation. Bolting a handhole plate or manway cover is the same fastening operation, executed in a defined sequence, when the cover and studs are presented in a fixtured setup.

sources.title: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot | Total Marine Technology Products
sources.claim: TMT's Boltron is a commercially supplied automated/autonomous flange bolting robot that tightens and loosens flange bolts on large bolted joints (heat exchangers, pressure vessels, piping) at refineries, power stations and other industrial sites; it performs only the nut-running step after being rigged onto the flange by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing the studs of a bolted pressure-boundary joint in a plant. It covers only the fastening sub-step of installing a manway cover or a flanged valve — it does not fit gaskets, place covers or make up fittings — so it cannot by itself carry a whole-instance judgment at the plant (E2) tier.

tasks.label: Assemble large vessels in an on-site fabrication shop prior to installation to ensure proper fit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shell-course assembly in the site fab shop: rolled plate cans set on turning rolls with a crane, seams drawn together with dogs, wedges and turnbuckles, roundness and edge offset checked, tacked, then longitudinal and circumferential seams welded out (SAW/FCAW), ground and dimension-checked before the section is released for erection.

Adding appurtenances to a shop-assembled vessel: laying out from prints and fitting nozzles, manways, stiffener/wind-girder rings, saddles, lifting lugs and pads onto the shell, tacking square and plumb, then welding out to code and checking projection/orientation tolerances.

Pressure-part subassemblies in the shop: fitting membrane/waterwall panel tubes and fin bar, tube stubs to headers, economizer or superheater bundle elements; aligning tubes to gauge, tacking, welding, and checking panel flatness/length before shipment to the erection front.

Open-air pre-assembly in the jobsite fab/laydown yard: crane-set duct sections, hoppers, casing modules, stack cans or tank floor/roof segments bolted and welded into large modules on cribbing, braced against distortion, squared with tape, level and laser, in outdoor conditions on an active construction site.

Trial (test) assembly and match-marking in the shop: bringing shipped-loose or field-jointed pieces together to verify fit, fitting internals such as baffles, trays, brackets and refractory anchors, recording dimensions, match-marking, then disassembling and tagging pieces for transport and field erection.

sources.title: ABC Of Automated Welding And Assembly | Pemamek
sources.claim: PEMA Assembly & welding station is a commercial machine that receives crane-loaded rolled shells on a powered fit-up/jig unit, pushes the shell against the ..., levels the edges with cylinders to hold roundness, then tack welds and rotates the vessel for seam welding; used by tank and pressure vessel makers.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: shop assembly of large vessels (tanks, pressure vessels) from rolled shell courses, including the fit-up that 'ensures proper fit'. Marked unclear because one operator steers the station by wireless control.

sources.system: PEMA Nozzle welding station / PEMA rollerbeds and column & booms

sources.claim: Pemamek's pressure-vessel nozzle welding station generates robot welding programs automatically from laser-scanned groove geometry and also welds circular and longitudinal seams, support legs and other external components on heavy-duty workpieces, with multi-layer welding.

sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 cell handles parts as large as 70 feet long and both of its vision/AI welding cells autonomously weld steel parts and ....

sources.title: Power generation welding automation | Pemamek

sources.transferJustification: Same class of work as shop assembly of boiler waterwall/membrane panels: tubes and fin bars are fed, aligned and seam-welded into finished pressure-part panels.

sources.system: PEMA micro panel line / stiffener mounting portals / PEMA VRWP robots
sources.title: Shipbuilding welding and production automation | Pemamek
sources.claim: Pemamek's shipbuilding panel solutions include mobile portals with stiffener manipulating ... that pick and fit stiffeners in any direction either manually or fully automatically, plus an automated profile assembly and tack welding station and robotized welding stations for micro panels and sub-assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling large stiffened steel plate modules (ship panels/blocks) from plate and profiles — comparable plate thickness, weld sizes and fit-up tolerances to duct, casing and hopper modules pre-assembled by boilermakers.

sources.title: Automated Panel Welding - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: Kranendonk's Panel Welding Gantry is a travelling gantry with two or more suspended 6-axis robots that automatically aligns, clamps and welds large stiffened panels for shipbuilding and heavy steel block/section assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly/welding of large heavy-steel stiffened panels and blocks, the closest industrial analogue to boilermaker pre-assembly of large plate modules.

sources.system: HD Hyundai autonomous collaborative welding robots
sources.developer: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries / HD Hyundai Robotics
sources.title: South Korean shipyard turns to AI-powered welding robots - UPI.com
sources.claim: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries has put tracked autonomous collaborative welding robots to work inside its Hull Assembly Plant 2 in Ulsan, welding steel plate cells of ship blocks alongside human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of the art in a structured human work facility (E2): the robot welds joints already fitted and tacked by people; it does not rig, align or fit the plate itself.

sources.system: Orbital tube-to-tubesheet welding heads (Polysoude and similar)
sources.title: Featured Story - Automated tube-to-tubesheet welding - Heat Exchanger World
sources.claim: Tube-to-tubesheet joints in boilers and heat exchangers are produced with fully automatic orbital TIG welding heads aiming at 100% reproducibility and near-zero defect rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining boiler/heat-exchanger tubes to headers and tubesheets, the same joints boilermakers fit and weld in pressure-part subassemblies; marked unclear because the head is positioned tube-by-tube by a technician.

tasks.label: Install refractory bricks or other heat-resistant materials in fireboxes of pressure vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled outage at a utility or industrial plant: re-bricking a firebox/furnace section of a boiler — cutting firebrick, buttering with refractory mortar, laying courses, arches and skewbacks around burner openings and tube penetrations, working off staging inside the confined, sooty vessel with temporary lighting.

Localized in-situ repair: chipping out failed refractory at burner throats, access doors, floor seals and tube penetrations, re-welding/checking anchors, then hand-packing and ramming plastic refractory or hand-troweling castable, feathered to blend with the sound existing lining; cramped confined-space work with hand tools.

Large-area monolithic lining in the field: mixing and gunning/spraying castable refractory over an anchored firebox wall, floor or hopper of a boiler or incinerator, then cutting back and finishing to specified thickness before dry-out.

Installing ceramic-fiber blanket/modules or insulating board in the firebox and on doors and burner throats: stud-welding pins to the shell/casing, compressing and impaling modules, trimming and sealing joints.

Fabrication/refractory shop: casting or spraying monolithic refractory into a rebuilt firebox component (burner throat, door, hopper panel) held on stands/rollers — forms set, castable placed and vibrated or gunned to thickness, then cured.

Fabrication/refractory shop: setting brick, precast shapes and fiber lining into a new or rebuilt pressure-vessel firebox component on stands — fitting, cutting and mortaring shapes to the shell contour and around penetrations.

sources.title: Tundish Robotics - Vesuvius
sources.claim: Vesuvius NextGen Tundish Spray Robot is a commercially deployed KUKA-robot cell that automatically applies a monolithic refractory spray lining to the interior of steel tundishes inside a fully enclosed, interlocked steel frame, controlling feed rate and lining thickness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing a monolithic (spray/gunned) refractory lining on the inner surfaces of a metallurgical pressure/holding vessel. Same material class (refractory spray mass), same accepted output (uniform lining of specified thickness that survives service heat), and the vessel is brought to and fixtured in a purpose-built enclosed cell — the E1 counterfactual for gunned castable lining of a firebox.

sources.system: Primetals BOF/LD converter relining machine (Ternium Santa Cruz)
sources.title: BOF Relining Made Faster — Metals Magazine
sources.claim: Even in purpose-built converter relining stands — the most machine-oriented refractory bricking environment in industry — brick laying is not automated; a Primetals expert states full automation of relining is not feasible, and the machines are operated by remote control from a platform carrying human bricklayers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying refractory brick inside a metallurgical vessel with a purpose-built machine. It bounds the E1 counterfactual for firebox brick lining: where the work is fully brought to the machine, brick placement is still done by human masons.

sources.title: German Steel Producer HKM Orders Customized Relining Machine From Primetals Technologies
sources.claim: The newest converter relining machines automate only brick logistics — magazine lifts and an arm-like manipulator deliver bricks to a roller table — while people inside the vessel still push the bricks into final position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refractory brick lining of a vessel in a purpose-built relining stand; shows that in the closest analog to an E1 setting, robotic hardware handles logistics only and the masonry itself remains manual.

sources.title: REX-ROBO™ LSG | Robot that automates refractory maintenance work
sources.claim: Krosaki Harima's REX-ROBO LSG automates the exchange and installation of refractory plates, nozzles and frames in ladle slide-gate maintenance at a fixed maintenance station, running predetermined robotic motions; first order received March 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation/replacement of refractory components in a hot vessel at a purpose-built station. Supports that fixtured, standardized refractory pieces can be installed robotically at E1, but the pieces are machined plates in a frame, not mortared brick fitted to a firebox contour.

sources.title: Robot Shooter ENG - Dominion
sources.claim: In-plant refractory gunning of furnace linings is performed with operator-driven shooter machines and manipulators rather than autonomous robots; Dominion's rotating shooter sprays castable into blast furnace stacks so workers need not enter the furnace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying monolithic refractory inside a large in-service vessel at a plant (an E2/E3-like setting). It is operator-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment above E1 for gunned lining work.

roles.title: Brickmasons and Blockmasons
roles.description: Lay and bind building materials, such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra-cotta block, with mortar and other substances, to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures.

tasks.label: Measure distance from reference points and mark guidelines to lay out work, using plumb bobs and levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional building: mason lays out CMU/brick wall lines on a poured concrete slab or floor deck inside the building shell — measures from column-line/control points, snaps chalk lines for wall faces, marks door openings and control joints. Active jobsite floor with debris and other trades working.

Exterior flat hard surface: laying out a site wall, perimeter brick veneer line, or building footprint on an existing slab-on-grade, paved area or parking deck from surveyor control points; outdoors, weather, equipment traffic.

Foundation/footing layout on raw ground: measuring from batter boards and property offsets, squaring corners with diagonals/3-4-5, dropping a plumb bob from string intersections to mark corner points, snapping the block wall line on a narrow poured footing in a trench; mud, rebar, uneven grade.

Vertical layout while the wall goes up: plumbing corner leads and jamb lines with spirit level and plumb bob, marking course heights on a story/corner pole, transferring points up from the floor below, marking guidelines on the partially built wall from scaffolding.

Repair, restoration or alteration of an existing structure: marking cut lines for a new opening in an existing brick wall, laying out a rebuilt chimney or replacement wall section to match as-found coursing on aged, out-of-plumb masonry; occupied or weathered buildings, scaffold access.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Autonomous Robotic Layout Solution Leverages HP's Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing to Reduce Cost and lnefficiencies in Construction
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially sold autonomous layout robot that prints lines, arcs, ... and text of the design directly onto construction-site slabs, replacing manual chalk-line layout.

sources.title: HP SitePrint - Robotic Layout Solution | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint navigates jobsites tracked by a robotic total station set on site control points, avoids obstacles, and is built to run on rough, bumpy site surfaces.

sources.title: HP SitePrint prints 2D plans on construction site floors - AEC Magazine
sources.claim: The robot is ruggedised for site conditions and prints on porous outdoor surfaces such as concrete, tarmac, pavement and plywood as well as non-porous finishes.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Case Studies | HP Official Site
sources.claim: Contractors have used HP SitePrint for production layout on real projects, including a multilevel parking garage (3,390 points over 16,485 sq ft) and data-centre slabs, with reported print accuracy of a few millimetres.

sources.title: BIM-Driven Layout for Construction | Dusty Robotics

tasks.label: Construct corners by fastening in plumb position a corner pole or building a corner pyramid of bricks, and filling in between the corners using a line from corner to corner to guide each course, or layer, of brick.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential construction: brick veneer on a new house/townhouse (or CMU foundation/stem walls) at a lot or subdivision. Mason plumbs corner poles or racks back a corner lead, strings a line, and fills in courses; ground level to one or two scaffold lifts; outdoor weather, mud, stacked material, other trades.

New commercial/institutional construction with open site access: brick veneer, CMU backup, or single-wythe block for warehouses, schools, retail, low-rise apartments. Long straight runs between built corner leads, line-and-level work, multiple lifts from scaffold/mast climber, mortar and units supplied by a forklift/tender.

Interior masonry inside a building shell: CMU partitions, stair and elevator shafts, fire walls in schools, hospitals, warehouses. Corners/leads built to layout lines on the slab, line strung, 8-inch blocks (~33 lb) laid with mortar in confined rooms with other trades working nearby.

Detailed or access-constrained masonry on new work: corner piers and columns, arched or soldier-course openings, corbels and banding, chimneys above the roofline, tight urban lots with no room for equipment. Corners set with special shapes and cut closures, lines shifted repeatedly.

Repair, restoration and alteration of existing masonry: rebuilding a spalled or leaning corner, parapet, or damaged wall section; cutting out old units, toothing into remaining work, matching existing brick size, bond and mortar color, and re-establishing plumb corners on an out-of-square old building.

Small owner-directed jobs at private homes: garden and retaining walls, mailbox and gate piers, steps and planters. Uneven ground, homeowner-chosen units, layout staked on site, corners built by eye/level and filled between with a line.

tasks.label: Apply and smooth mortar or other mixture over work surface.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Laying up CMU/concrete block walls on an active construction site (foundation walls, backup walls, warehouse and school walls): spreading and furrowing a mortar bed on the course below with a trowel, buttering head joints, bedding each block, cleaning squeeze-out. Site is open, weather-exposed, layout changes daily, other trades present.

Laying face brick / exterior brick walls and veneer on a house or low-rise building, working from ground or scaffold: spreading mortar beds along the line, buttering heads, adjusting bed thickness to keep courses level and plumb over openings and corners.

Finishing mortar joints — striking/tooling concave or raked joints on freshly laid work, and pointing/repointing existing masonry (raking out weathered joints and packing and tooling new mortar to match) on occupied or historic buildings.

Parging / skim-coating / scratch-coating a mortar or stucco mixture over a masonry surface — foundation wall damp-proof parge, chimney crown, block wall coat — troweled or sprayed on and floated smooth to an even thickness.

Refractory and industrial lining work at a plant: troweling refractory mortar between firebrick, applying castable or patching mix in boilers, kilns, ladles and furnaces during a shutdown, in hot, confined, dusty conditions.

Shop/yard prefabrication: bedding masonry units or placing and screeding a cementitious mix on a fixed casting bed or panel jig in a covered prefab/precast shop, with materials staged and the panel held in a mould or frame.

tasks.label: Calculate angles and courses and determine vertical and horizontal alignment of courses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First-course layout on a new footing or slab at an active jobsite: establishing building lines and square (and other) corner angles from stakes/control points, calculating bond spacing, dry-bonding units, chalking lines and marking opening locations for a brick or CMU wall.

Building and checking corner leads for a new wall: plumbing the lead corner with a spirit level, gauging course heights with a story pole/gauge rod, and stringing a mason's line between leads so the intervening courses run level and true — outdoor residential or commercial jobsite with other trades working nearby.

Course-by-course alignment control while running a wall between leads: checking each course level, plumb and to the line, adjusting unit position and bed-joint thickness, and keeping course heights on gauge to sill, lintel and top-of-wall elevations.

Angled and curved special geometry: computing angles for non-90-degree corners, radius/serpentine walls, arch soffits and skewbacks, corbels and chimney work; calculating bevel cuts and the course spacing needed to hit the specified rise and angle on site.

Repair, alteration and tie-in to existing masonry: gauging the coursing of an existing, often irregular or settled older wall, determining how new work must align vertically and horizontally with it, and toothing/matching into the existing bond.

sources.title: With new funding, Monumental plans to bring its construction robots to the U.S. - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Monumental's electric, autonomous robots lay brick and mortar to millimeter precision on active construction sites, working directly from digital building plans — i.e., the machine computes course positions and holds vertical/horizontal alignment itself.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous bricklaying necessarily includes the rated task: the system derives course heights and angles from the digital plan and places every unit to plumb/level alignment, which is the mason's coursing-and-alignment determination.

sources.title: Bricklaying robots from the Netherlands target the UK - Construction Management
sources.claim: Monumental's robot fleet has completed masonry walls on more than 100 homes plus a school, community centre, hotel ..., sold as finished walls under subcontract.

tasks.label: Break or cut bricks, tiles, or blocks to size, using trowel edge, hammer, or power saw.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New structural CMU/block wall on an open outdoor construction site (house, warehouse, retail pad): mason cuts blocks to length or height with a table masonry saw or cut-off saw for wall ends, openings, corners and closure units as the courses go up; dust, mud, weather, changing site layout.

Face brick / brick veneer laying on site: mason repeatedly cuts bats, closures, queen closers, rake and angle cuts using the trowel edge, brick hammer, or a portable wet saw, sizing each piece against a gap measured on the wall in progress, with the cut face matched for appearance.

Jobsite cut station on a larger commercial project: a stationary masonry table saw in a laydown area where a mason or tender batch-cuts assorted brick and block to a cut list (jamb units, sash blocks, bond-beam pieces, angle cuts) and stacks the output for the crew.

Repair, restoration, or renovation work in an existing structure (occupied building, basement, chimney, parapet on scaffold): cutting brick, block, or structural tile to fit patches, chases, and openings, with dimensions taken off irregular existing masonry and dust control indoors.

Masonry contractor's shop/yard or prefabricated masonry panel plant: cutting brick and block to size on a fixed wet saw from a cut list or shop drawing, indoors on a controlled floor with standard equipment, output palletized for delivery.

tasks.label: Interpret blueprints and drawings to determine specifications and to calculate the materials required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Remove excess mortar with trowels and hand tools, and finish mortar joints with jointing tools, for a sealed, uniform appearance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Brick veneer on a new commercial/institutional building: mason works from a mast-climber or scaffold, cuts off mortar squeeze-out with the trowel as each course is laid, then strikes head and bed joints with a convex jointer once the mortar is thumbprint-hard, tools around openings, corners and soldier courses, and brushes the joints; set time varies with sun, wind and temperature.

Residential work: brick veneer on a house, CMU foundation/stem walls, chimneys and fireplaces. Mixed unit types and joint profiles, tight access around scaffolds and ladders, ground-level and low-lift work; excess mortar is trimmed with the trowel and joints tooled concave, then brushed to a clean, homeowner-visible finish.

Repointing/tuckpointing existing or historic masonry: after joints are raked out, mortar is packed with a pointing trowel/slicker, then tooled to match the surrounding historic joint profile; excess is cut off the soft brick faces without smearing and the wall is brushed. Joint widths and unit faces are irregular; color and profile must match adjacent original work.

Interior CMU partition and structural block walls in a building shell: strike concave joints on exposed faces, cut mortar fins/protrusions flush on faces to be furred or painted, remove droppings from block faces, all in dim light with cluttered floors and other trades working nearby.

Prefabricated/precast masonry panel shop or on-grade panel bed: a panel is assembled horizontally at a fixed work station indoors with consistent materials and lighting; the worker cuts excess mortar from the panel face and tools every joint to a uniform profile before the panel is cured and shipped.

sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 robot autonomously plasters, sands and finishes drywall on active construction sites, showing autonomous finishing of a cementitious wall surface, but not tooling of individual mortar joints.

Transfer does NOT carry to this task: joint tooling requires tracking narrow (~10 mm) joint lines on an irregular unit face, judging mortar set state (thumbprint-hard), compressing with a jointer at controlled force, and shearing squeeze-out with a trowel without smearing unit faces — none of which the plastering robot's broad-area troweling demonstrates.

tasks.label: Fasten or fuse brick or other building material to structure with wire clamps, anchor holes, torch, or cement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential / light-commercial brick veneer over wood- or steel-stud framing: corrugated or screw-on veneer ties fastened through sheathing into studs at code spacing, then embedded in the mortar bed joints as courses rise; outdoor jobsite, weather, scaffold, coordination with framers and window installers.

New commercial/institutional cavity or composite wall with masonry (CMU) backup: brick outer wythe tied to backup with wire/adjustable eye-and-pintle ties bedded in the mortar joints of both wythes as the wall rises; jobsite with mast climbers or tube-and-clamp scaffold.

Masonry anchored to a structural steel or concrete frame: dovetail slot anchors, weld-on or bolted anchors, expansion anchors or epoxied dowels set in drilled anchor holes, torch/weld work at shelf angles and relieving angles; multistory building under construction.

Adhered and specialty units: thin brick or stone veneer bonded with cement/thinset to a prepared backup, glass block panels set with panel anchors and reinforcement, terra-cotta or stone held by wire clamps/cramps; interior and exterior work with tight tolerances and visible finish.

Repair / restoration / retrofit: re-anchoring loose or bulging veneer with helical remedial ties drilled into hidden backup, replacing corroded anchors, resetting displaced units, and patching/repointing to match existing; occupied buildings, swing stage or scaffold, unknown substrate conditions.

Industrial refractory work: firebrick and refractory lining fastened to furnace, ladle, boiler or kiln shells with metal anchors and welded studs, high-temperature mortar and gunned refractory, torch cutting of anchors; inside a plant during a shutdown or in a relining bay.

tasks.label: Clean working surface to remove scale, dust, soot, or chips of brick and mortar, using broom, wire brush, or scraper.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active new-construction jobsite, wall going up: mason brushes/sweeps loose mortar crumbs, brick chips and dust off the top course and bed joint (and off ties, sills, scaffold plank) as laying proceeds, working from ground or scaffold, in weather, around corners, openings and reinforcement.

End of a lift or of the job: mason scrapes hardened mortar droppings and smears off the finished brick/block face, sills and adjacent surfaces and wire-brushes dust and light efflorescence/scale before inspection, washing or coating, without damaging brick or green joints.

Restoration/repointing or chimney repair on an existing building: after cutting/raking out joints, mason wire-brushes and scrapes soot, scale, dust and loose old mortar out of the joints and off the masonry face so new mortar bonds; irregular historic units, ladders/scaffold, occupied premises.

Industrial refractory work inside a plant (boiler, kiln, furnace, ladle, incinerator): before relining, mason cleans slag, scale, soot and old refractory dust off the shell, brick courses and joint surfaces with brush, scraper and vacuum; confined, hot, dusty, plant-controlled access.

Prefab/precast masonry or panel shop: mason cleans the casting bed, jig or formwork surface of mortar/concrete residue and dust between units, and brushes chips off panel faces before the next pour or course; indoor plant with fixed layout and repeated setups.

Housekeeping around the work: sweeping brick fragments, mortar droppings and dust off floors, slabs, decks and scaffold platforms near the wall and mixer at breaks and end of shift, on an active site with tools, materials and other trades present.

sources.system: Mana precast pallet circulation system (cleaning unit)

sources.claim: Automated pallet-circulation lines in precast concrete plants include a cleaning station that removes concrete/mortar residue from the casting work surface with a rotating scraper and brushes before the next element is cast — the same clean-the-working-surface operation, performed by machine on work conveyed to it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning a cementitious work surface of hardened mortar/concrete residue and dust with scraper and brushes before the next material is placed. Same materials (mortar/concrete chips, dust), same tools (scraper, rotary brush), same acceptance standard (surface clean enough to bond/cast), performed automatically in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Automatic Machines for Precast Panels | Bianchi Casseforme
sources.claim: Dedicated brushing machines clean and prepare the long-line casting tables and pallets of precast concrete panel plants automatically between production runs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine brushing of a large cementitious work surface to remove residue and dust before the next casting; comparable debris (concrete/mortar chips, dust) and comparable acceptance (bond-ready surface) to a mason's brushed bed joint or panel face.

sources.system: FANUC R-2000iC/210F and LR Mate material-removal cells (brushing, deburring, blow-off)

tasks.label: Examine brickwork or structure to determine need for repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential call-out: mason walks a private home's exterior brick/block walls and chimney, looks at step cracks, spalled units, efflorescence and washed-out joints; scratches mortar with a tool, taps suspect units, climbs a ladder to the chimney crown and flashing, and decides what needs repointing, rebuilding, or nothing. Weather, landscaping and clutter as found.

Commercial/multifamily facade condition survey: mason (often with an engineer or property manager) examines a multi-story brick veneer or mass-masonry wall from grade, a lift, swing stage or scaffold; checks joint erosion, displaced or bowed brick, cracked lintels and shelf angles, sounds units for delamination, and produces a repair scope with quantities.

In-progress examination on an active repair/restoration jobsite: while cutting out and repointing or rebuilding, the mason repeatedly examines adjacent brickwork - sounding units, gauging joint erosion depth, probing behind removed brick - to decide how far the repair must extend and whether backup and anchors are sound. Scaffold, dust, partial demolition.

Interior masonry examination: basement/foundation CMU wall, interior brick partition, or fire/water-damaged wall in a home or small commercial building; mason checks bowing, horizontal and step cracks, deteriorated joints and moisture staining, and decides whether repair, tuckpointing or replacement is needed. Cramped, cluttered, poorly lit.

Industrial refractory work: refractory brickmason examines a furnace, boiler, kiln, ladle or converter lining in an operating plant (between campaigns or during a shutdown) to determine residual brick thickness, joint opening, spalling and hot spots, and to decide patch, gunning or full reline.

sources.system: MINSCAN LSC (MINSCAN robotic gunning applicator + Ferrotron LaCam + SCANTROL)
sources.title: MINTEQ - Refractories | Minerals Technologies Inc.

sources.system: LaCam / LaCam Torpedo laser lining measurement

sources.claim: Ferrotron/Minteq LaCam high-speed laser measuring units determine residual brick thickness and wear rate of refractory brick linings in converters, steel ladles and torpedo ladles; they operate as mobile or permanently installed measuring stations in steel plants worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: For the building-masonry instances this is the related task: automated condition examination of fired-brick work with joints, at a presentation position engineered for the machine, producing a map of where material loss requires repair - the same determination a mason makes on a wall, at comparable (cm-level) precision.

sources.system: Fully automatic refractory maintenance system (LaCam + MINSCAN)
sources.developer: Minteq International GmbH with Stahlwerk Bous/Saar GmbH
sources.title: Fully automatic refractory maintenance system (ResearchGate record)
sources.claim: A fully automatic refractory maintenance system combining the LaCam laser scanner (residual refractory thickness) with the robotic MINSCAN manipulator was installed on an electric arc furnace at Stahlwerk Bous in 2003, replacing intermittent manual assessment and repair of the lining.

sources.system: Climbing-robot facade inspection framework (simultaneous digital twin)
sources.developer: Zhiliang Ma et al., published in Buildings (MDPI)

sources.claim: A wall-climbing robot with autonomous coverage path planning, real-time deep-learning segmentation of cracks and spalling with metric quantification (mAP 0.775, ~1.1 cm length error) and a digital-twin platform was validated in the lab and on real building facades - research-grade output that maps defects rather than issuing an accepted repair scope.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exterior-wall defect examination (cracks, spalling) on real buildings. sources.title: DJI and Loveland Innovations Announce AI-Powered Roof Damage Detection Software Now Available on Mavic 3 Enterprise
sources.claim: Commercial property-inspection platforms fly automated drone patterns over homes and commercial buildings and apply deep learning to detect roof damage, but the workflow is built around inspection professionals and adjusters who review and sign off the assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior building-envelope condition assessment at private homes and commercial properties (E3). Cited to show the closest fielded systems address roofing materials and remain professional-in-the-loop decision support, so they do not substantiate autonomous masonry repair determination at E3 or E2.

tasks.label: Mix specified amounts of sand, clay, dirt, or mortar powder with water to form refractory mixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active construction site (new residential/commercial masonry): mason or tender proportions shovels of sand and bags of masonry cement/mortar powder into a portable paddle mixer, adds water from a hose or bucket, mixes to the specified consistency, dumps into wheelbarrows and mortar pans, and retempers batches through the day in varying weather.

Small hand-mixed batches for repair, restoration or tuckpointing at a home or occupied building: a few gallons mixed in a tub or bucket with a hoe or drill paddle, matching a specified mix (lime/sand/color-matched historic mortar, or fireclay/refractory cement for a firebox), judged by feel and color.

Large commercial job supplied with preblended mortar: a silo or bulk-bag continuous mixer is staged on site, the water ratio is set, and mortar/grout/stucco is drawn on demand into tubs and wheelbarrows for the crew all day.

Refractory work in an industrial plant (steel mill, boiler house, cement kiln, incinerator) during a reline or outage: weighing dry castable, plastic or refractory mortar, adding a tightly specified percentage of water, mixing in a pan/paddle mixer or mixer-pump near the vessel, checking ball-in-hand consistency and working within short pot life.

Shop or plant batching: mixing refractory castable for precast shapes, or mortar for prefabricated masonry panels, at a fixed mixing station inside a fabrication shop or plant mix room, with weighed dry components and metered water.

tasks.label: Remove burned or damaged brick or mortar, using sledgehammer, crowbar, chipping gun, or chisel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repointing an existing building facade: cutting/grinding deteriorated mortar out of joints to ~3/4 in. depth without spalling brick arrises, working off a ladder, swing stage or scaffold on an occupied building, dusty, weather-exposed, joint widths and mortar hardness varying course to course.

Cutting out individual spalled, cracked or burned brick units from a standing wall or chimney (often mid-wall) with chisel, chipping gun and small crowbar, breaking the unit out in pieces, cleaning the mortar bed and head joints, and leaving surrounding units undamaged so a replacement brick can be laid.

Partial demolition of a damaged masonry section at a residential or light-commercial site: taking a cracked wall section, parapet or chimney down with sledgehammer and crowbar to sound material, sometimes salvaging brick for reuse, with debris control and adjacent finishes to protect.

Refractory teardown during an industrial shutdown: removing burned, spalled or slagged firebrick and refractory mortar from a boiler, kiln, furnace, riser or ladle lining with chipping gun/jackhammer, in confined, hot, dusty conditions inside a plant, back to the steel shell/anchors ready for relining.

On an active new-construction site, removing a damaged, misplaced or out-of-plumb brick/block from freshly or recently laid work and chipping off hardened mortar droppings and squeeze-out before the wall is closed in.

sources.system: Spatial-AI robotic brickwork deconstruction system (UR20 + Robotnik RB-VOGUI+ mobile platform)
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Dörfler / Leutenegger groups)
sources.title: Robotic Deconstruction of Brickwork Enabled by Spatial Artificial Intelligence (preprint)
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator (UR20 arm on a Robotnik RB-VOGUI+ base with RGB-D camera, pneumatic drill and gripper) autonomously perceived, drilled out the mortar joints around, and extracted individual bricks from a mortar-bound brick wall of unknown geometry in a controlled experimental setup; 55 of 66 bricks were removed, mortar-joint breakage succeeded 82% of the time, ~631 s per brick, with only a safety approval button in the loop that the authors state can be omitted.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (mortar-bound clay bricks) and same physical operation as the task's core: breaking the mortar bond around a brick and freeing the unit from the wall; the paper's mortar-joint-breakage routine is the robotic analogue of chipping mortar with a chisel/chipping gun.

tasks.label: Lay and align bricks, blocks, or tiles to build or repair structures or high temperature equipment, such as cupola, kilns, ovens, or furnaces.

New two- to three-story house, apartment block, school or hotel: mason lays brick facade and/or structural walls on an active site shared with other trades, reaching upper storeys from scaffold, lift or floor decks, tying into openings, lintels and returns.

Repair/alteration of existing masonry on an occupied or standing building: cut out and replace spalled or cracked brick, rebuild a chimney top or parapet, close up or enlarge an opening, patch after other trades, matching existing units, bond and joint profile.

Bespoke small features at homes and landscapes: fireplace and firebox, chimney stack, brick steps and stoops, planters, mailboxes, pier caps and low garden/retaining walls, each a one-off three-dimensional shape built in a yard or interior room.

Refractory work at an industrial plant during a shutdown: laying and aligning firebrick in a kiln, oven, furnace hearth, boiler or steel ladle, in a hot, confined, debris-strewn vessel on the plant's maintenance schedule.

tasks.label: Spray or spread refractory material over brickwork to protect against deterioration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steel melt shop: gunning/spraying refractory over the hot brick lining of a production vessel (BOF converter, EAF hearth/slag line, teeming ladle, tundish) during the short window between heats or in the ladle prep bay. Fixed vessel geometry, known wear zones, laser thickness maps often available, heavy dust/radiant heat.

Plant shutdown/turnaround: gunning or shotcreting monolithic refractory over brickwork inside a large fired vessel — cement/lime kiln and preheater riser, waste-to-energy or utility boiler, blast furnace stack, incinerator. Access through manways and scaffold decks, geometry differs vessel to vessel, partially demolished lining, confined and dusty.

Refinery, foundry, or glass plant: hand-spreading refractory — trowelling plastic refractory, buttering a mortar/coating wash, or hand-gunning a protective layer over newly laid or existing firebrick in a fired heater, cupola, reheat furnace, or flue. Surfaces are curved, cluttered with burners, anchors, and tube penetrations; work is done off ladders and scaffolds.

Commercial/institutional equipment at a customer facility: coating or parging refractory over the brickwork of a crematory retort, bakery/pizza oven, package boiler, or small incinerator. Small chambers, doors and openings only, worker reaches inside to spread the material by hand.

Residential or light-commercial masonry: spreading refractory mortar/coating over the firebox brickwork or smoke chamber of a fireplace, masonry heater, or chimney in an occupied home. Cramped cavity, furnishings and dust protection around it, condition varies house to house.
