roles.title: Stonemasons
roles.description: Build stone structures, such as piers, walls, and abutments. Lay walks, curbstones, or special types of masonry for vats, tanks, and floors.

tasks.label: Set vertical and horizontal alignment of structures, using plumb bob, gauge line, and level.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stone/block wall of a building on an active construction site: mason sets corner leads, plumbs the corners with level and plumb bob, runs a gauge/mason's line between leads, and checks each course to line and level as the wall rises; open site, weather, uneven footing, other trades present.

Free-standing site walls, garden/retaining walls, piers and abutments outdoors: batter and plumb set with line and level (or batter frame), horizontal courses gauged from a datum, heavy irregular or dressed stone placed to that alignment on rough ground.

Flatwork outdoors: walks, patios, steps and curbstones set to grade — string lines and grade stakes pulled from benchmarks, bed screeded, each unit checked with a level for plane, fall and cross-slope, edges aligned to the line.

Stone veneer/cladding on a building facade or interior feature (fireplace, wainscot, column surround): level lines struck around the wall, plumb faces held with line and level, irregular pieces selected, cut and aligned course-by-course against existing framing or backup wall.

Interior flatwork inside a building: stone or large-format slab floors, hearths, and linings for vats/tanks laid to a level datum and gauge lines, checked with straightedge and level over a prepared substrate.

Restoration/repair of existing stone structures: replacement stones and rebuilt sections aligned to surrounding historic work that is itself out of plumb and irregular; alignment references improvised from the existing fabric.

sources.title: Monumental secures $32M Series B to accelerate construction automation - Tech.eu
sources.claim: Monumental operates a fleet of 150+ autonomous bricklaying robots that lay units and mortar to millimetre precision on real construction sites in the Netherlands and UK, having built walls for 100+ homes plus a school, hotel and canal walls — i.e. the robots themselves establish and hold the wall's vertical and horizontal alignment from a digital model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site masonry unit laying. Placing each unit to a modelled position with millimetre error is the machine equivalent of plumbing, gauging and levelling courses with plumb bob, line and level; same on-site environment and same alignment tolerances, though units are regular brick rather than irregular natural stone.

sources.title: Can robots build pretty things? - Monumental (Substack)
sources.claim: Developer account of the same system: three cooperating robots (layer, unit supplier, mortar supplier) autonomously construct brick walls, with a perception/kinematic chain held to sub-millimetre accuracy so final placement error is a few millimetres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wall construction. The article states the alignment problem explicitly — humans use guides and references, the robots use vision and kinematic chains to hold a few-millimetre final error — which is the alignment-setting function of this task.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report (RBR50 2025)
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X mobile blocklaying machine works outdoors in uncontrolled environments, converting a 3D CAD model into block positions and using dynamic stabilisation to place blocks accurately despite boom vibration and wind; five homes were completed in a US demonstration program with CRH ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site wall building from a CAD model. The laser-referenced, dynamically stabilised layhead sets each block's vertical and horizontal position on an open building site, substituting for plumb-bob/gauge-line/level control of wall geometry.

sources.system: HEAP (Hydraulic Excavator for an Autonomous Purpose)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Gramazio Kohler Research, Robotic Systems Lab) with Eberhard AG
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a six-metre-high dry-stone wall | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's autonomous excavator HEAP built a 65 m long, 6 m high dry-stone wall on a real outdoor site (Circularity Park, Oberglatt), scanning and localising multi-tonne boulders and demolition debris and placing each one in the algorithmically determined position without human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ dry stone wall construction with irregular natural stone. The machine holds the wall to a digitally planned face and batter — the alignment function this task performs with line, plumb bob and level — on an unstructured outdoor site.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot (and L3000 scribing robot)
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Partner Robotics' PavePal P900 floor tile paving ... automates indoor laying of large-format floor units (adhesive, placement, levelling) and has completed roughly 100,000 square metres of tiling work on commercial projects, with a companion scribing robot holding 2 mm layout accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying large-format floor units to a level plane and gauge lines. Holding each unit flush and to line over a prepared substrate is the same horizontal-alignment control a mason performs with straightedge, level and line on stone floors and paving.

sources.developer: Red Dot award entry (floor tile paving robot manufacturer)
sources.title: Red Dot Design Award: Floor Tile Paving Robot R-19
sources.claim: A floor tile paving robot recognised by the Red Dot award is described as a fully automated system ... laying large-format floor tiles, using an omni-directional chassis and a four-camera visual measurement and positioning system to place tiles consistently.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated placement of large flat units to a consistent plane and joint line, corroborating that camera-referenced levelling and alignment of floor/paving units is an automated, not teleoperated, capability.

sources.system: Robotic arm system for mortar-joint multi-leaf stone masonry walls
sources.title: Dynamic planning and assembly for constructing mortar-joint multi-leaf stone masonry walls with a robotic arm - IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A laboratory robotic-arm system builds mortar-joint, multi-leaf stone masonry walls, combining stone layout optimisation, vacuum grasping, automated pick-and-place and vision/sensor-guided trajectory correction with a digital twin providing real-time accuracy feedback.
sources.transferJustification: Direct analogue of the task's alignment function for natural stone: the planner and vision correction hold each stone to a planned face plane and course height inside a fixtured robotic cell, i.e. plumb/level control by machine with stones presented to the robot.

tasks.label: Lay out wall patterns or foundations, using straight edge, rule, or staked lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional job site: from drawings, lay out stone or masonry wall lines, corners, control lines and openings on a poured concrete slab, deck, or footing top — pull dimensions with tape/rule, snap chalk lines, check square with diagonals — before setting stone. Hard, printable surface; active trades around.

Open outdoor site, rough-graded subgrade, gravel pad, or asphalt: mark the footprint and pier/footing points for stone piers, abutments, or a foundation wall from plan coordinates; deliverable is painted lines/points (and offsets) used to excavate and set forms. Open sky, machine traffic.

Residential yard/landscape: lay out a garden, seat, or retaining wall, or the edge of a walk or patio, on turf, soil, and slopes among trees, fences, downspouts, and the existing house; drive stakes, run mason's line with a line level, mark curves freehand from a sketch, adapting to found conditions.

Interior of an existing, institution-controlled building (hotel lobby, hospital, school, office fit-out): lay out the base line and pattern for a stone veneer feature wall or a stone floor on a finished, level floor; snap reference lines from column/wall control, work around furniture and occupants, marks must be removable.

Restoration, chimney, or vertical veneer work: lay out course lines, plumb points, and the stone pattern directly on an existing wall, pier, chimney, or sheathed backup using story pole, straightedge, level and rule, scribing to irregular existing masonry and openings.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Layout with Dusty Robotics | Insights | Turner Construction Company
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics FieldPrinter is an autonomous mobile layout robot that prints full-scale building layout lines (wall locations and annotations) from BIM directly onto construction site slabs; field-tested and used by a major general contractor.

sources.title: Dusty Robotics Scales Project Layout Automation | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: The FieldPrinter replaces the mason/carpenter string-line-and-chalk layout method, achieving 1/16-inch accuracy, and had printed tens of millions of square feet of layout for contractors by 2022 — i.e., commercial-scale use on job-site slabs.

sources.title: HP announces autonomous construction layout printing robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is an autonomous layout robot that prints lines, arcs, ... and text of construction layouts onto concrete, tarmac, plywood, pavement, terrazzo, ..., including rough surfaces, on job sites.

sources.title: HP SitePrint A2PS9A - Autonomous Layout Printing Robot - Frontier Precision Shop
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a purchasable commercial product with an ink portfolio spanning tarmac, rough concrete, plywood and formwork and durability from permanent to erasable, positioning it for both new-construction slabs and finished floors.

sources.title: Civ Robotics FAQ | Answering Your Questions on Construction Layout Robots
sources.claim: CivDot/CivDot+ are rugged outdoor layout rovers that autonomously drive to plan coordinates on raw terrain and spray-mark them at ~8 mm accuracy; they have been used in the field by contractors since 2021 on earthworks, roads, foundations and construction staking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stakeout/coordinate marking for civil foundations. It is the same act as a mason's foundation layout — transferring plan geometry to ground marks at comparable (sub-inch) precision on the same outdoor graded surfaces.

sources.title: CivDot Mini, Compact Construction Layout Robot | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: CivDot Mini takes DXF blueprints and autonomously marks solid or dashed layout lines on outdoor paved surfaces (roads, parking lots, airports), explicitly replacing tape and string lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pavement pre-marking/striping. It produces the same output as a mason's chalked or strung wall line — a continuous marked line on the working surface set out from a drawing — on outdoor hard surfaces.

sources.title: Cansel | Tiny Surveyor Robot - Terra Model
sources.claim: TinySurveyor Terra is a commercially sold autonomous survey and stakeout robot for field layout, pre-marking and point ..., marking outdoor sites without a crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor construction stakeout and pre-marking — the same transfer of plan geometry to ground marks that foundation layout requires, on comparable outdoor graded and paved surfaces.

sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 | HOMAG
sources.claim: The WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridge, a gantry machine working over a fixtured panel on a production table, automatically applies predefined layout drawings from the digital data record onto the panel surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic marking of wall-panel layout in a prefabrication cell. It is the same act — drawing the wall's pattern lines on a fixtured, presented workpiece from a digital model at millimetre precision — as marking a veneer pattern on a backup panel.

tasks.label: Set stone or marble in place, according to layout or pattern.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior veneer of uniform cut or manufactured stone units (modular ashlar/coursed patterns) set in a mortar bed over a backup wall on a house or light-commercial building at an active construction site; courses run to line and story pole, joints struck.

Irregular natural stone veneer/facing - fieldstone, ledgestone, rubble - set in mortar on an exterior wall, chimney, column or fireplace; the mason selects each stone from the pallet, trims it with hammer or saw to fit the adjacent stones, butters and beds it, then points the joints.

Dry-stacked / boulder landscape and retaining walls in a yard, park or roadside: heavy irregular stone (100 lb to several tons) placed with machine assistance to a planned line, batter and height, each stone seated for stability against its neighbors.

Mortared landscape stonework and repair: garden and seat walls, steps, piers, wall caps and copings, plus resetting displaced stones or replacing damaged units in existing walls and monuments, at residential and small commercial properties.

Flagstone or cut-paver patios and walkways: units laid to a pattern on a prepared sand or mortar bed in a residential yard or commercial walkway, cut to fit at edges and curves, set to slope for drainage and to consistent joint width.

Interior stone/marble floors, thresholds and stair treads: gauged stone tile and slabs set to a layout in adhesive/mortar on a prepared interior floor in a building under construction or fit-out, with perimeter pieces cut to fit.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Gramazio Kohler Research, Robotic Systems Lab), with Eberhard AG

sources.claim: ETH Zurich's autonomous walking excavator HEAP scanned, grasped and placed irregular boulders to build a six-metre-high, 65-metre-long dry stone wall on an outdoor landscape site, with an algorithm choosing each stone's position and the machine executing the placement itself.

sources.title: Monumental raises $32 million to expand autonomous construction robots
sources.claim: Monumental operates a fleet of autonomous bricklaying robots as a subcontractor on real construction sites, having built the walls of more ... UK plus a school, hotel and canal walls, laying units and mortar to millimetre precision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying masonry units in a mortar bed to a planned coursed layout on an ordinary building site. Coursed cut or manufactured stone veneer uses comparable modular units, comparable joint precision, and the identical construction-site environment.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X mobile blocklaying machine builds block walls outdoors on uncontrolled building sites directly from a 3D CAD model, completing a house's walls in about a day; it completed the first five homes of a US demonstration program with CRH ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing heavy masonry units in courses per a digital layout at an open outdoor building site; comparable unit weight (to 45 kg), placement precision and site conditions to setting coursed dimension-stone units.

sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' R-19 floor tile paving robot is a commercialized, fully automated machine that vacuum-grips large-format tiles, applies cement to the substrate and lays each tile to millimetre precision using a four-camera vision positioning system on an omnidirectional mobile chassis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting large-format units into a fresh mortar/adhesive bed to a planned layout with millimetre joint accuracy. Gauged stone/marble tile and cut pavers are handled the same way (vacuum grip, adhesive bed, level and joint control).

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated indoor laying of large-format units into an adhesive bed on prepared floors; comparable to setting gauged stone/marble floor tile to a layout.

sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' construction robot fleet, which includes the floor tile paving robot among 28 commercialized models, has been used on more than 900 construction projects in China and abroad.
sources.transferJustification: Context for deployment scale of the tile-paving robots cited above; autonomy of individual machines not established in this source, so used only as supporting context.

sources.system: Robotic arm system for mortar-joint multi-leaf stone masonry walls (research prototype)
sources.developer: academic research group (abstract indexed alongside ETH dry-stone work)
sources.title: A framework for robotic excavation and dry stone construction using on-site materials | Request PDF (ResearchGate, related-work abstract)
sources.claim: A published robotic-arm system automates construction of mortar-joint, multi-leaf stone ..., combining stone layout optimization, sequence planning, vacuum grasping and vision-corrected automated pick-and-place of the stones.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (setting stones in mortar per an optimized layout) but demonstrated with a fixed robotic arm and stones presented to it, i.e. a purpose-built cell rather than a jobsite.

sources.developer: academic research team (Journal of Building Engineering)
sources.title: A scheme of installing ALC wall panels based on autonomous mobile robot - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A prototype autonomous mobile robot for installing ALC wall panels on building sites identifies panels, grasps, transports, adjusts and places them, navigating and avoiding obstacles by itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping, transporting and placing large heavy building units to a planned position, comparable to setting large stone units/copings once they are presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Remove wedges, fill joints between stones, finish joints between stones, using a trowel, and smooth the mortar to an attractive finish, using a tuck pointer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential exterior stone veneer (thin or full-bed) on a new or remodeled house: after stones are set and shims/wedges pulled, the mason bags or trowels mortar into irregular joints of varying width, packs and tools them with a tuck pointer/jointer to the specified profile, then brushes off and cleans smears from the stone faces. Work is from ladders, scaffold or grade, outdoors, in variable weather with mortar setting on a clock.

Landscape/hardscape stonework at a residence or park: garden and retaining walls, piers, columns, steps, mailbox pillars built of rough or split fieldstone. Joints of highly irregular width are filled and struck/raked or weathered, with cleanup on uneven ground amid plantings and existing structures.

Commercial or institutional dimension-stone / cast-stone cladding on a building facade: setting shims and lead wedges are removed once the mortar has set, joints are raked to depth, pointed with matched mortar, and tooled to a uniform concave or flush profile from scaffold or a mast-climber, meeting architect-specified joint width and color.

Interior stone work in a home or building under construction: fireplace surrounds, feature walls, stone floors and hearths. Joints are pointed and tooled in tight quarters near finished surfaces, with strict cleanliness requirements and hand-matched color for visible feature joints.

Restoration/repointing of existing historic stone masonry (church, monument, campus building, old retaining wall): deteriorated mortar raked out, joints of widely varying width and depth repacked with lime mortar in lifts, then tooled and brushed to match the historic profile, texture and color, working from scaffold on an aged, irregular wall.

sources.title: University Arts Building construction first in Nevada to use bricklaying robot
sources.claim: SAM100, the commercially deployed semi-automated masonry robot, lays brick and applies mortar on site, but human masons must clean and tool the mortar joints; the robot does not point or finish joints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: brick masonry joint finishing. Brick and stone pointing use the same mortar, tools (trowel, tuck pointer/jointer) and quality standard; the robot's inability to tool joints in the easier, regular-unit brick case bounds what is available for irregular stone joints.

sources.title: 6 Examples of Robotic Bricklaying and On-Site Assembly in Construction - Neuroject
sources.claim: Trade review of robotic bricklaying confirms SAM is an assistant: skilled human crew handle finishing tasks including tooling the mortar joints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tooling mortar joints in brickwork, the same operation with the same tools and mortar as stone joint finishing; the cited system explicitly leaves it to humans.

sources.title: Bricklaying robot startup Monumental emerges from stealth with $25 million funding round | Fortune
sources.claim: Monumental's autonomous bricklaying robots lay brick with real mortar on active construction sites, but a human mason still performs the pointing and smoothing of the mortar.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling and smoothing mortar joints in masonry walls. It is the same operation the stonemason task describes; the most advanced site masonry robot cannot do it.

sources.system: Monumental bricklaying robot fleet (Huissen, Hengelo projects)
sources.title: Monumental wil met €32 miljoen de VS veroveren met metselrobots | MT/Sprout
sources.claim: As of July 2026, Monumental's robots on live projects still have their joints struck by the human operator who supervises the robot; automating that step remains work in progress.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: striking/pointing mortar joints in masonry. Current-dated confirmation that no deployed masonry robot finishes joints; the capability is stated as future work, which cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: SMB Geveltechniek with TU Delft Robotics minor students / RoboHouse
sources.title: Delftse voegrobot voegt innovatie toe aan de bouwsector | Omroep Delft
sources.claim: A dedicated facade pointing robot (voegrobot) that applies mortar, smooths and brushes joints is at student-prototype stage with a Dutch facade contractor; it is not a deployed, worker-quality system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (filling and smoothing masonry joints), but only a prototype under development; autonomy and output quality are not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Robotic arm system for mortar-joint multi-leaf stone masonry walls
sources.developer: EPFL (Earthquake Engineering and Structural Dynamics group) / research consortium
sources.title: Dynamic planning and assembly for constructing mortar-joint multi-leaf stone masonry walls with a robotic arm (IEEE)
sources.claim: A laboratory robotic arm can autonomously place irregular natural stones in wet mortar to build a small multi-leaf masonry wall of comparable structural quality to mason-built walls; the reported work covers stone placement and packing, not pointing or tooling the visible joints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stone laying with wet mortar in a fixed robot cell. It shows the closest purpose-built-setting capability for stone with mortar, yet contains no demonstration of filling, tooling or finishing the face joints, bounding E1 capability for this task.

tasks.label: Clean excess mortar or grout from surface of marble, stone, or monument, using sponge, brush, water, or acid.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stone veneer or solid stone wall on an active construction site: as the wall goes up, the mason brushes and sponges green mortar smears, droppings and joint squeeze-out off irregular, textured face stone, working from ladder or scaffold with a bucket of water; weather, dust and site clutter vary by the hour.

Interior dimensional-stone tile or slab floor during finish-out of a building: after grouting, the worker sponges and rinses excess grout and haze off the stone in several passes, changing water, working around doorways, drains and pipe penetrations in an unfinished, cluttered space.

Final cleandown of a cured exterior stone or masonry wall: masking/wetting adjacent surfaces, applying dilute muriatic acid or a proprietary masonry cleaner with brush or sprayer, scrubbing stubborn mortar, then pressure-rinsing top-down from scaffold or lift, judging when the stone is clean without burning or bleaching it.

Shop or yard work on monuments and cut-stone units: cleaning excess setting mortar, grout and adhesive residue from faces, joints and lettered surfaces of headstones, bases, sills and copings resting on benches, pallets or carts before delivery or after setting the die on its base.

Detail cleanup in an occupied or finished home: hearth and fireplace surround, stone countertop or shower curb and entry steps; wiping mortar and grout residue off polished or honed stone in a furnished room while protecting adjacent floors, trim and fixtures.

sources.system: Fabrica AI autonomous tile grouting robot (V5)
sources.developer: Fabrica Robotics Pte Ltd (Fabrica AI), Singapore
sources.title: Fabrica Robotics Pte. Ltd. | Career Nexus 2026 (Singapore Institute of Technology)
sources.claim: Fabrica AI's autonomous tile grouting robot both applies grout and cleans excess grout off floor tiles, running unsupervised; humans only move it between rooms, reload grout and change water.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grouting and washing down floor tile. The physical act judged here is identical to the stonemason's - removing cementitious grout/mortar residue from a hard mineral surface with water and a scrubbing/wiping head - on comparable flat dimensional units in the same finish-out environment.

sources.title: Grouting robot | Fabrica AI
sources.claim: The grouting-and-cleaning robot is a sold product, not a lab demo: sales in Singapore and Australia with roughly 180,000 sqft ... pilots begun in the US.

sources.title: Fabrica Robotics - Singapore | SGInnovate
sources.claim: The grouting/cleaning robots operate on real construction sites under major contractors, i.e. in buildings under construction rather than in a lab or structured facility.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (grout application plus wash-down); cited here to establish the environment in which the cleaning is performed.

sources.system: Bianchi Brushing Machine (spazzolatrice) for long-line tables and pallets
sources.title: Automatic Machines for Precast Panels | Bianchi Casseforme
sources.claim: A commercial plant machine automatically removes hardened cementitious residue from flat casting surfaces using a scraper and a full-width rotating brush, with optional side brushes, under machine control in a precast panel production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of concrete/mortar residue from a flat work surface presented to the machine on a plant line. Transfers to cleaning mortar smears from stone units when those units are fixtured and conveyed to the cleaning station, the E1 counterfactual - same residue, same brush-and-water removal mechanism, same purpose-built line.

sources.title: 6 Axis Robot Arm for Stone Polishing | DINOSAW Robotic Grinder
sources.claim: Six-axis robot arms are sold for contact surface work on fixtured marble, granite and limestone pieces including tombstones and countertops, with adaptive force control keeping the tool aligned to the stone surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled abrasive surface finishing of fixtured monuments and countertops. It establishes that a machine can hold and track a contact tool over the exact stone geometries in this task inside a purpose-built cell; substituting a brush/sponge and water for the abrasive head is the same motion and lighter contact.

sources.title: Robotic Masonry Is Helping to Fill the Skilled Labor Gap - Construction Executive
sources.claim: The leading on-site masonry robot cannot clean its own work: SAM100 lays brick while human masons follow behind to clean up the mortar.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point as negative evidence for in-situ wall clean-down: the only widely used on-site masonry robot leaves mortar cleaning to humans.

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous at-height facade cleaning is deployed on high-rise buildings, but the deployed system cleans glass windows from a building maintenance unit, not mortar residue off stone.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to bound the negative judgment on exterior stone wall cleaning: the nearest deployed at-height cleaning robot handles flat glazing with squeegee/brush, not selective removal of hardened mortar from irregular stone faces.

tasks.label: Shape, trim, face and cut marble or stone preparatory to setting, using power saws, cutting equipment, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Jobsite trimming/fitting of veneer or wall stone while a wall or chimney is being built: mason measures the gap in the partly built wall, carries pieces to a wet masonry saw set up on site, cuts them to size and angle, then nips or chisels edges so the piece seats in that spot. Dusty, wet, weather-exposed, layout changes as the wall rises.

Hand shaping/dressing of irregular fieldstone or rubble on site with hammer, pitching tool and chisel: knocking off a corner, squaring a bed, creating a face on a rough stone selected from a pile so it fits a particular found gap in a dry-stack or mortared wall.

Shop or stone-yard sawing of dimension stone to a cut list: slabs and blocks of granite, limestone or marble cut into sills, treads, caps, hearths, cladding panels or countertops on a bridge saw / CNC sawjet from templates and shop drawings, then edged and stacked for delivery to the setting crew.

On-site cutting of flagstone, pavers, cobbles and curbstone for walks, patios and curbs: straight cuts, curved closures and split faces made with a jobsite masonry saw, splitter or hand set, sized against the laid course.

Shop shaping/facing/profiling of architectural or restoration stone that can be fully machine finished: running moldings and chamfers, mitered returns, tooled or sawn faces, lettering and plain profiles on limestone or marble units before setting.

Shop carving/facing of ornamental or figurative stone for restoration and facade work where accepted output requires hand-finished detail matched to existing historic stonework (foliate capitals, gargoyles, weathered profile matching).

sources.system: BACA Systems Autocut Line (Robo SawJet + Robo Lift, KUKA robots)
sources.title: Autocut Line — Automated Systems | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA Systems' Autocut Line is a commercial robotic stone-cutting cell in which a robot loads and unloads slabs on Robo SawJet tables, cutting programmed parts from granite/quartz/natural stone slabs at about 2,000 sq ft per shift ... a single operator.

sources.system: Park Industries TITAN Fab Center (CNC saw + router)
sources.title: TITAN CNC Fab Center | Saw + Router Machine for Countertops
sources.claim: Park Industries' TITAN Fab Center is a widely deployed CNC saw+router that, once a slab is fixtured on its table and the program scanned in, cuts, miters, shapes, edges and polishes stone parts to finished dimension under machine control.

sources.title: AI robots can already carve stone statues. Entire buildings are next
sources.claim: Monumental Labs runs seven-axis robotic carving arms at a New York plant that cut granite, limestone and marble into decorative architectural stone; delivered restoration work at Carnegie Hall and the Frick was mostly robot-cut, with trained carvers doing the hand finishing.

sources.claim: Robotor's stone-carving robots in Carrara generate their own toolpaths from a 3D model and shape marble blocks with diamond tooling without operator programming; they are sold as production machines for stone machining and sculpture.

sources.system: Robotic milling workflow for dry-stacked non-standard limestone assemblies
sources.developer: Lu, Zhu, Perutxet Olesti, Scully, Devadass (Construction Robotics, Springer)

tasks.label: Mix mortar or grout and pour or spread mortar or grout on marble slabs, stone, or foundation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/commercial jobsite: mason mixes a batch of Type N/S mortar in a paddle mixer or mortar box, then spreads bed joints on the poured footing/foundation and butters irregular natural stone as a veneer wall, pier or chimney goes up; outdoor, weather-variable, mix consistency judged by eye and adjusted per stone.

Building interior (fit-out or renovation): mason mixes thinset/setting mortar in a bucket with a drill mixer, spreads it with a notched trowel on the slab or scratch coat and back-butters marble/granite slabs or stone tile for a floor, fireplace surround or wall cladding.

Grouting newly set stone: mason mixes grout or pointing mortar and spreads/packs it over and into the joints of set stone or marble (floors, veneer, treads), then strikes and cleans the surface before it sets.

Restoration/repointing: mason mixes lime or custom-matched mortar in small batches and packs it into the raked joints of an existing historic stone wall, working from staging on a facade of varying joint widths and stone profiles.

Hardscape/flatwork: mason mixes mortar on site and spreads beds for steps, wall caps, curbstones and flagstone patios in a yard or streetscape, adjusting bed thickness on uneven ground for irregular stone thickness.

Fabrication shop or yard: mason/fabricator mixes grout, epoxy or setting mortar and pours it into anchor pockets and dowel holes, fills panel joints, or spreads filler/adhesive on marble slabs at a bench in a controlled shop.

tasks.label: Construct and install prefabricated masonry units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop/plant fabrication of prefabricated masonry units: brick or thin-stone slips and full units bonded with adhesive/mortar onto precast concrete backing or steel/timber-frame panels in a panel yard, working to shop drawings, then pointed, cured and racked for shipping.

Crane-set installation of large prefabricated stone/precast masonry panels on a commercial building frame: rigging and hoisting the panel, guiding it onto brackets/anchors, shimming and plumbing, bolting or welding connections, grouting and sealing joints, working from swing stage or lift at height on an active construction site.

On-site setting of precast/cast-stone trim units - copings, sills, caps, band courses, treads - on existing or newly built walls: units cut and fitted to length, bedded in mortar, aligned to string and level, dowelled/anchored, joints pointed and cleaned, outdoors in variable weather.

Residential installation of manufactured/prefabricated stone veneer panel systems over flat wall areas and wainscots (lath/scratch coat or panel clips, adhered units, corner pieces), inside or outside an occupied or under-construction house.

Prefabricated units on three-dimensional features in homes: fireplace surrounds and hearths, column and post wraps, mailbox/pier kits, chimney chases - fitting curved and mitred corner units to varying substrates in tight interior spaces.

Erecting walls and site elements from large prefabricated block/precast units on a prepared foundation at an outdoor construction or landscape site: large-format CMU/AAC block walls, precast steps, planters, segmental retaining-wall units, placed with mechanical assist and bonded with adhesive or mortar.

tasks.label: Smooth, polish, and bevel surfaces, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop or yard bench work on flat cut pieces: chamfering/beveling and polishing the exposed edges and faces of countertops, window sills, stair treads, wall caps, coping and thin veneer before delivery. Pieces are loaded onto a bench or machine table; straight and standard profile edges; wet grinding/polishing with progressive diamond pads.

Shop finishing of shaped, curved or carved pieces: bullnosed column drums, radius corners, sink aprons, molding runs, hearths, memorial markers and decorative carved elements. Complex 3D geometry, hand-held grinder/polisher or profiling machine, finish must be uniform over compound curves.

Job-site cut-and-fit finishing: after a piece is cut on site with a wet saw or grinder to fit a corner, jamb, outlet or riser, the mason eases/bevels the raw cut arris and polishes or hones the newly exposed face to match, working at the site cut station or tailgate, then sets the piece.

In-place dressing of already-set stonework: grinding mortar smears and lippage flush, knocking down high spots, smoothing a rough spot on a laid wall, pier, sill or step, and chamfering exposed arrises after setting. Work is at odd heights and angles, in situ, on scaffolding or kneeling, in weather and with other trades around.

In-place surface honing and polishing of large laid areas: grinding and polishing a laid stone or terrazzo floor, threshold or stair run, or refinishing a marble surface, including the field, perimeter edges, corners and around columns and door jambs, to a uniform gloss.

tasks.label: Lay brick to build shells of chimneys and smokestacks or to line or reline industrial furnaces, kilns, boilers and similar installations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reline the interior of a steel-mill vessel (ladle, converter, or torpedo car) with refractory brick in the plant's relining bay: vessel cooled and old lining removed, thousands of shaped magnesia/alumina bricks laid in tight rings up the cylindrical wall and bottom with near-zero joint thickness, on a schedule dictated by vessel turnaround.

Reline a rotary kiln (cement, lime) or similar cylindrical furnace during a plant outage: keyed refractory brick laid in rings inside a horizontal rotating shell, bricks held overhead against gravity with jacks/rigs until the ring keys, dusty and hot confined-space conditions with kiln rotation between rings.

Firebrick lining or patch relining of a boiler, incinerator, heat-treat furnace or process heater at an industrial plant: planar walls, floors, sprung arches, burner and tube penetrations laid with refractory mortar and anchors, work done inside the unit during a shutdown with scaffolding and cut-to-fit brick.

Build or rebuild the brick shell of an industrial chimney/smokestack or flue breeching: radial/tapered brickwork laid course by course from scaffolding or a climbing platform, outdoors at height, exposed to weather, with the geometry set out on site.

Build a residential or light-commercial masonry chimney shell in brick from the firebox/foundation up through and above the roof: flue liners set as the shell rises, corbelling, crown, flashing tie-ins, working off scaffold and roof at an occupied or active house site.

Line a fireplace firebox, wood-stove surround, or small chimney breast with firebrick, or make a localized brick repair to an existing chimney/flue: splayed and cut brick, tight refractory joints, confined access inside a dwelling.

tasks.label: Replace broken or missing masonry units in walls or floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior building wall: replace cracked, spalled, or fallen stone/masonry units in a stone veneer or solid stone wall on a house or small commercial building. Mason cuts the damaged unit out with grinder and chisel, rakes the surrounding mortar, cleans the pocket, cuts and shapes a replacement stone to fit the irregular void, beds it in mortar from a ladder or scaffold, points and tools the joints to match the surrounding work, then cleans the face. Weather, dust, and adjacent sound units that must not be damaged.

Landscape stone wall repair: reset or replace broken/missing stones in a dry-laid or mortared garden, seat, or retaining wall on residential or park property. Mason dismantles the loose or bulged section by hand, sorts salvageable stones, selects or trims new stones to fit irregular gaps, sets hearting and through-stones or beds units in mortar, and rebuilds to line. Uneven ground, vegetation, no two stones alike.

Residential flatwork: replace broken flagstones, pavers, or steps in a patio, walkway, or entry stair at a private home. Mason lifts out the cracked unit, chips away old mortar or excavates the sand/setting bed, re-screeds or re-beds, cuts a matching-thickness replacement (color and cleft face matched to weathered neighbors), sets it flush to adjoining units, and re-grouts or sweeps joint sand.

Historic/heritage restoration: replace deteriorated stone units (or install Dutchman patches) in a church, monument, courthouse, or landmark facade. Unit is cut out without damaging adjacent historic fabric, a replacement is quarried/carved to match profile and tooling, set in lime mortar with shims and pins, and joints are pointed and finished to match. Scaffold access, conservator specifications, irregular original geometry.

Institution-controlled exterior hardscape: replace cracked granite pavers, plaza slabs, curbstones, or stair treads at a campus, transit station, hospital entry, or municipal building during a scheduled maintenance window. Fixed layout, standard unit sizes from a known supplier, premises controlled and pedestrians routed around a barricaded work zone; still requires cutting out the failed unit, prepping the bed, setting, and jointing.

Interior stone floors and walls in a commercial or institutional building (hotel lobby, hospital corridor, office atrium): replace cracked marble/granite tiles or wall panels. Mason cuts out grout, removes the broken slab and old thinset without damaging neighbors, sets a matched replacement in thinset to plane with adjoining slabs, grouts, and blends the polish/finish. Occupied building, dust control, tight tolerances on lippage.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report

sources.claim: ETH Zurich's autonomous excavator HEAP scanned and placed multi-tonne boulders to build a new 6 m high, 65 m long dry-stone wall at an outdoor site; it builds a wall from scratch with heavy boulders rather than replacing broken or missing units in an existing wall.

Object scale (tonne boulders vs. hand-set stones), coarse fit tolerances, and the absence of any selective-removal or joint-finishing capability mean it does not carry over to replacing individual damaged units in an existing wall.

tasks.label: Remove sections of monument from truck bed, and guide stone onto foundation, using skids, hoist, or truck crane.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard upright cemetery monument (granite base plus die, roughly 300–1,500 lb in two or three pieces) delivered on a boom/crane truck that drives across turf to the grave plot in an active, maintained memorial-park cemetery; worker rigs the base with straps or a clamp, swings it off the truck bed onto the poured foundation, beds it, then hoists and hand-guides the polished die onto the base with setting compound, checking level, plumb and centering, and cleaning squeeze-out.

Flat granite or bronze-on-granite marker or small slant marker (roughly 100–400 lb) moved off the truck bed with skids, a two-wheel cart or a small tripod hoist because the plot is off the road; set on a foundation or compacted bed and leveled flush with the sod so mowers pass over it, in a maintained cemetery.

Large or multi-piece memorial — family monument, obelisk, mausoleum or columbarium components, sections of one to several tons — set with a truck crane in an older, tight or sloping cemetery: hand-signaled boom work between existing stones and trees, dowels/pins and epoxy between courses, shimming and plumbing of tall sections, on soft or uneven ground.

Monument sections unloaded from the delivery truck at the monument shop or fenced yard using an overhead hoist, gantry, forklift or jib crane, and staged on A-frames, pallets or a shop base for lettering, polishing or pre-assembly; indoor/paved, controlled premises.

Civic or architectural memorial component (statue base, cut-stone panels, veterans memorial die, park monument) crane-lifted from a flatbed and guided onto a prepared foundation at a public plaza, park or streetside site, with pedestrians, traffic control, and site-specific access constraints.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up and precisely setting down heavy, fragile polished granite pieces. Same material and comparable weights to monument sections; performance carries to setting a monument section when the piece and its base are presented in fixed, known positions inside a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Drill holes in marble or ornamental stone and anchor brackets in holes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stone/countertop fabrication shop prep: fabricator lays a marble, granite or quartz panel on a bench or machine table, lays out and drills dowel, kerf-pin or undercut 'back-bolt' holes in the edges or back face, blows them out and epoxies or screws in the anchor pins, straps or support brackets before the piece ships. Standard slab thicknesses, shop power, water-cooled diamond bits.

Interior stone cladding on a commercial jobsite under construction (lobby wall panels, marble toilet-partition stalls, column covers): mason scribes each panel to as-built conditions, drills anchor holes in the panel edges with a handheld or portable drill, and sets strap anchors/brackets in the holes with epoxy or lead before hanging the panel. Dusty, cluttered, other trades present.

Exterior stone veneer / facade panel setting from scaffold, swing stage or boom lift: drill kerf, dowel or clip anchor holes in the stone panels and anchor the brackets/clips in the holes, working at height in outdoor weather with panels staged on the deck.

Residential or occupied-space work: drill into marble/ornamental stone that is already set in place (countertop underside for a hidden bracket rod, vanity, fireplace surround, stair tread, wall panel) and epoxy in threaded rods or support brackets, working in a customer's home around finished surfaces and furnishings.

Field repair, restoration and monument work: drill holes in existing weathered or historic stone (cornice, coping, balustrade, headstone/monument die) in a cemetery or on a building, and anchor pins, cramps or brackets in the holes with epoxy, matching irregular existing conditions.

sources.title: SPARTAN™ | Sink & Seam CNC Router for Stone Fabrication
sources.claim: Commercially sold stone-shop CNC routers machine fixtured marble/granite/quartz pieces under program control, including coring holes and drilling anchor holes, with a 19-position automatic tool changer.
sources.transferJustification: Same task half in the same material: drilling anchor holes in fixtured marble/granite/quartz to shop tolerances; the operator loads and starts, the machine executes the drilling cycle.

sources.system: KEIL undercut anchor system (KEIL drill bits on CNC machining centers)

sources.transferJustification: Directly the drilling half of this task on ornamental stone facade panels, showing that the industry's anchor holes are routinely produced by programmed machines on fixtured panels rather than by hand.

sources.system: HOMAG DRILLTEQ D-110 / D-510 drilling and dowel-inserting CNC machine

sources.transferJustification: Related task (panel doweling) covering the second half of this task: machine-controlled drilling of a hole in a fixtured panel edge and automatic setting of an adhesive-bonded pin in that hole - the same geometry, hole diameters and tight tolerances as anchoring a dowel or bracket leg in a stone panel edge.

sources.system: WEINIG UniPin drilling and dowel inserting machine

sources.transferJustification: Related task: in a purpose-built cell a machine drills a hole in a fixtured panel and installs/sets a fastener in that hole to tighter tolerances than stone anchoring requires, showing the combined drill-then-anchor cycle is a solved E1 operation.

sources.title: robot chisel in italy carves detailed marble sculptures like a real artist

sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic marble machining) showing multi-axis robots hold tool-path accuracy in ornamental marble without wrecking it, supporting the drilling half of this task inside a fixtured robotic cell.

sources.title: Baubot Robot Breaks Guinness World Record for Most Holes Drilled in 24 Hours | Equipment World
sources.claim: A semi-autonomous tracked construction robot drills anchor holes in concrete from a BIM plan and sets anchors; used on tunnel projects to place handrail and pipe anchors, and it drilled 3,717 holes in 24 ... a record attempt.
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-site drill-and-anchor system, but it percussion-drills plan-located holes in structural concrete in tunnels; it is not evidence for water-cooled diamond drilling of finished marble or ornamental stone, where hole placement is set by fitting the piece and any spalling ruins visible work.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: A semi-autonomous mobile jobsite robot locates itself from BIM data and drills overhead anchor holes in concrete, with anchor installation still done by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (jobsite anchor-hole drilling) showing what is fielded today: hole drilling only, in concrete, from a digital plan - it does not set the anchor and is not used on marble or ornamental stone.

tasks.label: Dig trench for foundation of monument, using pick and shovel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Established cemetery: hand-dug foundation excavation for a headstone or family monument in an occupied section - a hole/trench roughly 3-8 ft long dug to frost depth, squeezed between adjacent memorials and existing graves, sod cut and set aside for replacement, spoil kept off neighboring lots, narrow drive lanes and trees limiting access.

New monument or memorial on open, machine-accessible ground: a new cemetery section, park, campus plaza or active construction site where the footing trench is excavated to staked lines and depth per plan, with no fragile neighbors within reach and room for a machine to work.

Private residence or garden job: trench for a small monument, sign base, or stone pier/wall footing dug amid plantings, fences, patios, irrigation lines and shallow utilities; access through a gate or side yard; sod and beds must be protected.

Difficult ground: rocky or root-bound soil, buried rubble/old fill, or frozen winter ground, where the small excavation is advanced with pick, bar and shovel; frequent obstruction breaking and hand mucking.

Repair or reset work: excavating alongside an existing sunken monument, curbing or wall footing to expose and underpin it, hand-digging within inches of finished stone that must not be chipped or shifted.

sources.system: Kawasaki Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators
sources.title: Kawasaki Develops "Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators", Achieved "Autonomous Operation" for Trench Excavation at Construction and Civil Engineering Sites
sources.claim: Kawasaki's Autonomous Excavation System plans and executes trench digging from 3D design data and LiDAR terrain sensing, autonomously excavating a 2 m x 0.6 m x 10 m trench and also leveling and compacting the trench floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is trench excavation to a 3D design; a monument foundation trench is the same operation in in-situ soil (an open cut to a specified line and depth, ready for concrete), at smaller scale and with comparable centimetre-level depth tolerance.

sources.claim: Built Robotics' aftermarket Exosystem converts a standard excavator into a fully autonomous trenching robot that digs to a planned trench profile with no operator in the ..., using geofences and exclusion zones for safety.
sources.transferJustification: Trenching for buried cable is the same physical operation as digging a foundation trench: an open cut in in-situ soil to a planned depth and alignment, performed outdoors on as-found ground.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous excavators (Bechtel solar projects)

tasks.label: Repair cracked or chipped areas of stone or marble, using blowtorch and mastic, and remove rough or defective spots from concrete, using power grinder or chisel and hammer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-place repair of chipped or cracked stone/marble in finished interiors (kitchen and bath countertops, floor tiles, thresholds, stair treads, fireplace surrounds) in occupied homes, hotels and offices: clean the void, mix and tint mastic/epoxy to match the stone, warm it with a torch or heat gun, fill, cure, then grind and polish flush by hand so the repair is invisible; furniture, occupants and finished adjacent surfaces must be protected.

Exterior stone repair on building facades, steps, walls, monuments and cemetery markers: cut or grind out the spalled/defective area with a small grinder or chisel and hammer, then patch chips and cracks with mastic/composite patching compound tinted to the stone, shape and dress it flush, working off ladders, lifts or scaffold in weather with variable stone types and unknown deterioration.

Repair of stone slabs and cut units in a fabrication shop or supply yard before installation: fissures, chips and corner breaks in marble, granite or limestone are filled with resin/mastic, cured, then ground and polished flat; pieces are moved by crane/A-frame and worked on saw horses or benches in a shop the employer controls.

Removal of rough or defective spots from cast-in-place concrete on an active construction site: grinding off form fins, offsets and high spots on walls, columns, curbs and slab edges with an angle grinder, and chipping out honeycombed or unsound concrete with chisel and hammer so the area can be patched, before stone or masonry is set against it; obstructions, rebar, other trades and changing access.

Grinding down a concrete floor or deck surface inside a completed, enclosed facility (parking garage, warehouse, plant floor, building being fitted out): removing laitance, high spots and rough patches over broad areas with a walk-behind or ride-on grinder so a topping, stone setting bed or coating can go down; premises controlled by the owner, layout fixed and swept clear.

sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the stone half of this task — filling cracks/voids in marble and granite with a curing filler and returning a finished surface — but with the slab brought to the machine.

sources.title: IonBreton | Resin Line For Repair Marble Granite Slabs
sources.claim: IonBreton is marketed as an automatic resin line whose purpose is repairing and restoring marble or granite slabs, including epoxy addition in a second pass to fill cracks and voids revealed after the first application.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the stone-repair half of the task (filling cracks and voids in marble/granite), performed on slabs presented to a fixed line.

sources.system: Monumental Labs robotic stone-carving cells (KUKA 7-axis arms)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grinding/carving of marble and limestone to a modeled geometry. sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stone machining of blocks in a fixed cell; transfers to grinding out defective or damaged stone areas on units brought to the machine (same materials, abrasive/milling tooling, fine tolerances).

sources.claim: Trade press reports the same fully automatic robotic grinding line for precast concrete elements in production, producing cleanly sanded, non-slip concrete surfaces that were previously done by hand.

sources.claim: Xingyi sells autonomous floor grinders (AT8/AT10) with the ATLAS FSG system that self-navigate a concrete floor, plan paths, detect obstacles and grind the full area with regulated pressure, without an operator walking the machine.

sources.title: Automated Floor grinding & dust collection robot
sources.claim: Legend Robot markets a floor grinding robot with intelligent path planning and integrated dust collection that performs fully automated grinding of concrete floors in parking garages, factory workshops and similar facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated abrasive removal of the top layer and rough spots of hardened concrete floors inside controlled facilities, the same removal operation this task specifies with a power grinder.

sources.title: Automated Concrete Removal and Demolition | Conjet
sources.claim: Conjet's ACR hydrodemolition robots remove unsound/deteriorated concrete from bridges, parking decks, dams and tunnels; the operator sets removal parameters and the machine then runs the removal automatically while being supervised from a distance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site removal of defective concrete from structures. It bears on the field concrete instance but covers only bulk removal to depth with high-pressure water, not small-area grinding of fins and high spots with a hand grinder.

tasks.label: Position mold along guidelines of wall, press mold in place, and remove mold and paper from wall.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential exterior: mason applies simulated/composition-stone facing to a house foundation, chimney, entry column or porch base. A paper-lined mold filled with stone mixture (or a texture mat over a fresh overlay) is aligned to chalked guidelines on the parged wall, pressed home by hand/tamping, then the mold is stripped and the treated paper peeled off. Outdoors, uneven ground, ladders/planks, weather and set-time judgment.

Commercial or institutional job on an active construction site: feature wall in a lobby, storefront base course, or exterior accent band. Work from scaffold or lift, other trades and debris present, layout lines snapped from architect's elevations, repeated mold placements must be offset/rotated so the finished pattern reads naturally.

Interior of a private home: fireplace surround or accent wall in an occupied or partly renovated house. Tight, furnished space, floors and trim masked, small molds pressed against a vertical (and sometimes overhead/return) surface, cast units and paper removed without staining adjacent finishes.

Outdoor landscape/hardscape walls: garden and retaining walls, pool surrounds, outdoor kitchens and pillars. Curved and battered faces, corners and caps, soil/mulch underfoot, sun and wind changing the set time of the mix during mold pressing and stripping.

Shop or plant work: the same mold-cast facing applied to wall panels, precast units or mock-up boards lying on benches/casting beds in a fabricator's shop or precast yard, with material staged, lighting and temperature controlled, and pieces moved by hoist.

sources.system: Elematic EDGE / PRO Double Wall shuttering and de-shuttering robots (E9)
sources.title: Precast wall production | EDGE Double Wall | Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Elematic's automated precast wall lines use shuttering and de-shuttering robots that pick mold/shutter profiles from storage and place them on the wall mold table to the programmed layout, magnet-clamp them, and after casting scan and strip them off the finished wall panel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and stripping molds/formwork on a wall element in a precast plant. It carries over the same verbs as this task — position a mold to layout coordinates on a wall workpiece, clamp it in place, later remove it from the hardened wall — with mm-level accuracy on comparable mold-sized objects, in the purpose-built environment the E1 counterfactual assumes. It does not cover peeling treated paper.

sources.system: Progress Maschinen & Automation shuttering robot (ebos control)
sources.title: Shuttering Robot | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Shuttering robots in precast plants select and position mold/shutter elements driven directly by CAD data, i.e. they set molds to digital 'guidelines' without an operator marking or aligning them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CAD-guided mold placement on precast wall pallets. It substantiates the 'position mold along guidelines' element of this task at production precision inside a purpose-built plant cell.

sources.system: Rimac / Global Machine Market 'Hybrid' Level 2 wet cast slab machine system
sources.title: Level 2 Wet Cast Slab Machine (Medium) - Global Machine Market
sources.claim: Commercial wet-cast production lines automatically dose molds with concrete/stone mixture and automatically demold cast stone and veneer stone units, with mold and product handling stacked/unstacked automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling molds with composition-stone mixture and stripping the mold from the cast unit — the same materials, mold release behaviour and set-time window as the mason's paper-lined mold, performed under machine control in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Airborne Automated Ply Placement (APP) robotic cells
sources.title: Automated Ply Placement - Airborne
sources.claim: Robotic ply-placement cells pick flexible sheet material, place it with high precision, and automatically remove the protective backing paper or ... from the placed layer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise placement of a flexible sheet onto a substrate plus automated peeling of its backing paper. This substantiates the 'remove paper' step of this task — peeling a treated paper liner off a freshly placed layer without disturbing it — in a purpose-built robotic cell.

sources.title: OKIBO-Smart Robots For Construction Sites
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous wall-working robots deployed on real construction sites apply and smooth plaster/joint compound; they map the site with 3D scanning and work alongside trades, but they only deposit material and do not handle, press or strip molds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of cementitious material to walls on site. It shows what site-level (E2/E3) autonomy covers — spraying and smoothing — and it does not extend to positioning a filled mold to guidelines, pressing it against the wall, stripping it and peeling the paper, so it cannot support a positive judgment for this task.

roles.title: Carpenters
roles.description: Construct, erect, install, or repair structures and fixtures made of wood and comparable materials, such as concrete forms; building frameworks, including partitions, joists, studding, and rafters; and wood stairways, window and door frames, and hardwood floors. May also install cabinets, siding, drywall, and batt or roll insulation. Includes brattice builders who build doors or brattices (ventilation walls or partitions) in underground passageways.

tasks.label: Measure and mark cutting lines on materials, using a ruler, pencil, chalk, and marking gauge.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough framing on a residential/light-commercial jobsite: at an outdoor cut station or on a lumber stack, the carpenter measures studs, plates, joists, rafters, headers and blocking with a tape and marks square, angle or plumb pencil cut lines with a speed/framing square. Uneven ground, wind, dust, crowned and bowed stock.

Sheet goods on site: measuring plywood/OSB sheathing, subfloor or drywall sheets on horses or a deck and snapping chalk lines or marking pencil rip and crosscut lines, including cut-outs around openings, sized to the as-built condition just measured.

Finish carpentry and cabinet installation in a house or interior fit-out: measuring an opening, wall run or cabinet reveal, transferring the dimension to base, casing, crown, door stock or a cabinet part, and marking a precise cut line (including miter angles) with a fine pencil or knife line to about 1/32 in.

Fitting to existing conditions: scribing a cabinet filler, stair skirt or trim to a wavy wall/floor with a compass or marking gauge, coping profiles, marking a rafter birdsmouth or notch against the actual member, or pattern-marking a replacement piece during repair/remodel.

Shop work: in a millwork/cabinet shop, contractor's shop or component plant, marking cut lines and machining marks on lumber, trim stock and panels from a cut list or shop drawing, with stock on benches, racks and carts and people moving through the space.

Deck/slab layout marking on the jobsite: measuring off control lines and snapping chalk lines on the concrete slab or plywood deck for wall plates and stud layout, and outlining floor openings, chases and penetrations that will subsequently be cut.

sources.title: Five Ways Dusty Robotics Transforms Layout Processes | Robins & Morton
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics FieldPrinter autonomously drives a construction slab or deck and prints full-scale BIM layout lines (walls, sleeves, penetrations, grid lines) at 1/16-inch accuracy, replacing tape-and-chalk layout; used in production on real jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chalk-line layout marking on installed decks and slabs. Same marking medium and surfaces carpenters mark, and the printed penetration/opening outlines are the very lines later cut, at tighter tolerance (1/16 in) than manual marking.

sources.title: Automated Layout for Framers | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Framing contractors use the same robot to print stud layouts, track locations and bracing details directly on the deck, replacing manual marking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carpenter layout marking on the deck. It substitutes for the pencil and chalk marks a framer makes for plates and studs; marking medium, surface and required precision match the task.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Autonomous Robotic Layout Solution Leverages HP's Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing to Reduce Cost and lnefficiencies in Construction | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially sold autonomous layout robot that navigates a construction site and prints lines, points, arcs and text on the floor in place of hand-snapped chalk; used by contractors such as Acciona on a hospital project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manual chalk-line layout marking on jobsite floors — the same marking medium and surface a carpenter uses when snapping lines on a slab or deck.

sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 | HOMAG
sources.claim: The WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 CNC multifunction bridge, which runs over fixtured framing/sheathing tables in timber-frame prefabrication plants, carries a marker unit that draws programmed lines and drawings onto panels to guide subsequent processing, alongside its saw and trimmer.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in machine form: measuring from the digital record and marking lines on sheathing/panel stock held on the machine's table at CNC precision, so downstream cutting and fastening follow the marks.

sources.system: Hundegger SC/K2 joinery machines and SPM-2 Speed Panel Machine
sources.title: Machines | Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger's automatic timber joinery and panel machines, fed by conveyors in prefab plants, perform inkjet marking of all kinds on beams, studs and panels (drywall, wood-based) in addition to sawing, drilling and milling.

sources.title: Alpine Linear Saw - Alpine - An ITW Company
sources.claim: Automated linear saws in wall-panel and truss plants measure incoming lumber and print position-dependent marks on the pieces (including wall-panel plate marking) inside an enclosed cutting center run by a single operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same material: the machine takes the measurement off the presented board and applies layout/cut marks on dimensional lumber that a framer would otherwise pencil on with tape and square.

sources.system: Vekta P3 printer on Razer linear saw
sources.title: P3 Printer | Vekta USA Advanced Automation
sources.claim: The Vekta P3 printer is a production printing head on the Razer linear saw that prints position-dependent information onto cut lumber components in real time in truss and frame plants.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in machine form: measuring and marking dimension-referenced lines and information onto lumber pieces, which is what the carpenter's pencil marks convey to the saw operator.

tasks.label: Follow established safety rules and regulations and maintain a safe and clean environment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ongoing and end-of-day housekeeping on a residential jobsite (new home or remodel): sweeping sawdust and nails off subfloor, picking up lumber offcuts, cutoff drywall and packaging, carrying debris out to a dumpster or truck, coiling extension cords and air hoses out of walkways, restacking material clear of paths, keeping stairs and exits clear. Layout changes daily; other trades, homeowners, weather and uneven surfaces.

Housekeeping and safety compliance on an active commercial/multifamily construction floor: clearing egress paths and stairwells of wood and drywall scrap, moving debris to bins or a trash chute, vacuuming/wetting down wood and silica dust, managing cords and hoses, meeting a general contractor's audited daily housekeeping standard at shift end while other trades work nearby.

Shop-based floor cleaning and dust control in a millwork/cabinet or prefab component plant: sweeping and vacuuming sawdust from open floor and aisles between shifts, on a fixed layout maintained by the employer.

Broader shop housekeeping in a millwork/cabinet or prefab plant: clearing offcuts and cutoffs from saw and CNC tables into scrap bins, emptying dust-collector drums and bags, returning clamps/tools and sheet stock to racks, keeping aisles and machine access clear, checking guards and e-stops.

Personal safety compliance while doing carpentry work: donning and using hard hat, eye and hearing protection and a respirator when cutting wood/masonry, tying off a fall-arrest harness on a roof or leading edge, using saw guards and push sticks, safe ladder/scaffold use, unplugging or locking out tools before blade changes, participating in toolbox talks.

Setting up and maintaining jobsite safety controls: building and maintaining temporary guardrails at floor openings, stair edges and balconies, cutting and fastening hole covers, hanging barricade tape and warning signs, securing lumber and sheet-goods stacks, checking GFCIs and damaged cords, keeping fire lanes and extinguishers accessible.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Skanska USA / Autodesk Research
sources.title: Spot on Site: Maximizing Jobsite Robotics for Evaluating Housekeeping | Autodesk University
sources.claim: Skanska, Autodesk Research and Boston Dynamics tested Spot for construction jobsite housekeeping, but the demonstrated capability was autonomous inspection missions that document and analyze cleanliness, not physically cleaning up debris.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (jobsite housekeeping) and same environment (active construction sites); cited as the limit of demonstrated capability — documentation of cleanliness rather than debris removal.

sources.system: Pulurobotics construction-site cleaning robot (NCC / Palmia / University of Helsinki trial)
sources.title: Testing Robotic Cleanup on a Construction Site - AEC Business
sources.claim: A construction-site cleaning robot built on the Pulurobot platform with an industrial vacuum was tested at a factory extension construction site in Finland; it remained a research prototype rather than a deployed product.

sources.title: Tennant Company Unveils X16 SWEEP for Autonomous, Around-the-Clock Industrial Sweeping
sources.claim: Tennant's X16 SWEEP, powered by Brain Corp's BrainOS, is a commercially available autonomous robotic sweeper for industrial floors that plans its own cleaning paths, self-docks to recharge, and picks up dust and debris — but it is designed to avoid larger 'problem debris' rather than pick it up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized floor sweeping of dust and loose debris. It transfers to the floor-cleaning portion of carpenter housekeeping in shops and fixed facilities (same hard floors, same loose sawdust/grit), but not to picking up offcuts, cords or stacked material.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals | Onshape
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo fully autonomous floor scrubbers are commercially deployed for routine floor cleaning in structured human work facilities worldwide, including factories, warehouses, airports and hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping a facility floor clean to an institutional standard. Transfers to the floor-cleaning component of shop housekeeping (hard floors, loose dust and grit, people present), not to manipulation of scrap or tools.

sources.date: 2022-2023 (Heavy Picker 4.0 launch; Kuljetusrinki line order Oct 2022)
sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots autonomously identify and pick bulky construction and demolition debris — including wood, metals, hard plastics and aggregates — off a sorting line inside purpose-built robotic sorting cells at material recovery facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing and binning mixed construction debris (wood offcuts, drywall, metal). Objects and gripping are comparable to jobsite scrap removal, but the debris must be conveyed to the fenced robot cell, so it supports only the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Epoch AI robot capability assessment (survey of deployed systems)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: A 2026 systematic assessment of autonomous robot capability finds that outside navigation, most industrial and household manipulation tasks are not commercially deployed, with handling new objects and environments the main bottleneck.
sources.transferJustification: Cross-cutting evidence on the state of autonomous mobile manipulation (clutter pickup, trash handling) used to bound positive judgments for unstructured jobsite cleanup.

tasks.label: Shape or cut materials to specified measurements, using hand tools, machines, or power saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough framing on an active residential jobsite: carpenter reads a plan/cut list, measures, and cuts dimensional lumber (studs, plates, blocking, joists, rafter birdsmouths and angle cuts) to length and angle with a circular saw and miter saw on sawhorses, amid mud, debris, weather and other trades.

Cutting sheet goods to size on site: ripping/crosscutting plywood or OSB sheathing, subfloor and concrete-form panels, and scoring/cutting gypsum board to fit around openings, using circular/track saw, table saw or utility knife, with dimensions taken from the structure as built.

Finish and trim carpentry cuts: baseboard, casing, crown, stair parts and cabinet trim cut to length with miters, bevels, compound angles and copes on a portable miter-saw station, to tight tolerances so joints close.

Shop or plant pre-cutting: a carpenter in a truss/wall-panel component plant, prefab housing factory, millwork or cabinet shop operating saws and CNC machinery to cut lumber and panels to the specified sizes in the cutting bill.

Cutting material already installed in place on an existing structure: cutting an opening in an installed wall/subfloor during remodel, trimming rafter tails or protruding studs, notching framing in situ, trimming a hung door or installed casework to fit.

sources.system: MiTek MatchPoint BLADE II linear saw (with Ranger delivery / Auto Deck staging conveyors)

sources.transferJustification: Direct: cutting framing lumber to specified lengths and angles, the same operation and material a carpenter performs with a miter/circular saw.

sources.title: Making the Cut: How Langs is Using the Blade II to Build a Safer, Smarter Future

sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ Nesting

sources.transferJustification: Direct: cutting plywood/OSB/gypsum sheet goods to specified sizes and openings, the same operation carpenters do with circular/track saws.

sources.title: Automatic Cross-Cut Saws Salvador SuperAngle 600
sources.claim: The Salvador SuperAngle 600 is an automatic optimizing crosscut saw that positions, clamps and cuts stock to programmed lengths with angles up to ±70 degrees and compound angles, as used for mouldings and trim components.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: cutting trim/moulding stock to specified lengths with miters and compound angles, the core of finish-carpentry cutting.
