tasks.label: Install structures or fixtures, such as windows, frames, floorings, trim, or hardware, using carpenters' hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction or replacement: set and fasten window units and exterior door units into rough openings of a wood-framed house - shim, plumb/level/square, fasten, flash and seal, working off ladders/staging on a live jobsite with variable openings and weather.

Interior finish trim in houses, apartments and remodels: run baseboard, door/window casing, crown, chair rail, stair skirt and closet shelving; scribe and cope to out-of-square walls, miter and fit joints, fasten with a finish nailer and fill, in rooms cluttered with other trades' work.

Finish flooring in residential rooms: lay underlayment and nail-down/glue-down/click-lock hardwood, engineered or laminate flooring; rack and stagger courses, undercut jambs, cut to fit at walls, closets and transitions, install thresholds and reducers.

Hardware and door hanging on site: hang pre-hung and slab doors, mortise and screw hinges, bore and fit locksets and strikes, install closers, pulls, drawer slides, shelf standards, bath accessories and grab bars in homes and finished spaces.

Commercial interior fit-out in a building under construction: set hollow-metal door frames and doors with hardware, install raised access floor panels and ceiling board/grid systems, and mount wall fixtures across large open floor plates.

Offsite prefab/modular plant: on the panel line, fasten sheathing and subfloor decking to wall/floor/roof elements, assemble rough openings and sub-assemblies, and set door/window units into panels, with material presented by conveyors, tables and cranes.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named "Robo-Buddy Floor"
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Floor autonomously installs raised access floor pedestals and panels on an active high-rise construction site, matching craftsman accuracy (1 mm), but craftsmen mark pedestal locations, set lasers and install the perimeter/cut panels (robot did the inner 350 of 700 m2 per floor).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: raised access floor panel laying vs. carpenter flooring installation. Comparable objects (>10 kg rigid panels), mm-level placement, unfinished building interior; but the robot lays only modular field panels on pedestals and leaves cut/perimeter fitting to craftsmen.

sources.title: A Production System for a New Era - The Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots can transform a job site!
sources.claim: The same Robo-Buddy platform installs ceiling systems autonomously on Shimizu jobsites - inserting hanger bolts and backing, holding ceiling boards and screwing them off, navigating to work locations by referencing BIM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ceiling board installation vs. installing structures/fixtures. Same jobsite environment and sheet-goods handling with powered fastening, so it bounds autonomous site installation today - repetitive modular panels on a grid, not fitted trim, windows or hardware.

sources.developer: Autovol (with Prefab Logic; House of Design robotics)
sources.title: Robots are the Future of Modular Construction - Modular Building Institute
sources.claim: In the most automated US modular plants, robots frame and sheathe walls and cut openings, but window, cabinet and MEP installation is still performed by tradespeople.

sources.title: Will Robots Install the Windows in Your Next House? | Glass.com
sources.claim: At Blueprint Robotics' modular plant a pneumatic gantry places window and door units into pre-cut openings in wall panels, but factory carpenters complete the fastening and flashing; the source does not establish autonomous control of the gantry.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor Robotic Sheathing / Sub-Assembly System
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic cells fully automate sheathing of prefabricated wall panels, ... (placing, gluing, nailing, sawing/routing, multi-layer build-up) and robotic sub-assembly of studs and rough openings, sold as a commercial production-line product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening sheathing and subfloor decking to fixtured wall and floor elements is the panel-line form of installing structural floor/wall coverings with powered fastening tools.

sources.title: GANNOMAT Express 807 Hinge Inserting and Drilling Machine - Akhurst Machinery LTD
sources.claim: Commercial CNC boring-and-insertion machines automatically bore and press-fit hinges and bore for handles, locks, bumpers and catches on cabinet doors in a single machine cycle, at industrial production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory hardware installation on fixtured doors/fronts vs. a carpenter installing hinges, pulls and lock hardware. Same hardware and tolerances; the machine performs the boring and the hinge insertion itself under machine control.

sources.system: Norfield Eagle Automatic Prehung Door Machine / Norfield 5000 line
sources.title: Eagle Automatic Prehung Door Machine - Norfield
sources.claim: Automatic prehung door machines mortise hinge pockets in door and jamb, apply hinges and bore lock/ball-catch holes under computer-logic control at up to about 400 doors per shift, assembling the door into its frame.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-hanging a door and applying its hinges and lock prep on a fixtured line is the E1 presentation of the carpenter's door-and-hardware installation instance - same components and fit tolerances.

sources.title: Watch a humanoid robot install drywall | Woodworking Network
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously picked up and fastened a gypsum board to a wall stud in a laboratory mock-up - a slow research demonstration, not a jobsite deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: board hanging vs. installing structures/fixtures. It is the closest humanoid demonstration of carpenter-style installation work, done in a lab mock-up far below worker speed, which bounds site-level (E3) capability.

sources.title: Tackling the housing shortage with robotic microfactories | MIT News
sources.claim: Reframe Systems' robotic microfactory currently automates only wall and ceiling framing; people complete the rest of the work, and window installation is a stated future goal rather than a shipped capability.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Partner Robotics' P900 floor tile paving robot ... sold commercially and has completed roughly 100,000 sq m of tiling, but the reporting does not establish unsupervised autonomy and the work is mortar-set tile in open field areas, not carpenter-installed wood/laminate flooring with cuts and transitions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor floor covering installation. Closest commercial floor-laying robot, but it lays adhesive-set tile over large open areas and does not do the cutting, undercutting and transition fitting carpenter flooring requires.

tasks.label: Verify trueness of structure, using plumb bob and level.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough framing on a residential or light-commercial site: after a stud wall is stood up, the carpenter holds a 4-6 ft spirit level (or hangs a plumb bob) on the end studs and corners and calls adjustments while a partner pushes and nails temporary braces; the check is repeated until the wall reads plumb and the line is straight. Cluttered deck, sawdust, wind, other trades working nearby.

Finish/fixture installation indoors: setting a door jamb, window unit, cabinet run, post or stair stringer and checking it with a 2-4 ft level and square, shimming and re-checking plumb/level/reveal until true before fastening. Interiors of houses or buildings under construction, or occupied buildings during trim-out.

Concrete formwork: verifying wall forms, column boxes, footing forms and anchor placements are plumb, level and square with plumb bob, level and string before the pour, on muddy or uneven ground outdoors, adjusting kickers and walers as needed.

Standalone verification pass over completed rough structure: walking a framed floor or completed area before drywall/next trade, checking walls for plumb, floors/ceilings for level, and openings for square, and recording out-of-tolerance locations for correction (QA/punch-style check on an active site).

Remodel/repair diagnostics in an existing occupied building: checking whether existing walls, floors, and door openings are plumb and level to plan the fix (shimming a floor, re-hanging a door), in furnished, cluttered rooms with no drawings.

Shop/prefab bench work: verifying that a shop-built assembly (wall panel, stair unit, cabinet box, window buck) is square, flat and true on the assembly table or jig before it ships or is installed, in a component plant or cabinet shop.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 / FieldLink autonomous scanning solution
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution
sources.claim: Trimble and Boston Dynamics sell a turnkey autonomous scanning solution in which the Spot quadruped follows predefined waypoint paths on construction sites and collects Trimble X7 laser scans on a schedule for design validation, with a dock for autonomous charging and data transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built laser scanning for design validation. Survey-grade (≈2 mm) point clouds of walls, floors and openings are the measurement from which plumb, level and square deviations are computed, i.e. the same determination a carpenter makes with plumb bob and level, over the same building elements.

sources.title: Construction | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot for construction with autonomous navigation of construction environments and programmed laser-scanning routes whose 3D data is integrated into BIM to minimize rework.

sources.title: Pomerleau | Boston Dynamics Case Study
sources.claim: General contractor Pomerleau runs Spot autonomously on a 500,000 sq ft active construction site, capturing data on a regular basis from ... with human intervention only for battery swaps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous repeat data-capture missions on an active jobsite. It establishes that the mobile platform navigates an unstructured, changing construction site unattended, which is the environment prerequisite for autonomous trueness checks.

sources.system: On-site measuring robot for post-construction quality assessment
sources.title: On-Site Measuring Robot Technology for Post-Construction Quality Assessment of Building Projects
sources.claim: A mobile on-site measuring robot with a 3D scanner autonomously navigates building sites and measures dimensions, wall evenness, wall alignment (verticality), floor heights and corner angles, automatically comparing results with construction quality standards; it was applied on two real building projects with 40% better efficiency than manual measurement.

sources.title: Verity verifies as-built point cloud data meets design specs
sources.claim: ClearEdge3D Verity automatically compares as-built point clouds with design/fabrication models and flags out-of-tolerance work, producing deviation heat maps and records of installed work.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robot: this is the automated analysis stage paired with robotic point-cloud capture. It shows the verification output (pass/fail against tolerance) is produced without a human taking measurements, completing the robot-captured verification workflow.

sources.system: ZEISS AICell trace with AIMax cloud sensor and CARFIT fixtures
sources.title: ZEISS installs new shopfloor measuring solution for complete car body inspection in North America
sources.claim: ZEISS AICell trace is a commercially installed robotic measuring cell that holds parts in smart fixtures and uses dual 7-axis robots with optical 3D sensors to check hundreds of dimensional features to CMM accuracy at production cycle time, giving instant pass/fail quality decisions at the line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated geometric conformity inspection of a large fixtured assembly against tolerance. Verifying that a fixtured wall panel, door unit or form assembly is square, flat and true is the same act on comparably sized rigid assemblies at far looser tolerance (~3 mm vs. sub-mm).

sources.title: MiCROTEC - Goldeneye: Scanner boosts performance and yield
sources.claim: MiCROTEC's Warpscan 3D board shape scanner, integrated in mechanized lumber lines, automatically measures the geometry of sawn timber in transport and detects shape deviations such as twist, curvature and cupping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-line geometric verification of wood members. Judging whether a piece of lumber is straight, flat and untwisted is the component-level version of verifying trueness, performed automatically on work presented by conveyor in a purpose-built line.

tasks.label: Build or repair cabinets, doors, frameworks, floors, or other wooden fixtures used in buildings, using woodworking machines, carpenter's hand tools, or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cabinet/millwork shop: carpenter or cabinetmaker builds cabinet boxes, face frames, doors and drawers to a cut list — breaking down sheet goods on a panel saw or CNC, edgebanding, boring, gluing/clamping and fastening carcases square in a shop with standard machines.

Residential/light-commercial construction site: carpenter builds wooden frameworks — laying out and nailing stud walls and partitions, setting joists, blocking, headers over openings, rafters/trusses — cutting members with a circular saw and fastening with a nail gun on an open, weather-exposed, cluttered site.

Building floors on site: setting/leveling joists, cutting and nailing subfloor sheathing to a deck, then laying and blind-nailing hardwood or engineered strip flooring, cutting boards to fit walls, undercutting jambs and racking the pattern in a partly finished building.

Doors on site or in a door shop: building or trimming door frames, sizing and beveling slabs, mortising hinges and boring lock sets, assembling jamb and slab into a hung unit, then plumbing/shimming it in the rough opening so it swings and latches with an even reveal.

Repair call in an occupied home, office, school or apartment: cutting out and replacing a rot-damaged door jamb or window frame, re-gluing/rebuilding a broken cabinet, replacing a split stair tread or water-damaged floorboards — diagnosing the damage and scribing new wood to existing, non-standard construction.

Shop fabrication of other wooden fixtures: stair stringers/treads, built-in shelving units, benches, counters and casework, machined from lumber and panel stock on shop machines and assembled square before delivery.

sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic system automates timber wall framing in prefabrication plants: robots cut and place studs and noggings, assemble rough openings and multi-studs, square the frame and apply/route sheathing on walls, floor cassettes and roof elements.

sources.claim: Kval sells complete prehung-door lines (automatic hopper/stacker, door sizer, CNC hinge/lock machining with automatic hinge applicator, and frame assembler) that build hung door units at 350+ doors per shift.

sources.title: Shimizu Corporation introduces robots for civil construction
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy locates itself from BIM and laser sensors on high-rise building sites and uses two arms to install ceiling boards and OA raised-floor pedestals and panels, screwing them into place.

Cited only to bound site capability — it handles pre-sized modular panels on a grid and does not cut, scribe or nail wooden members to fit, so it does not substantiate wood floor or frame building at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Remove damaged or defective parts or sections of structures and repair or replace, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior repair on an occupied single-family home: carpenter probes rotted clapboard/trim/fascia/deck boards, cuts back to sound wood with a saw and pry bar, extracts nails, mills or cuts a matching replacement piece, fits it to irregular existing conditions, fastens, caulks and primes. Ladder/scaffold access, weather, landscaping and homeowner property in the way.

Interior repair in an occupied home or apartment: cut out a water-damaged drywall section or spongy subfloor, remove a split door jamb, damaged stair tread, baseboard or cabinet part; scribe and fit a replacement to out-of-square existing work, fasten and blend. Furniture, finished surfaces and occupants must be protected.

Concealed structural repair in an existing building: expose and remove rot/termite/impact-damaged joists, rim joist, sill plate, studs or headers; temporarily shore the load, cut out the damaged member, sister or replace it and re-fasten. Cramped crawlspaces, attics, basements, poor light, unknown conditions behind finishes.

Remediation of damaged or defective work on an active construction site: tear out mis-cut or damaged framing, sheathing, blocking, stair carriages or concrete formwork found during inspection/punch-list, and rebuild to spec with hand and power tools amid other trades, debris and changing layouts.

Maintenance carpentry inside an institution (school, hospital, hotel, office, plant): repair or replace damaged doors, door frames, hardware blocking, casework, partitions, handrails and trim during occupied hours; work order specifies the item, conditions are as-found but the facility is controlled and standardized.

Bench/shop repair of a standardized wood assembly removed from service and set on a workstation: pallets, crates, shipping frames, formwork panels and similar nailed wood structures — identify broken members, pull or cut them out, and nail in replacement stock to a repeatable spec.

sources.system: Yaskawa Motoman robotic pallet repair systems
sources.date: 2024 (page current as of 2026; technology in service since 2010s)
sources.title: Pallet Repair — Yaskawa United Kingdom
sources.claim: Yaskawa Motoman supplies commercial robotic pallet-repair cells that sort pallets, dismantle them, remove and replace damaged board elements and nail in new stock, with parts fed from a conveyor in a fixtured, fenced cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repair of a nailed wooden pallet. A pallet is a nailed wood structure; the cell removes the damaged members and fastens replacement boards — the same remove-and-replace-with-fasteners operation as carpentry repair — but only on standardized components presented fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Jointec / Prepac / Yaskawa Motoman pallet dismantling and repair stations
sources.developer: Jointec AB with Prepac and Yaskawa Motoman
sources.title: The Future of Pallet Production Today – Robots Effectively Used in European Pallet Companies (Pallet Enterprise)
sources.claim: Robotic pallet dismantling and repair stations built by Jointec with Prepac and Yaskawa robots are in production use at pallet recyclers in Europe, including Kjell & Co in Karlstad, Sweden; 20 such robot systems were deployed across Europe covering nailing, dismantling and repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dismantling and repair of nailed wood pallets in a fixtured robotic cell — removal of damaged members and re-nailing of replacements, the machine-side analogue of a carpenter's remove-and-replace repair, restricted to standardized components.

sources.system: Robotic Pallet Dismantler (M-2) and Sort & Repair Systems
sources.title: Alliance Automation Drives Innovation with Lumber Feeding, Pallet Recycling, Over-sized Pallet Assembly and AI-Camera Production Tools (Pallet Enterprise)
sources.claim: Alliance Automation's Robotic Pallet Dismantler, sold and installed at US pallet recyclers, uses an end-of-arm tool to prep pallets and remove individual damaged components such as stringers and lead boards as part of sort-and-repair lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective removal of damaged members from a nailed wood assembly in a machine cell — the 'remove the damaged part' half of the task, on standardized pallet geometry brought to the machine.

sources.developer: Politecnico di Milano / INDEXLAB (Ruttico, Bordoni, Deval)
sources.title: Woodot: An AI-Driven Mobile Robotic System for Sustainable Defect Repair in Custom Glulam Beams (Sustainability 17(12):5574)
sources.claim: Woodot is an autonomous mobile robot ... finds defects (knots) on custom glulam beams on a timber shop floor, mills them out and plugs them with wooden inserts; detection F1 was 0.69 and flush plug placement succeeded in 87% of trials, i.e. a research prototype below skilled-worker reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing a defect from a timber member and installing a replacement plug. It is the closest autonomous demonstration of defect-driven remove-and-replace on wood, but is confined to surface knots on beams in a fabrication shop, with 87% placement success.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus autonomously installs asphalt shingles on residential ..., working from a gantry attached to the roof plane; the system covers installation of new material only, not survey-driven removal of damaged sections or fitted repair carpentry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ work on an existing house exterior. Cited to show the frontier of autonomous residential in-situ work is repetitive installation on a planar roof, not the cut-out, fit and fasten repair of damaged structural or finish carpentry.

sources.title: The case for autonomous demolition robots — talk.Build
sources.claim: Machines used to remove damaged sections of built structures on site — demolition robots such as Brokk — are remotely operated by a human, i.e. teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removal of damaged sections of a structure in situ. Cited as negative context: the deployed machines for on-site removal are human-operated, so they cannot support an autonomous completion judgment.

tasks.label: Install rough door and window frames, subflooring, fixtures, or temporary supports in structures undergoing construction or repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial framing crew on an active job site frames rough openings for doors and ... in stick-built wood walls: cutting and nailing headers, king/jack studs, sills and cripples to layout, plumbing and squaring the opening, in weather, on a mud-and-lumber-strewn site.

Setting frame units into prepared rough openings in a structure under construction: hollow-metal door frames anchored plumb in metal-stud or masonry partitions of a commercial interior, and residential window/door units shimmed, leveled and fastened into bucks, working off ladders/scaffold amid other trades.

Installing subfloor/deck sheathing on site: snapping layout, running construction adhesive, lifting 4x8 OSB/plywood sheets onto floor joists or trusses over an open crawlspace/basement, staggering joints and nailing off to pattern, then cutting openings for stairs and chases.

Erecting temporary supports during construction or repair: shoring posts and needle beams under a cut-out bearing wall in a remodel, temporary walls, wall bracing and guardrails, sized and wedged to fit an as-found, irregular existing structure.

Fixture and hardware rough-in on site: nailing blocking/backing between studs for cabinets, grab bars and fixtures, mounting brackets, hangers, hold-downs and anchors to layout, and setting rough built-in supports in a partially finished structure.

Carpenter in a panelized/modular component plant building the same elements off site: assembling wall panels with framed door and window openings, and floor cassettes with nailed sheathing, on production tables with overhead machinery and material feeds.

sources.system: SCADAware/Kawasaki BX250L wall sheathing cell (Rehkemper & Son)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: A fenced production cell of four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel rails at prefabricator Rehkemper & Son places and nails OSB sheathing onto prefabricated wood wall frames and cuts the sheathing to form window and door openings.
sources.transferJustification: Same materials (OSB/plywood sheathing, dimensional lumber studs) and same fastening operation (nail pattern into hidden studs) as site sheathing and opening framing; the cell also produces the window/door openings themselves.

sources.developer: WEINMANN Holzbausystemtechnik (HOMAG Group), distributed by Stiles Machinery
sources.title: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ Framing Stations - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ framing stations are commercially sold machines that position, index and nail studs (including opening framing members) into wall frames automatically from CAD/BIM data in panel plants.
sources.transferJustification: Rough door and window frames in wood construction are the framed openings (header, king/jack studs, sill, cripples) built into the wall frame; the framing station positions and nails exactly these members to CAD geometry.

sources.title: LIGNA Product 2025: AutoFloor System (Randek)
sources.claim: The Randek AutoFloor line automatically nails, glues, cuts and mills sheathing onto floor joist cassettes to produce finished floor elements in a purpose-built production line.
sources.transferJustification: A floor cassette is joists plus glued-and-nailed subfloor sheathing with milled openings — the same objects, adhesive/nailing operation and tolerances as installing subflooring over joists on site.

sources.system: Cosmic Robotic Workstation Cell / mobile microfactory with ABB IRB 6710
sources.title: ABB and Cosmic use AI-powered robots to rebuild homes in Los Angeles area
sources.claim: Cosmic Buildings' on-site mobile microfactory using ABB IRB 6710 robots fabricates custom structural wall panels (including openings) from BIM and delivers them for assembly, deployed on wildfire rebuild projects in the Los Angeles area.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that the framed-and-sheathed wall element with door/window openings — the output of the site instances — is produced by robots only when the work is brought into a purpose-built cell, even when that cell sits on the job site.

sources.system: Raise Robotics façade fastener installation robot (2x Universal Robots UR20)
sources.developer: Raise Robotics with Universal Robots, deployed by Harmon Inc.
sources.title: Raise Robotics deploys UR cobots with Harmon for high rise fastener installation
sources.claim: Raise Robotics' mobile platform with two UR20 arms autonomously drills and torques façade anchor brackets to survey layout on active high-rise construction sites for glazing contractor Harmon, with one worker supervising per location and ±3/16 in. placement accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing anchors/brackets (fixtures) into a structure under construction. It covers only repetitive fastener setting into concrete slab edges to survey layout, not the varied wood blocking, backing and built-in supports a carpenter installs.

sources.date: 2018 introduction; Shimizu Smart Site program ongoing
sources.title: A Production System for a New Era: The Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots can transform a job site!
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy robot uses imaging and laser sensors with BIM to locate itself on a building site and install ceiling hanger bolts, backing members and ceiling boards, or raised-floor pedestals and panels, under autonomous control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening board/panel material to a structure under construction. Objects differ from structural subflooring (drop-in access-floor panels and light ceiling boards, no adhesive or nailing to warped joists), and deployment beyond limited pilot sites is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Erect scaffolding or ladders for assembling structures above ground level.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential job site: carpenter carries a 24-28 ft fiberglass extension ladder from the truck, sets the feet on sloped/soft ground or over shrubs and hose bibs, walks it up against the fascia or wall, sets ~75-degree angle with 3 ft above the eave, levels the feet with a leveler or blocking, and ties it off before framing/roof-edge work.

Interior or porch work on a house or small remodel: carpenter positions stepladders, or two ladders with ladder jacks and a walk plank, around cluttered rooms and finished floors or uneven exterior grade to reach soffits, headers, ceiling framing and trim; repositions repeatedly as work advances.

Rolling ('baker') scaffold tower assembled on an interior slab or subfloor of a building under construction: unfold and lock frame sections, insert cross braces and pins, drop in the deck, fit casters and outriggers/guardrails, level it, then move and re-level it along the wall as ceiling, soffit and blocking work proceeds.

House exterior: erect pump-jack poles or a two-to-three-lift steel frame scaffold along a wall for siding, sheathing or window/trim work - set mudsills and base jacks on sloped landscaped ground, stack frames and braces, plank the lifts, add guardrails and wall ties, verify plumb and level.

Commercial/institutional construction site: crew erects multi-lift system or tube-and-clamp scaffold (or shoring towers for elevated deck formwork) around a structure - handling 30-60 lb components by hand or hoist, engaging couplers/ledgers, planking, installing ties, stair access and guardrails to an engineered, inspected (green-tag) standard amid other trades.

Renovation inside an occupied institutional building (school, hospital wing, office): carpenter sets ladders or a small scaffold/podium inside a barricaded work zone with protected finished floors and controlled access, to reach ceilings, door frames and soffits.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: The leading commercial scaffolding robot, KEWAZO's LIFTBOT, is a robotic hoist that autonomously transports scaffold components vertically; it does not assemble or erect the scaffold, which human erectors still do.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (material transport during scaffold erection). It substantiates only the hoisting sub-step, not erection: the robot moves parts along an already-built scaffold while people place frames, braces and planks, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.title: Robotics firm Kewazo gets a $10M lift | Construction Dive
sources.claim: LIFTBOT is an automated hoist that ...; the great majority of scaffolding projects remain entirely manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (vertical material handling for scaffold erection). Confirms that the commercially deployed scaffolding robot supplies parts to human erectors rather than erecting scaffold itself.

sources.title: Meet the robot that transports scaffolding | The B1M
sources.claim: The Kewazo robot's role is delivering scaffolding pieces to human scaffolders on site; erection itself is performed by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (component transport). Shows the division of labour - robot transports, humans erect - with no evidence of autonomous assembly of the scaffold structure.

sources.title: VIDEO: NASA's Valkyrie Robot Can Erect Scaffolding | ScaffMag.com
sources.claim: The closest robotic demonstration of actually building a scaffold is NASA's Valkyrie humanoid in a demonstration video; it is described as semi-autonomous and very slow, far from worker-rate erection.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (scaffold erection) but only a slow demonstration of unclear autonomy; per the autonomy rule it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Humanoid construction robots (review of current platforms)
sources.developer: University of Florida et al. (Scientific Reports review)
sources.title: Opportunities challenges and roadmap for humanoid robots in construction | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid/construction robot perception and manipulation is validated mainly in controlled settings and degrades with variable lighting, dust and clutter; use outside research institutes and pilot projects remains limited.
sources.transferJustification: General capability review for construction robots; used only to support negative judgments about ladder and scaffold erection, not to support any positive tier.

tasks.label: Maintain job records and schedule work crew.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine structural timbers and supports to detect decay, and replace timbers as required, using hand tools, nuts, and bolts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential crawl space or basement: carpenter probes sill plates, band joists, floor joists, girders and posts with an awl and moisture meter to find rot or termite damage; then shores the floor, cuts out and removes decayed members, sisters or replaces joists and sill sections, sets posts, and through-bolts connections with carriage/lag bolts. Confined, dark, dirt floor, live loads overhead, layout unique to each house.

Exterior deck, porch, stairs and exposed framing at a home: inspect posts, beams, ledger boards, joists and stair stringers for decay at ground contact and fastener holes; remove rotted members, replace with treated lumber, and re-fasten with lag screws, carriage bolts and hardware, working outdoors on uneven ground and at height.

Heavy timber structure - barn, historic building, mill building, church, or exposed timber truss roof: sound and bore-probe large beams, posts, braces and truss members for interior decay, install temporary shoring, cut out and remove decayed timbers or splice in a new section, fit and bolt the replacement with steel plates, nuts and bolts. Access by ladder/lift, member weights of hundreds of pounds.

Maintenance carpenter inside a controlled institutional or industrial building (school, warehouse, plant, hospital, campus): scheduled inspection of wood roof structure, mezzanines, timber columns, dock framing and platforms for decay or water damage; replaces the affected members in place with bolted connections during a maintenance window. Fixed layout, standard building, controlled access.

Outdoor timber infrastructure: boardwalk, timber bridge, dock/pier, bulkhead or retaining wall. Inspect stringers, caps, pilings and decking for decay and marine borers, replace decayed stringers/caps and re-bolt, sometimes over or in water, with equipment access and weather exposure.

Underground mine passage timber supports and brattices, or temporary shoring/formwork bracing on a construction site: examine props, caps, lagging and brattice framing for decay or crushing, and replace the failing timbers, fitting members to irregular rock or excavation faces and bolting/spiking them in place.

sources.title: Scanning And Optimization For The Planer Mill - Wood Business
sources.claim: Comact GradExpert graderless planer optimizers autonomously scan sawn lumber on a mill conveyor and detect decay, white speck, honeycomb, stain and other defects; over 45 systems delivered, i.e. the 'examine timber to detect decay' step is machine-performed in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated lumber grading. It substantiates only the inspection half of this task - machine detection of decay in sawn structural timber - and only where the timber is conveyor-presented to the sensor head, i.e. a purpose-built line.

sources.title: MiCROTEC - Goldeneye Transverse
sources.claim: MiCROTEC Goldeneye multi-sensor scanners commercially detect wood defects and grade/classify lumber on all four sides in a single conveyor pass using laser and colour imaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-line lumber quality scanning. Same inspection judgement (finding degraded wood) on the same material, but performed on fixtured, conveyor-fed boards rather than members in a standing structure.

sources.system: Yaskawa Motoman pallet repair / dismantling systems
sources.title: Pallet Repair - Yaskawa
sources.claim: Yaskawa Motoman supplies commercial robotic pallet repair cells that dismantle damaged wooden elements from an assembly, replace the damaged board elements, nail them, and handle the unit to and from a conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated repair of nailed wooden assemblies. It is the closest analogue to 'remove the decayed member and fit a replacement': same material (sawn softwood), same operation sequence (extract damaged member, insert new one, refasten), but with the assembly clamped and conveyor-presented in a fenced cell. Damage identification is often operator-selected on a touchscreen; machine execution of the dismantle/replace/nail sequence is automatic.

sources.system: Alpine / House of Design automated truss assembly system (ABB IRB 4600 robots)
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics with Alpine, an ITW Company
sources.title: Alpine and House of Design Launch Floor Truss Robotics - SBCA
sources.claim: Alpine (ITW) and House of Design deployed ABB-robot cells in truss plants in which robots pick and position structural lumber and assemble floor and roof trusses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of structural wood components. Shows robots can grip, position and fasten joist- and rafter-sized structural timbers to carpentry tolerances - the handling and fitting competence needed to set a replacement member - inside a fenced, fixtured cell.

sources.date: 2025-06 (LIGNA launch of robotic subassembly); system marketed since ~2018
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic framing system automatically cuts, places and nails studs and noggings for wall, floor and roof elements in a factory line, including straightening of stud material before nailing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic house framing in a plant. Demonstrates autonomous cutting-to-length, placement and fastening of dimensional framing lumber - the fabrication and fitting of a replacement joist or stud - but only with material fed and jigged by the machine line.

sources.system: Atlas Copco fixtured assembly / robotic nutrunner systems
sources.title: Fixtured Assembly Solutions | Atlas Copco
sources.claim: Atlas Copco supplies fully automated robotic bolt-tightening (fixtured nutrunner) systems used on production assembly stations, including a robot wheel-assembly station with fixtured tightening and vision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic threaded fastening. Covers the 'nuts and bolts' element of the task - autonomous bolt insertion and torque-controlled tightening - but only where the joint is presented in a known, fixtured position.

sources.developer: Tilbury Douglas (contractor deploying an off-the-shelf humanoid)
sources.title: Tilbury Douglas deploys £15,000 humanoid robot on live construction site - Construction News
sources.claim: The first humanoid robot trialled on a live UK construction site is limited to autonomously navigating and capturing 360-degree imagery, progress reports and safety monitoring - no manipulation, tool use, or structural repair.

sources.title: Hilti unveils new robot-powered drilling capabilities
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot, the most widely deployed jobsite manipulation robot, is a semi-autonomous mobile robot that drills BIM-specified holes in ceilings and walls; its jobsite capability is confined to drilling, not member removal or structural fastening.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound in-situ jobsite robot capability: it shows the state of the art for autonomous work inside buildings under construction is single-operation drilling from a BIM model, well short of inspecting and swapping structural timbers.

tasks.label: Fill cracks or other defects in plaster or plasterboard and sand patch, using patching plaster, trowel, and sanding tool.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home or apartment: carpenter patches settlement cracks, nail pops, door-knob dings and small holes in existing painted plaster/drywall walls and ceilings; furniture and finished floors must be protected, compound applied with knife/trowel, feathered and hand-sanded to blend into the surrounding finished surface.

New single-family or multifamily residential jobsite (unoccupied, under construction): filling screw dimples, seams, board gouges and other defects across freshly hung drywall in rooms, closets and hallways, then sanding the surfaces to a Level 4 finish ready for primer.

Commercial or institutional interior construction / tenant fit-out (unoccupied floors under construction): filling defects and joints over large runs of new drywall including high walls and ceilings, then sanding to Level 4/5; dusty, cluttered site with lifts and other trades working nearby.

End-of-job punch-list touch-ups at a jobsite: dozens of small scattered defects (screw pops, corner dings, scuffs, gouges) on already primed or painted walls; each spot filled with patching compound, feathered and spot-sanded without damaging finished floors, trim or adjacent paint.

Maintenance carpenter in an occupied institutional building (school corridor, hospital room, hotel, office suite): repairing localized wall damage - holes, cracks around door frames, impact damage - working around occupants and furniture, containing dust, filling and sanding the patch flush before repainting.

Nonstandard substrate or geometry: cracks in historic lath-and-plaster walls and ceilings, curved surfaces, cornices and moldings, or textured/knockdown ceilings where the filled patch must be sanded and the surrounding texture or profile matched; work from ladders or scaffold.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+ plastering and drywall-finishing robot
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ is described as a fully autonomous, AI-guided robot that applies plaster and joint compound and sands drywall on interior construction sites, navigating with onboard 3D scanning and no site preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of plaster/joint compound over board seams, fastener holes and surface imperfections followed by machine sanding uses the same materials, tool action, precision and accepted output (a smooth, paint-ready filled surface) as filling defects in plaster/plasterboard and sanding the patch.

sources.title: Okibo and PCI team up on Netflix House project in Pennsylvania - Engineering.com
sources.claim: Okibo's plastering/painting robots were used in production by a large US specialty contractor (Performance Contracting Inc.) on the 100,000-sf Netflix House interior construction project, performing drywall finishing work up to 12 ft without lifts or scaffold.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task: robotic compound application plus sanding of gypsum board surfaces on an active interior construction site is the mechanized form of filling board defects and sanding them smooth.

sources.title: OKIBO - Smart Robots For Construction Sites / Our Robot
sources.claim: Okibo states the EG7 is completely autonomous, guided by patented AI 3D scanning and real-time modeling with zero site preparation, markings or BIM, swaps its hopper for a dust collector for ..., and is sized for residential, multifamily and office interiors.
sources.transferJustification: Manufacturer description of the same plaster-application-and-sanding capability and of the machine's fit for residential and office interiors, the settings of the new-construction instances.

sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Built (Bluebeam)
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot maps the wall with onboard AI and vision, sprays joint compound over panel seams and fastener heads, and after drying uses an automated sanding head with 99.9% dust capture to reach a Level 4/5 finish, without plans or pre-made maps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling seams and fastener dimples (defects in plasterboard) with compound and sanding them flush is materially and dimensionally the same operation, on the same substrate, as filling cracks/defects and sanding the patch.

sources.title: Meet Canvas, the Drywall Finishing Robot Offering Level 5 Quality - Construction Junkie
sources.claim: Canvas robots have been used in production by union drywall contractors (Webcor, Daley's Drywall, Nevell Group) on projects including SFO's Harvey Milk Terminal and UCSF, taping, spraying and sanding rooms to Level 5; the operator positions the machine and sets the work area and the robot then executes the finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; also establishes that the machine's filled-and-sanded output is accepted at Level 5 quality by commercial drywall contractors on live jobsites.

sources.title: Scan&Sand in high-quality, complex, skilled sanding and finishing operations - Zivid
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand is an autonomous robotic sanding cell in which a workpiece is presented to the arm, scanned in 3D and sanded without CAD models or programming; it is in production at Janicki Industries sanding putty-surfaced tooling parts that were previously hand-sanded.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive sanding of a presented workpiece, including soft putty/filler surfaces, to a defect-free finish is the 'sand patch' half of this task performed in a purpose-built guarded cell.

sources.system: Vision-based adaptive autonomous surface crack repair robot
sources.title: Vision-Based Adaptive Robotics for Autonomous Surface Crack Repair (arXiv)
sources.claim: A robotic arm with RGB-D vision and a laser scanner autonomously detects surface cracks, measures them and fills them with pumped/extruded material, validated end-to-end on 3D-printed crack specimens in the laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous localization of a crack on a presented surface and deposition of filler into it is the 'fill cracks' half of this task, shown only in a fixtured laboratory setting.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7+ performs sanding, painting and Level ... at heights to 24 ft, with contractors reporting up to 5x productivity on Level 4 and 5 sanding jobs while meeting quality standards.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality accepted output (Level 4/5) for the machine fill-and-sand workflow on high walls and ceilings of interior construction sites.

tasks.label: Dig or direct digging of post holes and set poles to support structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential fence line in a customer's back yard: carpenter strings a layout line, digs 2-3 ft holes every 6-8 ft with a clamshell digger or one/two-man gas auger around roots, rocks, slopes, buried utilities and tight side-yard access, drops in 4x4/6x6 wood posts, plumbs and braces them, and backfills with bagged concrete or tamped soil.

Deck, porch, pergola or carport posts at a house: footing points transferred from the ledger/layout, holes augered or hand-dug to frost depth next to an existing structure and landscaping, tube forms set and footings poured, then 4x4/6x6 posts set on anchors, plumbed and braced until the framing ties them off.

Post-frame (pole barn) building on a graded rural pad: 4-5 ft deep holes drilled with a skid-steer or tractor auger (carpenter often directing the operator and checking depth), 6x6 or laminated columns set to a string line with correct embedment and uplift cleats, plumbed, braced, and backfilled with concrete or compacted fill.

Carpenter crew on an active commercial/institutional jobsite: small numbers of sign posts, bollards, temporary construction-fence or barricade posts, and shoring/brace posts for formwork; mixed hand and machine digging around underground services, trades and traffic, posts set plumb in concrete to a surveyed layout.

Long repetitive runs of posts driven into open ground on a large site: perimeter or agricultural fence line posts, stakes and temporary fence posts at surveyed spacing across open, graded or rough field ground, set by driving rather than by concreting.

Repair/replacement: a rotted or wind-snapped fence or deck post is replaced in place - old post and concrete plug broken out and removed, hole hand-dug and enlarged between existing panels, plantings and structures, new post set plumb in fresh concrete and re-attached to the existing framing.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 (with RPS 25 pile stabilizer)
sources.title: Built Robotics develops autonomous pile driving system
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ..., built on an excavator, that surveys, distributes, drives and inspects steel H-pile foundations for utility-scale solar arrays on outdoor construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving steel foundation piles. It substantiates only the 'set poles to support structures' element - vertical structural supports placed into unprepared outdoor ground on a surveyed layout to inch-level tolerance - not hole digging, wood posts, or concrete backfill.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 fleet (Blattner Energy projects)
sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous pile drivers are in commercial production use at scale on US solar construction sites, including a muddy Louisiana site, with roughly ten robots handling more than half the pile-driving scope and no humans handling the beams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar pile driving. Same environment class as open-ground post setting (as-found, muddy, graded field on an active construction site) and the same output class (structural posts set in the ground), but the posts are driven steel beams, not augered-and-concreted wood posts.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar - Built Robotics
sources.claim: On the RPD 35 the piles are pre-loaded into baskets by humans with other machines, after which the robot operates autonomously; a paired robotic stabilizer holds piles to plumb and z-height tolerance.
sources.transferJustification: Shows how the work is presented to the machine (posts pre-racked, geofenced site, GPS layout), which is what an E1/E2-style presentation of post setting would look like; still no hole digging or concrete backfill.

sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center
sources.claim: Built Robotics' retrofitted autonomous machines perform pre-drilling and trenching as well as pile driving on jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-drilling pilot holes for piles. It covers autonomous hole making in as-found ground, but the holes are pilot holes for driven steel piles, not post holes that receive a wood post and concrete.

sources.system: Epiroc Pit Viper (autonomous drilling, Rig Control System)
sources.title: Epiroc's Pit Viper - the past, present and future - International Mining
sources.claim: Epiroc Pit Viper surface drill rigs have drilled autonomously in open-pit mines for a decade, with more than 90 million metres drilled in autonomous mode and improved hole placement accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous blasthole drilling. It shows machines can drill holes to plan positions and depth in as-found outdoor ground (mine benches), but it drills large-diameter blastholes and never sets, plumbs or backfills a post.

sources.developer: Farmscan AG with Kidd Farm Machinery and Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: The Innovate UK Roto-Fence project demonstrated a tractor-mounted automated post driver that installs grazing fence posts to a farmer's plan with centimetre accuracy, with a human loading each post.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: agricultural fence post installation. Closest match to driven post lines in open fields, but it is a project demonstrator for temporary grazing fence posts, requires a human to load every post, and involves no hole digging or concrete.

sources.system: Autonomous vineyard trellis post robot (Ly et al., ICARSC 2015)
sources.title: A Fully Autonomous Robot for Putting Posts for Trellising Vineyard with Centimetric Accuracy
sources.claim: A research robot autonomously navigated to each vineyard trellis post location with centimetre accuracy and drove the post into the earth, with a human handing it each post.

sources.title: Ojjo Earth Truss Nextracker Datasheet

tasks.label: Finish surfaces of woodwork or wallboard in houses or buildings, using paint, hand tools, or paneling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction commercial/multifamily interior: taping joints, applying two or three coats of joint compound and sanding walls and ceilings of wallboard to a Level 4/5 finish, including inside corners and around openings, on an active jobsite.
Priming and painting large wallboard wall and ceiling areas on site with sprayer or roller before trim-out, masking floors/openings, in building interiors under construction.

Finishing installed woodwork in place: sanding, filling nail holes, caulking, and brushing paint, stain or varnish on trim, jambs, doors, casing and handrails, cutting cleanly to adjacent walls and finished floors.
Installing wood or composite paneling/wainscot as a finished wall surface in a room: measuring, scribing to out-of-plumb walls, cutting outlet and switch openings, fastening and trimming edges.

Punch-list and remodel touch-up in occupied or near-complete spaces: patching dings in wallboard and trim, spot filling, caulk repair, color-matched touch-up paint, refinishing damaged woodwork amid furniture and other trades.
Shop pre-finishing of millwork before installation: sanding, staining and spray-lacquering doors, panels, cabinet faces and trim stock in a shop finishing room/booth.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous AI-guided painting and drywall ... (EG6/EG7) operate on active construction sites in Europe and the U.S., navigating and working without site preparation.

sources.title: Netflix House ... goes up with help from robots that paint and finish drywall | Building Design + Construction
sources.claim: Okibo robots were used by contractor Performance Contracting Inc. on the 100,000-sf Netflix House project to paint and finish drywall, with reported 5x productivity on Level 4/5 sanding while meeting quality standards.

sources.title: Okibo launches EG7+ autonomous robot for painting and finishing - Engineering.com
sources.claim: The Okibo EG7+ performs sanding, painting and Level ... up to 24 ft, is battery powered and requires no site preparation or external references to operate.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robots work alongside human crews on U.S. jobsites, spraying joint compound and machine-sanding gypsum board to a Level 5 finish; the operator positions the machine and the robot scans and executes.

sources.title: Overhead coating lines: anthropomorphic robots | Cefla Finishing
sources.claim: Cefla's iGiotto anthropomorphic spray robot coats woodwork such as doors and window frames carried on an overhead conveyor through a purpose-built spray line and drying tunnel, in commercial wood-finishing plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory coating of the same woodwork (doors, jambs, window frames) with the same paints/lacquers a carpenter would brush or spray on site; substitutes for the coating step when the workpiece is presented fixtured on a conveyor.

sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics Unveils 100,000-Square-Foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics deploys AI-driven robotic cells at customer factories that autonomously sand, polish and spray parts of varied materials and geometries, including wood products, without per-part programming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding and coating of workpieces is the same surface-preparation-and-finish sequence carpenters apply to woodwork; it substantiates the sanding half of shop finishing when parts are presented in a cell.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and fastening sheet panel material onto a wall frame is the same handling and fastening operation as applying paneling/wallboard to a wall, with the wall presented fixtured on a line.

sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ Multi-Function Bridges - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges automatically fasten sheathing and plasterboard to timber wall elements and rout rough openings, including power outlet cut-outs, under CNC control in prefabrication plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting outlet openings in and fastening panel material to a wall frame matches the cut-and-fasten precision demanded when a carpenter applies paneling; demonstrated on gypsum board as well as OSB.

tasks.label: Cover subfloors with building paper to keep out moisture and lay hardwood, parquet, or wood-strip-block floors by nailing floors to subfloor or cementing them to mastic or asphalt base.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential construction: carpenter rolls out rosin/building paper over a plywood or OSB subfloor in an empty framed house, then racks and blind-nails solid 3/4" hardwood strip flooring with a pneumatic flooring nailer, staggering end joints, leaving expansion gaps, cutting rips at walls and around door jambs. Dusty site, materials stacked around, other trades present.

Renovation/retrofit in an existing occupied home: tear out old covering, check and level an out-of-flat subfloor, undercut door casings, lay paper and nail or glue engineered/parquet flooring around cabinets, stair nosings, hearths and thresholds, weaving into adjacent existing floors; furniture and occupants nearby.

Commercial/institutional interior fit-out (office, retail, school, restaurant): glue-down engineered plank or parquet block set into mastic/adhesive troweled over a concrete slab or plywood, large open field areas plus perimeter cuts, columns, doorways and transition strips, on a general contractor's schedule.

Gymnasium or large sports/assembly wood floor: lay vapor retarder/building paper over the slab, set a sleeper or subfloor panel system, then nail maple strip flooring across a large open area, holding expansion voids at walls and fitting to inserts.

Repair/patch work: replace damaged or water-stained boards in an existing hardwood or parquet floor, cutting out and weaving in matching pieces, re-nailing or re-cementing loose blocks over patched paper/mastic, blending with the surrounding floor.

Offsite/modular or manufactured-housing plant: carpenter covers the module deck with building paper and lays and fastens finish wood flooring on floor cassettes/modules at fixed stations in the plant, with materials staged and delivered to the station.

sources.system: Randek AutoFloor floor/roof element production system
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - AutoFloor System
sources.claim: Randek's AutoFloor is a commercial factory system that builds floor elements/cassettes on a jig, automatically feeding and handling tongue-and-groove wood-based boards, cutting sheets and openings, gluing, and nailing them to the supporting deck structure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: decking a floor element by machine in a factory. It is the same physical operation as this task's core step - pick a tongue-and-groove wood board, position it on a flat deck held in a fixture, engage the T&G joint, cut it to fit, and nail or glue it down - performed autonomously on a purpose-built jig line (E1). Objects (wood-based T&G boards), fastening method (automatic nailing and gluing) and the flat fixtured deck are comparable; the differences are board width and the visual finish tolerance of hardwood.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named "Robo-Buddy Floor"
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Floor autonomously travels a building floor under construction and lays raised-access floor panels and pedestals to within 1 mm, reaching craftsman accuracy; deployed on the SHIN-OSAKA DOI BLDG No.5 high-rise project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying modular floor panels over a prepared base inside a building. It demonstrates autonomous millimetre-accurate placement of floor units across a field - the pick-place-align element of laying parquet or strip flooring - but it neither nails nor cements units, nor cuts them to fit perimeters, and it handles only uniform pedestal-mounted panels, so it supports the placement step rather than a finished wood floor.

sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics Co., Ltd. (Country Garden)
sources.date: 2022 (Red Dot Product Design award; page retrieved 2026-07)
sources.title: Red Dot Design Award: Floor Tile Paving Robot R-19
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' R-19 floor tile paving robot is a fully automated mobile robot that applies cement adhesive to the substrate and lays large-format floor units into the fresh adhesive bed with millimetre precision using four-camera visual positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cementing rigid floor units into an adhesive bed - the same operation as this task's 'cementing them to mastic or asphalt base' variant, with comparable unit size (large-format tile vs parquet block/plank) and millimetre placement precision. It covers open field areas only, with perimeter cutting and fitting left to workers, so it substantiates field laying where pre-cut units are presented.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridge with facade shoe / batten shoe
sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: The state of the art for machine-fastening individual solid wood boards on prefab element lines is semi-automatic: WEINMANN's facade and batten shoes align and fasten boards, but a human still places each board on the element.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening narrow solid wood boards side by side to a fixtured element. Cited only as context - because board placement keeps a human in the loop, this item is treated as non-autonomous and is not used to support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Inspect ceiling or floor tile, wall coverings, siding, glass, or woodwork to detect broken or damaged structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home: homeowner reports damage, carpenter walks furnished rooms inspecting drywall/wall coverings, hardwood or tile floors, baseboards and trim, cabinets, window glass and sashes; looks for water stains, soft/rotted wood, cracked or loose tile, delaminated veneer; probes suspect wood with an awl or screwdriver, taps tile for hollowness, opens/closes doors and windows, and determines repair scope for an estimate.

Active new-construction or renovation jobsite: pre-close-in and punch-list inspection of installed drywall, trim/casework, floor and ceiling tile, glazing and door frames for breakage, gouges, cracked panes, warped or split lumber and damaged finishes; done amid other trades, dust, debris, temporary lighting and ladders, with findings logged for rework.

Institutional/commercial facility maintenance carpenter (school, hospital, hotel, office): routine and complaint-driven inspection rounds through occupied corridors and rooms checking suspended ceiling tiles, resilient/ceramic floor tile, wall coverings and corner guards, wood doors, frames and casework, and door/window glass for breakage, sagging, water damage or vandalism; writes work orders.

Building exterior: inspection of siding, fascia, soffit, trim, exterior door/window frames and glass from ladders, lifts or the ground; checking for storm/impact damage, split or loose boards, failed caulk, insect or rot damage found by probing and pressing; weather, vegetation and uneven ground at the site.

Shop, yard or receiving area: incoming or fabricated material check — glass panels/units, tile lots, lumber, plywood, prefinished millwork and cabinet parts examined for chips, cracks, breakage, warp, knots and handling damage before installation, with damaged pieces rejected or set aside.

sources.title: Product Solution | Osprey®25 by LiteSentry | Glass Magazine
sources.claim: LiteSentry/Softsolution Osprey 25 is a commercial in-line optical scanning system that automatically inspects flat glass for surface defects, edge chips, haze and dimensional errors as panes move through a tempering/processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory quality inspection of glass. It substantiates the carpenter's glass-damage-detection step for the E1 counterfactual because the objects (flat glass panes/units), the defect classes (chips, cracks, surface damage) and the accept/reject decision are the same; only the presentation (conveyor line) differs.

sources.title: Precision Glass Industries Strengthens Quality Control with New LineScanner and Osprey Complete | glassonweb.com
sources.claim: Osprey glass inspection units are installed and running in production glass plants, inspecting every pane for optical and surface quality on new tempering lines.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: in-line automated inspection of glass for defects/damage, deployed in industry, standing in for the human visual check of glass at an E1 inspection station.

sources.title: Defect detection performance of automated hardwood lumber grading system - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A validation study of the Microtec Goldeneye 300 multi-sensor scanner with GradeView grading software found automated hardwood lumber defect detection and grading accuracy within industry standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grading of sawn lumber. It transfers to the carpenter's check of woodwork/lumber for splits, knots, warp and handling damage because the material, the defect classes and the accept/reject output are the same, with boards presented on a conveyor as an E1 setting would present them.

sources.title: MiCROTEC - Goldeneye 900
sources.claim: MiCROTEC's Goldeneye scanners are sold commercially and use laser, 3D and colour imaging to recognise wood defects and classify lumber on all four sides at production speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wood defect recognition in a mill. Same materials and defect types as the carpenter's inspection of delivered lumber/millwork for damage; supports E1 only, since the wood is fed through the machine.

sources.title: Jackal-Based Robot Modernizes Site Inspection - Clearpath Robotics
sources.claim: QuicaBot, a Jackal-based autonomous inspection robot from NTU Singapore/Transforma Robotics, scans finished rooms with laser, thermal and colour cameras to find cracks, hollow tiles and out-of-tolerance walls and floors, but is positioned as an aid that roughly halves inspector labour rather than replacing the assessor.
sources.transferJustification: Closely related task: post-construction interior defect assessment (tile hollowness, wall cracks, floor evenness) in empty new units; cited to test whether in-situ inspection of tile/wall coverings can be completed, and it falls short of the whole instance (no woodwork, glass or damage-scope judgment; inspector still required).

sources.title: Construction | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot autonomously navigates construction sites on programmed routes to collect 360° imagery and laser scans of as-built conditions, indoors and outdoors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite/facility data capture. It shows a robot can traverse the settings of instances B and C and photograph surfaces, but the cited capability ends at data collection, not at determining that tile, glass or woodwork is broken or damaged.

sources.title: Top 10: AI Tools in Construction | Construction Digital
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous LiDAR rover scans live construction sites and compares the scan to the BIM model to flag installation deviations for project teams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated construction quality/progress verification. Cited to test instance B: the system detects geometric deviation from model, not physical breakage or damage of finished tile, glass, siding or woodwork, so it does not carry over to damage detection.

sources.title: How Drone Inspections Can Help Identify Hidden Roof Damage | Eagleview US
sources.claim: EagleView markets autonomous drone flights with AI-based damage detection for roof condition capture used by roofing contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior building envelope damage capture from the air. Cited for instance D; it covers roof surfaces from a distance and does not perform the close, tactile siding/trim/glass condition assessment (probing for rot, checking fasteners and soundness) the carpenter's instance requires.

tasks.label: Bore boltholes in timber, masonry or concrete walls, using power drill.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new-build interior: carpenter bores hundreds of anchor/bolt holes overhead into concrete deck soffits, metal-deck ceilings and concrete walls for hangers, bracing, ledger angles and bolted attachments, working from layout marks or a BIM/CAD plan on an active but broadly cleared construction floor, with dust control and depth control required.

Large commercial/industrial slab work: boring downward anchor-bolt holes in a concrete floor slab in dense repetitive patterns (equipment bases, rack stops, wall track, formwork bracing, sill/plate anchors) on a flat, swept slab in a building under construction; hundreds to thousands of holes to tight positional tolerance.

Residential and light-commercial jobsite anchoring: a few to a few dozen boltholes drilled into poured foundation walls, footings, CMU/brick, or through wood sill plates and ledgers into concrete for anchor bolts, hold-downs and deck ledger bolts — awkward positions, ladders, crawlspaces, uneven or muddy ground, no digital model.

Renovation/retrofit in an existing building (occupied or partly occupied): drilling anchor holes in existing concrete or masonry walls for door frames, brackets, equipment mounts, blocking and partition track; cluttered rooms, unknown rebar/utilities, mixed base materials, small hole counts, strict dust and noise limits.

On-site timber boring: boring through-bolt holes with auger/self-feed bits in wood framing and heavy timber in place — ledgers, beams, posts, hold-down anchor holes through plates and studs — often overhead, at height, or at odd angles on a partially framed structure.

Shop/prefab plant: boring bolt holes in timber components (glulam beams, posts, wall panels, trusses) off site before delivery, working from shop drawings at a bench or machine line inside a controlled facility.

sources.title: Jaibot New Capabilities - Hilti Canada (press release)
sources.claim: Hilti Jaibot, a commercially released semi-autonomous mobile drilling robot, marks and drills anchor holes from a BIM/CAD plan in concrete ceilings, metal-deck ceilings and vertical concrete walls between 0.9 and 4.8 m, executing the drilling automatically with integrated dust removal; it has been deployed on construction projects worldwide since late 2020.

sources.title: Meet the Jaibot drilling robot, a potential solution to the construction worker shortage
sources.claim: The Jaibot is in field use on US construction sites, described as the first commercialized semi-autonomous ..., positioned on site and then drilling ceiling holes in the planned locations on its own.

sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: Revolutionizing Construction: Introducing the World's First Fleet-Capable Downward Drilling Robot, Now Commercially Available
sources.claim: DEWALT/August Robotics' DALE downward-drilling robot autonomously drills anchor holes in the concrete floor slabs of data centers under construction; in a year-long pilot across 26 data center construction ... it drilled more than 230,000 holes at 99.97% accuracy with automatic dust extraction, and it became commercially available on 9 July 2026.

sources.title: Meet DeWalt's new robotic drill, designed to bore holes into data center floors - Fast Company
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage confirms the DEWALT/August Robotics drill roams under-construction data center floors and drilled over 90,000 anchor holes without human involvement, at roughly one hole every 80-180 seconds depending on size and depth.

sources.title: Automation on the Jobsite - Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: CSC Robo's Drillcorpio robots automate drilling of anchor holes into concrete on jobsites; the Df model self-navigates, positions itself, sets the angle and drills floors, walls and ceilings up ... ft, and can work either from BIM files or from physical marks read with a 3D camera. Commercially available in Asia-Pacific since 2023 and used on more than 30 commercial jobsites.

sources.title: Technical visit to CSC ROBO Robotic Centre - The Hong Kong Institution of Engineers
sources.claim: An engineering-institution site visit documented the Drillcorpio D3 performing automatic drilling and anchor installation on walls and ceilings with simultaneous dust collection, and the Df demonstrating autonomous navigation and drilling from loaded BIM/CAD plans and pre-planned markings.

sources.date: 2025 (product line, in commercial use for years)
sources.title: ROBOT-Compact | Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger CNC joinery machines (ROBOT-Compact/ROBOT-Drive lines) process timber members fed and clamped in the machine, automatically selecting drill bits from a tool changer to perform drilling, milling and marking operations on beams for carpentry, timber-frame, glulam and CLT construction.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (boring bolt holes in timber) with the workpiece conveyed and clamped in a purpose-built machine rather than drilled in place; hole diameter, depth and positional precision meet or exceed hand-drilled bolt holes.

sources.title: Glued Laminated Timber Fabrication | QB Corporation Services
sources.claim: Commercial mass-timber fabricators bore bolt holes in glulam members by CNC machine in the plant, producing the bolt and connection hole patterns needed for structural connections with better location accuracy than manual drilling.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task — boring boltholes in timber — performed with the timber brought to a fixed machine, showing machine completion of the drilling itself at the required precision.

tasks.label: Assemble and fasten materials to make frameworks or props, using hand tools and wood screws, nails, dowel pins, or glue.
