instances.label: Residential/light-commercial rough framing on an active jobsite: carpenter lays out plates, assembles stud walls, headers, floor/roof framing, blocking and temporary bracing flat on the deck or in place, fastening with a framing nailer, screws and construction adhesive; lumber is stacked on the deck, conditions are weather- and trade-congested.

Concrete formwork panel fabrication: carpenter builds flat job-built form panels and gang forms (plywood sheathing nailed/screwed to 2x lumber frames, walers, stiffeners) on horses or a lay-down area at the site or in the contractor's yard, to dimensions from the form drawings.

In-place formwork and shoring: assembling column/beam/wall forms around rebar in the excavation or on the deck, setting and bracing shoring posts and adjustable props, kickers, walers and ties, cutting and nailing bracing to fit as-found ground, rebar and existing structure.

Interior/remodel frameworks built to measured dimensions in an existing or partly finished building: soffit and bulkhead ladders, blocking/backing frames, closet and chase framing, non-bearing partition sections, screwed, nailed or glued together on site from field measurements.

Fit-in-place irregular frameworks in existing buildings: furring scribed to out-of-plumb masonry, framing notched around existing ducts/pipes/wiring, curved or angled forms and props, stair carriages with treads/risers glued, doweled and screwed to fit the actual opening.

Shop or component-plant fabrication: building wall panels, trusses, floor cassettes, jigs, mock-ups and temporary props at benches/jig tables in a component plant, prefab shop or site carpentry shop, with materials staged nearby and standard shop equipment.

sources.title: This Plant Runs Itself — Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic cells cut, frame, sheath and glue timber wall elements in offsite factories with humans limited to monitoring and unloading raw material; equipment is in use at manufacturers such as FrameTec (Arizona) and BoKlok.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic framing/sub-assembly modules automatically cut and place studs and noggings and assemble wall subcomponents (rough openings, U-/L-studs, double and triple studs) inside a robotic work cell with an automated squaring table.

sources.system: House of Design robotic roof/floor truss systems
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant — HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Builders FirstSource operates and ordered fully automated robotic truss assembly systems from House of Design; the software builds complex variable trusses and wall ..., and Louws Truss has run a robotic roof-truss plant since 2022.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of wood roof/floor trusses (placing dimensional lumber in a jig and fastening it into a framework). Same materials, same tolerances and same fixtured-table presentation as assembling site-built frameworks; fastening is by connector plates rather than nails.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robotic wall sheathing cell (SCADAware integration)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: At Rehkemper & Son's prefab home plant, four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel rails autonomously straighten warped studs, place 4x8 OSB sheets on framed walls and nail them to the studs per the digital wall design, then rout out window and door openings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nailing plywood/OSB sheathing onto a lumber frame in a fixtured cell. A job-built concrete form panel is the same operation and materials (sheet goods nailed to a 2x frame) at looser tolerance, so performance transfers to form-panel fabrication.

sources.title: These AI Robots Can Help Build Homes — Pro Builder
sources.claim: AUAR's containerised robotic micro-factory, built around an ABB robot, cuts lumber and assembles it into wood-frame wall, floor and roof panels, doing all the nailing and lifting itself; two units were shipped to US customer Rival Holdings.

sources.system: Cosmic Robotic Workstation Cell (ABB IRB 6710) mobile microfactory
sources.title: ABB and Cosmic Use AI-Powered Robots to Rebuild Homes in Los Angeles Area
sources.claim: Cosmic Buildings' mobile robotic microfactory with ABB IRB 6710 robots was deployed in Pacific Palisades, California, fabricating custom structural wall panels in an on-site robotic workstation cell for crews to assemble at the build site.

sources.title: The Next Step Into Automated Off-Site Construction in the US | HOMAG
sources.claim: JL Schwieters Construction (Hugo, Minnesota) runs a WEINMANN line where the FRAMETEQ F-500 framing station aligns studs, cuts top and bottom plates ... nails studs in the designed positions almost completely automatically, with one employee; the WALLTEQ bridge then nails sheathing.

tasks.label: Perform minor plumbing, welding, or concrete mixing work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial site: carpenter mixes bagged concrete in a wheelbarrow or portable mixer (or takes it off a ready-mix chute), fills post holes for a fence, deck, or sign post, braces posts plumb, crowns/screeds the top, and cleans tools. Uneven ground, weather, mix-water judgment by consistency.

Small mortar/grout/patch placements incidental to carpentry on a construction or remodel site: grouting anchor bolts and column base plates, dry-packing under a sill or threshold, patching a broken slab edge or a stair nosing, filling a small curb. Batch mixed by hand or in a mortar mixer, placed by trowel around existing construction.

Remodel plumbing in an occupied private home: cap or reroute a supply line, add a shutoff valve, reconnect a sink drain/P-trap or a water supply to a fixture after moving a wall or setting a vanity/cabinet; work under sinks and in wall cavities, then leak-test.

New-construction site pipe work incidental to framing: bore/notch studs and joists for pipe, hang and strap DWV or PEX lines, glue or crimp a few joints to adjust a rough-in the plumber left short, before drywall.

Jobsite welding in position: tack or fillet weld steel angle clips, embed plates, hold-downs, rebar dowels, or metal-stud/formwork connections against existing construction, often vertical or overhead, outdoors, on parts held by clamps or by hand.

Bench welding in the contractor's own shop: fabricate or repair a small steel bracket, stair-stringer connection, or form hardware on a shop welding table with clamps and a vise, then grind and paint.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 robotic welding cells (Obsidian AI)
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells autonomously weld steel parts (scanning, planning and welding without programming) and are commercially deployed in fabrication shops in the US and Canada — fenced, fixtured cells built around the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class (arc welding of steel parts) as the carpenter's minor welding; comparable steel members, fillet/tack welds and weld quality, but performed with the work brought to a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Path Robotics Rove mobile welding robot
sources.title: VIDEO: Rove four-legged robotic welder starts shipyard work - Marine Log
sources.claim: Path Robotics launched Rove, a quadruped-mounted mobile welding system using its Obsidian model, aimed at welding in shipyards and other high-variability facilities; early adopters were evaluating it in a shipyard as of April 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Welding of structural steel in a working facility rather than a fixtured cell; relevant to whether jobsite/shop welding could be done outside E1, but status is early-adopter evaluation, not accepted production output.

sources.developer: AIMIX Group (representative commercial batching plant supplier)
sources.title: Automatic Concrete Batching Plant - Maximize Your Project ROI
sources.claim: Automatic concrete batching plants proportion cement, aggregate, water and admixtures and mix concrete under computerized control, without an operator judging the mix by hand.
sources.transferJustification: This is the mixing half of the carpenter's concrete-mixing task performed by machine in a purpose-built plant: same material, same proportioning-and-consistency requirement, work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Weckenmann automatic concrete spreader / Gravimatic gravimetric spreading system
sources.title: Gravimatic – the new generation of fully automated concrete spreading (BFT International)
sources.claim: Automatic concrete spreaders (e.g., Weckenmann Gravimatic) dose and place fresh concrete into shutterings/moulds on precast pallet-circulation lines with essentially no operator, and have been standard equipment in modern precast plants for decades.
sources.transferJustification: Placement half of the concrete task: mixed concrete metered into a presented form/mould containing embedded steel, then vibrated and finished — the E1 analogue of filling a post hole or small form.

sources.system: ICON Magma portable mixing unit + Vulcan construction 3D printer
sources.title: Vulcan | ICON
sources.claim: ICON's Magma unit automatically mixes its cementitious Lavacrete with additives and water on the construction site, adjusting for weather, and feeds the Vulcan gantry printer that places the material; the system has been used to build homes at the Wolf Ranch development.
sources.transferJustification: On-site automated mixing of a cementitious material to a working consistency; placement, however, is limited to programmed print paths inside the gantry envelope on a prepared foundation, not free-form pours around posts or existing construction.

sources.system: Pipebots (in-pipe leak repair micro-robots); HP SitePrint (layout printing)
sources.title: Tiny robots unleashed in underground water pipes find and fix leaks autonomously
sources.claim: Searches for robots that install or connect building plumbing (supply lines, valves, traps, DWV/PEX joints) return only in-pipe inspection/repair micro-robots, layout printers, and factory assembly of fittings — no system that performs plumbing installation work.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterize the state of plumbing robotics: work inside buried mains, not cutting, fitting, joining and leak-testing fixture plumbing; does not transfer to the carpenter's minor plumbing instances.

tasks.label: Anchor and brace forms and other structures in place, using nails, bolts, anchor rods, steel cables, planks, wedges, and timbers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial jobsite: setting and securing footing and foundation-wall forms on uneven excavated grade — driving wood stakes, nailing kickers and diagonal braces, setting walers, snap ties and wedges, checking plumb/square/line before the pour.

Commercial jobsite: crane-set vertical wall/column gang forms and one-sided forms plumbed and braced with turnbuckle kickers anchored into the slab with drop-in anchors/anchor rods, tie rods torqued, forms tied off against wind and concrete pressure.

Slab-on-grade, curb and sidewalk edge forms on prepared grade: aligning form boards to string/laser line, driving stakes, nailing stakes to forms, adding braces and wedges so edges hold line and elevation during placement.

Temporary bracing of erected wood framing on a jobsite: nailing diagonal plumb-and-line braces, temporary wall braces, blocking and brace planks to hold walls, trusses and rafters true until sheathing/permanent bracing goes on.

Anchoring structures/assemblies to concrete or steel: bolting sill plates, hold-downs and post bases to cast-in anchor rods, torquing nuts, occasionally tensioning steel cable or strap bracing on the jobsite.
Shop/plant work: building, securing and bracing formwork, moulds and panel jigs inside a precast or component-manufacturing facility — fixed layout, indoor, controlled access, repeated element types.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page; system in commercial use since ~2010)
sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants — Sommer precast technology
sources.claim: Sommer's Multi-Function-Shuttering-Robot automatically places formwork (shuttering) profiles on casting pallets in precast plants, aligns them and activates their magnets to lock them in position — i.e., anchoring forms in place — plus demoulding, oiling and plotting, at up to 100 m2/hour.
sources.transferJustification: Same task at plant scale: securing formwork so it holds position and line against fresh concrete pressure; fastening is by integrated magnets rather than nails/wedges, but the tolerance demands and the accepted output (a correctly located, locked form) are comparable.

sources.title: Shuttering | Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Elematic sells shuttering and deshuttering robots for precast wall lines that automatically place side forms (shutters) on casting tables from active or passive storage, performing the shuttering, demoulding and accessory functions of a wall plant.
sources.transferJustification: Placing and securing side forms on a casting bed is the plant-line form of anchoring formwork in place; edge/side forms play the same role as staked slab-edge forms on grade.

sources.system: Shuttering robot in Huffcutt carousel precast plant
sources.title: Brand New Precast Concrete Wall Panel Plant | Huffcutt
sources.claim: A US precast plant (Huffcutt, Chippewa Falls, WI) runs a fully automated shuttering robot that selects the required shutters from production data, places them on the pallet and activates their integrated magnets, in an indoor carousel plant.
sources.transferJustification: Real US production deployment of automated form placement and securing, showing the capability is not merely a vendor demonstration.

sources.system: House of Design robotic truss and wall panel systems
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Builders FirstSource operates fully automated House of Design robotic truss and wall-panel systems that lift, preplate and assemble lumber members into finished trusses and panels in component plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and mechanical fastening of dimensional lumber into a held, squared assembly — the same handling, fastening and dimensional-tolerance demands as nailing braces, planks and blocking to hold a structure true.

sources.title: WEINMANN at the Dach+Holz | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges in timber-house plants automatically fasten sheathing and boards to framed elements with nailing and stapling units under CNC control, with screwing and nailing tools selectable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic nailing of boards/planks onto fixtured timber frames — the fastening operation used to brace and stiffen structures — executed to production quality on a purpose-built table line.

sources.title: Terabase Energy's Next-Generation Terafab Completes Field Testing, Ready for Deployment
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab is an on-site automated 'field factory' in which robots assemble and bolt solar modules onto steel torque tubes; the first-generation system was deployed on five solar projects and V2 completed field testing and is offered commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bolted fastening of heavy structural members into a fixed, aligned assembly on a purpose-built line — the bolting/anchor-rod content of anchoring structures, at production tolerances.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: The most capable commercially deployed construction-site robot in this area, Hilti's Jaibot, only drills and marks anchor holes from digital plan data and is described as semi-autonomous; no cited site robot sets, anchors or braces formwork or structural members.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context for the negative E2/E3 judgments: site-deployed robots reach hole drilling, not placement, anchoring or bracing of forms and members.

sources.title: Autonomous anchoring for robotic construction — Automation in Construction
sources.claim: On-site autonomous anchoring (driving posts and sheet piles into the ground) exists only as a research prototype robot evaluated in real-world environments, not as worker-quality construction equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (driving stakes/posts to anchor structures) cited as context showing on-site anchoring capability is prototype-level and does not include attaching or bracing forms.

tasks.label: Work with or remove hazardous material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Jobsite work with hazardous wood products: cutting and fastening pressure-treated/chemically treated lumber, MDF/plywood and engineered wood, generating treated-wood and wood dust; PPE, dust control, and segregating treated offcuts for disposal (no burning). Occurs on decks, framing, and remodel sites in variable weather and clutter.

Working with hazardous chemicals of the trade: construction adhesives, solvents, epoxies, two-part sealants, caulks, wood preservatives, spray foam and finishes — mixing and applying at the point of use, ventilating, wearing respirator/gloves, labeling and storing containers, disposing of rags and empties.

Silica-generating anchor work: hammer-drilling holes overhead and in walls/slabs of concrete or masonry to set anchors for ledgers, track, formwork and fixtures, using on-tool vacuum dust extraction or water, plus HEPA cleanup of the slurry/dust.

Saw-cutting cementitious and masonry materials: fiber-cement siding/backerboard, concrete block, pavers, cement board — using shrouded saws with vacuum or wet methods outdoors or in a cut station, then bagging dust and offcuts.

Lead-safe renovation in a pre-1978 house or school: erecting plastic containment, removing painted trim, doors, window units and plaster/wood components with lead-safe practices, misting, wrapping and bagging debris, HEPA vacuuming and wet-wiping to clearance.

Removal of asbestos-containing or mold/water-damaged materials during demolition: floor tile and mastic, pipe lagging, transite panels, or moldy drywall, insulation and framing; negative-pressure containment, wetting agents, controlled removal, double-bagging and labeled disposal.

sources.system: Hundegger Robot-Drive / Speed-Cut CNC joinery machines
sources.title: Maximum flexibility (timber-online.net)
sources.claim: Hundegger CNC joinery machines cut and machine structural timber fully automatically in timber-construction factories, with automatic conveyor removal of wood waste and an extraction system capturing fine dust around the machine — i.e., machine handling of the hazardous wood-dust/treated-timber cutting step inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated timber machining. Transfer: the carpenter's hazardous-material duty here is cutting treated/engineered lumber while controlling and disposing of the hazardous dust and offcuts; the CNC cell performs the same cuts on the same stock with integrated extraction and automatic waste removal.

sources.title: Machines | Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger markets fully automatic CNC-controlled joinery machines used across timber framing, prefabricated house and glulam production, indicating routine unattended machine operation on timber stock.

sources.system: PAR Systems automated sealant and adhesive dispense systems
sources.title: Adhesive Dispensing with PAR Systems
sources.claim: PAR Systems supplies commercial robotic cells that automatically dispense sealants and adhesives (including mix-on-demand two-part chemistries) onto presented parts with seam tracking and part localization, removing the human from contact with the hazardous chemistry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial sealant/adhesive application. Transfer: the carpenter's hazardous-chemical work is metering and applying adhesives, epoxies and sealants to a workpiece without exposing anyone; robotic dispense cells apply the identical chemistries (two-part epoxies, urethane sealants) to fixtured parts at production quality.

sources.title: Jaibot Drilling Robot - Hilti USA
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a commercially sold semi-automated construction robot that marks and drills anchor holes in concrete ceilings and walls on active construction sites with a built-in dust removal system, taking over the silica-dust-generating overhead drilling work from tradespeople.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-driven anchor-hole drilling. Transfer: the hazardous-material content of the carpenter's instance is respirable crystalline silica from drilling concrete; the Jaibot performs the same drilling in the same concrete on the same sites with integrated dust capture.

sources.title: Hilti Jaibot BIM-enabled Construction Jobsite Robot | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: The Jaibot self-locates from a robotic total station and then drills all holes within reach ... the operator supervising and repositioning it rather than controlling each drilling motion.

sources.system: Sellafield skip sorting and laser cutting cell (FANUC ARC Mate 120iC + M-900iB/360, integrated by Cyan Tec)
sources.title: FANUC reliability underpins autonomous laser cutting cell for Sellafield
sources.claim: An autonomous FANUC/Cyan Tec robotic cell installed in a shielded bunker at Sellafield sorts, laser-cuts (size-reduces) and repacks contaminated radioactive waste from skips with no human involvement in the operation — machine handling of hazardous contaminated material presented to a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic size reduction and repackaging of contaminated waste. Transfer: the carpenter's removal instances end in cutting contaminated material down and packaging it for licensed disposal under containment; this cell does exactly that autonomously on hazardous material brought to it inside an enclosure.

sources.title: Laser-focused on Revolutionary Robots | Southwest Research Institute
sources.claim: The SwRI/Xyrec Laser Coating Removal robot strips hazardous coatings layer-by-layer from large workpieces under closed-loop computer-vision control while immediately vacuuming the removed paint effluent, and moved into a custom-built facility for commercial launch of the service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of hazardous coatings. Transfer: lead-paint work requires removing a toxic coating from a component without dispersing it; the LCR removes coating under vision control with immediate capture of the hazardous effluent, on components presented to the machine.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic — Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Canvas drywall-finishing robots work as crew members on real commercial construction projects, spraying joint compound and machine-sanding with an integrated vacuum that captures 99.9 percent of the sanding dust — demonstrating robotic dust-hazard control during finishing on unstructured jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drywall sanding with dust capture. Transfer: shows that dust-generating hazardous work with integrated capture is executed by a mobile robot on an ordinary jobsite, the same environment class as the carpenter's dust-controlled cutting and drilling.

sources.developer: RWTH Aachen / Robotnik / Eurecat consortium (EU H2020)
sources.title: Bots2ReC - Analysis of Key Findings for the Application Development of Semi-Autonomous Asbestos Removal
sources.claim: The EU Bots2ReC project built mobile manipulators for semi-autonomous asbestos removal (grinding plaster, tiles and adhesive) in apartment buildings; the project ended in 2019 as a research demonstrator with roughly 90% surface accessibility and no completed comparison against manual abatement.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute / US DOE
sources.title: BOA: Asbestos Pipe-Insulation Removal Robot System — CMU Robotics Institute
sources.claim: Carnegie Mellon's BOA prototype crawler automatically stripped asbestos lagging from industrial pipe runs and bagged it under continuous vacuum, meeting the airborne fiber limit, but remained a phase-limited proof-of-concept (4-inch straight pipe, laborious emplacement) demonstrated for DOE sites.

tasks.label: Build sleds from logs and timbers for use in hauling camp buildings and machinery through wooded areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field build in the timber: carpenter selects and fells/bucks logs near the haul route, hews flats on two runners with axe/chainsaw, cuts saddle notches and bores holes, and spikes/bolts cross-bunks and a pull-nose together on the uneven forest floor, in mud, snow, or rain.

Putting an existing camp building on skids: jacking a bunkhouse or cook shack, blocking it, cutting and fitting runner timbers under the sills in situ, and bolting the sled frame to the building's sills at its site in the woods.

Build at the camp yard or landing from sawn mill timbers and hardware on hand: cutting runners and bunks to length with portable saws, boring with an auger, and drift-bolting the sled together on a rough, graded outdoor yard controlled by the logging outfit.

Shop fabrication of a heavy-timber sled/skid frame in a permanent carpentry or timber shop: timbers cut to length, ends shaped/turned up, notches and bolt holes machined, frame assembled with bolts and steel strap shoes, then trucked to the woods.

Field repair/refit of a damaged sled: replacing a split or worn runner, re-shoeing a runner with steel strap, refastening loosened bunks, done at the camp or along the haul road with hand and portable tools.

sources.date: 2026-04 (product page); machine line in commercial use for years
sources.title: 5-axis machining center - K2-Industry series - Hans Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger K2-Industry CNC joinery machining centres automatically saw, drill, and notch structural timbers (passing cross-sections up to 300 x 450 mm, optionally larger) without manual measuring or marking, in industrial timber-construction plants.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting runners and cross-bunks to length, shaping ends, notching and boring bolt holes in heavy timbers is the machining half of building a timber sled; the machine handles the same species, sizes and precision.

sources.system: Hundegger K2i 1300 6-axis robot CNC machine at Canadian Timberframes
sources.title: Canadian Timberframes Expands and Introduces a K2i machine with 6-Axis robot; to process mass timber
sources.claim: A commercial timber-frame manufacturer installed a Hundegger K2i 1300 CNC machine with an integrated 6-axis robot to process heavy/mass timber members in its 34,000 sq ft plant.
sources.transferJustification: Heavy timber members for frames are the same class of workpiece (large sawn/glulam beams) as sled runners and bunks; the cell machines them to shape unattended.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - AutoEyeTruss System
sources.claim: Randek's AutoEyeTruss system automatically identifies a laid-up timber truss by machine vision and picks, places, positions and ... connector plates without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Fastening a timber assembly (members joined by plates/fasteners at machine-set positions) is the assembly half of sled building; vision-guided automatic fastening handles member-to-member joints of comparable size and tolerance.

sources.system: House of Design robotic roof/floor truss assembly cells
sources.title: Louws Truss turns to tech and robotics | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: House of Design robotic truss lines have robots pick and place lumber members in sequenced layout on the assembly table and embed connector plates; such a line has been running in production at Louws Truss since 2022 and the technology is being adopted by Builders FirstSource.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic pick-place-and-fasten of dimensional lumber into a rigid frame at production quality is the same operation as laying up and fastening a sled's runners and cross-bunks in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Storti Flex 2600 automated pallet nailing system
sources.date: 2005-06 (trade press); machines in long-standing commercial use
sources.title: British Pallet Company Stays On Track for Growth, Expansion — Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Fully automated stringer-pallet nailing machines assemble wooden skids — deck members nailed across longitudinal stringers/runners — with no manual placement, in sizes up to 72 x 60 inches.
sources.transferJustification: A stringer pallet/skid is structurally the same object as a small timber sled: cross members fastened to longitudinal runners; the machine performs the complete build to accepted quality in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Krüsi CM-40 log home milling machine (CNC-controlled option)
sources.developer: Krüsi Maschinenbau (Switzerland), distributed by Timber Tools in North America
sources.date: 2025 (vendor page); product in long-standing commercial sale
sources.title: Log Home Milling Machine CM-40 Log Mill, CNC controlled or manual
sources.claim: CNC log-home milling machines process round logs, D-logs and square logs in a single pass, producing profiled, notched log members; over 800 manual and 23 ... units installed.
sources.transferJustification: Hewing flats and cutting notches in round logs is exactly what a log sled's runners and bunks require; log-home mills perform this machining on natural round logs under machine control.

sources.system: Optimized log bucking lines with laser/LED scanning (e.g., JoeScan-equipped mill lines)
sources.date: 2006-06 article; technology standard and updated through 2024 trade coverage
sources.title: Sawlines: Scanners, Computers Optimize Machines — Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Modern sawmill lines scan irregular natural logs (including sweep and crook) and automatically compute and execute optimized bucking and sawing solutions in the mill yard/infeed.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that rough, irregular logs — the sled's raw material — can be sensed and cut to size autonomously once conveyed into a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.title: Automated Harvesting With Robots In The Forest — Wood Business
sources.claim: Forest-industry R&D leaders state that no machine has been built that can work autonomously in the forest environment; harvesting automation efforts remain semi-autonomous or teleoperated.

sources.system: Mobile robot platform for on-site timber assembly (biomimetic shell pavilion)
sources.developer: University research team (published in Automation in Construction)
sources.title: Automated on-site assembly of timber buildings on the example of a biomimetic shell
sources.claim: On-site robotic timber assembly remains a research prototype: a tracked mobile platform with a robot arm and nail-gun gripper assembled prefabricated timber sticks into beam networks for a single pavilion test.

tasks.label: Construct forms or chutes for pouring concrete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new-build lot: carpenter snaps layout on excavated/graded ground, cuts and nails plywood-and-2x lumber footing and stem-wall forms (or sets handset panels/ICFs), stakes and braces them, plumbs and levels to string lines and grade stakes, adds keyways, sleeve blockouts and step forms on sloping ground; mud, rain, uneven soil and buried obstructions are normal.

Flatwork and site concrete: setting 2x or flexible edge forms and screed rails for slabs-on-grade, driveways, sidewalks, patios, curbs and equipment pads; driving stakes into subgrade, setting forms to grade/slope with laser or string, radius forms for curves, plus occasionally knocking together a wooden chute or splash board to direct truck concrete into a footing.

Commercial site: erecting modular gang/handset wall and column formwork (Symons, PERI, Doka) for basement walls, shear walls, cores and columns - laying out, hanging panels, installing snap ties and wedges, walers and strongbacks, blockouts for openings and embeds, crane-setting gang forms, then plumbing, aligning and bracing before the pour.

Elevated structure: building deck formwork and falsework - erecting shoring towers or post-shores over an in-progress floor, setting stringers and joists, laying plywood decking, forming beam bottoms and sides, edge forms, drops, pour stops, screed rails and openings, at height with congested trades around.

Precast/tilt-up casting yard or plant: forming elements on casting beds or pallets - setting side rails/shutters to element dimensions from shop drawings, fixing bulkheads, chamfer strips and blockouts for windows, doors and embeds, applying release agent, then stripping shutters after cure, inside a covered standardized production facility.

sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants - Multi-Function-Shuttering-Robot
sources.claim: Sommer's Multi-Function-Shuttering-Robot is a commercial machine in precast pallet circulation plants that scans the pallet, computes shutter positions, picks magnetic shuttering profiles from magazines, places and aligns longitudinal and cross shutters, activates magnets, sets recess/insert magnets and oils the casting surface - i.e. it builds the form the concrete is poured into.

sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production
sources.claim: Elematic's Shuttering Robot E9 is a fenced, CAD/BIM-driven robotic station that places shutters on the casting table according to the production plan for double walls, filigree slabs, solid walls and sandwich panels, and can also strip them after cure.

sources.title: Keegan Precast adds to portfolio with a new pallet circulation system - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: A fully automated third-generation Weckenmann shuttering robot is in production service at Keegan Precast in Ireland, shuttering double wall, floor slab and solid wall elements at a single pallet position on a pallet circulation line, reducing manual shuttering to a minimum.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robots on Guedel TrackMotion rails (SCADAware wall sheathing cell)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: A deployed four-robot cell at builder Rehkemper & Son fixtures timber wall frames on a motorized table, straightens warped studs, and nails OSB sheathing to the frame while cutting window and door openings from the digital design, holding roughly 1/16 inch alignment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fabrication of plywood/OSB-faced timber panels in a fixtured cell. Job-built concrete forms use the same materials (2x lumber frame, plywood/OSB face, nailed) at similar tolerances, so demonstrated cutting and nailing of sheathed panels transfers to building form panels when the work is fixtured on a table.

sources.system: Odico Factory-On-The-Fly robotic hot-wire formwork cutting
sources.title: Danish Tech firm launches robot system for construction sites
sources.claim: Odico's robotic hot-wire cutting system produces concrete formwork moulds, including double-curved geometries, from digital models; its formwork was used for load-bearing concrete at Fjordenhus, and the process is packaged as a containerized robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (fabricating formwork for concrete pours), performed by subtractive robotic cutting of EPS moulds inside a purpose-built robotic cell rather than by site carpentry; shows machine construction of pour-ready forms with non-planar geometry.

sources.title: Doka showcases automation-driven formwork solutions at bauma 2025
sources.claim: Doka's most advanced on-site formwork robot as of bauma 2025 is the DokaXbot Lift, a ..., ground-operated device for positioning slab formwork panels - an operator-controlled assist, not an autonomous formwork-erecting system; no autonomous site robot that builds or erects formwork was found.

tasks.label: Apply shock-absorbing, sound-deadening, or decorative paneling to ceilings or walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential interior: carpenter applies decorative paneling to walls/ceilings of a private home — shiplap, beadboard, plank accent walls, wainscot panels, tongue-and-groove ceiling boards. Measures, scribes to out-of-plumb walls, cuts around outlets/windows, glues and finish-nails to studs or furring; home occupied or under renovation.

Commercial fit-out, open field: installing acoustic/decorative ceiling panels or ceiling boards on a suspended grid across large open floors (offices, schools, big-box retail) in a building under construction — repetitive full-size panels on a regular grid, worked overhead from stilts/scaffold.

Commercial fit-out, edges and complex areas: perimeter and cut-to-fit ceiling panels, small rooms, corridors, soffits, panels notched around diffusers, sprinklers, lights and ducts; also ceiling panel replacement in existing occupied buildings.

Multifamily/commercial construction: applying sound-deadening layers to walls — soundboard, acoustical gypsum panels over resilient channel, mass-loaded barrier on party walls and mechanical rooms — full sheets screwed to studs/furring in an unfinished building, with openings cut for boxes.

Specialty acoustic/decorative wall panels: fabric-wrapped acoustic panels, perforated boards and wood-slat panels in theaters, studios, restaurants, conference and worship spaces; laid out to reveals, hung on Z-clips/impaling clips or furring, tight alignment tolerances in a custom one-off room.

Offsite prefabrication plant: applying gypsum/sound-deadening or decorative panel layers to wall and ceiling elements lying on production tables in a panelized/modular factory, fastening them and cutting openings before elements ship.

sources.system: 天井ボード取付ロボット (ceiling board attachment robot)
sources.title: 天井ボード取付ロボットと移動式天台を開発～システム天井施工における省人化と仮設材の大幅削減を実現～ (Kajima press release)
sources.claim: Kajima (with Tmsuk) developed a ceiling-board attachment robot that, from a simple tablet instruction, measures its position relative to the ceiling framing and autonomously moves and fastens suspended-ceiling boards; it has been introduced on an office building the company is currently constructing.
sources.transferJustification: システム天井 (system ceiling) boards are the suspended-grid acoustic/decorative ceiling panels used in office buildings — the same objects, the same overhead grid mounting and fastening precision as the US acoustic/decorative ceiling paneling task.

sources.system: 天井ボード取付ロボット (ceiling board attachment robot)
sources.title: 天井ボード取付ロボットと移動式天台を開発 (Kajima press release)
sources.claim: On the live office-building site the robot works from a 40-board stocker at about one board per minute until the specified area is done, selecting trajectories that avoid ducts and seismic braces above the grid, while the worker installs only the narrow areas the robot cannot reach; two robots plus one worker replaced a conventional two-worker crew.
sources.transferJustification: Same suspended-grid ceiling panel work; establishes worker-comparable pace and quality on an actual construction site, and that edge/narrow-area panels remain human work.

sources.title: 清水建設が天井施工ロボットをついに実用化、30年越しで開発成功 | 日経Robotics
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Ceiling, a two-armed autonomous mobile robot that grips a ceiling board and screws it to the ceiling framing, was applied on an actual Japanese construction site in March 2023, installing roughly 100 boards with a 100% success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Ceiling board application to overhead framing is the same handling, positioning and fastening operation as applying sound-deadening/decorative ceiling paneling, with panels of the same size and ~14 kg weight class.

sources.title: Autonomous Robot for Ceiling Board Construction Work "Robo-Buddy Ceiling" (IEEE Xplore)
sources.claim: Technical description confirming Robo-Buddy Ceiling is an autonomous mobile robot with two industrial arms — one carrying a laser sensor and screwdriver, the other vacuum pads to grasp the ... — built to replace skilled overhead ceiling-board work done on scaffolds.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy of the ceiling-panel installation system cited above; the object handled (plasterboard ceiling panel) matches the paneling task.

sources.title: This Plant Runs Itself — Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: At FrameTec's component plant in Camp Verde, Arizona, two Randek ZeroLabor robots apply sheathing panels to wall panels, fasten them and rout out door and window openings; Randek's commercially launched robotic system needs only line monitoring and raw-material unloading labor.
sources.transferJustification: Applying large sheet panels to a fixtured wall frame, fastening and trimming them is the same operation as applying sound-deadening or decorative panel layers — same 4x8-class sheets, same fastening precision, work brought to the machine.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 / M-500 multifunction bridge
sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges (brochure, Stiles Machinery)
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ CNC multifunction bridges carry out all sheathing work on timber-frame wall, ceiling, roof and gable elements fully automatically — fixing, formatting and cutting all openings — with gypsum plasterboard and facade panels among the listed materials and automatic board magazines available to feed boards.
sources.transferJustification: Planking wall and ceiling elements with gypsum plasterboard or facade/decorative panels in a fixtured production cell is the paneling operation itself, performed with the work brought to the machine (E1).

sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor (Phys.org)
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously picked up and screwed a gypsum board to a wall at a simulated residential construction ..., but only as a laboratory prototype, far slower than a craftsman.
sources.transferJustification: Wall board application is the closest analogue to sound-deadening/decorative wall paneling; cited to show that on-site (E3) wall paneling exists only as a slow lab prototype, not at worker quality.

tasks.label: Join edges of carpet and seam edges where necessary, by sewing or by using tape with glue and heated carpet iron.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home, stretch-in broadloom over pad in a living room or bedroom: installer trims the factory edges (double-cut or slotted-blade cut), slides hot-melt seam tape under the butted edges, runs the heated seaming iron along the tape while feeding the carpet onto it behind the iron, weights/rolls the seam, blends the pile and seals the cut edges. Kneeling work in a furnished room with walls, doorways and pad underfoot.

Private home, small or awkward seams: closet and hallway extensions, doorway transitions, stair landings, patching a damaged area with a donor piece, seams in irregular rooms. Short seams in tight space, pile-direction and pattern matching, frequent repositioning of the iron and body.

Commercial building (office suite, hotel corridor, school, clinic) direct glue-down broadloom: long straight seams butted into wet or pressure-sensitive adhesive, edges cut and seam-sealed with liquid sealer or trimmed with a row-cutter; work performed after hours in an occupied, institution-controlled facility with a fixed layout.

Large hospitality/pattern-matched installation (hotel ballroom, casino, convention space): wide-width patterned carpet where seams must be pattern-matched, edges pulled together with stay nails/stretchers while the hot-melt tape is ironed, seams rolled and cross-seams aligned over long runs inside a controlled commercial facility.

Shop or warehouse prefabrication: joining or sewing carpet pieces off site — hand-sewn or serged seams for custom area rugs, aviation/marine carpet, or panels seamed on a flat work surface before delivery to the job. Work is done on tables/floor in a company-controlled shop.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named "Robo-Buddy Floor"
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Floor autonomously installs raised access floor pedestals and panels on a live high-rise construction project to within 1 mm, showing the current frontier of autonomous flooring work — rigid modular panel placement, not flexible carpet seaming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor covering installation on a jobsite. Transfer to carpet seaming FAILS: the robot places rigid 10 kg panels onto pedestals at known grid positions; it does not trim carpet edges, lay hot-melt tape, control a heated seaming iron, or blend pile on a compliant, deformable material.

sources.title: Project Highlight: Advancing Automated Robotic Sewing - ARM Institute
sources.claim: The Sewbo/Siemens ARM Institute project demonstrated a robotic workcell that handles, aligns and sews structural garment seams (jeans side seams and rises) in denim with closed-loop monitoring, integrated into an existing apparel assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine sewing of textile seams in a fixtured workcell. Transfer to carpet seaming FAILS on objects and precision: denim panels are light, thin and machine-feedable, whereas broadloom carpet is 12-ft-wide, heavy, stiff pile goods whose seams are made with hot-melt tape and a heated iron and judged on invisible pile blending, pattern match and no peaking; no demonstration handles carpet.

sources.title: Sewbots® - Softwear Automation
sources.claim: SoftWear Automation's Sewbots use machine vision to steer fabric through a sew head and have automatically sewn T-shirts and similar light sewn goods in a factory workline; no carpet or heavy floor-covering application is shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sewing of textile goods. Transfer FAILS: light apparel fabric handled by vacuum grippers on a sewing table is not comparable to joining thick, heavy carpet edges; the cited worklines are product-specific (T-shirts, pillowcases) and no carpet seaming is demonstrated.

sources.title: Artificial Grass Seaming Technology | EasySeam Machine | Watersavers Turf
sources.claim: State-of-the-art carpet/turf seaming equipment remains a hand-guided device: the EasySeam machine is walked along the joint by an installer to activate the seam tape's adhesive, with the operator aligning the two edges by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Directly comparable task (tape-and-heat seaming of pile floor covering), cited to show the best available seaming machine is manually placed and guided by a worker, so it cannot support a positive autonomous judgment at any tier.

tasks.label: Cut carpet padding to size and install padding, following prescribed method.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Re-carpet of a bedroom or living room in an occupied private home: worker measures the room, rolls out rebond pad in strips over a plywood subfloor, cuts each strip to the room outline with a utility knife (around jambs, closet returns, floor vents), butts and tapes seams, staples the pad every few inches along seams and perimeter without covering the tack strip, and trims flush to the tack strip. Furniture and existing conditions vary house to house.

New-construction house or multifamily apartment unit, rooms empty and swept, plywood subfloor with tack strip already set: pad rolled out, cut to size room by room to a repetitive floor plan, stapled and seam-taped; several rooms per unit in one visit.

Stairs, hallways, closets and other irregular areas: pad cut into tread-sized pieces and stapled over each tread and nosing (or a full runner wrapped over nosings), plus small odd-shaped pieces fitted into closets, alcoves and around door casings.

Commercial job in an existing office, hotel or retail space over a concrete slab: adhesive troweled or spread, pad rolled out and cut to walls, columns and door openings, seams taped, pad rolled down; often performed after hours in a facility controlled by the building owner.

Repair or partial replacement: damaged or wet pad cut out and removed, subfloor cleaned, a matching patch of pad cut to the irregular opening, stapled or glued and taped to the surrounding pad before the carpet is re-stretched.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insulating and sheathing of floor cassettes in a prefab housing factory. It does not address on-site work.

sources.title: This Plant Runs Itself - Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: Trade press reports Randek ZeroLabor robots running in production offsite-construction plants, cutting, framing, sheathing and gluing building elements with little human input.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; this item establishes that the cell runs in real production with minimal human intervention rather than as a demo, supporting the 'limited intervention' requirement at E1.

tasks.label: Inspect the surface to be covered to determine its condition, and correct any imperfections that might show through carpet or cause carpet to wear unevenly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential re-carpet of bedrooms/living areas in an occupied or recently vacated home: after old carpet and pad are pulled, the installer walks the wood subfloor, pulls leftover staples and tack-strip nails, hammers or screws down popped/loose nails and squeaky spots, sweeps debris, scrapes off drywall mud, paint drips and old adhesive, fills gouges, seams and low spots with floor patch, and sands high spots so nothing telegraphs through the new carpet. Furniture, walls, doorways and pets/occupants are present.

New residential construction or a full-house re-carpet in an empty house: broad areas of plywood/OSB subfloor across many rooms on an active jobsite; sweep and vacuum construction debris, screw down squeaks, knock down or sand high panel seams and dried glue/mud ridges, fill nail holes and gaps, verify flatness before pad goes down.

Commercial or institutional interior (office suite, hotel guest floor, school, clinic) over a concrete slab: inspect slab for old adhesive residue, curling, cracks, high spots and depressions; scrape/grind residue and high spots, fill cracks and low areas with patching or self-leveling compound, feather edges, do moisture/pH checks, clean before glue-down carpet or carpet tile.

Stairs, closets, hallways and transitions in homes and small commercial spaces: confined geometry with treads, risers, nosings and thresholds; fix squeaky or loose treads, shim or plane transitions to adjacent hard flooring, remove old fasteners and clean tight corners so the carpet lies flat.

Problem substrates found on inspection: water-damaged or rotted subfloor sections, delaminated underlayment, badly out-of-level or springy floors, old plank floors requiring new underlayment - the installer cuts out and replaces sections, adds underlayment sheets, and does heavy leveling before carpet can be laid.
