sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System (FANUC six-axis robots, 3M vision system and repair controller)
sources.developer: 3M with General Motors and FANUC America
sources.title: General Motors and 3M Partner on New Robotic Paint System | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it robotic paint repair ... uses a vision system to find surface defects and robotically sands and polishes them out; GM installed the first automated paint repair application on a moving production line at its Spring Hill, TN assembly plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-vision inspection of a large surface for imperfections followed by localized abrasive correction to an appearance standard. It transfers because the work structure is identical to inspecting a floor and knocking down/smoothing defects that would show through a finish, with equal or tighter precision, though on fixtured sheet metal rather than a nailed-down subfloor.

sources.system: ACP-100 autonomous concrete polisher retrofit (LightWare SF40/C LiDAR)
sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing | LightWare LiDAR
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 retrofit gives concrete floor polishers autonomous LiDAR navigation, but the machine performs only the open-floor polishing pass while human contractors still do the hand grinding, caulking and cleaning parts of a flooring job.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-situ floor-processing system found; cited to show that on real building floors the automated machine covers only the open-area abrasive pass, so it does not substantiate whole-instance floor inspection and defect correction at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Canvas develops an automated robot for the drywall finishing
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot applies and sands joint compound to Level 4/5 finishes on commercial construction sites, but each machine works under a human operator's oversight and it finishes vertical drywall, not floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site application of compound and sanding to a flatness standard. Cited as the nearest jobsite analog, but it is wall-mounted work under continuous operator oversight, so it cannot substantiate autonomous floor inspection and imperfection correction at E3.

tasks.label: Take measurements and study floor sketches to calculate the area to be carpeted and the amount of material needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied residential home, retail carpet replacement: installer walks bedrooms, living room, hallway and closets with furniture in place and the homeowner present, tapes/laser-measures wall-to-wall dimensions, checks them against the salesperson's measure sketch, and calculates yardage, pad and trim including waste and seam placement for a 12-ft roll.

New construction or gut renovation (single-family, multifamily or commercial buildout): bare, unoccupied rooms on an active jobsite with other trades working, dust and debris; installer verifies field dimensions against architect's plans and computes carpet/pad area per room or unit and total material to order.

Occupied commercial facility (office suite, hotel guest floor, school, clinic) measured during or after hours: long corridors, open-plan areas and repeating rooms; installer measures runs, studies the floor plan, and calculates broadloom yardage or carpet-tile counts plus attic stock.

Stairs, closets and irregular areas in a residential job: counting treads and risers, measuring winders, bay windows, curved or angled walls and doorway transitions, then converting to running feet/yardage of carpet and binding.

Desk/shop takeoff with no new site measurement: installer or lead studies the architect's plan or the sales measure sheet at the shop, scales rooms, computes net area, waste allowance, seam diagram and the material order before loading the truck.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Trimble (deployed by Mace Group)
sources.title: How one construction contractor is using Spot the Robot Dog | Equipment World
sources.claim: Spot quadruped carrying a Trimble X7 laser scanner autonomously walked an active building project for Mace, stopping at designated waypoints to capture as-built scans used for dimensional comparison against the BIM model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built dimensional capture of building interiors. The physical act the carpet task requires is acquiring accurate room dimensions on site; the scanner captures the same wall-to-wall geometry a tape measure would, on an unstructured jobsite.

sources.developer: Trimble / Boston Dynamics (deployed by Hensel Phelps)
sources.title: See Spot Scan: Robots in Your Workplace - xyHt
sources.claim: Hensel Phelps used Spot with a Trimble X7 in autonomous waypoint-mission mode inside Denver International Airport's Great Hall renovation to capture as-built point clouds that were auto-registered on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior as-built measurement inside an institution-controlled facility (airport terminal). Same measurement output (room and corridor geometry at millimetre level) that the carpet area calculation is built from.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot autonomous indoor scanning
sources.title: SAJO Deploys 1st Autonomous Indoor Scanning Operation on a Construction Site In Canada with Spot the Robot
sources.claim: SAJO deployed Spot for autonomous indoor scanning of existing conditions across an 88,000 sq ft, seven-floor university building, with automated scan registration, self-docking, and point-cloud-to-architectural-plan comparison.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: capturing existing-condition dimensions of interior rooms. It produces the room geometry from which floor area is computed, in occupied/renovation building interiors.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC autonomous laser scanning module (on Spot)
sources.title: LEICA BLK ARC AUTONOMOUS LASER SCANNING MODULE (spec sheet)
sources.claim: The Leica BLK ARC is a commercially sold autonomous laser-scanning payload for Spot with SLAM-based autonomous navigation and stated indoor accuracy of about plus/minus 10 mm, adequate for room dimensioning.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the autonomous robotic scanner's measurement accuracy (about 0.4 in indoors) meets the tolerance carpet takeoffs are worked to (nearest inch plus allowance).

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with laser scanner / 360 camera (autonomous site scanning workflow)
sources.title: How autonomous construction scanning creates a repeatable site record | DroneDeploy
sources.claim: Autonomous quadruped scanning of construction interiors is an established commercial workflow; the robot walks predefined routes over stairs, ramps and uneven slabs while a laser scanner and 360 ... capture spatial data.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the stairs/irregular-area instance: the same autonomous scanning platform reaches and captures stairs and non-rectangular spaces that must be measured for stair carpet.

sources.system: ArcGIS Indoors / Generate Floor Plan From Point Cloud tool
sources.title: Preparing to Generate Floor Plans from Point Clouds - Esri Community
sources.claim: Shipping GIS/CAD software converts robot-captured indoor point clouds into floor plans automatically (ArcGIS Pro 'Generate Floor Plan From Point ...'), yielding room boundaries and areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related step: converts the robot's point cloud into room-level floor plans, the intermediate from which carpet area is calculated. It is non-robotic processing paired with the robotic capture cited above.

sources.system: MeasureSquare AI Takeoff (and Cyncly Measure Desktop)
sources.title: AI Takeoff Software | Measure Square
sources.claim: Flooring estimating packages automatically detect room areas from plans and compute material quantities, seams and cuts for carpet and other roll goods.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the calculation half of the task (area, waste, seam plan, material amount) once dimensions exist; being software only, it cannot by itself substantiate any on-site instance.

tasks.label: Install carpet on some floors using adhesive, following prescribed method.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Direct glue-down broadloom in a commercial fit-out (new or renovated office floor, school, church hall): installer chalks layout lines, cuts 12-ft-wide roll goods to room dimensions with allowance, spreads pressure-sensitive or multipurpose adhesive with a notched trowel over the swept/prepped concrete or wood subfloor, lays and butts sheets, cuts and seams edges, trims to walls and columns, and rolls the field with a 75-100 lb roller. Site is an active jobsite with trades, dust, temporary lighting.

Modular carpet tile (24x24 or 18x18 squares) set in releasable pressure-sensitive adhesive in office suites: gridline layout from room center, adhesive rolled or spread, tiles set tight with correct pile direction (quarter-turn/monolithic), perimeter and column tiles scribed and knife-cut, tiles fitted around workstations, floor boxes and door thresholds. Often phased around occupied areas in a managed building.

Residential/light-commercial glue-down over concrete: basement rec room, sunroom, stairs and porches with indoor-outdoor carpet. Rooms are small and irregular, furniture and appliances must be worked around, old flooring and adhesive scraped off first, carpet templated to closets, jogs and door casings, glued and rolled, transitions and cap trim installed.

Small glue-down details and repairs: stair treads and risers, hallways and vestibules, walk-off entry mats, patching a burned or stained section by cutting out and gluing in a matched piece, re-gluing loose seams or curled edges, gluing cove base or carpet cap trim, in occupied homes and businesses.

Phased glue-down in an occupied institutional facility (hotel corridor and ballroom, hospital wing, cinema, retail store) worked at night or in short closures: tear out old glued carpet, scrape and prep residue, spread adhesive, lay and seam new carpet around fixed furniture, doors and equipment, and return the space to service by morning.

sources.title: A Production System for a New Era — Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy is an autonomous two-armed construction robot deployed on Japanese building sites that installs ceiling boards and raised-floor pedestals and panels — the closest deployed 'floor covering installation' robot, but it handles rigid modular panels dry-laid on pedestals, not adhesive-spread carpet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing floor-system panels on a building floor. It shows autonomous mobile manipulation on jobsite floors, but the objects are rigid access-floor panels placed on pedestals with no adhesive spreading, no roll goods, no seaming and no scribing/trimming to walls, so it does not substantiate glue-down carpet installation.

sources.system: Floor tile laying robot (P900-class paving robot)
sources.title: Floor tile laying robot – ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: Commercially offered Chinese floor-tile paving robots navigate a room, apply tile adhesive and place rigid ceramic/porcelain tiles autonomously; this is the nearest demonstrated adhesive-plus-covering flooring automation, but it handles rigid tiles, not limp carpet requiring cutting, seaming and stretching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying a floor covering into adhesive. Transfer fails: rigid 450–900 mm tiles are gripped and set on a mortar/adhesive bed at fixed grid pitch, whereas carpet is limp roll goods that must be templated, knife-cut to walls, seamed and rolled; no source shows these machines handling textile floor covering.

sources.title: This Construction Robot Can Level Floors and Lay Tiles Automatically
sources.claim: A construction robot from Coboticz is shown in video automating floor leveling, adhesive application and tile ...; the demonstration is a video clip of tile work, with no evidence of textile/roll-goods installation and no established autonomy or field deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adhesive application and covering placement on a floor. Autonomy is not established from a promotional video and the material is rigid tile, so it cannot support a positive judgment for glue-down carpet.

sources.title: RoBuild Robotics | Autonomous Floor-Laying for Interior Finishes
sources.claim: RoBuild Robotics markets an autonomous floor-laying robot for luxury vinyl plank in commercial interiors; the product is an early-stage startup offering for click-lock rigid planks, not adhesive-set carpet, and no completed installation is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing resilient floor covering in commercial buildings. Objects are rigid interlocking planks placed without troweled adhesive; nothing documents cutting, seaming or gluing carpet, and autonomy/completion are unverified.

sources.title: meet lionel - Autonomous Floor Marking Robot
sources.claim: August Robotics' Lionel autonomously marks exhibition floor layouts in venues and operates over carpeted floors around people, showing autonomous navigation and floor-referenced precision in human work facilities — but it only marks lines, it does not install any covering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out floor plans (the chalk-line/layout step that precedes carpet gluing). It substantiates only autonomous layout marking; it performs no adhesive application, cutting, placement, seaming or trimming, so it cannot substantiate completing the installation.

tasks.label: Clean up before and after installation, including vacuuming carpet and discarding remnant pieces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home, one or more rooms re-carpeted: after seaming and stretching, the installer vacuums the new carpet (fiber shed, tuft ends, thread, dust), gathers carpet and pad offcuts, tack-strip cut-offs, seam tape and cardboard cores, bags or rolls them, and carries them out past furniture to the truck for disposal.

Residential pre-installation prep after old carpet and pad are torn out: sweep/vacuum the plywood or concrete subfloor free of dust, old pad crumbs, staples and nail fragments, remove leftover debris and haul the old material out to the truck, so the new pad can be laid.

Vacant rental/apartment turnover unit or new-build tract house: empty rooms, drywall dust and construction debris on the subfloor; vacuum before laying, vacuum the finished carpet, and carry remnants and trimmings out to a shared dumpster.

Occupied commercial facility (office suite, hotel corridor, school, clinic) re-carpeted after hours in phases: vacuum the finished broadloom or carpet tile with a commercial vacuum, collect tile scrap, offcuts, adhesive pails and cartons into bins, and move them to a loading dock or dumpster before the space reopens.

Active commercial new-construction or renovation job site: other trades working nearby, dusty and cluttered floors, temporary lighting; sweep/vacuum the slab before installation, then vacuum the new carpet and clear remnants to a debris pile or dumpster.

sources.system: Whiz (SoftBank Robotics / ICE Robotics, BrainOS navigation)
sources.title: Whiz Product Overview | Softbank Robotics
sources.claim: SoftBank Whiz is a commercially deployed autonomous vacuum sweeper that vacuums carpet in large commercial spaces (hotels, airports, offices, campuses) after a route is taught once, showing that the carpet-vacuuming portion of cleanup is automated at the level of a structured human work facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine commercial carpet vacuuming. It transfers to the post-installation vacuuming step because the surface, the soil (fiber, dust, small debris) and the acceptance standard are the same; it does not cover collecting or hauling remnants.

sources.title: Tennant Releases Small, Agile Autonomous Floor Cleaner – Ideal For Small Facilities
sources.claim: Brain Corp-powered Tennant autonomous floor-cleaning robots are in large-scale commercial deployment cleaning floors in retail, schools and healthcare facilities, indicating mature, reliable autonomous floor cleaning of mapped areas inside human work facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor cleaning of mapped commercial floor areas; transfers to the sweep/vacuum step of pre- and post-installation cleanup on both hard subfloor and carpet, but not to picking up and hauling scrap.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker autonomously identifies and picks bulky construction and demolition offcuts off a conveyor and drops them into chutes/bins inside a fenced sorting station — the discarding-of-remnants step when the scrap is presented as a purpose-built cell would present it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting of bulky construction/demolition offcuts. Objects (heavy, floppy, irregular building-material scrap), the grasp-and-drop-into-container action, and the accepted output (scrap segregated into a bin) match 'discarding remnant pieces' when the scrap arrives on a conveyor in a fenced cell.

sources.title: ZenRobotics 4.0 brings new smarts to automated garbage-picking
sources.claim: The Heavy Picker handles individual items up to 40 kg at 2,300 picks per hour using pre-trained AI recognition of hundreds of waste categories, showing worker-rate throughput and robustness for scrap handling in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Terex item: it quantifies payload and rate for picking bulky construction scrap into containers, the physical equivalent of tossing carpet and pad offcuts into a disposal bin.

sources.system: Tesla Optimus; Loki Robotics wheeled trash robot (as assessed by Epoch AI)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment finds that no robot can autonomously remove a trash bag from a bin, close it and carry it to an outdoor bin; the one wheeled system running shifts in corporate and campus buildings needs teleoperation for many edge cases and is ~10x slower than a human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting refuse inside a building and carrying it out to an external bin — the disposal half of this task. Negative evidence: it is unattained end-to-end at E2/E3, so remnant removal cannot be credited above a purpose-built presentation.

sources.title: Roborock Saros Z70 Robot Vacuum with OmniGrip™ Mechanical Arm
sources.claim: A consumer robot vacuum with a manipulator autonomously vacuums homes and picks up light stray items (socks, tissues, paper balls under ~300 g), placing them in designated spots — the limit of autonomous floor-object pickup in unstructured homes, far short of carpet offcuts, tack strip and hauling scrap to a truck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous home vacuuming plus pickup of small floor objects. It substantiates vacuuming at E3 but its 300 g payload and small-object repertoire do not cover carpet/pad offcuts, tack-strip cutoffs, or transport of scrap out of the dwelling.

sources.system: Clobot autonomous cleaning robot (POSCO E&C Shinbanpo 21 site)
sources.title: POSCO E&C deploys autonomous robots for post-construction cleanups
sources.claim: POSCO E&C deployed AI autonomous cleaning robots for post-construction cleanup of common spaces at an apartment reconstruction site, showing autonomous floor cleaning is entering construction settings — though the robots clean floors rather than collect and haul installation scrap.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-construction floor cleaning. It transfers to the sweeping/vacuuming component at a job site, but not to gathering remnants and carrying them to a dumpster.

tasks.label: Draw building diagrams and record dimensions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home measure-up before a carpet job: the estimator/installer walks a furnished, lived-in house (furniture, pets, kids' toys, closets, irregular rooms, stairs), measures each room wall-to-wall with tape/laser, and sketches a room-by-room diagram with dimensions, doorways, transitions and closet openings for the cut/seam plan.

Vacant residential space: a new-build house at the flooring stage (walls up, subfloor exposed, other trades working) or an empty existing house/apartment turn; measurer walks the empty rooms, records dimensions and stair counts, and draws the floor diagram used to order carpet and pad.

Commercial/institutional measure in a finished, operating building: office suite, hotel guestroom floor and corridors, school, clinic or retail store; measurer records corridor lengths, room dimensions, door openings and transitions and produces a dimensioned diagram/takeoff, sometimes working after hours around furniture and occupants.

Commercial construction or renovation job site: building under construction or gutted for remodel; measurer walks unfinished floors amid materials, debris and other trades to record as-built dimensions and draw the diagram for a carpet-tile or broadloom takeoff.

On-the-job diagram by the installing crew: while working in a home or small commercial space, the installer measures the room being carpeted, checks it against the ordered material, and sketches a quick layout/seam diagram with dimensions on paper or tablet amid tools, rolled goods and moved furniture.

sources.system: Spot quadruped with FieldAI Field Foundation Models
sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: FieldAI-powered Boston Dynamics Spot robots execute mapping and documentation missions autonomously on active construction sites with no prior maps and ..., deployed commercially with major contractors over two years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built mapping/documentation of building interiors. It carries over because recording a building's dimensions requires exactly this traverse-and-capture of interior geometry, in a less controlled setting than a finished building.

sources.system: Trimble X7 + FieldLink on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution
sources.claim: Trimble's X7 3D laser scanner integrated with Spot is sold as a turnkey product for autonomous scan missions on construction sites, with waypoint paths planned in FieldLink and scans auto-registered in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: survey-grade as-built capture of interior spaces. The captured point cloud yields the same wall-to-wall dimensions a measurer records, at far finer precision than carpet work requires.

sources.system: Spot + Trimble X7 at Denver International Airport terminal
sources.title: Exploring the use of bio-inspired autonomous robots in construction
sources.claim: Hensel Phelps used Spot carrying a Trimble X7 to perform autonomous walk-and-scan missions inside the Denver International Airport terminal, capturing as-built information compared against the BIM model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built dimensional documentation of a large occupied/institutional building interior; the deliverable (registered point cloud of rooms and corridors) is the dimensional record a floor diagram is drawn from.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot
sources.claim: The Leica BLK ARC mobile laser scanning module is a certified Spot payload enabling fully autonomous, repeatable scan missions of building and facility interiors; users plan a scan path and the robot scans on its own.

sources.system: Spot with Leica BLK ARC for facility reality capture
sources.title: Maintain Accurate Digital Twins with Autonomous Reality Capture | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets and describes routine autonomous robotic laser scanning of industrial facility interiors with Spot and the BLK ARC, converting existing inspection missions to scanning missions for repeat digital-twin capture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring interior reality capture inside operating, furnished facilities — the same traverse-and-measure activity required to record a building's dimensions in a structured human work facility.

sources.system: NavVis VLX / Leica BLK2GO SLAM scanners
sources.developer: NavVis / Leica Geosystems (study by academic authors)
sources.title: Assessment of SLAM scanner accuracy for outdoor and indoor surveying tasks
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed assessment finds SLAM mobile laser scanners (NavVis VLX, Leica BLK2GO — the handheld sibling of the robot-mounted BLK ARC) achieve about 5 mm accuracy indoors against total-station reference.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the mobile scanning sensors carried by the cited robots meet the precision a carpet measure needs (well under half an inch); it is a sensor-accuracy study, not an autonomy claim.

sources.developer: Tongji University authors, Computer-Aided Civil and Infrastructure Engineering
sources.title: Automatic generation of architecture drawings from point clouds
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed method automatically generates architectural drawings, including door labelling and annotated dimensions and areas, directly from building point clouds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing the dimensioned drawing itself from captured geometry. It supplies the 'draw the diagram and record dimensions' output step once a robot has captured the space; it is software, so it cannot by itself support a positive judgment.

sources.system: MeasureSquare Room Scanner (phone LiDAR) + MeasureSquare takeoff
sources.title: Room Scanner APP & Floor Plan Creator | Measure Square
sources.claim: Flooring-trade estimating vendor MeasureSquare sells a LiDAR room-scanner workflow in which a scan of a space produces a professional floor plan with wall-to-wall dimensions and door openings used directly for flooring quotes.
sources.transferJustification: Human-carried, not robotic; cited only to establish that a LiDAR-scan-derived dimensioned floor plan is an output the flooring trade accepts in place of a hand-drawn measure sheet.

tasks.label: Cut and install vinyl composition tile or vinyl base.
Fasten metal treads across door openings or where carpet meets flooring to hold carpet in place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home re-carpet: after stretching carpet in bedrooms/hallway, installer measures each doorway to hardwood, tile or vinyl, cuts a metal Z-bar/carpet-trim or double-edge tread to fit between jambs with a hacksaw or snips, nails or screws it to a wood subfloor, trims the carpet edge, hooks it on the pins and hammers the metal lip closed with a rubber mallet and tapping block; furniture, pets, uneven old floors and varied jamb profiles.

Apartment or rental turnover / budget re-carpet: several doorway transitions per unit to sheet vinyl or tile, plywood or concrete slab subfloor requiring masonry nails or adhesive, tight same-day schedule, tight closets and narrow hall doorways.

Occupied commercial or institutional facility (office suite, hotel corridor, clinic, school) worked after hours: metal edge/transition strips fastened to a concrete slab at doorways and long corridor breaks where broadloom or carpet tile meets resilient flooring; standardized layout, building staff control access.

New commercial construction or tenant fit-out: doorway and floor-transition strips installed while other trades, dust, debris and unfinished conditions are present; long runs, some ADA-compliant beveled metal treads screwed and anchored into slab.
Specialty work: metal stair nosings/treads over carpeted stairs, thresholds at exterior doors, and transitions on uneven or out-of-level substrates requiring shimming, scribing and custom cutting.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named "Robo-Buddy Floor"
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Floor is a twin-arm mobile construction robot that autonomously installs raised-floor pedestals and panels at an actual high-rise construction site; it is the closest deployed system to interior floor-covering installation, but it places standardized panels and does not cut, position or fasten metal transition treads, nor manipulate or secure carpet edges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior floor-material installation on a jobsite. Transfer fails for this task: the robot lays rigid 10 kg raised-floor panels on marked slabs, with no strip cutting, fastener driving into a doorway threshold, or compliant carpet-edge tucking under a metal lip.

sources.title: Meet DeWalt's new robotic drill, designed to bore holes into data center floors - Fast Company
sources.claim: DEWALT/August Robotics' DALE autonomously drills anchor holes in concrete floors of data centers under construction, showing autonomous floor-level drilling on a jobsite; it performs only hole drilling and neither places nor fastens metal transition strips nor handles carpet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling fastener holes in a building floor. It substantiates only the hole-drilling sub-step; the instance also requires cutting the tread to length, positioning it across a jamb, driving fasteners, trimming the carpet and closing the metal lip over the carpet edge, none of which DALE does.

sources.system: Prefab wall/floor panel nailing robot cell
sources.developer: Kawasaki Robotics (prefab house line); Randek ZeroLabor
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: Robotic cells in prefabricated-house factories autonomously nail sheathing panels to framed wall/floor elements presented on a fixtured line, the closest purpose-built (E1) precedent for driving fasteners into building floor assemblies; no such line has been shown fastening metal carpet treads or securing a carpet edge.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastener driving into fixtured wood building panels in a factory. It does not transfer to the whole instance: no cited factory system cuts and positions a metal tread across a door opening or tucks and clamps a carpet edge into it.

tasks.label: Move furniture from area to be carpeted and remove old carpet and padding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home or condo: crew clears a bedroom/living room — carrying out beds, dressers, sofas, TVs and boxes (some disassembled, some slid on the old carpet), then cuts the tacked-down carpet into strips, pulls it and the foam pad off the tack strips, pulls staples from the pad, hauls rolls out through doorways to the truck. Clutter, pets, tight doorways, varied floor plans.

Vacant residential unit (apartment turnover, empty house, remodel): little or no furniture to move; tear out worn carpet and pad over plywood or slab, cut into rolls, pull staples and damaged tack strip, sweep debris and load into a dumpster/truck.

Occupied commercial office suite (often after hours): move desks, task chairs, file cabinets and cubicle contents to an adjacent zone, then remove direct-glue broadloom or carpet tile, scrape residual adhesive and old pad remnants, stage debris for removal, keeping the space usable next morning.

Hospitality/institutional interior (hotel guest rooms and corridors, senior living, school, church): move beds, nightstands, tables or pews out of the room, strip old glued or tacked carpet and pad from rooms and hallways, remove staples and tack strips, and stage the old material for disposal.

Stairs, closets and tight/obstructed areas in any setting: remove carpet and pad from stair treads, risers and landings, work around toilets, radiators, hanging clothes and door casings, pry stair tack strips and pull hundreds of staples by hand.

sources.title: Why Brokk Original demolition power
sources.claim: Brokk's machines are the standard equipment class for interior demolition and strip-out work in tight indoor spaces, but they are remote-controlled by a human operator rather than autonomous, so they cannot substantiate autonomous completion of tear-out work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior demolition/floor and structure strip-out in occupied buildings — the nearest machine class to carpet and pad tear-out. Its operation is continuous remote control by an operator, so it does not support a positive autonomous judgment at any tier.

sources.title: Novastrip 1026: Asbestos Tile Removal-Tile Stripper
sources.claim: Purpose-built floor-covering removal machinery (tile/carpet strippers, ride-on scrapers) is human-operated equipment: the machine supplies force while a worker steers and judges the cut, so removal of installed floor covering is not performed under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removal of glued/fastened floor covering, essentially identical to pulling up old carpet and pad. The equipment is operator-driven, so it is not a robotic system acting under machine control and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor
sources.claim: The most capable general-purpose home humanoid shipping to houses still depends on human teleoperation for complex physical tasks, so no autonomous system is substantiated for clearing furniture from a room in a dwelling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household physical work including carrying and repositioning objects in homes. Reported reliance on teleoperation for complex tasks means it cannot substantiate autonomous furniture clearing.

sources.developer: Stanford University (SHAPE Lab) / University of Chicago
sources.title: RoomShift: Room-scale Dynamic Haptics for VR with Furniture-moving Swarm Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous furniture repositioning has been shown only in a research lab with a swarm of small scissor-lift bases moving lightweight tables and chairs a short distance for VR haptics; nothing in the demonstration removes flooring or carries heavy household furniture out of a room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving furniture within a room. Transfer fails: the demo repositions light, pre-selected furniture in a controlled lab and does no carpet or pad removal, so it does not substantiate the whole task instance.

sources.title: Figure 03 Is The Robot in Your Kitchen
sources.claim: Frontier home humanoid programs target light household chores such as laundry, dishwashing and tidying; there is no demonstrated capability for furniture clearing plus floor-covering demolition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of household objects in homes. The demonstrated repertoire is soft-goods and dish handling, not heavy furniture transport or destructive floor tear-out, so it does not transfer.

tasks.label: Measure, cut and install tackless strips along the baseboard or wall.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit carpet in an occupied single-family home: bedroom/living room over plywood/OSB subfloor. Installer pries out old strips, measures each wall run, snips tackless strip to length, sets it ~1/4 in. from the wall with pins angled toward the wall, hand- or air-nails it down, notches around door casings, closet returns, floor vents and inside/outside corners, gaps at doorways. Furniture and household clutter nearby.

Carpet over a concrete slab (basement, slab-on-grade room, condo): strip fastened with masonry pins, powder-actuated fasteners or adhesive/peel-and-stick strip; slab uneven, sometimes damp or painted, with old adhesive residue; strips cut around pipe penetrations, floor drains and door jambs.

New-construction house or apartment turnover: empty rooms, wood subfloor, standardized floor plans, several rooms/units per day. Strips run the full perimeter of many rooms and closets; site has drywall dust, debris, temporary lighting and other trades working nearby.

Commercial/institutional broadloom job (office suite, hotel guestrooms and corridors, school, clinic) during a scheduled refit or after-hours work: long straight perimeters, columns, built-in casework, door frames and metal transition strips; institution controls access and keeps the space swept and lit.

Stairs, landings, curved or angled walls and hard-surface transitions: short strip pieces cut and mitered for each tread and riser, doubled strips at stair nosings, strips segmented along curves, pieces fitted against thresholds in cramped positions.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sawing and nailing softwood/board stock onto a fixtured building panel from CAD data. It covers the measure-cut-fasten content of tackless-strip work with the same materials (softwood strip, nails/staples) and finer placement tolerance than the 1/4 in. wall gap, but only inside a fenced factory cell on work brought to the machine.

Commercial jobsite (office suite, hotel corridor, school, healthcare): cutting broadloom lengths off the roll for corridors, trimming carpet tiles and planks to fit at walls, columns and thresholds, cutting seam edges straight with a straightedge/row cutter, and cutting cove base or transition pieces. Shop binding/serging: fabricating an area rug or runner from a broadloom cut - squaring and cutting the piece, then finishing the perimeter with binding tape on a binding machine, serging yarn on an overlock serger, or applying self-adhesive edge binding, with mitered corners and a clean, straight finished edge.

On-site edge finishing after fitting: binding or taping raw carpet edges at closet cuts, stair-runner sides, doorway transitions and equipment cut-outs, using instant-bind tape, hot-melt seam tape or a portable binder, in the customer's home or a commercial space.

Patch and repair of resilient flooring in an occupied institutional facility (hospital corridor or ward, school, food plant, transit vehicle): damaged area cut out, new piece scribed and trimmed to the opening, seams welded or chemically sealed and skived so the joint is tight and cleanable, edges secured; done in a short off-hours window in an otherwise intact, standard-layout facility.

instances.label: Residential home: after sheet vinyl/linoleum is trowel-set into full-spread adhesive in a kitchen, bath or laundry over a concrete slab or underlayment, the installer works the sheet down from the center out with a hand/J-roller at edges, doorways, around toilet flanges and cabinet toe-kicks, then makes passes with a 75-100 lb floor roller, chasing out bubbles and blisters before the adhesive skins over.

New commercial/institutional build-out (school, retail, clinic, office) on an active construction site: large-area sheet vinyl or linoleum laid over a concrete slab, field rolled with a 100 lb three-section roller in both directions and hand-rolled at seams and perimeter, amid staged material, dust and other trades, within the adhesive's open time.

Renovation inside an occupied, institution-controlled facility (hospital wing, nursing home, school corridor) with the area cleared, barricaded and phased by facility staff: sheet goods rolled into adhesive with heavy and hand rollers, seams hand-rolled after heat welding, work completed and area returned to service on schedule.

Flash-coved sheet vinyl / sheet wall covering in healthcare, lab, food-service or clean-room areas: hand rolling the sheet into adhesive up the cove former and onto the wall, pressing inside and outside corners, vertical seams and cap-strip areas so the sanitary, water-tight finish has no voids or air pockets.

Repair/re-work in place: re-rolling blisters, bubbles and lifted seams in previously installed sheet goods, or re-adhering patch pieces after adhesive injection, in occupied homes and buildings with furniture and fixtures around.

tasks.label: Sweep, scrape, sand, or chip dirt and irregularities to clean base surfaces, correcting imperfections that may show through the covering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential renovation (occupied or vacant house/apartment): after tear-out of old sheet vinyl or VCT, the installer scrapes residual cutback adhesive and felt from plywood or slab subfloor, pulls staples and sets nail heads, chips high spots, feathers and sands patching compound, then sweeps/vacuums. 100-300 sq ft rooms of varying condition, furniture, doorways, appliances.

New commercial construction (school, retail, medical office shell): 2,000-20,000 sq ft open concrete slab prepared for LVT/VCT/sheet vinyl — shot-blast or grind laitance and curing compound, scrape drywall mud, paint and plaster splatter, chip ridges at joints and form marks, patch and sand, then vacuum. Active jobsite with other trades, stacked material, temporary power and lighting.

Renovation inside an operating institution (hospital wing, school corridor, office suite) worked nights or weekends in phased areas: strip old adhesive residue with scraper and grinder, feather patch, chip high spots, HEPA-vacuum to contain dust from occupied areas. Fixed layout, standard rooms and corridors, facility controls access.

Detail and edge work on any job: hand scraping and chipping along walls, in closets, around door casings, under toe-kicks and casework, on stair treads and risers, at transitions and floor penetrations; hand scraper, oscillating tool, sanding block, brush and vacuum, worked on knees in confined space.

Final clean-down of an already-corrected substrate immediately before adhesive: sweep and vacuum dust and debris across a large open floor (warehouse, gym, big-box retail, corridor) so nothing telegraphs through the covering or breaks the bond; no significant scraping or chipping required.

tasks.label: Measure and mark guidelines on surfaces or foundations, using chalk lines and dividers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional construction: large open floor plates (school corridors and classrooms, hospital wings, offices, retail big-box) on bare concrete slab or plywood subfloor. Installer measures the space, establishes square centerlines and border/pattern lines for VCT, LVT or sheet vinyl, and snaps chalk lines from drawings; active jobsite with other trades, dust and stacked material.

Renovation/recover inside an existing occupied facility the owner controls (classroom over summer break, hospital patient room at night, office suite, retail store after hours): old covering demolished, subfloor patched; installer measures the as-built room, works around door casings, casework and columns, and snaps centerlines plus border and transition lines.

Residential new construction and multifamily: LVP/sheet vinyl in framed and drywalled units and houses. Installer lays out unit by unit in enclosed rooms of 100-400 sq ft, snapping a starting line and perpendicular control lines relative to the longest wall and door thresholds; conditions vary unit to unit.

Occupied-home remodel: small, awkward, partly furnished rooms (bath, laundry, kitchen, basement landing) with toilets, cabinets and appliances in place, no drawings, out-of-square walls; installer measures with tape, snaps guidelines, and uses dividers/scribers to mark scribe lines for fitting sheet goods to irregular walls.

Specialty/decorative layout in a facility: gym or fitness-room rubber flooring, poured/decorative resilient floors, logo or multi-color pattern inlays and athletic game-line layout, requiring arcs, radii and pattern grid guidelines struck on the prepared subfloor.

tasks.label: Inspect surface to be covered to ensure that it is firm and dry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction interior (school, hospital wing, office/retail buildout) on a bare concrete slab in an active jobsite with other trades working: installer walks the whole area, looks for cracks, spalls, curing-compound or paint contamination, dust and debris, checks flatness with a straightedge, performs manufacturer-required moisture testing (in-situ RH probes per ASTM F2170 or calcium chloride) and pH, and issues a go/no-go with a list of prep needed before resilient sheet/LVT goes down.

Renovation inside an occupied, institution-controlled facility (retail store, clinic, gym, office floor) after tear-out of the old resilient flooring, done in phases or off-hours: installer inspects the exposed slab or underlayment for old adhesive residue, cutback, patch areas, hollow/loose spots found by walking and tapping, checks moisture with a meter over slab-on-grade and confirms fresh patch/leveler is cured and dry before covering.

Private home renovation (occupied dwelling, furniture and pets present, varied vintage construction): installer inspects a plywood/OSB subfloor or basement slab for deflection, squeaks, loose or damaged boards, protruding fasteners, water stains and past leaks, uses a pin/pinless moisture meter on wood and slab, checks for a vapor retarder, and decides whether the substrate is firm and dry enough for sheet vinyl, LVT, cork or rubber.

Quick small-job check: apartment turnover, single room, or small office—installer spends a few minutes on a visual pass, a hand/foot check for soft or damp spots, and one or two spot moisture readings before starting the same day.

Specialty/large-area job in a controlled facility (gym sports floor, ESD/static-control flooring in a lab or plant, seamless rubber): documented moisture testing across a large slab (multiple RH probe locations, 24-hour equilibration), bond/adhesion test patches, flatness verification, and written substrate acceptance report to the manufacturer's warranty standard.

sources.system: Spot with Enhanced Autonomy Package (jobsite documentation)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (with FARO, Trimble, contractor partners)
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous, repeatable reality-capture missions (360 photos, laser scans) on active construction sites, navigating changing jobsite floors without an operator; it documents conditions but does not measure substrate moisture, soundness, or issue a flooring-readiness determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite reality capture on construction floors. It shows a robot can traverse and image the same slabs a floor layer inspects, but it captures geometry/imagery only — no contact moisture testing, no hollow/soundness check, no accept-or-remediate decision — so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Implementation of a Fully Autonomous Platform for Assessment of Concrete Bridge Decks RABIT (ASCE Proceedings)
sources.claim: RABIT is a robotic platform that autonomously surveys concrete bridge decks with impact echo, ultrasonic surface waves, electrical resistivity and GPR to map delamination and concrete quality — the closest robotic analogue to checking whether a concrete surface is sound, but it is a research/FHWA prototype used on bridge decks and performs no moisture-for-flooring testing or readiness sign-off.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nondestructive condition assessment of a horizontal concrete surface (delamination = 'not firm'). Transfer is only partial: the deliverable is a deterioration map of a highway deck, not a dryness measurement or a substrate-acceptance decision for adhesive-applied floor covering, and it remains a prototype.

sources.title: Robotic Tank Inspection Services | Square Robot
sources.claim: Square Robot's SR-3 submersible robot autonomously navigates the bottom of in-service aboveground storage tanks and takes phased-array ultrasonic thickness readings for API 653 internal inspections — commercial robotic inspection of a floor's integrity, but on steel tank bottoms submerged in product, with no assessment of dryness or readiness to receive a covering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic inspection of a floor surface for soundness (corrosion/thickness). Objects and criteria differ materially — steel plate under liquid versus a concrete or plywood subfloor that must be judged clean, sound, flat and below a moisture threshold — so it does not substantiate this task's output.

sources.title: Equipment Management: The Right Tool for the Job Might Be a Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The Canvas drywall finishing robot uses lidar and vision to map wall surfaces and identify imperfections before applying compound on residential and commercial jobsites, but it is positioned and supervised by a user and evaluates surface geometry for finishing, not substrate firmness or moisture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic scanning of a building surface prior to applying a covering material. It is the nearest jobsite example of machine surface assessment, but it measures geometry for finish planning under operator control, and gives no moisture or soundness verdict.

sources.system: Tramex Hygro-i2 in-situ concrete RH probe kit (hand tool, not a robot)
sources.title: in situ concrete RH test as per ASTM F2170 | Tramex
sources.claim: The accepted dryness check for a slab before resilient flooring is a manual multi-step in-situ RH procedure — drilling, hole cleaning with brush and vacuum, sealed probe insertion, equilibration, then reading — and no robotic system was found that executes this ASTM F2170 protocol.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited to establish what the accepted output requires (drilled, cleaned, sealed in-situ probes plus visual/soundness assessment), which no cited robot performs, supporting the negative judgments.

tasks.label: Form a smooth foundation by stapling plywood or Masonite over the floor or by brushing waterproof compound onto surface and filling cracks with plaster, putty, or grout to seal pores.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home remodel (kitchen, bath, laundry): staple 1/4" plywood or hardboard underlayment over an existing wood subfloor before resilient sheet/LVT — scribing and cutting panels around cabinets, toilet flange and door jambs, staggering seams, driving staples on a 2"-6" pattern flush with the surface, then filling seams and staple dimples with patching compound and feathering smooth. Furniture, appliances and homeowners present; subfloor squeaks, humps and old adhesive vary room to room.

New residential construction jobsite: prep the plywood subfloor or slab before resilient flooring — brush/roll a waterproof or moisture-barrier compound, fill cracks, joints, gouges and low spots with cementitious patch or putty, feather edges to a flat, pore-sealed foundation. Active site with other trades, dust, debris, temporary lighting, unpredictable clutter.

Commercial/institutional renovation (school, office, retail, clinic) after demo of old flooring: patch cracks, spalls and old fastener holes in the concrete slab, apply waterproof/moisture-mitigation coating over the slab, skim-coat or install underlayment panels, working in phased areas with residual adhesive, cutbacks and uneven substrate.

Overnight/phased work inside an occupied, institution-controlled facility (grocery aisle, hospital corridor section, airport concourse gate area): a section of slab is exposed, cracks and joints filled with patch/grout and a sealing compound brushed on so sheet goods can be laid before the space reopens. Clean, standardized premises, controlled access, but tight time window and fixed furnishings.

Small localized prep and repair work: filling cracks and holes with plaster, putty or grout at thresholds, stair treads and landings, inside closets, under toe kicks and along wall lines; sealing porous spots and feathering small patches flush by hand in confined, awkward positions.

sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN's WALLTEQ M-300 CNC multifunction bridge automatically staples, nails, trims and marks sheathing panels onto fixtured timber elements, and is used for floor elements as well as wall and roof elements, in prefab component factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory sheathing of floor cassettes. It is the same physical operation as the task's first branch — laying sheet panels (OSB/plywood/board) over a floor substrate and fastening them with staples/nails on a set pattern, then routing openings — performed on a floor element fixtured on a work table, i.e. the E1 presentation of the same work.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic sheathing system uses two to five robots to place, fasten and trim sheet materials onto prefabricated wall panels, floor cassettes ... in an offsite factory line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sheathing of floor cassettes. tasks.label: Apply adhesive cement to floor or wall material to join and adhere foundation material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open commercial floor area (retail box, school cafeteria, open office plate) in new construction or shell fit-out: worker spreads adhesive with a notched trowel or roller across the prepared concrete slab in working-width sections and beds modular resilient goods (VCT, glue-down LVT/LVP, rubber tiles) into it within the adhesive's open time.

Cut-up commercial interior (hospital patient rooms and corridors, classrooms, restrooms, labs) with sheet vinyl or linoleum roll goods: pattern-scribed sheet, adhesive troweled to the subfloor around door jambs, columns, casework and floor penetrations, sheet rolled in, seams heat-welded, adhesive carried up walls for flash coving.

Residential glue-down resilient flooring in an occupied or newly built home: kitchen, bath, laundry or basement rooms, adhesive spread around cabinet toe-kicks, toilet flanges, thresholds and transitions in small irregular rooms with furniture and fixtures present.

Wall and trim work: applying cove-base cement or contact adhesive to vinyl/rubber wall base, stair treads and risers, nosings, transition strips and sheet wall-protection panels, then pressing the material to the wall or stair and rolling it out.

Athletic and specialty flooring: rolled rubber, poured-underlayment-backed or sound-deadening sheet goods in gyms, fitness rooms and multipurpose spaces; urethane or acrylic adhesive troweled over large open areas, heavy rolls laid back into the wet adhesive and rolled.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing floor material on a building site. It shows autonomous floor-covering installation in an as-found construction interior, but it uses mechanical pedestals rather than adhesive, so it is supporting context only.

tasks.label: Determine traffic areas and decide location of seams.
