tasks.label: Remove excess cement to clean finished surface.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential home, kitchen/bath/basement: after troweling adhesive and laying sheet vinyl or glue-down LVT, the installer wipes wet adhesive squeeze-out from seams and smears off the face of the new covering with a damp cloth or solvent-dampened rag, working around cabinets, toe-kicks and door jambs in an occupied or under-renovation house.

Commercial new-construction or renovation jobsite (office, school, retail): large areas of glue-down sheet vinyl, VCT or LVT; installer removes adhesive squeeze-out at seams and adhesive smears/footprints from the finished surface as work proceeds, amid other trades, staged material, dust and temporary lighting.

Occupied institutional facility (hospital, clinic, lab) in a barricaded renovation zone: heat-welded sheet vinyl with integral coved base; installer cleans adhesive from the sheet face, seam edges and the cove/base before welding and hand-off, to an inspected finish standard.

Athletic or specialty flooring (rubber sheet/tile gym floor, ESD or conductive tile, linoleum) in a gym, fieldhouse or plant: excess urethane/epoxy or acrylic cement squeezed at seams and edges must be removed from the surface with the correct solvent before it cures, without hazing or discoloring the covering.

Punch-list / final cleanup pass: scraping cured adhesive blobs, cement and leveling-compound spatter off the finished floor with a hand scraper and cleaner, plus removing adhesive from adjacent thresholds, base and transition strips before turnover.

sources.system: Laserax Robot Laser Cleaning Machine / Laserax Robotic Cell
sources.title: Robot Laser Cleaning Machine | Laserax
sources.claim: Laserax sells robot laser-cleaning cells in which an industrial robot removes cured epoxy/adhesive and other surface contaminants from parts, e.g. stripping epoxy from e-motor stator connector tabs to leave a clean surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removal of excess cured adhesive from a finished part surface. It transfers to 'remove excess cement to clean finished surface' because the object is hardened adhesive residue on a surface that must be left clean and undamaged, executed by a programmed robot on work presented in a fixed, purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Laserax Launches New Robot Cell for Laser Cleaning and Texturing
sources.claim: The Laserax robotic cleaning cell is a purpose-built enclosure with automated part feeding (conveyors, rotary tables) — i.e. the work is brought to the machine and presented in a known position.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the E1 environment (fenced cell, fixtured/conveyor-presented work) in which the adhesive-removal cleaning above is performed.

sources.system: PushCorp force-compliance devices and servo spindles on robotic deflashing cells
sources.title: Robotic Deflashing and Trimming Automation Applications by PushCorp
sources.claim: Commercial robotic deflashing/trimming cells use force-compliant tooling so a robot can remove excess material along contours and parting lines without overcutting the finished part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical removal of excess material (flash) from a finished surface. It transfers to scraping cured adhesive/cement off a floor panel because both require controlled contact force to shear off excess residue while leaving the underlying finished surface unmarred, and both are done on fixtured parts in fenced cells.

sources.system: Dürr EcoRS Clean F / EcoClean cleaning robots
sources.title: Dürr Painting Robot Equips Audi EV Topcoat Line | Products Finishing
sources.claim: Dürr supplies robot cleaning stations in which EcoRS Clean F robots wipe large finished car-body surfaces with feather rollers to an accepted appearance standard before painting; such cleaning robots are installed in production paint shops (e.g. Audi, BYD).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-executed cleaning of a large finished surface to an inspected finish standard inside a purpose-built booth; supports that robots can produce an accepted 'clean finished surface' when the workpiece is presented in a fixed, machine-built setting.

sources.title: Robotic Masonry Is Helping to Fill the Skilled Labor Gap - Construction Executive
sources.claim: On real masonry jobsites, even with the commercially deployed SAM100 bricklaying robot, removal of excess mortar from the finished work is still done by a ... mason.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous on-site cleanup work (removing excess cementitious material from newly finished work); shows the cleanup step remains manual on jobsites (E3) even where the placement step is automated.

sources.system: RoBuild LVP flooring robot (mobile base + arm + vacuum gripper)
sources.title: RoBuild Robotics | Autonomous Floor-Laying for Interior Finishes
sources.claim: On-site flooring robotics is at the stage of placing LVP planks in pilot installs; the demonstrated system places planks over an existing surface and shows no adhesive/cement cleanup capability.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic system to the occupation itself; its scope is plank placement only, substantiating that no fielded flooring robot performs adhesive squeeze-out cleanup in homes or jobsites.

sources.title: Autonomous Floor Cleaning Robot - Commercial Floor Scrubber | Avidbots
sources.claim: Fully autonomous commercial floor scrubbers are deployed in structured facilities (warehouses, airports, retail) for routine floor cleaning; their function is scrubbing general soil, not removing adhesive squeeze-out from freshly laid floor covering.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound E2 capability: autonomous machines clean floors in institution-controlled facilities, but they perform broad-area scrubbing of general soil and do not detect or remove adhesive/cement residue at seams on a newly bonded covering.

tasks.label: Heat and soften floor covering materials to patch cracks or fit floor coverings around irregular surfaces, using blowtorch.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential home (occupied or turnover unit): installer heats sheet vinyl or linoleum with a torch/heat gun in a bathroom or kitchen so the softened sheet molds cleanly around a toilet flange, supply pipes, door jambs, and inside/outside corners, then trims and rolls it into adhesive. Layout, subfloor condition and obstacles differ house to house.

Commercial/institutional fit-out (school, clinic, hospital, food service, lab) during construction or renovation: installer heats sheet vinyl or rubber goods to flash-cove the material up the wall, forming inside and outside corners with gusset cuts, and to wrap columns, door frames and floor drains. Other trades working nearby, dust, variable temperature.

Repair/patch of an existing installed resilient floor (home, store, corridor, apartment turn): heating the covering and its adhesive to soften and lift a damaged, gouged or curled section or seam, cutting and pattern-matching a patch, then heating it to seat and blend it into the surrounding floor.

Stairs and curved features: heating rubber or vinyl treads, risers, nosings and cove/radius pieces so they conform tightly over the nosing radius, curved walls or rounded thresholds without creasing, then bonding them in place in a stairwell or lobby.

Contractor shop or on-site staging area: heating rolled or stiff goods on a bench to relax curl and pre-forming detail pieces (corner gussets, coved corner blanks, formed edge strips) before they are carried into the room for installation.

sources.title: RoBuild Robotics | Autonomous Floor-Laying for Interior Finishes
sources.claim: RoBuild's mobile flooring robot places LVP planks autonomously and has been piloted in a real home; its scope is plank placement with a vacuum end effector, with no heating, forming, scribing or edge/corner fitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ resilient floor covering installation in homes. It marks the frontier of jobsite flooring robotics — dry plank placement only — and does not extend to heat-softening and forming sheet goods around irregular geometry.

sources.system: Legend Robot tile laying / paving robot
sources.developer: Shenzhen Legend Robot Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Tile Laying & Paving Robot
sources.claim: Legend Robot's commercial tile-laying robot lays large field areas in residential, hotel and office interiors, but human workers are still required to complete corners and edges — the irregular-geometry work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ floor covering installation on jobsites. It shows that even deployed floor-covering robots cannot handle the perimeter/corner/irregular-surface fitting that this heating-and-forming task consists of.

sources.system: Italpresse membrane press (wood membrane press line)
sources.title: Membrane wood press machine
sources.claim: Italpresse membrane presses are production machines built to laminate three-dimensionally shaped panels with heat-softened thermoformable PVC and similar plastic sheet, conforming and bonding the sheet to the contoured workpiece in an automatic press cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heat-softening PVC sheet and conforming it around irregular 3D contours with adhesive. Same material family (plasticized PVC sheet), same physics (soften with heat, stretch and press into corners/radii without creasing), performed on fixtured workpieces in a purpose-built machine.

sources.system: iGoldenCNC vacuum laminator / membrane press (iGC-V series)
sources.title: Vacuum Laminator Machine - iGoldencnc
sources.claim: Automatic CNC vacuum laminating machines heat PVC film and use vacuum and a silicone membrane ... it onto flat or 3D panels, with shaped cauls or mold forms used to guide film conformity on strongly curved or compound-curved surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heat-forming and bonding vinyl sheet over irregular contours. Corresponds to the installer's job of softening covering material so it seats into coves, corners and radii, but with the workpiece fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: Robotic thermoforming cell (Universal Robot arm with 2 kW heat gun)
sources.developer: research group, published in Journal of Computational Design and Engineering (Elsevier)
sources.title: Form-finding with robotics: Rapid and flexible fabrication of glass fiber reinforced concrete panels using thermoformed molds
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed fabrication study used an industrial robot arm carrying a 600 °C hot-air heat gun to heat thermoplastic sheet to a malleable state and imprint a shape into it, then cool it to hold the formed geometry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot manipulating a heat gun to soften a thermoplastic sheet and form it to a desired shape — the same tool-and-material operation as heating floor covering to make it pliable, demonstrated in a fixtured robotic cell.

sources.system: UR10e cobot trim cell at Kal Plastics
sources.title: Cobot creates 'cell manufacturing dream' for plastics thermoformer
sources.claim: A UR10e cobot mounted on a gantry is deployed in production at a thermoforming plant to trim formed plastic parts, covering the trimming step that follows heat-forming in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trimming heat-formed thermoplastic parts. The installer's heat-and-fit operation ends with cutting the softened covering to the finished line; this shows the trimming step is automated in the same purpose-built cells.

tasks.label: Disconnect and remove appliances, light fixtures, and worn floor and wall covering from floors, walls, and cabinets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home, kitchen/laundry: shut off water, gas and power; disconnect and pull out range, dishwasher, refrigerator and washer/dryer; remove old sheet vinyl or VCT and adhesive up to cabinet toe kicks; work around furniture, pets and homeowners.

Private home, bathrooms/halls/bedrooms: pull toilet, remove door thresholds and rubber/wood base, tear up worn sheet vinyl, linoleum or glued-down resilient plank, pull staples and damaged underlayment in tight rooms with doorways and stairs.

Occupied commercial or institutional building (retail store, school corridor, clinic, office suite) after hours: move shelving, desks and light fixtures/equipment aside, strip large areas of glued VCT, sheet vinyl or carpet tile with a scraper, and remove rubber cove base from walls; fixed layout maintained by the facility.

Tenant fit-out or renovation area under construction behind barriers: mixed debris, other trades working, uneven and unknown substrate conditions; remove leftover old floor covering, mastic, tack strip and wall covering before new resilient flooring goes down.

Specialty institutional removal (hospital OR/lab, commercial kitchen, cleanroom): disconnect and remove fixed equipment and light fixtures, cut out heat-welded sheet vinyl floor and coved sheet wall covering, remove static-dissipative flooring under containment protocols.

sources.title: Wolff Robo Stripper | Tools4Flooring.com
sources.claim: The closest machine to this task in the flooring trade, the Wolff Robo Stripper, is a remote-controlled (human-driven) floor scraper for large-area floor covering removal; it is not autonomous, so it cannot support a positive judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the removal half of this task (stripping worn floor covering), but it is continuously operated by a human via remote control, which the rules treat as teleoperation.

sources.title: Remote controlled demolition robots | Husqvarna US
sources.claim: Commercial interior demolition machines (Husqvarna DXR, Brokk) that could break out adhered coverings are remote-controlled by an operator, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior demolition/strip-out of building finishes. Capability does not transfer to an autonomous judgment because the machine requires continuous operator control.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous construction robots deployed on real jobsites today apply finishes (plaster, paint, drywall sanding); no comparable autonomous system removes existing floor or wall coverings or disconnects appliances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior finish work on construction sites. It shows the boundary of autonomous jobsite capability (spraying/sanding flat walls), not demolition, appliance handling, or utility disconnection.

sources.title: Autonomous Concrete Floor Polishing & LightWare's SF40/C LiDAR | Unmanned Systems Technology
sources.claim: Autonomous floor-surface robots exist for concrete polishing/grinding, i.e. abrading a bare slab, not for stripping adhered resilient coverings, cove base, or handling appliances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical floor surface preparation. It only abrades an already-bare slab in open areas and does not remove sheet goods, tile, base, or fixtures, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.system: UR10e-based automated unscrewing system for e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic disconnection/unfastening is demonstrated only at laboratory scale on small electronics in a fixtured cell, far from disconnecting gas, water and electrical services to household appliances in situ.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly/disconnection. Scale, fittings (compression nuts, gas flare fittings, flexible hoses), confined under-cabinet access and utility shut-off requirements are not comparable, so it does not substantiate appliance disconnection.

sources.title: Introducing Rufus, the Automated Roofing Robot from Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Automated tear-off (removal of worn covering) remains a roadmap item even for the leading autonomous exterior-covering robot, confirming no fielded autonomous covering-removal capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing/installing worn building coverings. Tear-off is only announced intent, which the rules exclude, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

roles.title: Floor Sanders and Finishers
roles.description: Scrape and sand wooden floors to smooth surfaces using floor scraper and floor sanding machine, and apply coats of finish.

tasks.label: Buff and vacuum floors to ensure their cleanliness prior to the application of finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential site-finished floor: between finish coats in an emptied house, the worker screens/buffs the floor with a rotary buffer plus hand abrasion at edges, closets and under toe-kicks, then vacuums the whole room (field, corners, baseboards, transitions) and tacks it so the next coat goes on defect-free.

Commercial/institutional interior (office suite, retail store, restaurant, school corridor) cleared of furniture: buff/screen longer open runs plus doorways, thresholds and column bases, then vacuum dust from the floor and adjacent surfaces before the sealer or topcoat.

Gymnasium or large sports floor screen-and-recoat: one large open maple field in an institution-controlled building, machine-buffed in overlapping passes with hand work at bleacher pockets and wall bases, then vacuumed and tacked before the finish coat and game lines.

New-construction or gut-renovation jobsite: newly sanded floor in a building still being worked in, with drywall dust, other trades' debris, temporary power and lighting; buff and vacuum room by room immediately before coating.
Stairs, closets, small baths and edge-only detail work: buffing treads, risers and tight corners with a hand pad or edger and vacuuming with a wand/brush attachment before finish.

sources.system: Cefla Finishing Smartclean PRO panel cleaning machine
sources.title: Smartclean PRO from Cefla Finishing: The ultimate complete panel cleaning solution for woodworking finish lines
sources.claim: Cefla Smartclean PRO is a commercially offered in-line woodworking machine that brushes wood panels/boards and extracts the dust so surfaces leave the cleaning stage clean immediately before coating - the same abrade-then-dedust step this task performs on floors, done in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-coating brushing/dedusting of wood surfaces on a finishing line. Same objects (wood boards/flooring stock), same purpose and acceptance standard (surface abraded and dust-free so the next coat is defect-free), performed by machine with integral extraction rather than by buffer and shop vacuum.

sources.system: Hardwood flooring prefinish line (sanding, denibbing and dust-collection stations feeding roller coaters)
sources.developer: Prefinishing plants profiled by Wood Floor Business (UV Crystal; Premiere Finishing & Coating)
sources.title: How Prefinished Wood Floors Are Made | Wood Floor Business
sources.claim: Automated hardwood-flooring prefinish lines abrade (denib) the boards between coats and remove the dust with integral dust collection before each next coat is roll-applied; this is the E1 form of buffing and vacuuming a floor before finish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: between-coat denibbing plus dust extraction on a wood-flooring finishing line. Identical material (finished wood flooring), identical purpose (clean, abraded surface accepted for the next coat); the same article notes powerful dust collection throughout the line is needed for the most flawless finish possible.

sources.system: Omnirobotic PSA-80 PRO autonomous sanding robot
sources.developer: Omnirobotic (distributed by AW Machinery / Wurth Machinery)
sources.title: The Future of Wood Sanding: Autonomous AI Robot. The Omnirobotic PSA-80 PRO
sources.claim: Omnirobotic's PSA-80 PRO is a commercially sold autonomous robotic sander that uses 3D vision and AI-generated toolpaths with force-controlled heads to prepare hardwood and panel surfaces before finishing, in a shop cell built around the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive surface preparation of hardwood workpieces immediately before a finish coat. Same material and comparable light-abrasion precision (force-controlled heads, burn-through protection), with the work presented to the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual for this task.

sources.developer: Shenzhen Legend Robot Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Automated Floor grinding & dust collection robot - Legend Robot
sources.claim: Legend Robot's Floor Grinding Robot performs in-situ autonomous floor abrasion with integral dust collection to prepare installed floors for coating, but only on concrete/hardener/epoxy substrates in garages, workshops and sports venues, at about 95% coverage with one operator supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile abrasive floor preparation with dust capture before a coating. Environment transfers (large indoor institutional floors), but objects and precision do not: a 1,250 kg diamond grinder cutting concrete cannot deliver the light, uniform screening of a thin wood finish layer, so it does not substantiate this task on wood.

sources.title: Janser GmbH: Vollautomatischer Roboter übernimmt Parkettschleifen (SN-Home.de)
sources.claim: Janser demonstrated the 'Weasel', a fully automatic parquet sanding robot that laser-measures the room, plans the sanding and controls its own feed, steering and contact pressure while sanding almost dust-free; it was a trade-show demonstration, with no evidence found of it delivering coat-ready floors in service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-room abrasion of a wood floor. Same material and setting as this task's buffing pass, but the demonstration covers field sanding only - no edge/corner work and no vacuuming to the dust-free standard a finish coat requires.

sources.developer: Tennant Company with Brain Corp; SoftBank Robotics
sources.title: Tennant Company Introduces Lithium-Ion Technology to AMR (Autonomous Mobile Robot) Floor Cleaning Machines - Brain Corp
sources.claim: Autonomous commercial floor-cleaning robots (Tennant BrainOS scrubbers, SoftBank Whiz vacuum sweeper) are deployed at scale in structured facilities such as stores, campuses and gyms, doing routine open-area scrubbing, sweeping and vacuuming - maintenance cleaning, not abrasive screening or pre-finish dedusting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor cleaning inside structured human facilities. It shows indoor navigation and open-area coverage are solved, but these machines wet-scrub or sweep for hygiene and leave perimeters and corners to staff; none is shown abrading a wood finish or reaching coat-ready cleanliness.

tasks.label: Scrape and sand floor edges and areas inaccessible to floor sanders, using scrapers, disk-type sanders, and sandpaper.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinishing existing hardwood floors in an occupied single-family home (furniture removed): after the big belt/drum machine does the field, the worker runs a disc edger around the perimeter of each room along baseboards and door casings, hand-scrapes the inside corners and behind door stops, and hand-sands to blend edge cuts into the drum-sanded field through successive grits. Old finish, pet stains, cupped boards and dust containment in a lived-in house.

New construction or gut-remodel residential job: freshly installed unfinished strip/plank floor in an empty house or apartment unit, no baseboard yet or new base installed. Worker edges the room perimeters, sands closets and small bathrooms/pantries with the edger and a random-orbit disc sander, and hand-sands transitions, working around drywall dust, trades traffic and temporary power.

Stairs, landings, thresholds and transitions: hand scraping and disc/orbital sanding of treads, risers, nosings, stringers and the small landing areas that no floor machine can reach; frequent grit changes, kneeling, and blending into adjacent finished floor. Residential or small commercial building.

Commercial/institutional wood floor (school or church gym, dance studio, stage, retail space) refinished off-hours by a contractor: edging the perimeter of a large maple floor along walls and bleacher pockets, sanding around floor inserts, sleeves, vent grates and door thresholds, and detail-sanding painted game-line areas before recoat. Facility staff control access and the room is cleared.

Tight and obstructed detail areas in homes: under cast-iron radiators and pipes, cabinet toe-kicks, around toilet flanges and vanities, inside closets and behind door casings — hand scrapers, carbide scrapers, small detail/corner sanders and folded sandpaper used on hands and knees to remove old finish and blend.

sources.title: PSA-80 PRO: Autonomous Cabinet Door Sanding – Omnirobotic
sources.claim: Omnirobotic's PSA-80 PRO is a commercially sold autonomous robotic sander for wood panels/doors that identifies parts with 3D vision and runs unattended after the operator loads a fixture table — i.e., wood sanding to finish-ready quality with the work brought to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding of hardwood components in a fixtured cell. It transfers to floor edge/corner sanding only under the E1 counterfactual (work presented to the machine): same material (hardwood), same abrasive process and finish-ready precision requirement (no burn-through, no cross-scratch).

sources.title: Woodworking Finishing Products – Omnirobotic
sources.claim: The same system sands hardwood and other wood panels and has dedicated internal- and external-corner sanding modes for tight angles and putty removal, with 3D-vision force-controlled heads sanding inside profiles without touch-ups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sanding of hardwood surfaces, edges and internal corners of fixtured parts. Corner/edge detail work is the closest industrial analogue to hand-scraping and edge-sanding a floor perimeter, but only when the workpiece is presented to the robot.

sources.title: GrayMatter scores $45M for robots that speed-up manufacturing with 'physics-informed AI'
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics has deployed roughly twenty autonomous robotic sanding cells at manufacturers, including furniture, that adapt in real time to ... — autonomous abrasive finishing of irregular surfaces inside purpose-built cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scan-and-sand surface finishing of varied parts in a fenced/fixtured cell. Supports E1 only: the parts are brought to the robot, scanned and sanded; nothing in the deployment is in-situ architectural work.

sources.title: Autogrinder | Time to break free | Husqvarna INT
sources.claim: The closest in-situ autonomous floor-surfacing machine is Husqvarna's Autogrinder 8 D, a self-navigating planetary grinder for concrete floors launched at Bauma 2025; it grinds and polishes planned open areas of concrete while the operator does other work, and perimeter/edge work on such jobs is still done with separate hand-guided edger machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-situ floor surface treatment inside buildings. It does NOT transfer to this task: it is a concrete planetary grinder covering open field areas on a planned path, not a wood-floor edger/scraper working baseboards, corners, stairs and obstructed recesses to a finish-ready wood surface.

sources.title: More Contractors See Benefits of Drywall Finishing Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot applies and sands joint compound on real commercial jobsites, showing that autonomous in-situ abrasive finishing exists in construction — but on vertical drywall from a lift-mounted arm, not on floor perimeters, stairs or obstructed floor recesses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ autonomous sanding of building surfaces on jobsites. Transfer fails for this task: the machine finishes flat vertical drywall at height and cannot run a floor edger along baseboards, scrape floor corners, or sand stair treads and toe-kick recesses at floor level.

tasks.label: Inspect floors for smoothness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home being refinished: after each sanding cut on oak strip flooring in living/dining/bedrooms, the worker crouches, runs a bare hand across the boards, uses a low, raking work light and daylight from windows to look for drum/chatter marks, deep scratches, cross-grain scratches and missed spots, then decides whether another pass or a finer grit is needed. Rooms are emptied but contain closets, vents, radiators and uneven old boards.

Private home, finish stage: after each coat of polyurethane/waterborne finish has dried, the worker inspects by touch and low-angle light for dust nibs, raised grain, bubbles, lap marks, roller/applicator streaks and skipped areas, and decides whether to screen/buff or spot-fix before the next coat. Judgment must be made within the coating window.

Perimeter and difficult areas of a residence: edges, inside corners, closets, stair treads and risers, under toe-kicks and around thresholds, hand-scraped or edger-sanded. The worker checks that edger swirl blends into the field, that no ridge or dish exists at the transition, and that scraped corners feel level with adjoining boards.

Commercial or institutional facility with a controlled interior (school gymnasium maple floor, church hall, restaurant, retail or office space): large open expanse sanded with a big machine; the worker walks the floor with raking light and a straightedge checking for waves/dishing, cut lines between passes, uniform scratch pattern, and smoothness around game-line and inlay areas before finishing.

New construction or unoccupied jobsite (new house, condo build-out): newly installed unfinished flooring is sanded amid construction dust, other trades, temporary lighting and no HVAC; the worker inspects for overwood at board joints, machine marks and grit-scratch remnants before applying finish.

sources.title: Paint Defect Inspection in Automotive Production
sources.claim: Robot-arm-mounted deflectometry sensors autonomously scan fixtured painted car bodies at inspection stations, detecting fine surface/finish defects with near-100% coverage and sub-micron height sensitivity, with results driving downstream robotic sanding and polishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inspecting a large coated surface for smoothness defects (dust inclusions, scratches, craters, runs, orange peel) and deciding where rework is needed — the same judgment a floor finisher makes on a sanded or coated floor, at finer precision (185 µm lateral, sub-micron depth). Transfer holds only where the surface is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: reflectCONTROL Automotive with Asis/Virtek defect-processing robots
sources.title: Precisely inspect and analyze painted car bodies | Micro-Epsilon
sources.claim: The same inspection system's output is used by force-controlled robots that grind and then polish each detected defect, showing machine-graded surface-quality decisions accepted in series production by premium car manufacturers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated finish-defect detection and classification on a coated surface; the accepted output (defect map driving rework) is the equivalent of a floor finisher's 'needs another pass / ready to coat' verdict, in a fixtured, purpose-built cell.

sources.title: The World's First Dual-Arm Autonomous Robotic Sanding Cell | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Dual-arm autonomous robotic sanding cells that scan each incoming part and plan their own sanding are deployed in production at a specialty-vehicle/fiberglass manufacturer, indicating machine-controlled surface-finish work meets production quality inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding with onboard scanning of each workpiece's surface; supports that surface-condition sensing and the resulting sand-more/stop decision function at production quality when the work is brought to the machine (E1), the same decision the floor sander's inspection produces.

sources.system: YOLOv5-based hardwood flooring defect inspection system
sources.title: An automatic machine vision-based algorithm for inspection of hardwood flooring defects during manufacturing
sources.claim: Automated machine-vision inspection of hardwood flooring surfaces for defects on a manufacturing line, replacing manual visual defect detection and classification.
sources.transferJustification: Same material and same inspection judgment (surface defects on hardwood flooring), but with boards conveyed past fixed cameras under controlled lighting — i.e., the work brought to the machine, supporting the E1 counterfactual only.

sources.developer: Transforma Robotics / NTU Singapore (Clearpath Jackal base)
sources.title: Jackal-Based Robot Modernizes Site Inspection - Clearpath Robotics
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile building-inspection robot measures evenness, alignment, cracks and hollowness in completed building interiors against construction quality standards; its floor assessment is mm-scale evenness, not fine sanding/finish quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ inspection of building floors/walls for evenness in a human-built interior. Cited to bound the E2/E3 judgment: it measures straightedge-scale evenness only, not sanding scratch pattern, swirl marks, missed spots or dust nibs, so it covers a sub-step rather than the whole inspection.

tasks.label: Attach sandpaper to rollers of sanding machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential refinishing job, belt-type big machine: in an emptied room of a house being renovated, the worker tips the drum/belt sander (Lagler Hummel, Bona Belt, Clarke EZ-8) back or opens the drum cover, releases the tension roller, strips the worn continuous abrasive belt off the drum, slips a fresh belt squarely over drum and idler, re-tensions and checks tracking; repeated for every grit pass amid dust, cords, baseboards and uneven old flooring.

Residential job, edger abrasive change: kneeling beside walls, closets and stair landings, the worker tips the 7-inch edger over, removes the spent disc (center bolt and washer, or hook-and-loop), seats a new disc concentric on the backing pad and retightens; done every few minutes because edger discs load and wear fast, in heavy dust with the machine hot.

Residential or light-commercial job, buffer / multi-disc planetary / orbital machine: the worker tips a Trio, FlexiSand or square-buff orbital sander and presses hook-and-loop abrasive discs, sanding screens or clamped abrasive sheets onto two or three driver pads or a rectangular platen, aligning each on center before screening between finish coats.

Commercial/institutional job (school gym, church hall, retail store, restaurant dining room) cleared by the facility and worked after hours: the same abrasive changes on drum machine, edger and buffer, performed on a fixed, swept floor inside a building whose owner controls access, with equipment staged in one corner.

Older sheet-type drum sander (Clarke Super 7R style rental unit): the worker cuts a sandpaper sheet to length, wraps it tightly around the drum, tucks both ends into the drum slot and tightens the internal clamp/expander with a wrench or lever so the paper is drum-tight and will not flap, then spins the drum to check.

tasks.label: Guide sanding machines over surfaces of floors until surfaces are smooth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinishing an existing hardwood floor in an occupied private home (rooms of 150-400 sq ft, furniture removed): worker punches nails, then walks a belt/drum or planetary sander over the field of the floor through a 3-grit sequence, working around door thresholds, register vents, cupped boards, pet-stain areas and old finish, leaving a flat, swirl- and chatter-free surface ready for stain.

Sanding newly installed unfinished hardwood in a new-construction house or condo unit before other trades finish out: unoccupied, open-plan continuous areas, plank ridges/overwood to level, dust containment, machine passes with the grain plus final buff/screen.

Full sand or screen-and-recoat of a large institutional/commercial wood floor - school gymnasium, dance studio, church hall, restaurant or retail space - performed off-hours in a building whose owner controls access; large open maple/oak field, game-line paint removal, tight flatness/appearance standards.

Detail abrasion where the big machine cannot reach: edger work along baseboards, in closets, under toe-kicks and radiators, plus stair treads, risers and landings; abrasion must be blended invisibly into the field sanding.

Hard-surface work done by the same floor-finishing crews: grinding/polishing a concrete or terrazzo slab in a warehouse, parking garage, factory or retail box - large open floor, planetary grinder with grit progression and dust extraction.

tasks.label: Apply filler compound and coats of finish to floors to seal wood.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinishing existing hardwood in an occupied single-family home (living room, bedrooms, hall): after sanding, trowel-spread wood filler over the whole floor to fill gaps/nail holes, let dry, screen, then apply sealer plus 2-3 coats of oil or waterborne polyurethane with T-bar/lambswool applicator, cutting in perimeter, door jambs, registers and cabinet toe-kicks by brush; furniture out but layouts, moldings and obstacles differ house to house; dust control and drying/recoat windows matter.

New construction or gut renovation (single family or multifamily unit): empty unfinished rooms on an active jobsite with other trades, temporary power/lighting, debris and protection; apply filler compound to the newly sanded floor, then sealer and finish coats room by room, sequencing exits and taping off the area.

Large open institutional wood floor - school/college gymnasium, dance studio or community hall closed for summer work: apply gym sealer and two coats of high-gloss sport finish over 6,000-12,000 sq ft with a T-bar applicator, maintaining a wet edge across the whole floor, cutting in walls, bleacher pockets and door thresholds; institution controls access and HVAC during cure.

Commercial/retail interior work off-hours - store, restaurant, office, church, hotel lobby: floors with fixed millwork, columns, booths and thresholds; apply filler where needed and two coats of finish overnight so the space can reopen, with tight scheduling and edge/detail work around fixtures.

Detail portions of jobs: stair treads, risers and landings, closets, thresholds, narrow hallways and under-radiator areas, plus spot filling and touch-up/recoats; filler pressed in by putty knife and finish applied by brush or hand pad in confined, awkward geometry, typically inside a house.

tasks.label: Remove excess glue from joints, using knives, scrapers, or wood chisels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home, glue-down engineered or solid strip flooring just installed: worker moves across the room on knees removing urethane/PVA squeeze-out from the face of board joints with a putty knife, plastic scraper and rag before the adhesive skins over; furniture, door casings and trim nearby, dust and varying light.

Renovation of an existing wood floor in a home: cured, hardened adhesive, construction glue blobs, drywall mud and caulk on and between boards must be chiselled and scraped out of the joints and off the surface before drum/orbital sanding, without gouging boards or leaving depressions.

Commercial/institutional glue-down wood floor (school gym, retail, office fit-out) during construction: large open bays of freshly glued flooring, squeeze-out cleaned from joints ahead of the sanding crew while other trades, cords, pallets and material stacks share the space.

Detail and confined work: stair treads, risers and nosings, thresholds, transitions, borders and feature strips, and joints against baseboards and toe kicks, where glue must be pared out of inside corners and tight reveals with a wood chisel or knife without marring adjacent finished millwork.

Parquet, herringbone, wood-block or medallion installation: many short joints and mastic bleed over a patterned field; excess adhesive scraped from each joint line and from the wear surface, some of it partly cured, before filling and sanding.

tasks.label: Align and straighten tile using levels, squares, and straightedges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom: tub surround / shower enclosure walls plus the small bath floor in a home or gut remodel. Tiles 3x6 to 12x24 set on walls with a niche, curb, corners and fixture penetrations; each course checked plumb, level and square with a torpedo level and straightedge, tiles tapped and shimmed to kill lippage in a room of 30-60 sq ft.

Detail and edge work in homes: kitchen backsplashes, decorative bands and mosaic accents, fireplace surrounds, stair treads and risers, and the cut perimeter/threshold pieces of larger jobs, aligned against cabinets, countertops and door casings with squares and short straightedges.

Residential floor field tile in open, cleared rooms of a new-build or gutted house (great room, kitchen, hallway), 12x24 or larger porcelain on a prepared slab or underlayment; layout lines snapped, tiles set in thinset and beaten flat, joints kept straight and lippage checked with a 6-10 ft straightedge and level.

Commercial/institutional interior floor field tile in large open areas during fit-out (school corridor, retail sales floor, hospital lobby, transit concourse); hundreds to thousands of square feet of standard-format tile aligned to control lines with laser/level and long straightedges, flatness held to spec.

Commercial restrooms, locker rooms and commercial kitchens: wall tile around partitions, doors, fixtures and chases, plus small sloped floors to drains; work is fixture-dense and space-constrained, with constant level, plumb and square checks.

Exterior and specialty work: patios, pool decks and plaza pavers, stone veneer on walls, and roof-deck/entry stone; units set on mortar or setting beds and aligned with string lines, levels and straightedges under weather and uneven site conditions.

tasks.label: Finish and dress the joints and wipe excess grout from between tiles, using damp sponge.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction or full-room remodel: after grouting a large open floor field (kitchen, entry, living area, laundry, whole-house porcelain/ceramic), the setter strikes/packs the joints and sponge-wipes the excess grout in successive damp passes, rinsing frequently, then removes haze. Room is empty of fixtures and furniture; tile is standard-format, joints 1/8–3/16 in.

Commercial/institutional project under construction (retail store, school corridor, hotel lobby, hospital wing, big-box): grouting large open floor fields of large-format porcelain or quarry tile, then dressing the joints and sponge-washing off the excess before it sets, working room by room ahead of other trades.

Residential bathroom/shower job: grouting tub or shower wall surrounds, niches, curbs, inside corners and adjoining small floor, then tooling joints and sponge-wiping the vertical surfaces from top down without pulling grout out of joints, followed by haze removal.

Detail vertical work: kitchen backsplashes around outlets and under cabinets, accent walls, fireplace surrounds, countertop edges, and commercial restroom/kitchen wall tile — small, edge-dominated fields where joints are dressed and excess wiped with a barely damp sponge to protect narrow joints and trim pieces.

Constrained horizontal work in occupied remodels: small bathroom floors grouted around an installed toilet flange, vanity and tub apron, closets, thresholds and transitions, hallway strips — sponge-wiping in tight, cluttered spaces with furniture, dust protection and homeowners present.

Specialty horizontal work: natural stone floors (marble/travertine) needing unsanded grout, minimal water and rapid haze removal to avoid staining; sloped mosaic shower pans; exterior patios, pool decks and stair treads where sanded grout is washed off in sun, wind or over drains.

sources.claim: A university-built mobile floor-grouting robot performed pre-cleaning, grout injection and post-grout cleaning of tiled floor joints in laboratory tests, with authors reporting quality comparable to manual work and one worker only preparing materials and supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Closely related: the robot's third stage is removing residual grout from the tile surface after filling, using an onboard brush rather than a damp sponge on fresh grout; it is cited only as supplementary support for grout cleanup on a flat, prepared horizontal tile field (E1-style presentation).

tasks.label: Cut and shape tile to fit around obstacles and into odd spaces and corners, using hand and power cutting tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel/repair in an occupied home: ceramic or porcelain floor and wall tile in a bathroom or kitchen. The setter measures and marks each odd piece against the actual condition, then cuts L-notches around a toilet flange, holes for shower valves and supply pipes, cuts around outlets, door casings, vent registers, and rips tapered pieces for out-of-square walls, using a wet saw set up in the garage/driveway plus angle grinder, hole saws, and nippers. Tight quarters, dust and water control, homeowner present.

New construction or commercial interior fit-out on an active jobsite (office, school, hospital, retail, multifamily): large runs of floor and wall tile where dozens to hundreds of cuts per day are made at a jobsite wet-saw station — perimeter rips, cuts at columns and door jambs, notches at floor drains and expansion joints, cove and base pieces. Layout varies, other trades working nearby, temporary power and water.

Large-format porcelain slab or natural stone slab work (countertops, vanities, shower walls, thresholds): field conditions captured by physical or digital template, then the slab is cut and shaped — sink and cooktop cutouts, faucet holes, radius corners, miters, scribed back edges — on shop saws/CNC sawjet or waterjet in a fabrication shop, with minor trim/scribe adjustments at install.

Exterior and natural dimension-stone work: flagstone patios and walkways, stone veneer, steps and treads. Irregular pieces are shaped to fit irregular gaps and curves using a hammer and chisel, stone splitter, angle grinder and gas saw, with each piece fitted by eye to its neighbors. Outdoors, weather-exposed, uneven ground.

Intricate decorative work: mosaic and small-format sheets, shower niches and curbs, pencil/bullnose trim, medallions and accent bands. Requires fine nibbling and radius cuts around fixtures, mitered outside corners, and precise small holes, using nippers, grinder with dry blade, and a wet saw with fine blade — done in the home or jobsite where the piece must match the installed condition.

sources.system: BACA Systems Autocut Line (robotic loading/unloading + Robo SawJet)
sources.title: Autocut Line | Fully Automated Cutting Line | Stone Fabrication | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA Systems' Autocut Line is a commercially sold, fully automated stone cutting line in which a robot arm loads and unloads slabs onto the Robo SawJet, which cuts parts to a programmed geometry inside a purpose-built cell in a fabrication plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting of stone/porcelain slabs to templated shapes. It transfers because the material (natural stone, porcelain), the cutting tools (diamond blade, abrasive waterjet), and the required output (a piece cut to a non-rectangular field geometry) are the same as tile cut-to-fit; tolerances are tighter than hand-cut tile.

sources.title: Robotics Are Revolutionizing Stone Cutting / Robo SawJet 2.0
sources.claim: The BACA Robo SawJet is a robot-arm-based sawjet, the most widely used robotic ... in the US stone industry, designed to cut intricate countertop parts (cutouts, notches, non-rectangular shapes) with high precision.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: robotic diamond-blade/waterjet cutting of stone and porcelain to programmed part outlines, which is the machine equivalent of cutting tile to fit odd spaces and obstacles.

sources.title: How to Cut Porcelain Countertops & Slabs for Stone Fabricators
sources.claim: CNC sawjets combining a diamond blade and integrated ... are commercially used to cut porcelain slabs and tile to high accuracy, including intricate, non-straight designs, sink cutouts and faucet holes, from a CAD program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cutting of porcelain slabs in a fabrication shop. Transfers to tile cut-and-shape because the workpiece material and thickness class, the cut geometries (holes, notches, curves, mitres) and the required fit precision are the same.

sources.system: CNC abrasive waterjet tile cutting (FedTech inlay service; HORD CNC waterjet tile cutter)

sources.claim: CNC-controlled abrasive waterjets are used commercially to cut ceramic, porcelain and natural stone tile into intricate custom shapes and inlays with accuracy and geometry not achievable by hand, driven directly by imported CAD files.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC waterjet cutting of tile stock into arbitrary shapes. Transfers because the same machines cut the same tile materials to arbitrary outlines, which is precisely what fitting around obstacles, odd spaces and corners requires.

sources.claim: Monumental Labs operates robot arms that carve and shape natural stone blocks to a programmed 3D geometry in a Brooklyn factory, removing about 95% of the material before human finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic shaping of natural stone with rotary cutting tools to a specified geometry. Transfers to shaping irregular stone pieces to fit a gap, since the machine removes stone to a scanned/target surface rather than a rectilinear cut.

sources.system: Prodim Proliner / Laser Products LT-2D3D digital templating
sources.title: Templating methods | Stone World
sources.claim: Field conditions that make tile and stone cuts irregular — out-of-square walls, niches, undermount fixtures — are routinely captured as digital point-cloud templates on site and fed to shop cutting machines, so that the required non-rectangular geometry arrives at the machine as a file.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robot; cited only to show how the odd-space geometry is presented to a purpose-built cutting cell at E1. It cannot by itself support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Determine and implement the best layout to achieve a desired pattern.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom remodel/new build: setter measures an out-of-square room, decides where to start the field so cut tiles at walls, tub, curb and drain are balanced, snaps chalk lines on floor and shower walls, dry-lays a course, and sets the first tiles establishing the running-bond or stacked pattern around niche, drain slope and fixtures. 12x24 porcelain, tight 40-60 sq ft space, other trades' debris present.

Residential kitchen backsplash, entry, fireplace or accent wall: setter centers the pattern on range/hood/sink, sets a level ledger or laser line, plans courses around outlets, cabinets and window returns, and lays out mosaic sheets or subway tile so cuts land symmetrically. Small area, vertical work, occupied home.

Large open commercial/institutional floor field (school corridor, retail, airport concourse, lobby, hospital): setter transfers control lines from drawings onto a screeded slab, establishes the grid for a straight or offset pattern with feature bands and column alignment, snaps or lasers the layout across thousands of square feet, and starts the field courses. Active fit-out phase.

Commercial/institutional wall and small-room work: restroom and shower walls, corridor wainscot, commercial kitchen walls, stair treads and risers, elevator lobbies. Setter establishes plumb/level datum lines, courses tile to end symmetrically at corners, doors, accessories and fixtures, and sets out the pattern vertically in confined rooms.

Decorative and complex-pattern work: herringbone, diagonal, basketweave, borders, inlaid medallions, mosaic murals, and vein-matched or book-matched natural stone. Setter lays out the pattern dry, marks reference axes, positions the medallion/mural center on the room or feature, and adjusts tile-by-tile so the motif reads correctly in the finished space.

sources.title: FAQs — Partner Robotics
sources.claim: Partner Robotics' P900 floor tile paving robot lays full-size floor tiles into adhesive on real jobsites, but the paving path is configured by a human operator on a tablet, the robot paves lane by lane, and only full (uncut) tiles are placed; perimeter cut pieces and leveling clips remain manual, and only straight and offset patterns are supported.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-to-field layout printing on open floor areas. Comparable precision (1/16 in.) and identical deliverable to the tile setter's control-line layout for a floor grid pattern; same active-jobsite conditions.

sources.claim: As of mid-2026 the US tile industry association's magazine reports that tile-installation robots are marketed mainly for large, open commercial floors with repetitive layouts and are best suited to ideal conditions; layout judgment when field dimensions conflict with plans is still human work.

tasks.label: Mix, apply, and spread plaster, concrete, mortar, cement, mastic, glue or other adhesives to form a bed for the tiles, using brush, trowel and screed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom/shower remodel in an occupied home: mixing thinset in buckets with a paddle mixer, combing beds onto shower walls over waterproofing, working around a niche, curb and bench, floating/sloping a mortar pan, and bedding a small bathroom floor; tight room, fixtures and finished surfaces to protect.

Residential open-area floor: a cleared kitchen, living room, entry or basement in a house or apartment (new build or gut remodel); mixing and spreading thinset with a notched trowel over a prepared slab or underlayment for medium/large-format tile, including doorway transitions and perimeter cuts.

Kitchen backsplash, countertop or small detail work: spreading mastic or thinset with a small notched trowel on a short vertical field between counter and upper cabinets, around outlets, window returns, edges and end caps.

Commercial/institutional interior floor during fit-out: school corridor, hospital lobby, retail store, office or transit concourse; mixing mortar in a mixer/pump, screeding and combing a bed over hundreds of square metres of prepared slab for porcelain or stone tile.

Commercial wet-area wall tile at rough-in: restroom, locker room or commercial kitchen full-height walls and corridor wainscot; combing thinset onto cement board around pipe penetrations, corners, door jambs and accessory locations.

Exterior stone and paver work: patio, walkway or pool deck units set in a mortar bed on a prepared base, stair treads, and stone veneer on facades or chimneys; uneven grade, weather exposure, variable unit thickness.

This is the E1 form of forming an adhesive bed: the panel is fixtured and presented, and dosing/coverage are machine-controlled.

tasks.label: Study blueprints and examine surface to be covered to determine amount of material needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel (bathroom or kitchen) in an occupied home: the setter walks the gutted or existing space, measures floor and wall areas with a tape or laser measure, notes niches, jambs, and cut-heavy areas, checks substrate flatness and condition, then computes square footage plus a waste allowance and lists tile, thinset, backer board, and grout quantities to order.

New residential construction: the setter studies architectural plans and the finish schedule for multiple rooms, verifies rough framing dimensions on site, and calculates per-room tile quantities and setting materials for the whole house.

Commercial project (hotel, school, retail, hospital): the setter or foreman studies detailed blueprints, tile layout/elevation drawings, and finish schedules, performs a quantity takeoff for large repetitive areas, and reconciles the takeoff with field-measured conditions before material release.

Small job — backsplash, entry floor, fireplace surround, or a stone accent: a quick site visit with a tape measure and visual inspection of the surface, followed by an on-the-spot quantity estimate of tile, trim pieces, and setting material.

Exterior or specialty surface — patio, pool deck, roof deck, or stone veneer facade: the setter measures an irregular, sometimes weathered outdoor surface, inspects it for slope, drainage, and soundness, and estimates stone, mortar, and membrane quantities including extra for cuts.

tasks.label: Measure and mark surfaces to be tiled, following blueprints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open floor areas in commercial/institutional new construction (lobbies, corridors, cafeterias, retail sales floors, concourses): read the finish plan, tie to building control lines, measure the area, establish center/reference lines for the tile grid, snap chalk lines and mark movement joints, borders and pattern starts on a prepared slab or underlayment on an active jobsite.

Small enclosed rooms in commercial/institutional buildings (restrooms, gang showers, commercial kitchens, hotel bathrooms): after walls, fixtures and waterproofing are roughed in, measure the as-built room, balance the field to avoid sliver cuts at walls and drains, and mark reference lines on backer board or mortar bed in a 40-150 sq ft space.

Residential floor tile in new houses and remodels (bathrooms, kitchens, entries, mudrooms): often no model, only a plan sheet or sketch; rooms are out of square, cabinets/toilets/doorways in place, house may be occupied; dry-lay, find the working center, snap layout lines on plywood, backer board or slab.

Wall tile layout: tub/shower surrounds, backsplashes, restroom wainscot and feature walls. Measure wall heights and widths, establish a level datum and plumb reference lines on out-of-plumb/out-of-flat walls, mark course heights, ledger positions, niche and accent-band locations and cut lines directly on the vertical surface.

Exterior and facade work: plazas, patios, pool decks, roof decks and stone cladding. Measure and mark paving grid lines, slopes/drain falls and expansion joints on outdoor slabs, or mark panel/anchor positions on building elevations and slab edges, exposed to weather and rough substrates.

Cut-piece and unit work: countertops, stair treads and risers, thresholds, medallions and mosaic inlays. Measure the substrate or cabinet run, transfer dimensions from the shop drawing, and mark layout and cut lines on the substrate or on the stone/tile pieces.

sources.title: HP SitePrint - Robotic Layout Solution | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially sold autonomous layout robot that prints CAD linework, text, arcs and points directly onto construction slabs with ±2 mm layout accuracy, and also captures and marks floor level deviations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic construction layout. The physical act is identical to the tile setter's — measuring the slab and marking reference/grid lines from the drawing onto the same surfaces (concrete, plywood, vinyl, terrazzo) — at tighter precision than chalk lines.

sources.title: HP SitePrint FAQ | HP Official Site
sources.claim: The robot navigates the site and prints autonomously, avoiding unmodeled obstacles, and needs only one person on site to run a layout session.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy (not teleoperation) for the layout-marking system used to substantiate the floor-layout instances.

sources.title: HP SitePrint FAQ | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint prints layout on outdoor and rough substrates including tarmac, pavement, wood and terrazzo, i.e. the surfaces used for exterior paving and deck work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior construction layout printing. Marking a paving grid on an exterior slab or deck uses the same surfaces and the same line-marking precision as interior tile layout.

sources.title: Valley Interior Systems Sets the Pace with HP SitePrint Robots
sources.claim: A US interior contractor has put a fleet of HP SitePrint robots into production use for interior layout, replacing manual tape-measure and chalk-line layout on its jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior construction layout. Same act (printing plan lines on the finished floor substrate) in the same environment (active building interiors) that tile setters lay out in.

sources.title: Comparison of dusty robotics and traditional layout methods (Construction Robotics, Springer)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed field comparison of the Dusty Robotics FieldPrinter against manual layout on a real 8-floor medical office building, showing large labor and rework reductions for multi-trade layout printed on the jobsite deck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic jobsite layout printing. It replaces exactly the measure-and-snap-lines work the tile setter performs, on the same floor substrates, at 1/16 in accuracy, on an active commercial construction site.

sources.title: Automated Layout for Mechanical | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics markets the FieldPrinter as automating the manual measure-and-mark layout step, printing points, lines and labels from coordinated CAD/BIM files onto the jobsite floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-trade jobsite layout. The vendor describes the identical work unit ('measure-and-mark') that this O*NET task names, executed on the floors tile setters lay out.

tasks.label: Lay and set mosaic tiles to create decorative wall, mural, and floor designs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom remodel: setting mesh-mounted 1"-2" mosaic (glass, porcelain, pebble) on a sloped shower pan, in a niche, and as a wall accent band; requires notched-trowel thinset, back-buttering, cutting sheets around the drain and valve, beating in for lippage control, then grouting, cleaning and caulking corners in an occupied, non-standard home.

Kitchen or bar backsplash in a home: setting mesh- or paper-faced mosaic sheets on a flat but out-of-plumb wall, cutting sheets around outlets, window returns and upper cabinets, aligning joints across sheets, finishing edges with trim, grouting and cleaning around installed appliances and countertops.

Commercial/hospitality job site (hotel lobby, restaurant feature wall, restroom, corridor, retail): installing a decorative mosaic field, border or medallion over a large flat wall or floor per shop drawings, on an active construction site with other trades, dust, temporary lighting and site-cut edges.

Pool, spa, fountain or exterior application: setting waterline mosaic bands, step markers, and bottom logos on curved shell surfaces outdoors, using epoxy or modified thinset, working from the deck/inside the shell in weather-exposed, uneven conditions.

Shop/studio pre-assembly of a custom mural or medallion: composing the artwork tile by tile from loose tesserae per the artist's cartoon on a bench or layout table, sorting colors, and mounting the completed sections onto facing/mesh sheets, numbered for later field installation.

sources.claim: Artaic operates a commercial robotic mosaic fabrication line in Boston whose gantry pick-and-place robot composes decorative wall, mural and floor mosaic designs from individual tesserae in a purpose-built cell, producing faced square-foot sections for later human installation.

tasks.label: Apply mortar to tile back, position the tile, and press or tap with trowel handle to affix tile to base.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom/shower tiling (remodel or new home): shower walls, sloped pan, curb, niche and bathroom floor in a small room with plumbing rough-ins or installed fixtures; small- to medium-format tile; most pieces are cut and fitted around valves, drains, corners and thresholds; each piece back-buttered and beaten in by hand.

Floor tile in an occupied-home remodel (kitchen, entry, laundry, living area): cabinets, appliances and furniture in place, access through doorways or up stairs, 12x24 or similar porcelain set in thin-set on a prepared substrate, pieces pressed and beaten flat to a lippage tolerance.

Floor tile in bare new-construction houses/apartment units: open, empty rooms, prepared slab or underlayment, tiles palletized on site, large-format porcelain set in thin-set, whole field tiles pressed/vibrated into the mortar bed with perimeter pieces fitted last.

Large open floor areas in commercial/institutional new construction (lobbies, corridors, retail, transit halls, schools, hospitals): active jobsite with other trades, control lines laid out, large-format porcelain or dimensional stone tile set in thin-set over hundreds to thousands of square feet.

Flat wall tile in commercial and multifamily buildings under construction: restroom, locker-room, kitchen and corridor walls; 8x12 to 12x24 field tile back-buttered or notch-troweled onto prepared plaster/board walls and pressed to full mortar contact, with cuts at edges and penetrations.

Natural stone and decorative work: heavy stone pavers and slabs, stair treads and risers, exterior stone veneer walls and pool copings set in mortar, plus mosaics, borders, medallions and backsplashes—irregular, heavy or tiny units, often outdoors or on vertical/3-D surfaces.

tasks.label: Mix and apply mortar or cement to edges and ends of drain tiles to seal halves and joints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom remodel: setting a shower or floor drain before tiling — mixing deck mud/mortar by hand or paddle mixer, packing it against the edges of the drain body, sealing the joint between the clamping-ring halves and riser to the sloped bed and waterproof membrane. Occupied private home, cramped bathroom, one-off layout and slope.

Commercial interior fit-out (restaurant kitchen, restroom, locker room, natatorium): setting floor drains and trench/channel drain sections into a mud bed — mixing mortar or cement, applying it to the ends and edges of drain sections and channel halves, sealing the joints and bringing them flush with the finished tile plane. Active jobsite inside a building shell with other trades working around.

Exterior or foundation drainage line: laying clay or concrete drain tile in an open trench — mixing mortar/cement on site and buttering the ends of each tile section and the edges of split-tile halves so the joints are sealed, working over soil at varying grade, in weather, with water and mud present.

Shop or precast/fabrication yard: pre-assembling drain-tile sections, split-tile halves, or channel-drain segments at a bench before delivery — mortar mixed in a shop mixer, applied to edges and ends, halves mated, joints struck and cleaned. Fixed layout, standard equipment, institution controls the premises.

Repair/remediation: reopening and re-mortaring failed joints, or resealing drain-tile halves already installed in an existing floor, crawlspace, or trench. Access is confined, the existing work is as-found, and there is debris, standing water, and unknown geometry.

tasks.label: Apply a sealer to make grout stain- and water-resistant.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom remodel: after grout cures, seal grout in the tiled shower/tub surround walls, niche and curb plus the bathroom floor in an occupied private home; applicator bottle or brush along joints in a 5x8 ft room crowded with toilet, vanity and glass, with excess wiped off glazed tile before it hazes.

Residential kitchen: seal grout on a tile backsplash running between countertop and upper cabinets (and around outlets, range hood, window returns), often plus a natural-stone countertop or sill; vertical, low-clearance work in a finished home with cabinetry and appliances that must not be dripped on.

Residential interior floor area (entry, kitchen floor, hallway, laundry, sunroom) in a private home cleared of furniture: sealer run along all grout lines of an open tiled floor or spread over the whole floor, dwelled, then excess wiped from the tile; edges at baseboards, thresholds and toilet flanges included.

New residential construction or multifamily unit: seal floor grout in bathrooms, kitchens, entries of unfinished repetitive units on an active construction site, with dust, other trades, temporary lighting, steps between rooms and no finished fixtures yet installed.

Commercial/institutional interior floor (school corridor, restaurant dining room, hospital wing, retail store) inside a facility under an owner's control: large open tiled floor, sealer applied with applicator or roller over grout lines and buffed/wiped, worked around fixed equipment and cordoned from occupants.

Exterior stone work: seal grout/joints and stone on a patio, pool deck, entry steps or stone cladding at a private property; irregular natural stone, weather and temperature constraints, edges meeting soil, planters, siding and pool coping.

tasks.label: Level concrete and allow to dry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel: leveling a small existing interior floor (bathroom, kitchen, entry, laundry, 30-150 sq ft) in an occupied or partly finished home before tile — grinding/patching high and low spots, priming, mixing and pouring self-leveling underlayment, working it out with a gauge rake and smoother around door thresholds, cabinet toe-kicks, a toilet flange and transitions, then leaving it to cure overnight.

New residential / multifamily construction: flattening the concrete floor of unfinished units or a garage/basement slab, or pouring a cementitious leveling course over a few hundred to ~1,000 sq ft of bare shell floor to laser-set elevations before tile; empty rooms, other trades on site, cure before setting tile.

Commercial or institutional fit-out: leveling a large open floor (1,000-20,000 sq ft) in a retail store, school, hospital wing, office or transit building under construction — pump-placed self-leveling underlayment or a screeded leveling layer over the slab, worked to flatness tolerance across a big continuous pour, then cured/dried before tile.

Mortar bed / deck-mud work: packing and screeding a sloped mortar bed to a drain for a shower floor, bathroom, locker room or commercial kitchen — small confined area, slope to drain, curbs and wall junctions, cut around the drain flange, then cure before waterproofing and tile.

Exterior work: leveling a concrete or mortar setting bed for a patio, porch, stair landing, pool deck or roof deck before stone/tile — irregular small areas, pitch for drainage, edges and steps, weather-exposed cure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom remodel in an occupied home: setter measures shower walls, curb and niche, then cuts galvanized diamond-mesh lath sheets with tin snips to fit stud bays and trim around the mixing valve, drain and corners before the mortar bed scratch coat. Tight, cluttered space; dimensions taken in situ with tape and pencil marks.

Exterior thin stone veneer or stucco base over sheathing on a house or small commercial building: measure wall runs and cut lath sheets to length and to fit around windows, doors, hose bibs and corners, working outdoors from ladders or scaffold in variable weather.

Commercial interior new construction (restroom, kitchen, pool deck, gang shower): batch-measure and cut many lath sheets at an on-site cut station for mortar-bed walls and floors, then final-trim pieces to fit penetrations and control joints amid other trades on an active site.

Ceilings, soffits, arches and curved surfaces: measure overhead areas and cut lath to size, notching around light boxes, sprinkler heads, ducts and pipes, often on a lift or ladder with the piece held overhead for fitting.

Contractor shop or fabrication facility work: cutting lath to standard sizes on a cut table for prefabricated mortar-bed panels, mud-set countertops or precut kits, from standard 27"x96" sheets with dimensions taken from a cut list or shop drawing.
