Transfers to the variant where an accessory (soap dish, niche shelf) is bedded in thinset/adhesive rather than screwed: same operation of laying a controlled adhesive bead on a fixtured substrate then placing the part to position.

sources.system: DALE (DEWALT / August Robotics downward drilling robot)
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: DEWALT Unveils the World's First Downward Drilling, Fleet-Capable Robot to Accelerate Data Center Construction
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics' DALE is a fleet-capable autonomous jobsite drilling robot that reads digital layouts and drills holes in concrete on data centre construction projects, launched commercially in 2026 — on-site autonomy is limited to drilling, not to handling and fastening finished fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite hole drilling. Cited to bound the state of the art on unstructured/institutional sites: the most advanced deployed construction robots drill holes in flat concrete decks and do not install or anchor finished fixtures on tiled walls, so E2/E3 is unsupported.

tasks.label: Prepare surfaces for tiling by attaching lath or waterproof paper, or by applying a cement mortar coat to a metal screen.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom/shower prep in a home (new build or remodel): staple roofing felt or sheet waterproofing over studs, cut and nail expanded metal lath around corners, curb and niche, cut around plumbing penetrations, then float a cement scratch coat on walls and a mortar pan sloped to the drain. Tight 3'x5' space, dust, other trades' materials on the floor.

Exterior stone/thin-brick veneer wall prep on a house or small commercial building: staple weather-resistant building paper over sheathing with proper laps and flashing, nail metal lath to studs, then apply a cement scratch coat and rake it, working from ladders/scaffold in outdoor weather.

Commercial/multifamily interior wet-area prep during construction (hotel bathrooms, commercial kitchens, locker rooms): waterproof membrane or paper plus lath on walls, and mortar beds sloped to floor drains, repeated across many similar rooms in an active jobsite with other trades working nearby.

Large interior floor mud-bed prep in a commercial space under construction (lobby, mall corridor, kitchen): roll out cleavage membrane/waterproof paper over the slab, lay and lap wire reinforcing mesh, then screed and compact a 1-1/4 in. mortar bed flat to tolerance around columns, thresholds and drains.

Apply-only job: float a cement scratch/leveling mortar coat onto metal lath already fastened by others on a large flat interior wall of a building under construction, bringing it plumb and true and scratching it to receive tile.

Shop/prefab work: prepping fixtured substrates on benches in a fabrication shop or bathroom-pod factory - attaching mesh/lath and paper to panels, countertop or hearth decks, and applying a mortar coat before tile or stone is set.

sources.title: Construction robotics: Okibo brings painting robot to America
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a self-contained, fully autonomous wall-finishing robot (drywall compound application, sanding, painting) working on active US and European commercial construction sites; it applies coating material to interior walls without external references or site preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying and finishing a wall coating on a jobsite. It shows autonomous navigation and coating of interior walls, which transfers partially to applying a mortar coat, but the material is joint compound/paint on flat drywall, not cement mortar keyed into metal lath, and the robot does no fastening of paper or lath.

sources.title: Plastering Robot - WEIBUILD Construction Robot
sources.claim: The Weibuild PMC-3000iE/6000iE plastering robot is a commercially sold mobile robot that autonomously navigates a building interior and pumps, applies, presses and levels cement plaster on indoor walls to ±3 mm/2 m, at 300-350 m2/day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of a cement mortar coat to a wall in a building under construction. Same material (cement plaster), same operation (pump, apply, screed to a plumb, flat plane) as a scratch/leveling coat; not demonstrated over expanded metal lath or on small, cut-up bathroom geometry.

sources.system: Mortar spraying and plastering integrated robot
sources.developer: Academic research team (published in Automation in Construction)
sources.title: Mortar spraying and plastering integrated robot for wall construction - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed mortar spraying and plastering robot autonomously sprays and levels a 10 mm cement mortar coat on walls with 0.38 mm average thickness deviation using vision and hybrid force-position control, in experimental (laboratory/mock-up) tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of a cement mortar coat of controlled thickness to a wall, the same physical operation as a scratch/leveling coat; demonstrated only on prepared test walls, not on metal lath or sloped mortar beds.

sources.title: Equipment Management: The Right Tool for the Job Might Be a Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Canvas 1200CX/2000CX drywall finishing robots are commercially deployed on US jobsites; an operator positions them and the machine sprays and sands compound over whole walls to Level 4/5 finish with minimal intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of a wet coating to interior walls on real construction sites, showing that coat-application (not sheet fastening) is automatable in jobsite conditions; it does not handle membranes, lath or cement mortar beds.

sources.title: Japanese researchers create humanoid bot that installs drywall independently | Construction Dive
sources.claim: The HRP-5P humanoid autonomously lifted a gypsum board and screwed it to a stud wall in a laboratory mock-up - the closest demonstrated analog to fastening sheet material to a framed wall - but the demonstration is slow, one-off and far from production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening a sheet material to a stud wall, the analog of nailing lath or stapling waterproof paper. Cited to show the state of the art is a slow laboratory demo, insufficient for worker-quality completion at any tier.

sources.title: WEINMANN at the Dach+Holz | HOMAG
sources.claim: Weinmann WALLTEQ multifunction bridges automatically staple and nail rigid sheathing to timber wall frames fixtured on factory tables; published assessment of such panel lines reports that building-wrap membrane installation on the panels is still done manually by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic stapling/nailing of sheet material to a fixtured wall panel in a purpose-built line. It covers rigid board sheathing only; no cited machine unrolls and staples building paper or places and fastens expanded metal lath, which the surveyed panel-line literature reports as manual work.

tasks.label: Remove and replace cracked or damaged tile.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home, floor: one to several cracked ceramic/porcelain floor tiles in a kitchen, entry or hall. Worker protects surroundings, grinds/rakes out grout joints, breaks out the cracked tile with hammer/chisel or oscillating tool without chipping neighbors, scrapes the old thinset off the slab or backerboard, checks for substrate cracking/hollow spots, dry-fits a matched replacement (often discontinued stock), back-butters and sets it flush within lippage tolerance, then grouts, cleans haze and seals.

Occupied home, wall/wet area: cracked or drummy tile in a shower surround, tub wall or backsplash, worked overhead or at chest height in a tight bathroom. Requires cutting grout without cutting the waterproofing, removing the tile and setting bed, patching membrane/backer if damaged, resetting a matched tile plumb and flush with the field, then grouting/caulking the change of plane.

Punch-list / warranty repair on an active construction or remodel jobsite before turnover: tiles chipped, cracked, hollow-sounding or set out of level by other trades, scattered across a bare, unfurnished floor. Same cut-out, remove, clean substrate, reset and grout sequence, done under dust control with other trades present and site conditions changing daily.

Occupied commercial/institutional facility (hotel lobby, hospital corridor, school, retail store, restaurant): replacing damaged floor or wall tiles in a controlled, fixed-layout building, usually after hours behind barricades, with strict dust/noise limits, fast-set mortar and grout so the area reopens by morning; must match the existing field and finish flush for traffic and cleanability.

Exterior/specialty repair: waterline pool tile, stone-clad entry steps, patio or plaza pavers, exterior wall tile. Work is outdoors on an as-found surface, often at odd heights or over water, with weather exposure, setting-bed or freeze-thaw damage to repair, and thick-bed mortar or epoxy setting materials.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Partner Robotics' PavePal P900 is a commercially sold floor tile paving robot that automates laying new tile on prepared indoor floors; the company reports roughly 100,000 sq m of tiling work completed. It lays new tile on cleared substrate and has no demonstrated ability to remove existing bonded, cracked tile or prepare a repair void.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is new tile installation on bare, prepared floors in new construction. It does not transfer to 'remove and replace cracked tile': the repair instance begins with selective demolition of a bonded tile inside an existing field, substrate cleanup and flush matching to neighboring tiles, none of which this robot performs.

sources.system: Fabrica AI autonomous tile grouting robot (V5)
sources.title: Grouting robot | Fabrica AI
sources.claim: Fabrica AI's grouting robot autonomously fills grout lines across a tiled room in apartments in Singapore, showing autonomous finishing work on tile floors, but only the grouting sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is grouting an already-tiled floor. It covers only the final sub-step of a tile repair and provides no capability for removing a damaged tile, cleaning the old setting bed, or setting a replacement flush with the field.

sources.title: Power & Efficiency with Remote-Controlled Demolition Machine - Brokk
sources.claim: Compact demolition machines used for interior strip-outs and selective removal (including tile and floor removal) are remote-controlled by an operator, not autonomous; industry commentary as of 2026 still treats autonomy for these machines as a future development.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is selective demolition/interior strip-out, the removal half of this task. It cannot support a positive judgment because the machines are continuously teleoperated, and they are far too coarse to extract one cracked tile without damaging adjacent tiles.

sources.title: Top 10: Construction Robotics | Construction Digital
sources.claim: Trade coverage in 2026 lists the Brokk 170 for selective demolition and describes it as remote-controlled; forward-looking commentary identifies only semi-autonomous assistance (tool pressure, controlled-depth removal) as the likely next step, indicating no autonomous selective-demolition system exists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is selective demolition. Confirms that as of 2026 the removal half of tile repair is performed by human-operated remote-control machines, so no autonomous system substantiates the removal step.

sources.developer: Singapore University of Technology and Design (research)
sources.title: Multispecies hybrid bioinspired climbing robot for wall tile inspection - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Wall tile condition assessment has been robotized (a climbing robot with AI acoustic recognition replaces manual sounding-rod inspection for delaminated tiles), but the system only detects defective tiles; repair/replacement remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is locating cracked/hollow tiles, the diagnostic first step of this task. It does not transfer further: the robot performs no removal, substrate preparation, setting or grouting.

tasks.label: Cut tile backing to required size, using shears.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom/kitchen remodel in an occupied home: setter measures the floor or wet-wall area and cuts cement/fiber-cement backer board (HardieBacker, Durock) sheets to size with backer-board shears, including notches and cut-outs around a toilet flange, supply lines and drains, working in a cramped room with tools and materials on the floor.

Commercial new construction or tenant improvement (hotel bathroom stacks, hospital, retail, school): setter batch-cuts backer board sheets to repeat sizes with shears in an unfinished, partly built space, mostly straight rectangular cuts, amid other trades and shifting material stacks.

Cutting galvanized metal lath, wire reinforcing mesh or hardware cloth to size with tin snips/shears for mortar-bed (mud) floors, shower pans and wall floats, trimming to fit around drains, curbs and corners on site.

Cutting flexible tile backing sheet goods — uncoupling/waterproofing membrane (Ditra, Kerdi), fabric-faced foam board and seam banding — to size and shape with shears on the jobsite floor before bonding.

Contractor's shop, staging area or prefab/panelization bay: cutting backer board and membrane to standard sizes ahead of installation for repeat units (e.g., identical hotel baths or shower pods), work benched on sawhorses or a cutting table under institutional control.

sources.title: KOBOT X — Kobots cutting robots
sources.claim: KOBOT X is a commercial mobile cutting robot for construction that cuts sheet materials up to 45 mm thick, explicitly including fibre cement board (the material used as tile backer board) and fibre gypsum, executing programmed cut geometry after the operator loads the sheet into the machine's own frame.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is cutting fibre-cement/gypsum sheet board to a specified size; tile backer board is the same class of material, thickness and dimensional tolerance, so cutting performance transfers directly. The machine still requires the sheet to be loaded into its own fixture, i.e. work brought to the machine.

sources.title: Kobots - cutting robots for the construction industry
sources.claim: The KOBOT Classic is a mobile board-cutting robot sold in four sizes for construction-site use; cuts are specified via smartphone and executed by the machine, with the board placed in the robot's own bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting building boards (gypsum, fibre cement, plywood) to required size on jobsites. Same sheet-goods geometry and tolerances as tile backing; the robot supplies its own fixtured cutting bed rather than working the site as found.

sources.system: SafanDarley Fully automatic cutting center M 310-6
sources.title: Fully automatic cutting center - SafanDarley
sources.claim: SafanDarley's fully automatic cutting center is a hydraulic guillotine shear with an automatic sheet feed, CNC pre-stop positioning and automatic product discharge, cutting sheet stock to programmed sizes without an operator handling each cut.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shearing thin sheet metal to required size. Metal lath and wire mesh tile backing are thin galvanized sheet stock cut by the same shearing action, at looser tolerance than the machine's rated repeat accuracy.

sources.system: KMT CNC waterjet cutting station for fiber cement board (FCB) lines
sources.title: MISC-FIBER CEMENT BOARD-WATERJET CUTTING | KMT Waterjet
sources.claim: Fiber-cement panel production lines include an automated cutting station that trims panels to the desired size, running unattended in multi-shift operation; KMT supplies CNC waterjet cutting for this station, which also cuts intricate contours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting fiber cement panels to size on a production line. Same material as cement backer board; CNC control allows arbitrary outlines and notches, covering the scribed/notched cuts a setter makes by hand.

sources.system: Zünd G3 / Q-Line flatbed digital cutters
sources.title: Composites | Zünd
sources.claim: Zünd flatbed digital cutters perform automated knife/blade cutting of flexible and composite sheet goods to programmed outlines, with vacuum hold-down and camera registration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: knife-cutting flexible sheet goods (composites, textiles, foams, gaskets) to programmed shapes. Uncoupling/waterproofing membrane and fabric-faced backing are the same class of flexible sheet cut with shears, at far looser tolerance.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor robotic sheathing system (deployed at FrameTec)
sources.title: This Plant Runs Itself - Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: At FrameTec's plant, Randek ZeroLabor robots apply sheathing board to wall panels and use routers to cut ... door and window openings, i.e. cut board material to specified geometry on a production line with minimal human input.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting of construction sheet board to required size and shape, including openings, in a fixtured production line — the same operation as sizing tile backing when the work is presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Remove any old tile, grout and adhesive using chisels and scrapers and clean the surface carefully.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full bathroom gut-out in an occupied private home: chisel ceramic wall tile off a tub/shower surround and floor tile off a mortar bed or plywood subfloor with hammer drill and chisels, scrape residual thinset, work around toilet flange, valves and door casing, bag debris and vacuum the substrate clean for new tile.

Residential kitchen or entry job: remove old floor tile and mastic/thinset around installed cabinets, appliances and thresholds, or strip a backsplash off drywall without destroying the board, then scrape and clean the substrate; homeowner's furnishings must be protected and dust contained.

Commercial renovation zone (retail store, school corridor, restaurant, hospital wing under refit): strip several thousand square feet of old tile and cured thinset off a concrete slab with walk-behind/ride-on scrapers and grinders, HEPA dust control, working around columns, floor drains and partially demolished partitions; substrate left flat and clean.

Small selective repair: remove a handful of cracked or hollow tiles and rake out the surrounding grout joints without chipping the adjacent field tile, clean out the joint and old adhesive, and leave the recess ready for replacement tile in an occupied home or facility restroom/lobby.

Substrate preparation before setting new tile on a construction site or fit-out: knock down mortar ridges, drywall compound, cured adhesive residue and paint or curing compound from a concrete slab or wall with scrapers and grinders, then sweep/vacuum and wipe the surface so thinset will bond.

sources.title: Automated Concrete Removal and Demolition | Conjet
sources.claim: Conjet ACR hydrodemolition robots remove concrete and surface material from structures; after the operator sets parameters and positions the machine, the robot runs the removal pattern by itself, leaving a surface described as ideal for bonding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled removal of bonded hard material (deteriorated concrete, mortar, coatings) from a substrate and cleaning it for re-bonding. Same physics and acceptance criterion as stripping a tile bed/thinset from a slab and leaving a sound, clean, bondable surface.

sources.system: Conjet ACR hydrodemolition robots (surface preparation configuration)
sources.title: Surface Preparation using ACR - Automated Concrete Removal | Conjet
sources.claim: The same Conjet ACR robots are marketed and used for surface preparation: clearing pre-existing coatings, rust and other tough ... and contaminants from a surface, with an optional vacuum port that captures the removed material.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing adhered surface layers (coatings, adhesives, scale) and capturing the debris, i.e., the adhesive-removal and surface-cleaning half of the tile setter's task, executed by machine on a substrate that must be left clean and bondable.

sources.system: GrayMatter GMR-AI Scan&Sand / Scan&Grind robotic cell
sources.title: Robotics Sanding Cell Tackles the High Seas - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics has deployed autonomous robotic abrasive material-removal cells at manufacturers; the robots scan each part and generate their own tool paths for sanding, grinding and polishing inside a fenced cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled abrasive removal of surface material from a fixtured workpiece whose geometry varies part to part, with in-cell dust capture — the scraping/grinding off of residual adhesive and mortar and cleaning of the substrate, done at the E1 presentation.

sources.system: Husqvarna DXR series / Brokk demolition robots
sources.title: Construction and demolition robots are building safer, smarter worksites
sources.claim: Commercial demolition robots used for breaking tile, masonry and concrete in refurbishment work (Husqvarna DXR, Brokk) are remote-controlled machines driven continuously by an operator, not autonomous systems.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (percussive removal of tile, mortar and concrete on site); cited to show that the on-site machines capable of this work are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive E2/E3 judgment.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The autonomous robots working unfenced on building sites today apply material (plaster, drywall compound, paint) rather than demolish or strip surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface work on an as-found interior construction site. Cited to characterize the limit of on-site autonomy (material application on flat walls), which does not extend to chiselling out tile, grout and adhesive.

tasks.label: Cut, surface, polish, and install marble and granite or install pre-cast terrazzo, granite or marble units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential kitchen/bath granite or marble countertop: field-measure/template, cut slab to size with sink and cooktop cutouts, transport and set the pieces on cabinet bases, shim and level, seam and polish edges and cutouts on site in an occupied or nearly finished home.

Setting marble/granite tile and small slabs on residential floors, shower walls, entries, stair treads and fireplace surrounds: layout, wet-saw cutting to fit around jambs, drains and fixtures, back-buttering and setting in thinset, leveling and grouting, in confined as-found rooms.

Large open commercial interior floor field (hotel lobby, mall, airport concourse, station) tiled with large-format marble/granite units over a prepared substrate: mortar spread and full-unit field laying to layout lines with tight, level joints, during construction or fit-out.

Commercial cut-in and unit work: scribing and cutting stone to fit walls, columns, drains and thresholds; setting precast terrazzo/granite/marble stair treads, risers, thresholds, wall base and window sills to line and level on an active job site.

Fabrication shop work on marble/granite slabs: slab layout, cutting parts to size with cutouts and miters, calibrating/surfacing, and honing/polishing edges and faces of countertops, treads and panels using shop saws, CNC and polishing machines.

On-site surfacing of installed marble or terrazzo floor fields: sequential grinding, honing and polishing of a large floor area with walk-behind/planetary machines and diamond abrasives in a commercial building during finishing or restoration.

sources.title: Robo SawJet 2.0 | Robotic Sawjet for Stone Fabricators | BACA
sources.claim: BACA Systems' Robo SawJet is a robotic sawjet that cuts granite/marble slabs into finished countertop parts; over 650 units are operating in North American stone fabrication shops.

sources.title: Fabricating Technology- Equipment | Stone World
sources.claim: Trade press describes the Robo SawJet as a KUKA-robot-powered dual-table sawjet that produces a fully cut slab, including radii, arcs and sink cutouts, in 12-30 minutes.

sources.title: Meet ROBOTOR, the Robotic Sculptor of Marble Statues - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: Robotor's multi-axis stone-milling robots carve and surface Carrara marble in a dedicated robotic workshop, using self-programming software and sensor-monitored continuous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic milling/surfacing of marble. It transfers to the 'cut and surface' step on the same material at equal or finer precision, in the same kind of purpose-built stone-processing cell.

sources.title: Polishing line for marble slabs - Pedrini
sources.claim: Pedrini supplies automatic industrial lines that hone and polish marble and granite slabs with sequences of operating heads under automated control.

sources.title: Straight 8 | Line Polisher | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA's Straight 8 line polisher edges, polishes and chamfers stone countertop pieces in a single continuous pass, and BACA's machine line includes robotic loading/unloading of parts.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Partner Robotics' P900 floor tile paving robot automates indoor tile laying (adhesive application plus placement) and has completed roughly 100,000 sq m of commercial tiling work, with markets in North America, Europe and the Middle East.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic laying of large-format floor tile. Transfers to setting marble/granite floor tile: same operation (spread mortar, place a heavy rigid unit to tight joints on a prepared floor) in the same tile formats used for stone.

sources.title: Floor Tile Paving Robot P900 | HKTDC Sourcing
sources.claim: Supplier specification for the P900 lists indoor tile laying at 15-18 sq m/h for formats up to 600x1200 mm and single-tile weights up to 30 kg - covering typical marble and granite floor tile - with over 100,000 sq m of commercial application.
sources.transferJustification: Payload and format range cover common marble/granite floor tile sizes, supporting transfer from ceramic to stone units.

sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Red Dot Design Award: Floor Tile Paving Robot R-19
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' R-19 floor tile paving robot is ... award-recognised, fully automated omnidirectional machine for paving large-format floor tiles using vision-based measurement and positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated large-format floor tile paving; transfers to marble/granite floor tile of the same formats laid in mortar beds on building floors.

sources.system: Tile laying robot / floor tile laying robot (Bright Dream-type construction robots)
sources.title: Construction Tile Laying Robot: Applications and Benefits - ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: Construction tile-laying robots perform whole-bed mortar laying for tiles up to 800x800 mm and are applied to stone tile laying in airports, stations, subways and plazas, using laser/visual navigation for autonomous adhesive laying, tile transport and paving.
sources.transferJustification: Names stone tile laying directly as an application of the autonomous tile-laying robot, supporting transfer from ceramic to stone units of the same size class.

sources.developer: ProBuild Robotics / Bright Dream-type construction robots
sources.title: Automated Concrete Floor Leveling Robots for High-Precision Construction - ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: Construction floor-grinding robots with automatic navigation and high-power grinding heads are sold for grinding stone and terrazzo ... as well as cured concrete and epoxy floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine grinding/polishing of hard mineral floors. Same machine class (planetary diamond grinder) and abrasive process used to surface and polish installed marble and terrazzo floors.

sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing - LightWare LiDAR
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 retrofits a concrete floor polisher with LiDAR-based autonomy so it self-navigates and runs a floor polishing job without a walk-behind operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grinding/polishing of large hard floors. The abrasive process, machine class and navigation problem match surfacing and polishing an installed marble or terrazzo floor field.

tasks.label: Spread mastic or other adhesive base on roof deck to form base for promenade tile, using serrated spreader.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional flat roof or plaza deck: setter spreads bituminous mastic/adhesive with a notched (serrated) spreader over a prepared, slightly sloped deck to receive promenade tile — a largely open field plus perimeter bands at parapets and feathering around roof drains, curbs and pipe penetrations. Outdoors, material hoisted to the roof, work paced by weather and adhesive open time.

Rooftop terrace / amenity deck on a multifamily or office building: moderate, irregularly shaped area with planters, HVAC curbs, railing posts, door thresholds and stair access; adhesive spread in sections between obstructions, keyed to the layout lines, on a substrate that varies in flatness.

Small residential roof deck, balcony or porch deck (under ~200 sq ft): tight access via interior stair or roof hatch, edges and thresholds dominate the area, adhesive spread by hand in one or two passes and tile set immediately before skinning over.

Repair/replacement of failed promenade tile on an existing, occupied building's roof deck: damaged tile and old mastic residue removed, substrate cleaned and primed, then fresh mastic spread in small irregular patches flush with the surrounding existing tile field.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor Robotic Gluing is a commercially offered, fully automated factory cell that reads CAD/CAM data and applies adhesive with controlled distribution across fixtured wall, floor and roof panel assemblies in offsite construction plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic adhesive application to prefabricated floor/roof panels. It transfers to spreading a mastic base on a deck at E1 because the physical act is the same — distributing a viscous adhesive over the full face of a flat, fixtured building element to a controlled pattern and film thickness, at precision at least as tight as a notched-trowel bed, with the workpiece presented to the machine.

sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Red Dot Design Award: Floor Tile Paving Robot R-19
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' R-19 floor tile paving robot is a fully automated mobile system that applies the cementitious adhesive bed to the floor substrate and then sets large-format tiles into the fresh bed with millimetre precision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying interior floor tile including machine application of the adhesive bed. It bears on this task because the adhesive-bed step is functionally the same act, but the demonstrated setting is interior building floors, not an exposed, sloped roof deck with drains and parapets.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Partner Robotics' PavePal P900 is a commercially sold indoor floor tile paving robot that has completed roughly 100,000 square metres of tiling work; the product is explicitly scoped to indoor tile laying.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanised floor tile installation with machine-applied bedding. Relevant because it is the largest real deployment of adhesive-bed-plus-tile robots, but it is indoor-only, so it does not substantiate work on an outdoor roof deck.

sources.system: Legend Robot Tile Laying & Paving Robot
sources.developer: Shenzhen Legend Robot Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Tile Laying & Paving Robot — Legend Robot
sources.claim: Legend Robot's tile laying robot controls adhesive spread and pattern, but by the manufacturer's own description it only handles large-area tiling while human workers finish corners and edges, and it runs with two workers (one operating, one refilling material).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic floor tiling with machine-applied adhesive. It establishes the boundary of current capability — open field only, with attending workers for operation, refilling and all perimeter/detail work — which is why a whole deck-spreading job is not completed autonomously.

sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Red Dot Design Award: Floor coating robot DPQ-02
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' DPQ-02 floor coating robot autonomously coats underground garage floors, controlling coating thickness with a manipulator and using automatic path planning and obstacle avoidance at 120 sqm per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a controlled-thickness liquid material over a floor slab. It shows machine spreading of coatings across facility floors, but a coating film is not a notched adhesive bed that must hold heavy promenade tile, and no roof-deck use is shown.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 robots autonomously apply and finish coatings on walls at active US construction sites, covering more than one million square ... — the most mature autonomous viscous-material spreading on jobsites, but limited to interior wall plastering, drywall finishing and painting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spreading of viscous compound over building surfaces on unstructured construction sites. Considered for E3, but it works on interior vertical drywall, not on exposed roof decks, and does not lay an adhesive bed for tile, so it does not substantiate this task.

instances.label: Shop pre-assembly of custom mosaic sheets: in the tile contractor's or fabricator's shop, the setter tapes manila/kraft paper with the drawn design to a bench, brushes water-soluble glue over it, and sets uniform machine-made tesserae (1" or smaller glass/porcelain) finished-side-down into the pattern; sheets are numbered for installation.

Jobsite lay-up: on an active construction/remodel site, the setter draws a border or medallion layout on paper from field measurements on a plywood table, brushes glue, and sets the job's standard tesserae face-down so the mounted sheets can be installed the same day; dust, variable lighting, other trades present.

Batch production of a large mural, pool graphic or logo: many square-foot paper-mounted sections assembled to a numbered cartoon in a mosaic fabrication facility, then labeled, packed and shipped to the install site.
Machine-cut stone mosaic patterns (marble basketweave, Greek key or rosette borders, hex fields) face-mounted onto kraft paper in a stone shop, with pieces coming pre-cut to size from the saw.

Artisanal/irregular work: hand-nipped smalti, salvaged tesserae or field-cut odd shapes of varying size and thickness, laid to a freehand-drawn cartoon or to a patch outline traced from an existing historic mosaic being matched; done in a studio or on site.

sources.title: Artaic Launches Mosaic Manufacturing Robot, Apollo

instances.label: Residential bathroom: build a dry-pack mortar underbed for a shower floor (pre-slope and top bed) in a home under renovation or new build — mortar mixed on site, packed and screeded to a 1/4-in-per-foot slope around a drain flange, tied into the curb and waterproofing, in a 3x5 ft cluttered space.

Interior wall underbed: fasten metal lath / reinforcing wire to studs or masonry with staples, screws or tie wire and apply scratch and float mortar coats plumb and flat (float-strip screeded) for wall tile or thin stone in shower walls or a commercial restroom on an active jobsite.

Large-area floor mortar bed: mud-set bed over cleavage membrane and welded wire reinforcing across a lobby, corridor or commercial kitchen slab in a building under construction — mortar hauled in, screeded to level or to floor drains, cut around thresholds and columns.

Dimension stone cladding anchoring: lay out and drill into concrete/CMU backup, set expansion or adhesive anchors, install steel angles, brackets and kerf clips with shims to plumb, and bend/twist wire anchors into stone anchor holes, working from scaffold or lift on an interior or exterior wall.

Small anchoring and support work: drill, anchor and level support brackets or cleats for stone countertops, vanities, tub decks, thresholds and window sills in occupied homes and small commercial spaces, fastening into wood framing, drywall/CMU or concrete.

sources.system: Hitachi dual-arm construction robot (with Waseda University)
sources.title: Robot System for Highly Efficient Work at Heights on Scaffolding under Unstable Installation Conditions
sources.claim: Hitachi's dual-arm construction robot autonomously inserts anchor bolts into holes in concrete walls with >99% success, using machine-learning control that copes with unstable scaffolding and imprecise hole location; demonstrated as an R&D system, not a shipped product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hammering post-installed anchor bolts into concrete. This is the same fastener, substrate and tolerance class as the tile/stone setter's 'install anchor bolts' element; the demonstration rig (fixed scaffolding, pre-drilled hole pattern) is a purpose-built machine setting, so it supports E1.

sources.title: Robots under Autonomous Control at Robot Lab | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy autonomously senses ceiling grid framing, inserts ceiling suspension bolts and screws boards to the base material under tablet-issued instructions; trialed in Shimizu's robot lab and sent to a high-rise building site in Osaka.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting suspension bolts and screwing panels overhead in building interiors. Comparable fasteners and hardware to installing brackets and anchor bolts for stone, but demonstrated only on a regular, pre-engineered ceiling grid — i.e., work presented in a known, machine-friendly pattern.

sources.system: Econ Drive automated concrete spreader (Progress Group carousel plant)
sources.title: Modernization of the industrial facility of A2C Prefa for more sustainability — Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: Precast concrete carousel plants use automated concrete spreaders that dispense a controlled quantity of cementitious material onto fixtured pallets/moulds from transmitted CAD/production data; installed commercially at A2C Prefa's plant in the Paris region.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a measured cementitious bed of specified thickness over a fixtured form. This is the core of 'building an underbed' — same material class and thickness control — carried out in a purpose-built pallet-circulation line (E1).

sources.title: Surface technology - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Precast plants finish the cast cementitious surface automatically: a trowelling machine with adjustable rotating vanes runs over the pallet at the trowelling station and smooths the element after an initial curing period.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: screeding and trowelling a fresh cementitious layer to a plane finish on a fixtured pallet — the finishing half of building a mortar underbed, at the same material and flatness class, in an E1 plant setting.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN multifunction bridges perform all planking operations on fixtured timber-frame elements fully automatically, including nailing, stapling and screwing sheet material to framing, driven by CAD data; sold commercially to house-building plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically fastening sheet material and hardware to a fixtured framed panel. Transfers to fastening metal lath, wire reinforcing and brackets to a presented substrate: same fastener types, millimetre placement accuracy, in a purpose-built gantry cell.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EP-1 plastering and finishing robot
sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous, AI-guided finishing robots (plastering, drywall finishing, painting) navigate construction sites and apply coatings to walls and ceilings; the painting/drywall robots are reported active on major European sites with over 1 million sq ft covered, and the EG7 plastering robot was launched in the US in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application and smoothing of a cementitious plaster coat on walls. Comparable material to a scratch/float coat, but the system does not install lath, wire ties or screeds to tile-setting float strips, so it supports the coating step only.

sources.title: Advanced Construction Robotics Launches The World's First Rebar Lifting, Carrying, And Placing Robot
sources.claim: TyBOT autonomously ties reinforcing steel intersections with wire on bridge decks, running on screed rails installed for it; commercially deployed, completing 101,564 ties on a Texas highway project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tie-wire installation. Closest demonstrated analogue to 'install wires' in stone setting, but it works only on a flat grid of bars beneath a gantry running on rails set up for the machine — a machine-oriented presentation of the work.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a ... deployed on construction projects worldwide that drills anchor holes from digital plans and marks them; anchor and bracket installation itself is still done by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling anchor holes on real construction sites. Shows only the drilling sub-step is automated in unstructured site settings; the setting of anchors, brackets and wire ties remains manual, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion at E2/E3.

roles.title: Cement Masons and Concrete Finishers
roles.description: Smooth and finish surfaces of poured concrete, such as floors, walks, sidewalks, roads, or curbs using a variety of hand and power tools. Align forms for sidewalks, curbs, or gutters; patch voids; and use saws to cut expansion joints.

tasks.label: Check the forms that hold the concrete to see that they are properly constructed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial flatwork: before pouring a driveway, sidewalk, patio or garage slab, the mason walks the site-built 2x4/2x6 lumber forms staked into graded soil — sighting line, checking grade and drainage slope with level/string, checking squareness and dimensions, confirming stakes are driven and braced, kickers set, joints tight so concrete won't leak, and forms oiled/clean. Mud, uneven subgrade, no BIM model.

Municipal curb, gutter and street sidewalk: steel or wood forms pinned to grade along a street or subdivision, including radii and ADA ramps; check line and grade against offset stakes/stringline, pin and brace count, joint alignment and form ties, slope tolerances, all in an open work zone with traffic and passing equipment.

Commercial slab-on-grade or elevated deck in a building under construction: perimeter edge forms, bulkheads, blockouts, embeds and screed rails plus deck shoring; verify dimensions and elevations against plans with laser level/total station, confirm bracing/shoring spacing and edge form support ahead of a large pour, while other trades work nearby.

Cast-in-place walls, footings and columns: modular panel formwork (Symons/EFCO-type) or job-built footing forms; check plumb, alignment, tie and waler spacing against pour rate, kickers and external bracing, tie tightness and panel joint tightness to prevent blowout or leakage, at an active foundation site.

Precast/tilt-up casting: side rails and blockouts set on a casting bed in a precast plant or a controlled casting yard; check mold dimensions, squareness, chamfer strips, embed/insert positions, magnet or clamp seating and form cleanliness before concrete is placed, under plant supervision and standard equipment.

sources.system: ZEISS AICell trace with AIMax cloud sensor
sources.title: ZEISS Installs New Shop Floor Measuring Solution for Car Body Inspection
sources.claim: ZEISS AICell trace / AIMax cloud is a deployed robot-mounted inline 3D metrology cell that automatically dimensions critical features (studs, rivets, nuts, hemmed edges) of every fixtured car body on a production line, with smart fixtures identifying the part in the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inline dimensional/presence verification of a large fixtured assembly against CAD. Checking a form presented fixtured in a purpose-built cell is the same operation — panel dimensions, member/tie spacing, presence of clamps and joint gaps — at far coarser tolerance (millimetres) than body-in-white work, so performance carries over.

sources.title: Chinese Baoye Group continues to invest in precast concrete production – Vollert
sources.claim: Vollert SMART SET shuttering and de-shuttering ... position formwork profiles on precast pallets automatically under CAD/CAM control in operating precast plants, so form geometry is machine-set and machine-known in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated setting of formwork in a precast circulation plant. It establishes that formwork can be presented and handled as fixtured work in a purpose-built robotic line, which is the E1 counterfactual for the form-checking instance.

sources.system: Smart Set shuttering robot line, Oschatz precast plant
sources.title: The Oschatz concrete plant banks on robot technology - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: In an operating precast plant, shuttering and insert placement by robots on the pallet line is monitored by laser and camera systems, i.e., machine verification of form/insert placement inside a purpose-built production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine monitoring of shuttering and insert placement. Confirms that in a purpose-built line the correctness of form and blockout placement is checked by laser/camera systems rather than by a human walking the forms.

sources.system: Spot Enterprise with Trimble X7 / FARO scanning payload
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot with laser-scanner payloads conducts programmed Autowalk missions on active construction sites without operator intervention, self-charging at a dock and capturing 3D scans/360 imagery for site documentation; deployed by contractors such as Hensel Phelps and Suffolk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reality-capture on an active jobsite. It shows robots can reach and scan formwork in an unstructured site, but it delivers point clouds and imagery only — no cited system makes the pour-ready determination about bracing, staking, tie tightness or joint tightness.

sources.system: DroneDeploy Concrete Sleeve AI / pre-pour analysis
sources.title: Drone Programs in Construction Update: Who's Doing What? | Commercial UAV News
sources.claim: DroneDeploy's Concrete Sleeve AI pre-pour report analyzes drone orthomosaics against coordinated drawings to flag misplaced, out-of-tolerance or missing sleeves, formwork, edge-of-slab and embed locations before a pour; used by Juneau Construction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-pour location verification of embeds/sleeves and edge-of-slab. It covers only the geometric-location portion of the form check, the flights are pilot-launched, and the deliverable is a report hours later, so it does not complete the instance.

sources.title: Automated Quality Inspection of Formwork Systems Using 3D Point Cloud Data
sources.claim: A 2024 peer-reviewed framework automates measurement of formwork member spacing (studs, wales, shores) from 3D point clouds, but it is an algorithmic pipeline applied to scan data rather than a deployed robotic system that performs the pre-pour check.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dimensional quality inspection of installed formwork. Shows the analysis step is partly automatable, but no robot performs the capture-plus-judgment loop on site, so it cannot substantiate completion at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Set the forms that hold concrete to the desired pitch and depth, and align them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial flatwork on a job site: setting 2x4 or steel edge forms for a driveway, sidewalk or patio - snapping a stringline off the house, driving stakes into varying subgrade, cutting and bending forms to radii, nailing/clipping them to stakes and shooting grade so the slab drains away at the specified pitch and thickness.

Municipal street work: setting curb, gutter and sidewalk forms along an existing roadway - staking to survey hubs and offsets, matching existing gutter flowline and driveway/ADA ramp grades, working around utilities, live traffic, weather and uneven subgrade.

Commercial slab-on-grade, footings and foundation walls on an active construction site: setting perimeter edge forms, keyways, blockouts and screed rails to laser/GPS elevations over vapor barrier and rebar, bracing them to resist the pour, on ground shared with other trades and equipment.

Interior or elevated pours in a building under construction: bulkheads and pour-stop/edge forms for topping slabs, equipment pads, curbs and stair pans in congested spaces - forms cut to fit around columns, penetrations and existing walls, set to marked elevations and slopes to drains.

Precast/prestress plant or shop: setting side rails, bulkheads and blockouts on a casting bed or pallet to the element's dimensions and thickness, squaring and clamping/magnetizing them before reinforcement and pour.

sources.title: GOMACO, Manufacturer of Concrete Slipform Paving Equipment: Press Releases (stringless)

sources.system: In situ Fabricator with Mesh Mould
sources.title: DFAB HOUSE
sources.claim: A mobile on-site robot fabricated a curved steel mesh serving as formwork and reinforcement for a concrete wall at the DFAB HOUSE research build - the only demonstrated on-site robotic formwork production found, and a supervised one-off research wall rather than flatwork forms set to pitch and depth.
sources.transferJustification: On-site robotic formwork creation, but a bespoke research wall with human-supervised operation; does not substantiate worker-quality edge/curb form setting on job sites.

tasks.label: Spread, level, and smooth concrete, using rake, shovel, hand or power trowel, hand or power screed, and float.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large-area interior slab-on-grade pour at a commercial/industrial building site (warehouse, big-box, parking-garage base slab): concrete pumped or chuted in, raked and spread, screeded to grade with laser/roller screed, bull-floated, then power-floated and troweled to a hard, flat finish over thousands of square feet of open floor on an active jobsite.

Residential/light-commercial exterior flatwork at a house or small site: driveway, patio, sidewalk, garage or basement slab. Concrete comes off the truck chute, is spread with rake and shovel, struck off with a hand or roller screed riding the forms, bull-floated, hand-floated and broom-finished; small irregular areas, slopes to drain, weather and site clutter.

Street/highway flatwork in the public right of way: sidewalk panels, ADA ramps, curb and gutter, approach slabs and pavement patches. Concrete placed from a chute or slipform machine, screeded, floated and broomed, worked around utilities, existing pavement and traffic control.

Structural placements on a building site: footings, foundation walls, grade beams, pile caps and equipment pads. Concrete is spread and consolidated inside congested formwork and rebar, then struck off with a screed and floated level at the top surface.

Elevated deck pour in a multi-story building under construction: pumped concrete spread on metal deck or shored formwork, screeded to laser grade, bull-floated and power-troweled; congested with rebar, embeds, edge forms and hose crews, at height.
Precast/prefab plant work: spreading, screeding and floating/troweling concrete in molds and on casting beds to finish panels, slabs and products inside the plant.

tasks.label: Monitor how the wind, heat, or cold affect the curing of the concrete throughout the entire process.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hot, windy day outdoor residential/light-commercial flatwork (driveway, sidewalk, patio, garage slab). Finisher stays on and around the fresh slab for several hours, feeling the wind, watching bleed-water sheen disappear, touching/pressing the surface to gauge set, checking air/surface temperature, and judging whether evaporation is outrunning bleeding so fogging, evaporation retarder, or an earlier finishing pass is needed. Site is a private lot, no controlled premises.

Large commercial slab-on-grade or floor pour inside an unfinished building shell during a full-shift placement: open doorways, temporary heaters and fans create drafts and uneven drying, sections set at different rates. Finisher tracks how conditions vary across the placement, times floating/troweling per section, and calls for door closures, plastic, or cure application. Active construction site, layout changes daily.

Cold-weather placement (near/below freezing): monitoring in-place concrete temperature for the first several days under insulating blankets, heated enclosures, or hydronic heat; checking thermometers/embedded probes, watching for freezing, thermal shock, and slow set; deciding when protection can safely come off before finishing or stripping. Outdoor jobsite.

Public-works pour under DOT/spec requirements (curb and gutter, sidewalk, pavement, bridge deck overlay): measuring air, concrete, and dew-point temperature, wind speed and humidity, computing evaporation rate against the ACI chart, ordering fogging/curing per spec, and documenting conditions throughout placement and cure. Roadway right-of-way with traffic and open weather.

Precast/casting-yard or plant production work: monitoring cure of cast elements or products held on heated beds, under tarps/blankets, or in steam/vapor curing enclosures; tracking element temperature and humidity through the cure cycle and deciding on strip/ship timing. Premises and layout controlled by the plant operator.

sources.system: Kraft AutoCure® (with VaporWare V2 data recording, Match-Cure)
sources.date: 2021-06 (product page last modified); product line in commercial sale for years
sources.title: AutoCure® - KraftCuring
sources.claim: AutoCure is a commercial curing measurement-and-control system that measures concrete and curing-environment temperature and relative humidity and automatically drives the curing regime for precast concrete, i.e. it monitors and manages how heat and humidity affect curing throughout the cycle.

sources.title: Kraft Vapor Curing Technology for Eco Stone Precast Infra. - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: Deployed installation: a precast producer's curing chambers run a fully automated multi-phase curing cycle (preset, controlled ramp ~10 K/hour, soak at up to 50 °C and ~99% RH) managed by AutoCure using temperature and humidity sensors, vapor valves and motorized controls in five independent zones.

sources.system: Vollert/Weckenmann circulation plant curing chamber with temperature controller
sources.title: Vollert|Weckenmann plant ensures high production output and quality
sources.claim: Working precast circulation plants use curing chambers whose heat input is regulated by an automatic temperature controller, holding the elements' curing temperature profile without a worker watching the weather.

sources.system: Low-cost thermal mapping system on a mobile robot (KAIST/Inha)
sources.developer: Alex Junho Lee, Younggun Cho, Hyun Myung (KAIST, Inha University)
