sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses robotic concrete-curing temperature monitoring, the closest robotic analogue to this task; cited to show that on-site robotic cure monitoring exists only as a research demonstration, so it cannot support completion at worker quality at E2/E3.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR (autonomous inspection rounds; construction site documentation missions)
sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Legged robots run autonomous thermal inspection rounds and autonomous scanning missions on construction sites, capturing thermal and 360° data on schedule; no concrete-curing judgement (bleed water, set timing, evaporation-rate response) is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous thermal inspection rounds in industrial/construction settings; cited to show the limit of on-site robotic sensing — periodic thermal capture of assets, with no demonstrated assessment of fresh-concrete set state or weather-driven curing decisions, so transfer to this task is not established.

tasks.label: Mold expansion joints and edges, using edging tools, jointers, and straightedge.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential flatwork: driveway, patio, or walkway at a private home. After screeding and floating, the mason kneels/reaches from the edge, runs a hand edger along every form line to round the perimeter, then cuts control joints with a jointer guided by a straightedge board laid across the wet slab, timing each pass to the concrete's set and re-floating tool marks. Site is a fenced yard with obstacles, slope, weather.

Municipal sidewalk, curb-and-gutter, and ADA ramp work in a street right-of-way: edging along forms and back of curb, tooling transverse contraction joints at spacing, setting/tooling around expansion-joint filler board at driveways and structures, working next to live traffic and utilities.

Commercial/industrial slab-on-grade or interior floor pour (warehouse, big-box, distribution center) on an active construction site: tooling perimeter and construction-joint edges, isolation joints around columns, blockouts and dock pits with edger and straightedge while the main field joints are later saw-cut.

Site-cast structural and architectural elements: steps and stair treads/nosings, equipment pads, retaining-wall caps, curbs, pool decks and ramps. Edging tight around obstructions, forms and inserts, tooled joints in short irregular runs, often on scaffolds, in trenches, or overhead-constrained spaces.

Precast/prestressed plant or shop work: mason finishes exposed faces and edges of elements cast in beds or on pallets indoors — chamfering/rounding edges, tooling formed grooves and joint reglets — in a fixed-layout, institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: Huffcutt precast wall panel plant shuttering robot (carousel line, ebos control)
sources.developer: Huffcutt Concrete / Progress Group-type carousel equipment
sources.title: Brand New Precast Concrete Wall Panel Plant | Huffcutt
sources.claim: US precast plant runs a fully automated shuttering robot that places profiled magnetic side forms on casting pallets from CAD data, molding the element's edge and groove geometry, followed by an automated finishing process, all indoors on a pallet carousel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forming the edge profile, chamfer and joint groove of a concrete element. It transfers because the accepted output of this task is concrete with specified rounded/chamfered edges and grooves at set positions; on a fixtured pallet a purpose-built line produces that geometry without hand tooling, and the page also states the plant's finishing process is automated.

sources.system: Elematic Automatic Shuttering Station E9 / shuttering robot
sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: Commercial shuttering robot for precast wall/slab lines performs the demolding, shuttering and accessory placement of a precast plant automatically, defining element edges and recesses on the casting table.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: molding element edges/joint profiles with machine-placed profiled forms in a fixtured plant line, substituting for hand edging and jointing; same objects (fresh concrete elements), same edge-geometry tolerances, purpose-built environment.

sources.system: Integrated intelligent smoothing/roughening end-effector robot for precast concrete
sources.developer: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology (Gang et al., Sensors 24:3336)
sources.title: A Robotic Solution for Precision Smoothing and Roughening of Precast Concrete Surfaces: Design and Experimental Validation
sources.claim: A robotic end-effector on a manipulator autonomously smooths and roughens precast concrete surfaces in a factory production setting, pressing a trowel-type tool onto the concrete along programmed paths with consistent quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact tooling of a fresh precast concrete surface with a force-controlled trowel end effector. It transfers to edging/jointing because both require pressing a shaped hand-tool along a defined path on plastic concrete, and in a fixtured plant the path geometry is known in advance.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics / Guangdong Bojiatuo basement glazing (troweling) robot and related floor finishing robots
sources.developer: Bright Dream Robotics; Guangdong Bojiatuo Construction Technology
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction: Challenges and Opportunities (Encyclopedia MDPI entry)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art concrete floor finishing/polishing robots follow pre-programmed paths over the field of a slab but cannot work the edge zones, which remain manual; no reviewed system tools perimeter edges or control joints.
sources.transferJustification: Same object and site (fresh slab surface on building floors); establishes that deployed on-site concrete finishing robots explicitly exclude the edge zone that this task is about.

sources.system: Wirtgen SP 33 / SP 15i slipform pavers with AutoPilot 2.0
sources.title: Wirtgen builds slab, barrier, curb versatility into slipform paver model – Concrete Products
sources.claim: Slipform pavers that extrude curb, gutter, barrier and sidewalk profiles — the machine method of molding concrete edges on the job site — use stringless 3D control that assists a human operator rather than running unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: molding concrete edges/profiles in the field. Cited to show the closest on-site edge-molding machinery is operator-run, not autonomous, and does not tool the joints, so it cannot support an E3/E2 positive judgment.

tasks.label: Signal truck driver to position truck to facilitate pouring concrete, and move chute to direct concrete on forms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential flatwork: driveway, sidewalk, patio or garage slab at a private home. The mason hand-signals the ready-mix driver backing the truck across a lawn/apron near forms and utilities, hangs and swings chute extensions, walks the chute along the forms and calls for faster/slower discharge and truck repositioning until the forms are filled.

Commercial/institutional building site: footings, grade beams, foundation walls and pier forms on rough-graded, muddy ground. The mason spots the mixer truck at each pour point (watching for trench edges, rebar cages, overhead lines), adds chute sections, and directs concrete into narrow forms without overfilling or knocking forms out of alignment.

Public right-of-way street work: curb and gutter, sidewalk panels and ADA ramps poured from the truck chute inside a traffic-controlled work zone, with the truck creeping along the curb line while the mason signals the driver and swings the chute over the forms.

Large commercial slab-on-grade or elevated deck where the truck cannot reach the placement point: the mason spots the truck at the discharge station and manages the chute into a pump hopper, buggy or wheelbarrow, coordinating truck movements and discharge rate with the placing crew.

Repair/replacement pour inside an existing controlled facility (warehouse or plant floor section, loading dock, interior slab) during a shutdown: the truck backs to a door or bay, the mason signals the driver in a confined, fixed-layout space and runs the chute through the opening into the formed area.

sources.system: eCon Drive concrete spreader (Ebawe Anlagentechnik / Progress Group)
sources.title: Most automated carousel plant in Ireland takes shape at Kilsaran - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: A fully automatic rail-mounted concrete spreader autonomously fills shuttered molds (forms) with dosed quantities of fresh concrete on a precast pallet-circulation line at Kilsaran Precast, Ireland.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-directed discharge of fresh concrete into formwork. The worker's task is to get concrete from the delivery vehicle into the forms at the right place and rate without spillage or overfill; the spreader travels over the shuttered mold and doses concrete into it under program control, using the same material and the same acceptance criteria (forms filled to depth, minimal waste), in a purpose-built machine line.

sources.system: Elematic Shuttle E9 automated concrete distribution system
sources.title: Concrete transportation for walls | Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Fully automatic rail-borne concrete transport positions and delivers concrete from the batching plant to the casting station in precast plants, replacing a human-directed delivery vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning the concrete supply at the pour point. In the purpose-built setting the automated shuttle replaces the human-signalled ready-mix truck, so the 'signal the driver into position' element of the task is performed by the machine system rather than by a worker guiding a driver.

sources.title: Distributor P7 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: A rail-mounted distributor automatically transfers concrete from the shuttle into the casting machine that fills the forms, with the combined system described as fully automatic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring and directing fresh concrete from a moving supply vessel into the casting equipment that fills the forms — the machine analogue of moving the chute to direct concrete onto forms, same material and same continuous-flow control problem.

sources.system: UltraSpan concrete distributor with ebos software (Progress Group)
sources.title: Concrete distributor - UltraSpan Technologies, Winnipeg, CA
sources.claim: Concrete distributors spread fresh concrete into pallet molds automatically under software control, matching the shapes and thicknesses required.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: directing concrete discharge into forms. The distributor performs the placement decision (where and how much concrete goes into each form) automatically, which is the productive core of the human task of aiming the chute along the forms.

sources.system: Smart Cast automatic concrete spreader (Progress Group), Shanghai Baoye plant
sources.title: Shanghai Baoye relies on advanced precast construction technology from Germany - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: An automatic concrete spreader integrated with plant control software places the specified quantity of concrete at the specified location in a working precast plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a controlled quantity of fresh concrete into a form at a specified location, which is what the mason achieves by signalling the truck and aiming the chute; here the traversing program replaces the human's positioning and flow-rate signalling.

sources.system: Ligchine laser screeds, Brokk demolition robots (jobsite remote-control equipment)
sources.title: Robots in the Mix - Autonomous Remote Tech in Concrete Equipment | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Concrete-jobsite machinery automation is currently wireless remote (operator-in-the-loop) control of screeds, demolition robots and loaders; no autonomous system guides a ready-mix truck or handles the discharge chute on site.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context for the negative judgment at E2/E3: trade coverage of concrete-jobsite robotics as of 2025 describes remote/teleoperated machines, with no autonomous system spotting mixer trucks or manipulating discharge chutes.

tasks.label: Direct the casting of the concrete and supervise laborers who use shovels or special tools to spread it.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial slab pour (garage, basement, patio): the finisher meets the ready-mix truck, tells the driver where to spot the truck and how fast to discharge, and calls out to two or three laborers where to pull, shovel, and rake the mud to grade before screeding.

Sidewalk, curb, gutter, or driveway flatwork: the finisher directs discharge into narrow forms section by section, telling laborers where to move concrete with shovels and come-alongs and when to consolidate, while watching for form blowouts and keeping the pour ahead of set.

Large commercial floor slab placed by boom pump or conveyor: the lead finisher directs the pump operator by radio and hand signals over the placement pattern, and directs a placing crew of laborers with come-alongs, vibrators, and wet screeds to keep the pour to the laser-screed sequence.

Structural pours (walls, columns, footings, bridge decks, elevated decks): the finisher directs lift sequence, drop height, and rate of placement, tells vibrator operators where to consolidate, and coordinates with the pump/bucket operator and inspector during a continuous pour.

Small repair or specialty placement (equipment pads, stair landings, patch pours with a mixer or buggies): the finisher directs one or two helpers wheeling and dumping concrete into place and spreading it, adjusting instructions as the small batch is placed.

tasks.label: Produce rough concrete surface, using broom.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential exterior flatwork: after screeding, bull-floating and edging a driveway, sidewalk, patio or steps at a private home, the mason drags a broom across the plastic slab at the right set window to leave uniform straight striations, then re-tools edges and joints; slab shapes are irregular, obstacles (posts, downspouts, thresholds) intrude, and weather/mix set drives timing.

Commercial/industrial exterior flatwork on a construction site: parking lots, aprons, sidewalks and loading pads broom-finished in large panels behind a laser screed and float crew, sometimes with a ride-on broom-and-cure machine, working from the pour edge, keeping broom lines square to traffic and lapping passes without marring.

Municipal right-of-way work: small sidewalk panels, curb ramps, gutters and driveway aprons broom-finished in a live street environment with traffic control, utility castings, tree roots and varying panel geometry; texture must meet agency slip-resistance specifications.

Roadway/bridge work: applying a broom, burlap-drag or tined rough texture to fresh concrete pavement or a bridge deck behind a slipform paver or deck-finishing machine, coordinated with curing spray over long linear pours in tight set windows.

Interior slabs inside a building under construction that call for a broom or scratch finish for slip resistance (garage ramps, mechanical rooms, dock aprons, wash-down areas), broomed by hand after floating in areas cluttered with formwork, columns, embeds and other trades.

Precast/product plant finishing: applying a broom or raked rough texture to the exposed face of freshly cast precast elements (stair treads, balcony and ceiling slabs, curb and paving units) on casting beds or a pallet circulation line, to a repeatable plant standard.

sources.system: Vollert SMART CAST automatic concrete distributor with built-in roughening device
sources.developer: Vollert Anlagenbau (installed at Gebr. Kaltenbach GmbH & Co. KG)
sources.title: Manufacturers of precast concrete elements increase product quality and system productivity through modernization investments
sources.claim: Vollert's CAD/CAM-controlled SMART CAST concrete distributor on a precast pallet-circulation line at Gebr. Kaltenbach includes a built-in roughening device that automatically drags an even rough texture into the fresh concrete surface of prefabricated ceiling slabs as part of the automated casting cycle (up to 4 slabs per hour).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically roughening the fresh top surface of a cast concrete slab. It is the same physical act as broom finishing - dragging a toothed/bristled head across plastic concrete to leave uniform striations to a specified texture - on the same material and in the same set window, performed automatically on fixtured pallets in a plant line.

sources.system: Smoothing-and-roughening robot with integrated intelligent end-effector (Sensors 24:3336)
sources.developer: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology (Gang, Duan, Wang, Nan, Song)
sources.title: A Robotic Solution for Precision Smoothing and Roughening of Precast Concrete Surfaces: Design and Experimental Validation
sources.claim: A Cartesian-gantry robot with a multi-DOF end-effector designed to fit existing precast (PC) component production lines autonomously smooths and then roughens the fresh surface of precast concrete elements, planning texture paths (including around embedded obstacles) and switching modes without an operator; experimentally validated for smoothing precision and texture variety.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic roughening (raking/brushing) of precast concrete surfaces. Same workpiece (fresh concrete), same tool action (dragging a textured head to leave striations) and same acceptance criterion (uniform texture), performed over a fixtured element on a production line - the E1 form of broom finishing.

sources.title: Concrete Finishing Equipment & Broom Cure Machine | Somero
sources.claim: Somero's Broom + Cure machine mechanizes bull-floating, brooming and curing of jobsite paving slabs with a 14-ft broom/spray-bar/float head on a boom, but it is a ride-on laser-screed-derived machine driven by a human operator; no autonomous navigation or unattended operation is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (machine brooming of jobsite slabs), cited to show that the only commercial jobsite brooming machine is operator-driven; under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive E2/E3 judgment.

sources.system: Smooth G1 concrete floor leveling and troweling robots
sources.title: iF Design - Basement Concrete Troweling and Leveling Robot
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' Smooth G1 system uses a floor leveling robot and a floor troweling robot that navigate and path-plan automatically over fresh in-place slabs on building sites, but the finish produced is a leveled/troweled smooth surface, not a broomed rough texture, and the machines run on top of the slab they finish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous finishing of in-place fresh slabs on construction sites. Transfer to brooming does NOT hold - these machines produce a smooth troweled finish and traverse the slab surface, which would destroy a broom texture; cited to document the limits of jobsite finishing autonomy.

tasks.label: Apply hardening and sealing compounds to cure surface of concrete, and waterproof or restore surface.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Spray-applying membrane-forming curing compound or cure-and-seal onto a freshly placed and finished interior slab-on-grade (warehouse, big-box, manufacturing floor) on an active construction site, immediately behind the trowel/broom crew: uniform coverage at a specified rate, working around columns, embeds, joints and edges, without marring the green surface, and finishing before the surface dries out.

Curing and later sealing outdoor residential/small-commercial flatwork — driveways, sidewalks, patios, steps, curb-and-gutter — sprayed or rolled from the perimeter and along edges, on cluttered, uneven, sloped sites with landscaping, vehicles and weather (wind, sun, threat of rain) to work around; includes masking and cleanup at adjacent surfaces.

Highway, street and bridge work: applying curing compound to fresh pavement, curb and gutter, and applying penetrating deck sealers/silanes to hardened bridge decks and approach slabs inside a live traffic work zone, with paving trains, hauling traffic, and short weather windows.

Inside an enclosed, owner-controlled facility (existing warehouse, distribution center, retail store, parking structure, plant): grinding/polishing an existing concrete floor and spray-applying densifier/hardener and a guard sealer over large open bays, with racking, columns and wall edges to detail, floor swept and area cordoned off by the facility.

Waterproofing: spray- or roll-applying membranes, crystalline slurries, or elastomeric coatings to concrete foundation walls, below-grade walls, plaza and parking decks, and tank/pit interiors — congested with penetrations, corners, cove details and trench access on an active construction or renovation site.

Restoring deteriorated concrete: grinding/shot-blasting the surface, patching spalls and voids, applying a polymer-modified resurfacer or overlay, and sealing — on existing sidewalks, steps, loading docks and garage decks, each site laid out differently and taken as found.

sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 is a retrofit autonomy kit that lets a concrete floor polishing machine self-navigate and grind/polish large warehouse floors without an operator riding it, using 360-degree LiDAR.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical polishing/grinding of concrete floors. It is the 'restore surface' half of this task, and it demonstrates autonomous, full-coverage traversal of large concrete floors in an enclosed facility — the same coverage motion needed to spread hardener or sealer over the same floors.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 robot autonomously sprays plaster and paint and finishes drywall on real construction sites, navigating by onboard 3D scanning with no site preparation, and has covered over a million square feet of work in Europe before its US launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray application and finishing of a wet coating (plaster, paint) on building surfaces. It shows a mobile robot metering and spraying a liquid/paste coating to uniform coverage, the same act as applying sealing or hardening compound — but on interior vertical surfaces, not fresh horizontal slabs or exterior flatwork.

sources.system: Floor paint coating robot (ProBuild Robotics flooring robot line)
sources.developer: ProBuild Robotics (distributor of Chinese construction robots)
sources.title: Intelligent Flooring Robots: Automated Construction Operations – ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: A floor paint coating robot marketed for underground parking lots, labs and clean workshops performs epoxy floor coating with automatic navigation, feeding and mixing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying epoxy floor coating to a cured concrete floor. Same substrate, same act (spreading a liquid coating to specified thickness over a large indoor floor) as applying hardener/sealer; vendor documentation only, no independent deployment record.

sources.title: Dafang AI: Intelligent Construction Leading The Future (Medium)
sources.claim: Dafang AI's DMB01 floor coating robot is described by its developer as automatically applying epoxy floor primer, intermediate and top coats according to the coating and job requirements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-coat liquid application to indoor concrete floors — the same physical act and substrate as applying hardening/sealing compounds; corroborates that indoor floor-coating robots are a real product category.

sources.title: Robotic Sealing Applications — Encore Automation
sources.claim: Industrial robot cells routinely apply sealing and protective coating materials to workpieces held in fixtures on a conveyor line, with on-arm vision correcting for part position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of sealer and protective coatings to fixtured workpieces inside a fenced cell. The physical act — metering and spraying a sealing compound to a specified film over a presented surface — is the same as applying curing/sealing compound to a concrete element brought to the machine; concrete adds no manipulation difficulty, only a different substrate.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics construction robot fleet (indoor spraying, floor grinding, concrete finishing)
sources.title: Building the Future: How Bright Dream Robotics is Transforming Construction Sites with Robot Workers
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics fields a commercialized fleet including wall-spraying, floor-grinding and concrete-smoothing machines used on more than 900 Chinese construction projects, including interior spray coating of walls and ceilings at a Hong Kong public housing site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine spray-coating of building surfaces and machine floor grinding/finishing on construction sites. The report does not establish whether these units run autonomously or under operator control, so it is treated as teleoperated and used only as context.

sources.title: TinyMobileRobots launches robot TinySurveyor — Global Highways
sources.claim: TinyMobileRobots' TinySurveyor is a GNSS-guided robot that drives outdoor pavement and terrain and sprays pre-marking paint, needing only one person supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor spraying of a liquid coating onto pavement. It shows navigation and spray control on roads, but it lays down thin marking lines rather than a uniform full-coverage curing or sealing film, so it does not by itself substantiate completion of the curing/sealing instances.

tasks.label: Operate power vibrator to compact concrete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large building floor slabs and elevated decks (warehouse, industrial, institutional, parking decks): as the pump/truck places concrete, the finisher runs a vibrating truss or laser-screed vibrating head across the pour and works a poker vibrator at edges, columns, embeds and thickened sections; active building site, sequencing with placement, weather and traffic of other trades.

Light flatwork on private and municipal jobs: driveways, sidewalks, patios, small pads, hand-formed curb and gutter. Short pours, hand-guided vibrating screed and brief poker use at edges, headers and thickened sections; hand-set forms, tight access around houses/streets, varied grades and shapes.

Heavy civil flatwork: highway pavement, bridge decks, airport aprons, tunnel inverts, barrier and parapet. Gang or paver-mounted vibrators, deck finishing screeds with vibrating pans, plus hand pokers along headers, edges and around deck reinforcement; live work zones, exposed weather, tight pour windows.

Formed vertical elements on building and civil jobs: walls, footings, columns, retaining walls, pier caps. Immersion (poker) vibrator inserted in lifts through congested rebar and ties, withdrawn slowly, judged by feel, sound and surface mortar; must avoid form damage, rebar contact and segregation.

Plant and casting-yard production: precast/concrete-products shop where the worker fills fixed forms on a repeated cycle and consolidates with form vibrators, a vibrating table or a poker; standard products, fixed stations, indoor controlled conditions.

sources.system: dBright Dream Robotics (博智林) concrete-floor screeding robot (地面整平机器人)
sources.title: Q/BZL P0008—2021 广东博智林机器人有限公司企业标准 地面整平机器人 Concrete-floor screeding robot
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' concrete-floor screeding robot is defined by the developer's product standard as a robot with a high-precision laser measurement system, real-time control of actuator height and high-frequency vibrating motors that carries out fast, high-precision screeding of concrete floors on command.
sources.transferJustification: A vibrating screed head is the power vibrator used to consolidate slab concrete; the robot's high-frequency vibrating motors perform the same consolidation of fresh slab concrete that the mason's vibrating screed performs.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics concrete-floor screeding robot
sources.title: 全自动“摆平”混凝土！“佛山造”建筑机器人首单完工 (南方plus)
sources.claim: The same screeding robot autonomously completed the basement floor slab of Building 8 at the Fengtong Garden project in Shunde, planning its own screeding path with GNSS navigation and working unmanned to within 5 mm accuracy — a real building construction site.
sources.transferJustification: Consolidating and screeding a fresh slab with a vibrating head is the slab form of the vibrator task; the robot did it on the same kind of reinforced slab pour a cement mason handles.

sources.developer: China Railway (CREC Investment / China TIESIJU Civil Engineering Group)

sources.claim: A slab concrete vibrating robot developed by CREC units has been put into use on Qingdao Metro Line 5, walking, turning and vibrating automatically with set vibration time, depth, frequency and amplitude, run by one remote supervisor; inverted-arch concrete passed the client's Class A inspection standard.

sources.system: 4th-generation intelligent side-wall concrete vibrating robot (智能振捣机器人)
sources.developer: China Railway Fifth Bureau / Qingdao Metro (equipment supplier partnership)
sources.title: 青岛地铁9号线迎来新“工友” 智能振捣机器人助力“智能建造”
sources.claim: A 4th-generation intelligent side-wall vibrating robot was put to work on the Changcheng Road station of Qingdao Metro Line 9: parameters (vibration time, spacing, insertion points, layer thickness) are set before the pour and the machine then vibrates the side-wall concrete automatically, with infrared laser scanning adjusting insertion depth to the rising concrete level; the crew fell from 8 to 3.

sources.system: Intelligent side-wall concrete vibrating robot (侧墙振捣机器人)
sources.developer: PowerChina project department with equipment maker
sources.title: 加速“智造”，智能振捣机器人“上岗”！ (中国电建)
sources.claim: A comparable intelligent side-wall vibrating robot was introduced on the side-wall pours of Shenzhen Metro Line 15 work area 10, controlling side-wall concrete vibration precisely through an automated control system after points and frequency are set.

sources.system: Columbia CPM+60 concrete products machine with Columbia Vibration Technology (CVT)
sources.title: Columbia Partnership — Stowell Concrete
sources.claim: Columbia Machine concrete-products machines vibro-compact concrete in steel moulds on production pallets automatically inside a plant; a CPM+60 machine is the core of Stowell Concrete's plant, its Columbia Vibration Technology providing controlled mould vibration for uniform compaction.
sources.transferJustification: Machine vibration of concrete held in a fixed mould is the fixtured form of the vibrator task: the same consolidation of fresh concrete, with the work brought to the machine.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION

Highway or airport paving: dowel bars at transverse joints and tie bars at longitudinal joints installed into the fresh slipformed slab at programmed spacing, depth and alignment, with the slab surface repaired/refinished behind the insertion. Closed paving work zone on a prepared, stringline- or GPS-referenced base.

Residential decorative work: stamping a freshly poured patio, driveway, walkway or pool deck with mats/texture skins to a brick, ashlar-slate or stone pattern - applying color release, placing and tamping mats in sequence and register, hand-detailing joints, edges and against walls, all timed to the set of the concrete in ambient conditions.

Commercial / municipal decorative work: stamped or patterned crosswalks, plaza paving, storefront entrances and hardscape bands, often larger areas with integral color, saw-cut/stamped grid patterns and texture skins, done under traffic control or around an occupied building.

tasks.label: Wet surface to prepare for bonding, fill holes and cracks with grout or slurry, and smooth, using trowel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior cast-in-place concrete walls in a multi-story building under construction: after formwork is stripped, the mason wets and plugs hundreds of uniform form-tie / screw holes per floor with cement grout or patching mortar and strikes each flush with a small trowel; work moves floor to floor amid other trades.

Vertical cast-in-place concrete at a building or bridge site: irregular defects — honeycomb/rock pockets, spalled corners, tie-cone recesses, bugholes on exposed architectural walls — are dampened, packed with grout or slurry, and rubbed/troweled to blend with the surrounding surface (sack-rub finish).

Outdoor flatwork repair: sidewalks, curbs, driveways, slab edges and steps. The mason hoses down the prepared area, mixes and places patch grout or slurry into spalls, chips, and cracks, then trowels and re-textures (broom/edge finish) to match adjacent concrete, working in sun, wind, or cold with the public and traffic nearby.

Interior floor slab in a building under construction or being renovated: filling voids, honeycomb, crane/core holes, blockout edges and shrinkage cracks in the slab with grout or cement slurry, then troweling smooth and flush so the slab can take flooring or a coating; dusty, cluttered, changing layout.

Existing owner-controlled facility (distribution warehouse, manufacturing plant, parking structure): during a shutdown window the mason cleans and dampens joint-edge spalls and cracks in the floor slab, fills them with grout or semi-rigid filler, and trowels/shaves them flush to the traffic surface; fixed layout, facility staff control access.

Precast/prestressed concrete plant: after panels are stripped, patch lift-insert holes, tie holes, bugholes and chipped edges — dampen, pack patch mortar, trowel flush and match the panel face — with panels lying on beds or set in racks inside the plant.

Interior floors of a commercial or multifamily building: mixing cementitious self-leveling underlayment, floor topping/overlay, or repair mortar for a large interior area, using barrel/paddle mixers or a mixing-pump/pump-truck setup, inside a building under builder control with fixed layout and utilities.

Formed exterior and structural elements: curb and gutter, retaining and foundation walls, bridge/parking-structure elements — chipping off form fins, grout runs and snap-tie protrusions and grinding rough projections after stripping, in street work zones or on open sites, often at height or on uneven ground.

In-service facility floors: renovation, restoration and coating-prep grinding of high spots, ridges and lippage on existing concrete floors in occupied or completed warehouses, plants, garages and retail buildings, scheduled around operations with the area cordoned off.
