tasks.label: Cut out damaged areas, drill holes for reinforcing rods, and position reinforcing rods to repair concrete, using power saw and drill.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-depth repair / slab replacement on a jointed concrete highway or city street: mason lays out the patch limits over a spalled or faulted joint, makes perimeter saw cuts with a walk-behind diamond saw, the damaged slab is broken out, then he drills dowel holes into the exposed vertical faces of the adjacent sound slabs with a gang/hand rotary drill, blows them clean, epoxies and positions the dowel bars. Live traffic beyond cones, weather and subgrade conditions as found, tight lane-closure window.

Sidewalk, curb, gutter, driveway or ADA ramp repair: cut out a cracked/heaved panel or spalled curb section with a handheld or walk-behind saw, break and haul out the debris, drill holes into the abutting existing concrete for tie/dowel bars, epoxy and set the rods, position mesh or #4 bars before repour. Residential and downtown right-of-way, utilities and tree roots underneath, uneven access.

Bridge deck or approach-slab patching: delaminated areas located by sounding, perimeter saw-cut to a square outline, concrete removed around existing top mat, holes drilled into sound concrete for supplemental dowels/anchors, replacement reinforcing bars positioned and tied to exposed steel. Work-zone on an in-service structure, overhead and edge exposure, variable depth of deterioration.

Interior floor slab repair in an operating warehouse, distribution center or manufacturing plant: saw-cut out a spalled joint or damaged slab section during a shutdown window, drill dowel holes into the adjacent slab edges, epoxy and position dowels/rebar for the patch. Fixed layout, institution controls access, racking and equipment nearby, dust control required.

Structural concrete repair of walls, columns, beams or parking-garage decks: chip and saw out concrete around corroded reinforcement, drill into sound concrete for supplemental dowels or splice bars, position replacement reinforcing rods before forming and patching. Vertical and overhead work off scaffolds or lifts inside a facility the owner controls.

Repair of precast or cast concrete elements in a plant, shop or yard: a damaged or mis-cast panel, curb, barrier or beam on stands is saw-cut to remove the defective area, holes are drilled for reinforcing rods, and rods are positioned before the section is recast. Piece is handled by crane, work benched at a fixed station.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler — The Construction Index
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E is a commercially deployed robotic system that autonomously measures positions, drills holes in concrete shaft walls and installs steel anchor bolts, with an operator on site only for quality control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling anchor holes into hardened concrete and setting steel rods in them. Same workpiece material, same hole diameters/depths and mm-level positional tolerance as drilling for reinforcing dowels, and the robot both drills and inserts the rod, i.e. the second and third steps of this task.

sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators — Schindler Global Large Projects
sources.claim: Schindler states the robot works fully autonomously once installed in the shaft, completing a floor's drilling and anchor setting; it has been in commercial customer projects since 2020.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (drill concrete, set steel rod); this item establishes the autonomy level rather than the operation.

sources.title: Precast concrete saw E9 — Elematic
sources.claim: The Elematic Saw E9 is a commercial machine that automatically saws hardened pre-stressed concrete slabs to programmed geometry on a production bed, taking cut data from the plant planning system and locating itself by laser.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diamond sawing hardened, reinforced concrete to a defined outline. Same material and blade technology as cutting out a damaged patch; in a purpose-built line the slab is fixtured on the bed and the cut lines are given, which is the E1 form of the 'cut out damaged areas' step.

sources.title: Cost-efficient and flexible hollow core saws — Elematic Concrete Issues
sources.claim: Elematic describes the Saw E9's operation as loading planned cut data and starting the machine, which then executes the cuts using laser positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the concrete sawing step runs without step-by-step operator control once the workpiece is presented on the bed.

sources.title: Meet the Jaibot drilling robot, a potential solution to the construction worker shortage — Denver7
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercialized semi-autonomous construction robot that follows a digital plan to mark and drill anchor holes in concrete on building jobsites, working through its mission on its own after being positioned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out and drilling holes in concrete on real jobsites. Shows only the drilling sub-step transfers to field settings; the robot does not cut out damaged concrete or place reinforcing rods.

sources.system: Conjet hydrodemolition robots / Aquajet Aqua Cutter
sources.title: Automated Concrete Removal and Demolition — Conjet
sources.claim: Hydrodemolition robots are used commercially to remove deteriorated concrete from bridge decks and parking decks, but the operator sets the cutting parameters, positions the machine and starts each pass.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing damaged concrete in situ. Cited only as context for the removal step; because the machine is set up and steered pass-by-pass by an operator its autonomy is unclear, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: ACR reveals IronBot, a rebar-placing robot, at ConExpo — Equipment World
sources.claim: Advanced Construction Robotics' TyBot autonomously ties rebar intersections and IronBot lifts and places rebar bundles on bridge decks; on one bridge project IronBot placed 147,032 ... shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling and placing reinforcing bars in the field. Covers only the 'position reinforcing rods' step on open new-construction decks, not cutting out damage or drilling dowel holes into existing concrete.

tasks.label: Wet concrete surface, and rub with stone to smooth surface and obtain specified finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cast-in-place structural concrete inside a building under construction: after forms are stripped from walls, columns, stair/elevator cores or parking-garage walls and soffits, the mason hoses the surface down and rubs it with a carborundum stone to knock off fins, form-panel marks and joint offsets and produce a uniform smooth finish. Indoor, floor level to roughly ceiling height, dusty active site with other trades working.

Heavy-civil / outdoor formed surfaces: bridge parapets, abutments, pier columns, wingwalls, retaining walls and culverts requiring a DOT-specified rubbed finish. Surface is wetted and rubbed with a carborundum stone, sometimes with a grout/sack rub, working outdoors from the ground, ladders, scaffold or a manlift over uneven terrain and in variable weather.

Small localized patch-and-blend rubbing on residential or light-commercial jobs: tie holes, honeycomb, bug holes, chipped step nosings, curb and gutter faces and foundation-wall patches are wetted and stone-rubbed over areas of a few square feet, at odd angles and on varied geometry, to match surrounding texture.

Precast / architectural concrete plant or casting yard: stripped panels, stair units, copings, cast-stone units and custom members are wetted and rubbed or ground to the specified exposed-concrete finish while resting on stands, tables or tilt-tables in the finishing bay.

Flatwork: wet rubbing/stoning hardened slab surfaces — garage and warehouse slabs, sidewalk panels, slab edges and exposed floor areas — to remove trowel marks and blemishes and bring the surface to the specified smoothness before coating or exposure.

sources.system: Scan + Grind system (ABB robot + FerRobotics AAK 617 Concrete + accell integration) at STS Fertigteile
sources.title: Fully automatic robotic grinding process for precast concrete elements relieves workers | CPi worldwide
sources.claim: A fully automated ABB robot cell with the FerRobotics AAK 617 Concrete force-controlled end-effector grinds the exposed surfaces of precast concrete elements (stairs, balconies, custom members) to a specified look or slip-resistance class in a precast plant, replacing manual finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive grinding rather than wet stone rubbing, but the object (hardened concrete surface), the goal (smooth the formed surface to a specified finish/texture class) and the required force and path control are the same; the cell replaces the hand finishers who previously did this work.

sources.system: Automated scanning grinding of precast concrete (AAK 617 Concrete end effector)
sources.title: Automated scanning grinding precast concrete Active Angular Kit end effector AAK 601 Concrete - FerRobotics
sources.claim: The same system scans the concrete element and drives the grinding tool along predefined paths with regulated constant contact force to reach the desired grinding pattern or ....
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: force-controlled abrasive finishing of hardened concrete surfaces to a specified surface quality, which is the output the rubbing task must deliver.

sources.system: Concrete Interior Wall Polishing Robot / Concrete Ceiling Polishing Robot
sources.title: Construction Industry Council kicks off robot workshops to herald the robotics revolution in construction | The Standard
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' Concrete Interior Wall Polishing Robot ... finish cast-in-place concrete walls and ceilings on building sites by autonomous polishing with dust extraction, guided by 3D models from a surveying robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dry abrasive polishing of stripped cast-in-place concrete walls/ceilings instead of wet stone rubbing, but it is the same operation on the same surfaces — removing form marks and protrusions from formed concrete to reach a specified smooth finish.

sources.system: Concrete ceiling polishing robot and concrete interior wall polishing robot (Bozhilin fleet)
sources.title: Guangdong Bozhilin Robot Co., Ltd. ... Application of construction robots in Fengtong Garden Project (transl. of Architecture, Issue 8, 2022) | DayDayNews
sources.claim: On the Fengtong Garden project in Foshan, Bright Dream Robotics' concrete-finishing robots worked at production scale on an active building site: the ceiling polishing robot finished about 110,971 m2 and the interior wall polishing robot about 42,477 m2, with one operator supervising up to three machines.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the previous item; this source establishes that the autonomous concrete surface-polishing robots ran at commercial scale on a live, unstructured building site rather than only in demonstrations.

sources.title: Autonomous Concrete Floor Polishing & LightWare's SF40/C LiDAR | Unmanned Systems Technology
sources.claim: The ACP-100 is a retrofit autonomy kit that lets a standard concrete floor polishing machine self-navigate and run a floor polishing job inside buildings before fit-out, freeing crews for hand grinding and edge work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine grinding/polishing of a hardened slab rather than hand stoning, but it produces the same output the flatwork instance requires — a slab surface abraded to the specified smoothness — over the same surfaces and site conditions.

sources.system: Basement glazing robot and floor grinding robot
sources.developer: Guangdong Bojiatuo Construction Technology (Bright Dream Robotics group)
sources.title: Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction | Encyclopedia MDPI (from Drones 6(12):424)
sources.claim: A concrete floor glazing/polishing robot performs autonomous surface treatment of concrete floors using motion-control and integrated navigation, though wall edges still require manual finishing; a related floor grinding robot carries a water tank and needs one attending operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wet polishing/glazing of concrete floors with rotating abrasive tooling, the machine equivalent of stoning a slab; same material and same specified-smoothness output, and the source is explicit about autonomy and its edge-work limitation.

sources.title: A Robotic Solution for Precision Smoothing and Roughening of Precast Concrete Surfaces: Design and Experimental Validation
sources.claim: A robotic system with a multi-DOF intelligent end-effector for smoothing (and ...) was designed and experimentally validated for factory precast production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic smoothing of concrete surfaces in a fixtured factory setting; supports that the surface-smoothing step itself is within reach of a purpose-built cell, corroborating the deployed FerRobotics/ABB evidence.

tasks.label: Clean chipped area, using wire brush, and feel and observe surface to determine if it is rough or uneven.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sidewalk, curb, gutter or driveway-apron repair in the public right-of-way: after chipping out a spalled or broken area, the mason wire-brushes the chipped pocket and its edges to remove loose crumbs, dust and laitance, then runs a hand over it and eyes it to decide whether it is uniformly rough and sound enough to bond a patch or needs more chipping. Outdoors, weather, pedestrian and vehicle traffic, kneeling at grade.

Residential / light-commercial repair: chipped basement or garage slab, patio, steps, porch nosing, or foundation wall in an occupied home. Cluttered, varied access (tight corners, stair nosings, vertical faces); the mason brushes the chipped area clean and feels and sights it for roughness or unevenness before patching.

Commercial or institutional building under construction: after form stripping, honeycomb, voids and chipped edges on walls, columns, beams and slabs are chipped back, wire-brushed clean of dust and loose material, then felt and visually checked for roughness/unevenness before grout patching. Active jobsite with changing layout, debris and other trades.

Infrastructure repair in a traffic-controlled work zone: bridge deck, parapet, barrier wall, parking-structure deck or column spall. The chipped or saw-cut area (often vertical or overhead, with exposed rebar) is wire-brushed clean and then felt and observed to judge whether the substrate is uniformly rough and sound for repair mortar.

Industrial plant or warehouse floor repair during a scheduled shutdown: chipped joint edges, spalled slab areas and dock aprons inside a facility with fixed layout and controlled access; the area is brushed clean and inspected by hand and eye for roughness/unevenness before patch material is placed.

Precast concrete plant or casting yard: chips, blowholes and broken edges on precast panels, stairs or curbs are cleaned with a wire brush at a repair station and the surface felt and observed for roughness/unevenness before rubbing or patching. Indoor plant, standard stations, elements moved by crane or forklift.

sources.system: FerRobotics AAK 617/601 Concrete + ABB robot cell (accell integration) at STS Fertigteile
sources.date: 2024-12 (case study page; system in production earlier)
sources.title: Automated scanning grinding precast concrete Active Angular Kit end effector AAK 601 Concrete - FerRobotics
sources.claim: Fully automatic robotic cell at precast maker STS Fertigteile scans a concrete element placed on a traversing table and then grinds its surfaces with a force-controlled angle-grinder end effector (AAK 617 Concrete), reaching right into edges and corners, to a specified surface / anti-slip class.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive surface treatment of hardened concrete. Same material and comparable precision (surface texture/anti-slip class, edges and corners), with the 3D scan of the component substituting for the mason's look-and-feel judgment of surface condition, on a fixtured workpiece.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System (FANUC six-axis robots)
sources.title: 3M and GM Partner on First-Ever Robotic Paint Repair System on Moving Assembly Line
sources.claim: A vision system autonomously finds and categorizes localized surface defects on a large workpiece, plans the repair, and robots sand and polish only the defect area, on a moving assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: localized defect find-clean-verify. It demonstrates the perception half of this task - autonomously locating a blemished patch on a large surface, treating only that patch with abrasives, and checking the result - which is what 'clean the chipped area and observe whether it is rough or uneven' requires.

sources.title: Finessing Features: 3M and GM partner on robotic paint repair system for moving vehicle assembly line
sources.claim: The defect-detection-and-abrasive-repair system is installed and running in a GM production plant, establishing deployed production capability rather than a demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the previous item (localized abrasive defect repair with automated inspection); this item establishes deployment maturity inside a fenced industrial cell/line.

sources.system: FANUC force-sensor material removal robots (deburring, grinding, polishing)
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercial force-controlled material-removal robots keep an abrasive or brush tool pressed to a part at constant force while compensating for dimensional deviations, i.e. adapting to an irregular, non-nominal as-found surface inside an industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled abrasive/brush contact work on parts whose geometry varies. Wire-brushing a chipped pocket requires exactly this - maintaining brush pressure on an irregular surface - and the tolerance demanded for patch preparation is far looser than deburring tolerances.

sources.system: FerRobotics ASK Brush / Active Compliant Technology end effectors
sources.title: Grinding, sanding, polishing, deburring - FerRobotics
sources.claim: Brush end effectors with servo-controlled contact force and integrated dust extraction are offered as standard robotic tooling for grinding, sanding, polishing and deburring, so a powered brush tool is available to an industrial robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic brushing. Supplies the specific tool (powered brush under active contact-force control with extraction) that an E1 concrete grinding/defect-repair cell would carry to wire-brush a chipped area.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile plastering/painting/drywall-sanding robots with onboard 3D scanning operate on active construction sites and have covered over a million square feet, but their work is planned coverage sanding of planar plaster/gypsum finishes, not locating and brushing out individual chipped concrete pockets or judging their roughness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite surface finishing/sanding. Cited to bound the E3 judgment - it shows jobsite mobility and scan-driven sanding of soft planar wall finishes, not defect-targeted abrasive cleaning of hardened concrete spalls with a roughness/soundness verdict.

tasks.label: Build wooden molds, and clamp molds around area to be repaired, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sidewalk, curb-and-gutter or driveway-apron repair in a public right-of-way: mason measures the broken-out section, cuts 2x4/2x6 lumber and plywood on site with a circular saw, assembles a form to match the existing grade and radius, sets it against the sound concrete, stakes/braces it and screws or clamps it to the adjoining slabs. Traffic, utilities, tree roots and irregular break lines vary at every location.

Vertical or overhead structural patch on a parking garage column, bridge pier/beam or building wall: after chipping out spalled concrete, the mason builds a plywood-and-lumber form box (often with a chimney/head box), fits it to the irregular sound-concrete perimeter, and clamps it tight with through-bolts, she-bolts, wedges or strongbacks while working off scaffold or a lift.

Interior slab, stair-tread or loading-dock patch inside an occupied facility (warehouse, school, hospital, manufacturing plant): mason builds a wooden edge mold/dam around the saw-cut patch area and clamps or anchors it to the slab, working around racking, traffic lanes and facility rules.

Defect repair on an active new-construction jobsite: honeycombed or blown-out wall/curb-return sections are formed with wooden dams cut from scrap lumber and clamped/wedged against the green concrete, amid stacked material, mud, rebar and other trades.

Small residential/light-commercial repairs: porch steps, step nosings, garage-floor edges, stoops. Mason builds a small wooden mold, shims it to the existing profile and clamps or braces it against the damaged element in a private yard or garage.

Shop or plant work: in a precast yard, cast-stone shop or contractor's yard, a portable element (precast panel corner, cast-stone piece, damaged step) is set on a bench or pallet and a wooden mold box is built and clamped around the damaged area for recasting.

sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic's E9 automatic shuttering station is a commercially sold shuttering robot that performs demolding, shuttering and accessory placement on flat steel pallets in a precast wall plant, driven by CAD data with standardized magnetic steel shuttering profiles. It does not fabricate wooden molds from lumber and does not clamp molds against an irregular damaged area of existing concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is formwork/mold setting and clamping. Transfer fails for this task: the robot places standardized steel profiles held by magnets on a flat machine pallet for casting new elements, whereas the task requires cutting and assembling wooden molds and clamping them tight against the irregular perimeter of a chipped-out repair area on existing concrete.

sources.system: CREATE (Concrete Robotics Engineering in Automation Technology)
sources.developer: Ruhr University Bochum, Institute of Concrete Structures
sources.title: Robots Produce Precise, Durable Concrete Components in Three Hours | Newsportal - Ruhr-Universitat Bochum
sources.claim: The CREATE research facility at Ruhr University Bochum uses three industrial robots inside a purpose-built test hall to assemble formwork, place reinforcement, pour and rapidly cure modular concrete components. The article contrasts this with conventional practice, where formwork is built by workers out of wood on site. The system produces new standardized modules; it does not build molds around damaged existing structures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic formwork assembly. It substantiates only that formwork for new, digitally specified modules can be assembled robotically inside a purpose-built cell; it gives no evidence of fabricating a wooden mold fitted and clamped to the irregular boundary of a concrete repair.

sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are commercial CNC gantry machines in timber-prefabrication plants that saw, trim, drill, screw, staple and nail wooden members and sheathing on fixtured element tables from CAD data. They fabricate flat rectilinear wooden assemblies in a jig; they cannot measure a damaged concrete area, fit a mold to it, or clamp a mold onto a workpiece.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated wooden assembly (cutting and fastening lumber). It covers only the 'build a wooden mold' half of the task, in a fixtured factory jig with pre-defined panel geometry, and provides no capability for setting and clamping that mold around a repair area.

sources.system: Mobile 3D-printing repair robot (Dielemans workflow, reviewed in Cement and Concrete Research)
sources.developer: TU Munich / academic review in Cement and Concrete Research
sources.title: Advancing construction in existing contexts: Prospects and barriers of 3d printing with mobile robots for building maintenance and repair - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: State-of-the-art in-situ robotic repair of damaged building components uses mobile robots that scan the damage and additively deposit material; the reviewed work involves no formwork carpentry and remains at research-demonstration stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic in-situ repair of damaged building elements. It shows scanning-plus-deposition demonstrations only; no cited in-situ system builds or clamps molds, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task in the field.

sources.title: How robots are revolutionising formwork assembly - Doka
sources.claim: On-site formwork automation offered by a leading formwork maker is limited to powered handling of standardized modular climbing panels with worker involvement, not to fabricating or clamping molds for repairs; it remains at prototype stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is jobsite formwork handling. It shows only assisted movement of proprietary modular panels, so it cannot substantiate building wooden molds or clamping them around a repair area.

tasks.label: Sprinkle colored marble or stone chips, powdered steel, or coloring powder over surface to produce prescribed finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial/warehouse slab pour inside a building under construction: after screeding and bull-floating, broadcast metallic or mineral dry-shake hardener (often pigmented) over thousands of square feet of freshly floated concrete, in two passes, at a specified coverage rate (e.g. 1-3 lb/sf), timed to the bleed-water window; mechanical ride-on spreader for the field, hand-cast at edges and columns.

Residential or light-commercial decorative flatwork outdoors (driveway, patio, pool deck, walkway): hand-broadcast dry-shake color hardener in an arcing motion over the fresh slab, work it in with a float, and later cast powdered antiquing release over the surface before stamping; site-specific layout, obstacles, sun/wind/temperature affect the set window.

Seeded exposed-aggregate work outdoors (plaza, entry walk, feature slab): sprinkle colored marble or stone chips uniformly over the surface of the fresh placement, embed them with a float or roller, and later expose them; chip size/color and coverage set by the specification and a job-site mock-up.

Interior decorative topping or terrazzo-style finish placed inside an existing, operating institutional or commercial building (school, hospital, retail) during a renovation or off-hours shutdown: sprinkle marble chips or coloring powder over the topping and work it in; protected indoor conditions, controlled access, but hand-carried materials and site-specific room layouts.

Precast/architectural concrete plant or a countertop/step shop: broadcast stone chips, color hardener, or coloring powder over wet-cast panels, steps or slabs on casting beds/molds, then float or trowel in, under shop lighting with standardized molds and material staging.

sources.system: Masa L 9.1 / XL 9.1 block making machine (face mix filling unit)
sources.title: Concrete block production machine - L 9.1 and XL | Masa Group
sources.claim: Masa L 9.1 / XL 9.1 concrete block making machines are fully automatic plant machines that deposit a second, differently colored facing layer (face mix) over the surface of freshly formed concrete units in the mould to produce the prescribed finished surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a pigmented/decorative facing material over the top surface of fresh concrete to produce a specified colored finish. Same material class (pigmented cementitious/aggregate topping), same objective (prescribed surface finish), executed under machine control with the workpiece fixtured in a mould on a purpose-built line, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual for the mason's dry-shake/chip broadcast step.

sources.system: Hydraulic terrazzo tile making machine / production line
sources.developer: Zest (tile machine manufacturer); comparable lines from Qunfeng Group
sources.title: Good Quality Terrazzo Tile Making Machine Factory In China
sources.claim: Terrazzo tile production machines automatically mix marble/stone chip aggregate with cement and pigment and feed the chip-bearing face material into the moulds of a hydraulic press, producing tiles of prescribed color and chip finish without a worker distributing the chips.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: distributing colored marble/stone chips over the face of a cementitious product to a prescribed decorative finish. Objects (marble chips, pigment, cement) and required outcome (uniform, spec-matching chip finish) are the same as the mason's seeding/sprinkling step; only the presentation differs, which is what the E1 counterfactual assumes.

sources.system: Roofing-line granule applicator (hopper dispenser plus slate drum)
sources.developer: Owens-Corning Fiberglas (patented apparatus; industry-standard shingle line equipment)
sources.date: Patent 4,478,869 (1984); practice standard in current shingle plants
sources.title: Applying granules to strip asphaltic material (US Patent 4,478,869)
sources.claim: Roofing plants apply colored mineral granules to a moving coated sheet by dispensing them from hoppers at a controlled rate, embedding them to produce the prescribed colored surface finish, i.e. machine broadcast of granular material over a fresh tacky surface on a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: broadcasting colored mineral granules at a prescribed coverage rate onto a fresh, still-plastic surface so they bond and produce the specified colored finish. This is the same physical operation as sprinkling stone chips or color hardener; it is done entirely by machine where the work is conveyed to the applicator (E1 presentation).

sources.title: STS-11M Topping Spreader – Somero
sources.claim: On real job sites, dry-shake toppings and color hardeners are spread with operator-ridden or walk-behind mechanical spreaders (Somero STS topping spreaders, Morrison spreaders) or by hand; no autonomous broadcasting machine is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task, but the machine is an operator-driven tool rather than an autonomous system, so it cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3; it establishes the current on-site state of the art.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics concrete construction robot line (ground leveling robot, floating robot, basement glazing/troweling robot)
sources.title: 科技赋能建筑业 博智林开拓“建筑机器人”应用蓝海 _ 经济参考网
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics fields a commercialized line of autonomous concrete construction robots (placing, leveling, floating, basement power-troweling) that work on fresh slabs at building sites, but the product line covers screeding/floating/troweling and floor grinding and coating - not broadcasting dry-shake hardener, chips, or coloring powder.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that autonomous machines can work on plastic concrete at construction sites, but only for placing/leveling/troweling; nothing in the line broadcasts granular hardener or chips at a prescribed rate, so it does not transfer to this task and is cited only to support the negative E2/E3 judgments.

tasks.label: Fabricate concrete beams, columns, and panels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Site-cast tilt-up wall panels at a commercial construction site: the mason chalks and sets edge forms and blockouts on the casting slab, sets rebar mats, embeds and lift inserts, places ready-mix, then screeds, floats and trowels the panel face. Outdoors, weather-exposed, layout and panel sizes differ job to job.

Precast/prestressed plant, standard flat elements: solid and sandwich wall panels, double/filigree walls and hollow-core floor planks produced to shop drawings on fixed steel beds or a pallet circulation line - shuttering, reinforcement, casting, vibration, surface floating, kiln curing, stripping.

Precast plant, architectural cladding panels: form liners, reveals, thin-brick or exposed-aggregate faces, project-specific shapes; the mason lays up the form, casts and works the face to the specified texture, then patches and cleans the panel.

Precast/prestressed plant, structural frame members: beams, columns, double-tees and bridge girders on long-line beds - set and close heavy steel side forms, tension strands, place rebar cages/stirrups and hardware, place and vibrate concrete, screed and finish the top, steam cure, strip and patch.

Cast-in-place beams and columns on a jobsite: erect and align column/beam forms to line and grade, place cages and inserts, pour by pump or bucket with vibration, strip the forms, then rub, patch and grout the exposed concrete faces. Congested, changing site conditions.

sources.system: Elematic EDGE Wall production line (plotter, Shuttering Robot E9, casting machine, compaction station)
sources.title: Precast wall production | Highly automated EDGE Wall | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic EDGE Wall is a commercially sold, highly automated pallet-circulation line for precast wall panels in which a plotter marks the layout, a shuttering robot places the side forms, a casting machine places concrete with a compaction station, and pallets move automatically to curing and tilting.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task for panels: the line fabricates solid, sandwich and double wall panels with openings and inserts. For the site-cast tilt-up instance the transfer is object-for-object - a large flat reinforced wall panel with blockouts, embeds and a finished face - produced with the work fixtured on a pallet.

sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: The Elematic Shuttering Robot E9 carries out the full shuttering/deshuttering cycle of a precast wall plant - placing shutters per the production plan, activating magnets, plotting, demolding all shutters, and cleaning and oiling them - for double walls, filigree slabs, solid walls and sandwich panels.

sources.system: Huffcutt carousel precast plant (shuttering robot, concrete spreader, automated finishing, pallet stacker)
sources.developer: Huffcutt Concrete (plant technology by Weckenmann / ebos)
sources.title: Brand New Precast Concrete Wall Panel Plant | Huffcutt
sources.claim: Huffcutt Concrete (Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin) operates a deployed carousel precast wall-panel plant in which a fully automated shuttering robot sets shutters from CAD data, an automatic concrete spreader pours to the element contour, pallets are stacked automatically for kiln curing, and the plant's finishing process is automated to give a consistent finish whatever texture is specified.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a US plant: fabrication of architectural and structural precast wall panels, including the surface finish, on a machine-built carousel line.

sources.system: Progress Wire Center rebar automation (with MSR straightening/cutting/bending machine)
sources.developer: Progress Maschinen & Automation (Progress Group), installed at Gebr. Ott
sources.title: Automated lattice girder transport at Gebrueder Ott - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: At Gebr. Ott's precast plant a Progress 'Wire Center' robot fabricates rebar and lattice girders from coil and places the reinforcement automatically on the circulating pallets to CAD specification, closing the reinforcement step of panel fabrication.

sources.system: Weckenmann third-generation shuttering robot on a pallet circulation system
sources.developer: Weckenmann Anlagentechnik, installed at Keegan Precast
sources.title: Keegan Precast adds to portfolio with a new pallet circulation system - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: Keegan Precast's pallet circulation system shutters double wall, floor slab and solid wall elements with a fully automated Weckenmann shuttering robot - a second deployed example of robotic panel fabrication lines in operation.

sources.title: Concrete extruder for hollow core casting | Elematic P7
sources.claim: The Elematic Extruder P7 casts prestressed hollow-core floor planks on long beds and is offered ready for fully automatic operation, showing that flat prestressed panel elements are cast, compacted and surface-formed by machine without an operator working the concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Hollow-core planks are the flat prestressed floor/wall panel product of the same plants; the machine performs the placing, compaction and surface forming a mason would otherwise do by hand.

sources.system: Sommer circulation system finishing screeds, rollers and 'helicopter' smoothing devices
sources.title: Circulation System *** Sommer Anlagentechnik GmbH ***
sources.claim: In precast plants, surface treatment of panels on circulation lines is performed by line-integrated finishing screeds, rollers and 'helicopter' power-float devices positioned within the pallet circuit.

sources.system: Elematic Caster P7 / frame caster P7 (beam and column molds)
sources.title: Caster P7 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: The casting machine used to fill precast beam and column molds on Elematic's frame (beam and column) line is run by an operator with a ... controller, with only a semi-automatic version offered - beam and column casting is not an autonomous operation even in modern precast plants.

tasks.label: Polish surface, using polishing or surfacing machine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ride-on or walk-behind power trowel (surfacing machine) floating and finishing the open field of a large interior slab pour — warehouse, big-box shell, parking structure, basement garage — with repeated passes timed to the concrete's set; the perimeter strip is handled separately by hand.

Walk-behind power trowel / power float on a small interior pour: residential garage or basement, small commercial room or equipment pad. Tight space, obstacles (columns, drains, doorways, embeds), and much of the surface is within reach of walls so edge blending is part of the same job.

Diamond grinding and polishing a cured concrete floor to a specified gloss in a large open interior (warehouse, retail sales floor, showroom, factory bay): planetary grinder/polisher, multi-grit pass sequence with densifier, dust extraction, floor cleared and access controlled.

Grinding/polishing in small or obstructed areas: perimeter strips and corners, around columns, doorways and fixtures, stair treads, small rooms and residential garage floors, using edge grinders and hand-held polishers to match the field finish.

Exterior flatwork: driveway, patio, sidewalk or curb-adjacent slab finished outdoors with a power float/trowel or surface grinder — irregular shapes, slopes to drain, weather and sun affecting set, uneven access, adjacent landscaping and traffic.

Surface dressing and repair with a grinder/surfacing machine on existing in-place work: grinding down trip hazards or high spots on sidewalks and slabs, removing form marks and blemishes on walls and patched areas, blending to surrounding finish.

sources.title: Autonomous Concrete Floor Polishing & LightWare's SF40/C LiDAR | Unmanned Systems Technology
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 is a retrofit kit that makes a walk-behind concrete polishing machine navigate and polish a floor autonomously, targeted at warehouse floors before racking/occupancy; humans still do the hand grinding and edges in parallel.

sources.developer: Shenzhen/Nanjing Legend Robot Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Automated Floor grinding & dust collection robot — Legend Robot
sources.claim: Legend Robot sells a Floor Grinding Robot (1250 kg, 780 mm grinding width) that performs fully automated grinding and polishing of concrete floors with one supervising operator, quoted at 800-1,000 m2/day rough grinding and 3,000-4,000 m2/day polishing, for underground parking garages, factory workshops, ... and sports venues.

sources.system: XINGYI AT8 Autonomous Floor Grinder (ATLAS FSG)
sources.developer: Fujian Xingyi Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd.
sources.title: AT8 Automatic Robot Grinder | XINGYI
sources.claim: Xingyi, a floor-grinder manufacturer, sells the AT8 autonomous floor grinder with laser + visual navigation and the ATLAS FSG control system, aimed at superflat industrial/warehouse floor grinding with multi-pass layered cut control.

sources.developer: Fujian Xingyi Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Xingyi Selected for Wenzhou's 2026 "AI + Construction" Pilot Program
sources.claim: The AT8 floor grinding robot was demonstrated and tested in a municipal 'AI + Construction' pilot programme in Wenzhou in 2026, with self-navigation, path planning, full-coverage grinding, obstacle detection and adjustable ....

sources.developer: Bright Dream Robotics / Guangdong Bojiatuo Construction Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction: Challenges and Opportunities (Drones 2022, 6, 424)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review reports Bright Dream Robotics' basement glazing (power-troweling) robot finishing fresh concrete basement/garage floors autonomously along a pre-programmed path with integrated navigation; the strip at the wall edge must still be finished manually.

sources.developer: Bright Dream Robotics / Guangdong Bojiatuo Construction Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction: Challenges and Opportunities (Drones 2022, 6, 424)
sources.claim: The same review describes Bright Dream Robotics' floor grinding robot, used to remove floating slurry from hardened concrete in underground garages and indoor workshops with a single person controlling it — autonomy level not clearly established.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics construction robot fleet
sources.title: Senior Management from Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics Co Ltd Visited the CKSRI — HKUST Robotics Institute
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics reports large-scale commercial use of its construction robot line-up on Chinese building sites, corroborating that its floor finishing robots are field-deployed rather than lab prototypes.

sources.system: Concrete polishing robot with omnidirectional mobile mechanism (Cho et al.)
sources.developer: Cho et al., Korean Society of Manufacturing Technology Engineers
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction (review, Section 2.3.2)
sources.claim: Research concrete polishing robot with omnidirectional mobile base that smooths/polishes concrete floor surfaces along a preset trajectory with no manual operation, intended for residential floors, warehouses, basements and factories.

sources.system: DINOSAW multi-head automatic slab polishing machine
sources.title: Multi-head Automatic Marble & Granite Polishing Machine
sources.claim: Industrial multi-head automatic polishing lines under PLC control, with laser scanning of the slab profile, polish fixtured cement-based terrazzo and engineered-stone slabs to a mirror gloss on a conveyor bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine polishing of cement-based terrazzo/engineered-stone slabs with sequenced diamond abrasive heads to a specified gloss and flatness. This is the same abrasive surfacing operation a concrete finisher performs with a planetary polisher, on comparable cementitious material and to comparable surface precision; at E1 the slab is presented fixtured on the machine bench, which is exactly how these lines work.

sources.title: Breton Kappa G | Slab Polisher Granite Quartz
sources.claim: Breton supplies fully automatic multi-spindle slab polishing lines (e.g. Kappa G with two independent beams of ten spindles each) used in industrial stone/agglomerate plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed multi-head abrasive polishing of a fixtured slab. Corroborates that purpose-built polishing cells for hard mineral slabs (including cement-bound agglomerates) are standard commercial equipment, i.e. the E1 version of machine polishing is routine industrial practice.

tasks.label: Cut metal division strips, and press them into terrazzo base so that top edges form desired design or pattern.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Thin-set epoxy terrazzo in new commercial construction (school, hospital, airport concourse): worker snaps layout lines from the architect's drawings on a prepared slab, cuts zinc/brass L-strips to length with snips or a chop saw, and beds them in epoxy/silicone along the grid and control-joint lines; active jobsite shared with other trades, debris and changing conditions.

Cement (sand-cushion or bonded) terrazzo: worker cuts strips and presses them into the fresh sand-cement underbed so the top edges sit exactly at finish grade, straight and level, forming the perimeter and the field grid before the topping is poured; active jobsite.

Custom decorative design: worker hand-bends and cuts strips to curves, letters, logos and medallions, mitres and butts joints, and works from a full-size pattern or stencil transferred to the floor; intricate radii and tight tolerances, on the jobsite.

Stairs, landings, cove base, thresholds and transitions: strips cut and fitted to treads, risers, nosings, columns, door openings and irregular as-built edges, often scribed to existing construction and set vertically or on sloped surfaces.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: divider strips cut and set into flat molds/casting beds for panels, stair treads, sills and bases before the terrazzo mix is poured; fixed indoor shop with standard molds and repeat patterns.

Repair/restoration in an existing occupied building or residence: damaged strip sections cut out and replaced, new strips cut and bedded to match the adjacent pattern and elevation of the existing terrazzo floor.

sources.system: Form Master shuttering & deshuttering robot (Progress Maschinen & Automation)
sources.title: Shuttering Robot | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Progress Group's Form Master shuttering robot selects metal shuttering profiles from storage per CAD data and positions them on the flat mould/pallet surface fully automatically with high precision, forming the CAD-defined outline pattern for each precast element.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated shuttering of precast moulds. It is the same core act as setting division strips - laying thin metal profiles out on a flat bed in a CAD-defined pattern at millimetre precision, with their top edges defining the cast surface - performed in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Alpha Beton | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: The Form Master is in production use in operating precast plants (e.g., Alpha Beton, Belgium), carrying out all shuttering work steps fully automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (automated mould shuttering); this item establishes that the CAD-driven metal-profile layout robot is deployed commercially in real plants, not only demonstrated.

sources.system: FrameTek CNC abrasive waterjet cutting (Creative Edge)
sources.title: Akron-Canton Airport atrium features Tree of Life terrazzo design
sources.claim: Terrazzo divider/frame metal is routinely cut to shape by CNC waterjet machines in a fabrication plant, directly from CAD, to 0.002 in. tolerance, including curved leaf forms and lettering that are later installed by hand on the jobsite.
sources.transferJustification: This is the 'cut metal division strips' half of the task itself, performed by a machine under CAD control in a purpose-built plant; only the pressing/setting into the terrazzo base is left to the human installer.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X mobile blocklaying robot works from a 3D CAD model, cuts blocks to size on board, applies construction adhesive and places each block with dynamically stabilised precision; five homes were completed in a US demonstration program in 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic masonry. It shows machine-controlled cutting of elements to size plus placement into a fresh adhesive/mortar bed at CAD-defined positions and elevations - the 'press into the base to the correct line and height' element of the terrazzo strip task, though with much larger, rigid units.

sources.title: FieldPrinter autonomous robot automates jobsite layout - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: Autonomous jobsite layout robots print BIM-derived lines and pattern geometry directly on construction floors, but only mark the surface; they do not cut or install any material.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite layout. Cited to characterise what field robots actually do on active construction floors - line marking only - supporting the negative judgment that no fielded system sets terrazzo divider strips in situ.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Indoor floor-tile paving robots are sold commercially for laying standard-format tiles into a mortar bed inside buildings, but they handle only rigid modular tiles of fixed sizes and do not cut or set thin metal strips.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior floor finishing. Cited only to bound the state of the art for in-building floor work; it does not substantiate cutting or embedding division strips, so it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Push roller over surface to embed chips in surface.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential seeded exposed-aggregate flatwork: on a freshly screeded and bull-floated driveway, patio or walkway at a private home, the mason broadcasts decorative pea gravel/chips over the surface and pushes a seeder/tamping roller across it, working around forms, edges, slopes and yard obstacles, on a timing window set by concrete set and weather, until every chip is embedded and covered by a thin layer of paste.

Interior decorative floor in a commercial building under construction or renovation (retail, restaurant, lobby, gym): colored chips, quartz or flake are broadcast into a fresh topping slab or resin coat over a large open floor and a roller is pushed over the area to embed them evenly, amid other trades, dust, stacked material and varying room geometry.

Public outdoor flatwork: sidewalk panels, plazas, bus pads or streetscape work where decorative or anti-skid aggregate is broadcast on fresh concrete and rolled in, curbside with traffic control and pedestrians, uneven access, and weather exposure.

Plant/shop production: architectural precast panels, paving slabs or cast steps produced on casting beds or pallets in a precast yard, where aggregate/chips are spread over the fresh cast face and a roller is run over the panel to embed them, indoors under a controlled production schedule.

Small, confined or irregular in-place work: patching and re-seeding a damaged decorative area, stair treads, small pads, curb returns and tight courtyards, where a small hand roller is worked over limited areas of existing in-place concrete alongside hand-tool edge work.

sources.system: Vollert roller (surface technology, pallet circulation line)
sources.title: Surface technology - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Vollert's precast plant surface-technology line includes a roller machine that travels lengthways over a fixtured steel pallet to compact and distribute fresh concrete from the top after casting — i.e., a purpose-built machine that pushes a roller over a fresh concrete surface presented on a pallet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: roller compaction/distribution of fresh concrete from the top in a precast line. Same tool (a roller traversing the fresh surface), same workpiece (freshly cast concrete on a fixtured pallet) and same requirement of uniform pressure across the panel that embedding broadcast chips needs; the fixtured presentation removes the navigation and geometry variability of site work.

sources.title: Surface technology - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: The same plant line includes an automatic trowelling machine that travels over the fixtured pallet and finishes the exposed upper face of the fresh precast element with adjustable rotating vanes and add-on discs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine surface finishing of the top face of fresh concrete. It establishes that timed, contact surface-finishing passes over a fresh cast face are executed by machine to product-acceptance quality when the panel is fixtured on a pallet, which is the presentation assumed for this task at E1.

sources.system: Olmet carousel plant / pallet circulation system with bladed-trowel surface polishing device
sources.title: Carousel plant - Olmet Italy
sources.claim: Carousel (pallet circulation) precast plants are highly automated production lines in which the upper face of the semi-dry concrete panel is finished by an integrated bladed-trowel surface device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated top-face finishing of fresh concrete panels. Corroborates that machine passes over the fresh cast face are standard, accepted practice in purpose-built precast lines, the environment assumed for this task at E1.

sources.system: Weckenmann carousel wall panel line at Molin Concrete Products (Ramsey, MN)
sources.title: Carousel Course – Concrete Products
sources.claim: Automated carousel precast lines in North America form, pour, cure and finish wall panels in a continuous line with minimal human contact, showing these fixtured lines are in commercial production use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated production-line finishing of fresh concrete panels. Establishes real deployment (not just vendor catalog) of purpose-built, fixtured concrete finishing lines in which surface-treatment machines pass over the fresh cast face.

sources.system: Smooth G1 basement concrete troweling and leveling robot
sources.title: iF Design - Basement Concrete Troweling and Leveling Robot
sources.claim: A mobile robot system for jobsite concrete floors performs autonomous leveling and, after initial set, troweling, planning its path and positioning itself on basement floor slabs, with one person doing auxiliary work; it does not handle broadcast decorative chips or roller embedding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous finishing passes over a fresh in-situ slab. Cited to show the closest jobsite systems level and trowel large open slabs; none is documented embedding broadcast decorative aggregate with a roller, so it does not carry over to this task's chip-embedding quality judgment or to edge/small-area work.

tasks.label: Apply muriatic acid to clean surface, and rinse with water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential exterior flatwork: after stripping forms on a new driveway, patio, walk or steps, the mason mixes dilute muriatic acid in a plastic pail or pump sprayer, wets the slab, applies acid to remove mortar smears, form-oil stains and efflorescence, agitates with an acid brush/broom, then flushes with a garden hose while keeping runoff off plantings, siding and adjacent lawn.

Interior slab etch before coating in an occupied commercial/industrial building (warehouse aisle, retail back-of-house, service garage bay): floor pre-wetted, diluted muriatic acid spread and scrubbed to open the surface profile, dwell until fizzing stops, neutralized, then rinsed repeatedly and the slurry picked up with a wet vac/squeegee; coating applicator will pH-test and reject an uneven or residue-laden etch.

Decorative concrete: acid wash of colored, stamped or exposed-aggregate flatwork at a home or commercial plaza to brighten aggregate and remove lime bloom without burning the color or streaking; requires masking/protection of adjacent glass, metal, stone and plantings and careful uniform coverage.

Equipment and tool cleaning at the contractor's yard or ready-mix plant: dilute acid sprayed or brushed on wheelbarrows, mixers, chutes, floats, forms and mixer drums/hoppers to dissolve hardened concrete build-up, allowed to dwell, agitated, then rinsed with a pressure washer or hose.

Vertical surfaces on an active jobsite: acid wash of poured walls, columns, curbs, retaining walls or block/masonry to remove mortar smears and efflorescence, worked from the ground, ladder or scaffold, wetting first, applying acid top-down in sections, and rinsing thoroughly before it dries.

Fabrication shop/precast plant: acid etching or acid washing of precast panels, architectural units, counters or cast pieces on stands or a casting bed to achieve a uniform etched finish, followed by a water rinse into a plant drainage/neutralization system.

sources.system: Sioux Ready Mix Truck Wash (TW40 power unit / TWR40 wash tower)
sources.date: 2024-10 (product page; system reported in trade press 2022)
sources.title: Automatic Ready Mix Truck Wash - Concrete Truck Wash Systems | Sioux Corporation
sources.claim: Sioux's automatic ready-mix truck wash is a purpose-built drive-through wash bay at concrete plants whose sensors start a PLC-controlled cycle that sprays cleaning chemical onto concrete-encrusted surfaces and then cleans and rinses them with high-pressure water — i.e. chemical application plus water rinse of concrete build-up entirely under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chemical cleaning of hardened concrete residue off equipment. It is the same physical operation as the rated task — wet the surface, apply a cleaning chemical (acid-based concrete removers are standard for this duty), dwell, then flush with water — performed on concrete-fouled surfaces by a sensor-triggered, programmable machine in a purpose-built bay.

sources.system: Cleaning / oiling machine in Olmet pallet circulation (carousel) plant
sources.title: Pallet circulation system / carousel plant - Olmet Italy
sources.claim: Precast concrete carousel plants use a self-propelling cleaning/oiling machine that scrapes and brushes hardened concrete residue off the casting surface and then sprays a chemical (release agent) uniformly over the plate and side elements through adjustable nozzles, as an automated station in the production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of concrete residue from a large flat casting surface followed by uniform machine spraying of a liquid chemical over that surface — the same coverage-level precision, comparable large flat concrete-contacted workpiece, and it shows the cleaning-then-liquid-application sequence running unattended in a purpose-built plant line.

sources.system: Continuous HCl pickling line (carbon steel strip)
sources.developer: steel plant process line (e.g. Fives push-pull/continuous pickling lines)
sources.title: Pickling Line Acid Regeneration and Tank Maintenance
sources.claim: Continuous carbon-steel pickling lines apply hydrochloric acid (muriatic acid) to clean scale from the strip surface and then run the strip through an automated rinse section that removes residual acid, with acid concentration and rinse effectiveness controlled by the process line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hydrochloric-acid surface cleaning followed by a water rinse. It is the literal chemistry and sequence of the rated task, executed at industrial scale entirely by machine on work conveyed to the line, showing that acid dosing, dwell and rinse-to-cleanliness are solved when the work is presented to purpose-built equipment.

sources.title: Robotic Floor Scrubbers | Floor Cleaning Machines | Tennant Company
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic floor scrubbers (Tennant BrainOS fleet, thousands deployed) navigate human-occupied facilities and clean concrete floors by dispensing water and detergent, scrubbing, and recovering the solution — but they perform maintenance cleaning with neutral detergents, not multi-stage acid etching with dwell, neutralization and pH verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a cleaning solution to a concrete floor in a structured facility with recovery of the spent liquid. Cited to show the closest E2-level capability; it does not substantiate the rated task because no source shows these machines handling corrosive acid, sequencing acid/neutralizer/rinse passes, or delivering a coating-acceptable etch.

sources.system: Sherpa cleaning drone; Lavo AI autonomous pressure washing robot
sources.title: Lucid Bots Raises $20 Million Series B to Accelerate the Buildout of America's Leading Exterior Cleaning Platform
sources.claim: Lucid Bots sells exterior cleaning robots — the operator-piloted Sherpa drone (soft wash: chemical application, dwell, rinse) and the newly launched Lavo AI ... ground pressure-washing robot for flat concrete such as parking structures — with roughly 1,000 robots across its operator network.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior washing of concrete surfaces. Cited for completeness at E3; the chemical soft-wash sequence is performed by the operator-piloted Sherpa drone (FAA Part 107 pilot required), and no source shows the autonomous Lavo unit dosing acid, controlling dwell, or containing/neutralizing acid runoff on new flatwork.

tasks.label: Spread roofing paper on surface of foundation, and spread concrete onto roofing paper with trowel to form terrazzo base.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-build institutional/commercial project (school, courthouse, airport concourse): mason cleans the structural slab in a large open floor area, rolls out overlapping roofing/tar paper (isolation sheet), lays wire mesh, then shovels, spreads and screeds a stiff sand-cement underbed roughly 1.25-3 in. thick and floats/trowels it flat and to elevation, ready for divider strips. Dusty open shell, other trades nearby, mortar delivered by buggy or pump.

New-build corridors, lobbies and rooms broken up by columns, door openings, thresholds, floor drains, curbs and cove-base transitions: paper must be cut and fitted around penetrations and turned up at walls, mesh clipped, and the underbed hand-troweled tight to walls, doorways and edges at varying elevations.

Renovation/restoration inside an existing building (school wing, historic courthouse): work zone is a gutted room reached by stairs or freight elevator; existing slab is uneven and out of level, elevations must be matched to adjoining existing floors and thresholds, small crew hand-carries paper, mesh and mortar, dust control and limited working hours.

Stairs, landings, ramps and small irregular areas: mason cuts and fits paper on treads, risers and sloped landings, secures mesh, and hand-trowels the base mortar onto stepped, sloped and partly vertical surfaces to nosing lines and shallow thicknesses.

Small residential or light-commercial job (entry foyer, bathroom, small shop floor): small flat area over a residential slab, hand-mixed or small-batch mortar, paper cut to fit the room, base spread and troweled by hand in tight quarters with homeowner belongings or shop fixtures nearby.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous mobile robot that applies plaster and finishes/paints interior surfaces on active construction sites; it is the closest commercially active system for autonomously spreading cementitious material in an unstructured building shell, but it works on walls/ceilings and does not lay sheet membranes or place a thick floor underbed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-applied plaster/finish coats. It shows autonomous cementitious spreading is possible in an as-found construction site, but on vertical surfaces, with no sheet-membrane laying and no thick sand-cement underbed placement, so it does not substantiate completion of this task at E3 or E2.

sources.title: ZP-415A Concrete Laser Screed Robot_Construction Robots_Suzhou Fangshi Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.claim: Fangshi's ZP-415A laser screed robot performs laser-guided leveling of freshly poured concrete floors (5-15 cm thickness) on building floors with unmanned movement; it levels a wet pour but does not lay isolation paper or place a semi-dry terrazzo underbed over it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: screeding poured floor concrete. Comparable material and floor setting, but it covers only leveling of a wet pour and gives no capability for laying roofing paper or troweling a stiff terrazzo underbed to a finished elevation.

sources.system: Clapa Floor Master / MAI FLOOR MASTER XL screed machines
sources.title: Clapa - Automatic Floor Screeding Robots & Machines
sources.claim: On-site machines that spread, compact and level cement-sand and semi-dry screeds exist commercially (Clapa Floor Master, MAI FLOOR MASTER XL), but they are guided by an operator with a ... rather than operating autonomously, and the separating/isolation sheet under a floating screed is still laid by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spreading and leveling semi-dry sand-cement screed, essentially the underbed half of this task; because it is operator-remote-controlled it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier under the autonomy rule.

sources.system: Pallet circulation system with shuttering robot, automated concrete spreader and smoothing station (Progress/Weckenmann/Vollert-type lines)
sources.title: Master computers 4.0: production control systems in the technological... - Concrete Plant + Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: In precast concrete plants, workpieces on steel pallets pass through a purpose-built machine line in which the pallet is cleaned, shuttered by robot, reinforced, then concreted by an automated concrete spreader, compacted and power-smoothed under master-computer control, producing flat concrete layers of specified thickness on a fixtured bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine placement, screeding and smoothing of a concrete layer of controlled thickness onto a fixtured flat bed with reinforcement inserted - the same operation as spreading and troweling a terrazzo underbed, at equal or better flatness tolerance, in a purpose-built (E1) setting.

sources.system: Fully automatic gypsum board production line (paper unwinding and forming station)
sources.developer: Shandong Yurui Machinery Group (line supplier); same process used in Knauf/USG-type plants
sources.title: Hot Oil Gypsum Board Production Line - Shandong Yurui Machinery Group Co.,Ltd
sources.claim: Fully automatic plasterboard production lines unwind a continuous paper sheet onto the forming table and deposit and spread a cementitious (gypsum) slurry onto that paper, forming and leveling it to a controlled thickness before cutting - a single machine line that both lays the paper and spreads the mix over it, entirely under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying paper on a flat forming surface and spreading a cementitious mix over the paper to uniform thickness. It is the same pair of operations as this task (paper spread on the surface, mix spread over the paper to form a base), same material class, tighter thickness tolerance, in a purpose-built machine environment.
